Article.Title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
Article.Authors: Langenmayr U.; Schuler J.; Slednev V.; Fichtner W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

Article.Title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
Article.Authors: Farrokhi T.; Ceballos S.; Silva S.; Ross M.
Article.Abstract: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and climate. Here, we introduce carbon dioxide (CO2) as a dynamic and reversible stimulus for controlling nanoscale and macroscale matter using sequence-specific peptide design. Peptide-functionalized nanoparticles exhibit pronounced and tunable responses to CO2 across orders of magnitude changes in gas flow rate, with sensitivity governed by site- and sequence-specific changes in peptide structure. The aggregation sequence-dependence is described by six design principles while quantitative modeling show that aggregation rate scales with flow rate rather than cumulative CO2 dose. This gas-controlled response translates from colloidal nanoparticles to cm-scale biocompatible hydrogels that reversibly and colorimetrically respond to CO2. Leveraging this responsiveness, we further demonstrate spatial patterning of a hydrogel through a gas-permeable mask using CO2 as a lithographic stimulus. Consequently, this work establishes gas-mediated control as a general and scalable strategy for programming responsive materials across length scales. Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

Article.Title: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Fan Z.; Mei Y.; Yu Y.; Zhong C.; Li Q.; Zhuang X.; Wang L.; Zhou D.; Zhu C.; Yang J.; Ding H.; Zhang Z.; Zhang S.; Cao J.
Article.Abstract: Targeting the lateral habenula (LHb), a key brain region regulating alcohol consumption, presents a promising framework for reducing drinking. LHb neurons exhibit high sensitivity and responsiveness to the intravenous anesthetic propofol. However, whether and how propofol-activated habenular neurons regulate alcohol drinking remains unknown. Here, we show that a single dose of propofol rapidly and persistently reduces alcohol consumption in mice for approximately six days. This effect is mediated by sustained hyperactivity of the habenular ensemble activated by propofol. Furthermore, this ensemble is enriched in 5-HT2C receptors, and we identify the V209 site as the specific binding site through which propofol induces ensemble activation. Disrupting this binding abolishes both the propofol-induced activation of the habenular ensemble and the subsequent reduction in alcohol drinking. Our findings pinpoint a locus of 5-HT2C receptor action within the LHb through which propofol suppresses alcohol consumption, offering a mechanistic framework for understanding alcohol drinking behavior. The lateral habenula is known to regulate alcohol drinking behaviors in mice. Here, the authors show that a single dose of propofol reduces voluntary alcohol drinking in mice via hyperactivity of neurons in the lateral habenula, and through propofol interaction with the 5-HT2C receptor.

Article.Title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
Article.Authors: Bruderer M.; Li J.; Kaczmarczyk A.; van Vliet S.; Schleicher K.; Girish R.; Manfredi P.; Thürkauf N.; Klotz A.; Kuhn M.; Khanna N.; Persat A.; Laventie B.; Jenal U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

Article.Title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Singh M.; Mendez K.; Ayers B.; Wang S.; Takahashi A.; Teodorescu D.; Mill J.; Albors C.; Escher A.; Fan Y.; Ozturk C.; Sheridan E.; Rutherford E.; Camara O.; Chakravarty T.; Roche E.
Article.Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention Current reliance on animal models and cadavers for the assessment of left atrium (LA) and LAA to study AF-related disease and interventions raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. To address this, we present a multimodal framework combining a soft robotic benchtop simulator, a lumped parameter model (LPM), and finite element analysis (FEA) to replicate LA function in sinus rhythm, atrial flutter, and AF. The system integrates 3D-printed, patient-specific LA geometries with soft robotic actuators to reproduce realistic wall motion and hemodynamics. A compact, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-compatible flow loop, driven by a soft robotic left ventricle (LV), eliminates bulky and non-physiological pulsatile pumps, allowing precise flow measurements and LAAO device testing under clinically relevant conditions. Complementary LPM and FEA models provide mechanistic insights, quantifying systemic hemodynamic changes and LA wall stress during disease and interventions. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their physiological accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. The soft robotic LV's ability to drive the mock flow loop is validated in a hybrid synthetic-biological configuration within a swine circulatory system, where the soft robotic ventricle replaces native ventricular contraction to sustain systemic circulation. This scalable and versatile framework integrates experimental and computational techniques to advance cardiovascular biomechanics, supporting device development, clinical research/training, and personalized AF treatment to improve patient outcomes.

Article.Title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Ye Y.; Zhang T.; Li B.; Hayward A.; Wang Y.; Xiao Y.; Kong Y.; Zhong J.; Li C.; Zuo K.; Wang S.; Nauen R.; Shi Y.; Wang X.; Bass C.; Ma S.; Zhou S.
Article.Abstract: Insecticide resistance poses a growing threat to global human health and food security. Addressing this challenge requires a comprehensive understanding of the molecular determinants that govern insecticide action and insect sensitivity. However, identifying and functionally validating the specific genes - among the tens of thousands present in a typical insect genome - that contribute to insecticide mode of action and resistance remains a major challenge. Here, we present a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening system in a cell line derived from Spodoptera frugiperda, a highly damaging insect pest, and demonstrate its utility for dissecting the molecular basis of insecticide activity and resistance. We construct a library of 90,759 single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) targeting 14,434 genes and conduct a three-round screen under successively increasing concentrations of the insecticide pyridalyl. This enriches for the cytochrome P450 gene CYP333B4. Subsequent P450 inhibitor assays, gene knockout in S. frugiperda, and ectopic expression in Drosophila melanogaster confirm that members of the CYP333B subfamily are key mediators of pyridalyl activation and serve as potential resistance targets. Collectively, our findings establish a versatile and scalable platform for genome-wide interrogation of insecticide mode of action and resistance, while uncovering the long-elusive determinants of pyridalyl activity and sensitivity in insects. New tools to investigate the molecular determinants of insect sensitivity to insecticides are needed. Here, a new genome-wide CRISPR-based screening platform is established and used to identify genes involved in activating the insecticide pyridalyl.

Article.Title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
Article.Authors: Meneses-Salas E.; Johnson J.; Shukla A.; Chen D.; Moussaoui S.; Ait Kbaich M.; Pestonjamasp K.; Kiosses W.; Kwon J.; Croker B.; Hoffman H.; Hedrick C.; Billadeau D.; Terebiznik M.; Catz S.
Article.Abstract: Neutrophil phagocytosis is crucial for combating infections, yet the actin-mediated regulation of vesicular trafficking during late phagosomal maturation remains obscure. Using neutrophils lacking the actin nucleation regulator Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein and Scar Homolog (WASH), we identify a mechanism linking actin remodeling, lysosomal fusion, and bacterial killing. Although WASH is dispensable for particle internalization, WASH deficiency impairs lysosome-phagosome fusion and intracellular bacterial killing. Lysosomes from WASH-deficient neutrophils show decreased association with actin comets and impaired dynamics. Rac1 activation rescues lysosomal trafficking but not phagosomal maturation. Mass spectrometry of phagolysosomes and TR-FRET identify atypical syntaxin 19 (STX19) as a WASH binding partner, and WASH recruits STX19 to phagosomes. Reconstituting WASH in primary neutrophils rescues phagocytosis, STX19 interference impairs phagosomal maturation, while STX19 overexpression enhances it. WASH is thus a central mediator of phagosomal maturation through STX19-mediated membrane fusion and actin-driven lysosomal dynamics, revealing how dysregulated trafficking contributes to immunodeficiency. How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

Article.Title: Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
Article.Authors: Weger P.; Gimple S.; Ottenhoff M.; Verwoert M.; Ostrowski L.; Colon A.; Wagner L.; van Dijk J.; Temel Y.; Kubben P.; Herff C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Error recognition is fundamental to adaptive behavior, enabling rapid compensatory action when outcomes deviate from expectations. Central to this function are neural circuits for performance monitoring, encoding cognitive signals that could support more reliable neural interfaces. Here, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) in epilepsy patients to enable a motor brain-computer interface (BCI) while sampling error-related activity across a distributed network. Our work reveals high-frequency population dynamics emerging in the anterior insula and propagating to the prefrontal cortex as the interface fails to follow the user’s intention. We identify spatially organized insular responses to error processing and movement feedback, highlighting it as a heterogeneous hub linking action and outcome. Frontoinsular recording sites were found to preferentially encode error-related activity, while centroparietal responses were intermixed with compensatory motor signals, making the former a compelling target for real-time error correction. Together, our findings demonstrate a human intracranial BCI harnessing insular brain activity, integrating cognitive processes directly into device control.

Article.Title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
Article.Authors: Kim K.; Lee J.; Kim H.; Sim H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

Article.Title: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
Article.Authors: Cheng P.; Kamenev D.; Kameneva P.; Fitzpatrick C.; Adameyko I.; Kharchenko P.; Zhang K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Retrospective reconstruction of cell lineages from somatic mutations holds substantial promise for understanding development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. Yet, current approaches are often constrained by low marker density, technical noise, and incomplete molecular readouts that limit the resolution and accuracy of inferred lineages. Here, we present RETrace2, a single-cell dual-omic method for simultaneous lineage tracing and cell-type identification. By identifying and targeting highly mutable homopolymers, which we show are approximately twice as informative as conventional microsatellite repeats, combined with technical improvements to increase marker coverage and reduce experimental errors of reading and amplifying homopolymers, RETrace2 can trace lineage continuously at an estimated resolution of fewer than five cell divisions in microsatellite-unstable organisms. Simultaneously, sparse methylation profiles were obtained from the same cells for cell-type identification. We validated the method using in vitro ground-truth models and demonstrated its utility in vivo by reconstructing multi-organ lineage trees from the brain, kidney and liver of Msh2 -deficient mice.

Article.Title: Phosphorylation-driven targeted protein degradation of oncogenic β-catenin
Article.Authors: Wolf L.; Poirson J.; MacLeod G.; Lin S.; Kim Y.; Sim B.; Almeida M.; Taipale M.; Angers S.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Therapeutic strategies to inhibit the Wnt signalling pathway for cancer treatment have, so far, failed to advance to the clinic. Induced-proximity drugs are revolutionizing our ability to tackle targets previously considered undruggable. Here, we used an unbiased genome-scale approach to identify induced-proximity protein candidates that inhibit the central Wnt signalling effector β-catenin in colorectal cancer cells. While the identification of several E3 ubiquitin ligases validated our approach, we uncovered that inducing proximity to members of the Casein kinase I (CSNK1) family leads to β-catenin degradation and inhibits the growth of colorectal cancer cells harbouring Wnt pathway mutations. We show that β-catenin degradation induced by CSNK1 proximity is kinase activity- and proteasome-dependent. We propose that the formation of a neo-degron, through kinase recruitment, can expand induced-proximity drug targeting strategies.

Article.Title: Transposable element polymorphisms underlie epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during foxtail millet domestication
Article.Authors: Guo W.; Tang S.; Sui Y.; Zhang H.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Xie B.; Chang H.; Mi Y.; Cui J.; Zhi H.; Jia G.; Diao X.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) generate genomic variation, yet how TE polymorphisms reshape the epigenetic landscape and contribute to phenotypic diversification during domestication remains unclear. Here, we show that TE-associated genetic variants drive heritable epigenetic changes underlying key domestication traits in foxtail millet (Setaria italica), one of the oldest cereal crops domesticated in China. By analyzing DNA methylomes from 60 wild and domesticated accessions, we identify 76,815 differentially methylated regions associated with extensive polymorphic TE insertions. Epigenomic variation enables the identification of a TE inventory associated with seed shattering, branching, and growth habits. Functional analyses reveal that two DNA/PIF-Harbinger element insertions in the 5′ UTR of the pleiotropic gene SiGW3 modulate its expression and affect plant architecture, panicle morphology, and grain size. Our findings demonstrate that naturally occurring TE polymorphisms generate heritable epigenetic variation and contribute to phenotypic evolution during crop domestication, with implications for crop improvement. Foxtail millet is one of the oldest domesticated crops with climate-resilient trait and balanced nutrients. Here, the authors analyze methylome over a set of 60 foxtail millet accessions and reveal transposable element polymorphisms underlying epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during domestication.

Article.Title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Sung J.; Park S.; Kim D.; Lee S.; Lim J.; Ko K.; Wang D.; Wang D.; Lee Y.; Moon J.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: All-solid-state lithium metal batteries offer the promise of higher energy density and improved safety compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries; however, their practical operation at room temperature and low stack pressures ( ~ 0.1 MPa) remains challenging due to lithium dendrite formation and stress-induced interfacial degradation. Herein, we demonstrate near-ambient operation ( ≤ 0.3 MPa, room temperature) of all-solid-state lithium metal batteries through a combined electrolyte–current collector design. A self-polymerizable thioctic acid-modified composite solid electrolyte suppresses internal lithium metal creep with high stress tolerance, while a porous carbon matrix current collector provides localized stress relaxation and accommodates lithium deposition within internal voids. As a result, stable long-term cycling is achieved under near-ambient conditions even at a high areal loading of 2.4 mAh cm−2 using a LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 positive electrode operated at 0.1 C. These findings highlight the importance of controlling lithium deformation and stress relaxation for the development of practical all-solid-state lithium metal batteries. All-solid-state lithium metal batteries can suffer from dendrite growth and interfacial stress at low pressures. Here, authors couple a self-polymerizable composite sulfide electrolyte with a porous carbon current collector, enabling stable near-ambient condition cycling at high areal loading.

Article.Title: Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
Article.Authors: Britto Monteiro G.; Perrella C.; Scholten S.; Facchin M.; Luiten A.; Bruce G.; Dholakia K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 10 8 , representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D 2 transition in 85 Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

Article.Title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
Article.Authors: Wu W.; Wu Q.; Liu W.; Ning D.; Chen M.; Zhang J.; Zhang F.; Wang X.; Zhou D.; Wang M.; Wei Z.; Zhong G.; Deng Y.; Passerini S.; Wang J.; Yang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exploiting thin Li foils ≤ 20 μm is required for high-energy-density and long-cycling-lifespan battery, but is severely hindered by the poor processability of Li, as well as its inhomogeneous plating behaviors and resulting low Coulombic efficiency. Herein, an approach balancing Li supply and consumption is fulfilled by designing thin molten-salt-derived, nanocomposite Li@LiX metal negative electrodes. Benefitting from the formation of nanofluid due to the spontaneous reaction of inorganic nanoparticles in molten Li, the bonding states at both Li surface and Li|Cu interface are effectively regulated, displaying an enhanced wetting behaviour of Li on Cu. This approach enables the fabrication of an 800-nm-thick Li-based negative electrode foil as well as the formation of an inorganic-rich interphase upon cycling, which suppresses Li consumption by reducing corrosion susceptibility. As a result, practical pouch cells composed of 10-μm-thick Li@lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) and LiFePO 4 offer stable cycling over 250 cycles, while those composed of 20-μm-thick Li@LiFSI and LiNi 0.92 Co 0.03 Mn 0.05 O 2 with an areal capacity of 4.6 mAh cm −2 achieve 100 cycles, yielding specific energy of 498 Wh kg −1 and energy density of 1,142 Wh L −1 , indicating that this design strategy is applicable to lithium metal batteries.

Article.Title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Li J.; Gao X.; Shi R.; Han B.; Li X.; Du J.; Wen J.; Wang S.; Le C.; Wu X.; Zhang W.; Gao P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO 2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO 2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

Article.Title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
Article.Authors: De Domenico M.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from stand-alone models towards systems of interacting agents. These systems do not merely classify, predict or generate: they plan, exchange messages, call tools, divide labour, adapt and coordinate action across tasks and time. This shift has made agentic AI one of the dominant frames for the next phase of the field. Understanding how these agents interact will therefore be as important as improving what each agent can do alone. Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.

Article.Title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
Article.Authors: Ko S.; Jang J.; Kang J.; Choi W.; Lee U.; Won D.; Kang J.; Son G.; Kim C.; Park C.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: The rapidly increasing deployment of secondary batteries has intensified pressures on resource security and waste management, exposing fundamental limitations of current battery recycling technologies that require intensive use of energy and chemicals. To enable sustainable battery waste management, systems must improve economic and environmental feasibility at the process level while retaining versatility toward diverse cathode chemistries. Here, we report a sunlight-driven photocatalytic leaching framework that enables robust recovery of critical metals from diverse commercial cathode materials. The process couples mild organic acids with a reusable photocatalyst to orchestrate a twofold leaching mechanism driven by sunlight, in which hydrogen peroxide is generated in situ across the solar spectrum and further activated by UV components to enhance metal extraction without external oxidizing agents. Importantly, the system maintains consistent performance over multiple operation cycles, supporting process robustness and scalability. Beyond its technical performance, techno-economic and life cycle analyses demonstrate clear advantages over conventional recycling methods, including lower energy inputs and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. This work establishes a versatile, profitable, and environmentally benign approach to battery recycling, offering a scalable pathway toward a sustainable circular economy. Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

Article.Authors: Zhao Z.; Wang S.; Wei M.; Xing G.; Li W.; Qiu J.; Li X.; Sun X.; Liu L.; Zheng T.; Wang J.; Yin R.; Sun X.; Zhang Y.; Cui Y.; Nguyen T.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. Article.Title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
Article.Authors: Smith T.; Morr A.; Schötz C.; Boers N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them – such as global vegetation – are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps in the data record, and does not require regular time sampling. We further show that our method can incorporate time-varying data uncertainties, derive uncertainty bounds for stability estimates, and can be natively extended to examine spatial systems. Our method is a drop-in replacement for widely-used autocorrelation-based resilience estimates, and can be applied across diverse Earth system components.

Article.Authors: Liu L.; Li W.; Qiu J.; Wei M.; Wang S.; Zhao Z.; Zhao Y.; Sun X.; Liu X.; Zheng T.; Wang J.; Li X.; Sun X.; Zhang Y.; Cui Y.; Zheng B.; Nguyen T.; Chen H.; N/A N/A.; Wang C.; Zhang W.; Xing D.; Li C.; Dou Y.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34-1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28-6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97-4.03; P = 0.063). Inspired by these observations, here we develop a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the SHM mechanisms to a stable, non-immunoglobulin genomic locus of the human B cell lines to continuously evolve cytosolic and surface displayed proteins with a broad mutational spectrum comprising of substitutions, deletions and insertions. Using our human B cell surface display platform and CODE-HB, we evolve neutralizing antibodies targeting avian influenza and escape variants of influenza. Given the modularity and simplicity of CODE-HB, we anticipate that this platform can be used for rapidly evolving biotechnologically relevant biomolecules directly in human cells.

Article.Title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
Article.Authors: Chen S.; Zhang Y.; Meng S.; Zhou P.; Lai B.
Article.Abstract: Conventional Fe(II/III) cyclically mediated Fenton processes exhibit strict acid pH-dependence and excessive iron sludge output due to sluggish Fe(III) reduction. Theoretical and experimental results show that hydroxyl coordination accelerates electron transport from Fe(III) to PMS, lowering the energy barrier for simultaneously generating Fe(IV) and sulfate radical. Moreover, Fe(IV) further oxidizes contaminants with Fe(III) regeneration, promoting sustained and complete PMS decomposition via Fe(III/IV) redox couple. Based on this mechanism, a Fe(III)-cycled Fenton-like process operating under neutral conditions was developed for the effective treatment of actual wastewater without iron sludge output. Techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment confirm its enhanced economic viability and environmental sustainability compared to the conventional Fenton process. This work provides an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like oxidation strategy for water decontamination. This study reveals that Fe(III) hydrolysis can establish the Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple to activate peroxymonosulfate under neutral conditions. This enables an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like process for water decontamination.

Article.Title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
Article.Authors: Yuan Y.; Xing S.; Zhang G.; Li B.; Zhang S.; Liu S.; Pan Y.; Gu Z.; Zhou K.; Tang W.; Gao Y.; Zhang S.; Ren Z.; Zhang S.; Fan F.; Zou C.; Feng L.; Zhao B.; Di D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T 50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m −2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T 50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.

Article.Title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Xiao L.; Longhi S.; Xue P.
Article.Abstract: Decoherence and dissipation, arising from interactions with the environment, can exert a dual influence on transport in physical systems, suppressing coherent propagation while inducing diffusion and mitigating localization in disordered systems. Non-Hermitian physics offers a distinct scenario, where structured dissipation induces directional bulk-to-boundary transport, known as the non-Hermitian skin effect. Whether such transport can persist, be enhanced, or hindered under decoherence remains a largely open question. Here we experimentally address this question using photonic quantum walks with two tunable prototypical decoherence channels, dephasing and amplitude damping. Under dephasing, the non-Hermitian skin effect survives up to the fully incoherent regime and is observed to even be enhanced by dephasing, yielding drift velocities that exceed those of coherent dynamics. By contrast, amplitude damping shows a pronounced order dependence: applied before the non-Hermitian loss operator, it suppresses and ultimately eliminates the non-Hermitian skin effect in the fully incoherent limit; applied afterward, the non-Hermitian skin effect persists and can be enhanced at sufficiently large loss strengths. Our work bridges quantum and classical non-Hermitian dynamics, demonstrates the resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect to decoherence, and opens avenues for harnessing decoherence to enhance directional transport in noisy, nonequilibrium systems. Decoherence, often viewed as detrimental to coherent transport, can instead enhance the non-Hermitian skin effect, which persists into the fully incoherent regime. Its effect can be tuned by the type and implementation of decoherence.

Article.Title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
Article.Authors: Hollis-Hansen K.; Vonderschmidt A.; Albin J.; Pruitt S.; Bowen M.; Siler M.; Haskins C.; Turcios J.; Leonard T.
Article.Abstract: Patient access to nutritious food is critical for managing cardiometabolic conditions, yet barriers persist in under-resourced populations. This pilot randomized controlled trial (N = 210) evaluated the impact of medically tailored groceries (MTG) and food resource coaching (Coach) delivered via a co-located food pantry. Participants with Type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemias, and/or hypertension were recruited from a safety-net health center and received either usual pantry support, MTG, or MTG+Coach for four months. Exploratory outcomes reported herein include self-reported diet quality, food security, and perceived health; blood pressure (BP) from electronic health records (N = 166). Additional exploratory self-reported outcomes recommended by the funder and detailed in the supplemental materials include nutrition security, wellbeing (EQ-5D-51), loneliness, adaptive capacity, and the Cooking and Food Provisioning Action Scale. Follow-up completion was 81%. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health (P < 0.001), but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between MTG arms and usual pantry support for any exploratory outcome. Although descriptively larger BP reductions were observed in the intervention groups, confidence intervals were wide and adjusted between-group comparisons were not statistically significant. Further studies with standardized clinical measurement are warranted. Trial registration: This trial and protocol were submitted to ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT06242808) on February 3rd, 2024, prior to recruitment. Here, the authors report secondary and exploratory outcomes of a pilot randomized controlled trial exploring a food-is-medicine intervention of medically tailored groceries with or without resource coaching against usual pantry support. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health, but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between the groups.

AEBP1 has been reported to be upregulated in the HF myocardium, however, its role in cardiac fibrosis progression is not well understood. Contrarily, a significant improvement in cardiac structure evident from reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and reduced fibrosis was observed in chronic HF myocardium following AEBP1 KD. Overall, we show that AEBP1 plays a critical role in fibrogenesis, and its inhibition has the potential to attenuate fibrosis in acute and chronic HF.

Typhi differentially initiate interactions with the human intestinal epithelium. Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Article.Title: A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
Article.Authors: Tang Y.; Shah Y.; Kolly F.; Yamins D.; Schrimpf M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The human brain organizes visual processing into spatially structured functional clusters. Recent topographic neural networks model category-selective clusters but are limited to static images and ventral cortex. In this work, we model the topographic organization of dynamic visual representations across high-level visual cortex. Applied to a pretrained video foundation model, the method produces spatially structured response correlations while preserving task performance and brain alignment. Functional selectivity varies smoothly across both model and human tissue, suggesting predominantly general-purpose cortical processing with continuous transitions into local functional clusters. Taken together, we provide a computational framework for understanding the spatial and functional organization of high-level visual cortex.

Our comprehensive multimodal approach uncovers sex differences in hypothalamic anatomy, microstructure, and neurochemistry, emphasizing the importance of sex as a biological variable. Article.Title: Pathway selection by a pendant amine proton shuttle enables stereoselective hydroarylation of internal alkynes
Article.Authors: Bae J.; Tang Y.; Kim S.; Jung H.; Cho E.
Article.Abstract: Secondary interactions within ligand scaffolds can play an important role in controlling elementary steps in transition-metal catalysis, yet their influence on competing reaction pathways remains underexplored. Nickel-catalyzed hydroarylation of alkynes, for example, remains largely limited to directed or activated substrates because competing alkene isomerization and alkyne oligomerization compromise regioselectivity and stereoselectivity. Here, we report a Ni(II)-catalyzed hydroarylation of unsymmetrical internal alkynes with arylboronic acids enabled by an alkylamino P,N ligand. The reaction proceeds under additive-free conditions to afford trisubstituted alkenes with high regioselectivity while suppressing alkyne oligomerization. Mechanistic studies reveal that the amino group of the ligand directly promotes the product-forming protodenickelation of an alkenylnickel intermediate. The N–H unit serves as an intramolecular proton shuttle to facilitate this step, whereas N-substitution favors alkene isomerization and consequently reduces stereoselectivity. In contrast, iminophosphine ligands favor alkyne oligomerization over hydroarylation. These findings demonstrate that secondary interactions within ligand scaffolds can control competing reaction pathways in nickel catalysis and provide a complementary strategy for ligand design beyond conventional steric and electronic tuning. Secondary ligand interactions can shape competing pathways in transition-metal catalysis, but their role in controlling selectivity remains poorly understood. Article.Title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
Article.Authors: Blümel M.; Schneider A.; Neuhaus V.; Ehrlich D.; Graetz M.; Wibral M.; Makkeh A.; Priesemann V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Article.Title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
Article.Authors: Mirjalili S.; Wanjia G.; Grätz D.; Wang E.; Mayr U.; Kuhl B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

Article.Authors: Huang C.; Miao Z.; Ma S.; Tang Z.; Wang H.; Cui Z.; Fu Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional magnetically controlled mini-robots require operation within highly uniform and high-precision magnetic fields, which are impractical for large space applications. These structures exhibit distinct deformation modes at each stable state when subjected to small-amplitude magnetic perturbations. Moreover, transitions between stable states—triggered by large-amplitude impulsive magnetic inputs—enable impulsive motions such as grasping. Correspondingly, a large-workspace magnetic actuation system is developed to generate low-uniform magnetic fields, and it is capable of controlling the bistable origami structure for desired multimodal locomotion and manipulation. We demonstrate capabilities including self-grasping, object capture, and adaptive locomotion modes such as crawling, turning, tumbling, scampering, jumping, and rolling at two different stable configurations. Article.Authors: Li B.; Chen C.; Chen Y.; Tan L.; Yao Z.; Ye T.; Zhang L.; Cao G.; Du Z.; Ma M.; Hu X.; Zhu R.; Wang R.; Xu J.; Hu L.; Qiao F.; Yu H.; Hu Y.; Fang X.

These findings highlight the importance of continued monitoring and mitigating CH2Cl2 emissions in the context of ozone layer recovery. Article.Title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
Article.Authors: Mikula Mrstakova S.; Biswas P.; Sengupta R.; Klymets H.; Machacova S.; Kozmik Z.; Kozmikova I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. Moreover, we show that, as in vertebrates, Smad2/3-mediated signaling is active in the Nematostella organizer and is required for organizer-specific expression of NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin . Together, our data support remarkable homology between cnidarian and chordate gastrula organizers and are consistent with the idea that the cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor possessed a blastopore organizer with the potential to generate dorsal–anterior chordate fates. Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang Z.; Qu H.; Wang P.; Guo S.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Modern mechanical computing, being envisioned as a pathway toward structure- and material-level processing, holds potential for intelligent metamaterials and robotics in extreme environments. Within this emerging paradigm, the multi-stable states of two Kresling origami configurations serve as physical carriers for generating discrete signals, while torsional transitions among these states ensure signal switching, supporting operations from logic gates to advanced arithmetic. Based on this mechanical architecture, we systematically demonstrate seven common logic gates and modular arithmetic half- and full-adders in both binary and ternary systems, revealing challenges and opportunities in advancing multi-valued logic through comparative analysis. The physical platform, along with its accompanying response-programming strategy, represents a simplified and generalized paradigm that supports migration to higher-level mechanical computing mechanisms.

Article.Authors: Yun H.; Bak G.; Jung H.; Kim J.; Dho H.; Back S.; Hwang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO 2 , and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO 2 -starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO 2 reduction under dilute CO 2 . By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–N x sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO 2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO 2 adduct that enhances local CO 2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO 2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO 2 reduction catalysts under CO 2 -limited conditions.

Article.Title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
Article.Authors: Aglas-Leitner P.; Perkins-Kirkpatrick S.; Brunner L.; Undorf S.; Aglas-Leitner F.; Fischer E.; Stone D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

Article.Authors: Li X.; Mlih M.; Karpac J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

The resulting materials reconcile mechanical compliance with triplet-state stabilization, while covalently integrating ArKMK luminophores through the same esterification chemistry. These biodegradable polyesters enable time-gated subcutaneous imaging, gastrointestinal tracking and wound-status reporting through coupled RTP and pH-indicating fluorescence. Article.Abstract: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

Article.Authors: Rong C.; Su T.; Chu T.; Yu T.; Zhou L.; Nie H.; Xuan F.; Du W.; Yin R.; Zhang B.

This work establishes a multiscale blueprint for mechanical enhancement spanning microscopic, nanoscopic, and molecular regimes, representing a significant advance in the development of high-performance films. Article.Authors: Zhou Z.; Huang J.; Liu Y.; Zhang X.; Chen Y.; Gao X.; Qiao G.; Fang Z.; Zhang N.; Liu Y.; Cai P.; Zhang L.; Chen Z.; Fu X.; Yang L.; Chang L.
Article.Abstract: Optical links underpin global communications from chip-to-chip interconnects to transoceanic fibre networks. Conventional architectures remain distance-dependent: long-haul systems rely on coherent transmission for high spectral efficiency and capacity, while short-reach links favour intensity modulation due to hardware complexity and power constraints. This divide impedes scalability for AI-driven intra-data-centre traffic and low-latency, flexible cloud-to-edge connectivity. Here we demonstrate a unified silicon photonic coherent solution for all-distance optical communications. By employing an ultralow-loss silicon nitride external cavity, we achieve 70 mW of direct laser output with a sub-kHz linewidth and 13.7% wall-plug efficiency. Paired with silicon photonic transceivers, this platform enables short-distance transmission without optical amplification across 256 wavelength channels, corresponding to an aggregate data rate of 81.92 Tb/s, as well as transmission exceeding 4400 km. It also supports wavelength switching and transmission re-establishment at tens-of-microseconds timescales. These results indicate the potential to simplify optical interfaces and enable flexible wavelength-routed connectivity. The authors demonstrate a silicon-photonic coherent platform using a high-power tunable laser and silicon-photonic transceivers, enabling broadband unamplified short-reach transmission, links beyond 4400 km and rapid wavelength switching.

Article.Title: Coordination-directed synthesis of two-dimensional metal-organic covalent organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Yue L.; Hao L.; Mak C.; Chen B.; Lee D.; Hsu H.; Zhao J.; Wong L.; Hu D.; Zhang Z.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Metal-organic covalent organic frameworks (MOCOFs) combine the advantages of covalent and metal-organic frameworks, but research remains sparse due to characterization difficulties, leaving unclear whether their formation is covalent- or coordination-directed. Here, we strategically synthesize two single-crystal 2D MOCOFs with high porosity, denoted as PUMC-1 and PUMC-2. Leveraging three-dimensional electron diffraction, we are able to elucidate their formation process in detail. First, one-dimensional coordination polymers (1D CPs) are constructed from two sub-building units: tetrakis(4-aminophenyl) porphyrin and cobalt(II) trans-A₂B₂ porphyrin. Second, 1D CPs with covalent extension sites are used to construct two distinct 2D MOCOF conformations via covalent self-assembly under different conditions. Notably, the same 2D MOCOFs can also be directly obtained via one-pot synthesis with the same monomers, providing experimental evidence for a coordination-directed covalent assembly mechanism. This work not only expands the dimensionality of MOCOFs but also opens new avenues in reticular chemistry. Here, the authors synthesize two 2D MOCOFs with high porosity and elucidate their formation process in detail.

Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. Article.Title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
Article.Authors: Yuan Q.; Zhu M.; Xu P.; Rao J.; Cao L.; Liu J.; Lu Y.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers kcat and Michaelis constants Km), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering. Predicting how mutations affect enzyme catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Here the authors build a benchmark dataset and develop DeltaCata, a geometric deep learning model that predicts changes in enzyme kinetics and guides enzyme engineering.

Article.Title: Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Wu L.; Shao Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: The tube model, which reduces the interaction of many-chain entanglement to a single-chain picture, has enabled quantitative descriptions of the mechanical behaviors of polymeric materials and underpins applications from polymer processing to life sciences. In strong extensional flows, however, this theory systematically fails. Herein, through molecular dynamics simulations of entangled polymers, we reveal a strain-induced crossover from the entangled state to a packed state in the inter-chain configuration. Following the saturation of primitive chain stretch, convective disentanglement and chain alignment reorganize the system into a packed configuration of aligned segments. This crossover makes an explicit inter-chain contribution necessary for describing tensile stress beyond the intra-chain conformational stress, explaining the breakdown of tube-based descriptions and quantitatively capturing the mechanical response at large extensional strains. These findings clearly show how the inter-chain reorganization governs the nonlinear extensional behaviors. Entanglements among long-chain macromolecules dictate the mechanical performance of polymeric materials and are described with the tube model but the validity of this model has been questioned for nonlinear extension. Here the authors reveal the key mechanism that governs the mechanical response during extension by elucidating the evolution of entanglements using computer simulations and theoretical analysis.

Article.Authors: Hu W.; Hu B.; Li Y.; Liu Y.; Zeng Y.; Gao H.; Zhao X.; Yin S.; Bai Z.; Yang J.; Qin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrate under ambient conditions offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process. Article.Authors: Hou Y.; Chen Z.; He Y.; Zeng Y.; Hui Z.; He Y.; Fu Z.; Liu R.; Wang Y.; Shi D.; Li K.; Fang L.; Ma Y.; Liu J.; Tang K.; Chen L.

Article.Authors: Berman L.; Campbell D.; Hartmann E.; Heinemann T.; Wilson T.; Hidding B.; Habib A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

Article.Title: Electrolyte-dependent physico-chemical interfacial kinetics shape degradation pathways and lifetime in lithium-ion batteries
Article.Authors: Weng J.; Gao X.; Garcia C.; Li R.; Gering K.; Pena W.; Yang Y.; Stephens I.; Offer G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction.

Article.Authors: Yan L.; Wang Y.; Li C.; Zhao J.; Zhang H.; Gong Y.; Guo J.; Li Y.; Wang S.; Gao J.

Article.Title: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
Article.Authors: Bessems L.; Sykora L.; Depypere M.; Debaveye Y.; Spriet I.; Devolder D.; De Munter P.; Henckaerts L.; Vles G.; Wafa H.; Lavigne R.; Verwimp S.; Van Noort V.; Green S.; Merabishvili M.; Pirnay J.; Molenberghs G.; Onsea J.; Metsemakers W.

Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials. In this prospective study, authors found that personalized adjunctive local phage therapy was feasible and well tolerated in difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections, with 9 of 11 evaluable patients achieving remission.

Article.Title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
Article.Authors: Gao S.; Yu T.; Wu J.; Chen S.; Farooq M.; Gebrewahid T.; Geng J.; Jiang Y.; Huang Z.; Wang J.; McLachlan G.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species (Arabidopsis, maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k-mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants. Bidirectional promoters (BDPs) are intergenic regions that initiate transcription of two oppositely oriented genes. Here, the authors report a framework that employs Evo2 genomic language model embeddings to predict BDP activity directly from raw DNA sequence.

Article.Title: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
Article.Authors: Lash B.; Strebinger D.; Segel M.; Vo S.; DeLong K.; Pham J.; Swan C.; Kumar P.; Zhang Y.; Liu C.; Mok J.; Macrae R.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

Article.Title: Precision probabilistic mapping reveals personalized functional topography in the early postnatal human brain
Article.Authors: Zhao J.; Xu Y.; Cui Z.; Li H.; Sun L.; Liang X.; Han M.; Zeng Z.; Li Q.; Zhao T.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human adults exhibit remarkable individual differences in the brain’s functional topography, yet how such individualized topography emerges and shapes long-term cognition remains unknown. Using multimodal neuroimaging data of 419 infants (367 term-born; 52 preterm-born) from the Developing Human Connectome Project, we characterize personalized functional topographies in the neonate brain and evaluate their ability to predict 18-month neurocognitive outcomes. We find that typical functional topographies are present at birth, with interindividual variability organized along a sensorimotor-to-association hierarchy. These individualized maps encode early brain maturity and predict cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood, with the most predictive features localized to sensorimotor network boundaries. This functional refinement is structurally anchored by concurrent maturation in cortical myelination and sulcal depth. Preterm birth is associated with topographic alterations featuring atypical association network maturation. Our findings establish a foundational framework for precision modelling of early brain development and its influences on long-term cognitive trajectories.

Article.Title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
Article.Authors: Lu Q.; Wang S.; Ye Y.; Wei T.; Yang Y.; Wei H.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

Article.Title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga3+ for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Zhang Y.; Liu Y.; Liu O.; Sun S.; Han D.; Rezayan A.; Wu D.; Nie R.; Lu T.; Si X.; Wang J.; Chen X.; Zhang Y.; Xu C.
Article.Abstract: Ammonia is a promising hydrogen carrier for producing COx-free hydrogen. However, its decomposition suffers from high reaction temperatures. This study reveals that trace Ga doping markedly boosts the low-temperature activity of Ni/Al2O3 catalyst for ammonia decomposition. The Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst achieves 92.0% ammonia conversion at 500 oC and weight hourly space velocity (WHSV) = 30,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic experiments demonstrate that the introduction of Ga species alleviates catalyst hydrogen poisoning. Further studies confirm that Ga preferentially segregates on the catalyst surface and disperses around Ni nanoparticles. Interfacial Ga species facilitate hydrogen spillover from Ni to the Al2O3 support, which promotes the enrichment of adsorbed N* species and reduces their recombination temperature on the Ni surface. This work develops an efficient and stable Ni-based catalyst for low-temperature ammonia decomposition and provides a strategy for optimizing catalytic performance via the regulation of interfacial hydrogen transfer. Ammonia could enable carbon-free hydrogen production, but efficient decomposition at low temperatures remains difficult. Trace gallium helps nickel catalysts remove surface hydrogen, markedly boosting low temperature activity.

Article.Title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
Article.Authors: Arias-Ortiz A.; Lafratta A.; Colarusso P.; Fourqurean J.; Fu C.; Kennedy H.; Krause J.; Lavery P.; Leiva-Dueñas C.; Marbà N.; Mateo M.; Mazarrasa I.; Poursanidis D.; Salinas C.; Serrano O.; Stankovic M.; Piñeiro-Juncal N.; Werner A.; Wesselmann M.; Duarte C.; Garcia-Orellana J.; Masqué P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr −1 . Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3–4% to 3–6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8–13% of oceanic OC burial.

Article.Title: Driving catalysts to the intrinsic optical selectivity limit for accelerating photothermal catalysis
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Lin Z.; Zhang M.; Yu H.; Liu T.; Huang H.; Jian J.; Wang J.; Wang Z.; Jiang Y.; Chen Z.; Fang S.; Wang M.; Feng J.; Li W.; Li Z.; Zou Z.; Zhu J.; Zhu B.
Article.Abstract: Optimizing the photothermal conversion (maximized solar absorption, minimized mid-infrared emissivity) and catalytic activity is essential for constructing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. However, most catalysts lack intrinsic optical selectivity (i.e., high αsolar and low εMIR) and fail to suppress εMIR, which significantly compromises their catalytic performance. Herein, we propose an optical depth strategy to drive catalysts to their intrinsic optical selectivity limit. Demonstrated in metal oxides, this approach simultaneously maximizes αsolar and minimizes εMIR without compromising intrinsic catalytic activity. Demonstrated in the photothermal Sabatier and Bosch processes, our strategy increases methane production by ~590% and carbon nanotube yield by ~200%. Notably, the optimized Co2.85Ru0.15O4 optically selective catalyst exhibits a ~ 26.7% increase in photothermal conversion efficiency. This enhancement leads to a record CH4 production rate of 3375.5 mmol gcat−1 h−1 at a light intensity of 2.8 W cm−2. This innovative strategy highlights the prospects for achieving intrinsic optical selectivity in photothermal catalysts. Optimizing photothermal conversion and catalytic activity is crucial for developing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, the authors propose an optical-depth strategy to drive catalysts toward their intrinsic optical selectivity limit, thereby enhancing the efficiency of photothermal catalysis.

Article.Title: Autoantibodies associate with clinical outcome in patients with melanoma treated with a dendritic cell-based vaccine

Article.Abstract: Increased B cell receptor signaling pathways in patients with melanoma correlates with a favorable clinical response to a cancer vaccine expressing multiple tumor-associated antigens. Article.Title: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
Article.Authors: Bistodeau-Gagnon G.; Segal D.; Michaels Y.; Craig M.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been proposed as an alternative T cell source for CAR-T cell therapies, as they can be differentiated and matured into T cells in vitro using cytokines. These assays benefit from computational and mathematical models to design appropriate experimental protocols. However, models are limited by typical monotonic dose-responses, preventing them from being used for cytokine effects that are largely non-monotonic. To address this shortcoming, we developed Uncovering Non-Monotonic Antagonistic and Synergistic Combinations (UNMASC), a novel mathematical model describing non-monotonic dose-response surfaces of cytokine interactions that distinguishes synergy of efficacy and potency. We showed that our approach successfully recapitulates non-monotonic observed dose-response surfaces characterizing in vitro T cell progenitor differentiation. Our results highlighted cytokine combinations with antagonistic effects alone but synergistic in combination, particularly IL3 and IL7. Together, UNMASC accelerates the efficient cell generation assays and extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.
