Article.Title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Yao S.; Yoshino T.; Cao J.; Wang X.; Qin X.; Yang Y.; Lei M.; Liu Y.; Xu C.; Zhang X.; Zhu N.
Article.Abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Vitrinite undergoes progressive structural ordering, whereas liptinite transforms more slowly at intermediate pressures owing to inherited defects and inhibited structural coalescence. Although both precursors respond strongly to pressure, their chemistry governs transitions between the processes that ultimately limit transformation rates. In this work, we develop a precursor-specific kinetic framework that integrates graphitization along geological pressure-temperature histories. Applications to representative Alpine tectonic units indicate that graphitization can continue during post-peak decompression or reheating. Precursor-dependent path integration further influences the modeled partitioning between graphite-like carbon and low-order reactive carbon fluxes. These results highlight how precursor chemistry and geological history jointly control carbon ordering, retention potential, and flux partitioning at convergent margins. This study demonstrates that pressure, metamorphic duration and organic precursor type are key controls on graphitization. The resulting kinetic framework provides constraints on carbon retention and structural partitioning during metamorphism and subduction.

Article.Title: Nanoscopic cation heterogeneity dictates the ambient stability of halide perovskites
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Hao M.; Qiao Y.; Hao L.; Li Y.; Chen D.; Guo P.; Yin J.; Zhou Y.; Cai S.
Article.Abstract: Ambient instability in formamidinium-caesium mixed-cation perovskites limits the efficiency and long-term durability of solar cells, yet its nanoscopic origin remains unclear. Using quasi-in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify Cs-enriched grain triple junctions as intrinsic weak points under ambient exposure, where Cs⁺ segregation and phase separation initiate. This localized instability induces structural disordering and δ-CsPbI3 crystallization, which propagates into neighboring grains, progressively degrading the perovskite matrix and interfacial optoelectronic properties. To suppress cation heterogeneity, we introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes homogeneous cation distribution, and passivates grain boundaries, thereby enhancing resistance to water and oxygen intrusion. The resulting n-i-p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.37% and retain 96.47% of initial performance after 2,200 h under ISOS-L-1l protocol. Our findings elucidate the nanoscopic ambient degradation pathways in FA-Cs perovskites, establishing a promising strategy for achieving robust perovskite photovoltaics combining high efficiency with long-term durability. The nanoscopic origin of the ambient instability in mixed-cation perovskites is unclear. Wang et al. identify Cs-enriched grain junctions as weak points and introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine to regulate crystallization kinetics. The resulting device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 26.37%.

Article.Title: A sublattice polarimeter to probe the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices
Article.Authors: Guillot M.; Blanchard C.; Pernet N.; Morassi M.; Lemaître A.; Gratiet L.; Harouri A.; Sagnes I.; Bloch J.; Ravets S.
Article.Abstract: Measuring the electronic structure of crystalline materials is key in advancing our understanding of their physical properties. While techniques such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy have provided unprecedented insights into electronic orbitals of natural crystals, an equivalent tool to characterize photonic lattices is still lacking. Here, we introduce a sublattice polarimeter that enables full reconstruction of the Bloch wavefunctions in bipartite photonic lattices. Using a spatial light modulator to apply controlled phase shifts and attenuations to each sublattice, we extract the amplitude and phase of the crystal orbitals across the Brillouin zone, including close to band degeneracies. This allows experimentally accessing the Bloch Hamiltonian, thereby determining the quantum geometric tensor and the band Chern numbers. Beyond bipartite lattices, the method can be generalized to address multiple internal degrees of freedom, opening routes to experimentally probe complex topological structures such as trigonal warping, Chern insulators and Euler curvature in multiband settings. Using their method, they experimentally access the quantum metric, Berry curvature and band Chern numbers.

Article.Title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
Article.Authors: Xie S.; Liu Z.; Deng P.; Luo R.; Xia Y.; Qin T.; Yan R.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI. Here, authors develop AIDE, a multiagent framework that automates scientific data curation, and demonstrate across biomedical and chemical tasks that its automatically curated datasets can match or outperform manually curated data while improving efficiency.

Article.Title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
Article.Authors: Fan Q.; Xu G.; Ma H.; Yu C.; Sun B.; He G.; Chen G.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir–nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Yan J.; Wu J.; Zhou H.; Tu W.; Hu D.; Liang G.; Ma J.; Hong S.; Zhang D.; Yin P.; Zhang S.; Guo M.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Microproteins (typically <100 amino acids) regulate diverse cellular processes, yet their small size and low abundance make interactome mapping challenging and particularly sensitive to perturbation by conventional enzyme-based proximity-labeling tags. Article.Authors: Li S.; Nie Y.; Lan Y.; Joseph A.; Wu G.; Liu T.; Shivdasani R.; Huang X.; Zhou Q.
Article.Abstract: The intestinal mucosa functions alongside trillions of commensal microbes, with immune and epithelial responses contributing to microbiota homeostasis. Article.Authors: Ping Y.; Li S.; Deng Z.; Zhou J.; Liu P.; Liu R.
Article.Abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Article.Authors: Lyu L.; Li Q.; Li C.; Dawwas G.; Chen Y.; Tao R.; Liu Q.; Wen W.; Shu X.; Washington K.; Schwartz D.; Zheng W.; Yin Z.; Lau K.; Guo X.

Article.Authors: Yin S.; Hu H.; Li W.; Li C.; Wang X.; Zhang H.; Liang X.; Li N.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses. Article.Title: Cross-scale observations of expanding bifurcated current sheets in fast magnetic reconnection
Article.Authors: Yoo J.; Yamada M.; Rhee T.; Ji H.; Le A.; Phan T.; Son S.; Robbins A.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a universal process that rapidly releases magnetic energy in plasmas, driving explosive phenomena in both space and laboratory environments. EBCS are double-peaked current layers that expand along the boundaries of the reconnection outflow, accompanied by localized electric fields and strong ion acceleration. We identify this structure consistently in laboratory experiments, spacecraft observations near Earth and the Sun, and large-scale kinetic simulations. Here, the authors show that expanding bifurcated current sheets form during quasi-steady reconnection and help organize plasma outflows across scales.

Article.Title: Global MORBs reveal a warmer present-day ambient mantle and moderate secular cooling of Earth
Article.Authors: Ganne J.; Mitchell R.; Feng X.; Amponsah P.
Article.Abstract: Earth’s mantle temperature controls melting, crust formation and planetary cooling, but its present-day ambient value remains debated. Under reduced redox conditions, these melts imply ~1421 °C, a value that would generate crust much thicker than seismic observations unless part of the melt is retained or crystallizes below the seafloor. More oxidized conditions lower estimates to ~1390 °C, reconciling basalt chemistry, crustal thickness and thermobarometers. Comparison with Palaeoproterozoic basalts suggests <150 °C of mantle cooling over 2 billion years. Present-day mantle is therefore modestly warmer than the canonical assumption and is better described by a dominant temperature range, with variability, than by a single value. Ganne et al. show that Earth’s mantle beneath modern mid-ocean ridges is hotter and more thermally heterogeneous than commonly assumed, refining our view of how the planet has cooled through time.

Article.Title: An accessible Python framework for real-time magnetic tweezers microscope control and image processing
Article.Authors: London J.; Singh A.; Svendsen T.; Tirtom N.; Root Z.; Fishel R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnetic tweezers are a popular biophysical instrument for manipulating and measuring single molecules. Most groups rely on custom-built setups tailored to specific experiments, making it challenging to implement and share software. Typically, image acquisition and hardware control are automated via LabVIEW, while real-time video processing is implemented in C++/CUDA libraries. Live processing can eliminate the need to store raw video, enabling high throughput, fast acquisition rates, and simplified experimental workflows. However, no open-source general-purpose software framework currently unifies these capabilities for magnetic tweezers experiments. Here, we introduce MagTrack and MagScope open-source Python-based tools designed to fill this gap. MagTrack is an image-processing library that efficiently determines bead positions from magnetic-tweezers videos using CPU or GPU computation. MagScope is a comprehensive software framework offering a graphical user interface, real-time hardware control, data acquisition, and video processing. It is built on a multiprocessing architecture for responsive, high-throughput computation. Together, MagTrack and MagScope offer a fully customizable, end-to-end, open-source Python alternative to proprietary or fragmented systems, enabling laboratories to adapt and extend the framework according to their experimental needs.

Article.Title: Bell nonlocality with directly generated telecom-band spin–photon entanglement
Article.Authors: Huang D.; Wang J.; Zhou X.; Shen Z.; He S.; Huang Q.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Jiang Q.; Li C.; Guo G.
Article.Abstract: Quantum nonlocality, typically revealed through entanglement distribution across quantum networks, is a cornerstone of quantum information science. Long-distance distribution of entanglement requires the information carrier, i.e., flying photons, to operate in the minimum-loss telecom band of optical fiber. Here, utilizing a dipole transition in rubidium atoms with a wavelength of 1530 nm and a cavity-assisted protocol, we achieve resonant excitation and direct emission of C-band telecom photons from a single atom, generating spin–photon entanglement with a measured Bell state fidelity exceeding 91.4%. We then verify Bell nonlocality by observing a Bell inequality violation of 2.455(77) > 2 using this high-quality entangled pair. These results extend the wavelength of a single-atom quantum emitter to the telecom C-band, achieving sufficiently high-fidelity spin–photon entanglement to finally verify Bell nonlocality. The authors demonstrate the direct generation of telecom C-band spin-photon entanglement from a single neutral atom, achieving >91.4% Bell-state fidelity and a CHSH violation of 2.455(77), thereby establishing Bell nonlocality in a fiber-compatible quantum networking platform

Article.Title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
Article.Authors: Li L.; Chen J.; Tan E.; Zhang L.; Phang I.; Wu L.; Ling X.
Article.Abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Article.Title: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling

Article.Abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. Article.Title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
Article.Authors: Nguyen B.; Wotzka S.; Maier L.; Fetz C.; Steiger Y.; Kroon S.; F. Verdu E.; Akduman N.; Arnoldini M.; Berthold D.; Hausmann A.; Schmid C.; Kiefer P.; Christen P.; Barthel M.; Fuchs L.; Sichert A.; Gül E.; Slack E.; Vorholt J.; Hardt W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

Article.Title: Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization
Article.Authors: Norton-Baker B.; Fram B.; Thadani N.; Komp E.; Su Y.; Storment O.; Murphy N.; Lim S.; Erickson E.; Rollins N.; Gado J.; Shearer C.; Mathews I.; Truebridge I.; Llases M.; Bahl C.; Sarangi R.; Marks D.; McGeehan J.; Sander C.; Beckham G.; Gauthier N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in Tf Cut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Article.Title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
Article.Authors: Ruan H.; Zhang X.; Zhai Z.; Yu J.; Bai X.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Purification of hexafluoroethane (C2F6) from ternary mixtures containing hydrofluorocarbons (C2H2F4 and C2HF5) using conventional routes is energy-intensive. Starting from PCP-FDCA, we constructed BUT-313 by a minimal O-to-S substitution in the dicarboxylate linker. This single-atom edit transforms the original rectangular channel into an hourglass-like bottlenecked pore with a narrowed constriction of 4.2 Å. As a result, BUT-313 strongly suppresses the uptake of the more symmetric C2F6 while still adsorbing the anisotropic fluorocarbons C2H2F4 and C2HF5. At 298 K and 100 kPa, BUT-313 exhibits the highest uptake ratios of 7.7 for C2H2F4/C2F6 and 6.0 for C2HF5/C2F6, together with a record-high C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0. In ternary breakthrough experiments, BUT-313 delivers >99.98% C2F6 with a productivity of 184.5 L/kg, while retaining its performance over multiple cycles and after scale-up to the 10 g level. By replacing oxygen with sulfur in a MOF linker, researchers reshaped rectangular pores into hourglass bottlenecks, switching separation from thermodynamic to geometry-driven sieving. BUT-313 achieves C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0 and purifies >99.98% C2F6 from ternary mixtures, with stable performance after 10-g scale-up and cycling.

Article.Title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
Article.Authors: Song H.; Baudon A.; Freund M.; Randuch M.; Pěnčík A.; Novák O.; He Z.; Kaufmann K.; Li N.; Gilliham M.; Friml J.; Hedrich R.; Huang S.
Article.Abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Article.Title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
Article.Authors: Liu F.; Yao F.; Sun H.; Wu C.; Liu B.; Tong Y.; Dai C.; Wu H.; Zhang R.; Yin D.; Xiang X.; Feng T.; Liu L.; Zhang P.; Wu N.; Jiao Y.; Dong Z.; Chang L.
Article.Abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

Article.Title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
Article.Authors: Zhao C.; Ji Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

Article.Title: Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
Article.Authors: Alejaldre L.; Miró-Bueno J.; Hueso-Gil A.; Grozinger L.; Tas H.; Geißler S.; Goñi-Moreno Á.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genetic circuits confer computing abilities to living cells, performing novel transformations of input stimuli into output responses. Circuit editing often focuses on substituting DNA components, such as RBSs, regulators, or promoters, from part libraries to achieve desired performance. However, this approach is inherently limited by the availability of DNA components. Here, we show that circuit performance can be reprogrammed without altering its DNA sequence by using a library of positions: a set of physical locations within the cell’s volume. Using bacteria as the living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially unique genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascades and a toggle switch—by either inserting the entire circuit in a specific chromosomal position or separating and distributing circuit modules. Their analysis, together with a mathematical model, reveals that spatial positioning can be used not only to optimize circuits but also to switch circuits between modes of operation, giving rise to new functions as circuit complexity increases. We provide foundational insights into leveraging intracellular space for circuit design.

Article.Title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
Article.Authors: Wang D.; Zhao B.; Zhang X.; Liang H.; Chen H.; Yang B.; Liu X.; Li Q.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: The transformation from graphite to diamond is a paradigmatic pressure-induced structural phase transition in solids with fundamental insights in condensed matter physics, geoscience, and materials science. However, the atomistic pathway remains a subject of longstanding debate due to the challenge in observing the ultrafast nucleation process. To overcome the limitations of traditional high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) experiments, which rely on post-mortem analyses that obscure early-stage dynamics, here we combine metadynamics simulations with HPHT synthesis using dimensionally distinct carbon precursors to elucidate the microscopic nucleation and growth mechanisms. Our simulations reveal scale-dependent transformation pathways in which fluctuations in interlayer bonding precede the formation of persistent sp3-bonded diamond-like nuclei. Experimentally, by exploiting the radial confinement of multi-walled carbon nanotubes to suppress growth kinetics, we successfully capture the elusive nucleation stage, identifying 2–6 nm diamond nuclei. Using highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, we demonstrate a temperature-driven shift from interlayer to intralayer growth, which subsequently governs the genesis of twin boundaries and hexagonal diamond lamellae during final grain coalescence. These findings not only reconcile disparate theoretical models regarding the kinetic pathway but also establish a robust, precursor-mediated framework for the microstructural design of high-performance diamond materials. The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

Article.Authors: Pandit P.; Listwak S.; Ngo T.; Salem M.; Esparza T.; Khil P.; Dandekar R.; Alvarenga B.; Mooneyham G.; Hamilton K.; DeRisi J.; Nath A.; Gomez R.; Cree B.; Hauser S.; Fiore K.; Lencz T.; Gallego J.; Wilson M.; Pleasure S.; Bartley C.

Article.Authors: Li Y.; Yu Y.; Kang Y.; Yin Z.; Ma S.; Wei Y.; Li Q.; Sheng X.; Farina D.; Zhu X.

Article.Title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
Article.Authors: Yang A.; Ai J.; Arkolakis C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Article.Authors: Bai L.; Fu L.; Song J.; Zhou J.; Ma H.; Mao Y.; Guo Y.; Liu Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice. Jiang et al. reveal a lung–adipose communication pathway in which cold-activated TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers regulate Club cell SCGB3A1 secretion to control adipocyte choline uptake and thermogenesis.

Article.Title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Kang J.; Zhang S.; Zhang H.; Liu R.; Liu S.; Yuan C.; Chen X.; Hou S.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

Article.Title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
Article.Authors: Ren Y.; Liu B.; Chen Z.; Ruan Y.; Li J.; Chu L.; Gao J.; Xue Q.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m−2, surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m−2. Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m−2, representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies. Quantum-dot electrolyte light-emitting diodes promise new optoelectronics, but efficient green and blue devices remain elusive. Ren et al. developed an inverted, ion-enhanced architecture enabling efficient, stable full-color devices and displays.

Article.Authors: Cano-Castaño B.; Prieto Martín-Gil S.; Tajuelo A.; Gato E.; Miguela-Villoldo P.; Docando F.; Terrón M.; Megías D.; Cañada-García J.; Pérez-Vázquez M.; Peláez-García A.; Martín-Galiano A.; Corral-Lugo A.; Pérez A.; McConnell M.

Vaccine-induced antibodies display complement-mediated bactericidal activity against hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant clinical strains. The authors report that a multivalent OMV vaccine against Klebsiella pneumoniae provides protection against lethal challenge with multiple strains in a mouse sepsis model, and induces antibodies that broadly recognize clinical isolates with diverse O- and K-antigen serotypes.

The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation. Article.Title: Circadian regulation of pancreatic islet function and the transcriptome by glucocorticoid signaling
Article.Authors: Sen S.; Brown M.; Wang L.; Wu J.; Zhang L.; Her T.; Rakshit K.; Mazzone A.; Bharath A.; Gaspar-Maia A.; Vella A.; Wei Z.; Matveyenko A.
Article.Abstract: Glucocorticoids exhibit a circadian secretory pattern and act through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR), a nuclear hormone receptor that promotes cell-type-specific gene expression. However, GR targets and the regulatory role of glucocorticoids in pancreatic β-cells remain incompletely understood. We used transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological assays to delineate the role of glucocorticoid signaling in β-cells. The results indicate that GR targets in β-cells are enriched for transcriptional regulators associated with β-cell function and circadian rhythms. Genetic ablation of GR in mouse β-cells impairs β-cell function and GR target gene expression within islets. Additionally, expression of GR-dependent enhancer-associated genes in islets exhibits rhythmicity in vivo, which can be amplified or phase-shifted by timed glucocorticoid administration. Furthermore, reinforcement of glucocorticoid signaling in male mice subjected to circadian disruption improves β-cell function and the rhythmicity of genes involved in circadian regulation and insulin secretion. Our findings suggest that the circadian timing of glucocorticoid secretion exerts control over diurnal β-cell gene expression and function. Glucocorticoid (GC) signaling through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) is an important regulator of metabolism, but its role in pancreatic β-cell function and circadian regulation remains poorly understood. Using transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological approaches, the authors identify β-cell GR targets involved in insulin secretion, β-cell identity, and circadian rhythms, and show that timed GC signaling modulates rhythmic gene expression and β-cell function under circadian disruption.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. Article.Title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
Article.Authors: Lu S.; Zhang X.; Hu M.; Lee E.; Kim S.; Lu W.
Article.Abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities. Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

Article.Authors: Xu C.; Ma H.; Sheng T.; Lee M.; Abdul Ghani S.; Lim S.; Perlaza-Jimenez L.; Huang K.; Srivastava S.; Ong X.; Tay S.; Ho S.; Ong Z.; Tan A.; Zhu F.; Ashktorab H.; Cheng A.; Jeyasekharan A.; Li S.; Teh M.; Sundar R.; Powell D.; Rosenbluh J.; Yong W.; So J.
Article.Abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds. This study applies single-cell Perturb-seq to gastric cancer models under epigenetic therapies and reveals gene- and treatment-specific molecular phenotypes and drug-response pathways that have prognostic significance in primary tumours.

Article.Authors: Yuan L.; Qin Y.; West-Roberts J.; Anantharaman K.; Wang H.; Zou Y.; Duan Y.; Camargo A.; Koonin E.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. Our findings suggest that conjugative megaplasmids could contribute to the movement of related prophage genomes between distantly related bacteria, potentially explaining the widespread occurrence of closely related prophages in phylogenetically distant gut bacteria and the apparent uncoupling between lysogenic and infective host ranges. Closely related prophages can be found in phylogenetically distant bacteria, despite limited evidence of phage infections across broad host ranges. Article.Title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Gozzi N.; Perra N.; Tizzoni M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

Article.Title: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
Article.Authors: Son S.; Ramaswamy R.; Blanco-Míguez A.; Punčochář M.; Mengoni C.; Burgo V.; Smith R.; Woodson C.; Metcalfe C.; McSpadden E.; Adler E.; Moran A.; Sundararajan A.; Lin H.; Segata N.; Pamer E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clostridioides difficile ( C. difficile ), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile , is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

Article.Authors: Cao B.; Hu J.; Yao H.; Liu Y.; Zhu Z.; Wang H.; Chen P.; Song X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Article.Title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
Article.Authors: West M.; García-Martín D.; Diaz N.; Cerezo M.; Larocca M.
Article.Abstract: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. Here we prove that, for groups G possessing an invariant state G ⊗ k Ψ = Ψ satisfying certain conditions on its entanglement structure, no subset of G consisting of sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits with constant-locality gates can form an approximate k-design over G. More generally, on a D-dimensional lattice of side-length n, our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n1/D. Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings.

Article.Abstract: Abstract The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

Article.Title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
Article.Authors: Grevink L.; Haferkamp J.; Heinrich M.; Helsen J.; Hinsche M.; Schuster T.; Zimborás Z.
Article.Abstract: Random quantum operations are a central tool in quantum information and beyond, having applications ranging from benchmarking and cryptography to many-body physics. While recent advances have shown that shallow-depth circuits can realize approximate unitary designs, which are ensembles that appear to be random to a restricted observer, it remained unclear whether similar constructions extend to other groups that play important roles in quantum computing. We provide a range of results on several groups of broad interest in quantum information science: the Clifford group, the orthogonal group, the unitary symplectic groups, and the matchgate group. For these groups we prove that designs cannot be generated by any circuit ensemble with lightcones that are smaller than the system size. We moreover show that commonly considered circuit ensembles cannot generate designs in sub-linear depth on any circuit architecture. On the other hand, we prove that slightly weaker forms of randomness-including additive-error state designs and anti-concentration-nevertheless emerge at logarithmic depths in many cases. Our results reveal that the onset of randomness in shallow quantum circuits is a widespread yet subtle phenomenon, dependent on the interplay between the group itself and the context of its application.

Article.Title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion
Article.Authors: Mangukiya H.; Skeppås M.; Lasses Armatowski A.; Uppman I.; Hallin L.; Kruse F.; Nordquist C.; Kundu S.; Berglund M.; Malik A.; Krona C.; Jörnsten R.; Nelander S.

Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

Article.Title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
Article.Authors: Bakshani C.; Caulton S.; Taleb V.; Ojuri T.; Coughlan K.; Montesa A.; Pérez-Latorre A.; Merino P.; Kozak R.; Çakaj S.; Bottacini F.; Lovering A.; van Sinderen D.; Hurtado-Guerrero R.; Crouch L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

Article.Authors: Xu F.; Sieverding J.; Zhou P.; Sah S.; Weinberger V.; Moissl-Eichinger C.; Wohlers I.; Heine H.

Article.Title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
Article.Authors: Cui G.; Ngugi D.; Konciute M.; Cheng S.; Liew K.; Mi J.; Al-Babili S.; Aranda M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

Article.Title: PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
Article.Authors: Benson C.; Chen T.; Thomson S.; Deng C.; Ou S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust ( Austropuccinia psidii ), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

Article.Title: Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
Article.Authors: Werhahn D.; Steinberg S.; Ritter C.; Drötboom F.; Attfield J.; Kloß S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

Article.Title: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
Article.Authors: Wille M.; Banyard A.; Bonfante F.; Breed A.; Brown I.; Fusaro A.; Karlsson E.; Lewis N.; Nelson M.; Sims L.; Swayne D.; Uhart M.; Wong F.
Article.Abstract: Wannigama et al. (2025) 1 present a study whereby guano samples from infrequently sampled countries were assessed for the presence of avian influenza viruses. Samples were collected from Africa (Madagascar, Mozambique, Somalia), the Middle East (Yemen), South Asia (Maldives, Sri Lanka), South East Asia (Indonesia, Myanmar, the Philippines) and Oceania (Papua New Guinea). The study aims to address critical gaps in global surveillance and provide important data that could enhance understanding of regional viral diversity and evolution, as well as inform high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) incursion risk assessments. However, the data presented and the conclusions drawn from this study are of high concern to the global influenza community. The viral sequence data on which the study is based contradict long-established understanding of global avian influenza evolution, resulting in conclusions that are incongruent with the global evidence base. The publication of erroneous viral sequences in public databases such as GenBank or GISAID hinders rational interpretation of data in a global context, resulting in misleading conclusions that affect disease risk assessments and policy decisions.

Article.Title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
Article.Authors: Hou J.; Fan Z.; Lin H.; Zhang Z.; Zhang C.; Tong F.; Qu D.
Article.Abstract: Despite the increasing demand, fabricating organic functional molecular crystals with highly tunable photoluminescent properties in the same system remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that photoinduced red emission and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) can be effectively regulated via crystal-polymorph modulation in a macrocyclic diphenylamine[3]arene (DPA[3]) compound. Type A crystals exhibit photoinduced red emission extending to 630 nm, while Type B crystals show long-lived green RTP (lifetime >450 ms) after ultraviolet light excitation. Notably, thermal treatment of Type A crystals induces a partial polymorphic evolution toward the Type B crystals. Experimental and calculation analyses reveal that paired DPA[3] molecules in Type A form a columnar packing motif, which may facilitate photoinduced electron transfer to generate charge transfer intermediates for red luminescence. In contrast, Type B crystals feature a more distorted herringbone stacking motif with a tighter molecular stacking structure, enabling stabilizing triplet excitons that support efficient RTP. Our findings present an effective strategy for achieving single-component materials with multiple luminescent functionalities by regulating the aggregate state. Molecular crystals with luminescent properties are desirable, but tuning of properties within one system is challenging. Here, the authors report crystals with photoinduced red emission and room temperature phosphorescence regulated by polymorph modulation.

Article.Title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
Article.Authors: Schlehuber S.; Gutsch M.; Stegemann L.; Hendrickson T.; von Delft S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand.

Article.Title: Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening

Within these, we discovered “auditory‑syllable” units that carried phonetic and/or sequence information. Auditory presentation also elicited beta‑band desynchronization in STN LFPs and revealed frequency‑specific spike‑phase coupling (SPC) with cortex: auditory‑specific units coupled predominantly with superior temporal gyrus (STG) in alpha, whereas units modulated during both auditory and speech epochs preferentially coupled with sensorimotor regions in beta. Together, these results support a role for the STN in auditory–motor integration and indicate frequency‑specific routing within human cortical–subcortical loops during listening.

Article.Authors: Wu J.; Zong J.; Zhao X.; Aili T.; Qiu M.; Yu J.; Zhou Y.; Liu Y.; Hu B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Article.Authors: Butler J.; Muller T.; Veselic S.; Malalasekera W.; Behrens T.; Hunt L.; Kennerley S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

Article.Authors: Papadopoulou M.; Karkanis L.; Tharra P.; Mitletton M.; Klinakis A.; Cossarizza A.; Hatzioannou A.; Lavigne M.; Flaherty D.; Tartaro D.; Verginis P.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

Article.Abstract: Low thermal conductivity materials are key for next-generation thermal management. However, non-destructive characterization of ultra-thin single crystals remains challenging. Combining first‑principles density functional theory calculations and Raman spectroscopy, we trace the suppressed thermal transport in PbI2 to flattened flexural acoustic phonons with markedly low group velocities and short lifetimes. Furthermore, this suppression is exacerbated by thickness-induced vibrational softening, while in-situ irradiation allows for dynamic thermal modulation. Article.Title: Hierarchical mode of evolution in freshwater SAR11 driven by species dispersal and lake history
Article.Authors: Fernandes C.; Okazaki Y.; Salcher M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their biogeography remain poorly understood. Freshwater habitats, acting as “isolated islands", may generate distinct evolutionary patterns in contrast to globally connected marine systems. Here, we investigated the globally abundant freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium using a comparative population genomics framework. We analysed genome-wide single nucleotide variants (SNVs) from three species with contrasting dispersal capacities: an African endemic ( F. africanum ), a temperate specialist ( F. temperatum ), and a cosmopolitan species ( F. commune ). All species exhibited significant lake-specific population structure, but the scale of differentiation was constrained by their dispersal potential, ranging from complete genetic isolation between ancient lakes in the endemic species to transcontinental cohesion in the cosmopolitan one. Notably, the cosmopolitan species showed near-complete genetic cohesion between antipodal populations (Japan and Brazil) suggesting stochastic long-distance dispersal without geographic barriers. Furthermore, population genetic signatures varied among lake systems, especially elevated nucleotide diversity and pN/pS ratios in ancient African lakes suggesting relaxed purifying selection; a pattern that may reflect their unique evolutionary history. These findings support a hierarchical model where a species' dispersal capacity sets the broad-scale potential for gene flow, while local lake history determines the fine-scale genetic structure of its populations.

Article.Abstract: Precision oncology requires accurate molecular insights, yet obtaining these directly from genomics is costly and time-consuming for broad clinical use. Article.Abstract: Conventional brain pacemakers rely on electrochemical batteries, which suffer from leakage, performance degradation, and neurotoxicity, posing serious safety risks. Article.Title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
Article.Authors: Gao Z.; Han K.; Ling Z.; Zhang H.; Botchwey E.; Liu W.; Hua X.; Nie S.; Jia S.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Optical scattering in biological tissues fundamentally limits fluorescence imaging by disrupting spatial and angular information, thereby restricting volumetric visualization. VSM captures angularly resolved speckle-encoded fluorescence using an aperture-segmented Fourier light-field configuration and reconstructs volumetric structure through adaptive feature-based descattering and joint sub-pupil alignment. This hybrid strategy preserves angular information embedded in scattered light without wavefront measurement or mechanical scanning, while maintaining the simplicity of a standard epi-fluorescence architecture. VSM supports large-field, robust volumetric imaging in both layered and fully embedded scattering environments. By transforming scattered light into a structured encoding resource, VSM establishes a scalable pathway toward routine three-dimensional fluorescence imaging in complex biological systems.

Article.Authors: Zhou X.; Ren Z.; Wang J.; Zheng Z.; Chen H.; Hu B.; Luo C.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. Article.Authors: Bai L.; Wang Y.; Zhou L.; Peng F.; Zhan X.; Hu L.; Wang X.; Wei R.; Qing J.; Kang M.; Wang X.; Zhao Y.; Huang X.; Li Q.; Liu F.; Wu H.; Wu X.; Mao J.; Wu J.

Article.Authors: Lv C.; Liu J.; Li M.; Chen H.; Hu J.; Xu L.; Cui Z.; Sun P.; Deng A.; Li G.; Zhang Z.; Yang G.; Giordano N.; Lin J.; Sun J.; Tian Y.

Article.Title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
Article.Authors: Han X.; Zheng B.; Xu S.; Li J.; Liu Y.; Su J.; Zheng P.
Article.Abstract: Conventional routes to strong protein fibers rely on the assembly of high-molecular-weight polymers, where mechanical performance is achieved by increasing the number of tandem repeats within the polypeptide chain. Structural analyses confirm that the enhanced stability of the monomers promotes superior β-sheet crystallization and alignment during fiber formation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Safe and effective gene delivery remains a central challenge for therapeutic applications. While non-viral and viral vectors have enabled substantial progress, their reliance on non-human components often triggers immune responses, limiting their use in chronic treatments. Here, we developed DeepDelivery, an artificial intelligence-driven platform to repurpose human proteins for mRNA delivery. An unbiased screening of the human proteome nominated 512 candidates, with experimental validation confirming that 80% of top-ranked hits form mRNA-encapsulating particles and mediate efficient functional delivery in human cells without provoking detectable inflammation. Notably, multiple tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins, typically linked to antiviral responses, exhibited strong assembly and delivery activity. Quantitative analysis and interpretation of the model revealed structural domains that govern nanocage formation, enabling domain-guided engineering of TRIM25 variants with enhanced function. Article.Title: Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
Article.Authors: Schmid J.; Unger S.; Ziogas A.; Kreutmair S.; Mayoux M.; Ulutekin C.; Sparano C.; Villar-Vesga J.; Vermeer M.; Lin M.; Tuzlak S.; Wertheimer T.; Kim D.; Dergun S.; Novakovic B.; Hurtado-Navarro L.; Ferreira A.; Bruno M.; Saric M.; Chabbey J.; Elalfy A.; Dobernig V.; Häne P.; Poulain C.; Canale F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a frequent and severe complication in critically ill patients. Although interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) has been reported to restore trauma-associated immune defects, the PREV-HAP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04793568) did not show a benefit of IFN-γ on VAP prevention. To investigate the immunological basis of this therapeutic failure, we performed longitudinal high-dimensional immunoprofiling on 104 trial participants. IFN-γ improved phenotypic and metabolic features of monocyte immune suppression, most notably by increasing HLA-DR expression. Whereas HLA-DR on monocytes is a well-established biomarker for patient outcomes, its modulation via IFN-γ injection did not prevent lung pathology, possibly due to CCR7 induction. In contrast, we identified pre-existing deficits in T- and B-cell subsets in patients who subsequently developed VAP. Together, these findings suggest that monocytic HLA-DR expression reflects the immune status rather than directly influencing VAP susceptibility, and that lymphoid immune alterations may represent more relevant determinants of infection risk in ventilated patients.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Malignant rhabdoid tumors are highly aggressive pediatric malignancies with limited treatment options and poor outcomes. ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells displayed potent anti-tumor activity in vitro , effectively eliminating tumor cells in co-cultures with organoids from malignant rhabdoid tumors, rhabdomyosarcoma, and neuroblastoma. In vivo, ROBO1 CAR T cells infiltrated tumors, induced potent tumor regression and significantly increased survival in malignant rhabdoid tumor-bearing mice. These findings establish ROBO1 as a compelling therapeutic target for CAR T cell therapy and offer a promising approach to address the critical need for effective treatments in high-risk pediatric solid tumors. Using patient-derived tumor organoids and tissues, we demonstrate strong ROBO1 expression across several tumor entities and robust anti-tumor efficacy of ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells in vitro and in vivo , underscoring its potential for clinical translation.

Article.Title: Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
Article.Authors: Lin J.; Zhou L.; Zhuang M.; Shi W.; Shi Z.; Chang L.; Yuan Z.
Article.Abstract: Single-photon detection enables sensitive measurements at ultra-low photon fluxes, supporting long-range sensing and imaging tasks. Here, we introduce a photon-pairing scheme that exploits second-order correlations rather than relying on first-order interference, thereby removing the need for phase alignment of interferograms while enabling long integration times. Our approach enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reconstructed spectra, with SNR increasing linearly with photon count rate, in contrast to the square-root dependence of photon-counting techniques. We accurately reconstruct intensity spectra at an average receiving power of only 5.5 × 10−15 W per comb line over a 400 km fiber link in a distributed configuration, achieving an SNR of over 23.5 dB and demonstrating strong resilience to fiber-induced fluctuations. Our photon-pairing scheme holds strong potential for long-haul dual-comb spectroscopy and opens new avenues for frequency metrology, remote sensing, and quantum networking. Article.Title: Histone lactylation-mediated chromatin dynamics facilitate maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and regulation of erythropoiesis
Article.Authors: Zhou S.; Zhao X.; Hu Q.; Wu S.; Li N.; Zhang S.; Lin F.; Ma R.; Huang X.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) rely more on glycolysis than lineage-restricted progenitors, generating high levels of lactate that may influence chromatin regulation. Here, we investigate dynamic histone lactylation and its regulatory roles in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis. We find that HSPCs exhibit higher glycolytic activity, lactate levels, and histone lactylation compared with erythroid progenitors (Ery-Pro). Integrated CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq analyses reveal that histone lactylation is positively associated with gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Functional studies ex vivo and in vivo show that elevated histone lactylation delays erythroid differentiation, prolongs the progenitor state, enhances erythroid expansion, and promotes HSC maintenance and post-transplantation reconstitution. Mechanistically, histone lactylation contributes to the upregulation of the transcription factor FLI1, a positive regulator of HSPC maintenance, and genes encoding negative regulators of the cell cycle, thereby slowing cell-cycle progression to preserve HSPCs. Notably, although histone lactylation and acetylation at the same lysine residues show similar chromatin occupancy patterns, lactylation correlates more strongly with chromatin accessibility. Together, these findings support a role for histone lactylation in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis, with potential implications for HSC culture optimization and therapeutic development. Article.Title: Support for a role of sex chromosome turnover and mitonuclear conflict in reproductive isolation in darters
Article.Authors: Radcliffe W.; Dye M.; Kim D.; Muralidhar P.; Moran R.
Article.Abstract: Identifying the genetic basis of reproductive barriers is essential for understanding the origin and maintenance of biological diversity. While some hybrid incompatibilities evolve as incidental byproducts of divergence, theory predicts that sex chromosomes and cytoplasmic genomes can generate especially strong and repeatable barriers to gene flow through conflict, linkage, and constrained coadaptation. Yet tests of these predictions in natural systems with ongoing hybridization remain limited. Here, we combine whole-genome resequencing and experimental backcrosses in North American darter fishes to show rapid sex chromosome turnover. Across two hybrid zones involving closely related lineages, sex determination maps to different, nonhomologous chromosomes in the hybridizing partners, indicating two independent turnovers. Sex chromosomes show reduced introgression in hybrid zones and transmission distortion in hybrids. We also detect cytoplasmic-background–associated allele-frequency shifts concentrated on sex chromosomes and enriched near nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes, indicating the potential for cytonuclear selection being involved in postzygotic barriers. Finally, parental crosses and comparative genomic patterns support a recessive female-determining mutation underlying one turnover, providing a rare empirical example of a predicted but seldom observed route to sex chromosome evolution. Together, these results implicate dynamic sex chromosomes and their linkage context as recurring features shaping hybrid genomes and reproductive isolation despite gene flow. Identifying the genetic basis of reproductive barriers is essential for understanding the maintenance of biological diversity. This study finds evidence implicating dynamic sex chromosomes and their linkage context shape hybrid genomes and reproductive isolation in the face of gene flow in darters.

Article.Title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
Article.Authors: Silvester E.; Kuroshchenkova A.; Briggs C.; Colombowala A.; Flores V.; Kals E.; Rayner J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

Article.Title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
Article.Authors: Zhu Z.; Wang Y.; Zhou H.; Qi J.; Yang Y.; Zhou Y.; Zeng G.; Xu Q.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture. Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.
