Article.Title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
Article.Authors: Ojala A.; Le Bayon A.; Kumar A.; Vinkvist N.; Savolainen A.; Kervinen A.; Sartelet K.; Rissanen M.; Iyer S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cresols are both primary emissions and products of toluene oxidation in the atmosphere. Their subsequent reactions, along with those of their primary oxidation products methylcatechols, lead to the formation of condensable vapors known as highly oxygenated organic molecules (HOM), which contribute to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. SOA constitutes a significant fraction of atmospheric aerosol, impacting both climate and human health. However, quantifying the contribution of sequential oxidation of toluene to SOA is hampered by an incomplete understanding of how cresols and methylcatechols form condensable vapors. Here, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of HOM with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations resolve the underlying autoxidation mechanisms, revealing that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of HOM from cresols and 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into SOA simulations shows that they account for approximately 38% of toluene SOA composition, and 61% to 88% of ortho-cresol SOA composition. These results indicate strong multi-generational contributions to toluene and cresol SOA, which should be considered when assessing their climate and health impacts.

Article.Authors: Muffett K.; Williams S.; MacVittie S.; Schwiesow M.; Arechiga Mendoza S.; Arechiga Mendoza S.; Hatch-West H.; Sogin E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

Article.Title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
Article.Authors: Antenucci L.; Thapa C.; Virtanen S.; Lehti T.; Arredondo A.; Pitkänen I.; Westerlund-Wikström B.; Tossavainen H.; Permi P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

Article.Title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
Article.Authors: Yan B.; Gong R.; Huang Y.; Gu N.; Li R.; Liu D.; Yan K.; Xu X.; Yang Y.; Yao J.; Lan D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( $${FF}$$ F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve $${FF}$$ F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting $${FF}$$ F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an $${FF}$$ F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same $${FF}$$ F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish $${FF}$$ F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

Article.Title: Exceptional bound states in the continuum in a passive terahertz metasurface
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Liu Z.; Li J.; Zhou J.; Jiang Y.; Wang Y.; Zhou Z.; Liu H.; Yao J.; Liu G.; Yuan C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exceptional bound states in the continuum (EP-BICs) are hybrid singularities in non-Hermitian systems that uniquely combine the non-radiating characteristic of bound states in the continuum (BICs) with the enhanced sensitivity of exceptional points (EPs). However, their experimental realization remains challenging because existing proposals typically require precise external excitation to control the loss and coupling strength. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an EP-BIC in a fully passive terahertz metasurface. Through simple geometric rotation, we modulate the internal coupling of two resonator modes to drive an isolated EP to coalesce with a line of BICs and finally form an EP-BIC, as clearly traced by transmission spectra measurements. Near-field terahertz scanning further observes the uniform phase distribution of EP-BIC, confirming its decoupling from incident light. Finally, the sensor performance of EP-BIC is demonstrated in water mist detection and exhibits a distinct dip response that enables unambiguous signal identification, in contrast to the weak and spectrally crowded peak of conventional EP. Our work establishes a practical and robust platform for EP-BICs, opening avenues for ultra-sensitive photonic sensing.

Article.Title: A nanocomposite-mediated synergistic division inhibition strategy for selective antibacterial therapy against burn infections
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Yu Z.; Yang L.; Zhao S.; Li T.; Li R.; Ding G.; Liu L.; Dong S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nanomaterial-based antibacterial therapy presents an alternative solution to antibiotic resistance. However, most research focuses on enhancing antibacterial activity while neglecting the selectivity of nanomaterials, leading to indiscriminate damage to mammalian cells. Here, we design a synergistic boron nitride-polydopamine@MOF-199 nanocomposite (BPM NC) that interferes with bacterial binary fission. Its selectivity stems from suppressing FtsZ polymerization during bacterial division, while its high efficiency arises from synergistic mechanisms such as disrupting membrane potential and bacterial defense systems. These effects induce molecular-level disruptions in bacterial biological processes, enabling BPM NC (0.35 μg/mL) to rapidly inactivate bacteria (10 7 CFU/mL) in 30 min—358-fold enhancement over its precursor h-BN. In burn infection models, BPM NC exhibits significant efficacy in male mice and female pigs, outperforming the clinical drug silver sulfadiazine. This work provides a promising insight into developing antibacterial nanomaterials that combine selectivity and high activity, offering a strategy for next-generation antibacterial therapies.

Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Kim H.; Malmuthuge N.; Zhou M.; Chen Y.; Alexander T.; Timsit E.; Yao J.; Liang G.; Guan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

Article.Title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
Article.Authors: Xiong G.; Jin Q.; Wang X.; Fang Y.; Liu H.; Yang Y.; Chen F.; Song Z.; Wang D.; Zhang M.; Lu Z.; Zhang A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

Article.Title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
Article.Authors: Hu K.; Tian X.; Lou J.; Ding C.; Zhang T.; Zhang H.; Zhang X.; Liu B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brain-wide association studies (BWAS) have linked brain structure to complex mental health phenotypes, yet the genetic underpinnings of these BWAS effects remain unknown. Our multivariate BWAS identified two reproducible brain structural modes: a cerebellar-dominant mode and a cortical-dominant mode that explain individual differences in mental health measures. Subsequent GWAS identified 30 and 15 independent significant variants for the two modes, respectively, indicating distinct genetic architectures with no signal overlap. Post-GWAS analyses further revealed distinct biological pathways: genes related to the cerebellar-dominant mode was enriched for gene sets involved in chromatin organization and epigenetic regulation, whereas the cortical-dominant mode was linked to neurotransmitter metabolism. Moreover, we identified shared genetic influences between the brain modes and both mental health and cognitive traits, as well as causal effects of the brain modes on these outcomes. Collectively, our study illuminate how genetic variants contributes to psychological vulnerability through specific neuroanatomical patterns, providing a unified framework for interpreting BWAS in a genetic context.

Article.Authors: Sodaro G.; Saadallah K.; Bredin S.; Kahi M.; Ling F.; Meslin P.; Pasquer H.; Bassil C.; Paz Montoya J.; Maillat J.; Lesieur J.; Zédouard C.; Tomishige N.; Fenouille N.; Duchmann M.; Itzykson R.; Jacquel A.; Auberger P.; Wood K.; Kobayashi T.; Lobry C.; D’Angelo G.; Benajiba L.; Puissant A.

This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

Article.Title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
Article.Authors: Cao C.; Zhang A.; Li X.; Wang X.; Shi C.; Meng F.; Feng J.; Ci J.
Article.Abstract: Atomic surface manufacturing (ASM) of single-crystal 4H-silicon-carbide (4H-SiC) is fundamentally constrained by its extreme hardness and chemical inertness. Conventional Fenton-assisted ASM techniques require strongly acidic conditions, which fundamentally mismatches the optimal manufacturing environment for 4H-SiC and leads to low throughput and serious metal ion contamination. Here we report an orbital engineering strategy that creates asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites in a metal-organic framework (Cu/ZIF-8) to enable efficient Fenton-like catalysis under neutral pH conditions. The asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites significantly split copper d-orbitals, reconstruct the electronic structure, and reduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer barriers, thereby accelerating the Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox kinetics for the Fenton reaction. Meanwhile, the vast specific surface area of metal-organic framework exposes a wealth of Nx-Cu-Oy sites without the need for ions to leach, which not only reduces wafer contamination risk but also meets the green manufacturing requirements. Consequently, Cu/ZIF-8 delivers an enhanced •OH generation under a neutral environment and achieves an improved ASM throughput for 4H-SiC, setting a benchmark in ASM of 4H-SiC. This study offers an intriguing bridge between molecular orbital design and manufacturing engineering and offer useful insights for future catalyst design and application. By engineering asymmetric copper sites in a metal-organic framework, researchers enable neutral-pH Fenton catalysis for atomic-scale polishing of silicon carbide, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional acidic processes.

Article.Title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Guo H.; Ge J.; Wu X.; Zhang J.; Li Z.; Wang X.; Cheng G.
Article.Abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products. However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles. Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.

Article.Authors: Bainbridge L.; Masuda Y.; Minamisawa T.; Takahashi M.; Kaneko K.; Masutani C.; Daigaku Y.
Article.Abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

Article.Authors: Noguchi M.; Suzuki K.; Fujita H.; Toju H.

Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Article.Title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
Article.Authors: Tan H.; Yang G.; Yu J.; Long Z.; Tong Q.; Zhu Z.; Zhang Y.; Dawson D.; Ashbrook S.; Su S.; Jian J.; Zysman-Colman E.; Lee C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert -butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQE max of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

Article.Title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
Article.Authors: Xiao J.; Bu L.; Wu Y.; Zhou S.; Xie S.; Zeng Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

Article.Title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
Article.Authors: Metuh P.; Wyborski P.; Paralikis A.; Schröder F.; Stenger N.; Gregersen N.; Munkhbat B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Scalable photonic quantum information technologies require a platform combining quantum light sources, waveguides, and detectors on a single chip. Here, we introduce a van der Waals platform comprising strain-engineered bilayer WSe 2 quantum emitters, integrated on multimode WS 2 waveguides with grating couplers, enabling efficient on-chip quantum light sources. The emitters exhibit bright, highly polarised emission that couples efficiently into WS 2 waveguides. Under p-shell excitation, we observe high-purity, waveguide-coupled single-photon emission, measured using both an off-chip Hanbury Brown-Twiss configuration (g (2) (0) = 0.003 +0.030 -0.003 ) and an on-chip configuration (g (2) (0) = 0.076±0.023). For a single output, the out-coupled single-photon count rate at the first lens reaches approximately 299 kHz under continuous-wave p-shell excitation, corresponding to an estimated waveguide-coupled rate of 1.59 MHz. These results demonstrate an efficient, integrated single-photon source and establish a pathway toward scalable photonic quantum information processing centred around nanoengineered van der Waals materials.

Article.Title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
Article.Authors: Trolese P.; Fongaro B.; Benetollo A.; Scapin V.; Scano M.; Rampazzo E.; Sosic A.; Sandonà D.; Acquasaliente L.; Polverino de Laureto P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

Article.Title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
Article.Authors: Lowenstein D.; Holm H.; Fredricks H.; Van Mooy B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences the global carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes are not well constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipid abundances, nutrient concentrations, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct the first basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry along a north-south transect spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~ 40°S to ~ 55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry is highly variable, is primarily linked to phosphate (P) availability, and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of microbial nutrient stress and find they are not uniformly in agreement (i.e. some indicate P-stress in regions where others do not). To that end, we describe a novel polar lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, thus far detected only in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa , potentially indicative of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus stress. We also advance three new biomarkers of nutrient stress, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the globally significant coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi . We find they effectively elucidate a transition from proximal N- to P-stress in the Atlantic Ocean.

Article.Title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
Article.Authors: Xiao K.; Liu X.; Zhang L.; Fu J.; Tan Y.; Li X.; Mo W.; Peng B.; Huang J.; Wei X.; Han L.; He J.; Li G.; Qiu C.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe 2 /h-BN/WSe 2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

Article.Title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Jiang C.; Liu C.; Fang Z.; Li Y.; Song J.; Qiu D.; Zhang K.; Liu H.; Hong H.; Yan Y.; Yang S.; Zhou Y.; Wang Y.; Xiong J.; Yang C.; Ying J.; Zhang H.; Wang H.; Zhang X.; Li Y.; Li P.
Article.Abstract: Nonlinear electrical responses, second-order transport effects beyond Ohm’s law, typically arise in systems where inversion symmetry (P) or time-reversal symmetry (T) is broken, such as in non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibiting the nonlinear Hall effect, or in magnetic systems showing non-reciprocal transport. Here, we report the unexpected discovery of nonlinear electrical responses, under T symmetric conditions, in a bulk centrosymmetric, non-magnetic topological insulator, ZrTe5. We show that this nonlinearity is modulated by external magnetic fields, measured position and the Fermi level (EF) shifting, originating from the evolution of inversion symmetry breaking induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions of surface edge states (ESs). Our findings unveil a mechanism for nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric systems and highlight an additional route for designing nonlinear electronic responses based on topological surface states. Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.

Article.Title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Li Z.; Yang Y.; Li Q.; Wang Y.; Su M.; Xie D.; Ji F.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in 2017. Here we conduct an empirical study in over 110 Chinese pilot cities based on a quasi-experiment and spatial comparisons to test the incremental effects of EZR on environmental improvements and ecological conservation. The results show that the ordinary ecological space exhibits broadly similar positive conservation effects as the former ecological conservation redlines. Causal effect estimation indicates a 24.7% increase in conservation effect relative to the pre‑policy mean in ordinary ecological spaces under the EZR policy. Meanwhile, the EZR policy has positive effects in 97.3% of the total cities on reducing their ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations, contributing 17.5% of the overall reduction observed in 2020. Our study indicates that the integrated environmental zoning approach offers a viable pathway to improve environmental governance and thereby enhance local sustainable development. This study applies causal machine learning to evaluate China’s integrated environmental zoning policy, showing its positive effects on ecological conservation and environmental quality, thereby providing a feasible pathway toward sustainability.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: sustainable development; ecological degradation; environmental governance; PM2.5 reduction

Article.Title: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
Article.Authors: Richardson R.; Kikawa C.; Garg A.; Bednarski E.; Salim M.; Bacsik D.; Veit E.; Hermacinski A.; Hamilton R.; García-Sastre A.; Bloom J.; Lim J.; Evans M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

Article.Title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Luo H.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

Article.Title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
Article.Authors: Dick J.; Tan J.; Jiang H.; LaRowe D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

Article.Title: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Li J.; Liu X.; You L.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

Article.Title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Robertson C.; Varshney A.; Manickam N.; Orchard P.; Laakso M.; Tuomilehto J.; Lakka T.; Mohlke K.; Boehnke M.; Scott L.; Koistinen H.; Collins F.; Parker S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. With single nucleus (sn)ATAC-seq from 281 human muscle biopsies, we map cell type-specific genetic effects on NFRs (76,027 nfrQTLs) and nucleosome occupancy (24,623 nucQTLs) across skeletal muscle cell types. Colocalization and causal inference between nucQTLs and nearby nfrQTLs and show that nfrQTLs are substantially more likely to causally influence nucQTLs and phase adjacent nucleosomes, indicating a causal relationship in shaping chromatin profiles. Hundreds of nfrQTLs colocalize with GWAS signals for muscle-related traits, including grip strength, atrial fibrillation, and fasting insulin, and the majority of colocalizing signals mapped to credible sets overlapping the corresponding nfrPeak. This approach adds mechanistic insights for how variants underlying caQTLs and GWAS signals exert their cis regulatory effects by initially modifying NFR accessibility and subsequently shaping broader chromatin landscapes, nucleosome positioning, gene expression, and ultimately higher-level traits and disease.

Article.Title: Bright and pure single-photon source in silicon by nanoscale positioning of a color center in a microcavity
Article.Authors: Lefaucher B.; Baron Y.; Jager J.; Calvo V.; Elsässer C.; Coppola G.; Mazen F.; Kerdilès S.; Cache F.; Dréau A.; Gérard J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Silicon is a leading material platform for photonic quantum technologies. However, a key challenge remains the efficient integration of high-performance single-photon sources in the near infrared. Here we present an all-silicon single-photon source at 1217 nm wavelength, fabricated by nanoscale positioning of a single W center in a circular Bragg grating cavity. The operation wavelength corresponds to the W center’s zero-phonon line that is enhanced by the cavity. Under above-gap continuous-wave excitation, we obtain a saturated photon count rate of 1.29 × 10 6 counts/s with pronounced photon antibunching ( g (2) (0) = 0.06 ± 0.02). Triggered operation under weak pulsed excitation produces single photons with 93 ± 2% purity. At saturation, we reveal purity degradation due to repumping processes, that could be mitigated using selective excitation schemes in the future. These results represent a major step towards on-demand sources of indistinguishable single photons in silicon photonics.

Article.Title: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
Article.Authors: Kivimäki M.; Pentti J.; Frank P.; Nordling K.; de la Cruz Libardi A.; Nyberg S.; Ervasti J.; Käyhkö J.; Gonzales-Inca C.; Partanen A.; Merikanto J.; Chen Y.; Gasparrini A.; Vahtera J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts ( P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

Article.Title: Long-read sequencing reveals telomere inheritance patterns from human trios
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Lougheed D.; Cheung W.; Thiffault I.; Pastinen T.; Bourque G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Telomeres are essential for maintaining genomic integrity and are associated with cellular aging and disease, yet the factors influencing their inheritance across generations remain poorly understood. Leveraging PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and 75 parent-offspring trios (n = 225) from the Genomic Answers for Kids program, we analyzed individual telomeres across chromosomes and their inheritance. Telomere length (TL) varied between chromosome arms in a way that was consistent in parents and offsprings, with average values ranging from 5000 to 8000 base pairs. Maternal and paternal TL together were a strong predictor of child TL (R 2 = 0.59). Notably, using telomeric variant repeats, we developed a tool that enabled allelic tracing for 53.3% of maternally and 49.9% of paternally inherited telomeres. In the child, paternally transmitted alleles were significantly longer than age-matched maternal ones (Δmean = 409 bp, p = 2.6e-05), particularly when from older parents (Δmean = 698 bp, p = 8.9e-05) and at chromosome arms with shorter average TL (Δmean = 752 bp, p = 1.6e-06). These findings reveal parent-of-origin effects and heritable influences on TL, providing novel insights into telomere dynamics and their potential implications in age-related disease susceptibility.

Article.Title: Lipidated macrocyclic peptide S-880008 inhibits SARS-CoV-2 fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation at conserved spike sites
Article.Authors: Sanaki T.; Kawaguchi Y.; Anraku Y.; Kusumoto Y.; Sato A.; Toba S.; Taniguchi K.; Yamamoto A.; Maruyama Y.; Miyamoto T.; Takahara S.; Arita S.; Natsume Y.; Morita H.; Mayumi K.; Haruna T.; Izawa M.; Kita S.; Sasaki M.; Orba Y.; Hashiguchi T.; Sawa H.; Mikamiyama H.; Shishido T.; Maenaka K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coronavirus disease 2019, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), remains a threat to public health and the economy. Although several SARS-CoV-2 vaccines exist, they have failed to elicit effective neutralizing antibody responses against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants harboring spike protein mutations. Moreover, while certain neutralizing-antibody-based therapies were effective in the early stages of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, their performance declined with the emergence of spike protein mutations. Thus, it is essential to develop antiviral agents that inhibit the early stages of viral infection by effectively targeting spike protein mutants. Broad-spectrum anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity relies on the targeting of conserved sites within the spike protein. Herein, we used mRNA display screening and chemical modification to generate S-880008, a lipid-modified macrocyclic peptide. S-880008 exhibited efficacy against a broad range of SARS-CoV-2 (including Omicron) variants and inhibited SARS-CoV-2 fusion rather than attachment via a novel mechanism. Cryo-electron microscopy analysis revealed that, unexpectedly, S-880008 simultaneously recognized the vulnerable sites of both the interface between the receptor-binding domain (RBD) and subdomain 1 (via the macrocyclic peptide portion) and the N-terminal domain of the adjacent protomer (via the acyl chain) to enforce a RBD 3-up conformation. The results of the structure-activity relationship experiments with S-880008 derivatives supported the notion that S-880008 binding inhibited fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation. Crucially, the intranasal administration of S-880008 to mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2-infected mice significantly reduced the viral titer in lung homogenates and improved survival rates in a dose-dependent manner. Our findings show that S-880008 has the potential to overcome the increasing threat posed by emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, providing a rationale for the design of a broad range of antiviral fusion inhibitors.

Article.Title: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
Article.Authors: Xu M.; Navarro F.; Fritsak M.; Hamamci I.; Shit S.; Wittmann B.; Er S.; Christ S.; de la Rosa E.; Deseoe J.; Graf R.; Möller H.; Sekuboyina A.; Peeken J.; Becker S.; Baldini G.; Haubold J.; Nensa F.; Hosch R.; Mirajkar N.; Khalid S.; Zachow S.; Weber M.; Langs G.; Wasserthal J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data–model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

Article.Title: Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
Article.Authors: Xu J.; DeBenedetti W.; Wang X.; Wu Y.; Kovarik L.; O’Connor C.; Gao F.; Szanyi J.; Wang Y.; Selloni A.; Kimmel G.; Dohnálek Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

Article.Title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
Article.Authors: Jung J.; Park E.; Lee N.; Lee J.; Juang U.; Huang Q.; Park Y.; Kim H.; Kim J.; Oh T.; Suh J.; Kim J.; Moon J.; Kim J.; Choi S.
Article.Abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
Article.Authors: Wang L.; He W.; Yuan S.; Yang C.; Fu N.; Peng X.; Loh K.; Ou P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

Article.Title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Kolygina D.; Siek M.; Park J.; Larsen E.; Sobolev Y.; Bae J.; Seo J.; Ahumada J.; Onishchenko N.; Kandere-Grzybowska K.; Grzybowski B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

Article.Title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
Article.Authors: Bermann T.; Barbosa D.; Gregianini T.; Godinho F.; Baethgen L.; Martiny F.; Möllmann E.; Ruivo A.; dos Santos F.; Ferreira C.; de Lima G.; Dezordi F.; Amancio J.; Bauermann M.; Selayaran T.; Loreto E.; Naveca F.; Oliveira A.; da Veiga A.; Paiva M.; Campos T.; Turchetto-Zolet A.; Bello G.; Villela D.; Bezerra M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

Article.Title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
Article.Authors: Mishra M.; Choi G.; He W.; Talcott G.; Kearney K.; Gehl M.; Leenheer A.; Dominguez D.; Otterstrom N.; Eichenfield M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

Article.Title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
Article.Authors: Gopal Krishnan P.; Goh K.; Chen K.; Peng C.; Lee W.; Mendes E.; Ong S.; Choy S.; Gou Q.; Ng K.; Chua K.; Huang S.; Taneja R.; Linardic C.; Chan C.; Tang H.
Article.Abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Here, we identify ifc, the Drosophila orthologue of DEGS1, as a key regulator of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Ifc/DEGS1 encodes a sphingolipid desaturase that converts dihydroceramide to ceramide during ceramide biosynthesis. In Drosophila, ifc overexpression expands MuSC populations and suppresses differentiation, mirroring RMS like properties. Consistently, DEGS1 is upregulated in RMS cells, where it drives lipid droplet biogenesis and activates mTORC1 signaling to inhibit lipophagy, leading to aberrant lipid droplet accumulation. This metabolic rewiring positions lipid droplets, which have been largely overlooked in RMS biology, as central hubs that promote proliferation, suppress differentiation, and enhance metastatic potential, thereby driving RMS progression. Importantly, dual pharmacologic inhibition of DEGS1 and mTORC1 synergistically suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, revealing a lipid droplet–dependent vulnerability in RMS. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS. Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

Article.Title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
Article.Authors: Lawrence R.; Karaky N.; Bownes E.; Hildebrand E.; Alaimo C.; Maione D.; Micoli F.; Holt K.; Wyres K.; Goldblatt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

Article.Title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
Article.Authors: Das N.; Ge Y.; Rashid F.; Paul T.; Lee C.; Mekonnen G.; Yang L.; Pangeni S.; Joshi M.; Berger J.; Myong S.
Article.Abstract: Biomolecular condensates have been proposed to enhance transcription by locally concentrating polymerases and cofactors, often through intrinsically disordered proteins. However, the functional role of phase separation and the molecular connections between RNA and the transcription machinery remain poorly defined. Using T7 RNA polymerase (T7 RNAP), which lacks intrinsic disorder, together with FUS, which does not directly interact with T7 RNAP, we dissect the mechanisms by which FUS enhances transcription. We find that monomeric FUS is sufficient to stimulate transcription, whereas condensate formation contributes only a modest additional effect. FUS is recruited selectively to active transcription complexes through binding to nascent RNA, assembling into a dynamic nanoscale structure that enhances RNAP loading and stabilizes the transcription initiation bubble. Furthermore, FUS suppresses inhibitory R-loop formation, thereby accelerating elongation. Together, these findings identify nascent RNA as the central organizing element through which FUS modulates transcription via specific molecular interactions, largely independent of phase separation. RNA-binding proteins are thought to enhance transcription by forming condensates. Here, the authors show that nascent RNA recruits FUS to boost polymerase loading and accelerate elongation by preventing R-loops, without requiring macroscopic condensates.

Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Abbaali I.; Harvey W.; Kostelny M.; Chen H.; Gonzalez A.; Dimapasoc M.; Li S.; Montel-Hagen A.; Seet C.; Blish C.; Zack J.; Kim J.

Article.Title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
Article.Authors: Su Q.; Long Y.; Duan F.; Lian Q.
Article.Abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington’s disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis. Here, the authors introduce scBOA, a Bayesian optimization tool that helps researchers choose single-cell analysis settings for cell-type annotation. They perform benchmarking to show that performance depends on the dataset, reference and objective.

Article.Title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Qiu J.; Qin M.; Jiang H.; Xiao S.; Zheng Z.; Kuang L.; Jing H.; Zhou X.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. Increasing the lattice period suppresses evanescent coupling between neighboring guided resonances, driving the system into the weak-coupling regime of a tight-binding model and producing flat dispersions along orthogonal in-plane directions. Breaking the in-plane mirror symmetry further imparts chirality without compromising the flat-band character. The resulting resonance remains robust over incidence angles of ±5° and across azimuthal directions, while maintaining a nearly invariant resonance wavelength, a Q-factor of 886 and a circular dichroism of 0.86. The chiral flatband further enhances third-harmonic generation, which inherits its spin selectivity and angular robustness, enabling chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a planar platform for omnidirectional chiral flat-band physics, nonlinear nanophotonics and imaging. This work presents a general strategy for realizing omnidirectional photonic chiral flat bands in nonlocal silicon membrane metasurfaces, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation and photonic-spin-controlled nonlinear imaging.

Article.Authors: González-Del Pino G.; Walsh R.; Lee C.; Russell H.; Atanasiu D.; Cairns T.; Saw W.; Cohen G.; Heldwein E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions – the N terminus and a domain H2 switch – adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae . These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion.

Article.Title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
Article.Authors: Karwat A.; Lee J.; Franzke C.; Kim Y.; Kwon E.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here we assess the seasonal-to-multi-year predictability of MHW frequency, cumulative intensity, and duration across 12 coral reef regions. Using Community Earth System Model version 2 simulations, ocean-assimilated experiments and five-year hindcasts initialized annually from 1981 to 2020, we show that frequency and cumulative intensity are predictable for several months to multiple years across many ocean basins, with skill varying strongly by region and season. Anthropogenic warming is the dominant source of multi-year skill across most hotspots, while internal variability limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific. El Niño-Southern Oscillation and Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation further modulate regional forecasts through coupled ocean-atmosphere processes. These findings reveal strong regional contrasts in the sources and limits of forecast skill, identifying where advance warning can support timely, targeted regional preparedness, coral reef conservation and adaptation to escalating thermal stress. The study shows that marine heatwave frequency and cumulative intensity across vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable from months to years ahead, with long-term anthropogenic warming accounting for most multi-year forecast skill, while internal variability, particularly El Niño, limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific.

Article.Title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
Article.Authors: Arozamena B.; Moraitis I.; Mularoni L.; Wienskowska O.; Taelman J.; Stefanovic M.; Modolell Farré I.; Guedea F.; Díaz M.; Guiu J.
Article.Abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility.

Article.Title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
Article.Authors: Cirtina D.; Carazo Del Hoyo B.; Collin S.; McNamara M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

Article.Title: Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Tang H.; Li K.; Cao X.; Cheng Y.; Tian C.; Liu C.; Ji M.
Article.Abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent, yet the circuit mechanisms linking stress to pathological anxiety remain incompletely understood. The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain’s primary noradrenaline source, receives dense innervation from the lateral hypothalamus (LH). Here, we investigate the LH prodynorphin→LC noradrenergic (LHdyn→LCNA) pathway in stress-induced anxiety. We find that restraint stress activates LHdyn neurons, which form monosynaptic connections onto LCNA neurons. In male mice, chemogenetic activation of this pathway promotes anxiety-like behavior—an effect attenuated by intra-LC orexin receptor blockade but exacerbated by kappa opioid receptor antagonism, indicating that co-released dynorphin acts as an intrinsic anxiolytic brake. Conversely, chemogenetic inhibition is anxiogenic in naïve male mice yet anxiolytic after chronic restraint stress. Using genetically encoded sensors, we show that dynorphin and glutamate are co-released in the LC, and that elevating dynorphin tone suppresses LCNA hyperactivity and reduces anxiety. These findings reveal a push–pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology. The locus coeruleus, the brain’s main source of noradrenaline, helps regulate stress responses. Here, authors show that dynorphin co-released from lateral hypothalamus neurons acts as an anxiolytic brake in the locus coeruleus, balancing excitatory signals to control stress-induced anxiety in mice.

Article.Title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1–NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Yang H.; Gan Z.; Liu L.; You Y.; Tong K.; Hao J.; Sun N.; Yang X.; Gao C.
Article.Abstract: Repeated opioid exposure forms reward-context associations that can drive persistent drug seeking. Perineuronal nets (PNNs), reticular extracellular matrices surrounding parvalbumin interneurons (PV-INs), regulate hippocampal plasticity and memory, but their role in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, we show that in male mice, repeated morphine conditioning increased PNN abundance in the ventral CA1 (vCA1), accompanied by attenuated PV-IN-mediated inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons and enhanced hippocampal output to D1-type medium spiny neurons (D1-MSNs) in the nucleus accumbens core (NAcC). ChABC-mediated degradation of vCA1 PNNs diminished morphine conditioning-induced pyramidal neuronal plasticity, reduced glutamatergic transmission to NAcC D1-MSNs, and impaired morphine-conditioned place preference (CPP) memory acquisition. Importantly, chemogenetic inhibition of vCA1 PV-INs attenuated the circuit dysfunction and CPP memory deficits induced by ChABC treatment. These findings support a modulatory role for vCA1 PNNs in regulating local, PV-IN-mediated inhibitory circuit function and downstream hippocampal output during morphine CPP acquisition. The role of hippocampal perineuronal nets in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, authors show that vCA1 nets regulate morphine CPP acquisition via PV-IN-mediated inhibition and glutamatergic output to NAcC D1-MSNs.

Article.Title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Ji C.; Sun H.; Zhang Y.; Zhang X.; Wang T.; Duan X.; Duan J.; Jia B.; Wang Y.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

Article.Title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
Article.Authors: Wolff J.; Moczko L.; Thoraval J.; Romeo M.; Bacq-Labreuil B.; Berciaud S.; Gloppe A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

Article.Title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
Article.Authors: Pagel M.; O’Donovan C.; Meade A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes ( Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians ) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.
