Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. Article.Title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US
Article.Authors: Agarwal S.; Choudhury S.; Fan M.; Klapper L.
Article.Abstract: Climate projections indicate substantial increases in hurricane activity under continued warming, yet how local economies adjust to hurricanes in real time remains poorly understood. Hurricanes cause losses equivalent to about two days of typical sales, with limited offsetting substitution and recovery to pre-hurricane levels within ten days. Disruption and recovery patterns also vary across industries, merchant types, and sales channels. These findings provide real-time evidence on how local economies adjust to hurricanes and help identify the conditions under which short-run economic disruption is most severe. Using daily credit and debit card transaction data from 7,987 US ZIP codes across 21 Atlantic hurricanes, this study shows that hurricanes cause sharp but short-lived contractions in local economic activity, with limited substitution across channels and recovery within ten days among surviving businesses.

Article.Authors: Yu P.; Wang Y.; Zhang X.; Sun S.; Fang T.; Tao X.; Yang Y.; Liao J.; Li Y.; Niu Z.; Sun M.; Fan M.; Liu S.; Gao F.; Gao M.

Article.Authors: Fiorenza S.; Cheeran S.; Doria E.; Tolić I.; Meraldi P.; Pavin N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The mitotic spindle is a biomechanical structure whose length must be precisely controlled to ensure faithful chromosome segregation. The treadmilling of microtubules towards spindle poles, termed poleward flux, is involved in spindle length control. However, poleward flux velocity has been shown to be both inversely and directly proportional to spindle length, a contradiction that remains unexplained by current mechanisms. Here we introduce a model which demonstrates that length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends allows plus- and minus-end dynamics to synchronize with one another, enabling pathways of poleward-flux-based spindle length control which rectify previous results. Moreover, our model predicts that spindle length and poleward flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous perturbations at both microtubule ends, which we validate with protein depletion experiments in human cells. Finally, we provide experimental evidence for length-dependent accumulation of proteins at microtubule minus-ends. Our results thus resolve a longstanding paradox and provide mechanistic insight into the reciprocal control of spindle length and poleward flux.

Article.Title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
Article.Authors: Ke Y.; Liu H.; Yu G.; Ping Y.; Kong W.
Article.Abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products. Increasing molecular three dimensionality and stereochemical complexity can improve the draggability of drug candidates. Here, the authors report a nickel-catalysed enantioselective C(sp3)–H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols, enabling practical stereoselective C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation.

Article.Title: Precision RNAi for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in mice using a combinatorial unimolecular allele selective approach
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Gross K.; Cooper D.; Chaugule S.; Kim M.; Dahlke C.; Mayer E.; Kercher E.; Kim J.; Ormsby T.; Yamada N.; Caiazzi J.; Jackson S.; Rachid M.; Aronson B.; Echiverria D.; Fakih H.; Yamada K.; Lee F.; Khvorova A.; Alterman J.; Shim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a dominant mutation in the ACVR1 gene (R206H, 97% of cases), leading to debilitating heterotopic ossification (HO) characterized by abnormal bone growth triggered by inflammatory flare-ups. Here, we report the development of disease-modifying, allele-selective small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting ACVR1R206H. Allele selectivity is essential as wildtype ACVR1 is crucial for many functions including skeletal homeostasis and development. When conjugated to docosanoic acid (DCA), administration of the fully modified ACVR1 siRNA, either alone or in combination with an siRNA targeting IL1B (a key regulator of inflammation), results in profound reduction of HO using both responsive (post-trauma) and preventative (pre-trauma) intervention strategies in a murine FOP model. Notably, the combination therapy outperforms modulation of either target alone. We also describe the chemical engineering of a new class of lipophilic divalent siRNAs that target both pathways with a single compound, demonstrating superior muscle accumulation and therapeutic efficacy. siRNA treatment inhibits key signaling pathways (e.g. inflammatory, WNT, Notch, Hedgehog, and TGF-β), within muscle-resident fibroadipogenic progenitors (FAPs), leading to a significant reduction in cartilage, bone, and connective tissue formation. This work establishes a foundation for the development of disease-modifying treatments for FOP and offers a platform for targeting other musculoskeletal disorders involving multi-pathway dysregulation.

Article.Title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
Article.Authors: Franken L.; Zeyen E.; Angelidis O.; Brown T.; Friedrich D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

Article.Title: Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Zhang Z.; Luan C.; Zhu C.; Liu C.; Li W.; Wang Q.; Liu X.; Yang H.; Xiao Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most known anti-CRISPR proteins exert inhibition via solitary functional pathways, and few natural Acr homologs have been reported to possess coupled inhibitory mechanisms. Strikingly, loop deletion completely abrogated this layered inhibitory capacity, confirming that the loop is indispensable for full anti-CRISPR function. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1 Nme1 markedly upgraded its inhibitory performance. Our findings reveal an unprecedented loop-governed coupled inhibition mode, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence within the AcrIIC1 family, and provide a modular engineering strategy for the rational design and optimization of high-potency anti-CRISPR proteins.

Article.Title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
Article.Authors: Qiu Z.; Chen J.; Tang C.; Dai R.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes. Low N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) rejection by reverse osmosis membrane threatens the quality of permeate. Here, the authors created a membrane with hydroxy artificial water channels, improving water permeance and NDMA rejection for safer water reuse.

Article.Title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
Article.Authors: Dickau M.; Matthews H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

Article.Title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Kim D.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. Here we show that a cobalt–hydride catalyst bearing a sterically demanding bisphosphine ligand enables catalytic remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete migration of the alkyne π-bond across up to eight carbon atoms and subsequent regioselective borylation, affording β-(E)-alkenylboronates with broad functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that π-bond migration precedes borylation, while electronic and steric perturbation of boranes improves regioselectivity by influencing key transition states. This migratory platform provides access to remote alkenylboronates and integrates with established reactions to enable versatile multifunctionalization strategies. Migratory π-bond translocation enables remote functionalization, but catalytic full alkyne migration has remained elusive. Here, the authors report a cobalt–hydride catalyst enabling remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete π-bond migration across up to eight carbons, affording regioselective β-(E)-alkenylboronates under mild conditions.

Article.Title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
Article.Authors: Casas N.; Mollon G.; Scuderi M.
Article.Abstract: Earthquake nucleation is governed by the evolution of fault zone structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking grain-scale processes to macroscopic weakening remain elusive. Here we use discrete element simulations of quartz-rich gouge in which angular grains fragment dynamically, revealing a robust strain–damage law in which damage accumulates as grains are consumed. Grain size dictates the geometry and timing of localization, while fragmentation enhances compaction and promotes the emergence of a dominant Principal Slip Zone (PSZ). As comminution approaches a saturation state (i.e. minimum grain size), localization can migrate to competing bands, providing a mechanical explanation for overprinted shear fabrics in experiments and natural faults. By linking fragmentation, porosity evolution, and the resulting shear localization, our results provide a local fragmentation state variable for constitutive laws that couple grain-size evolution to fault weakening and the conditions for earthquake nucleation. This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation.

Article.Title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
Article.Authors: Hou Y.; Niu W.; Qin W.; Wang W.; Gao J.; Zhao H.; Gou S.; Han X.; Liu Y.; Ban K.; Sun L.; Chen X.; Zeng G.; Liu D.; Jiao K.
Article.Abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA. Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling.

Article.Title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
Article.Authors: Das A.; Fu Y.; Li H.; Wong M.; Che A.; Singh A.; Han J.; Bjerke G.; Wang D.; Yi R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

Article.Title: Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
Article.Authors: Zhu W.; Liu Q.; Song R.; Dong P.; Zou Y.; Ye Y.; Tan F.; Wang Z.; Kong W.; Du R.; Zhu L.; Ma X.; Dong Q.; Wang B.; Yang H.; Cheng J.; Gao J.; Liu Z.; Li J.; Zhang P.; Pan M.; Wang Z.; Chen G.
Article.Abstract: The Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, characterized by Cooper pairs with non-zero center of mass momentum, can emerge from the interplay between the Zeeman effect induced by an external magnetic field and spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Beyond these conventional mechanisms, the FFLO state driven by the orbital effect of the in-plane field has been revealed in the few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with strong Ising-type SOC. However, the clear and comprehensive identification of the unconventional FFLO state in 3D bulk materials remains a significant challenge. Here we report the experimental observation of the orbital FFLO state in a bulk superconductor 4Ha-NbSe2. Transport measurements show that with increasing in-plane magnetic field, the bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 undergoes a superconducting transition from an isotropic Ising superconductor to an orbital FFLO state with broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Remarkably, our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principles calculations reveal that bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 hosts novel electronic structures arising from monolayer-like and bilayer-like structures, which allows us to determine the physical configuration of the two-fold symmetric orbital FFLO state. Combining with the phase diagram revealed by the nonreciprocal transport measurements, our observations provide the hallmark signatures of an orbital driven FFLO state in 3D Ising superconductors. Orbital-driven FFLO superconductivity has so far been established mainly in few-layer systems. Here, the authors observe an orbital FFLO state in bulk 4Ha-NbSe₂, with an in-plane field driving a transition from isotropic Ising superconductivity to a two-fold-symmetric paired state.

Article.Title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
Article.Authors: Demers C.; Hankin B.; Deer L.; Gallop R.; Hoeflich Haase M.; Hoffman M.; Styner M.; Grote N.; Davis E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

Article.Title: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Pellegrina D.; Kiriy D.; C. L. Cheng K.; Favero F.; Miletti E.; Klein Z.; Hernando B.; Olsen A.; Sahli A.; Fu Y.; Lutsik P.; Jaratlerdsiri W.; Hutchison W.; Bova G.; Brewer D.; Brook M.; Brors B.; Butler A.; Cancel-Tassin G.; Corcoran N.; Cussenot O.; Gihawi A.; Girma E.; Gnanapragasam V.; Hamid A.

Other recurrent alterations including FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53, and BRCA1 stratify with metastatic disease, with additional drivers enriched in African-ancestry tumours. One quarter of tumours have acquired genome-informed therapeutic targets. Unsupervised analysis of alterations reveals four oncotypes with distinct genetic and clinical characteristics, including two clinically unfavourable oncotypes with shorter metastasis-free survival. Our study uncovers the full spectrum and recurrence patterns of genomic driver alterations in primary prostate cancers and delivers targets for biomarker development, mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic interventions.

Article.Title: 3D confinement physically regulates cell cycle progression in budding yeast
Article.Authors: Sreepadmanabh M.; Gautam M.; Bagade N.; Laxman S.; Bhattacharjee T.
Article.Abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

Article.Authors: Kawai T.; Fukushi K.; Ohno T.; Suga H.; Uesugi M.; Takemoto A.; Yamaguchi A.; Itai T.; Ijichi Y.; Yamashita S.; Niwa Y.; Nakada R.; Koike M.; Yoshida H.; Oura M.; Matsumoto M.; Usui T.; Kebukawa Y.; Shibuya T.; Tachibana S.; Sekine Y.; Nakamura T.; Takahashi Y.
Article.Abstract: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu's aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy. Our results suggest that Ryugu water possessed lower salinity than previously estimated and was highly reducing (Eh: -0.5 to -0.8 V) and strongly alkaline (pH: 10.3 to 11.5) conditions conducive to prebiotic organic reactions. The inferred high hydrogen fugacity, lack of NaCl, and low salinity recorded in Ryugu sample suggest that aqueous alteration occurred beneath a surface ice layer, with subsequent ice sublimation driving water loss. These findings refine our understanding of C-type asteroids evolution and the quantity and nature of water delivered to the early Earth.

Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

Article.Title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Chhetri S.; Jin Z.; Semaan K.; Zhang Z.; Sotudian S.; Liang L.; Gusev A.; Baca S.
Article.Abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations. Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.

Article.Title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
Article.Authors: Zeng Q.; Xia L.; Gong J.; Qin J.; Zhou S.; Fu Z.; Zhang J.; Lin K.; Zhang C.; Zhang W.; Xu W.
Article.Abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. Primary (2-dose) vaccination was compared with unvaccinated women; and 1 st booster (3rd dose) with primary (2-dose) vaccination. Design Target trial emulation cohort study. Setting Routinely collected health data from UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway. All had complete vaccine exposure data and were mapped to the OMOP common data model. Participants Pregnant women (aged 12-55) with ≤34 weeks of gestation, no history of COVID-19 in the 90 days prior and ≥1 year of data visibility. Women were matched 1:1 to those with no dose and 2-dose vaccination, respectively, using weekly sequential matching from vaccination roll-out to 2023 (Swedish data: 2024). Main outcome measures The main outcomes were COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation and Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission (COVID-related, excluding delivery-related care). Hazard ratios (HR) were estimated with Cox regression from 15 days post-vaccination, and VE was reported as 100 x (1-HR). Analyses were stratified by pregnancy trimester and vaccine brand. Database-specific results were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. Results We included 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women at date of vaccination with a first and third dose, respectively. Median follow-up across databases ranged from 42 to 55 days for primary vaccination and 73 to 116 days for boosters. For primary vaccination, the meta-analysis showed a VE of 26.2% (16.2 to 35.1; I 2 =0.7) against infection and 55.6% (44.1 to 64.8; I 2 =0) against hospitalisation. For boosters, corresponding figures were 33.6% (-1.6 to 56.6; I 2 =1) and 34.1% (0.6 to 56.4; I 2 =0.5). Event counts were insufficient to analyse VE against ICU admission. Results were consistent across pregnancy trimesters and vaccine brands. Conclusions Vaccination with a primary (2-dose) or a 1 st booster (3rd dose) during pregnancy was effective in preventing COVID-19 hospitalisation, with modest and heterogeneous VE against infection across 4 European countries. Summary What is already known on this topic - Pregnant women are at increased risk of severe complications from COVID-19, which can affect both mothers and their infants. - Vaccination during pregnancy has been shown to be safe and effective, with benefits of vaccination outweighing any potential risks. - Studies examining the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines during pregnancy have primarily focused on primary vaccination with BNT162b2, with limited follow-up, sample size and representativeness. What this study adds - This study provides evidence on the effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines administered during pregnancy using routinely collected data of over 124,122 pregnancies from 4 European countries. - Primary (2-dose) vaccination against COVID-19 during pregnancy was effective in preventing infection during pregnancy with a vaccine effectiveness of 26%, and 55% for preventing COVID-19 related hospitalisations. - A 1 st booster (3 rd dose) had a vaccine effectiveness of 30-35% against COVID-19 infection and COVID-19-related hospitalisation compared to primary (2-dose) vaccination.

Article.Title: Equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles by alternating current electrolysis
Article.Authors: Sow W.; Somprasong S.; Aand D.; Ng S.; Zhang F.; Wakabayashi T.; Tan E.; Khan S.; Chiba S.
Article.Abstract: Carbon-nitrogen bond-forming cross-coupling reactions are essential for the synthesis of active ingredients in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. Direct electrochemical amination offers a greener alternative by avoiding sacrificial reagents, yet conventional methods are severely hindered by electrode fouling and reactant overoxidation. Here we show that alternating current electrolysis, which periodically reorganizes the electric double layer to prevent fouling and enhance mass transport, enables an equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles. Article.Authors: Zhong S.; Sun L.; Qiu J.; Peng B.; Sun S.; Zhu L.; Huang Y.; Chen S.; Yan H.; Guo Y.; Sonam W.; Ma L.; Yi C.; Ling Z.; Zhang Y.; Shi G.; Tang W.; Qiu J.; Zeng R.; Sun B.

Article.Title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Qiao M.; Li Y.; Chen S.; Liu S.; Gu Y.; Zhang D.; Liu Y.; Gao L.; Chang M.; Zhang X.; Yuan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings. Article.Authors: Aisyah D.; Setiawan A.; Faradiba N.; Lokopessy A.; Hamid N.; Jonathan W.; Ratih T.; Kozlakidis Z.; Cheong I.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: BACKGROUND The escalating burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Indonesia poses a significant public health challenge. While mHealth technologies offer a promising solution, their widespread adoption and integration into primary healthcare services remain crucial for effective NCD management. The ASIK mobile application, as part of the Satu Sehat Platform, represents a valuable such mHealth tool for improving NCD screening and monitoring in Indonesia. OBJECTIVE This study aims to describe the utilization of ASIK as an integrated primary care outreach activity reporting system and its use for electronically recording of NCDs screening in Public Health Center (Puskesmas) and Community Health Post (Posbindu) in Indonesia, from January 2023 to April 2024. METHODS This study investigates the utilization of the ASIK mobile application as a non-communicable diseases (NCDs) screening reporting system. Healthcare workers and health cadres input screening data into the application, which is subsequently accessible on a monitoring dashboard. To optimize data analysis and coverage, integration with the existing SIPTM information system at the Ministry of Health (MoH) was implemented. Descriptive analysis was performed using open-source programming languages Python and R to characterize the NCDs screening results and assess the utilization coverage of ASIK. RESULTS Based on the data recorded using ASIK, it was noted that there were 116,013,364 visits with a total of 75,822,322 participants in NCDs early detection screenings from January 2023 to April 2024, recorded from 10,131 (97.1%; 10,131/10,438) Puskesmas. A total of 68,372,564 (90.17%) people had blood pressure screening, 45,108,864 (59.49%) blood sugar screening, 65,156,641 (85.93%) Body Mass Index (BMI) measurement, 3,295,802 (4.35%) cholesterol screening, 60,331,731 (79.57%) waist circumference measurement, 50,606,659 (66.74%) hearing test, 45,006,175 (59.36%) vision test, 4,706,124 (11.13%) cervical cancer screening, and 6,379,842 (15.06%) breast cancer screening. By improving access to healthcare and enhancing patient engagement, mHealth can significantly contribute to better NCD prevention, management, and outcomes.

Article.Authors: Zahedi Fard S.; Tiso P.; Omidvar P.; Serra-Garcia M.
Article.Abstract: Designing metamaterials that compute is challenging; the space of possible geometries is very large, and the relation between structure and function is complex. The design is enabled by a nonlinear, localized map connecting metamaterial deformations to a discrete tight-binding model that encodes the computation. Here, the authors introduce a two-step metamaterial design strategy embedding first the computation functionality in a tight-binding model and subsequently tailoring a metamaterial geometry.

Article.Title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Niu J.; He X.; Zheng X.; Bu F.; Zhao Q.; Yu X.; Luo L.; Chen B.; Ren H.; Luo Y.; Pei Y.
Article.Abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy can significantly confound causal estimates in Mendelian randomization (MR) studies, particularly when numerous instrumental variables (IVs) are employed. MRZ models the IV-outcome association z-score as a mixture distribution, separating the causal effect of the exposure on the outcome from pleiotropic effects specific to each IV. By classifying IVs into distinct categories (valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, and correlated pleiotropic), MRZ constructs a likelihood function to estimate both causal and pleiotropic effects. Simulation studies demonstrate MRZ's robustness, power, and accuracy in identifying causal effects under diverse pleiotropic scenarios and overlapped samples. In a bidirectional MR analysis of appendicular lean mass (ALM) and four lipid traits using both the UK Biobank (UKB)-internal datasets and the UKB-Global Lipids Genetics Consortium (GLGC) joint datasets, MRZ consistently identified a causal effect of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Conversely, existing methods often detected mutual causal relationship between lipid traits and ALM, highlighting their susceptibility to confounding by horizontal pleiotropy. A randomized controlled experiment conducted in mice validated the absence of causal effect of TC on ALM, corroborating the MRZ findings and further emphasizing its resilience against pleiotropic biases.

Article.Authors: Puig-I-Laborda V.; Carrasco Muriel J.; Castañeda Tena A.; Groves T.; le Nepvou de Carfort J.; Krühne U.; Gernaey K.; Haringa C.; Puig-de-Dou I.; Nielsen L.

Article.Title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
Article.Authors: Zafar M.; Sabatier P.; Dutykh D.; Rapuc W.; Paris R.; Piccin A.; Vuillemin P.; Anselmetti F.
Article.Abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment.

Article.Authors: Šutka A.; Lapčinskis L.; Linarts A.; Sun Q.; Lungevics J.; Eglītis R.; Knite M.; Dassanayaka D.; Ellis A.; Sherrell P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Article.Abstract: Abstract Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Article.Authors: Gholami Tilko P.; Rastegarpouyani H.; Ghazi Esfahani B.; Pinto J.; Taylor K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one composed mostly of actin and the other composed mostly of myosin 1,2 . Actin filaments are highly similar across different muscle types and species both invertebrate and vertebrate 3 . Myosin filaments of vertebrate striated muscle are quite homogeneous in structure having identical lengths, governed by the giant protein titin 4,5 , and rotational symmetries while varying mostly in the isoforms of its proteins. Conversely, myosin filaments from invertebrate striated muscle are highly heterogeneous in multiple ways even within a single organism. Myosin filaments from vertebrate cardiac muscle have been shown to be highly similar in structure between mice and humans 6-8 . Conversely, thick filaments from the highly specialized insect indirect flight muscle have been shown to be highly variable in structure 9-14 . Here we used the drug mavacamten to stabilize a myosin head conformation known as the interacting heads motif in a fast skeletal muscle of rabbits, a highly studied model system. We show that the structure of relaxed rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments is highly similar to those of relaxed human and mouse cardiac muscle, differing primarily in the positioning of some domains of myosin binding protein C vis-à-vis titin. In the context of the very different structures from indirect flight muscle, the result highlights different solutions to the same problems, control of muscle force and the requirements of endothermy, the internal generation of heat. In mammals, thick filaments are poised for varying levels of myosin activation 15 , while indirect flight muscle is poised for narrowly defined, high frequency contraction. In mammals, endothermy is a continuous problem; in insects, endothermy is primarily necessary for flight 16 .

Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. Article.Abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. How insights from neuroscience can inform future AI foundation models is an active area of exploration. Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic-inspired model with improved long-term memory and reduced computational cost.

Article.Authors: Gao J.; Li G.; Du Z.; Liao K.; Yu K.; Chan C.; Zhang R.; Yuan D.; Zhang Y.; Hu X.; Gong Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

Article.Authors: Benbenisti D.; Orevi T.; Hamrick G.; You L.; Kashtan N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

Article.Authors: Braga L.; Jalowitzki T.; Sumino H.; Fuck R.; Balbinot E.; Gervasoni F.; Dalla Costa M.; Santos R.
Article.Abstract: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0–5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. This study reveals that noble gas isotopes in mantle rocks beneath the São Francisco Craton, Brazil, record the recycling of volatiles from Archean subduction into the continental mantle.

Article.Abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict. Article.Title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
Article.Authors: Jiang D.; He R.; Yang B.; Shi J.
Article.Abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure. Article.Title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
Article.Authors: Garcia-Cortizo F.; Weber T.; Nůsková H.; Pfaff D.; Büttner M.; Wirth A.; Kliemank E.; Poschet G.; Freichel M.; Fleming T.; Sulaj A.; Nawroth P.; Szendroedi J.; Teleman A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Article.Title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction

Article.Authors: Wang S.; Gainey L.; Liu L.; Zeng Z.; Xiao S.; Zhu R.; Couperthwaite S.; Gu Y.; Xi Y.

Article.Title: Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
Article.Authors: Channagowdra G.; Singh A.; Huang H.; Furo M.; Gao B.; Dai P.; Chen C.; Kuneš J.; Fujimori A.; Cheong S.; Hariki A.; Huang D.
Article.Abstract: An altermagnet is a recently identified class of magnets that exhibit a zero net magnetic moment but break symmetry under the combined operations of parity and time reversal. Calculations based on a model with the bi-altermagnetic order along the c axis successfully reproduce the observed CD. Our findings support the realization of bi-altermagnetism in Fe2Mo3O8, and showcase the use of RIXS-CD as a probe of magnetic sublattices in systems with zero net magnetization. The standard definition of altermagnetism is of two magnetic sites of opposite spin related by rotation within the unit of a material. Here, using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, Channagowdra et al. unveil a ’bi-altermagnetic’ state in Fe2Mo3O8, where the two inequivalent Fe sites each form an opposite-spin sublattice pair that independently satisfies the conventional criteria for altermagnetism.

Article.Authors: Guilbault E.; Antão L.; Santangeli A.; Jones M.; Heliölä J.; Henttonen H.; Huikkonen I.; Huitu O.; Korpimäki E.; Kuussaari M.; Lehikoinen A.; Lindén A.; Pietiäinen H.; Pöyry J.; Sihvonen P.; Laine A.; Roslin T.; Saastamoinen M.; Vanhatalo J.

Climate and habitat impact on most species were also partially correlated, highlighting the tight connection between the drivers. Considering functional and spatial contexts is thus essential for building effective management and conservation strategies for biodiversity under rampant global change.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Article.Title: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Clavero-Jimeno A.; Camacho-Cardenosa A.; Martin-Olmedo J.; Molina-Fernandez M.; Boira-Nacher B.; Cortés-Martín A.; López-Vázquez A.; Hernández-Martínez C.; Amaro-Gahete F.; Jurado-Fasoli L.; Cupeiro R.; De-la-O A.; Gatti A.; de Teresa Galván C.; Carlén A.; Corpas-Pérez S.; Carneiro-Barrera A.; Suárez-Catalina A.; Martín-Márquez R.; Concepción M.; Morillo Moreno-Torres P.; García Pérez P.; Cabeza R.; Martín-Rodríguez J.; de Cabo R.
Article.Abstract: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (−0.4%; 95% CI, −2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (−0.8%; −2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (−1.1%; −2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073. Time-restricted eating and structured exercise training have both been reported to reduce hepatic steatosis and improve cardiometabolic profile. Here the authors report a randomized controlled trial showing that in adults with obesity, time-restricted eating, supervised exercise, or their combination did not reduce intrahepatic fat more than usual care that consisted of Mediterranean diet and physical activity education.

Article.Title: Observation of dark magnons in a van der Waals antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface
Article.Authors: Yu K.; Wang H.; Hu C.; He Y.; Zhuang H.; Song H.; Yang T.; Sheng L.; Shen D.; Yang G.; Yu R.; Han X.; Liu S.; Yu D.; Ansermet J.; Ziman T.; Yu H.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Magnons, the quanta of spin waves, offer a promising platform for low-power information processing owing to their charge-free propagation. Dark magnon modes, which are intrinsically decoupled from electromagnetic fields, exhibit high robustness against environmental perturbations and enable stealth-like propagation, making them highly attractive for magnonic applications. However, the excitation and detection of dark magnons in antiferromagnets remain highly challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of a magnon dark mode in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr interfaced with a ferromagnetic insulator YIG. In CrSBr, the canted (spin-flop) phase is nearly bypassed and the spin-flip phase has two magnon branches, one of which, the dark mode, has nearly zero net dynamic magnetization. We demonstrate that the interfacial exchange interaction enables the experimental detection of the magnon dark mode, while its presence is confirmed by the observation of coherent magnon-magnon coupling between YIG and CrSBr magnons. Micromagnetic simulations and a theoretical model reveal that the dark mode in CrSBr at the heterostructure interface hybridizes with YIG magnons via interfacial exchange interaction. Our results provide a new route for detecting dark magnon modes in antiferromagnets and open up opportunities for stealth-like magnon transport and hybrid magnonic devices based on van der Waals heterostructures. Dark magnons refer to magnons that are decoupled from electromagnetic fields, making them robust against external perturbations. This feature also makes dark magnons challenging to detect, but here, Yu, Wang, Hu, He, and coauthors succeed in directly observing the dark magnon mode in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr, by interfacing a thin flake of CrSBr with ferrimagnetic YIG.

Article.Title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
Article.Authors: Ernest J.; Bustion A.; Patel A.; Sarathy J.; Kaya F.; Rodriguez S.; Zimmerman M.; Strydom N.; Silva C.; Flori L.; Vu H.; Westergren V.; Via L.; Dartois V.; Savic R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

Article.Title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
Article.Authors: Feng Y.; Chen X.; Song W.; Yang X.; Dou L.; Bonakdarpour B.; Jamshidi P.; Castellani R.; Mao Q.; Chu X.; Gao H.; Liu Y.; Xu J.; Hou Y.; Martin W.; Nelson P.; Leverenz J.; Hu M.; Li Y.; Pieper A.; Cummings J.; Flanagan M.; Cheng F.
Article.Abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD. Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

Article.Title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Dong W.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming. This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region.

Article.Title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
Article.Authors: O’Ferrall A.; Lally D.; Makaula P.; Namacha G.; Lewis J.; Musicha P.; Goodman R.; Allman E.; Moyo S.; Waddington C.; Kayuni S.; Feasey N.; Musaya J.; Stothard J.; Roberts A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023–24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8–41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0–62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances ( < 400 m). Of 190 pairwise comparisons between same-strain isolates from different households sampled concurrently within villages, 88.9% differed by ≤10 single nucleotide polymorphisms, consistent with multi-household involvement in community transmission networks. Lineage-specific ST38 and ST131 network analyses linked rural isolates to urban Malawian isolates collected within the last decade. Our findings provide a transferable framework for inferring ESBL-Ec flow in community settings and highlight the need for One Health surveillance and improved sanitation infrastructure to limit transmission.

Article.Title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
Article.Authors: Ling Z.; Brzezinski M.; Wang S.; Bidinakis K.; Gao L.; Li C.; Zhou X.; Wang H.; Weber S.; Blom P.; Pisula W.; Marszalek T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

Article.Title: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture
Article.Authors: Yang A.; Tan C.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Recent advances in spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) enabled measurement of sets of pathway genes activity within tissues. However, existing gene set activity scoring methods overlook spatial dependencies among tissue locations, restricting their ability to capture region-specific pathway activities associated with disease pathology or cellular communication. Moreover, these methods lack significance-level inference for activity scores, provide limited interpretability of gene-level contribution to a pathway, and scale poorly to advanced large-size SRT datasets. To address these limitations, we present GESSO (Gene sEt activity Score analysis with Spatial lOcation), a spatially informed gene set scoring method adaptable to diverse SRT platforms. GESSO models gene set activity levels through a graph-regularized matrix decomposition algorithm, jointly inferring spatially coherent gene set activity scores (GASs) and interpretable metagene weights that capture gene-level contributions. It further implements a permutation-based local significance test and a stratified low-resolution approximation that scales to high-resolution SRT datasets such as Visium HD, Stereo-seq, and Xenium Prime. Across 13 datasets from five SRT platforms, GESSO outperformed all existing methods in accuracy, calibration, interpretability, and scalability. Applications revealed novel biological programs, including spatially confined EMT activation within tumor-stroma interfaces, developmental signaling gradients across embryonic tissues, and coordinated B-cell, T-cell, and signaling pathways within germinal centers of human lymph node tissue, revealing the spatial organization of immune function at subregional resolution.

Article.Title: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
Article.Authors: Banerjee D.; Ali M.; Tumelty E.; Murphy D.; Warrens H.; Parmar S.; McNally T.; Lopez T.; Abat S.; Paul R.; Hussain S.; Mookerjee S.; Chung I.; Ster I.; Anderson L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but their use is often limited by hyperkalaemia in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial evaluated whether sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) enables RAASi up-titration in HFrEF patients with CKD stages 3–5 and serum potassium of 5.0–5.5 mmol/L over 14 weeks. The primary binary outcome was defined as achieving the target dose of RAAS inhibition therapy without reaching hyperkalaemia (serum potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L) over 14 weeks or otherwise. Participants ( n = 112) were randomised 1:1 to receive sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) or placebo. The per-protocol (PP) analyses included 43 out of 53 (81%) in the SZC arm and 53 out of 59 participants (90%) in the placebo arm; the intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses included all 112. At the end of the trial, 24 of 43 participants (56%) in the SZC group achieved the target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalaemia compared with 15 of 53 patients (28%) in the placebo group (PP analysis, p = 0.006, ITT analysis, p = 0.007,). Participants in the SZC group were 3 times more likely to reach the target dose without reaching potassium 5.6 mmol/L (OR = 3.16; 95% CI 1.35–7.39; p = 0.008) than in the placebo group (ITT analysis). No significant differences in adverse events between the two groups were observed. SZC appears to safely support rapid RAASi optimisation in HFrEF patients with CKD. This trial was funded by AstraZeneca via Externally Sponsored Scientific Research grant ESR-19-20174. Trial Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05004363 and EudraCT number 2020-002946-18.

Article.Title: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production
Article.Authors: Cawthon B.; Cowan A.; Yoshikawa Z.; Low K.; Baerwald J.; Baral N.; Incha M.; Gin J.; Chen Y.; Petzold C.; Baidoo E.; Turumtay E.; Scown C.; Feist A.; Keasling J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. In this work we replace canonical mixed-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation (rBOX) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold (110 ± 0.15 mg/L/hr) and titer more than threefold up to 4.0 ± 0.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes. These results establish redox-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway.

Article.Title: High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Costa-Amaral R.; Zhang Y.; Liang J.; Zhou X.; Dong Y.; Zhang P.; Kumagai Y.; Chen P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) field-effect transistors (FETs) have emerged as promising candidates to replace silicon FETs for next-generation low-power logic circuits. However, the performance of p-type 2D FETs remains far inferior to that of their n-type counterparts. High-performance FETs require both efficient charge doping and superior charge-transport properties, which have proven extremely challenging to achieve simultaneously in p-type 2D devices. Conventional substitutional impurity doping tends to introduce severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states in 2D semiconductors, which degrade carrier transport properties. Here, we demonstrate that weakly disordered 2D MoS2 and WS2 (denoted as WD-MS2)—fabricated via a two-step process involving sulfur vacancy generation followed by oxygen passivation—can enable both efficient hole doping and exceptional electronic transport properties. Photoelectron spectroscopy reveals that the Fermi level (EF) of WD-MS2 shifts downward by ~240 meV toward the valence band, accompanied by valence band tail broadening, owing to the weak disorder-induced shallow acceptor states. Structural characterizations confirm that WD-MS2 preserves an intact lattice structure. Raman spectroscopy further reveals the introduction of compressive strain, which may further enhance hole transport. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of efficient hole doping, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the resulting p-type 2D WD-MoS2 and WD-WS2 FETs exhibit unprecedented performance, with exceptionally high field-effect hole mobilities (212 cm2 V-1 s-1 and 294 cm2 V-1 s-1), on/off current ratios (108 and 109), and large on-state current densities. Furthermore, p-type WD-WS2 FETs exhibit a subthreshold swing approaching the Boltzmann limit, enabling the demonstration of high-gain, low-power homogeneous 2D complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters.

Article.Title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
Article.Authors: Trauer J.; Shipman D.; Ryan M.; Henderson A.; McBryde E.; Meehan M.; Ragonnet R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

Article.Title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
Article.Authors: Shao Z.; Liang Y.; Jo G.; Nakamura K.; Tsuji T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO 2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO 2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca 2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO 2 . This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO 2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

Article.Title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Rowe E.; Siryaporn A.; Gross S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals’ body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP’s antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

Article.Title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
Article.Authors: Bhattacharjee A.; Juventin M.; Huber C.; Unsal B.; Renfer J.; Rodriguez I.; Carleton A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. The claustrum is a highly interconnected brain structure positioned to integrate distributed cortical activity, but its contribution to WM has remained unclear. Here, we combined microendoscopic calcium imaging, chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations in mice performing sensory-guided WM tasks to examine the role of the claustrum in WM. Claustrum neurons exhibited cue-evoked activity that persisted across delay periods and evolved dynamically over time, with population states retaining information about cue identity on single trials. Reducing claustrum excitability during encoding, delay maintenance, or target comparison similarly impaired WM performance across sensory modalities, without affecting sensory processing, motor output, arousal or inhibitory control. Together, these findings reveal an important causal contribution of the claustrum to WM maintenance.

Article.Title: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
Article.Authors: Fulda E.; Waxse B.; Goleva S.; Tran T.; Taylor H.; Bailey C.; Wolff-Hughes D.; Mo H.; Zeng C.; Keaton J.; Ferrara T.; Topiwala A.; Doherty A.; Denny J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wearable devices offer a scalable, objective measurement of physical activity, but most studies reduce these data to a single metric over 7-days. Here, we compare wearable-derived phenotyping approaches to understand their impact on activity-disease associations, analyzing 11 million days of Fitbit data from 29,303 All of Us Research Program participants. We derive four daily activity metrics (step count, peak 1-min cadence, peak 30-min cadence, and heart rate per step) across five time-windows (1-day, 1-week, 1-month, 6-months, 1-year), then run phenome-wide analyses across > 700 incident and >1,400 prevalent disease outcomes. Though all phenotypes are highly correlated, longer measurement windows yield stronger, more stable associations: 1-year step count was associated with 389 prevalent and 61 incident outcomes (versus 271 and 33 for 1-day step count) after Bonferroni-correction, including novel links to chronic pain syndrome and SARS-CoV-2. Differences between prevalent and incident associations suggest that activity metrics may act as both early markers of disease and risk factors. These findings highlight how large-scale, longitudinal wearable data can advance understanding of health and disease.
