Article.Title: Fatigue links sociodemographic risk to pain intensity and spread in 2 surgical cohorts
Article.Authors: Sun M.; Ansari B.; Clauw D.; Harris R.; Sluka K.; Kaplan C.; Brummet C.; Lindquist M.; Wager T.; N/A N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Why some surgical patients develop pain that extends beyond the original site of injury while others do not remains poorly understood. The recently proposed Risk of Pain Spread (ROPS) framework integrates multiple psychosocial risk factors associated with widespread pain, but its generalizability to surgical populations has not been established. Using 2 large presurgical cohorts of participants undergoing total knee arthroplasty or thoracic surgery, we evaluated the generalizability of the ROPS framework and examined relationships among psychosocial and sociodemographic factors, surgical-site pain, nonsurgical-site pain, and widespread pain using complementary latent-variable, regression, Bayesian network, and mediation analyses. Across cohorts and analytical approaches, fatigue emerged as the most consistent correlate of pain outcomes, independent of other measured risk factors. Fatigue also occupied a central position within the conditional dependency structure of psychosocial and pain variables and accounted for substantial shared variance linking sleep disturbance, depressive symptoms, neuroticism, adverse childhood experiences, and socioeconomic disadvantage with pain intensity. Nonsurgical-site pain consistently occupied a position linking pain intensity with widespread pain across complementary analyses. Together, these findings externally validate the ROPS framework in clinically relevant surgical populations and identify fatigue as a central correlate linking biopsychosocial vulnerability with pain burden.

Article.Title: Astrocyte Orai1 signaling promotes spinal excitatory synaptic potentiation and neuropathic pain after nerve injury in male mice
Article.Authors: Tsujikawa S.; Shetti A.; Grant R.; Novakovic M.; Prakriya M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neuropathic pain after peripheral nerve injury is a multifactorial condition mediated partly by inflammation in the spinal cord that results in potentiation of excitatory synaptic transmission in nociceptive circuits. Glial cells including astrocytes are key mediators of the underlying inflammation, but the signaling checkpoints that regulate astrocyte-driven spinal cord inflammation and sensitization of nociceptive circuits are not well understood. Here, we identify Orai1-mediated store-operated Ca 2+ entry (SOCE) as an important regulator of spinal astrocyte cytokine production, metabolic reprogramming, and pain hypersensitivity in mice. Conditional deletion of Orai1 in astrocytes attenuated mechanical allodynia after nerve injury in male but not female mice, despite comparable SOCE suppression in both sexes. Orai1 deficiency also attenuated production of proinflammatory cytokines after SOCE activation, including TNFα, IL-6, and IL-33, both in vivo and in vitro. Electrophysiological recordings revealed that astrocyte Orai1 deletion prevented injury-induced enhancement of glutamatergic synaptic transmission in dorsal horn neurons, linking astrocytic Ca 2+ signaling to central sensitization. Metabolomic profiling showed that Orai1 loss disrupted glycolysis and TCA cycle intermediates while promoting accumulation of immunomodulatory metabolites such as itaconate, consistent with a less inflammatory astrocyte metabolic state. These findings identify Orai1 channels as integrators of astrocyte Ca 2+ signaling, immunometabolism, and excitatory synaptic potentiation after nerve injury, and identify a sexually dimorphic astrocyte mechanism governing neuropathic pain pathogenesis. Targeting astrocyte Orai1 channels may provide a selective therapeutic strategy for male-predominant chronic pain.

Article.Title: Mineralocorticoid receptor signaling reduces somatostatin expression in developing sensory neurons and drives neonatal pain after early-life stress
Article.Authors: Eid F.; Serafin E.; Muniz M.; Woodke S.; Booher J.; Zhang J.; Baccei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early-life stress (ELS) causes pain hypersensitivity in neonatal mice and alters the transcriptional profile of the immature dorsal root ganglia (DRG), highlighted by a marked reduction in the expression of a neuropeptide, somatostatin (Sst), which is known to constitutively suppress peripheral nociceptive transmission during adulthood. However, the mechanisms that drive plasticity in gene expression within the developing DRG and neonatal pain after ELS remain unclear. Here, we investigated the degree to which ELS-induced neonatal pain was mediated by corticosterone signaling onto sensory neurons and potential changes in peripheral Sst transmission. The conditional knockout of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), but not the glucocorticoid receptor, from immature DRG neurons prevented ELS-evoked neonatal pain. In contrast, the systemic administration of the selective MR antagonist eplerenone failed to acutely influence pain after ELS, thus suggesting that MR activation enhances pain during the neonatal period via canonical effects on gene transcription. Meanwhile, hind paw injection of the Sst receptor antagonist cyclo-somatostatin increased spontaneous nocifensive behaviors in control pups, but not in pups previously subjected to ELS, raising the possibility that a disruption in tonic antinociception mediated by peripheral Sst contributes to neonatal pain after ELS. Furthermore, administration of the peripherally restricted Sst analog octreotide reversed noxious cold and pressure hypersensitivity in neonatal mice after ELS. Finally, the selective deletion of MR from sensory neurons prevented the ELS-induced decrease in Sst expression. Collectively, these results provide novel mechanistic insight into the effects of chronic early-life adversity on nociceptive processing in the developing nervous system.

Article.Title: Targeting GPR183 to reduce peripheral sensitization: evidence from rodent and human tissue analyses
Article.Authors: Oberkrom K.; Braden K.; Li E.; Shah S.; Maric D.; Mannes A.; Pacifico P.; Jayaraj N.; Arnatt C.; Menichella D.; Sapio M.; Salvemini D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral sensitization is a key process in the development of painful inflammatory conditions, driven in part by immune-cell mediator release following tissue injury. The G protein–coupled receptor, GPR183, predominantly expressed on immune cells, regulates their migration, positioning, and mediator production. However, its role in peripheral sensitization and the specific immune cells involved remains insufficiently understood. In rats, intraplantar injection of 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), the most potent endogenous GPR183 ligand, produced long-lasting nociception that was prevented by the selective GPR183 antagonist SAE-14. We found that both isoforms influence this response, independent of cyclooxygenases. In a well-characterized rat incisional injury model, GPR183 protein expression increased in injured paw tissue, and SAE-14 reversed hypersensitivity. Meta-analysis of human postsurgical skin samples similarly showed elevated GPR183 expression and transcriptional changes favoring 7α,25-OHC production after injury. We identified macrophages, Langerhans cells (LCs), and T cells as the principal GPR183 -expressing cell types in human skin. Ablation of LCs and removal of mature B and T cells revealed that 7α,25-OHC-evoked hypersensitivity does not depend on these cell types, leaving GPR183 + macrophages as the most likely drivers of GPR183-induced hypersensitivity. Overall, our findings define the cellular and molecular pathways linking GPR183 to peripheral sensitization and highlight GPR183 antagonism as a promising strategy for pain management.

Article.Title: Mechanisms of behavioral activation, cognitive therapy, and mindfulness meditation for chronic pain: a test of specific vs shared mechanism models in a randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Day M.; Ward L.; Borckardt J.; Burns J.; Newman A.; Ehde D.; Chan J.; Reed D.; Friedly J.; Thorn B.; Mendoza M.; Drever S.; Jensen M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study tested hypotheses regarding the mechanisms of 3 psychological chronic pain treatments: behavioral activation, cognitive therapy, and mindfulness meditation. The aim was to evaluate the degree to which improvement in the primary outcome (pain interference) was accounted for by preceding changes in cognitive content (pain catastrophizing), cognitive process (mindful nonjudgment), and/or behavior (activity level) during treatment (Primary Aim) and after treatment (Secondary Aim). A total of 302 adults with chronic low back pain were enrolled in a 3-arm parallel randomized clinical trial and completed twice daily ecological momentary assessments of outcome and hypothesized mechanism variables. Participants also wore an activity monitor daily during and after treatment. Slopes were calculated for 4 phases (early treatment, late treatment, early post-treatment, late post-treatment), and analyses of variance were conducted. Structural equation modeling evaluated potential cross-lagged effects. The analyses of variance results showed significant improvement in pain interference, pain catastrophizing, and nonjudgment, but not activity level, with no between treatment differences. The structural equation modeling analyses testing the potential mechanism role of pain catastrophizing and nonjudgment during treatment and after treatment mostly found nonsignificant cross-lagged effects, although changes in outcome and mechanism were significantly correlated at nearly all time periods. Taken together, the strongest support was found for a Shared Mechanisms Model to explain how 3 theoretically unique treatments exert change both during and after treatment. The findings are among the first to delineate the potential mechanisms underlying the variability in post-treatment trajectories of maintenance vs relapse after psychological chronic pain treatment.

Article.Title: Pain education in Brazilian medical schools: a national curriculum analysis
Article.Authors: Silva T.; Domingues F.; Medeiros D.; Gandolfi A.; Reis F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, yet undergraduate medical education remains insufficient to prepare future physicians for its assessment and management. The International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) has proposed a competency-based curriculum framework; however, its implementation in Brazilian medical education is unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the availability of pain education in Brazilian medical schools and assess its alignment with the IASP Curriculum Outline on Pain for Medicine. We conducted a national cross-sectional documentary analysis of all medical schools registered in the Brazilian Ministry of Education database between May 2024 and December 2025. Institutional websites were systematically screened for publicly available curricular documentation, and data were independently extracted by 2 reviewers. Variables included the presence of pain-related content, existence of a dedicated pain course, course workload, timing within the curriculum, and type of offering. Among 447 identified schools, 277 (62.0%) provided accessible curricular information. Only 47 institutions (16.9%) offered a stand-alone pain course, and 29 had detailed syllabi for item-level analysis. Most analyzed courses were mandatory and delivered in the early years of training. Alignment with IASP competencies was incomplete across all domains, with greater coverage of neurobiological and pharmacological content and limited inclusion of pain assessment and measurement, psychosocial and behavioral management, public health, ethics, and care for special populations. Pain education in Brazil is inconsistently structured and only partially aligned with international recommendations, indicating the need of comprehensive, competency-based curricular reform.

Article.Title: The analgesic efficacy of opioids in different application modalities for the treatment of breakthrough cancer pain—a systematic review with network meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Dinges H.; Thiedmann S.; Weyland J.; Volberg C.; Schmitt F.; Wulf H.; Schubert A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breakthrough cancer pain episodes often require oral immediate release opioids or parenteral opioid treatment. Different formulations and application modalities have been approved for this condition. This study aimed to identify the most effective of the available substances and applications to treat breakthrough cancer pain. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review with network meta-analysis. The database search included MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Embase, and Web of Science. Eligible were randomized controlled trials comparing opioids and application modalities for the treatment of breakthrough cancer pain episodes. Primary end points were the pain intensity difference (PID) at 15 and 30 minutes. Secondary end points were side effects and adverse events, as well as dichotomous outcomes of treatment success. Frequentist network meta-analysis was conducted using the package netmeta in R. From 5133 records initially identified by the literature review, 23 studies were eligible for quantitative analysis. Compared with placebo, the most effective interventions at 15 minutes (PID) were intravenous or subcutaneous applications of morphine, and intranasal fentanyl or sublingual fentanyl tablets. After 30 minutes (PID), the most effective interventions were still subcutaneous and intravenous morphine, but also sublingual fentanyl tablets. Intranasal fentanyl spray was equally effective as buccal and other transmucosal applications by 30 minutes. The quality of evidence on the topic is poor as most studies are phase III trials for drug approval. The risk of publication bias is therefore high. Sublingual fentanyl tablets were as effective as intravenous or subcutaneous morphine and are a practical modality for self-administration.

Article.Title: The sympathoadrenal contribution to inferior vena cava formation
Article.Authors: Murashima A.; Matsumaru D.; Moriguchi T.; Shima Y.; Inoue M.; Yokoyama C.; Morohashi K.; Kubota Y.; Ueki T.; Hitomi J.; Isogai S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although vascular development is fundamental during embryogenesis, the developmental basis and tissue interactions underlying anatomical variation in major veins are not fully understood. The renal segment of the inferior vena cava exhibits significant anatomical variations that often affect the safety of retroperitoneal surgery. Using mouse embryos, we show that the renal segment of the inferior vena cava is not primarily dependent on the subcardinal vein as classically proposed, but instead forms from a vascular plexus closely associated with the developing para-aortic ridge. Genetic models further indicate that sympathoadrenal development in the para-aortic ridge contributes to the proper organization and remodeling of this vascular network. This revised developmental framework highlights a sympathoadrenal–vascular coupling as a developmental basis for inferior vena cava formation and thereby challenges classical subcardinal vein-dependent models.

Article.Title: Corticosteroid treatment dysregulates perirhinal circadian rhythms and synaptic function in rats
Article.Authors: Claydon M.; Troy O.; Birnie M.; Kershaw Y.; Barker G.; Heesom K.; Warburton E.; Bortolotto Z.; Lightman S.; Conway-Campbell B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glucocorticoids regulate the stress response, circadian rhythms, and numerous physiological processes, including cognition, cardiovascular function, metabolism, and immunity. Synthetic glucocorticoids (sGCs), such as methylprednisolone (MPL), are widely prescribed for inflammatory and autoimmune disorders, yet their often severe cognitive side effects remain poorly understood. Here, we examine the impact of chronic MPL treatment on circadian regulation and the synaptic proteome in the perirhinal cortex (PRh) of male rats, a region critical for object recognition memory. We find that corticosteroid signaling in the PRh is subject to circadian modulation across the light–dark cycle, and that MPL disrupts this pattern. MPL alters endogenous circadian and ultradian clock gene expression, and proteomic analyses reveals dysregulation of proteins essential for synaptic transmission and plasticity. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrate impaired synaptic signaling, and behavioral testing shows PRh-dependent novel object recognition deficits. These findings highlight a mechanistic link between sGC treatment, circadian disruption, and cognitive impairment, with broad implications for understanding the cognitive side effects of widely used sGC therapies.

Article.Authors: Stoinski L.; Konkle T.; Hebart M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Occipitotemporal cortex (OTC) is known to support visual object processing, yet identifying general principles underlying its coarse-scale functional organization remains challenging. Previously proposed organizational dimensions, such as animacy or real-world size, may not generalize to more diverse, naturalistic stimuli and strong intercorrelations of object properties complicate determining which dimensions, if any, dominate OTC organization. We addressed these challenges through detailed analyses of the cortical topography underlying 15 object properties, using fMRI responses to thousands of natural images, focusing on animacy and size given their established prominence. Our results confirm many characteristics of the purported animacy-size organization, but reveal distinctions that challenge dominant notions of this organization, highlighting the importance of generalizing to large-scale naturalistic data. Beyond animacy and size, many properties could alternatively serve as organizational dimensions, yet none emerges as clearly dominant throughout OTC. Together, our findings reveal a more refined animacy-size organization than previously assumed and highlight challenges of assigning individual principles to account for OTC organization.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic biomarkers reveal jasmonic and salicylic acid states under field herbivory in Arabidopsis thaliana
Article.Authors: Tomita A.; Maeda T.; Mori-Moriyama N.; Nomura Y.; Kurita Y.; Kashima M.; Betsuyaku S.; Sato Y.; Nagano A.
Article.Abstract: Plants coordinate defence against pathogens and herbivores through the crosstalk between salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) signalling pathways. Leveraging these data, we develop and validate machine-learning-based transcriptomic biomarkers that independently measure the SA and JA response states from gene-expression data. Applying these biomarkers to field-grown A. thaliana shows that SA/JA response states are associated with the abundance and co-occurrence patterns of herbivores on individual plants. Our study provides a strategy for decoding hormonal responses to biotic environments from field transcriptomes, bridging the gap between molecular signalling and ecological dynamics.

Lunar regolith simulant LMS-1 shows particularly strong barrier-damaging and inflammatory effects in differentiated bronchial epithelial cells and in the in vivo mouse model. Article.Title: DECTIN1+ myeloid-derived suppressor cells mediate therapeutic effect of MSCs in haplo-HSCT for severe aplastic anemia
Article.Authors: Yu F.; Jia G.; Li P.; Xia S.; Hao R.; Wang H.; Liu D.; Zhu H.; Ding L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a life-threatening bone marrow failure disorder marked by pancytopenia and marrow hypoplasia. Here, we demonstrated that haplo-HSCT significantly restored the proportion and immunosuppressive capacity of bone marrow myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in SAA patients, and DECTIN1 + MDSCs emerged as central immunoregulators. MSC coinfusion further enhanced this effect. Mechanistically, MSC-derived exosomal ANXA2 upregulated DECTIN1 expression in MDSCs, which in turn activated STAT3 signaling to increase TNFAIP3 expression, thereby suppressing inflammatory T-cell responses. These changes were also reflected in peripheral blood. Human bone marrow organoid experiments confirmed that MSC coinfusion promoted DECTIN1 + MDSC expansion and accelerated bone marrow microenvironment recovery. Our findings revealed a previously unrecognized MSC-mediated mechanism and highlighted DECTIN1 + MDSCs as key immunoregulatory mediators and potential therapeutic targets in SAA.

Article.Title: IDR acquisition from human ortholog reprograms Snf11 to form HDAC-compartmentalizing condensates and drives yeast flocculation
Article.Authors: Cheng Y.; Han T.; Xin Y.; Zhang W.; Zhang J.; Zhang Y.; Han Z.; Hu Z.; Jia X.; Long J.; Xie J.; Zhao K.
Article.Abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates protein function by organizing proteins into dynamic condensates, yet how divergence in LLPS among orthologs gives rise to species-specific functional outputs remains poorly understood. These condensates activate the adhesion genes FLO1 and FLO11 , triggering calcium-dependent flocculation absent in wild-type cells. Mechanistically, Snf11-QPGY sequesters histone deacetylase subunit Rpd3 within condensates, reducing its occupancy at FLO promoters and promoting histone acetylation and transcriptional activation. Substituting QPGY with a heterologous LLPS-competent IDR restores condensate formation but does not recapitulate QPGY-driven transcriptional-phenotypic outputs. These findings reveal how evolutionary diversification of IDR sequences drives functional divergence among orthologs and offer a framework for engineering IDR-dependent regulatory modules.

Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Xu J.; Li S.; Yi W.; Xiao L.; Li J.; Feng F.; Zhang B.; Yang X.

This comprehensive study elucidates the role of SCO in stress response and mood regulation through a novel regulatory axis: the SCO-CSF-barrier axis.

Article.Title: Acquired resistance to vorinostat in cutaneous T cell lymphoma involves augmented ERK phosphorylation
Article.Authors: Kizhakeyil A.; Poh Z.; Wong B.; Tan J.; Bluethgen S.; Kok Y.; Bi X.; Taib N.; Huang D.; Ong C.; Lim S.; Kelleher D.; Tan S.; Grigoropoulos N.; Verma N.
Article.Abstract: Background: Vorinostat is the first approved histone deacetylase inhibitor used in many countries for treating advanced cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). Article.Abstract: We present a mother machine-like microfluidic device tailored for high-throughput, long-term tracking of non-adherent T-cell proliferation via live-cell microscopy. Article.Authors: Yang X.; Qin J.; Xiong X.; Zhu J.; Zhang J.; Wang Y.; Qi Y.
Article.Abstract: Handwriting Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) offer a direct brain-to-text pathway, holding significant promise for neural rehabilitation. However, existing research has primarily focused on alphabetic languages. Unlike the sequential nature of alphabetic handwriting, logographic characters like Chinese incorporate complex spatial structures that embed semantic information, presenting a greater challenge for neural decoding. To address this, we propose Brain-Writing-BERT, a novel BCI framework that learns the structural semantic priors from logographic characters to facilitate decoding. We evaluate our system with a clinical participant in Chinese character decoding tasks. All clinical and experimental procedures were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ref.ChiCTR2100050705, date of registration: 03/09/2021, registry name: Research on Brain-Computer Interfaces for Individuals with High Cervical Spinal Paraplegia). Article.Authors: Patil M.; Sharma A.; Pandey P.; Irulappan V.; Acharya K.; Kandpal M.; Qamar A.; Verma P.; Ranjan A.; Senthil-Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Co-occurring abiotic and biotic stresses can have negative or positive interactions with plants. Article.Authors: Ebisu I.; Tanaka T.; Kawasaki Y.; Murakoshi S.; Shibata K.; Kato Y.; Konno M.; Bondar A.; Shihoya W.; Inoue K.; Nureki O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Schizorhodopsins (SzRs) are light-driven inward proton pumps found in Asgard archaea, contrasting with most microbial rhodopsins that export protons. Thermostability also diverges: Mt SzR relies on proline-rich loops and electrostatic interactions, while M sSzR achieves stability through reinforced trimerization and extensive interhelical aromatic packing. Structural and mutational analyses highlight the adaptability of SzRs and provide a framework for engineering robust photoreceptors for optogenetics and synthetic biology.

Article.Authors: Chen X.; Lin J.; Ning P.; Liu D.; Zhang R.; Chi Z.; Zeng Y.; Yu Z.; Yu S.; Yang S.

Article.Authors: Deshpande M.; Xing J.; Gumerov V.; Dunleavy R.; Castillo H.; Crane B.; Zhulin I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract PAS domains often bind cofactors, whereas related Cache domains are thought to function exclusively as ligand-binding modules. Article.Title: Dynamic climate and ecological expansion drive body morphology evolution in fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Fang Z.; Liu B.; Ding Z.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Cephalopods originated in the Cambrian approximately 500 million years ago, evolving from externally shelled ancestors to forms with diverse morphologies. Despite their morphological diversity, the macroevolutionary patterns and drivers of their diversification remain incompletely understood. We identify five peaks in morphological diversification, indicating rapid evolutionary phases during historical periods. Morphological disparity exhibits a time-lagged response to evolutionary rate shifts. Sea surface temperature and ecological factors are macroevolutionary drivers shaping evolutionary rates and morphological disparity. Major environmental perturbations, including the end-Permian and end-Triassic mass extinctions and Early Triassic and Toarcian hyperthermal events, are associated with reduced evolutionary rates, whereas post-Cretaceous conditions correspond to elevated rates driven by ecological release and adaptive radiation. Our results show that cephalopod morphological evolution is governed by coupled environmental and ecological processes that structure evolutionary dynamics over deep time.

Article.Authors: Li J.; Bai Z.; Yang R.; Liu Y.; Lian B.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer often returns or spreads after treatment, and therapies that can destroy tumors while also engaging the immune system are urgently needed. Article.Title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
Article.Authors: Pogorevc N.; Upadhyay M.; Simčič M.; Sandoval-Castellanos E.; Horvat S.; Medugorac I.

However, some regions show signatures compatible with balancing selection. Overall, our results show that hybridization between domestic and wild Capra is biologically possible, that most shared haplotypes likely predate domestication, and highlight the importance of distinguishing introgression from balancing selection when interpreting shared genomic variation across species.

Article.Title: Predicting discrete traits in evolving systems
Article.Authors: Prall J.; Surya K.; Bender E.; Feigin L.; Meade A.; Organ C.
Article.Abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. Predictions using discrete data are central to imputation, forecasting, and hypothesis testing in biology. Here, using accuracy and log loss, we benchmark these models across scenarios varying in tree size, evolutionary rate, and trait coevolution. Against non-phylogenetic baselines, they increase accuracy by 23 percentage points and lower log loss by 92% on average; different Markov implementations perform similarly. Log loss rises as terminal branch lengths elongate, a direct consequence of the Markov process. Last, we provide a tutorial and empirical demonstration for the evolution of unexpected character states (outliers). Our study provides a framework for imputing missing data, reconstructing ancestral traits, and testing evolutionary hypotheses.

Article.Title: Genomic taxonomy reveals distinct evolutionary architectures within the Enterobacter cloacae complex
Article.Authors: Liao Y.; Chen F.; Liou C.; Li Y.; Cheng H.; Lin C.; Wu H.; Liu P.
Article.Abstract: The Enterobacter cloacae complex is a major nosocomial pathogen group, yet its taxonomy remains poorly resolved below the species level, obscuring the evolutionary drivers of virulence and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show, by analyzing 254 clinical isolates from Taiwan alongside 6,493 public genomes, that a genome-resolved taxonomic framework corrects taxonomic assignments for 54.9% of public genomes, primarily by resolving Enterobacter hormaechei into its five subspecies. Subspecies-level resolution reveals two distinct evolutionary patterns. Virulence determinants and intrinsic resistance genes are strongly associated with subspecies identity and remain globally conserved, including near-universal carriage of the salmochelin locus in E. hormaechei subsp. steigerwaltii and strict linkage of chromosomal AmpC β-lactamases to specific species. By contrast, acquired carbapenemases show pronounced geographic variation independent of taxonomy. These findings demonstrate that subspecies represent the fundamental biological and epidemiological units within the Enterobacter cloacae complex and highlight the importance of subspecies-resolved genomics for diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and global surveillance.

Article.Title: Biofilm selection activates c-di-GMP synthesis by the bifunctional enzyme MbaA
Article.Authors: Lorentzen Ø.; Abel S.; Johnsen P.; Frøhlich C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing biofilm formation remains incomplete, limiting the development of targeted interventions against biofilm-associated infections. By selecting for Vibrio cholerae biofilms, we identified mutations in the polyamine-regulated, bifunctional enzyme MbaA that alter its enzymatic activity in metabolizing the conserved second messenger cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP). These mutations occur in both the c-di-GMP-producing GGDEF domain and the c-di-GMP-hydrolyzing EAL domain of MbaA. Mutagenesis and enzyme kinetic analyses revealed regulatory crosstalk between these domains, where mutations in either domain enhanced production of c-di-GMP by MbaA while concurrently reducing its hydrolytic activity. In the wild-type enzyme, c-di-GMP metabolism is post-translationally regulated by specific polyamines. Biofilm-selected mutations not only shift MbaA’s enzymatic activity but also disrupt this regulation, rendering the enzyme insensitive to external polyamine signaling. Our findings illustrate how evolutionary pressure can rewire existing enzymes, promoting a biofilm-associated lifestyle.

Article.Title: Early-life adversity induces social anxiety and cognitive deficits alongside neurobiological changes in rats
Article.Authors: Ham J.; Hong N.; Slobodian H.; Urlacher V.; Cantwell E.; Tong A.; Annor-Bediako J.; Hastie B.; Veltri M.; Montina T.; Iwaniuk A.; Pellis S.; McDonald R.
Article.Abstract: Mood disorders such as anxiety often originate early in life, yet rodent models of early-life adversity are typically assessed only in adulthood using a limited array of behavioral assays. Here we show how neonatal isolation affects social behavior, learning and memory, neuron structure, and blood metabolites in Long Evans rats ( Rattus norvegicus ). Juvenile isolated rats play less with unfamiliar peers but interact typically with cage mates, consistent with a social anxiety-like phenotype. As adults, isolated rats show reduced cooperation and increased aggression, whereas traditional anxiety tests do not reveal increased generalized anxiety. Females show pronounced cognitive and motivational deficits. Isolation is also associated with reduced dendritic spine density in the medial prefrontal cortex, sex-specific neuronal changes in the dorsolateral septum, and shifts in glucose and amino acid metabolism. Together, these findings reveal selective, sex-dependent consequences of early-life social deprivation across behavioral, neural, and metabolic domains.

Article.Title: Canonical correlation analysis identifies single nucleotide polymorphism combinations and gene expression associated with membranous nephropathy
Article.Authors: Osborne A.; Hayward S.; Colby E.; Andag U.; Kalra P.; Koziell A.; Radresa O.; Skroblin P.; Taal M.; Welsh G.; Saleem M.; Campbell C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In membranous nephropathy (MN), an autoimmune kidney condition, univariate genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified Human Leucocyte Antigen ( HLA ) and M-type phospholipase A2 receptor ( PLA2R1 ) genetic risk variants. Multivariate-single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) canonical correlation analysis (CCA) with transcriptomics analysis, can uncover additional insights within this context. We applied CCA to our National Unified Renal Translational Research Enterprise (NURTuRE)- chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Salford Kidney Study (SKS) European datasets, identifying 1095 HLA and 46 PLA2R1 SNPs showing significant MN correlation, and single-cell gene enrichment. Top SNP combinations showed greater significance in both MN by multivariate-SNP CCA, and MN and diabetic nephropathy (Type 1) by allele frequency analysis compared to healthy and non-MN groups. ATF6B , C2, CYP21A2 , and HLA-DRB1 colocalised with top HLA SNPs and showed significant differential expression in MN (published immune transcriptomics datasets). HLA-DQB1, HLA-DRB5 and RNF5 showed significant differential expression with lead SNP genotype status in MN and CKD. These previously unreported SNP and gene results are candidates for MN and potentially Type 1 diabetic nephropathy risk prediction.

Article.Title: Susceptibility of Achromobacter spp. to bacteriophages and phage/antibiotic combinations
Article.Authors: Orlotti M.; Turki N.; Tourneur M.; Rani P.; Leonard J.; Kanhirun N.; Blanc A.; Su A.; Huang Y.; Koch G.; Pride Z.; Oh J.; Bates M.; Amamoto A.; Carrico V.; Serrano Buelna B.; Knight R.; Bradley J.; Conrad D.; Pogliano J.; Cobián Güemes A.; Pride D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Achromobacter infections pose significant challenges to people with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). It is a growing problem in people with CF because it is difficult to eliminate with antibiotics, leading to chronic lung infections that increasingly acquire antibiotic resistance. Here we identified a cadre of 26 bacteriophages that target clinical Achromobacter isolates. We tested these phages against a collection of 56 Achromobacter isolates and found that all were susceptible to multiple of these phages. We also evaluated whether we could restore the activity of certain antibiotics by using them as adjunctive therapy to phages in vitro. We found that when meropenem (a beta lactam antibiotic) was added to the phages, improved susceptibility (decreased MICs) was demonstrated in many isolates regardless of whether the Achromobacter was initially susceptible to meropenem. The data presented here suggests that combination therapy using meropenem with an active phage should be considered for treatment of Achromobacter infections regardless of pre-existing antibiotic susceptibility.

Article.Title: Melatonin regulates LIN-42/PERIOD through its receptor PCDR-1 to promote dark adaptation in Caenorhabditis elegans
Article.Authors: Duan J.; Tang X.; Du Y.; Luo Q.; Zhu Q.; Zou Y.; Ma Y.; Zou C.
Article.Abstract: Organisms that live in lightless spatial niches (e.g., caves or soil) develop a daily clock using other senses, such as taste, smell, temperature, or mechanical senses. However, how these organisms, which experience only muted daily environmental cycles, use a circadian clock to adapt to darkness is worth exploring. In this study, we found that lin-42 /PERIOD was highly expressed in worms grown in darkness. lin-42 knockdown induced a phenotype of accelerated aging in worms under dark conditions. Melatonin inhibited the production of reactive oxygen species through its receptor, PCDR-1, thus maintaining lin-42 expression in darkness. Conversely, daylight inhibited lin-42 expression by ROS production due to suppression of melatonin synthesis. Moreover, we found that insufficient melatonin synthesis or lin-42 deficiency activated the transcription factor DAF-16/FOXO, which induced lipid accumulation in the worms. Our results suggest that the molecular network composed of melatonin and the LIN-42/PERIOD enables C. elegans to adapt to darkness.

Article.Title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
Article.Authors: Cavalet-Giorsa E.; Wicker T.; Krattinger S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. Here, using k -mer-based approaches applied to a large diversity panel, we refine previous estimates of the geographical and temporal origins of the three known Ttbtr1 loss-of-function alleles and show that they emerged in distinct wild emmer subpopulations. For this, we generated a chromosome-scale dika wheat assembly carrying the recently discovered Ttbtr1-Ab allele. Our analyses reveal that the Ttbtr1-A alleles reside on an introgression from the southern judaicum wild emmer population into northern wild emmer wheat, providing an explanation for the long-standing debate about the Ttbtr1-A origin. We further demonstrate that the Ttbtr1-Aa and Ttbtr1-B alleles are already present in wild emmer wheat, with evidence indicating that they arose prior to the advent of agriculture. Together, these findings support a model in which key domestication genes in domesticated crops were selected and combined from standing genetic variation in wild relatives.

Article.Title: Directional blood flow within a shared capillary network links the nucleus of the solitary tract and area postrema in rats
Article.Authors: Carson K.; Roy R.; Stern J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS) and the area postrema (AP) form a tightly coupled dorsal medullary complex that integrates visceral and humoral signals governing autonomic and cardiometabolic regulation. While their neural interconnections are well characterized, the organization and functional significance of their shared vascular network remain poorly understood. Here, we used in vivo two-photon microscopy in rats, combined with fluorescent vascular labeling and retrograde neuronal tracing, to visualize and quantify blood flow within the AP–NTS microcirculation. We identified direct capillary connections between the two regions, confirming a continuous vascular network previously inferred from ex vivo studies. Analysis of red blood cell trajectories revealed that blood flow across these junctions is predominantly unidirectional, from the NTS toward the AP. Morphometric measurements showed that AP capillaries are nearly twice the diameter of those in the NTS, implying a lower local vascular resistance and providing a structural basis for this directionality. Despite these geometric differences, capillary flow velocities were similar between regions, consistent with active regulation that maintains stable perfusion dynamics. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized, functionally asymmetric vascular pathway within the dorsal medulla. By enabling the directed transfer of diffusible neurohumoral signals from the NTS to the AP, this specialized microvascular network adds a novel layer of communication between two key brainstem autonomic centers and may represent an additional mechanism for the integration of visceral and circulating information.

Article.Title: Nutrient-dependent bet-hedging between reproduction and sporulation in Bacillus subtilis
Article.Authors: Zhu M.; Wang Y.; Pei Y.; Liu Y.; Wang X.; Dai X.
Article.Abstract: To thrive in nature, bacteria must constantly balance growth with long-term survival in response to nutrient availability. Although sporulation in Bacillus subtilis is a classical survival strategy, how the sporulation program is regulated by nutrient conditions during exponential growth remains elusive. Here we show that the Spo0A-mediated sporulation program is strongly modulated during exponential phase across different carbon sources and is accompanied by pronounced population heterogeneity on poor carbons. We further identify the transition-state regulator AbrB as a key modulator that integrates growth and sporulation, promoting growth under favorable conditions while facilitating sporulation under poor nutrients. On good carbon sources, AbrB optimizes cellular resource allocation by directly suppressing the unnecessary expression of adaptive pathways. In contrast, on poor carbon sources, where the Spo0A-signaling pathway is strongly activated, AbrB promotes sporulation by repressing the expression of a plasmid-encoded Rap-family phosphatase gene, which otherwise interferes with the Spo0A signaling pathway. Together, these findings reveal a dual-control strategy that fine-tunes the trade-off between growth and survival and promotes bet-hedging under poor growth conditions, with important implications for both fundamental biology and synthetic biology.

Article.Title: Structural analysis of the specificity of three neutralising human monoclonal antibodies against poliovirus
Article.Authors: Bahar M.; Swanson J.; Zhou D.; Puligedda R.; Porta C.; Dessain S.; Macadam A.; Rowlands D.; Stonehouse N.; Fry E.; Stuart D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite a global eradication programme, pathogenic polioviruses (PVs) still circulate, dictating a need for improved vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics. Understanding their antigenic properties has been based largely on studies in mice. Here we study three human monoclonal antibodies specific for the native conformation and either PV1, 2 or 3, determining high-resolution structures of complexes with virus-like particles. The anti-PV1 and anti-PV2 Fabs bind around the icosahedral 3-fold axes, whilst the anti-PV3 Fab binds the canyon. We reveal the basis of serotype specificity and discrimination between native and expanded antigenic states. The anti-PV3 antibody partly penetrates the canyon and makes numerous serotype specific interactions on the south canyon face, distinguishing it from a pan-serotype and pan-antigenic state PV antibody. These structures show that human antibodies often span more than one classical antigenic site and can bind deeper crevices than murine antibodies, expanding our understanding of the antigenic landscape of PV capsids and potentially informing the design of better reagents, antivirals and vaccines against PV.

Article.Title: FAK- and TGF-β1-dependent biomechanical alterations in microvascular endothelial cells exposed to fluid shear stress gradients
Article.Authors: Sánchez-Rendón J.; Keskin E.; Oder N.; Reuss A.; Michalaki E.; Fuller G.; Dunn A.; Bastounis E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Endothelial cells (EC) form a dynamic monolayer barrier that regulates vascular permeability and is highly sensitive to mechanical cues, including shear stresses (SS) generated by blood flow. While spatial shear stress gradients (SSG) are linked to vascular pathologies such as atherosclerosis, their direct effects on cellular biomechanics across EC subtypes remain underexplored. Here, using an impinging flow device compatible with videomicroscopy, we demonstrate that exposure of two EC types to SSG causes an immediate and sustained two-fold decrease in migration speed, accompanied by enhanced coordination of collective motion and directional migration against the flow. Concurrently, EC traction and monolayer stresses increase acutely upon flow onset and continue to rise linearly over time. Mechanistically, FAK-mediated mechanotransduction governs flow-opposed migration, whereas the time-dependent increase in traction depends on TGF-β1 signaling and actomyosin contractility. Together, these findings identify SSG as key regulators of EC mechanics, collective dynamics, and signaling, with important implications for vascular disease diagnostics and therapeutics.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of quiescent epimastigotes as a resource for investigating Trypanosoma cruzi persistence
Article.Authors: Olmo F.; Hesketh A.; Hage H.; Monneuse J.; Taylor M.; Costa F.; Da Silva C.; Bequet F.; Escudié F.; Mercer D.; Saliou A.; Chatelain E.; Kelly J.; Abi-Ghanem J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chagas disease is caused by infection with the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi . Despite triggering a strong immune response, infections are typically life-long and can result in severe cardiac and/or digestive tract pathology. Current drugs have limited efficacy, and treatment failure is a common outcome. Eliminating a non-replicating T. cruzi sub-population that can persist after therapy has been a key challenge for the drug-development community. Here, we describe the transcriptome and proteome profiles of a low-proliferative sub-population of epimastigote forms of the parasite isolated from exponentially growing cultures on the basis of reduced turnover of transiently-induced red fluorescent protein. This partially quiescent sub-population was characterised by down-regulation of genes/proteins involved in translation, transcription, metabolism, mitochondrial function and DNA replication, and by up-regulation of proteins that promote exit from the cell cycle in other organisms. Differential expression was considerably more pronounced at a protein than an RNA level. These data provide a resource that can be exploited to dissect the mechanistic basis of quiescence, as a step towards refining the drug-development screening cascade.

Article.Title: Mathematical and experimental models of interactions among subclones and immunity in melanoma
Article.Authors: Hirsch M.; Ergun J.; Chin S.; Graff C.; Yee D.; Perez-Guijarro E.; Merlino G.; Day C.; Przytycka T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Melanoma tumors often contain heterogeneous subclones, typically with proliferative or invasive phenotypes. These subclones interact with each other and the immune system to shape tumor progression. Understanding interactions between subclones and the tumor microenvironment is a fundamental challenge for melanoma treatment. To analyze such interactions, we developed dedicated in vivo melanoma mouse and mathematical models. In the experimental models, admixtures of proliferative and invasive subclones of varying proportions were implanted into immunocompromised and immunocompetent mice. Tumor growth and subclone composition were tracked over time. In parallel, we built a computational model to capture the system dynamics. By estimating parameter values of our mathematical model using experimental measurements, we found that, while the proliferative subclone outgrew the invasive subclone, T cell activities selected for the invasive subclone. Initial subclonal proportion in this dynamic system determines the overall tumor sensitivity to immune response. The key interactions identified in this study provide insights into how intratumor heterogeneity and immune pressure influence melanoma progression, suggesting strategies for optimizing individualized therapy.

Article.Title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
Article.Authors: Lengerer B.; Bertemes P.; Szucs A.; Ladurner P.; Mertens B.; Grosbusch A.; Wattiez R.; Flammang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens, comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. Here, we generated a high-quality de novo genome assembly of the starlet cushion star, Asterina gibbosa, enabling full-length gene identification of Sfps. Proteomics of deposited footprint material identified 34 candidates; in situ hybridization localized 10 to the tube foot adhesive epidermis. Nine (designated Agib-Sfps) were homologous to known A. rubens Sfps and one encoded a trypsin-like proteinase. Anti-peptide antibodies revealed distinct footprint labelling patterns for Agib-Sfp7 and Agib-Sfp8, although mostly associated to the thin layer in contact with the substrate. Comparative analyses indicate a conserved core adhesive toolkit and domain repertoire between species, alongside species-specific reshuffling of domains across Sfps. These results refine the molecular model of asteroid adhesion and provide targets for sequence recombinant production toward seawater-compatible biomimetic adhesives.

Article.Title: Disruption of arn lipid A aminoarabinosylation confers AmpCmediated cephalosporin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: Hardie Boys M.; Wardell S.; Pletzer D.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in chronic cystic fibrosis infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa is shaped by pathogen-specific adaptation, yet the mechanisms driving cephalosporin resistance in epidemic clinical lineages remain incompletely defined. This arn-linked resistance was also observed in LESB65 but absent in laboratory strains PAO1 and PA14. Article.Authors: Coutinho L.; Palmieri E.; Gonzalez A.; Heinz W.; Moffat R.; Ridnour L.; Cheng R.; Pore M.; Butcher D.; Edmondson E.; Rangel M.; Wong S.; Lipkowitz S.; Glynn S.; McVicar D.; Li X.; Anderson S.; Billiar T.; Chang J.; Lockett S.; Wink D.

While COX2+ cells occupied oxygenated-to-intermediate zones, B7H4+ populations were enriched in intermediate-to-hypoxic regions, and CD44v6 remained broadly distributed. Poor-outcome patients showed high COX2 at the tumor-stroma interface as well as altered COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ clustering phenotypes. These findings identify COX2-dependent microenvironments as clinically relevant features of therapeutic resistance. Diclofenac preferentially depleted hypoxic compartments preserved following cisplatin treatment alone, supporting the targeting of spatially organized inflammatory niches to improve therapeutic response.

Article.Title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
Article.Authors: Huang R.; Jiang J.; Liu J.; Zhang C.; Wang H.; Zhang X.; Wang H.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when facing ambiguous cues in mate-choice decisions, yet how such advice optimizes outcomes remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Computational modeling quantified the decision optimization parameter ( β ). It showed that only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) model—best fit behavioral data, indicating that optimization arises from reciprocal adaptation rather than one-way influence. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more effectively promoted optimization. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that trial-level INS predicted momentary optimization, while task-level INS robustly forecasted overall decision improvement. Together, these findings demonstrate that decision optimization emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice enhances decision quality and social well-being.

Article.Title: Analysis of structural modifications and metagenomic sequencing during the ensiling of Caragana korshinskii provides insights into how extrusion pretreatment promotes lignocellulose degradation
Article.Authors: Bai B.; Ge G.; Qiu R.; Bao J.; Liu M.; Zhao M.; Ma W.; Sheng P.; Jia Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: In this study, to address the problems of poor silage fermentation quality and difficulty degrading lignocellulose interfering with resource utilization of Caragana korshinskii biomass, the effects of extrusion pretreatment (temperature 140°C and screw speed of 400 rpm) on its ensiling process were investigated. Results showed that pretreatment significantly improved silage quality, with lactic acid and water-soluble carbohydrate content increasing significantly ( P < 0.05), neutral detergent fiber content decreasing significantly ( P < 0.05), and hemicellulose degradation rate increasing by 31.64 ± 1.20% compared with the normal silage group. Microstructure analysis showed that pretreatment destroyed the dense biomass structure, increased specific surface area and porosityenhanced hydrophilicity, and reduced crystallinity, thus promoting the degradation of hemicellulose and cellulose. Metagenomic analysis further showed that extrusion pretreatment remodeled the microbial community structure, increasing the proportion of lactic acid bacteria such as Weissella and Companilactobacillus , and significantly increased the abundance of genes encoding debranching enzymes (CE3 and CE12) involved in hemicellulose degradation as well as main chain hydrolases (GH43 and GH8) ( P < 0.05). This study provides insights into the mechanisms by which extrusion pretreatment improves Caragana korshinskii silage in terms of physical and chemical structure and microbial functions, and this in turn may provide a technical and theoretical basis for understanding how efficient ensiling can be achieved more broadly in high-lignocellulosic feedstocks.

Article.Title: Widening the BRCAness therapeutic window for its synthetic lethality effects with PARP inhibitors
Article.Authors: Fernandez A.; Salman Y.; Castillo R.; Glackin C.; Shen B.
Article.Abstract: This review examines the expanding role of PARP inhibitors in cancer therapy, moving beyond the traditional model of single-strand break repair inhibition and BRCA-dependent synthetic lethality. We highlight emerging evidence that PARP inhibitors induce cytotoxicity through replication-associated DNA damage, including defects in Okazaki fragment maturation and replication gap accumulation. By integrating recent mechanistic insights with findings from CRISPR-based screens, we outline how disruptions in DNA replication and repair pathways define a broader BRCAness phenotype. We further emphasize the clinical implications of these discoveries, including novel combination strategies that extend the therapeutic applicability of PARP inhibitors beyond prevailing treatment regimens.

Article.Title: iTBS and cTBS to an individualized dlPFC target produce differential working memory improvement and session-dependent putamen deactivation
Article.Authors: Sun I.; Gregory D.; Abd-Elmoniem N.; Patel M.; Casalvera A.; Gura H.; Rodriguez C.; Brighter G.; Rueda Mora S.; Chandrashekar S.; Makhoul W.; Lynch K.; Oathes D.; Sheline Y.; Balderston N.
Article.Abstract: We evaluated the effects of individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) theta-burst stimulation (TBS) on working memory performance and task-related BOLD activity in 115 healthy adults (iTBS: n = 63; cTBS: n = 52). Stimulation was delivered to an individually-localized left dlPFC target identified using task-based fMRI, with each TBS visit consisting of five 600-pulse trains delivered as either the intermittent (iTBS) or continuous (cTBS) protocol. Participants completed the Sternberg Working Memory paradigm at baseline and approximately 24 hours after each visit. Groups were well-matched at baseline on all behavioral and neural measures. iTBS produced a significant improvement in working memory accuracy across sessions while cTBS did not, with a significant Group × Session interaction confirming differential trajectories. Both groups showed reaction time speedup across sessions, consistent with a shared practice effect. Despite these behavioral differences, BOLD activity at the dlPFC stimulation site showed no significant effects of Group, Session, or their interaction. Whole-brain analyses revealed significant session-dependent attenuation of bilateral putamen deactivation during the retention interval in both stimulation groups, with greater putamen deactivation at baseline correlating negatively with working memory accuracy. These results demonstrate that individualized task-based fMRI targeting can link TBS to circuit-level behavioral change, and that downstream subcortical responses may be more sensitive indices of TBS effects than activation at the stimulation site. The absence of a sham condition limits causal inference; observed differences reflect stimulation pattern rather than absolute TBS effects.

Article.Title: Cortex-wide neuronal dynamics underpin quasi-periodic patterns in resting-state fMRI
Article.Authors: Mandino F.; Shen X.; Horien C.; Papademetris X.; Strittmatter S.; Keilholz S.; Xu N.; Lake E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) captures whole-brain activity fluctuations non-invasively in humans and animals. Beyond task/stimuli-locked responses, fMRI measures large-scale patterned activity during rest. Among these, quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) represent recurring waves of activity that unfold over seconds and exhibit consistent spatiotemporal characteristics. Notably, certain fMRI-QPPs are well-preserved across species and altered in various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, our collective understanding of their neural underpinnings is limited given the indirect nature of blood-oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) fMRI signals. Simultaneous measures of local field potentials have provided some affirmation that fMRI-QPPs have neural origins, but these point-measurements are limited to a handful of sites. Here, we use a unique multimodal implementation of simultaneous wide-field calcium (WF-Ca 2+ ) imaging and fMRI to investigate the neural origins of fMRI-based QPPs. We uncover a robust time-locked correlation between QPPs detected by cortex-wide fluorescent WF-Ca 2+ imaging of neural activity and QPPs of BOLD-fMRI. These data validate the hypothesis that BOLD-fMRI QPPs derive from preceding slow waves of neural activity with regional and temporal precision.

Article.Title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer drivers and EMT revealed by genome-wide methylome profiling in NSCLC
Article.Authors: Chwialkowska K.; Niemira M.; Ostrowska A.; Zeller A.; Reszec-Gielazyn J.; Kozlowski M.; Mroz R.; Naumnik W.; Sierko E.; Moniuszko M.; Niklinski J.; Kretowski A.; Kwasniewski M.
Article.Abstract: Carcinogenesis is driven by dynamic and heterogeneous epigenomic alterations promoting tumour evolution and affecting therapeutic resistance. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation sequencing (RRBS) on 260 lung methylomes from 130 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. Here we show that gene-body hypomethylation involved lung cancer drivers, while promoter hypomethylation targeted miRNA genes linked to EGFR signalling, EMT, and PD-L1 regulation. Upstream transcription factor analysis also implicated epigenetic control of EMT, EGFR and immune pathways, through SNAIL, SLUG, SMAD3 and BRD4 . Promoter hypermethylation represented multi-gene epi-oncodriver mechanism associated with GPCRs. Subtype-specific patterns were additionally observed: adenocarcinoma showed alterations in neurotransmitter signalling, whereas squamous cell carcinoma embraced canonical oncogenic pathways. We provide a genome-wide methylome analysis in NSCLC, revealing epigenetic alterations that may contribute to tumour progression and therapeutic resistance linked to EGFR , EMT and immunological responses. These findings highlight the translational potential of epigenetic profiling to inform clinical strategies in NSCLC.

Article.Title: A mMono-Bac1.0 system for recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors with higher flexibility, throughput and yield
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Qi Y.; Han D.; Deng J.; Zhu Z.; Chen P.; Zhu X.; Liu L.; Ren Q.; Qiu Y.; Wang J.; Li C.; Liu J.; Wu Y.; Liu Q.; Jia F.; Wang H.; Wen P.; Xu F.
Article.Abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) holds immense promise for therapeutic applications, but high production costs limit its widespread clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for manufacturing breakthroughs. Here, we establish a modular Mono-Bac system with the p24 -NanoLuciferase (Nluc) reporter Bacmid for rAAV production, named mMono-Bac1.0, enhancing manufacturing flexibility, throughput and yield simultaneously. The system introduces two key technology to the pFD/Cap-(ITR-GOI)-Rep transfer vector-based Mono-Bac framework. First, a modular pGB-AAV Donor construction strategy enables one-step all-in-one AAV transfer vector assembly and effortless switching of capsids or GOIs, thus facilitating high-throughput combinatorial production. Second, an engineered p24 -Nluc Bacmid enables rapid (<5 min) quantification of infectious recombinant baculovirus (rBV) titers and real-time monitoring of Nluc activity in culture supernatants to determine the optimal harvest point (log RLU ~ 6.5), thereby maximizing rAAV yield. This system has the potential to advance baculovirus expression vector (BEV)-based rAAV manufacturing into a data-driven era, supporting efficient industrial-scale production.

Article.Title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
Article.Authors: Misir M.; Kroth P.; Wohlrab S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. Phylogenetic reconstructions reveal early aureochrome diversification in the stramenopile lineage, originating in a heterotrophic ancestor before photosynthesis was acquired. This challenges the assumption that aureochromes are restricted to phototrophs, suggesting an ancestral role in spectral light signaling. We find that, despite changes in light quality and photoperiod by latitude, diatom aureochrome domain architecture remains conserved. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

Article.Title: Chronic exercise induces a pathway-dependent electrophysiological signature in the mouse hippocampus
Article.Authors: Muela P.; Makarova J.; Muñoz-Arnaiz R.; Aballay J.; Cintado E.; Herreras O.; Trejo J.
Article.Abstract: Chronic physical exercise enhances hippocampal function, yet its impact on network activity remains poorly defined. We explored whether treadmill running leaves durable imprints detectable through electrophysiological techniques and spatial transcriptomics. Field potentials (FPs) were recorded in anesthetized male C57BL/6 J mice after a chronic exercise protocol. Using machine learning to analyze FP generators, we were able to reliably classify animals into their correct group by Lateral Perforant Path (LPP) activity alone. Classification rested on a multifeatured signature rather than any single feature. Schaffer Collateral and Lacunosum-Moleculare generators showed changes that did not achieve statistical significance. Exploratory spatial transcriptomics identified a coordinated enrichment of calcium signaling and long-term potentiation programs in the dentate gyrus. These findings demonstrate that exercise-induced plasticity is not a global shift but a localized remodeling of specific synaptic inputs, with changes detectable at both circuit and molecular levels. These durable, pathway-specific imprints persist in the absence of active task engagement, suggesting a reorganization of the brain’s memory circuitry.

Article.Title: Specification of bone marrow sinusoids requires TIE2-mediated positive feedback involving COUP-TFII and VEGFR3
Article.Authors: Li X.; Jia X.; Sun Z.; Li T.; Xu B.; Cao X.; Ding K.; Wang Y.; Shi Y.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The bone marrow (BM) vascular network plays crucial roles in driving bone development and supporting hematopoiesis, yet the mechanisms governing its specialized architecture, particularly sinusoidal morphogenesis, remain inadequately characterized. We show in this study that TIE2 ( Tek ) was highly expressed by BM sinusoidal endothelial cells (SEC) and the endothelial Tek excision led to BM sinusoidal capillarization. Particularly, the BM sinusoids displayed thinner vessel diameter with the aberrant mural cell coverage in the Tek mutants. Mechanistically, TIE2 insufficiency led to a dramatic decrease of VEGFR3 in BM-SECs while its expression in hepatic sinusoids was not obviously altered. The RNA-seq analysis showed that GO terms enriched for the downregulated genes were related to the biological processes including sinusoidal development while pathways related to arterial ECs and angiogenesis were upregulated in the bone marrow of Tek mutants. The alteration of sinusoidal VEGFR3 expression occurred within 48 h after the induced endothelial deletion of Tek . Consistently, the defective BM sinusoidal formation was validated with the induced Tek deletion in VEGFR3 + SECs. The insufficiency of TIE2 ligand ANGPT1 also led to reduced sinusoidal VEGFR3, accompanied by similar BM sinusoidal defects. Furthermore, disruption of sinusoidal morphogenesis was observed in mutant mice with the endothelial excision of Nr2f2 (COUP-TFII), displaying a decreased expression of BM sinusoidal TIE2 and VEGFR3. These findings suggest that ANGPT1/TIE2 and COUP-TFII form a reciprocal regulatory loop to coordinate BM sinusoidal specification via regulating VEGFR3.

Article.Title: Evolutionary genomics of ancient and endangered Achnatherum breviaristatum on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Zhang X.; Su X.; Wu G.; Yang Y.; Liu J.; Yuan L.; Ren G.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Climate change and human activities threaten biodiversity on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), renowned for its endemic species. We examined genomic diversity and evolution of Achnatherum breviaristatum, an endangered grass species endemic to the QTP. A. breviaristatum diverged from its sister lineage ~15 million years ago, and contrasts with two widespread and ecologically dominant monotypic genera within the same lineage—Neotrinia splendens and Psammochloa villosa—which thrive in arid northwestern China. Using newly generated chromosome-level genome assemblies and population resequencing data for A. breviaristatum and N. splendens, together with publicly available genomic data for P. villosa, we reveal that A. breviaristatum exhibits lower genetic diversity and heterozygosity based on resequencing reads mapped to the respective reference genomes. All species experienced parallel demographic declines since the Quaternary glaciation, with reductions during the Pleistocene. The endangered status of A. breviaristatum likely results from weaker clonal reproduction relative to its relatives, combined with Pleistocene vegetation shifts and anthropogenic activities. A reduced genetic load in A. breviaristatum may mitigate the effects of its low genetic diversity and contribute to its persistence. This study highlights interactions among climatic shifts, reproductive strategy, and human impact in shaping endemic species’ fates, providing genetic insights for conservation in vulnerable ecosystems. A comparative genomics study on grasses from the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau reveals how demographic decline, reduced clonal reproduction, and Pleistocene climate shifts have driven low diversity in an endangered endemic species, while reduced genetic load may have enabled its persistence.

Article.Title: Developmental restriction of the jaw skeletal muscle cardiogenic potential
Article.Authors: Díaz-Díaz C.; Ocaña O.; Isern J.; Muñoz-Cánoves P.; Torres M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of mortality worldwide and heart failure remains an end-stage disease with no other treatment than transplantation. A promising field to tackle heart failure is cardiomyocyte implantation. Whereas cardiomyocyte generation from pluripotent cells has shown promising results, direct derivation of cardiomyocytes from somatic stem cells is still challenging. Skeletal muscle progenitors have been extensively studied as a source of cardiac cells, due to their cellular and functional similarities. During development, the right ventricular myocardium and jaw skeletal muscles derive from a common pool of myogenic mesodermal progenitors. Previous studies have reported the derivation of cardiomyocyte-like cells specifically from adult jaw muscle stem cell populations, but not from other skeletal muscles, suggesting that developmental origin endows cardiogenic potential. Here we evaluated the cardiogenic potential of satellite cells and mesenchymal progenitor cells from the masticatory muscle by reproducing, optimizing and diversifying previously described protocols. We consistently found that stem cells from masticatory muscles are unable to differentiate into cardiac cells under any tested cardiogenic environment. Furthermore, pharmacological erasing of repressive epigenetic marks did not activate cardiogenic potential, suggesting that barriers restraining lineage plasticity are profound and unlikely to be reversed by simple exposure to cardiogenic environments.

Article.Title: Cleavage of xanthone and flavone C–glycosidic bonds by the enzyme complex LaGME from gut Lachnospiraceae
Article.Authors: Liu W.; Tao X.; Fan S.; Li X.; Liu Z.; Zhang H.; Li J.; He W.; Zhang D.; Zhang T.; Zhang T.; Pang X.; Yang Z.; Ma B.; Xiang H.; Yu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aglycones, the bioactive metabolites of C– glycosides, can be obtained through the deglycosylation of naturally abundant C– glycosides. However, C– glycosides are more resistant to enzymatic and chemical degradation. Gut microbiota and its enzymes are known to cleave the C–C glycosidic bond, but only a limited number of active strains and functional enzymes have been identified. Here we show that a new C– deglycosylation gene cluster encoding the g lycoside- m etabolizing e nzyme from La chnospiraceae (LaGME), an enzyme complex consisting of a C – g lycoside o xidoreductase (LaCGO1) and a C – g lycoside e limination enzyme complex (LaCGE), was discovered using the DUF6379 domain-containing protein as a probe. LaGME demonstrates significant activities toward xanthone-type and flavone-type C– glycosides. After investigation into heterologous expression, structural determination and catalytic mechanism, a LaGME-mediated one-pot cascade enzymatic reaction system was developed for green production of aglycones. This research provides an approach to uncover C– glycoside-metabolizing enzymes in nature, as well as a preliminary basis for the sustainable production of value-added bioactive aglycones from glycosides.

Article.Title: Analysis of 515 human proteomes defines plasma extracellular vesicle core composition, corona and coisolated networks
Article.Authors: Carvalho A.; Falcón-Pérez J.; Beck H.; Matthiesen R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, yet their proteomic profiling remains confounded by massive co-isolation. Here, we resolve this heterogeneity through a meta-analysis of 515 human plasma EV proteomes. We demonstrate that the reproducible core proteome is overwhelmingly governed by predictable, surface-charge-driven mass-action that dynamically mirrors synthetic nanoparticle corona formation. By quantitatively decomposing the core isolate against pan-synthetic coronas and agonist-induced platelet EVs, we trace the core isolate to three main mechanistic origins: an electrostatic plasma corona, ex vivo platelet vesiculation and biological macromolecular co-isolates. Crucially, the residual vesicular cargo strongly correlates with thrombin-induced platelet degranulation, indicating that phlebotomy-induced trauma contribute to the bulk signal. We provide a modular atlas that mathematically distinguishes biophysical coronas from these cellular co-isolates, establishing a new framework for interpreting biological origin in plasma EV proteomics.

Article.Title: Tamoxifen targets Wisp2 to impair subcutaneous adipocyte progenitor self-renewal and adipogenic differentiation
Article.Authors: Thomas N.; Sankofi B.; Cen H.; Sekhri M.; Murguia S.; Cherian M.; Stout M.; Miller B.; Rudolph M.; Wellberg E.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Breast cancer endocrine therapy, which systemically disrupts estrogen receptor signaling, increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk in some women. Sustained treatment with low-dose tamoxifen depletes subcutaneous adipocyte progenitors and promotes glucose intolerance and hepatic lipid deposition in obese female mice. Hyperplastic adipose tissue expansion, especially in subcutaneous depots, preserves metabolic health during a chronic positive energy balance by facilitating nutrient storage and attenuating inflammation. Adipocyte progenitors are renewed in part through Wnt signaling pathway activation, which is altered in women with obesity or T2D. Estrogen receptors are expressed in several adipose cell types, but the distinct actions of tamoxifen in adipocyte progenitors and the mechanisms that explain their depletion during endocrine therapy are not defined. The direct impact of tamoxifen was evaluated in subcutaneous adipose stromal cells from humans and adult mice. Self-renewal, proliferation, and differentiation were measured, and analyses of gene expression and progenitor or preadipocyte populations were performed. Mechanistic insight was gained from primary adipose stromal cells of obese female mice, in which the Wnt1 inducible signaling pathway protein 2 (Wisp2) was lost following endocrine therapy. Wisp2 gain and loss of function studies were carried out in adipose stromal cells to define the link between estrogen signaling and adipocyte progenitor maintenance. We found that tamoxifen treatment disrupts the protection of adipocyte progenitors by estrogen, mediated through suppression of Wisp2. These studies reveal potential metabolic effects of tamoxifen therapy that precede and could drive T2D development in breast cancer survivors.

Article.Title: Assessing whole-cortex excitability from electromagnetic brain signals
Article.Authors: Pellegrino G.; Duma G.; Schuler A.; Daub M.; Marinazzo D.; Arcara G.; Soddu A.; Rasero J.
Article.Abstract: Cortical excitability is a core feature of brain function shaped by microcircuitry, large-scale networks, and neurochemistry. In humans, it can be inferred from indirect electrophysiological measures, yet it remains unclear whether these capture a single construct or multiple processes. We systematically compared established excitability metrics using whole-head magneto-encephalography (MEG) recorded at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation in a large sample of healthy adults. These measures included stimulus-driven synchronization, spectral power, aperiodic (1/f) activity, signal complexity, long-range temporal correlations, and phase–gamma synchronization. Hierarchical clustering identified six distinct excitability dimensions with limited redundancy, indicating that cortical excitability is inherently multidimensional. Aperiodic and alpha-band measures were strongly coupled and most spatially aligned with stimulus responses, while temporal, complexity, and synchronization metrics were largely independent. Regional differences were most pronounced in integrative and internally oriented areas. Each dimension also related differently to cortical morphology and neurotransmitter receptor density, highlighting diverse neurobiological substrates and supporting multimodal approaches to studying excitability.

Article.Title: Single-cell atlas reveals NLRP2 associated mitochondrial dysfunction in estrogen induced Macrobrachium nipponense sex reversal
Article.Authors: Cai P.; Gao Z.; Jiang S.; Zhang W.; Xiong Y.; Qiao H.; Jin S.; Fu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sex reversal is widely used in biological breeding, but its cellular and molecular consequences in crustaceans are poorly understood. Here, we combine estrogen induced feminization, single cell RNA sequencing, histology and RNA interference to dissect gonadal development in the oriental river prawn ( Macrobrachium nipponense ). Feeding post-larval males with 17β-estradiol generated neo-females with ovary like gonads. Single cell profiling of testis, ovaries and neo-female gonads produced a gonadal atlas in which, using newly validated markers, we resolved major oogenic and spermatogenic cell types. Cell-type composition and pseudotime analyses showed that neo-female gonads are dominated by early germ cells, whereas mature oocytes and spermatozoa are strongly depleted; histology confirmed this developmental arrest. Stage resolved differential expression and KEGG enrichment consistently highlighted oxidative phosphorylation as the most perturbed pathway across key germ-cell stages. Among the affected genes, MnNLRP2 displayed primary spermatocyte specific and testis enriched expression and was conserved among decapods. RNA interference of MnNLRP2 in PL10 prawns shifted phenotypic sex ratios toward females and altered sex steroid levels, reducing MT in males while elevating E 2 in females; knockdown in adults caused spermatogenic arrest and down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation components. These findings provide unprecedented insights into crustacean germ cell dynamics and the metabolic and transcriptional networks governing incomplete sex reversal, thereby offering critical resources for reproductive biology and aquaculture research.
