Article.Title: Breaking new ground into RAD51 BRC repeats interplay in homologous recombination
Article.Authors: Rinaldi F.; Franco P.; Veronesi M.; Romeo E.; Bresciani V.; Varignani G.; Catalano F.; Bernetti M.; Masetti M.; Langer J.; Girotto S.; Cavalli A.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Homologous recombination (HR) is a critical repair pathway involving numerous proteins that ensure error-free DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) repair. Dysfunction in HR components can compromise genome integrity. Despite advances, many aspects of HR remain poorly understood. Notably, even one of the earliest identified and most critical interactions, between RAD51 and BRCA2, remains incompletely characterized, mainly due to the lack of structural data. This study presents a comprehensive biophysical analysis of the RAD51–BRC repeats interaction, integrating computational and experimental approaches. Starting with assessing the correlation between the binding affinities of individual BRC repeats and their impact on RAD51 disassembly, our investigation extends to larger BRCA2 truncations, offering unprecedented insights into the molecular determinants of RAD51 recognition. As mutations in the BRC repeats impair RAD51 recruitment and are associated with cancer, these results provide a valuable framework for interpreting pathogenic variants and guiding precision medicine therapies. Article.Title: Ultra large docking reveals novel chemotypes and a distinct binding mode for Porcupine inhibition
Article.Authors: Kim C.; Coria J.; Radchenko D.; Cheng H.; Li J.; Wang B.; Hu Q.; Moroz Y.; Li X.; Liu F.
Article.Abstract: Wnt signaling is essential for embryonic development and adult tissue homeostasis, and its dysregulation contributes to cancer and other human diseases. Porcupine (PORCN), a membrane-bound O-acyltransferase (MBOAT) required for Wnt palmitoylation and secretion, has emerged as an important therapeutic target. Despite promising preclinical results, PORCN inhibitors have shown limited clinical activity to date, motivating the search for new chemotypes and binding modes. Here, we docked a library of 1.3 billion molecules against PORCN and identified 16 novel compounds that inhibit Wnt signaling. These hits are structurally distinct from known PORCN inhibitors, and structure-based optimization of one series yielded sub-micromolar leads. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that the lead inhibitor binds PORCN in an unreported mode within the palmitoleoyl-CoA chamber, positioned closer to the cytosol than existing inhibitors. Together, our findings expand the chemical and structural space available for targeting PORCN and provide new starting points for development of Wnt signaling antagonists.

Article.Title: Kidney-derived mitochondrial extracellular vesicles trigger acute lung injury in sepsis via mtDNA-cGAS-STING in pulmonary endothelium
Article.Authors: Jiao Y.; Zhang H.; Xie X.; Pi M.; Fu Q.; Zhu W.; Song J.; Bo J.; Zhang T.; Chen M.; Gu X.; Ma Z.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis often leads to multiple organ failure, but how injury in one organ propagates to another remains poorly understood. Here we show that the injured kidney releases mitochondria-rich extracellular vesicles (mitoEVs) into the circulation, which travel to the lung and trigger acute lung injury. In septic mice and cultured renal tubular epithelial cells, sepsis promotes the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles by upregulating sorting nexin 9. Blocking this process in kidney tubules reduces the release of mitoEVs and protects against lung injury. Once taken up by lung endothelial cells, the mitochondrial DNA carried by these vesicles activates an innate immune pathway involving cGAS and STING, with ZBP1 serving as a potential cooperative partner for this activation. This leads to endothelial barrier disruption, immune cell recruitment, and respiratory failure. In patients with sepsis, higher levels of circulating mitoEVs associate with lung injury and death. These findings identify a kidney-to-lung signaling axis that may be targeted therapeutically.

Article.Title: Genome-wide analyses reveal recent diversification and hidden diversity in Amazonian howler monkeys, including two new species
Article.Authors: Batista R.; Semedo T.; Beck R.; Bittencourt P.; Ceríaco L.; Cuadros-Espinoza S.; da Silva M.; de Melo F.; Deo R.; de Vries D.; Farh K.; Farias I.; Gibson M.; Goodhead I.; Gubili C.; Hermosilla-Albala N.; Hrbek T.; Janiak M.; Kuderna L.; Mahabir D.; Marqués-Bonet T.; Melin A.; Mendoza A.; Mittermeier R.; Nash S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Complex ecological and evolutionary patterns shaped the rich biodiversity of the Neotropics. Understanding how diversity emerges and is maintained is key to anticipating potential biotic responses to current anthropogenic changes. Howler monkeys ( Alouatta ) are one of the most successful radiations inhabiting this region. However, 11 of the 16 taxa currently recognised are classified as threatened by the IUCN Red List, and the genus faces increasing threats from deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and hunting. Here, we present a genomic-wide analysis covering 11 of the 13 recognised Alouatta species. Our results indicate that most of this genus’ diversity in Amazonia originated in the last million years, driven by major biogeographic and ecological factors, such as geographical barriers (e.g., Amazonian rivers, and the Andes), as well as by ecological gradients, including savanna-forest mosaics and ecotonal zones. Historical biogeographic reconstructions support a trans-Andean origin for Alouatta . Based on integrative taxonomy, including genomic and morphological evidence from numerous specimens, we formally identify groups and provide descriptions for two new species. Our findings underscore the power of genome-wide data to uncover hidden diversity and to inform conservation strategies, particularly in rapidly transforming tropical ecosystems where undescribed species may already be at risk.

Article.Title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
Article.Authors: Cecconello C.; Claria-Ribas P.; Cartagena García C.; Busnel J.; Dalli J.; Perretti M.; Norling L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Non-classical monocytes and VCAM-1 + synovial fibroblasts were lower at peak arthritis while pro-resolution MerTK + CD206 + macrophages were increased at resolution onset. Lipid mediator profiling of arthritic paws identified a distinct repertoire of molecules in ω3-fed mice, with elevated EPA-derived resolvin E2 (RvE2) and RvE4, compared with increased TXB 2 and PGF 2α with a normal diet. Pharmacological treatment of mice with RvE2 and RvE4 concomitant with arthritis induction, attenuated arthritis and increased MerTK + CD206 + macrophages in arthritic joints. Synovial explant treatment revealed reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and enzyme release including IL-6, CCL2 and MMP-9. In arthritic patient blood, RvE2 and RvE4 (100 nM) lowered monocyte ICAM-1 expression. Collectively, these data identify cellular and molecular determinants of an ω3 diet in pre-clinical and human settings, highlighting therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Myristic acid promotes in vitro maturation and developmental competence of porcine oocytes
Article.Authors: Yan J.; Zhang K.; Gao X.; Xu S.; Ning F.; Liu K.; Zhang X.; De Felici M.; Zhang T.; Wang J.; Shen W.
Article.Abstract: The present study examined how antral follicle size influences oocyte meiotic maturation and developmental competence from a metabolic perspective and explored strategies to improve the meiotic maturation and quality of oocytes derived from small antral follicles. Untargeted metabolomics revealed dynamic metabolic changes during porcine antral follicle development, with increased fatty acid synthesis and enhanced activities of related enzymes in oocytes from larger follicles. In vitro, myristic acid (MA) improved meiotic maturation (polar body extrusion, spindle morphology, chromosome dynamics) and survival of oocytes from small follicles by reducing Annexin V expression and ROS levels. MA also enhanced their developmental competence after parthenogenetic activation. Molecular and cytochemical analyses showed that MA altered the transcriptional profile, increased lipid storage, and boosted mitochondrial number and function. Finally, MA upregulated SIRT1, activated PPARα, and increased CPT2 expression, suggesting a potential mechanism underlying its effects on these oocytes.

Article.Title: Structure-function tethering of human locus coeruleus connectivity reveals a noradrenergic cortical hierarchy
Article.Authors: Zhu Q.; Fan L.; Wu Y.; An S.; Li Y.; Wang H.; Yao N.; Li Y.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is the primary source of cerebral norepinephrine and plays a broad role in cognition. Here, we show the macroscale organization of human LC connectivity using 7 T diffusion and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Structural and functional connectivity exhibit a dominant rostral-caudal gradient, with structure-function tethering lowest in the intermediate LC and increasing toward its rostral and caudal portions. In the neocortex, this pattern is expressed as steeply increasing tethering from the central sulcus toward anterior and posterior regions. Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas tracing further reveals preferential LC projections to somatomotor cortex. The cortical expression of LC structure-function tethering exhibits a network-level hierarchy and aligns with a behavioral axis. Additionally, this cortical expression shows significant spatial covariance with norepinephrine transporter concentration, fiber length, and gray matter volume. Together, these findings provide MRI-based evidence for a hierarchical macroscale organization of human LC connectivity linking structural and functional architecture to cortical and behavioral variation.

Article.Title: Metabolic sensor Gpr35 links dietary lipids to itch mediating neural circuits
Article.Authors: Wheeler J.; Lyfenko A.; Zurek N.; Song K.; Wangzhou A.; Bontala S.; Deep O.; Casey J.; Kubofcik R.; Schaffer D.; Melhem H.; Keyes G.; Davis J.; Niess J.; Price T.; Ramsden C.; Kim B.; Alles S.; Mishra S.

Collectively, our findings establish Gpr35 as a critical neuro-metabolic sensor in healthy and disease conditions.

Article.Title: Aberrant RNA sensing and host-specific immunopathology in highly pathogenic influenza infections
Article.Authors: Dey A.; Patel A.; Chandra A.; Kesavardhana S.
Article.Abstract: Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections.

Article.Title: Towards a sequential microbiome therapy for HPV-associated cervicovaginal dysbiosis
Article.Authors: Molina M.; Zhang Y.; Steenbergen R.; Melchers W.; Du J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. Multiomics studies indicate that hrHPV persistence is linked to reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic alterations that may compromise epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. In this Perspective article, we introduce a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework designed to restore cervicovaginal ecological balance and support viral clearance. SMT is a two-phase, strain-resolved strategy. The first phase targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting or microbiota-modulating approaches to create a window for ecological reset. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

Article.Title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
Article.Authors: Nasr E.; Pechlivanis N.; Strepis N.; Amato P.; Bernt M.; Bhardwaj A.; Blankenberg D.; Brites D.; Cumbo F.; Do K.; Ferrari E.; Griffin T.; Grüning B.; Hiltemann S.; Hyde C.; Jagtap P.; Kumar A.; Malla M.; Mehta S.; Métris K.; Momin S.; Nelson T.; Oba A.; Pavloudi C.; Péguilhan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform’s utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

Article.Authors: Filipe A.; Dede A.; Chlastakova A.; Levytska V.; Kopecka J.; Snebergerova P.; Makusova L.; Zirovnicka T.; Kreckova T.; Cisarova Z.; Ribeiro C.; Perner J.; Sojka D.; Jalovecka M.

Article.Title: Developmental and genetic modulation of evidence integration dynamics in zebrafish sensorimotor decision-making
Article.Authors: Garza R.; El Hady A.; Bahl A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Animals integrate information over time and maintain persistent internal representations of cues to guide decision-making. How the underlying behavioral algorithms of individual animals depend on factors such as experience, developmental stage, or genotype remains poorly understood. Drift-diffusion models provide a powerful theoretical framework to describe and predict performance metrics across a wide range of species. The stochastic nature of these models and the typically limited throughput of most experimental designs challenge the automatic inference of latent variables. Here, we combine high-throughput behavioral assays in larval zebrafish with drift-diffusion modeling, revealing that larvae progressively develop more persistent, self-reinforcing integration dynamics during early development. This effect is reduced in fish carrying mutations in genes linked to human epilepsy and schizophrenia. Our results show that behavior-based drift-diffusion modeling can offer a scalable, automated approach to generate experimentally testable hypotheses about the algorithmic implementation of sensorimotor integration in health and disease.

Article.Authors: Lemaire J.; Mangione R.; Loveland J.; Fusani L.; Canoine V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The capacity to regulate corticosterone release following a stressful event is an essential component of the physiological flexibility required to maintain homeostasis and ensure adaptive responses to environmental change. Hg blood concentrations were negatively correlated with corticosterone responsiveness, suggesting impairment of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis function. These results demonstrate that environmental Hg contamination is associated with reduced stress responsiveness and physiological flexibility, which likely limits the ability of Hg-contaminated individuals to cope with novel environmental stressors. Article.Title: PDE10A identified by cross-hemisphere visual cortex proteomics restores adult ocular dominance plasticity involving cAMP/CREB signaling
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhu Z.; Xu J.; Dong S.; Mo E.; Li Q.; Li Z.; Zhao Y.; Chang P.
Article.Abstract: Ocular dominance plasticity (ODP) is robust during the critical period but is restricted in adulthood. The molecular programs that distinguish this permissive state and whether they can be pharmacologically engaged in adulthood remain unclear. Article.Title: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting species B adenoviruses largely mimics the DSG2 receptor engagement mechanism
Article.Authors: Vassal-Stermann E.; Berthollet C.; Zhang W.; Fenel D.; Ehrhardt A.; Lieber A.; Schoehn G.; Effantin G.; Fender P.
Article.Abstract: Species B human adenoviruses (B-HAdVs), including HAdV7, HAdV3, and the re-emerging HAdV55, cause severe respiratory disease and engage desmoglein-2 (DSG2) through their fiber knob. Cryo-electron microscopy structures at 1.8 Å and 2.0 Å resolution for 6G7 and 5C5 respectively, reveal distinct binding modes: 6G7 engages the trimeric fiber knob at a 3:3 antibody: knob ratio, whereas 5C5 binds the apex at a 1:3 ratio. These findings establish the fiber knob apex as a vulnerable site for antibody-mediated neutralization and identify 5C5 as a candidate targeting pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Vassal-Stermann et al. identified two monoclonal antibodies that neutralize HAdV7 and cross-react with pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Cryo-EM reveals that the potent antibody 5C5 blocks the conserved DSG2 receptor-binding site at the fiber knob apex, defining a vulnerable target for broad neutralization.

Article.Title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
Article.Authors: Li X.; Ma T.; Han X.; Hai S.; Yin L.; Wang L.; Wang J.; Li H.; Yang Q.; Guan X.; Li Y.; Ding H.

HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

Article.Authors: Miao Y.; Cui Q.; Li Z.; Zhang T.; Zhang R.; Zhao Q.; Zhou H.; Zuo Y.; Wang Q.; Zhang Y.; Zheng Z.; He W.; Liu C.; Huang Q.; Zheng H.; Yuan Y.

Article.Title: Albendazole induces ferroptosis through the USP7-GPX4 axis in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Guan T.; Lin X.; Qiu Y.; Huang Z.; Liang Z.; Liao P.; Zhang H.; Ou C.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) is an aggressive hematological malignancy that still requires the development of novel therapeutic strategies. Here, leveraging a drug-repurposing strategy, we performed a high-throughput screen of 3008 U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drugs and identified albendazole (ABZ), a benzimidazole anthelmintic, as a potent agent against B-ALL across multiple preclinical models. Mechanistically, ABZ directly binds ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) and triggers its autophagy-dependent destabilization, subsequently promoting the ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby inducing ferroptosis in B-ALL. Article.Title: Lactate drives the emergence of tumor cells with centrosome amplification through CP110 lactylation
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Miao R.; Ding S.; Quan Y.; Zhu T.; Zhang F.; Liu D.; Chen H.; Cao H.; Zhang Y.; Fang Y.; Xu J.; Shou Y.; Wang Q.; Liu Y.; Li Y.; Chen J.; Sun L.; Lin Y.; Liu J.; Chen L.; Xu T.; Wang W.; Hou Y.; Fan G.

Mechanistically, through systematic screening of centrosomal proteins, we identified CP110 and its key lactylation site at lysine 690 (K690), as critical drivers of CA in tumor cells. Furthermore, CP110-K690 lactylation promotes genomic instability, accelerates cellular proliferation, and enhances metastatic potential by driving CA, collectively facilitating malignant progression. Importantly, inhibition of CP110-K690 lactylation effectively disrupts this pro-tumorigenic signaling axis. Article.Abstract: Abstract Zooplankton form a vital link between phytoplankton and higher trophic levels, including commercially exploited fish, making recent declines in copepods and increases in meroplankton a major concern. The two methods showed strong agreement for holoplanktonic crustaceans and gelatinous predators, but weaker correspondence for meroplankton. The far greater taxonomic insight from meroplankton groups provided by eDNA revealed a shift towards higher relative sequence abundance of soft sediment (mainly sublittoral) fauna, rather than from rocky nearshore. Trait-based analysis showed long-term increases were mainly fine filter feeders, including many meroplankton larvae. This suggests that changes in water column processes, linked to declining nutrient supply and a shift towards smaller phytoplankton, were contributing to broader changes in the pelagic food web and benthic-pelagic coupling.

Article.Title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
Article.Authors: Zeng L.; Liu Y.; Zhang C.; Fan Y.; Sun J.; Liu Y.; Xu Z.; Cao Y.; Li O.; Zhang C.; Fan G.; Zhang J.; Zhao Y.; Liang X.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Lu H.
Article.Abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. Article.Authors: Mordhorst L.; Weiskopf N.; Morawski M.; Mohammadi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Axon caliber determines signal conduction velocity and varies within and across the bundles that form the brain’s wiring. Our knowledge of this organization derives largely from 2D histology, assuming cylindrical axons whose calibers are described by their radius. However, recent 3D histology reveals substantial along-axon variability in radius, calling into question 2D-derived insights into axon radius and conduction velocity. We show in 450,000 3D axon reconstructions from male rats that—despite this individual variation—axon bundles possess stable radius distributions at the ensemble level. These distributions are faithfully captured by 2D cross-sections and yield robust conduction velocity predictions, as along-axon variability has only a modest effect. Conduction in large axons is particularly stable, supporting time-critical signaling. With 2D sampling validated, we leverage 46 million human corpus callosum axons from 2D histology to determine sample size requirements across neuroscience applications. Article.Title: Genetic interaction between Adgrg6 and Sox9 reveals a feedforward mechanism for postnatal spinal stability
Article.Authors: Aceves V.; Xu Z.; Zhang C.; Kim J.; Ito J.; Mathers K.; Lassar A.; Liu Z.; Gray R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common spinal disorder in children and is best understood as a complex polygenic condition. Here, we use spatial transcriptomics to characterize altered gene expression in the spine of a conditional Adgrg6 mutant mouse model of AIS (Adgrg6-cKO), revealing reduced expression of Sox9 and several components of extracellular matrix organization in the intervertebral disc. We further show that SOX9 occupies regions of open chromatin within the Adgrg6 locus in cells isolated from the mouse intervertebral disc. Finally, we demonstrate a strong genetic interaction between Adgrg6-cKO and a hypomorphic Sox9 allele that increases both the penetrance and severity of AIS-like pathology in mice. Collectively, these findings support a self-reinforcing feedforward regulatory circuit, where Adgrg6 and Sox9 are co-regulated to maintain extracellular matrix gene expression in the annulus fibrosus and paraspinal tissues. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the functional significance of AIS-associated GWAS loci near ADGRG6 and SOX9 and establish combined Adgrg6–Sox9 insufficiency as a tractable model of polygenic scoliosis susceptibility.

Article.Authors: Granö I.; Kahilakoski O.; Laine M.; Kirchhoff M.; Ahola O.; Soto A.; Matsuda R.; Nieminen A.; Pieramico G.; Rissanen I.; Sinisalo H.; Tommila T.; Roine T.; Nieminen J.; Souza V.; Ilmoniemi R.; Lioumis P.; Mutanen T.
Article.Abstract: Mapping forms the basis for understanding the functional organization of the brain and for developing targeted interventions in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Article.Title: Exceptional preservation in cherts reveals complex cuticular architecture in one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoans
Article.Authors: Zhang M.; Dong L.; Hua H.; Liu W.; Qin S.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Ecdysozoans, animals characterized by a periodically moulted cuticle, became major components of Cambrian marine ecosystems, yet the structural organization of their earliest non-mineralized cuticles remains poorly documented. Here we report Spinosoma reticulatus gen. et sp. nov., a millimeter-scale ecdysozoan from Fortunian cherts on two paleogeographic blocks: the Liuchapo Formation, South China, and the Yurtus Formation, Tarim Block, dating to ca. 538 Ma. This occurrence represents one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoan body-fossil records and may predate the classic Kuanchuanpu scalidophoran assemblages. The material preserves a terminal mouth with large circumoral spines and abundant cuticular fragments. Its cuticle comprises a fibrous mesh, short upright plate-like structures, and hollow ridged spines. Morphological and Raman data support an ecdysozoan affinity, whereas scalidophoran placement remains tentative. Spinosoma reveals a previously undocumented cuticular architecture, suggesting that early ecdysozoan ecological breadth and integument diversity are underestimated in the earliest phase of the Cambrian Explosion.

Article.Authors: Wybo W.; Ewert L.; Linssen C.; Babu P.; Pastorelli E.; Paolucci P.; Morrison A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While subcellular mechanisms in the dendrites of neurons govern the implementation of learning and memory in the brain, large-scale network simulations featuring such processes remain challenging to achieve. Here, we fill this gap by implementing a framework for the massively parallel simulation of simplified dendrite models with customizable subcellular dynamics. We leverage the NEural Simulation Tool (NEST), the neuroscientific reference with respect to efficient massively parallel simulations of point-neuron networks. By co-opting the model description language NESTML, we generate C++ code implementing user-configurable subcellular dynamics. We show that the generated models run efficiently, leading to scalable NEST network simulations. To showcase relevant functionalities, we provide a proof-of-concept demonstration that a key sensory computation – the association of top-down context arriving at distal dendrites in layer 1 and feedforward sensory input arriving perisomatically – can be achieved in a single-shot fashion through apical calcium dynamics. Our work thus unlocks the study of how dendritic processes shape network function and learning at scale.

Article.Title: SQSTM1/p62-LC3A–mediated autophagic clearance of stress granules prevents apoptosis under hyperosmotic stress
Article.Authors: Yi Q.; Zhang C.; Hu S.; Wang Z.; He L.; Zhang M.; Man Z.; Bai Y.; Liu Y.

These findings highlight the critical role of the SQSTM1–LC3A axis in SG turnover and cell survival under chronic stress.

Article.Authors: Gu M.; Chen W.; Hu C.; Jia X.; Xiao W.; Lu G.; Gong W.; Lu D.

Genetically modified expression of UCP1 in NK cells is a potential therapy for patients with tumors. UCP1 loss in tumor-infiltrating NK cells drives CD36/FABP4-dependent fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial DNA release and NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis. Article.Authors: Luo C.; Wang S.; Lyu Q.; Lyu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Objective To elucidate the sex-specific trajectories of endothelial cell (EC) transdifferentiation and their contribution to distinct atherosclerotic plaque phenotypes in males and females. We identify a novel, direct EC-to-adipocyte trajectory and pinpoint KLF2 and CREB5 as key regulators, offering new mechanistic insights into why premenopausal women develop more stable atherosclerotic lesions than men.

Article.Abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder exhibits substantial intrinsic subtype heterogeneity, necessitating the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomic insights into conserved and divergent oligodendrocyte lineage programs across species
Article.Authors: Han X.; Zuo L.; Zhang Z.; Yu Y.; Hu J.; Long Q.; Tian X.; Wei J.; Zhang R.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLLCs) are essential for myelination and neural support, yet how their transcriptional programs are conserved or diverge across species remains unclear. We analyzed around one million hippocampal single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from humans, cynomolgus macaques, rhesus macaques, and mice. OLLCs exhibited high transcriptional conservation, with precursor subtypes preserved but oligodendrocytes showing species-specific diversity. We identified primate-specific regulators such as CNDP1 and temporally shifted ETV1 expression, which were validated by immunofluorescence staining and qRT-PCR. Disease module analysis showed OLLCs provide a conserved substrate for brain aging and neurological disorders, with rhesus macaques displaying greater concordance with humans than cynomolgus macaques or mice. Analysis of OLLC aging trajectories identified primate-specific activation of Wnt pathways in oligodendrocyte precursor cell, contrasting with ribosomal enrichment in mice. These findings define conserved and divergent OLLC programs and underscore nonhuman primates—particularly rhesus macaques—as highly relevant translational models for human myelin biology.

Article.Title: A role for the BBSome in restricting the entry of non-ciliary proteins into cilia
Article.Authors: Cevik S.; Yenisert F.; Kantarci H.; Pucak D.; Gallrein C.; Stöckl S.; Dünninger X.; Cakici O.; Stigloher C.; Kirstein J.; Kaplan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cilia possess the inherent ability to restrict the entry of non-ciliary components through the ciliary gate. Mutations in genes encoding components of the ciliary gate result in various cilia-related diseases known as ciliopathies. Yet, how non-ciliary residents are prevented from accumulating in cilia remains unclear. Here, we observe ciliary accumulation of non-ciliary proteins in BBSome-deficient mutants (Bardet-Biedl syndrome), a phenotype reminiscent of ciliary gate-defective mutants such as mks-5 and nphp-4 . Time-lapse imaging shows that these non-ciliary proteins move bidirectionally along cilia at IFT velocities, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) reveals that the non-ciliary protein ELMD-1 associates with the IFT component IFT-43 in BBSome-deficient mutants, indicating that they are mis-loaded onto IFT trains. This misloading allows them to bypass the ciliary gate. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) suggests the gate remains largely functional, supporting a potential two-step model of ciliary composition control: cargo selection/loading and ciliary gating. We propose that defects in cargo selection/loading (and potentially export) alter ciliary composition, allowing unintended protein entry.

Article.Title: Inhibition of spinal astrocytic GPR177 attenuates neuropathic pain by modulating C3/C3aR signaling in male rats
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Yang M.; Li A.; Liu Y.; Guo K.; Yang Y.; Yao Y.
Article.Abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) remains refractory to conventional therapy partly because its pathogenesis is incompletely understood. G protein-coupled receptor 177 (GPR177), a multi-pass transmembrane protein, regulates Wnt trafficking and secretion. Here, we use a chronic constriction injury model in male rats and find GPR177 predominantly expresses in spinal astrocytes and co-localizes with complement component 3 (C3). During NP development, astrocytic GPR177 expression increases, accompanied by activation of C3/C3a receptor (C3aR) signaling in the spinal dorsal horn. Gpr177 silencing with siRNA alleviates nerve injury-associated hypersensitivity and reduces the increases in GPR177, glial fibrillary acidic protein, C3, and C3aR. Intrathecal administration of the C3 inhibitor compstatin and the C3aR antagonist SB290157 reduces hypersensitivity and suppresses C3/C3aR activation, supporting the involvement of C3/C3aR signaling in NP development. These findings demonstrate that spinal GPR177 contributes to NP by activating astrocytes and regulating the C3/C3aR signaling pathway, suggesting the GPR177/C3/C3aR axis as a potential therapeutic target for NP.

Article.Title: Anatomical differences in the brain organization between Australopithecus and early Homo based on computational neuroanatomy
Article.Authors: Amano H.; Tanabe H.; Bruner E.; Ogihara N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Encephalization is a hallmark of human evolution, but how regional brain morphology changed during early hominin evolution remains unclear. Here, we show regional brain morphological differences between sampled Australopithecus and early Homo specimens. Using computed tomography and endocranial casts, we generated brain models for Australopithecus africanus , Homo habilis , and Homo ergaster using an anatomically homogeneous cross-species interpolation technique. Our reconstructions suggest that the posterior cerebellum was enlarged in early Homo compared with the sampled A. africanus specimens. In contrast, relative frontal lobe volume remains largely unchanged among the sampled fossils. We also identify enlargement of temporoparietal regions that, in modern humans, are associated with functions including social communication and tool use. By integrating fossil endocranial morphology with comparative neuroanatomical information from extant primates, the present approach provides a quantitative framework for generating and testing hypotheses about regional brain evolution in extinct hominins.

Article.Title: Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity
Article.Authors: Yeo J.; Chae J.; Kwon S.; Han J.; Kusen I.; Lim J.; Lee H.; Kim H.; Haam S.; Cheong J.; Kim T.; Moon S.; Jung Y.; Lee J.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: Wnt proteins regulate adult tissue homeostasis and repair by driving stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. High-performance Wnt preparations have enormous therapeutic potential, especially alongside various stem cell technologies. Currently, a major limitation of most Wnt preparations is that they inevitably require fetal bovine serum (FBS) or detergents to maintain Wnt solubility and activity. Recently, afamin (AFM) was identified as a serum factor that solubilizes Wnt3a in conditioned media (CM), obviating the requirement for animal sera. Here, we show that serum albumin (SA) helps maintain the activity and stability of AFM-solubilized Wnt3a in CM, likely through a stabilizing effect. We further demonstrate, using test-tube assays, that SA alone efficiently solubilizes purified Wnt3a (pWnt3a) independently of AFM. This approach enables the conversion of conventional detergent-solubilized pWnt3a (CHAPS-pWnt3a) into SA-pWnt3a through dialysis-mediated detergent removal. Together, these findings define a simple and robust SA-based strategy for preserving Wnt3a activity, addressing a long-standing challenge in both experimental and therapeutic settings.

Article.Title: Dysregulation of the Hippo pathway enhances PD-L2 transcription to promote immune evasion in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ando T.; Okamoto K.; Sato K.; Goto Y.; Izumi H.; Kataoka N.; Ueda Y.; Kobayashi Y.; Omachi K.; Maeda Y.; Furusho H.; Iglesias-Bartolome R.; Yoshimoto T.; Shintani T.; Yanamoto S.; Miyauchi M.; Gutkind J.; Kajiya M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Hippo pathway and its downstream effectors, YAP/TAZ, exhibit aberrant regulation in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, facilitating cancer cell growth. However, the influence of YAP/TAZ on cancer immune evasion remains poorly understood. Herein, we show that cancer patients harboring mutations regulating the Hippo pathway and YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may be sensitized to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy owing to genome instability and PD-L2 expression. LATS1/2 deletion, accompanied by YAP/TAZ hyperactivation, was associated with loss of squamous differentiation and genome instability, which may contribute to elevated DNA damage. Our data suggest that YAP/TAZ may recruit TEAD, BRD4, and RNA polymerase Ⅱ to the super-enhancer and promoter regions of PD-L1 and PD-L2 . YAP/TAZ predominantly contribute to PD-L2 expression, which is associated with Stat3 activation, partially enhancing PD-L1 transcription. YAP/TAZ-activated cells can be targeted by antigen-specific T cells but evade them through PD-L2. These findings suggest that Hippo pathway alterations and associated YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may serve as potential prognostic factors for stratifying patients undergoing ICI therapy. Targeting YAP/TAZ/TEAD could offer a promising treatment avenue for cancers harboring YAP/TAZ hyperactivation.

Article.Title: Hdac3 shapes adipocyte size, death susceptibility, macrophage turnover, and vascular remodeling in a mouse model of obesity
Article.Authors: Coppi L.; Severi I.; Bonacina F.; Villa S.; Peri C.; Longo R.; Senzacqua M.; Perugini J.; Galli C.; Pedretti S.; Mitro N.; Catapano A.; Norata G.; Giordano A.; De Fabiani E.; Crestani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The crosstalk between adipocytes and macrophages is crucial in adipose tissue biology. The aim of this study was to investigate the role of adipocyte-expressed histone deacetylase 3 (Hdac3) on adipose tissue plasticity and immune cell composition in response to high-fat feeding. Here we show that adipocyte-specific deletion of Hdac3 gene in mice affects the response to high-fat overload, by reducing fat mass and adipocyte size in visceral fat of knockout mice. In the absence of adipocyte Hdac3, visceral fat shows vascular remodeling and increased macrophage content. Colocalization of F4/80 with Ki-67 indicates proliferation of resident macrophages. This is coupled with increased crown-like structures and adipocyte death in visceral fat of knockout mice, exacerbated by high-fat feeding. Hdac3 silencing in cultured adipocytes and inactivation in mice promotes a pro-apoptotic microenvironment, as assessed by positivity to Annexin V and cleaved Caspase 3. In conclusion, we propose that Hdac3 acts as a rheostat in visceral fat, differentially affecting lipid accumulation and adipocyte size during the progress of high fat diet (HFD) feeding, and limiting cell death, vascularization, and macrophage proliferation, in a mouse model of obesity.

Article.Title: Relationship between X chromosome mosaicism, neuroanatomy and cognitive performance in females
Article.Authors: Karipidis I.; Klabunde M.; Jordan T.; Chromik L.; Hosseini S.; Reiss A.; Hong D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Females have two X chromosomes, one of which is inactivated early in development with specific regions and genes ‘escaping’ inactivation. Thus, X chromosome loss putatively results in decreased ‘dosage’ of X chromosome escapee and pseudoautosomal genes, impacting downstream pathways. Evidence from Turner syndrome indicates that X chromosome monosomy results in consistent neuroanatomical and cognitive phenotypes. However, it remains unclear whether mosaic karyotypes, with mixed proportions of 45X and 46XX cells, attenuate these phenotypes. We examined whether X chromosome mosaicism is predicted by neuroanatomical and cognitive features. Higher proportion of 46XX cells was significantly predicted by structural properties in somatosensory, motor, visual, and language brain areas, and by performance in visuospatial, fine-motor, and language tasks. Thus, mosaicism partially ‘rescues’ phenotypes linked to full 45X monosomy and may explain the role of the X chromosome not only across heterogeneous phenotypic expression in females, but also in sex differences observed in neuropsychiatric conditions.

Article.Title: FLASHS reveals multiscale spatial gene programs at atlas scale
Article.Authors: Yang C.; Zhang X.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue architecture, but detecting spatially variable genes at atlas scale remains difficult because biologically relevant patterns are multiscale, sparse, and often non-parametric. Here we show that FlashS, a frequency-domain kernel test using random Fourier features, sparse sketching, and a kurtosis-corrected null, retains Gaussian-kernel flexibility at near-linear per-gene cost without permutation. Across 50 benchmark datasets spanning 9 spatial transcriptomics platforms, F lash S achieves the highest ranking accuracy among 14 compared methods while maintaining calibrated inference under simulation and full-atlas permutation. In human heart tissue, it recovers a mitochondrial biogenesis program that co-localizes with ventricular cardiomyocytes. On the Allen Brain MERFISH atlas containing 3.94 million cells, F lash S completes in minutes on a single workstation and separates biological signal from negative-control barcodes even when p-values saturate.

Article.Title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies
Article.Authors: Patel K.; Zhao X.; Xie Z.; Zhi D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

Article.Title: Single-cell and spatial mapping reveals GCLC+ mesenchymal tumor cells linked with favorable outcomes in TNBC
Article.Authors: Girnius N.; Vallius T.; Chen W.; Launonen I.; Palomino-Echeverria S.; Lin J.; Mills C.; Kauppila S.; Kronqvist P.; Ellonen A.; Perala M.; Withnell E.; Chen Y.; Secrier M.; Santagata S.; Sorger P.; Färkkilä A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oxidative stress response (OSR) is suggested as a therapeutic target in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, the cell type specificity and spatial distribution of OSR genes and proteins remain poorly defined. We re-analyzed public datasets, demostrating high OSR gene expression in TNBC tumor cells. We generated a multiplex immunofluorescence dataset of 345 TNBC samples that showed OSR proteins GCLC and NQO1 are differentially expressed across tumor, immune, and stromal cells, and elevated in inflamed regions. We identified a mesenchymal-like tumor cell state characterized by co-expression of GCLC and vimentin (GCLC⁺VIM⁺), with increased proliferation and reduced anastasis-associated signatures, suggesting a vulnerability to chemotherapy. Consistently, TNBC cell lines with higher GCLC expression showed increased sensitivity to cisplatin. Moreover, patients with higher proportions of GCLC⁺VIM⁺ tumor cells had longer overall survival. Our findings indicate that OSR proteins are expressed in spatially and phenotypically distinct tumor microenvironments, and that the GCLC⁺VIM⁺ tumor cell state is associated with favorable outcomes in TNBC.

Article.Title: Anatid herpesvirus 1 US10 recruits TRIM13 to ubiquitinate STING for autophagic degradation and immune suppression
Article.Authors: Tian Y.; Tian B.; Xiao Z.; Ran R.; Cai D.; Wang M.; Wu Y.; Yang Q.; Zhang S.; Zhu D.; Liu M.; Zhao X.; Sun D.; Huang J.; Ou X.; Wu Z.; He Y.; Pan Y.; Jia R.; Chen S.; Cheng A.
Article.Abstract: The innate immune response is central to antiviral defense, and viruses have evolved sophisticated evasion strategies. Anatid Herpesvirus 1 (AnHV-1) is a pathogenic alphaherpesvirus causing immunosuppression with economic and biosecurity impacts, yet its evasion of immune signaling pathways remains poorly understood. Here we show that AnHV-1 tegument protein US10 suppresses innate immunity by targeting stimulator of interferon genes (STING) for autophagosome-lysosome degradation. US10 associates with STING and binds the autophagy-related protein microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B), enhancing delivery to lysosomes. Mechanistically, US10 recruits E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing protein 13 (TRIM13) and induces stress in the endoplasmic reticulum through the Protein kinase R-like Reticulum Kinase (PERK). These synergistic actions inhibit type I interferon (IFN-I) production and IFN-stimulated gene expression. Deletion of US10 reduces viral replication and pathogenicity while enhancing immune activation in cells and animals. Our findings uncover a dual autophagy-based mechanism of immune evasion and highlight potential therapeutic targets against AnHV-1 and related alphaherpesviruses.

Article.Title: Individualized morphometric-similarity deviations in autism linked to cortical hierarchy and microarchitecture
Article.Authors: Mamat M.; Chen Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: A bstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is marked by profound neurobiological heterogeneity, yet it remains unclear whether atypical brain organization reflects a diffuse low-amplitude pattern shared broadly across individuals or distinct spatially specific deviations that vary from person to person. Resolving this question requires methods that move beyond group averages to map individualized cortical atypicality against normative expectations. We built subject-level morphometric similarity networks in which edges quantify multivariate morphometric similarity between cortical regions. We then applied hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) normative models to estimate region-wise deviations from age- and sex-adjusted norms while accounting for site variation. Individuals with ASD carried a greater burden of extreme regional deviations, yet those deviations were focal and idiosyncratic rather than uniformly distributed. The spatial pattern of deviation aligned with canonical cortical hierarchies, shifting similarity toward sensory and visual poles and away from association cortex. Moreover, edge-level testing identified a sparse reconfiguration concentrated in occipito-temporal and cross-network connections. Clustering of individual deviation maps identified two robust subgroups that differ in the global sign of deviation and in their cognitive and molecular correlates. These results show that cortical atypicality in ASD is constrained by brain gradients, expressed in subgroup-specific forms, and linked to distinct biological and cognitive axes.

Article.Title: Maltreatment predicts centiles of individual variation from normative brain growth in children
Article.Authors: Mohn J.; Bauer M.; Hoffmann F.; Rasmussen J.; Tietze A.; Entringer S.; Winter S.; Buss C.; Heim C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to maltreatment in childhood is posited to profoundly disrupt brain development with adverse consequences for cognitive development and health across the lifespan. Here we use “brain charts” from the largest available neuroimaging database to quantify individual brain volumes relative to normative brain growth distributions in 299 children, aged 3 to 13 years, including 123 children with clinically verified maltreatment exposure. Using magnetic resonance imaging, we obtain volumes of cortical grey, total white, and subcortical grey matter and derive chart-based centiles for each child and tissue type. In our sample, children with maltreatment exposure exhibit lower mean brain centiles across tissues than unexposed children. Associations of greater maltreatment severity with lower brain centiles do not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Lower brain centiles are associated with lower intellectual ability and more behavioural problems. These findings provide evidence for widespread differences in brain structure associated with childhood maltreatment and their relevance to intellectual ability and behavioural functioning.

Article.Title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Aziz N.; Kortagere S.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

Article.Title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang Z.; Huang Z.; Yu X.; Wang Z.; Qiu H.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. Yet it remains difficult to quantify, at genome scale, how histone-modification landscapes encode these burst kinetics. Here we show that DeepBurst, a deep learning model, predicts gene-specific burst-frequency and burst-size regimes from histone-modification profiles around transcription start sites. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

Article.Title: Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
Article.Authors: Janshoff S.; Sirkinti L.; Nocke M.; Bechtel T.; Gömer A.; Brüggemann Y.; Steinmann E.; Brown R.; Todt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

Article.Title: Identification of candidate key genes involved in natural rubber biosynthesis in Periploca sepium
Article.Authors: Lu G.; Yong J.; An Y.; Lang S.; Zhang H.; Chen R.
Article.Abstract: Natural rubber is a critical industrial material facing supply shortages. Periploca sepium has emerged as a promising alternative for producing the rubber component cis-polyisoprene. To investigate its biosynthesis, we performed genome and transcriptome sequencing. Our results indicate that this plant possesses complete mevalonic acid (MVA), 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate/2-C-methyl-D-erythritol-4-phosphate (DXP/MEP), and polyisoprene pathways, as well as contains corresponding rubber particle membrane proteins. Using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, we identified 11 key genes positively correlated with levels of cis-polyisoprene and precursor allylic diphosphates (IPP/DMAPP, GPP, FPP, GGPP). Overexpressing acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, and 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate reductoisomerase genes from the MVA and DXP/MEP pathways in P. sepium increased IPP/DMAPP levels. Molecular docking and enzyme assays indicated that cis-prenyltransferase exhibits the highest affinity for FPP, suggesting it is the dominant initiator of IPP condensation in cis-polyisoprene biosynthesis. Overexpressing the FPP synthase gene enhanced FPP levels, leading to increased cis-poly7isoprene content. Overexpressing cis-prenyltransferase, small rubber particle protein, and rubber elongation factor genes, especially in combination, significantly raised cis-polyisoprene content and high-molecular-weight proportions. These findings demonstrate that targeted gene up-regulation can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium. The candidate key genes involved in rubber biosynthesis in P. sepium were identified via genome and transcriptome sequencing combined with WGCNA. Up-regulation of the key genes by overexpression, especially in combination, can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium.

Article.Title: In vivo replication of a fully functional nerve net in a clonally reproducing animal
Article.Authors: Sakib E.; Hofacker L.; Noack C.; Ströbel F.; Giez C.; Wittlieb J.; Klimovich A.; Bosch T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nerve nets are considered the evolutionarily oldest form of nervous system. How such networks develop and how complex nervous systems become fully functional is largely unknown. In a phylogenetically ancient animal, the freshwater polyp Hydra , we demonstrate how a nerve net consisting of distinct neuronal populations is precisely replicated over the course of asexual proliferation by budding. During this process, precursor cells first accumulate at the site of the emerging neural network, followed by a stepwise formation of functional neural circuits composed of distinct neuronal populations. These circuits become arranged according to an accurately controlled spatiotemporal pattern and take control of behaviors independently of the existing parental network. Since similar processes also govern the formation of more complex nervous systems in other invertebrates and vertebrates, we suggest that the basic requirements for a neuronal network to replicate were already in place at the beginning of the evolution of the nervous system.

Article.Title: Evolution towards higher unitary conductance in mammals makes BK channels more efficient and precise
Article.Authors: Hepburn I.; Hellemans S.; Taniguchi T.; Bourguignon T.; De Schutter E.
Article.Abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. Mammalian BK channels are distinguished by an exceptionally high unitary conductance (~250 pS), while invertebrates exhibit a significantly lower unitary conductance. We confirmed the evolutionary trend to high unitary conductance and used computational models to examine how differences in unitary conductance affect calcium activation of BK channels and influence neuronal dynamics. We show that mammalian BK channels are activated more efficiently by calcium and generate stronger repolarizing currents than lower unitary conductance channels. Channels with lower unitary conductance require greater channel density in the cell membrane, leading to stronger competition for calcium and reduced activation. In contrast, high unitary conductance channels minimize competition, enabling more effective activation and repolarization. Incorporating these channel properties into a neuronal model revealed that mammalian-type BK channels enhance spike-timing precision, consistent with the evolution of fine motor control and advanced neuronal processing in mammals.

Article.Title: Pooled CRISPR screens identify genes and non-coding genomic regions that regulate red blood cell density
Article.Authors: Brosseau N.; Pincez T.; Lo K.; Lo C.; Beaudoin M.; Lettre G.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Genome-wide association studies have identified >1,000 loci associated with clinically important red blood cell (RBC) traits, such as hemoglobin concentration and cell volume. However, few of these associations have been characterized at the molecular level such that most causal genes and variants remain elusive. Here, we performed pooled CRISPR screens in an erythroid cell line to identify genes and regulatory non-coding sequences that control RBC density. We perturbed 556 candidate genes and genomic sequences near 2,114 GWAS variants. We used a density gradient to detect the impact of these CRISPR perturbations on cell density. After validation, we found 17 genes and 13 regions near GWAS variants that regulate cell density. Some of these genes have previously been implicated in RBC biology (e.g. ATP2B4 , CCND3 , EPOR ) although many are novel (e.g. CHTF8 , CTU2 , DNASE2 ). We confirmed that deletions in the osmotic stress response kinase gene OXSR1 increase cell density, and a phosphoproteome analysis in OXSR1-depleted cells indicated that this phenotype is accompanied with a dephosphorylation of the upstream kinase WNK1 and the downstream target KCC3 ( SLC12A6 ). We also combined CRISPR perturbations and RNA-sequencing to show how a non-coding genomic sequence near rs13255015 regulates the expression of the transcription factor ZFAT in cis and SLC4A1 in trans . SLC4A1 encodes Band3, a known regulator of RBC hydration and volume. Our results suggest experimental strategies to characterize GWAS findings and provide new molecular insights into the regulation of complex RBC traits.

Article.Title: Distinct roles of the Lyve1 lineage in mouse heart development
Article.Authors: Klaourakis K.; Kulkarni S.; Zvonickova K.; Kalisch-Smith J.; Smart N.; Sparrow D.; Jackson D.; Riley P.; Vieira J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The genetic mouse model Lyve1 Cre is widely used to study lymphatic endothelial cells, but its activity in the embryonic heart has not been comprehensively defined. Here we show that the Lyve1 lineage contributes to multiple cardiovascular cell types, including venous endothelium of the sinus venosus forming coronary vessels, endocardial cells generating complementary coronary territories and valve structures, lymphatic endothelial cells required for cardiac lymphatic development, and tissue-resident macrophages within the embryonic myocardium. Functional perturbations studies show that Notch1 gain-of-function in Lyve1 + lineages disrupts vascular development, whereas Prox1 deletion causes severe edema, blood-filled lymphatics, and perinatal lethality. Mid-gestation mutants exhibit underdeveloped blood-filled lymphatics despite intact blood vasculature, and by late gestation cardiac lymphatics are largely depleted. These findings reveal distinct cardiovascular roles of the Lyve1 lineage and establish Lyve1 Cre as a versatile but non-specific model, underscoring the need for careful interpretation when investigating heart development and regeneration.

Article.Title: Threshold-free neural network models for swim bout detection of larval zebrafish
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Kroeschell G.; Zhu Y.; Mumm J.; Yi J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of swim bouts is essential for decoding motor behavior in larval zebrafish, yet conventional threshold-based methods rely on subjective cutoffs and per-experiment tuning. To address this limitation, we developed threshold-free deep learning models operating on tail-curvature time series: an offline model for post hoc analysis and an online model for real-time detection. Both improved precision over threshold-based methods, particularly for low-amplitude bouts. Using the offline model, we show that a head-fixed, closed-loop preparation largely preserves naturalistic swimming kinematics. Repeated trials reduced bout frequency and increased interbout interval, whereas genetic background primarily affects bout duration and maximum amplitude; notably, casper larvae lacked the late-trial decline observed in wildtype and nacre. We further show that detector choice can alter inferred behavioral outcomes. Together, these results establish a high-throughput framework for robust and reproducible analysis of zebrafish swimming behavior across experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Extragonadal role of FSH in regulating corneal homeostasis in Keratoconus
Article.Authors: Chatterjee A.; Kanu L.; Ross A.; Yeung V.; Boychev N.; Venkateswaran N.; Saeed H.; Yang M.; Hutcheon A.; Ciolino J.
Article.Abstract: Keratoconus (KC) is a multifactorial, progressive, ectatic disease of the cornea, which often manifests during puberty. Using a 3D collagen hydrogel system, co-culture models, and patient-derived tears, we found the following: FSH levels were low in KC patients; FSH supplementation inhibited MAP kinase signaling, leading to decreased MMP2 activity and increased collagen accumulation; FSH increased pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion, driving macrophage polarization, migration, and tunneling nanotube formation; FSH regulated the HDAC1-miR-29b feedback loop in chromatin immunoprecipitation and overexpression studies; Gene ontology linked FSH to leukocyte adhesion and extravasation; and Motif analysis identified NF-Y as a possible HDAC1-interacting partner. Collectively, FSH plays a dual role in keratoconus by regulating collagen accumulation through the MAP Kinase-MMP2 axis and inflammation through the HDAC1-miR-29b pathway. Human patient tears, 3D corneal hydrogel model, and co-culture model were used to identify the role of FSH in the cornea. We found that the FSH played a dual role in the regulation of corneal extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation.

Article.Title: PATZ1 remodels the nucleosome landscape to promote chromatin accessibility in injured neurons
Article.Authors: Krishna N.; Menon A.; Kumaran M.; Kesireddy D.; Venkatesh I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adult central nervous system neurons fail to regenerate after injury, in part due to epigenetic constraints that maintain a growth-restrictive chromatin state. Here we use nucleosome-resolution profiling to reveal that PATZ1 induces widespread nucleosome eviction at regeneration-associated gene loci. PATZ1 treatment dramatically reduces both nucleosome occupancy and fuzziness, indicating active chromatin remodeling rather than passive destabilization. This remodeling occurs preferentially at distal regulatory elements, where PATZ1 drives a greater than 3-fold expansion of H3K27ac-marked active enhancers. Nucleosome eviction at these sites precedes enhancer activation, establishing a mechanistic link between chromatin remodeling and transcriptional reprogramming. Our findings demonstrate that targeted nucleosome eviction at enhancers underlies PATZ1-mediated chromatin reorganization, providing mechanistic insight into how epigenetic barriers to CNS regeneration can be overcome.

Article.Title: Inhibition of DCLK1 promotes spinal cord injury recovery: implications for KATNA1 phosphorylation in microtubule-dependent neurite outgrowth
Article.Authors: Li S.; Ma A.; Lei C.; Meng Z.; Zhu J.; Zhang G.; Tan W.; Tan M.
Article.Abstract: Functional recovery after spinal cord injury (SCI) remains challenging, requiring therapeutic targets. Mechanistically, we identified the microtubule-severing protein KATNA1 as a downstream target of DCLK1. DCLK1 directly phosphorylated KATNA1 at threonine 118 (T118), suppressing its microtubule-severing activity. DCLK1 overexpression inhibited, whereas DCLK1 knockdown or inhibition enhanced KATNA1 function. The T118D mutation reduced KATNA1 activity, while T118A resisted DCLK1-mediated suppression. In neurons, DCLK1 inhibited KATNA1-induced neurite outgrowth, whereas DCLK1 inhibition restored this effect. Together, these results identify DCLK1 as a promising therapeutic target for SCI and reveal a mechanism by which DCLK1 regulates KATNA1 phosphorylation to modulate microtubule severing and neurite outgrowth.

Article.Title: Standardizing deoxygenation studies in coral biology
Article.Authors: Million W.; Alderdice R.; Dilernia N.; Kühl M.; Pacherres C.; Pernice M.; Randall C.; Skeer A.; Suggett D.; Voolstra C.; Camp E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deoxygenation, the global loss of biologically available oxygen (O 2 ) from the world’s oceans, presents a pervasive and intensifying threat for reef-building corals that will require coordinated efforts to understand and manage. However, recent expansion of coral deoxygenation experimentation has produced methodological gaps, limiting collective knowledge generation. Here, we show that growing divergence in this field arises primarily from differences in focal phenotypes, deoxygenation exposures, and experimental execution that together prevent biological from technical variation from being disentangled between studies. To address this, we propose a series of recommendations to establish the foundation for a future standardized framework for coral deoxygenation methodology. Such efforts are critical to establish a robust consensus of scientific data to support effective management of reef deoxygenation. Waiting decades for diverging methodologies to prompt a call for standardization may be imprudent given the urgent threat of deoxygenation and the abundant methodological divergence present in coral deoxygenation experimentation.

Article.Title: SGLT2 inhibitors attenuate diabetic kidney disease by suppressing YAP dependent ferroptosis
Article.Authors: Feng L.; Feng C.; Li H.; Wang T.; Zhang H.; Zhao Y.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide renal protection in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) through mechanisms beyond glucose lowering, but these remain incompletely understood. In a diabetic rat model, dapagliflozin attenuates renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and fibrosis alongside reduced YAP activation and ferroptosis. In high-glucose-treated renal tubular epithelial cells, YAP promotes nuclear translocation, upregulates ACSL4 and transferrin receptor expression, induces iron accumulation and mitochondrial damage, and drives ferroptotic cell death. YAP knockdown and pharmacological inhibition both confirm an upstream regulatory role for YAP in ferroptosis. Mechanistically, YAP and TEAD4 enhance ACSL4 promoter activity through a conserved TEAD-binding motif, an effect suppressed by dapagliflozin. These findings identify the YAP/TEAD4-ACSL4 axis as a therapeutic target underlying glucose-independent renoprotection by SGLT2 inhibition.

Article.Title: Organelle associations and metabolic rewiring of size-defined hepatic lipid droplets
Article.Authors: Liao Q.; Fu X.; Wang Y.; Xu Y.; Cao Z.; Wang Y.; Pan B.; Wang J.; Liu P.; Yang Z.; Zhang S.

Moreover, comparative proteomics of fasted livers reveals a clear ‘division of labor’: Large LDs (L-LDs) function as specialized mitochondrion-coupled ‘putative fueling hubs’, whereas small LDs (S-LDs) serve as lysosome-coupled ‘putative trafficking and turnover hubs’. Crucially, in vivo stress recruits mitochondria to both pools, supporting a ‘parallel programs’ model where S-LD-associated mitochondria are hypothesized to power the energy-intensive degradative machinery. Article.Title: Vascular tree structure-based perfusion phantom fabrication using modified Hele-Shaw cell method
Article.Authors: Das S.; Rakshe M.; Sarkar S.; Paul R.; Marathe S.; Abraham N.; Gandhi P.; Varma H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tissue phantoms that mimic microvasculature and perfusion are essential for modelling vascular function, guiding interventions, and calibrating imaging systems, which require faithful replication of vascular geometry and flow. Conventional fabrication strategies, including wire-based molding, lithographic micromachining, and additive manufacturing, offer useful capabilities but remain constrained by predefined designs, rectangular channel cross-sections, limited scalability, and high production costs. Reliance on predefined digital vascular models restricts design flexibility and limits the ability to capture the natural variability and complexity of real vascular systems. Here, we present a lithography-free, fractal-generating approach based on a modified Lifted Hele–Shaw Cell (LHSC) technique, in which vascular networks emerge spontaneously via interfacial fluid instabilities. Unlike pre-designed methods, these structures are governed by fluid properties and flow conditions, enabling adaptive, physiologically relevant geometries with smooth Gaussian cross-sections and natural diameter tapering. We demonstrate four phantom designs: a planar vascular tree, an anatomically guided cerebral network, a retinal vascular model, and a conformable curved substrate phantom. Validation using Laser Speckle Contrast Imaging confirms structural fidelity and physiologically relevant flow consistent with Murray’s law. This platform uniquely integrates realistic vascular architecture with emergent, fractal driven formation, highlighting its potential as a reproducible and biologically relevant alternative to conventional vascular phantom fabrication. Furthermore, the availability of such realistic in vitro vascular models can reduce reliance on animal experiments and contribute towards more ethical and sustainable preclinical research.

Article.Title: FOXO3 induces chromatin changes in a model of DNA damage-induced senescence
Article.Authors: Brown A.; Arevalo J.; Holcom A.; Finch A.; Maybury-Lewis S.; McNamara A.; Webb A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract FOXO transcription factors are critical for cellular homeostasis and have been implicated in longevity in several species. We find that FOXO3 functions as a pioneer factor in human cells, directly altering chromatin accessibility to regulate gene expression. Unexpectedly, FOXO3’s pioneer activity at many sites is achieved through a two-step process, in which chromatin accessibility is initially reduced, then transitions to an open conformation. The direct FOXO3 network comprises chromatin remodelers, including the SWI/SNF remodeling complex, which we find is functionally required for FOXO3 activity. We also identify a novel secondary network of activator protein-1 (AP-1) transcription factors deployed by FOXO3, which orchestrate a neuronal-specific subnetwork. Together, this hierarchical FOXO3 pioneer network regulates key cellular processes including metabolism, proteostasis, epigenetics and proliferation, which must be tightly controlled under changing conditions that accompany aging.

Article.Authors: Simmons C.; Behrmann M.; Ayzenberg V.
Article.Abstract: The processes of recognizing objects and acting upon or with them have traditionally been attributed to computations associated with ventral and dorsal visual pathways, respectively. The results revealed substantial spatial overlap in connectivity in the networks generated from a dorsal and a ventral seed - with the greater similarity of these object networks within an individual than the similarity of each network separately across individuals. This overlap persisted for both tools and non-tools even after controlling for the shared variance between pathways. Article.Title: Phospholipid remodeling of the cardiomyocyte membrane affects cardiac function
Article.Authors: Bujo S.; Fujiwara T.; Kubota M.; Toko H.; Kawana H.; Kano K.; Ito M.; Ishizuka M.; Umei M.; Kadowaki H.; Zhai B.; Kishikawa R.; Takeda N.; Harada M.; Takeda N.; Aoki J.; Komuro I.

LPLAT7/LPGAT1 suppression induced myocardial contractile dysfunction associated with cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) activation and abnormal calcium handling, partially rescued by pharmacological PKA inhibition. Conversely, Lplat7/Lpgat1 overexpression partially improved pressure overload-induced cardiac dysfunction with selective restoration of PC(40:6), a major stearic acid/DHA-enriched PC species. These findings highlight the contributory role of LPLAT7/LPGAT1-dependent membrane PL remodeling in cardiac function and heart failure. Cardiomyocyte LPLAT7/LPGAT1 regulates membrane phospholipid composition and cardiac function. Its loss reduces stearic acid- and DHA-enriched phosphatidylcholine and causes PKA activation, abnormal calcium handling, and contractile dysfunction, whereas overexpression partially improves pressure overload-induced dysfunction

Article.Title: A Colletotrichum orbiculare-based fungal model recapitulates conserved cellular defects of Niemann–Pick type C disease and enables therapeutic evaluation
Article.Authors: Sano H.; Takezawa S.; Saomoto N.; Chiba A.; Tanaka C.; Kato N.; Nishiuchi T.; Nishisaka H.; Kitatani K.; Kodama S.; Kubo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Niemann–Pick type C disease is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in NPC1 or NPC2 , leading to lipid accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration. Current mammalian models recapitulate major pathological features but are limited by long disease courses and low throughput. Here, we establish the plant-pathogenic fungus Colletotrichum orbiculare as a scalable eukaryotic model of Niemann–Pick type C disease. Introduction of disease-associated mutations into fungal NPC1 or NPC2 homologs abolishes pathogenicity, showing that NPC dysfunction compromises lipid-dependent morphogenesis required for host penetration. Conversely, human NPC1 partially restores fungal infection. Together, these findings support functional conservation of NPC-dependent cellular processes across kingdoms. Miglustat and 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin restore pathogenicity through distinct lipid pathways. These complementary modes of rescue indicate that NPC1 and NPC2 dysfunction converges on lipid-dependent morphogenesis closely linked to actin organization. By connecting lipid metabolism, actin organization, and pharmacological rescue to a measurable infection outcome, this fungal model provides a tractable and scalable platform for mechanistic and therapeutic exploration.
