Article.Title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation
Article.Authors: Tawk C.; Saab G.; Abdallah G.; El Khoury J.; Aouad R.
Article.Abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.

Article.Abstract: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines prevent new infections but do not treat established HPV-associated lesions, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies targeting viral tumor antigens. Article.Abstract: Retrobulbar block is widely used for vitreoretinal surgery, but the conventional transcutaneous technique advances a sharp needle blindly through the lower eyelid. Article.Title: Critical analysis of the new European framework for non-fossil flexibility and the questions left unanswered
Article.Authors: Mastropietro P.; Rodilla P.; Chaves Ávila J.
Article.Abstract: The 2024 Electricity Market Design Reform introduced a new European framework for non-fossil flexibility. The first national flexibility needs assessments were published in July 2026, and indicative objectives and support schemes for non-fossil flexibility will soon be introduced. However, we argue that this new framework, which will influence the development of European power systems as they transition to low-carbon resources, is based on a flawed theoretical foundation and exhibits significant overlap with the European resource adequacy framework. No flexibility metric has been defined for the flexibility needs assessment. No flexibility standard/target has been calculated based on the economic equilibrium between the cost of additional flexibility and the cost of not relying on it. We identify three underlying metrics for flexibility needs, we present alternative approaches to define flexibility products and identify open questions that need to be addressed before the new flexibility framework moves to the implementation phase.

These findings identify a frequency-dependent bottleneck in VPL-to-S1FL transfer, rather than local cortical responsiveness, as a constraint on sustained cortical expression of temporally dense sensory input.

Article.Authors: Atouife M.; Jenkins J.
Article.Abstract: Forecasting the cost evolution of emerging clean technologies is crucial for informed policy, investment, and decarbonization decisions, yet it remains deeply uncertain. Article.Abstract: Broad-spectrum antimicrobials profoundly alter gut microbial ecosystems; however, post-antimicrobial recovery remains incompletely understood. Article.Title: The lagged and cumulative effects of permafrost and seasonally frozen soil on water use efficiency in the Qilian Mountains, Northwest China

Article.Abstract: Permafrost in the Qilian Mountains is highly sensitive to climate change, affecting ecosystem energy, water, and carbon cycling. Article.Title: Unrealized optimal designs challenge models of constraint in early vertebrate evolution
Article.Authors: Leflaëc E.; Ballell A.; Sanisidro O.; Ferrón H.
Article.Abstract: Jawed vertebrates dominate modern vertebrate diversity, whereas most jawless vertebrate lineages disappeared during the Devonian. Combining photocatalysis with renewable energy and water treatment could offer a practical route to microplastic management, provided catalyst recovery, toxicity, and scale-up challenges are addressed.

Article.Abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60–70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

This review summarizes bTBI advances in experimental models, research techniques, primary/secondary pathological mechanisms, neurobehavioral phenotypes, and prognostic factors, differentiating animal and clinical evidence. Article.Title: Multimodal in vitro biocompatibility assessment of functionalized PEDOT neural interfaces

Article.Abstract: Conductive polymers such as poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) have emerged as promising neural interface materials due to their favorable electrochemical and mechanical properties. However, biological assessment of new bioelectrode coatings remains dependent on conventional cytotoxicity assays and animal studies, providing limited insight into cell-material interactions. Here, we present a multimodal in vitro framework for evaluating the biocompatibility of functionalized PEDOT coatings as neural interfaces. Standard PEDOT:PSS, functionalized PEDOT:polydopamine (PDA), and PEDOT:dopamine-grafted hyaluronic acid (DAHA) coatings were characterized electrochemically and assessed using SH-SY5Y cells through viability measurements, profilometry, 3D reconstruction, immunofluorescence imaging, and targeted gene expression analysis. Article.Title: Transcriptomic conservation defines autoimmune stem-like T cells and uncovers their dependence on Apex1
Article.Authors: Kousnetsov R.; Pirogovsky K.; Hawiger D.
Article.Abstract: Stem-like T cells (T STEM ) critically govern autoimmune responses. Unlike individual transcriptional master regulators of specialized T cells, the primary molecular determinant of T STEM , Tcf1, is shared with naive and other T cells. To unequivocally identify autoimmune T STEM , we established transcriptomic characteristics conserved across multiple immunological settings. We leveraged such conserved features to faithfully distinguish T STEM arising de novo among other Tcf1 + T cells and confirmed their autoimmune functions in vivo in a model of multiple sclerosis. We further detected the transcriptomically identifiable T STEM in corresponding human diseases, and among such T cells we uncovered a specifically increased expression of apurinic/apyrimidinic endodeoxyribonuclease 1 ( APEX1 ). By rigorously investigating Apex1-deficient T STEM in a disease model, we confirmed indispensable roles of Apex1 in governing the disease-producing functions of autoimmune T STEM . Article.Title: Sequence of aerobic and resistance exercise influences short- and long-term glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: A randomized trial
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Zha Y.; Chen B.; Jia Y.; Chen Y.; Zhang Z.; Wei L.; Sun Z.; Tan X.

Aerobic exercise was performed on bicycle ergometers for 30 min at 40%–70% heart-rate reserve; resistance exercise targeted major muscle groups at 60%–80% 1RM. Compared with pre-exercise levels, mean glucose ( p = 0.043) and HbA1c ( p = 0.007) decreased only in AR group. At week 8, AR showed lower glucose during exercise and recovery ( p = 0.036) and greater nocturnal glucose reduction ( p = 0.015) than RA. Article.Abstract: Abstract Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), also known as myositis, are a rare and heterogeneous group of autoimmune disorders characterized by chronic inflammation of skeletal muscle. Article.Title: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in Drosophila
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sensory processing relies on an intricate interplay between specialized sensory circuits and the broader brain. Feedforward neurons form an information bottleneck, consolidating diverse visual features from the OL and distributing them through modular pathways for higher-order processing. Feedback neurons densely innervate OL structures, conveying contextual signals in the central brain via precise recurrent loops. Bilateral neurons link local visual circuits across the two OLs, providing a substrate for inter-ocular processing. These findings reveal how early visual pathways interface with brainwide circuits to support diverse brain functions and enable context-dependent flexibility in sensory computation. Article.Authors: Bartsoen E.; Vloeberghs R.; Saberi P.; Desender K.; Wöhr M.
Article.Abstract: Rats display advanced empathic abilities, yet current research is focused on empathy toward negative affect, largely neglecting positive affective states. It relies on ethotransmission (i.e., acoustic emotional communication) of affective states to conspecifics via ultrasonic vocalizations (USV), i.e., alarming 22-kHz USV (negative affect) and laughter-like 50-kHz USV (positive affect). Specifically, we subjected rats to playback of 22-kHz or 50-kHz USV, while assessing their acoustic startle response (ASR), which is known to be emotionally modulated (i.e., potentiated and attenuated by negative and positive affect, respectively). Article.Abstract: Across the animal kingdom, olfactory dysfunction and anosmia have been associated with disruptions in sleep. In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, various studies have demonstrated that broadly inhibiting olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) similarly disrupts sleep/wake cycles, suggesting that baseline ORN signaling is an integral component of olfactory modulation of sleep. However, due to the diversity of ORNs and combinatorial nature of olfactory processing, many of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which ORNs modulate sleep remain unclear. In this study, we addressed this gap of knowledge by characterizing the contributions of different ensembles of ORNs, individual ORN types, and a known modulator of ORNs on baseline sleep architecture. We find that the activity of distinct ORN types are important for day and nighttime sleep and heterogeneously shape parameters of sleep architecture. Importantly, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are adjusted across mating status, suggesting that distinct ORN types are recruited within the context of sleep depending on the demands of the animal. Furthermore, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are in part shaped by heterogeneous serotonin (5-HT) receptor expression. Together, this work identifies cellular and molecular pathways bridging olfaction and sleep, and helps establish a circuit model that can be used to further characterize the behavioral consequences of sensory dysfunction.

Article.Title: An explainable machine-learning framework for seasonal early warning of West Nile virus using predictive climate data
Article.Authors: Pappa A.; Kioutsioukis I.
Article.Abstract: Reliable early-warning systems capable of forecasting West Nile virus (WNV) outbreaks months before the transmission season remain limited. We developed an explainable machine-learning framework that uses seasonal climate forecasts rather than in-season reanalysis, combined with epidemiological, climatic, hydroclimatic, demographic, land-cover, and spatial predictors. The model was independently evaluated under real-world conditions at municipal and regional scales in Greece during 2022–2025 and across 887 areas in 14 European countries during 2022–2024. Explainability analysis identified epidemiological memory, seasonal temperature, hydroclimatic persistence, and environmental suitability as key determinants of outbreak risk. Across Europe, the model detected 89% of outbreaks in previously unaffected areas, demonstrating transferability and the potential of integrating prospective climate information with epidemiological history to support targeted WNV surveillance, vector control, and public health preparedness. Skill losses were not attributable to climate forecast errors, highlighting the value of higher frequency epidemiological surveillance (mosquitoes, sentinels) data, which are rarely publicly available.

Article.Title: Nemo-like kinase limits T cell activation while preserving anti-tumor responses
Article.Authors: Peer S.; Koutník J.; Thuille N.; Siegmund K.; Klepsch V.; Pfeiffer M.; Humer D.; Bantsich P.; Olson W.; Albrecht-Schgoer K.; Baier G.; Gruber T.
Article.Abstract: T cell dysfunction limits the efficacy of cancer immunity, yet the molecular checkpoints that preserve T cell function within the tumor microenvironment are not fully understood. In this study, we identify a previously unrecognized, T cell-intrinsic role for nemo-like kinase (NLK) as a critical mediator of sustained anti-tumor responses. In our experiments, NLK emerged as a dual-function modulator: although NLK deficiency in CD4 + and CD8 + T cells increases proliferation and cytokine production in vitro via enhanced NFAT and AP-1 activation, its loss in vivo paradoxically impairs tumor control. In murine tumor models, NLK-deficient tumor-infiltrating T cells exhibit blunted effector activity resulting in accelerated tumor progression. Conversely, human chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells that overexpress NLK demonstrate superior killing capacity toward target tumor cells. These findings establish NLK as an essential early brake on T cell activation while protecting against their chronic dysfunction, and reveal a molecular pathway that sustains anti-tumor immunity.

Article.Title: Neurocognition of dance: Guidelines for using dance as model behavior and research subject in cognitive neuroscience
Article.Authors: Meletaki V.; Christensen J.; Darda K.; Rai L.; Orlandi A.
Article.Abstract: Dance and movement science bridges cognitive psychology, neuroscience, cultural studies, philosophical aesthetics, and the performing arts. The field has evolved significantly, examining physical, social, psychological, and neural aspects of dance and movement execution and perception, contributing to a deeper understanding of human cognition and of dance itself. As the field expands, shared guidelines that support methodological rigor, reproducibility, and cultural relevance are of paramount importance. This paper synthesizes current research and introduces a comprehensive seven-principle research design framework for using dance in cognitive neuroscience. Key elements include the operationalization of "dance" in empirical sciences, the definition of who is a dancer, measures of expertise, and the importance of a culturally sensitive, holistic, and interdisciplinary approach to its investigation in the laboratory and in ecologically valid settings. This framework benefits research in dance and movement aesthetics, as well as investigations in social cognition, affective neuroscience, computer science, and artificial intelligence.

Article.Authors: Kheyfets V.; Sweatt A.; Zhang H.; Li M.; Hu C.; Nemkov T.; Aizin M.; Heerdt P.; Dzieciatkowska M.; Stephenson D.; LaCroix I.; D’Alessandro A.; Cendali F.; Oldham W.; Hansen K.; Zamanian R.; Stenmark K.

Article.Title: Monocyte TNF superfamily receptor dysregulation in tuberculosis-type 2 diabetes mellitus comorbidity
Article.Authors: G N.; Radhakrishnan R.; GV J.; Suresh K.; Hissar S.; Vankayalapati R.; Pavan Kumar N.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases susceptibility to tuberculosis (TB) and contributes to immune dysregulation, partly through altered monocyte signaling. Although our earlier work has demonstrated that T2DM alters monocyte subsets and promotes hyper-inflammatory responses during TB, the mechanisms underlying dysregulated TNF superfamily pathways in TB-T2DM comorbidity are underexplored. A study cohort of 176 individuals (TB, TB-T2DM, T2DM-only, and healthy controls) was evaluated. Classical monocytes (CD14 + CD16 − ; n = 20/group) from peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry for cytokines and activation markers upon stimulation with purified protein derivative (PPD), whole-cell lysate (WCL), and TLR2/4 ligands. Plasma TNF superfamily receptors ( n = 44/group) were quantified using Human ProcartaPlex 12-plex multiplex ELISA. Associations were analyzed using Spearman correlation, and integrated network analyses including protein-protein interaction (PPI), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and Gene Ontology (GO) were performed. In the results, TB-T2DM individuals exhibited significantly increased intercellular cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, IL-1β, IL-1α, IL-10, and TNF-α) and activation markers (PDL-2, CD163, and CD206) compared with TB or T2DM ( p < 0.05). Multiplex ELISA revealed significant decreases in CD137, CD40, GITR, TNFR1/2, and TRAIL-R1/R2 and increases in CD27, CD30, and Fas (APO-1) expression in TB-T2DM. Correlation analysis revealed weak-to-inverse associations between cytokine-associated markers and activation markers with multiple TNF-receptor superfamily members ( p < 0.05). PPI analysis identified a highly interconnected TNF superfamily network, with TNFRSF1A, TNFRSF9, and CD95 as central hubs and KEGG enrichment in cytokine signaling, NF-κB pathway, death signaling, and TNF receptor binding. Together, hyperglycemia-associated monocyte dysfunction alters TNF superfamily receptor expression and receptor-cytokine integration, contributing to impaired immune regulation in TB-T2DM comorbidity.

Article.Authors: Makkar H.; Meena J.; Mir R.; Gupta A.; Bakhshi S.; Chopra A.; Tanwar P.; Yadav R.; Singh L.; Goel H.; Pandey A.; Keshari P.; Bhattacharya S.; Majhi R.; Singh A.; Kaushik S.; Sarangarajan S.; Viswanathan G.; Dass J.; Pushpam D.; Seth R.

Epitypes were associated with survival, with E1 showing poorer outcomes than E2 and E3. Projection onto an independent pediatric AML cohort showed partial conservation of epitype-associated methylation programs. These findings suggest that epigenetic stratification can capture clinically relevant heterogeneity beyond conventional genomic classification.

Article.Authors: Zhao Z.; Dang K.; Zhou Z.; Peng Y.; Liu Y.; Zhan S.; Jiao S.; Wang Z.; Niu J.; Zheng Q.; Zhao D.; Fu L.; Dai Y.; Zhang P.; Gu P.; Wang Y.; Wan Q.; Wang Y.; Lv Y.; Chu W.; Yu Y.; Zhou X.; Qiu H.; Kang Z.; Ma M.

These findings support deep-learning-based fundus-image analysis for AS screening in real-world clinical settings, and retinal-structure analyses for exploring AS pathophysiology.

Article.Authors: Thakur B.; Alam J.; Cronin K.; Patel P.; Anasti K.; Pai Kane A.; Hossain A.; Do H.; Mansouri K.; Spence T.; Edwards R.; Pathirage R.; Janowska K.; Lella M.; Cook A.; Siliciano J.; Siliciano R.; Gnanakaran S.; Saunders K.; Haynes B.; Acharya P.; Alam S.

Structural comparisons revealed hinge points and regions of flexibility in the BCRs suggesting a highly dynamic structure of the BCR complex. Article.Title: Unveiling the failure behavior of rock and steel slag-based backfill composites for deep mining safety
Article.Authors: Hao J.; Zhang L.; Cao J.; Luo Y.; Zeng X.; Xin F.; Bao M.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: The global transition toward a low-carbon heavy industry urgently demands the high-value upcycling of industrial solid wastes such as steel slag (SS), while deep underground mining encounters unprecedented structural stability challenges. Cementitious paste backfill synthesized from multi-solid wastes offers a sustainable dual solution for waste valorization and underground space stabilization; however, the multi-field failure mechanisms of rock-backfill composite structures remain insufficiently understood. Herein, we systematically investigate the triaxial mechanical behavior, energy dissipation, and 3D microstructural damage evolution of rock and SS-based backfill composites. By continuously tracking the interactive failure process between the surrounding rock and the backfill core, we demonstrate that increasing lateral confinement drives a distinct transition in the failure regime from brittle axial splitting to ductile shear-dilation. Moreover, through quantitative morphometric filtering, we successfully decouple stress-induced micro-crack networks from pre-existing voids, revealing that lateral stress effectively mitigates shear-crack opening and drives matrix void compaction. Finally, the inflection point in the energy dissipation ratio (Ud/Ue) is identified as a physics-driven, quantitative precursor for predicting macro-structural collapse.

Article.Authors: Xia T.; Li Y.; Jia X.; Tian X.; Huang X.; Li L.; He Z.
Article.Abstract: Climate change and human activities alter agricultural pest distributions. We developed ensemble species distribution models to assess current habitat suitability of Bactrocera dorsalis using bioclimatic and human activity variables and project future shifts under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios using bioclimatic variables only. Incorporating human activity variables improved current model performance. Mean diurnal range (Bio2), isothermality (Bio3), and maximum temperature of the warmest month (Bio5) were key climatic predictors. Suitable habitats expanded under all future scenarios, particularly toward northern and central-eastern China, with the greatest increase under SSP3-7.0 in the 2070s. Multivariate environmental similarity surface and most dissimilar variable analyses indicated environmental similarity across most projected areas, whereas novelty in some regions was primarily associated with Bio3. These findings support targeted surveillance and pest risk management while highlighting the importance of assessing environmental novelty in future projections.

Article.Authors: Jiang Y.; Wu L.; Li W.; Li L.; Huang Z.; Gui Y.; Wang J.; Liu R.; Jing C.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) display heightened seizure susceptibility, in which neuronal hyperactivity during seizures correlates with exacerbated Tau pathology and cognitive impairment. Further validation in an AAV-based mouse Tau propagation model revealed robust bidirectional interactions: pathological Tau overexpression worsened seizure outcomes, while seizures accelerated Tau propagation across brain regions, inducing neuronal loss and gliosis. Article.Authors: Csikos V.; Lysaker C.; Hauger B.; Strope T.; Barnaba C.; Smith K.; Allen J.; Puchalska P.; Thyfault J.; Wilkins H.
Article.Abstract: Exercise and fasting strategies are linked to improved brain health. Despite this little is known about how these interventions affect neuronal mitochondrial quality control. Neurons exposed to exercise serum exhibited increased markers of mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy. Proteomics analysis of exercise serum-treated neurons revealed changes in mitochondrial and autophagy-related proteins and upregulation of mitochondrial biogenesis, protein quality control, and redox signaling pathways. Article.Authors: Drel V.; Varadarajan S.; Abd El-Aziz T.; Jasrotia R.; Venkatesan M.; Madesh M.; Singh B.
Article.Abstract: Aberrant Ca 2+ signaling, mediated by multiple ion channels, is increasingly recognized as a central driver of irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Article.Authors: Cano-Garcia O.; Guzmán-Díaz K.; Rivera-Tello S.; Vélez-Pérez H.; Morales J.; Ramos-Loyo J.; Romo-Vázquez R.; Paredes O.

NoGo conditions yielded directionally higher odds ratios than Go, with early NoGo showing the greatest sequential constraint.These results demonstrate that inhibitory processing is associated with dynamic reconfigurations of shared networks expressed at the sequential syntax level. Conditional successor analysis and MSA capture local motifs points and global temporal structure respectively, establishing sequence-based methods as a principled framework for linking millisecond-scale brain dynamics to cognitive function.

Article.Title: Institutional design of community energy storage: Value creation, capture, and distribution
Article.Authors: Li N.; Koirala B.
Article.Abstract: Community energy storage can create economic value, but how ownership, market access, pricing, and network tariffs shape its creation, capture, and distribution alongside grid impacts remains unclear. Network tariffs change the relative benefits of individual and shared batteries and, in the community examined, narrow PV-non-PV savings gaps under shared storage. Broader market access can increase peak imports and exports, whereas contracted-capacity charges can moderate import peaks. These findings suggest that institutional design can play an important role in balancing economic performance, distributional outcomes, and grid impacts.

Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioral developmental plasticity refers to the lasting changes in an organism’s behavior that occur during development in response to external and internal cues, enhancing survival and reproduction. Clinical ELISA validation in prospective local and independent external cohorts, supported by tissue immunohistochemistry, demonstrated robust diagnostic performance across both cohorts: serum EPHB2 achieved AUCs of 0.794–0.839 for adenoma detection and 0.816–0.897 for distinguishing CRC from healthy controls, and effectively discriminated neoplastic from benign inflammatory lesions (AUCs of 0.817–0.874). Mechanistic analyses further revealed that EPHB2 expression is associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling activation in colorectal tumorigenesis. Collectively, these findings establish serum EPHB2 as a promising candidate biomarker that warrants further prospective evaluation for early detection of colorectal neoplasia.

Article.Title: Ancient human genomes reveal farmer-pastoralist interactions in the formation of Iron Age Qin people
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang R.; Ma H.; Zhao J.; Dang W.; Yang W.; Di N.; Hu K.; Li Z.; Xie M.; Tao L.; He H.; Yang X.; Qiu L.; Wu X.; Yang T.; Tang G.; Sun Z.; Wang C.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: The Yellow River's Ji-shaped bend region is a key agro-pastoral transition zone in northern China, yet the genetic interactions between Central Plain farmers and Eastern Eurasian Steppe pastoralists remain unclear. We analyzed three Late Neolithic individuals from the Lushanmao site and 34 Iron Age individuals from the Liuying site associated with the Qin people. The Lushanmao population derived ∼93% of its ancestry from Yangshao-related Yellow River farmers (NYR) and ∼7% from Ancient Northeast Asian (ANA) pastoralists. The Iron Age Qin people retained dominant NYR ancestry and minor ANA ancestry while acquiring an additional southern East Asian (SEA)-related components. However, the Qin people showed no detectable West Eurasian genetic influence, indicating that West Eurasian cultural elements in Qin culture were not accompanied by genetic admixture. These findings illuminate the complex farmer-pastoralist interactions that shaped populations in this strategically important region.

Article.Title: Diet-attributable colorectal cancer in Asia: Regional heterogeneity in burden and dietary intake
Article.Authors: Zhan Y.; Lv W.; Wang Z.; Tong Y.; Wu X.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer incidence is rising rapidly in Asia, with dietary factors being major modifiable risk factors. We assessed disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), mortality, age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), estimated annual percentage change, and population-attributable fraction using Global Burden of Disease 2023 data. Spatial alignment between 2018 Global Dietary Database intake and 2018 attributable ASDR was examined using Spearman correlation and bivariate maps. High-income Asia Pacific recorded the highest diet-attributable ASDR and ASMR in 2023, while South Asia recorded the lowest. Among Asian subregions, High-income Asia Pacific recorded the highest ASDRs attributable to diets low in whole grains, high in red meat, and high in processed meat. Within each subregion, diets low in whole grains or milk generally ranked first. Whole grains, milk, calcium, and fiber showed clearer spatial alignment. Given the heterogeneity of diet-attributable burden in Asia, region-specific dietary prevention strategies should be prioritized.

Article.Title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and genomic diversity in Quilombola communities during Brazil’s gamma VOC wave
Article.Authors: Ferreira de Almeida Rego F.; Santos L.; Cucco M.; de Moraes L.; Veras Florentino P.; Junior J.; de Araújo Oliveira V.; Nihei J.; Vicentini F.; Leal Reis J.; Fernandes C.; Li G.; de Oliveira C.; Pedreira da Silva Filho H.; Khouri R.
Article.Abstract: COVID-19 has disproportionately affected vulnerable populations worldwide; yet, data on SARS-CoV-2 transmission and variant diversity in Brazil's descendants of enslaved individuals, known as Quilombola, remain scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Cachoeira, Bahia, in people seeking care, between February and March 2021, testing 700 oropharyngeal swabs by RT-qPCR and 591 plasma samples for IgM/IgG antibodies. These results reveal complex transmission dynamics and variant diversity within marginalized Quilombola populations, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions, expanded diagnostic coverage, and prioritization of these communities in vaccination campaigns to address health inequities.

Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) microelectrodes may improve electric-field coupling to confined cells, but their fabrication often requires complex metallization or specialized equipment. Swelling generated COC features approximately 10 μm high, while spin-coated TMX formed an approximately 80 nm conformal conductive layer. Article.Title: LKMHCpan: Transformer-optimized HLA-I pseudo-sequences enhance neoantigen prediction for immunotherapy
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Liu S.; Yao M.; Chen H.; Yu Y.; Zhang B.; Jia M.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate peptide-HLA class I binding prediction is fundamental for identifying tumor neoantigens and advancing personalized immunotherapy. We present LKMHCpan, a pan-specific predictor that leverages transformer networks to optimize HLA-I pseudo-sequences representation through attention-guided integration of 88 key residues primarily within the α1, α2, and α3 domains. LKMHCpan achieves a mean precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.93, generalizes robustly to untrained HLA-I alleles, and supports peptides longer than 11 amino acids. Neoantigen burden from LKMHCpan significantly stratified clinical outcomes in two immunotherapy-treated cohorts: metastatic melanoma ( n = 73) and lung cancer ( n = 309), with high-burden patients exhibiting clinical benefit. Its ability to resolve binding motifs for untrained alleles and single-amino-acid HLA-I mutants highlights its potential for elucidating complex peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) interactions. LKMHCpan provides a scalable framework for neoantigen discovery and prognostic assessment in precision immunotherapy.

Article.Title: Targeted degradation of a constitutively active GPCR oncoprotein
Article.Authors: Saca V.; Chen Y.; Burdette C.; Huber T.; Sakmar T.
Article.Abstract: To assess the feasibility of using proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) to target G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), we constructed a degron-tagged GPCR library in which a HaloTag7 protein fusion tag was engineered into the cytoplasmic carboxyl terminal tail. HaloPROTAC3 treatment resulted in recruitment of the VHL E3 ligase, yielding a time- and dose-dependent decrease in receptor expression and decreased agonist-dependent receptor signaling. We then focused on human cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CysLTR2). The CysLTR2 mutant L129Q constitutively signals through heterotrimeric G proteins and drives tumorigenesis in uveal melanoma (UM). We observed a HaloPROTAC3 dose-dependent decrease in receptor levels in primary human melanocytes expressing the engineered CysLTR2-L129Q mutant. Our results support the potential utility of using PROTACs as GPCR degraders.

Article.Title: Exercise imprints a persistent tumor intrinsic suppressive state in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Tobias G.; Gomes J.; de Almeida N.; Dantas W.; Oliveira E.
Article.Abstract: Exercise reduces colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, yet whether it acts directly and durably on tumor cells has been difficult to establish. Using syngeneic murine models, we show that aerobic exercise training suppresses primary tumor growth, pulmonary metastasis, and cachexia, and imprints a tumor-intrinsic suppressive state that persists ex vivo . Tumor cells from exercised mice retain reduced growth after serial transplantation into untrained hosts, and tumors of exercised mice show reduced expression of a subset of microRNAs and of their biogenesis machinery, including Dicer . This state is accompanied by intracellular serine depletion and a steady-state metabolite signature consistent with reduced glycolytic biosynthesis and increased mitochondrial substrate use. Across human CRC cohorts, lower DICER1 expression is associated with better clinical outcome, paralleling the exercise-conditioned state. These findings indicate that exercise can impose a persistent, tumor-intrinsic regulatory and metabolic constraint, broadening the conceptual basis for physical activity in cancer biology.

Article.Title: Nested paradoxes around how biodiversity constrains business: Why biodiversity conservation requires paradox thinking
Article.Authors: Pollach I.; Søndergaard H.; Linneberg M.; Schaper S.; Barfod A.; Kristensen J.
Article.Abstract: Mounting evidence of nature degradation has led governmental and non-governmental actors to put pressure on companies to address their impact on biodiversity, as their economic value creation contributes directly or indirectly to biodiversity loss. However, designing effective mitigation measures requires acknowledging the complex interplay of political, social, and economic constraints that shape corporate decision-making. We elucidate how a paradox perspective provides a productive way of understanding corporate biodiversity engagement, or the absence thereof. Specifically, we illuminate how corporate biodiversity engagement is shaped by nested paradoxes operating at all levels of the economic system, wherein responses to higher-level paradoxes structurally constrain possible responses to lower-level paradoxes. We argue that meaningful corporate biodiversity engagement necessitates concerted actions across all levels, thereby empowering companies to engage with biodiversity in a proactive and consequential manner.

Article.Title: Hippocampal tangential insertions of high-density silicon probes in head- fixed mice enhance spatial sampling
Article.Authors: Kala A.; Evander V.; Tukker J.; Kremkow J.; Schmitz D.; Sibille J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The hippocampus is a key structure within the medial temporal lobe which plays a central role in the formation and consolidation of declarative memories. Despite technological progress, a full understanding of hippocampal rhythms, neuronal population activity, and the underlying connectivity remains elusive, partly due to its complex morphology in a croissant-like shape which limits coronal and sagittal approaches. To address this limitation, we propose two different tangential insertions of high-density electrode probes (Neuropixels 1.0) aligned to either the dorsal or ventral sections of the hippocampus. Each approach enables the placement of up to 384 recording sites within the hippocampal formation. Both insertions are performed in head-fixed conditions, which can be easily combined with detailed monitoring of the animals’ behavioral states including spontaneous running and facial movements. The two proposed tangential dorsal and ventral insertions capture almost continuously the physiology of the hippocampus across 3.84 mm of tissue. We show that when placed across the pyramidal layer, such insertions can harness ripple oscillations from approximately 130 channels, corresponding to about ∼1.3 mm of tissue, with a coverage of 2 channels every 20 µm. Furthermore, such insertions enabled us to record up to 400 hippocampal neurons simultaneously from a single probe, endowing us with the capability to capture putative functionally connected neuronal pairs. Although the conventional orthogonal/vertical approach is optimal for recording the laminar organization of hippocampal activity, we demonstrate how, for the longitudinal axis of hippocampus, tangential insertions can substantially increase spatial reach and sampling resolution, enabling a more detailed description of activity along this axis.

Article.Title: Environmental phthalate and chronic kidney disease: Epidemiology, mechanistic pathways, and clinical implications
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Cao H.; Li Q.; Tan Y.; Li Z.; Chen S.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major global health problem, and early detection and risk control are still limited. Phthalates—widely used plasticizers with endocrine-disrupting effects—have been increasingly implicated in CKD-related outcomes. Human studies have reported associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and kidney-related markers, commonly reflected by the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), although the direction and magnitude of these associations vary by metabolite, population, study design, and outcome definition. Mechanistic evidence is currently dominated by studies of di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and its metabolite mono-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), suggesting potential involvement of oxidative stress, inflammation, regulated cell death, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and extracellular-matrix (ECM) remodeling in experimental models. However, the extent to which these mechanisms apply to other phthalates or alternative plasticizers remains uncertain. The evidence remains heterogeneous across populations and exposure contexts, and key limitations include its observational nature, exposure-measurement bias, reverse causality, and uncertainty regarding temporality and mixture effects. Future longitudinal, pharmacokinetic, and intervention studies are needed to determine whether phthalate biomarkers have clinically meaningful prognostic or predictive utility.

Article.Title: Multiomic crosstalk between plasma metabolites and inflammation in IBD via MR and mouse validation
Article.Authors: Pei J.; Lu C.; Zeng T.; Zhao Y.; Chen C.; Wang J.; Chen Y.; Yuan X.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is refractory with gut dysbiosis and recurrent colonic inflammation. While microbiome and omics alterations in IBD have been studied, multi-omics integration analysis is underutilized. This study explored causality and therapeutic targets in "multi-omics-IBD" axes by bibliometric analysis to identify hotspots, two-sample MR and two-step mediation analysis to explore gut microbiota-driven "plasma metabolite-inflammation homeostasis" axes in IBD regulation. Protein targets were screened via cross-platform p-QTLs MR, meta-analysis, colocalization; key metabolites' anti-inflammatory effects validated through metabolic enrichment, druggability assessment, in vitro and in vivo experiments. Bibliometric analysis showed IBD-multi-omics research focuses on microbiota, inflammation, pathological mechanisms, with growing focus on biomarkers and drug targets. Sensitivity analyses identified multi-omics biomarkers, 24 therapeutic metabolites and three regulatory axes: Klebsiella-Gly-β-MCA-CCL20/IL-10RA, Clostridium sp CAG-632-Lauroyl-L-carnitine chloride-IL-10/IL-8, Treponema D/Spirochaetia-4-vinylphenol-IL-10RA. RAW264.7 macrophage cell and mice experiments confirmed three metabolites' anti-inflammatory effects, with Gly-β-MCA most effective, Lauroyl-L-carnitine chloride targeting IL-10 to alleviate Crohn' s-like colitis. This study clarifies multi-omics-IBD causality and potential drug targets, supporting precision anti-inflammatory therapy via "metabolism-inflammation" axes.

Article.Title: Highly twinned cobalt selenide with abundant selenium vacancies for efficient nitrogen reduction reaction
Article.Authors: Shang L.; Li C.; Zhang S.; Qiu K.
Article.Abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) offers a promising approach to produce ammonia (NH3) under ambient conditions. However, the ammonia yield rate and Faradaic efficiency were still limited by the chemical inertness of nitrogen. Here, we report the introduction of Se vacancies in CoSe nanorods via an ions-exchange method. Se vacancies can improve the NRR activities by the lending of N2 activation. As a result, the ammonia yield rate reached as high as 106.7 μg h–1 mg–1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 21.2% at -0.3 V (vs. RHE). More importantly, the ammonia is directly derived from nitrogen, which was demonstrated by the isotopic experiments using 15N2 as a nitrogen source. This work not only provides a strategy for creating Se vacancies, but also offers an important pathway for the development of efficient catalysts for NRR. Ammonia (NH3) golds significant importance as carbon-free energy carrier, and industrial feedstock.[1-3] Currently, industrial-scale NH₃ is produced via the highly energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process, which operates under elevated temperatures (400–600°C) and high pressures (200-400 atm). However, this process emits substantial quantities of greenhouse gases, giving rise to significant environmental concerns. To achieve carbon neutrality, the Haber-Bosch method must be transformed into a low-carbon process. Powered by renewable energy sources, such as solar cells, the electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) under ambient conditions offers a promising route toward sustainable NH₃ production.[4-9] Despite the numerous NRR catalysts reported to date, the Faradaic efficiency and ammonia yield of NRR remain relatively low due to the inherent chemical inertness of N₂ molecule.[8-12] Vacancy engineering is widely acknowledged in the literature as an effective strategy for enhancing the catalytic activity of electrocatalysts.[13-17] For instance, Qiu et al. demonstrated that introducing oxygen vacancies into OER and ORR catalyst significantly improves its catalytic performance,[18] while Qiao et al. enhanced the catalyst's capability to activate and adsorb nitrogen molecules by incorporating nitrogen vacancies into nitrides.[19] Nevertheless, research on vacancy engineering specifically for NRR remains limited. Investigating the impact of vacancies of different elements on NRR performance could provide crucial insights for the design of highly efficient catalysts. In this work, we report a highly twinned CoSe nanorod with a large density of Se vacancies (denoted as V-CoSe) via an two-steps ion-exchange method, which exhibits significantly superior Faradaic efficiency and NH3 production rate. The theoretical calculations suggest that the Se vacancies are essential for NRR of V-CoSe, which greatly promote the adsorption and activation of N2. This work provide a new strategy to introduce vacancies into catalysts for green and sustainable NH3 production. Ion exchange is a particularly attractive synthetic tool for adjusting the atomic/electronic structure of electrocatalysts. Herein, V-CoSe nanorods with atomic steps were prepared via the two-steps ion-exchange method. First, CoO nanorods were fabricated using single-crystal ZnO nanorods as sacrificial templates. After cation-exchange, ZnO nanorods were completely transformed into CoO nanorods. Second, V-CoSe nanorods were synthetized using CoO nanorods as sacrificial templates (Fig. S1). After cation-exchange, CoO nanorods were completely transformed into V-CoSe nanorods (Fig.1a). As shown in Fig. S4, large-area, uniform growth of CoSe on the carbon fibers is evident. Compared to the smooth surfaces of the ZnO (Fig.S2), CoO (Fig.S3) and pristine CoSe (Fig. S5) nanorods, the V-CoSe nanorods exhibit significantly rougher surfaces. TEM and high-resolution imaging (Fig 1b,c) reveal that the CoSe nanorods synthesized via ion exchange possess abundant twin boundaries and atomic steps. This structure can be primarily attributed to the rearrangement of atoms within the crystal lattice during the anion exchange process.[20] Fig. 1e shows the Three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions images of V-CoSe from two-dimensional (2D) high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (Fig. 1d), which clearly reveals the surface of V-CoSe nanorod is full of cavities, which should be caused by the release of crystal stress during the anion exchange process. These cavities can significantly enhance the mass diffusion during NRR. The XRD patterns (Fig. 2a) and TEM-EDS results (Table S1) demonstrate CoO were completely converted into V-CoSe after cation exchange. Both the V-CoSe nanorods and pristine CoSe nanorods exhibit the hexagonal phase structure (PDF card No.89-2004).

Article.Title: Prognostic value of circulating cell-free Epstein-Barr virus DNA CpG methylation in extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma
Article.Authors: Xing T.; Wang W.; Deng H.; Gong Y.; Shang C.; Wu Y.; Du K.; Li Y.; Wu J.; Wang L.; Li J.; Zhang X.; Xu W.; Liang J.
Article.Abstract: Extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma (ENKTL) is an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated malignancy, and circulating EBV DNA serves as a key prognostic indicator. Notably, only CpG-methylated EBV DNA, not whole-blood or plasma EBV DNA, effectively identified high-risk patients and predicted significantly poorer outcomes ( p < 0.001). Integrating it into the prognostic index of natural killer cell lymphoma (PINK) model created PINK-CpGE, which showed improved predictive accuracy (AUC 0.9333 vs. 0.8897). Overall, cell-free CpG-methylated EBV DNA served as a superior prognostic biomarker for ENKTL.

Article.Title: Plastic shifts in web architecture alter signal physics and influence collective behavior and ecological prevalence
Article.Authors: Parthasarathy B.; Jami U.; Satyamurthy N.; Abhinai V.; Krishna M.; Shaikh N.; Vamsi Dasu K.
Article.Abstract: Certain animals build sophisticated structures that act as sensory organs outside the body. However, we know remarkably little about how these structures shape the physics of information transmission that ultimately influence behaviours, fitness and population outcomes. We investigated this problem using an Indian social spider whose web architecture shifts plastically from multiplanar three-dimensional (3D) webs in natural vegetation to planar two-dimensional (2D) webs on anthropogenic substrates. Using a custom-built, field-deployable vibration analyses system, we discovered that differences in web architecture generate fundamental trade-offs in vibrational signals. Interestingly, planar 2D webs transmit fast-but-noisy vibration signals, triggering rapid collective recruitment of spiders, whereas multiplanar 3D webs transmit slower and clearer signals that enable precise hunting by fewer individuals. Despite capturing similar amounts of prey and incurring lethal mistakes while attacking dangerous prey, colonies with 2D webs produced more clutches, grew larger, and were more prevalent in human-modified habitats. Our playback experiments confirm that fast signals causally increase collective recruitment, and our mechanistic models demonstrate that this fast-but-noisy information regime emerges directly from 2D web topology. Our results reveal that even simple topological shifts in extended phenotypes reshape micro-scale signal properties, biasing collective responses that scale-up to fitness consequences and ecological prevalence.

Article.Title: Hydrogen adsorption and dissociation on late transition metal doped C24/C2N heterostructure
Article.Authors: Latif S.; Ayub K.; Sheikh N.; Hammud H.; Yar M.
Article.Abstract: Hydrogen dissociation is essential for many hydrogen-related applications and requires efficient catalysts based on earth-abundant elements. Through density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the effect of the late first-row transition metals on H 2 activation and dissociation was investigated on single-atom catalysts supported on a C 24 /C 2 N heterostructure. Metal-support interactions, H 2 adsorption, dissociation pathways, activation barriers, and electronic structures were systematically evaluated. The metal-support interaction was found to be the strongest for Fe@C 24 /C 2 N (−5.09 eV), and the dissociation barrier for H 2 was the lowest for Ni@C 24 /C 2 N (0.23 eV). The molecular-level understanding of bonding and charge transfer during H 2 activation was gained using non-covalent interactions (NCI), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM), natural bond orbital (NBO), and electron-density-difference analyses. The molecular dynamics simulations further supported the structural stability of the selected systems under the simulated conditions. These results elucidate the relationship between the type of transition metal, the nature of the interaction with the support, and the activation of H 2 , and offer guidance for the development of catalysts for hydrogen-related applications.

Article.Title: Characterization of lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation of LUHMES cells
Article.Authors: Hanquier J.; Iyer M.; Evans T.; McCourry D.; Berryhill C.; Doud E.; Smith-Kinnaman W.; Mosley A.; Cornett E.
Article.Abstract: Over one-third of human lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and lysine demethylases (KDMs)-the enzymes responsible for adding or removing methylation on lysine residues within proteins-are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Consequently, several studies have explored the roles of specific KMTs or KDMs in neuronal differentiation, and alterations in histone methylation patterns have been identified. It is now widely recognized that KMTs and KDMs also target non-histone proteins, yet knowledge of how non-histone lysine methylation changes during neuronal differentiation remains limited. Here, we address this gap using quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics to identify and measure changes in non-histone lysine methylation at three different stages in the Lund human mesencephalic (LUHMES) neuronal differentiation model. We identify 74 lysine methylation sites with significant differences in abundance across differentiation. Our analysis reveals lysine methylation on many non-histone proteins involved in neuronal differentiation and neurodevelopment, including signaling molecules, cytoskeletal proteins, RNA splicing factors, and transcription factors. Overall, this work broadens the understanding of non-histone lysine methylation in a neuronal differentiation model and offers a valuable resource of lysine methylation sites on proteins of biological and clinical significance for future research.

Article.Title: Chemogenetic hyperpolarization in the entorhinal cortex during sleep facilitates delta oscillations and memory consolidation
Article.Authors: Gunin S.; Vu J.; Haam J.
Article.Abstract: Memory consolidation is a crucial step in long-term memory formation, during which stable memory representations are formed using recently encoded labile memories. The entorhinal cortex (EC) mediates such brain-wide memory reorganization by exhibiting delta oscillations during sleep, through hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels. We tested the feasibility of chemogenetically manipulating EC delta oscillations and examined whether such manipulations affect memory consolidation. We demonstrate that membrane hyperpolarization via the activation of the inhibitory chemogenetic receptor hM4Di paradoxically facilitates delta oscillations in the EC by activating HCN channels, whereas membrane depolarization via the activation of the excitatory chemogenetic receptor hM3Dq induces the opposite effect. Furthermore, we show that chemogenetic depolarization during sleep following learning impairs memory consolidation, whereas chemogenetic hyperpolarization enhances it. Our study provides insights into the effects of chemogenetic manipulation on neural oscillations and identifies EC delta as a key regulator of memory consolidation efficiency.

Article.Title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants
Article.Authors: Mathew B.; Halder A.; Jaiswal N.; Panda S.; Pramanik D.; Peela S.; Garg A.; Tripathi S.; Samanta S.; Gupta P.; Malhotra V.; Ahuja G.; Sengupta D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evolution shapes the structure and content of genomes, yet the contribution of local sequence composition to variant selection remains poorly understood. We hypothesize that variants arising in high-kGain contexts are more likely to persist due to evolutionary favorability. We validated this hypothesis across multiple systems. In E. coli and S. cerevisiae long-term evolution experiments, we found that fixed, essential, and parallel mutations consistently show elevated kGain scores. This trend held in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in an in-house antibiotic adaptation experiment, where a high-kGain fusA Y515N mutation conferred resistance and maintained fitness when overexpressed, demonstrating a causal link between kGain and adaptive potential. To enable cross-species generalization, we trained a transformer-based neural network regressor on LTEE-derived mutations to predict kGain from sequence alone. The model achieved high correlation in held-out in-domain data (Pearson r = 0.81) and accurately predicted kGain trends in out-of-domain data (Pearson r = 0.82), demonstrating that k-mer-based sequence constraints learned from one genome can be effectively transferred to others. Together, our results establish kGain as a biologically meaningful, scalable metric for probing within-genome sequence selection, offering a complementary lens to existing conservation-based frameworks for understanding evolutionary fitness and variant persistence.

Article.Title: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids

Article.Abstract: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity in vivo . Article.Abstract: The Cdk1 activator Cdc25C contains a long intrinsically disordered regulatory region (IDR) that mediates the IDR-catalytic domain interaction, substrate recruitment via interaction with cyclin B, self-association, and heterotypic interactions with numerous partners. Before M-phase entry, site-specific phosphorylation selectively rewires the IDR-mediated interaction network, promoting cyclin B recruitment to modestly activate Cdc25C. At M-phase entry, site-comprehensive phosphorylation globally dismantles all four classes of IDR-mediated interactions to enable robust Cdc25C activation. Article.Abstract: Abstract Cryptochromes and photolyases are blue-light-sensitive flavoproteins that generally bind flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and have distinct functions. Cryptochrome 4a (CRY4a) is a protein expressed in the double-cone photoreceptors of the retina in migratory songbirds like European robin ( Erithacus rubecula ) and is hypothesized as the primary sensor for avian magnetoreception. This experiment resulted in successful binding of 8-HDF to Xl 6-4PL, but not to Er CRY4a. We studied the binding of MTHF using in vitro reconstitution followed by UV-Vis spectroscopy and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) assays. No interaction was observed between MTHF and Er CRY4a. We found no similarity at the relevant binding sites between the sequences of Er CRY4a with proteins shown to bind MTHF or 8-HDF. This suggests that the binding pocket is not conserved. Article.Abstract: Blue light from light-emitting diode (LED) displays is widely encountered; however, its effects beyond the retina are poorly understood. Immunofluorescence showed a progressive decline in nestin signal in the inner nuclear layer, which correlated with a composite behavioral deficit score across animals. Article.Title: Geographic and thematic gaps in wildfire resilience research
Article.Authors: Fong C.; Halpern B.
Article.Abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and destructive around the world, threatening lives, homes, and natural landscapes. Building or maintaining systems for wildfire resilience has emerged as a crucial strategy for addressing wildfire risks and impacts, balancing a need for fire on the landscape to support healthy natural systems with a desire to mitigate loss of human life and structure. Our review of over 1,500 wildfire resilience studies shows that while research is growing, it is unevenly distributed across regions and topics, often focusing on habitats while paying less attention to human communities, infrastructure, and other aspects that matter for people's lives and well-being. By highlighting these gaps, our work helps guide scientists, policymakers, and communities toward more integrated and equitable strategies for living safely with fire. Understanding where research is lacking can improve planning, strengthen resilience efforts, and support decisions that protect both people and ecosystems.

Article.Title: Distinct cellular mechanisms underlie ON orientation selectivity in the mouse retina
Article.Authors: Han X.; He S.; Sun L.
Article.Abstract: Orientation selectivity (OS) is a fundamental visual computation. We characterized three morphophysiologically distinct ON orientation-selective ganglion cell (OSGC) populations in the mouse retina: S345 OSGCs and two less frequently recorded groups, putative S13 and S15 OSGCs. Mechanistic analyses focused on S345 OSGCs, which exhibited robust orientation tuning and continuous dendritic stratification across inner plexiform layer strata S3–S5. TTX abolished orientation tuning, whereas 2,3-dihydroxy-6-nitro-7-sulfamoylbenzo[f]quinoxaline (NBQX) reduced orientation-dependent inhibition and eliminated OS, implicating AMPA/kainate receptor-dependent recruitment of spiking inhibitory circuits. Physiologically identified spiking orientation-selective amacrine cells exhibited asymmetric inward-current responses, with orientation bias persisting in TTX. These findings expand the known diversity of ON orientation-selective retinal neurons, suggest distinct patterns of excitation and inhibition underlying their orientation signals, and identify a spiking GABAergic inhibitory mechanism shaping OS in S345 OSGCs.

Article.Title: Consequences of climate-driven relocation in the Prehispanic US Southwest
Article.Authors: Ortman S.
Article.Abstract: As humanity copes with a warming planet, there is a growing recognition that in some situations entire communities may be forced to relocate. This perspective paper summarizes an especially well-understood episode of climate-driven relocation that took place in the Four Corners region of the US Southwest in the 13 th century CE. This episode is well understood due to an exceptional archaeological record with high temporal resolution, oral traditions that have been maintained in descendant communities, a long history of research, and significant investment in synthesis of both archaeological and paleoclimatic records. The account is also well established in that it is based on a robust quantity and quality of evidence and high agreement among experts. The account is organized around questions that are often raised regarding community relocation in the present, thus providing an example of how archaeological research can contribute to the knowledge base for successful climate change adaptation responses today.

Article.Title: White-tailed deer milk promotes rapid SARS-CoV-2 RNA degradation through synergistic ionic and enzymatic mechanisms
Article.Authors: Tobar L.; Smith W.; Raso H.; Brown K.; Ceci A.; Urbano M.; Roby C.; Mahmutovic D.; Biesemier A.; Capelluto D.; Aiello I.; Raso D.; Finkielstein C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract White-tailed deer (WTD) represent the most significant SARS-CoV-2 wildlife reservoir in North America, yet the role of antiviral mechanisms in vertical transmission remains unexplored. We investigated SARS-CoV-2 antibody responses and viral stability in milk from lactating WTD and humans to characterize species-specific antiviral mechanisms. SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies were detected in milk and serum in WTD specimens using complementary immunoassays, providing the first evidence of humoral immune responses in wildlife milk. Despite antibody presence indicating prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure, viral RNA was undetectable in all WTD milk samples. This pattern aligns with observations in human milk, where viral RNA was also undetectable both during active infection (when nasal swabs were positive) and during antibody-positive periods following recovery. In vitro stability studies revealed striking species differences: all SARS-CoV-2 variants (A, B.1.1.7, BA.1.1.529) rapidly degraded in WTD milk within 30 min at physiological temperatures, while remaining mostly stable in human milk for up to 60 min. Biochemical characterization identified multifactorial degradation mechanisms in WTD milk, including 5-20 fold elevated mineral concentrations (sodium, magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium), enhanced protease activity, and increased lactoperoxidase levels. Individual mineral supplementation revealed variant-specific susceptibilities, with B.1.1.7 showing pronounced sensitivity to ionic stress. Mechanistic studies demonstrated synergistic effects between elevated ionic concentrations and proteolytic activity, with heat-labile and heat-stable degradation pathways contributing to viral inactivation. These findings reveal that WTD milk possesses intrinsic antiviral properties fundamentally different from human milk, representing an evolutionary adaptation that may impact viral persistence and transmission dynamics in wildlife populations. These findings reveal antiviral mechanisms in WTD milk that represent a previously unrecognized component of pathogen control in wildlife reservoirs, with important implications for understanding wildlife-pathogen interactions and zoonotic risk assessment. Author Summary White-tailed deer (WTD) have become the primary wildlife reservoir for SARS-CoV-2, with millions of infected animals across North America. Despite this significance, the presence of protective antibodies and viral behavior in WTD milk remained unexplored. We collected milk samples from lactating WTD during hunting seasons to investigate whether WTD produce neutralizing antibodies similar to those found in human milk and to examine how the virus behaves in this biological fluid. Our analysis revealed that WTD milk contains antibodies capable of neutralizing SARS-CoV-2. When we compared viral stability between WTD and human milk, we observed that WTD milk rapidly degrades viral genetic material within 30-40 min, while the same virus remains stable in human milk for over an hour. We identified that WTD milk contains mineral concentrations 5-20 times higher than human milk, including elevated levels of sodium, magnesium, and potassium, along with enhanced enzyme activity that breaks down viral components. These findings indicate that WTD milk functions as a protective barrier rather than a transmission route. This has implications for understanding viral persistence in wildlife populations and assessing potential risks to human health. Our work demonstrates that deer milk possesses multiple biological defense mechanisms that may protect offspring from viral infections, contributing to our understanding of wildlife immunity and pandemic preparedness.

Article.Authors: Singh J.; Tiwari V.; Sharma A.; Shukla S.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to neuronal injury in Parkinson's disease, and astrocyte-derived mitochondria may offer neuroprotection by restoring neuronal bioenergetics. Using mitochondrial labeling and co-culture assays, we obtained evidence consistent with the release of astrocytic mitochondria, their uptake by injured neurons, and their association with the neuronal mitochondrial network. Building on this observation, we investigated whether direct delivery of functional astrocytic mitochondria could augment endogenous support during neuronal injury. Infused astrocytic mitochondria reduced oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, improved mitochondrial respiration, normalized calcium homeostasis, reduced early neuronal apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial mass. In vivo , stereotactic infusion restored TH immunoreactivity in the SNpc and improved motor and non-motor behavioral deficits. These findings support the potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for Parkinson's disease.

Article.Authors: Zhang W.; Zhang Y.; Li F.; Li Y.; Gong H.; Luo J.; Yuan S.; Luo X.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-read sequencing technologies have significantly enhanced genome resolution capabilities, but their inherent high error rate (1-15%) still constrains constrains the accuracy of assembly and other downstream analyses. Validated across diverse datasets, DADEC reduced the error rate by an average of approximately 97.3%, significantly outperforming mainstream tools, demonstrating exceptional robustness particularly in complex scenarios. It also enhanced assembly contiguity, yielding more complete and continuous sequences, and effectively promoted strain-level metagenomic classification. Compared to the second-best performing tool, the False Discovery Rate and False Negative Rate were reduced by 73.8% and 84.8%, respectively. DADEC breakthroughy resolves the core conflict in the error correction field, thereby advancing the application of long-read technologies in complex genomic research.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Objective: Chemotherapy resistance remains a barrier to improving the prognosis of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC), and among several novel approaches to overcome chemotherapy resistance, modulating N6- methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification was found to be an important strategy. Article.Authors: Wei D.; Feng W.; Chen S.; Zhu T.; Jiang W.; Hou X.; Lin J.
Article.Abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria threatens global health by eroding the efficacy of existing antibiotics, underscoring the urgency of alternative therapies like phage therapy. Although bacteriophages are promising owing to their abundance, diversity, and potent bactericidal activity, their therapeutic durability is compromised by the rapid emergence of phage resistance. Here, we explore receptor complementarity as a proof-of-concept rational strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This study demonstrates that phage resistance imposes substantial fitness costs while still permitting bacterial survival under phage pressure. By isolating phages with distinct receptor dependencies, we constructed receptor-diverse phage cocktails that decreased the frequency of phage resistance. Notably, these receptor-informed cocktails suppressed phage resistance in vitro and yielded improved prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy in the Galleria mellonella preclinical in vivo model. Collectively, this work offers preclinical proof-of-concept for receptor-guided cocktail design to enhance the performance of phage-based interventions against MDR pathogens.

Article.Abstract: Adjustable ring-mode (ARM) laser welding mitigates thermal asymmetry and porosity in dissimilar-thickness aluminum lap joints for power batteries. Keyhole volume <0.55 mm 3 causes unstable penetration and vapor trapping; >0.59 mm 3 , stable penetration ≥0.25 mm 3 keeps open vapor channels and reduces porosity. Recoil-pressure spatial standard deviation (SSD) evolution, not magnitude, controls pore susceptibility: case 3 holds SSD=151.60 Pa (70–90 ms, maintain-then-smooth trend, 2.333% porosity), while case 2 rapidly falls to 106.06 Pa with 0.504 mm 3 keyhole volume and 4.251% porosity. Optimal ring-core power ratio: 0.8–1.2. Combined volume threshold and SSD evolution clarify pore suppression and guide power battery joining optimization.

Article.Title: RNA-binding proteome dynamics following ischemia-reperfusion injury in the kidney
Article.Authors: Hinrichs S.; Bohl K.; Haselhorst S.; Lopes F.; Wagener B.; Göbel H.; Müller S.; Finke S.; Neumann T.; Pollmann B.; Rieger C.; Rademann P.; Benzing T.; Boor P.; Schermer B.; Müller R.; Ignarski M.
Article.Abstract: Acute kidney injury is a frequent complication in hospitalized patients and is associated with increased mortality. Despite its relevance, no targeted therapies are available. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are essential regulators of cellular function and have been implicated in acute kidney injury, but a comprehensive analysis of their role is lacking. We investigated RNA-binding protein regulation in porcine kidneys subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury following cardiopulmonary resuscitation, a model closely resembling human renal physiology. Enhanced RNA interactome capture combined with mass spectrometry was used to identify and quantify RBPs. Proteomic and transcriptomic analyses complemented these data. To assess evolutionary conservation, RBP profiles were also obtained from human kidney tissue. We identified multiple RBPs regulated at the transcript, protein or RNA-binding level after ischemia-reperfusion injury. Among these, we found RBPs displaying altered RNA-binding, including metabolic enzymes previously implicated in ischemic stress. These findings suggest that energy metabolism is linked to RNA regulation during kidney injury. Renal ischemia–reperfusion injury alters the RNA-binding landscape, affecting both regulatory and metabolic RBPs. The conservation of these proteins in human kidneys highlights their translational relevance and identifies RNA–protein interactions as potential therapeutic targets in AKI. An interactive online database (https://shiny.cecad.uni-koeln.de/porcine_rbpome/) provides open access to these data.

Article.Title: Ion regulatory mechanisms supporting hypersaline tolerance in the coastal rock pool mosquito Aedes togoi
Article.Authors: Chiang J.; Khodikian E.; Phelan O.; Parra A.; Peach D.; Durant A.; Matthews B.
Article.Abstract: The coastal rock pool mosquito, Aedes togoi, is a remarkable example of a saline-tolerant mosquito. While most mosquitoes are obligate freshwater breeders, Ae. togoi larvae and pupae inhabit coastal rock pools that span freshwater to hypersaline conditions. We explore the ability of Ae. togoi larvae to tolerate hypersaline conditions by profiling the salt gland, an ion regulatory nexus within an anatomically unique, elaborated anal canal. We present a de-novo chromosome-scale genome assembly for Ae. togoi , highlighting its relatively small genome size and differences in chromosomal structure as compared to other Aedine mosquitoes. We detail repeat content and curate key multi-gene families encoding ion-transport proteins enriched in the larval salt gland, building a model of the machinery that likely facilitates hyperosmotic urine formation. Our work provides insights into molecular and anatomical adaptations that underpin the ability of mosquitoes and other insects to thrive in hypersaline rock pools and other dynamic environments.

Article.Title: Chemogenetic manipulation of the cortical amygdala alters binge-like alcohol drinking in male mice and neural network function in male and female mice
Article.Authors: Xiao T.; Chen Y.; Kimbrough A.
Article.Abstract: Binge drinking is a prevalent and clinically significant behavior contributing to alcohol use disorder. Sex differences in binge drinking are observed in both humans and preclinical studies, including differences in alcohol intake and underlying neural regulatory mechanisms. The cortical amygdala (CoA) has been implicated in alcohol-related behaviors, but its role in binge-like drinking and associated brain-wide co-activation patterns remains unclear. We tested whether CoA activity regulates binge-like alcohol consumption in a sex-dependent manner and examined CoA-associated brain-wide network organization in binge-like drinking. Binge-like alcohol intake was assessed using a 6-week Drinking-in-the-Dark paradigm. Saline or deschloroclozapine was administered 30 min before drinking in mice with inhibitory hM4Di, excitatory hM3Dq, or mCherry control virus. Locomotor and anxiety-like behavior were assessed 24 h after the final 4-h DID session. Brains were collected 120 min after drinking onset during a final DID session under chemogenetic manipulation. Whole-brain Fos mapping was performed, and brain-wide co-activation networks were constructed, followed by graph theory analyses. CoA inhibition significantly reduced binge-like alcohol consumption in male mice, but not females, although the drug × sex × virus interaction was not significant. CoA activation did not alter alcohol intake in either sex but increased locomotor activity in females but not males, although the corresponding sex interaction was not significant. Anxiety-like behavior was unaffected. CoA inhibition was associated with distinct brain-wide network configurations, including differences in CoA-associated module composition, hub-like node distribution, and co-activation patterns involving alcohol-relevant limbic and hypothalamic regions. These findings support a sex-dependent pattern of CoA regulation of binge-like drinking, with the reduction in alcohol intake detected in males but not females and demonstrate that CoA activity shapes brain-wide Fos co-activation patterns during alcohol consumption.

Article.Title: Inhibition of the sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1PR1) as a therapeutic target for aromatase inhibitor-induced musculoskeletal symptoms in mice
Article.Authors: Herz S.; Khan A.; Betancourt-Toscano I.; Tiron C.; Ton V.; Selley D.; Damaj M.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the leading cause of cancer death among women worldwide with estrogen receptor positive (ER+) BC comprising 70-80% of all cases. Adjuvant therapy with aromatase inhibitors (AIs), such as letrozole (LTZ), is the standard of care in ER + BC patients to prevent recurrence but many patients cease treatment prematurely due to the development of musculoskeletal side effects (i.e. arthralgia, myalgia, decreased grip strength) referred to as aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal syndrome (AIMSS). The lack of efficacious treatments available for AIMSS and premature treatment cessation being linked to increased patient mortality highlights the critical importance of identifying new therapeutic targets for its management. Here, we directly link LTZ treatment with increased levels of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1PR1) endogenous ligands in spinal cord tissue of female ovariectomized (OVX) ICR mice. We therefore investigated the impact of reducing S1PR1 activity as a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating AIMSS-related behaviors. In C57BL/6J OVX female mice, we found that pharmacological inhibition using the selective and competitive S1PR1 antagonist, NIBR-0213, effectively alleviated AIMSS-like behaviors after acute and repeated dosing regimens, with limited therapeutic effectiveness when given prior to LTZ treatment. In a conditioned place preference (CPP) paradigm, LTZ- but not vehicle-treated animals preferred the NIBR-0213 paired chamber, unmasking the presence of a tonic-aversive state driven by LTZ treatment. These findings identify S1PR1 as an important mediator to AIMSS and suggest that S1PR1 antagonists may be most effective as acute interventions to provide relief from the sensory and affective burden of AIMSS.

Article.Title: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide reduces alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors during withdrawal in Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats
Article.Authors: Palmisano M.; Mrizak H.; Gonzalez A.; St Onge C.; Erikson C.; Cruz B.; Flores-Bonilla A.; Vlkolinsky R.; Sharlai O.; Benedict J.; Bajo M.; Leggio L.; Ciccocioppo R.; Roberto M.
Article.Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have emerged as promising pharmacotherapeutics for alcohol use disorder (AUD). Semaglutide reduced voluntary alcohol consumption in a dose-dependent manner, and it produced anxiolytic-like behaviors during withdrawal in the open field test. In naïve animals, semaglutide reduced locomotor activity, lowered blood glucose levels, and decreased fat mass and GABAergic transmission in the IL mPFC. Article.Title: Ligand-specific effects of 5-HT2A receptor antagonists on fear extinction in C57BL/6J mice: Comparative insights from MDL 11,939 and MDL 100,907
Article.Authors: Tyulmenkova A.; Stackman R.
Article.Abstract: Serotonin (5-HT) 2A receptors (5-HT2AR) modulate corticolimbic circuits underlying fear extinction, but the behavioral consequences of 5-HT2AR antagonism during extinction remain poorly defined. Here, we examined the systemic effects of the 5-HT2A/2C antagonist MDL 11,939 (Glemanserin) and the selective 5-HT2A antagonist MDL 100,907 (Volinanserin) on fear extinction in adult female and male C57BL/6J mice. Repeated administration of MDL 11,939 significantly impaired extinction in male mice, evidenced by increased freezing across extinction trials and an increased number of trials required to reach extinction criterion. Neither acute nor repeated MDL 11,939 altered extinction in female mice. In males, MDL 100,907 produced a transient increase in freezing during extinction but did not delay extinction acquisition and had no effect in females. Because MDL 11,939 has reported affinity for 5-HT2C receptors, we tested potential contributions of 5-HT2C receptor antagonism in a separate cohort of male mice given repeated administration of the selective 5-HT2C antagonist SB 242084 (0.25 or 0.5 mg/kg).
