Article.Title: Spatial distribution patterns and quantitative analysis of traditional villages in the Qiantang River Basin using geographic detectors
Article.Authors: He Y.; Ding C.; Bai C.; Yan D.; Hu M.
Article.Abstract: The distribution pattern and agglomeration characteristics of traditional villages play a crucial role as historical and cultural assets in rural development, emphasizing the significance of regional cultural preservation and rural revitalization. This study examines 362 national traditional villages in the Qiantang River Basin (QRB) in Zhejiang to uncover their spatial settlement patterns and analyze the influencing factors. Employing spatial analysis methods such as the nearest neighbor index, geographical concentration index, and kernel density estimation, the study elucidates the spatial distribution of these villages. Utilizing the geographical detector model, it identifies key factors associated with their spatial distribution, quantitatively assessing their explanatory power and interaction patterns among natural, economic, and cultural dimensions. The study also suggests strategies for the protection and sustainable use of traditional villages in the QRB. The research findings reveal that traditional villages in the QRB exhibit a clustered distribution pattern, characterized by a spatial structure of “two cores and multiple clusters”. This agglomeration tendency is observed at the county level, with a distinct pattern of concentration in the southwestern mountainous regions and sparsity in the northeastern plains. Various factors such as slope, altitude, per capita disposable income, road network density, and the proportion of the primary industry play significant roles in shaping the spatial distribution of these traditional villages. A multifactor detection model demonstrates that the distribution pattern of traditional villages in the QRB is a result of the dynamic interplay between natural features and human influences. The impact of each factor varies across different stages, highlighting the complex nature of village distribution. This quantitative analysis assesses the varying degrees of influence exerted by the natural environment, socioeconomic conditions, and historical heritage on the distribution of traditional villages, addressing limitations of previous qualitative studies. This study not only enhances our understanding of the factors driving the distribution of traditional villages but also provides a scientific foundation for the strategic conservation of these villages in the QRB and the management of cultural heritage on a basin-wide scale.

Article.Title: Impaired spatial memory destabilization and updating in middle-aged male mice is reversed by muscarinic receptor stimulation
Article.Authors: Huff A.; Jardine K.; Kot O.; Kalisch B.; Winters B.
Article.Abstract: Reminder cues associated with earlier learning can destabilize memories, rendering them modifiable. Memory updating deficits may occur during aging, but these have not been thoroughly explored. Cholinergic dysfunction during aging could potentially contribute to these memory updating deficits, as among its many functions, acetylcholine is critical for memory destabilization. We hypothesized that mice would display memory destabilization and updating deficits with increasing age, and that pro-cholinergic manipulations could alleviate these deficits. In the current study, we show that in young (3-months), but not middle-aged (10–15-months), male C57 mice, object location memories readily destabilize. These middle-aged mice had a significant downregulation in expression of hippocampal vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT). Critically, mice at both ages could acquire and retain basic object-location memories. Moreover, pre-reactivation administration of an M1 muscarinic cholinergic receptor agonist appeared to promote memory destabilization in middle-aged mice, enabling memory updating. Finally, a brief period of enrichment yielded behavioural effects consistent with enhanced memory updating, and these were associated with elevated expression of hippocampal VAChT. This research expands our understanding of the critical involvement of cholinergic system changes in age-related cognitive deficits, highlighting an underappreciated role for cholinergic transmission in memory updating functions distinct from merely learning and remembering.
Article.TopicFields: Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Memory and Neural Mechanisms; Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Memory Processes and Influences; Neuroscience > Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience > Neuroscience and Neuropharmacology Research

Article.Title: Crowding-induced phase transition in Oedaleus asiaticus as a developmental stage-gated, irreversible multi-gene switch
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Guo N.; Rostami E.; Gao H.; Liu M.; Li L.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. The current investigation assessed how developmental stages and population density impacted phase transitions and which genes served as key regulatory elements of this process. The results showed that the younger nymphs were, the higher proportion that shifted from solitary to gregarious phase, whereas adults never switched; a density of 60 insects produced the highest transition rate, whereas lower or higher densities resulted in fewer gregarious individuals. The gregarious locusts maintained their original physical characteristics when they were grown in solitary conditions. Transcriptome analysis showed that gregarious individuals exhibited strong gene expression increases which included the juvenile-hormone acid methyl-transferase gene ( JHAMT ) and the phenylalanine hydroxylase gene ( Hn ) and the DOPA decarboxylase gene ( DDC ) and a chemosensory protein gene ( CSP ). RNAi silencing of JHAMT , Hn , DDC or CSP resulted in a major decrease of phase transition occurrence while JHAMT , Hn and DDC knock-down caused partial albinism. The research demonstrates that population density functions as the key trigger for phase transition while gene interactions with their respective metabolites undergo central regulatory functions. Nonetheless, since the locusts used in this study were field-collected and reared for less than two generations, the results should be interpreted within the context of environmentally induced plasticity rather than genetically fixed phase differences.

Article.Title: Self supervised multi scale learning for WiFi CSI contactless human activity recognition with potential applications in health monitoring
Article.Authors: Xu H.; Yao D.; Liu W.; Li L.; Ma L.; Jiang C.
Article.Abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) provides a privacy-preserving and contactless sensing modality for human activity recognition, but practical CSI recognition remains challenged by limited labeled data, heterogeneous motion dynamics, and signal perturbations. This study proposes CSI-MSRNet, a self supervised representation-learning framework that combines CSI-aware contrastive augmentation with a lightweight temporal and subcarrier multi scale encoder. The encoder models motion evolution at multiple temporal receptive fields and complementary frequency-selective responses across OFDM subcarriers, while Efficient Multi-Scale Attention is used only as a lightweight feature-refinement component rather than as the primary methodological novelty. Self supervised pretraining is restricted to the training partition, after which the encoder is fine tuned with different proportions of labeled samples. Experiments were conducted on the public UT-HAR and NTU-Fi HAR benchmarks using the SenseFi data partitions. Main recognition and low-label experiments were repeated five times with random seeds 42–46, and low-label subsets were independently sampled by stratified class sampling in each run. CSI-MSRNet achieved 98.76 ± 0.18% accuracy on UT-HAR and 99.85 ± 0.21% on NTU-Fi HAR. With only 1% labeled data, the corresponding accuracies were 73.6 ± 2.4% and 77.8 ± 2.8%, respectively. Controlled synthetic tests further indicated improved tolerance to amplitude noise and random subcarrier loss. These results should be interpreted as benchmark-level behavioral recognition rather than evidence of subject-independent generalization, clinical monitoring effectiveness, or embedded-device deployment. The framework therefore provides a computationally lightweight approach with potential applications in smart-home and health-related behavioral sensing.

Article.Title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal a senescence-associated lipid-metabolic macrophage phenotype driving immunosuppression and poor prognosis in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhao B.; Liao Y.; Ye S.; Jiang N.; Lu W.; Chen Y.; Chen W.; Huang Y.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their functional heterogeneity remains poorly understood, especially regarding the interplay between cellular senescence and lipid metabolism. We integrated multi-omics and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize a novel macrophage subpopulation termed senescence-associated lipid-metabolic (SALM) macrophages. Using eight machine learning algorithms, a prognostic model based on SALM signatures was developed and internally evaluated via nested cross-validation in a combined TCGA–GSE39582 cohort. Spatial multiplex immunofluorescence and qPCR were employed for experimental validation. SALM macrophages exhibit elevated IL-10/STAT3 signaling, terminal differentiation, and a core gene module enriched in senescence and lipid metabolism pathways. They interact strongly with T cells via immunosuppressive ligands IL-10 and MIF. Spatial analysis confirmed p16 + CD68 + IL-10 + cell enrichment at the tumor front. The SALM-based prognostic model achieved high accuracy (AUC = 0.972), and a corresponding nomogram showed potential for personalized prognosis prediction. SALM macrophages drive immunosuppression in CRC through a senescence-lipid metabolism axis, serving as a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Design and characterization of beta-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 to enhance luteolin solubility and anticancer efficacy: bioinformatic and biologic assessment
Article.Authors: Kharazmi F.; Homayouni Tabrizi M.; Jafarinia M.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a cause of cancer-related mortality, while luteolin, a flavonoid, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, and low bioavailability. This study developed a luteolin-loaded β-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8) nanocarrier intended to improve drug retention, pH-responsive release, and anticancer activity against colorectal cancer cells. ZIF-8 nanoparticles were synthesized by room-temperature precipitation, coated sequentially with β-cyclodextrin and chitosan, crosslinked using sodium tripolyphosphate, and loaded with luteolin by post-synthetic incubation. Molecular docking using MOE 2024 investigated luteolin interactions with KRAS (PDB 6MBU), chitosan-binding protein (4ZXE), and VEGF (2VPF), with 5-fluorouracil as a computational comparator. FTIR, dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, pH-dependent surface-charge measurements, and FESEM characterized the formulation. Encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were quantified spectrophotometrically; release was assessed by dialysis at pH 7.4, 6.5, and 5.5. HCT116 colorectal carcinoma and normal human dermal fibroblasts underwent MTT testing. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, AO/EB microscopy, SOD activity, FRAP, and qRT-PCR for CASP3, SOD1, and IL6 evaluated cell-death and stress responses. The particles showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 228.95 ± 2.7 nm, a PDI of 0.139 ± 0.04, and a zeta potential of − 27.24 ± 0.32 mV, indicating a uniform nanoscale dispersion. Synthesis yield was 78.5 ± 3.2%. Measured luteolin retention increased with feed concentration, reaching 83.5 ± 1.44% encapsulation efficiency and 16.1 ± 1.53% loading capacity. Release was slower under physiological conditions and accelerated in acidic media, supporting pH-responsive behavior; model fitting was descriptive, with Higuchi favored at pH 7.4, Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 6.5, and the lowest AIC assigned to Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 5.5. In HCT116, free luteolin produced an IC 50 of 166.5 ± 12.3 µg/mL, whereas Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8 reduced the IC 50 to 45.96 ± 2.3 µg/mL (approximately 3.6-fold greater potency; p < 0.001). The formulation IC 50 in HDF cells was 128.7 ± 8.4 µg/mL, yielding an HCT116/HDF selectivity index of 2.8. At 66 µg/mL, total apoptosis reached 48.9 ± 2.9%, compared with 1.3 ± 0.3% in controls. FRAP antioxidant capacity decreased to 0.578 ± 0.015 versus 0.801 ± 0.022 in controls. CASP3 and SOD1 transcripts increased 4.98-fold and 4.10-fold, respectively, while IL6 peaked at 10.92-fold at the intermediate dose. The dual-coated nanocarrier enhanced luteolin potency and apoptosis-associated responses in HCT116, with selectivity relative to HDF cells. Docking and characterization findings are supportive, not proof of KRAS inhibition, tumor targeting, or in vivo efficacy; validation remains necessary.

Article.Title: Physical literacy and health-related quality of life: the serial mediating role of resilience and positive mental health
Article.Authors: Mumu S.; Reena I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical literacy (PL) is recognized as a multidimensional construct that supports physical activity and health. Beyond physical competence, PL includes motivation, confidence, knowledge, and understanding. However, the role of positive psychological resources in explaining the relationship between physical literacy and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among university students has received limited empirical attention. This study examined whether resilience and positive mental health (PMH) mediate the relationship between PL and physical and mental components of HRQoL. In this cross-sectional study,159 undergraduate and graduate students from a single university in Louisiana, US completed the perceived physical literacy instrument, adult resilience measure-revised, positive mental health scale, and short form 12 health survey online. PROCESS Model 6 was utilized to analyze the mediation model. Age and sex were added as covariates. PL is positively associated with resilience, PMH, and both physical and mental HRQoL. PMH significantly mediated the relationship between PL and mental HRQoL, and a significant serial indirect association through resilience and PMH was identified (B = 0.227, 95% bootstrap CI [0.109, 0.403]). In contrast, no significant indirect effects were observed for physical HRQoL. The final model explained 35.1% of the variance in mental HRQoL. These findings suggest that physical literacy is associated with mental HRQoL through a psychosocial pathway in which resilience supports positive mental health. Findings from this study can be utilized to inform policy that seeks to identify modifiable psychological and behavioral determinants of HRQoL and meaningfully enhance the university health promotion program to support health outcomes of students in higher education.

Article.Title: Experimental and finite element analysis of coupled electro-thermal responses of concrete-encased grounding electrodes under lightning impulses
Article.Authors: Sarker M.; Zubair H.; Algarni S.; Alqahtani T.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: Grounding systems are critical for maintaining the safety and transient stability of high-voltage and smart-grid infrastructure subjected to lightning-current impulses. This study presents an integrated experimental and three-dimensional finite element method (FEM) investigation of conventional copper-bonded steel rod and concrete-encased grounding electrodes under standardized 8/20 µs impulse-current conditions. Laboratory experiments were conducted using an impulse-current generator with a maximum current capability of 1.5 kA, while a COMSOL Multiphysics model was developed and validated against the experimentally accessible current range and subsequently used to investigate higher-current conditions numerically. Three representative soil types of clay, sandy loam, and gravel were considered to evaluate transient impedance, ground potential rise (GPR), current-density distribution, soil-ionization behavior, and electro-thermal response. Experimentally, the concrete-encased configuration reduced impulse impedance by approximately 33–49% across the investigated soils. FEM analysis showed a reduction in peak current density from 69 to 43 A/m², corresponding to approximately 38%, together with a larger effective current-conduction region. Numerical predictions at higher current levels indicated delayed soil-ionization onset and lower temperature rise for the encased configuration compared with the conventional rod. These high-current results are identified as FEM predictions rather than direct experimental measurements because they exceed the 1.5 kA capability of the laboratory generator. The validated experimental numerical framework demonstrates the potential of conductive concrete encasement to improve impulse-current dispersion and reduce localized electrical and thermal stress in grounding electrodes. Further high-current experimental validation is required to confirm the predicted behavior beyond the laboratory test range.

Article.Title: Urinary metal exposure and type 2 diabetes mellitus: the potential mediating role of biological aging in older adults
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Chen F.; Ren H.; Zhang X.; Zhuo L.; Guo X.; Cui C.; Zhang P.; Zhang Y.; Zhang Y.; Ding L.; Lei L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasing, and environmental exposures may contribute to diabetes susceptibility. Metals are widespread environmental contaminants associated with metabolic disorders; however, the role of aging-related processes in this association remains unclear. A total of 843 participants were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of six metals (Pb, Zn, Mn, Cr, As, and Co) were measured, and phenotypic age was calculated based on nine biomarkers. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline models, weighted quantile sum regression, and exploratory mediation analysis were performed. Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr exposures were significantly associated with increased T2DM risk (all P < 0.05). Mixed metal exposure was also associated with higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.515, 95% CI: 1.277–1.884). Additionally, Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr were positively associated with phenotypic age, and each one-year increase in phenotypic age was associated with a 39.5% higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.395, 95% CI: 1.323–1.471). Phenotypic age may partially explain the associations between metal exposure and T2DM risk, with estimated mediation proportions of 10.9%–22.2%. Urinary metal exposure was associated with increased T2DM risk and higher phenotypic age. Phenotypic aging may represent a potential pathway linking environmental metal exposure with diabetes susceptibility.

Article.Title: Relationships between reproductive steroids, glandular microbiota, and volatile chemical signals in naturally cycling versus hormonally contracepted female lemurs
Article.Authors: Grebe N.; Boulet M.; Bornbusch S.; Greenwald L.; Dimac-Stohl K.; Grady J.; Drea C.
Article.Abstract: Olfactory communication directs socio-reproductive interaction in animals, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Endocrine action and microbial fermentation both influence the manufacture, composition, and expression of vertebrate chemosignals, involving volatile organic compounds (VOCs); however, there has been no integrative investigation of a putative tripart relationship between reproductive hormones, microbes, and VOCs. Our longitudinal experimental study of normative and contracepted females characterizes pairwise and tripart relationships in two scent-marking primates: ring-tailed lemurs ( Lemur catta ) and Coquerel’s sifakas ( Propithicus coquereli ). We used (1) serum enzyme immunoassays to quantify progesterone (P 4 ), estradiol (E 2 ), and the synthetic progestogen, medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA), (2) Illumina sequencing of the bacterial 16 S rRNA gene to identify microbiota in genital (labial) secretions, and (3) gas chromatography-mass spectrometry to characterize labial VOCs. Despite species differences in hormone concentrations, contraception expectedly muted natural variation in the E 2 /P 4 ratio and introduced initially supraphysiological MPA concentrations. Normative and induced hormonal variation was reflected in the microbial and/or chemical composition of labial secretions; however, predictive power varied by species, potentially reflecting socioecological variation or differences in glandular specialization. These results highlight the importance of cyclical endocrine variation in female reproductive signaling and the overriding effects on VOC manufacture of a disturbed glandular microbiome during contraception.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics > Primate Behavior and Ecology; Neuroscience > Sensory Systems > Olfactory and Sensory Function Studies; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics > Animal Behavior and Reproduction

Article.Title: Forecasting legal coastline based on highest astronomical tide as a predictive model for land–sea integration
Article.Authors: Setiyadi J.; Pratomo D.; Sukotjo B.; Pranowo W.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a highest astronomical tide (HAT)-referenced legal coastline framework to support the integration of terrestrial and marine cadastre in Bekasi Regency, Indonesia. Six Landsat image epochs acquired between 2015 and 2024 were processed and normalised to HAT derived from an 18.6-year tidal record at Pondok Dayung Tidal Station, selected as a regional reference because of its comparable tidal characteristics with the study area. Water bodies were delineated using the modified normalized difference water index (MNDWI), with scene-specific thresholds determined by the Otsu method and refined through morphological post-processing. This procedure produced a vertically consistent legal coastline for each selected observation epoch. The bounding-box area of the coastline decreased by 6.33 km 2 between 2015 and 2024, indicating a net contraction of the coastal spatial envelope despite localised erosion and accretion. A random forest regression model was used to hindcast the 2024 coastline and achieved an RMSE of 12.8 m, a mean displacement of 9.6 m, an MAE of 10.7 m, and an R 2 of 0.84. The resulting six-epoch dataset provides a consistent geospatial record of coastline change over a 10-year calendar period and supports scenario-based projections of future HAT-referenced coastline positions. The proposed legal coastline is intended as a scientific spatial reference for future harmonisation of land–sea administration, spatial planning, and coastal risk management; it does not replace existing statutory boundary definitions in Indonesia.
Article.TopicFields: Earth and Planetary Sciences > Earth-Surface Processes > Coastal and Marine Dynamics; Environmental Science > Ecology > Coastal wetland ecosystem dynamics; Environmental Science > Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law > Coastal and Marine Management

Article.Title: Effects of bonded rapid maxillary expansion and miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion on craniocervical posture, sagittal pharyngeal airway dimensions, and hyoid bone position
Article.Authors: Tuhan Kutlu E.; Baser B.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to compare the effects of bonded rapid maxillary expansion (RME) and miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) on skeletal measurements, craniocervical posture, sagittal pharyngeal airway dimensions, and hyoid bone position using lateral cephalometric radiographs. This retrospective cohort study included 60 patients with transverse maxillary deficiency treated with bonded RME or MARPE. The bonded RME group included 30 patients (17 females and 13 males) and the MARPE group included 30 patients (16 females and 14 males). Lateral cephalometric radiographs obtained before treatment (T0) and 6 months after completion of active screw activation (T1) were analyzed using ImageJ software. Generalized estimating equation models were used for repeated-measures comparisons, and chronological age was included as a covariate. After adjustment for age, no significant group × time interaction was observed for any skeletal measurement. ANB showed a significant time effect, whereas SNA, SNB, SN–GoGn, NSL/NL, and FH/ML did not show significant time-dependent changes. No significant group, time, or group × time interaction effects were detected for sagittal pharyngeal airway or hyoid measurements. Significant group × time interactions were observed for NSL/OPT, NSL/CVT, and CVT/HOR, indicating different craniocervical postural change patterns between the groups. In skeletal Class I patients with transverse maxillary deficiency and normal vertical growth patterns, bonded RME and MARPE showed comparable skeletal, sagittal pharyngeal airway, and hyoid outcomes after age adjustment. The absence of significant sagittal airway and hyoid changes should be interpreted within the limits of two-dimensional cephalometric assessment. The craniocervical posture findings should be considered exploratory and interpreted cautiously.
Article.TopicFields: Dentistry > Orthodontics > Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics; Medicine > Surgery > Craniofacial Disorders and Treatments; Dentistry > Oral Surgery > Cleft Lip and Palate Research

Article.Title: Selectively VO2-loaded terahertz metasurface for dual-state broadband polarization conversion and near-unity absorption
Article.Authors: Nipun M.; Islam M.; Arifuzzaman M.; Haque M.; Naidu R.; Rifatur Rana S.; Khan H.
Article.Abstract: A selectively VO 2 -loaded terahertz metasurface is studied for dual-state polarization conversion and absorption. The ground-backed unit cell consists of a broken diamond-shaped Au resonator, two square VO 2 loading regions, a circular VO 2 ring, and a polyimide spacer. With VO 2 in the insulating conductivity state, the structure operates as a reflective cross-polarization converter. PCR x remains above 0.90 from 1.5150 to 2.5849 THz, while PCRγ exceeds 0.90 from 1.5270 to 2.6726 THz. In the metallic conductivity state, A x remains above 0.90 from 1.5700 to 1.9970 THz and reaches 0.9997 at 1.8050 THz. At this frequency, the normalized impedance is 0.970 − j 0.014, and VO 2 accounts for 97.14% of the dissipated power. The conversion mechanism is supported by polarization-resolved reflection, rotated-axis phase response, and asymmetric current paths. The absorber state is associated with reflection suppression, resonator-ground coupling, and loss in the metallic VO 2 regions. Four-pass and six-pass mesh solutions differ by less than 1% in the principal response measures. Angular and tolerance analyses further show that the main features of both operating states are retained under the investigated conditions. The results numerically demonstrate dual-state terahertz operation through conductivity-state switching of selectively loaded VO 2 within a single planar unit cell.
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials > Metamaterials and Metasurfaces Applications; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Antenna and Metasurface Technologies; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Terahertz technology and applications

Article.Title: The mediating role of depression, anxiety, and stress between health literacy, life satisfaction, and psychological maladjustment in young Turkish adults
Article.Authors: Mert A.; Sarigül A.; Turan M.
Article.Abstract: The present study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Turkish version of the Mini-DASS and to test the mediating role of depression, anxiety, and stress in the association between health literacy and both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment. Two consecutive studies were conducted. Study 1 evaluated the psychometric properties of the Turkish Mini-DASS using item analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), criterion validity, and internal consistency reliability. Study 2 tested a proposed mediation model. Participants were Turkish young adults recruited online (Study 1: N = 460; Study 2: N = 905). In Study 1, EFA supported the original three factor structure of the Mini-DASS with acceptable factor loadings, and all subscales demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency. CFA indicated good model fit indices, supporting the validity of the three-factor model. In Study 2, mediation analysis revealed significant indirect effects of depression, anxiety, and stress in the association between health literacy and both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment. The Turkish Mini-DASS is a brief, reliable, and valid measure of psychological distress, encompassing depression, anxiety, and stress. The mediation findings indicated that health literacy is associated with both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment, and that depression, anxiety, and stress functioned as mediators in this association, highlighting the potential relevance of psychological distress in explaining how health literacy relates to individuals’ broader psychosocial functioning.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Experimental and Cognitive Psychology > Anxiety, Depression, Psychometrics, Treatment, Cognitive Processes; Health Professions > General Health Professions > Health Literacy and Information Accessibility; Psychology > Clinical Psychology > Health and Well-being Studies

Article.Title: Performance enhancement of electrohydrodynamic thruster using sub unit electrode configuration
Article.Authors: Jiang X.; Tsubata H.; Shimizu S.; Nozaki T.
Article.Abstract: Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) propulsion has garnered significant interest as a lightweight and silent thrust generation technology, owing to its lack of moving parts and low vibration characteristics. However, enhancing the thrust output and energy efficiency of EHD thrusters remains a key challenge. This study introduces a novel thrust enhancement electrode configuration that incorporates a sub unit for an EHD propulsion system. Experimental results demonstrate that the introduction of the sub unit substantially increases thrust generation compared with the conventional electrode system without a sub unit. At an applied voltage of 22 kV, the conventional configuration generates a thrust of 50.23 mN, whereas the sub unit electrode system achieves 64.09 mN, representing an approximate 27.59% increase in thrust. To further enhance thrust generation, an additional structure, termed the sub unit plus, is implemented beneath the original sub unit electrode system. This enhanced configuration optimizes aerodynamic interactions within the investigated range, resulting in a thrust output of 68.70 mN. The sub unit plus electrode system delivers an additional 7.19% increase in thrust over the sub unit configuration alone, and a total improvement of 36.77% relative to the conventional system. These results indicate an engineering trade-off between maximizing absolute thrust and maintaining thrust to power ratio of the configuration. Overall, the incorporation of sub unit structures is crucial in enhancing thrust output. The proposed design strategy provides a promising pathway for improving thrust performance in EHD propulsion systems and provides valuable insights for the development of higher thrust output EHD thrusters.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Electrohydrodynamics and Fluid Dynamics; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Aerosol Filtration and Electrostatic Precipitation; Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Plasma and Flow Control in Aerodynamics

Article.Title: Clinical and imaging characteristics of difficult-to-treat patients with rheumatoid arthritis and peripheral psoriatic arthritis with ultrasound-confirmed inflammation
Article.Authors: Omaña-Iglesias O.; Novell G.; Azuaga A.; Frade-Sosa B.; Sarmiento-Monroy J.; Cuervo A.; Ponce A.; Corzo P.; Farietta S.; Ruiz-Esquide V.; Gómez-Puerta J.; Cañete J.; Ramírez J.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the proportion of Difficult To Treat (D2T) disease according to three operational definitions in a population of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and peripheral Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) with ultrasound (US)-confirmed inflammation, and to characterize its clinical, structural, and therapeutic features. Cross-sectional study involving RA or peripheral PsA who had active disease, established through both clinical and US examination. D2T disease was categorized according to three criteria: an operational treatment-failure-based D2T definition, requiring inadequate response or failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and ≥ 2 b/tsDMARDs with different mechanisms of action (MOAs); a time-dependent criterion, defined by failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and two or more b/tsDMARDs with different MOAs over a period of less than 12 months and a very refractory criterion, requiring failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and ≥​ 3 b/tsDMARDs with different MOAs. A total of 148 patients were included. Overall, 31.7% fulfilled the treatment-failure-based D2T definition, 12.1% the time-based definition, and 18.2% the very refractory one. Treatment-failure-based D2T disease was more frequent in RA ( p = 0.033) and associated with longer disease duration ( p < 0.001), cardiovascular comorbidity ( p = 0.037), US proliferative synovitis ( p = 0.034), erosive disease ( p < 0.001), combined therapy (csDMARD + b/tsDMARD) ( p < 0.001), and prior tsDMARD ( p < 0.001). Time-based D2T disease was equally present in both RA and PsA, associated with combined therapy ( p = 0.008), tsDMARD use ( p = 0.002), and nail involvement ( p = 0.019). Very refractory D2T disease was more prevalent in RA ( p = 0.029) and associated with longer disease duration ( p = 0.014), erosive disease ( p < 0.001), US proliferative synovitis ( p = 0.046), combined therapy ( p = 0.003), and tsDMARD exposure ( p < 0.001). D2T disease defines a severe phenotype characterized by cumulative disease burden, structural damage, comorbidities, and treatment refractoriness. Erosive disease, combined therapy, and tsDMARD exposure emerged as associated factors across definitions, emphasizing early disease control and comprehensive management.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Rheumatology > Rheumatoid Arthritis Research and Therapies; Medicine > Rheumatology > Spondyloarthritis Studies and Treatments; Medicine > Hematology > Autoimmune and Inflammatory Disorders Research

Article.Title: Exploring sustainable use intention of AIGC image enhancement technologies among designers
Article.Authors: Zhou B.; Wan B.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates designers’ sustainable use intention toward AIGC-assisted image enhancement technologies in low-light mural design. An extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework was developed to examine how image-related performance perceptions, facilitating conditions, and effort-related factors influence designer experience and sustainable use intention. Survey data from 557 designers were analyzed using a two-stage Structural Equation Modeling–Artificial Neural Network (SEM–ANN) approach. The SEM results indicate that facilitating conditions exert the strongest direct influence on sustainable use intention, while performance expectancy substantially influences designer experience. Resource and organizational support significantly contribute to facilitating conditions, whereas technological accessibility shows no significant effect. Designer experience and sustainable use intention are also positively associated with social influence. These findings highlight the importance of organizational and resource support alongside perceived technological performance, extending the application of UTAUT to AIGC-assisted creative design and providing practical guidance for image enhancement tool adoption.
Article.TopicFields: Decision Sciences > Information Systems and Management > Technology Adoption and User Behaviour; Computer Science > Computer Graphics and Computer-Aided Design > Digital Media and Visual Art; Computer Science > Human-Computer Interaction > Innovative Human-Technology Interaction

Article.Title: Hierarchical graph attention and memory-augmented learning for spatio-temporal network intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Nune S.; Moka D.; Jerith G.; Srinivas P.; Udata S.
Article.Abstract: Graph neural networks are increasingly used for network intrusion detection, but their reported advantages often depend on evaluation choices. We present STAR-IDS, which builds a graph from every window of ten consecutive network flows, applies two-level graph attention and a prototype memory bank, and estimates prediction uncertainty with Monte Carlo Dropout. STAR-IDS was evaluated on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v3, with real IP-address nodes and flows ordered by start time, and on the IoT dataset NF-ToN-IoT-v2, using block-wise splits that prevent leakage, temporally blocked cross-validation, five paired seeds and controlled baselines (E-GraphSAGE, GAT, GCN, GraphSAGE and a graph-free MLP) trained under identical conditions. On NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, STAR-IDS achieved 87.61% ± 1.22% accuracy and 86.41% macro-F1, and no difference from the baselines or ablations was statistically significant after Holm correction; on NF-ToN-IoT, the graph-free MLP was the most accurate model (81.10% vs. 77.21%). The uncertainty estimates separated erroneous from correct predictions with an AUC of 0.89, and on that dataset flagged predictions were 16–25 percentage points less accurate than auto-accepted ones. Control experiments show that shuffling flows before windowing, synthetic node identifiers and forward-in-time splits change accuracy by up to 68 percentage points.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting; Computer Science > Hardware and Architecture > Network Packet Processing and Optimization

Article.Title: High-throughput mineralogical characterization using automated in-situ microscopy and Raman spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Stigliano L.; Cosmidis J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation in natural and engineered systems is controlled by complex interactions among physicochemical variables and organic molecules, making large-scale systematic exploration of mineralization pathways challenging. Here we present a high-throughput experimental and analytical workflow that enables rapid, particle-resolved characterization of mineral formation. The platform integrates miniaturized mineralization experiments in multi-well plates with automated optical microscopy, particle detection, morphometric analysis, machine-learning classification, and targeted Raman spectromicroscopy. Applied to calcium carbonate precipitation mediated by organic additives, the workflow enables particle-resolved morphological analysis and mineral phase identification. Across 307 experiments involving 23 organic additives, automated imaging revealed ten reproducible particle morphologies. Raman spectromicroscopy showed that each morphotype consistently corresponds to a single mineral phase, either calcite or vaterite. A Random Forest model trained on morphological descriptors classified particle types with a mean accuracy of 97 ± 1%, enabling automated quantification of morphotype populations across experimental conditions. Systematic screening showed that organic additives strongly influence particle populations, modifying particle number, size distributions, and accessible particle morphologies. Time-lapse imaging further enables rapid estimation of particle growth rates, providing a practical metric to identify conditions that promote or inhibit mineralization. This integrated workflow provides a scalable framework for mapping mineralization pathways across multidimensional chemical spaces.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: vaterite; calcite; random forest; calcium carbonate precipitation; particle morphology; automated microscopy; microplates; organic additives; mineral phase identification; high-throughput experimentation; particle growth rate
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Biomaterials > Calcium Carbonate Crystallization and Inhibition; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geochemistry and Petrology > Mineralogy and Gemology Studies; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Microbial Applications in Construction Materials

Article.Title: Synergies in streamlining: AI and Lean Management in Polish healthcare administration
Article.Authors: Garski J.; Walkowiak D.
Article.Abstract: Administrative tasks consume 15–30% of healthcare budgets, and applying artificial intelligence (AI) tools within Lean Management (LM) is theorized to yield substantial efficiency gains, yet professional perceptions of this integration remain largely unexamined. In this exploratory cross-sectional survey of 330 Polish healthcare professionals across five role groups (April–September 2025), we introduce the AI-Lean Synergy Index, an exploratory formative composite measure of perceived AI-LM synergy pending confirmatory validation, derived from a 39-item instrument grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (average Cronbach’s α = 0.844). The Index yielded a median of 0.60 (interquartile range 0.30), with 88.9% of respondents ( n = 244) perceiving moderate to very high synergy. A 41.8-percentage-point perception–application gap separated belief that AI can improve healthcare quality (69.1%) from conscious application of AI to administrative efficiency (27.3%), while perceived implementation barriers were uniformly high (median 4.0/5.0 across 11 categories). Healthcare managers scored significantly higher than physicians (median 0.60 vs. 0.50; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.045, post-hoc p = 0.0304), a difference consistent with a champion–skeptic dynamic and, alternatively, with role-specific referents for administrative efficiency. We propose an evidence-informed priority framework: governance, competency development, pilot projects, and change management for translating perceived synergy into administrative practice in centrally financed health systems.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Health Informatics > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education; Medicine > Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health > Healthcare Quality and Management; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

Article.Title: Evaluating the decomposition of agricultural legume species to estimate nutrient recycling in Mediterranean climates
Article.Authors: De Prato L.; Harrison R.; Scanlan C.; Howieson J.; Steel E.; Yates R.
Article.Abstract: Legumes enhance the sustainability of Mediterranean farming systems by increasing soil nutrient levels, improving soil water and carbon retention, and reducing reliance on synthetic fertilisers through biological nitrogen fixation. However, the environmental and biological complexity of residue decomposition necessitates a clear understanding of how different crop residues decompose in synchrony with the nutrient requirements of subsequent cereal or oilseed crops. To address this, litterbag experiments were conducted at two distinct agroecological zones within the Western Australian Wheatbelt (Kendenup: 730 mm rainfall, Brown Gravelly Chromosol; Konnongorring: 350 mm rainfall, Grey Chromosol sandy duplex). Residues from nine legume species (grain legumes: Lupinus angustifolius, Vicia faba ; traditional pastures: Trifolium subterraneum, Vicia sativa, V. villosa ; novel ley legumes: Ornithopus sativus, Trigonella balansae, Trifolium spumosum ) and wheat ( Triticum aestivum ) were monitored from summer to winter (60 weeks) to assess decomposition patterns and associated C and N dynamics. Decomposition rates were significantly higher at the high-rainfall Kendenup site, with all species showing 70–85% biomass loss by 60 weeks compared to 50–75% at Konnongorring, reflecting moisture as the primary driver of decomposition. Across both sites, T. aestivum exhibited the slowest decomposition and highest N immobilisation (final C:N ~ 35), followed by grain legumes L. angustifolius and V. faba (final C:N 30–40). Vetch species ( V. sativa, V. villosa ) and T. spumosum decomposed most rapidly, achieving final C:N ratios of 11–19. Novel ley legumes O. sativus and Trig. balansae displayed intermediate decomposition rates and achieved a C:N ratio of 25–35, potentially optimising N release synchrony with subsequent crop demand. These findings provide the first comparative assessment of second-generation ley legumes ( O. sativus , Trig. balansae ) alongside traditional pasture and grain legumes under field conditions in Mediterranean environments. Results demonstrate that novel pasture legumes provided sustained N release, potentially optimising nutrient synchrony with subsequent cereal crops better than either fast-decomposing traditional pastures or low N fixer grain legume residues. This species-specific decomposition information addresses a critical knowledge gap in managing N cycling in evolving Australian farming systems, where increases in N harvest index and changes to ley systems have altered N dynamics. This study demonstrates that, while edaphoclimatic conditions were strongly associated with residue decomposition in the Mediterranean environments of Western Australia, species selection substantially influenced the timing of N release. Novel ley legumes offer intermediate decomposition patterns that may better balance availability and consistency of N release compared to traditional legume options, with potential implications for managing nutrient synchrony, cereal biomass, and grain quality (protein and grain size) in evolving rotational systems.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil Carbon and Nitrogen Dynamics; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Agronomy and Crop Science > Agronomic Practices and Intercropping Systems; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Agricultural Science and Fertilization

Article.Title: Virtual screening of Withania somnifera phytochemicals identifies scopoletin and linoleic acid as predicted dual-target AChE/BACE1 candidates for alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Alsrhani A.; Riaz S.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder driven by interlinked pathological processes, including cholinergic deficit and amyloid-β accumulation, limiting the efficacy of single-target therapies. Multitarget-directed ligands capable of simultaneously modulating acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and β-secretase 1 (BACE1) offer a promising but underexplored strategy, particularly from natural product sources. Although the withanolides of Withania somnifera have been extensively studied for neuroprotection, its non-withanolide phytochemical fraction remains largely unexplored as a source of dual-target anti-AD agents. Here, from 129 initially retrieved non-withanolide phytochemical entries, duplicate removal across plant parts yielded 80 unique compounds, of which 76 returned valid SwissADME outputs; these compounds, derived from W. somnifera were evaluated using an integrated in silico pipeline comprising ADMET and toxicity profiling, molecular docking against AChE (PDB: 7E3H) and BACE1 (PDB: 7F1D), PASS-based bioactivity prediction, BioTransformer metabolite profiling, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, with donepezil as the reference inhibitor. Twelve compounds satisfied pharmacokinetic filtering criteria, and this screening identified scopoletin and linoleic acid as the leading dual-target candidates, showing computationally predicted binding affinities toward AChE (− 7.7 and − 7.9 kcal/mol) and BACE1 (− 5.2 and − 5.8 kcal/mol) respectively, together with favorable blood–brain barrier permeability and low predicted toxicity. Molecular dynamics analysis further showed that the AChE-linoleic acid complex maintained conformational stability comparable to the AChE-donepezil reference complex over the full 100-ns trajectory, supporting a physically stable binding mode. These findings identify scopoletin and linoleic acid as predicted dual-target AChE/BACE1 candidates from W. somnifera , offering a computational foundation for their experimental validation as multitarget neuroprotective candidates against Alzheimer's disease.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Pharmacology (medical) > Cholinesterase and Neurodegenerative Diseases; Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Drug Discovery > Computational Drug Discovery Methods; Medicine > Complementary and alternative medicine > Phytochemicals and Medicinal Plants

Article.Title: Genomic analysis links phage susceptibility to the K5 capsule in uropathogenic Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Nagano D.; Hanawa T.; Tanaka M.; Tanji Y.; Matsuda T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) is the leading cause of urinary tract infections, which can progress to bloodstream infections, while the increasing prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing strains limits treatment options. Although bacteriophage (phage) therapy is promising, identifying effective phages is resource-intensive. Genomic predictors of phage susceptibility could facilitate phage selection; however, the underlying bacterial traits remain uncharacterized. Here, 49 ESBL-producing UPEC clinical isolates and 42 phages were analysed to investigate bacterial genomic features associated with the phage susceptibility. Independent susceptibility clustering and genome-wide association analyses facilitated identification of K5 capsule biosynthesis genes as shared genomic features associated with susceptibility to specific phage clusters. The K5 strains were broadly susceptible, whereas three strains remained nonsusceptible; genome analysis revealed mutations in capsule biosynthesis genes linked to reduced capsular polysaccharide levels. Phage adsorption assays using the K5 capsule fraction supported the K5 capsule as a receptor for these phage clusters. Furthermore, phages associated with K5 susceptibility were predicted to encode putative depolymerases similar to K5 lyase, extending this mechanism to phages effective against ESBL-producing UPEC. These results support the K5 capsule as a receptor for phages targeting ESBL-producing UPEC and highlight its potential as a predictor of phage susceptibility.
Article.TopicFields: Immunology and Microbiology > Virology > Bacteriophages and microbial interactions; Immunology and Microbiology > Microbiology > Escherichia coli research studies; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Bacterial Genetics and Biotechnology

Article.Title: Dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network for spatiotemporal correlation modeling of mine microseismic events and intelligent rockburst risk level reasoning
Article.Authors: An J.; Zhou J.; Li H.; Wang X.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Deep mining releases accumulated strain energy violently, and microseismic arrays record the fracturing that precedes rockbursts. Graph neural networks have already been applied to seismic and microseismic tasks such as phase association, source characterisation and event forecasting; what those graphs share is a topology anchored to a fixed sensor array and a single edge semantics, so they cannot follow an event field that turns over as the working face advances. This paper proposes a dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network (DHGAT). Every event enters as a node that retains four feature channels — waveform, source parameter, spatial and temporal — and three edge types (spatial proximity, temporal sequence, feature similarity) are rebuilt inside a 48 h sliding window. Relation-specific multi-head attention aggregates neighbours separately for each edge type, a semantic-level layer learns how much each relation contributes, and a gated recurrent encoder tracks the evolving graph embedding before four risk grades are assigned: no risk, low, moderate and high. On a 24-month catalogue of 7956 events from one deep metal mine, DHGAT reached 91.9 ± 0.4% accuracy, 0.853 ± 0.008 macro-F1 and 0.887 ± 0.006 quadratic weighted Kappa over ten runs, ahead of the strongest static heterogeneous baseline (HAN, 89.2% and 0.788) and of every other baseline at p < 0.01; recall on high-risk events reached 80.0%. Relation weights migrate from spatially dominated during gradual stress build-up to temporally dominated in the final hours before failure, which mirrors the shift from distributed microcracking to localised coalescence, and a perturbation test confirms that the attention carries the discriminative signal. Inference costs 46 ms per window on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. All data come from one mine, so the reported thresholds require recalibration before transfer.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Geotechnical and Geomechanical Engineering; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Geomechanics and Mining Engineering

Article.Title: Network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of dioctyl terephthalate in systemic lupus erythematosus pathogenesis
Article.Authors: Fang T.; Long S.; Wang T.; Chen T.; Yang H.; Zhong F.
Article.Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) may serve as an environmental risk factor for multiple diseases. Here, we explore potential molecular associations between DOTP exposure and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and identify candidate targets and pathways that may underlie these associations. Integrated network toxicology and transcriptomics identified SLE-associated targets. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses revealed underlying mechanisms. Machine learning was used to prioritize candidate DOTP–SLE targets. CIBERSORT assessed target-immune cell infiltration relationships. Molecular docking evaluated DOTP-target binding affinities. We identified 39 DOTP-associated SLE targets. Enrichment analyses linked them to inflammatory cytokine production and immune activation. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) and machine learning prioritized six key targets (NFKB1, TLR4, CASP9, CDK5, DNMT1, PRKCD). Exploratory CIBERSORT analysis described associations with LM22-derived reference profiles, while ROC analysis characterized within-cohort discrimination and an exploratory nomogram summarized the combined candidate-gene pattern. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and these key targets. Our research results suggest a potential link between DOTP exposure and SLE progression through specific genes and pathways, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and the relevant SLE targets. The ROC and nomogram analyses provided supplementary within-cohort characterization of the prioritized candidate genes. This study provides mechanistic insights into DOTP-associated SLE and supports the development of targeted prevention strategies.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Rheumatology > Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Research; Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Drug Discovery > Computational Drug Discovery Methods; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Effects and risks of endocrine disrupting chemicals

Article.Title: ChGBO_QRNN: chronological gooseneck barnacle-based quantum recurrent neural networks for intrusion detection in IoT-SDN
Article.Authors: Jyothi B.; Thaiyalnayaki S.
Article.Abstract: There has been significant growth in the number of heterogeneous components configured within the Internet of Things (IoT) to allow effective data communication. However, IoT components are resource-constrained, and there are no standardized security procedures for communication within IoT platforms. While various solutions have been developed to secure communication in the IoT ecosystem, the existing approaches are not always reliable enough to address cyber threats and unwanted intrusions originating from IoT endpoints. Thus, this research presents a Chronological Gooseneck Barnacle Optimization-based Quantum Recurrent Neural Network (ChGBO_QRNN) for intrusion detection in SDN-IoT. Here, the proposed system contains three phases, which include a sniffer, a detector, and a sensor phase. In the sniffer phase, the features are extracted from the packets, and the extracted features are utilized for intrusion detection. In the detector phase, intrusion detection is carried out by the Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks (QRNN), and ChGBO is employed for training. In the sensing phase, the boundary of the attack is checked. If any concept drift is detected, the identification of a new attack is done using the proposed ChGBO_QRNN. Furthermore, the ChGBO_QRNN has gained weighted Accuracy, weighted True Positive Rate (TPR), weighted True Negative Rate (TNR), weighted F1-score, and weighted precision as 91.868%, 90.134%, 92.894%, 92.072%, and 92.978%.

Article.Title: Redox driven inflammatory and senescence-associated changes in Channa striata exposed to insecticide Fipronil with ascorbic acid-mediated modulation
Article.Authors: Yadav S.; Dubey A.; Jain A.; Singh S.; Dwivedi S.; Dwivedi S.; Tiwari V.; Srivastava R.; Dubey I.; Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Fipronil (FIP), a widely used second-generation phenylpyrazole insecticide, is known for its broad-spectrum and systemic activity. The present study evaluated the toxic effects of commercial FIP (80% WG) on the striped snakehead fish, Channa striata , following 15, 30, and 45 days of exposure, and assessed the protective role of ascorbic acid (AA). Fish were divided into six groups: control, AA control (50 mg L⁻ 1 ), 0.002 mg L⁻ 1 FIP, 0.002 mg L⁻ 1 FIP + AA, 0.004 mg L⁻ 1 FIP, and 0.004 mg L⁻ 1 FIP + AA. FIP exposure significantly ( p < 0.05 ) increased erythrocytic ROS levels and protein carbonyl content, while GST activity declined markedly. SOD and CAT activities exhibited biphasic responses during the exposure period. Significant ( p < 0.05 ) alterations were observed in senescence-associated gene expression profiles. Correlation and Principal Component Analysis revealed associations among oxidative stress markers, DNA damage response genes, inflammatory signaling, antioxidant defense, and senescence-associated gene expression. Co-exposure with AA partially alleviated oxidative stress and moderated gene expression changes, indicating its protective potential against FIP-induced toxicity.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Environmental Toxicology and Ecotoxicology; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Aquaculture disease management and microbiota; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Immunotoxicology and immune responses

Article.Title: Experimental study on corrosion mitigation and shear behavior of novel repairable rock bolts
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Qian S.; Lin Z.; Cai Z.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Based on the concept of repairable anchorage for post-damage performance recovery and corrosion protection in jointed rock masses, this study develops novel repairable structures in the form of rock bolts: the extrusion-crushing repairable (ECR) bolt and the hot-melt repairable (HMR) bolt. Chloride wet–dry cycling tests and double-shear tests were conducted on separate groups of double-jointed rock mass specimens to investigate their anticorrosion effectiveness and restoration capability. Preliminary results indicate that both repairable bolts can release repair materials after damage to partially restore sealing conditions, suppress corrosive ingress, and enhance shear resistance. Specifically, the ECR bolt demonstrated the potential for superior corrosion resistance, achieving higher peak shear load and greater external work to peak load under the tested conditions. This improvement may be associated with the infiltration and adhesion of the released polyurethane–ethyl acetate repair agent, which helps seal damaged regions and restore grout integrity over a wider area. In contrast, the HMR bolt provides localized sealing and partial reinforcement through thermally activated melting of EVA adhesive, leading to comparatively moderate enhancements in corrosion resistance and shear capacity. Observations of the failure characteristics further elucidated the reparative mechanisms and the differences in mechanical responses among the bolt systems. This work suggests that integrating repair functionality into rock bolting systems may provide a promising approach for mitigating damage and corrosion in rock engineering.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Geomechanics and Mining Engineering; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Grouting, Rheology, and Soil Mechanics

Article.Title: Clinical and serological differences associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Sjögren’s disease: a real-world multicenter analysis
Article.Authors: Cafaro G.; Lepri G.; Colafrancesco S.; Dei B.; Peruzzi A.; Guiducci S.; Priori R.; Baldini C.; Quartuccio L.; Cipriani P.; Alunno A.; Berardicurti O.; Valentini I.; Gerli R.; Bartoloni E.; N/A N/A.; Baldini C.; Berardicurti O.; Cipriani P.; Priori R.; Quartuccio L.; Alunno A.; Atzeni F.; Bardelli M.; Colafrancesco S.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) is a common metabolic comorbidity in patients with Sjögren’s disease (SjD), but their clinical and serologic profile remain incompletely characterized. We retrospectively compared SjD patients with and without DM and explored factors associated with a history of cardiovascular (CV) events. Patients with DM were compared with individually age- and sex-matched non-diabetic comparators. Group comparisons used appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests. Associations with DM were examined using logistic regression adjusted for age and disease duration and, in sensitivity analyses accounting for the matched design, conditional logistic regression stratified by reconstructed matched sets. A clinically prespecified Firth logistic model fitted to the original observed data evaluated factors associated with a history of CV events. Among 245 patients (95% female; mean age 70 ± 12 years), 100 had DM. Compared with non-diabetic patients, those with DM had higher BMI and more hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia. Disease activity was similar but ESSDAI was available for only 54% of patients. After adjustment for age and disease duration, DM was associated with lower odds of anti-SSB/La positivity (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25–0.88) and low C3 (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10–0.76); estimates were similar in conditional analyses accounting for matched sets (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25–0.91, and OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.09–0.80, respectively). Thirty-one patients had a history of CV events. In the primary Firth model (n = 239), age (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02–1.12; p = 0.005) and hypertension (OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.27–9.54; p = 0.012) were associated with CV history. Anti-SSB/La, smoking and current HCQ use were not significantly associated with CV history. Multiple-imputation results were consistent. Adjusted metformin analyses showed no statistically significant associations. Type 2 DM was associated with a clinical and serologic profile characterized by greater metabolic burden and lower prevalence of serological markers associated with B-cell activity. In the exploratory CV analysis, age and hypertension were associated with a history of CV events. These observational findings, in particular the serological associations, were identified at nominal significance without correction for multiple testing and require independent and prospective validation.

Article.Title: Comparing self-regulation, anxiety, and willingness to communicate across blended, face-to-face, and online instruction in female EFL learners
Article.Authors: Shi H.; Salimi V.; Izadpanah S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Technology-enhanced language instruction has expanded the range of instructional options available to EFL learners, yet evidence comparing blended, online, and face-to-face modes across multiple cognitive and affective outcomes remains limited, particularly among advanced EFL learners. This study compared self-regulated learning strategies (SRLSs), foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA), and willingness to communicate (WTC) in English writing across these three instructional modes. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was conducted with 360 advanced female EFL learners in Iran (120 per group), selected through two-stage cluster sampling from language institutes. Learners participated in 10 instructional sessions delivered through blended, online, or face-to-face modes. Pre-test and post-test measures of SRLS, FLCA, and WTC were collected using self-report questionnaires. One-way ANCOVAs were conducted for each outcome, controlling for the corresponding pre-test score, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. After adjustment for baseline scores, statistically significant between-group differences were observed for SRLS, FLCA, and WTC. The blended group had higher adjusted SRLS scores than the online and face-to-face groups (partial η² = 0.411) and higher adjusted WTC scores in English writing (partial η² = 0.266), but lower adjusted FLCA scores than both comparison groups (partial η² = 0.136). No statistically significant differences were observed between the online and face-to-face groups for any outcome. These findings identify a consistent pattern of adjusted between-group differences associated with instructional mode among advanced female Iranian EFL learners. They do not establish comparative efficacy or causal superiority of blended instruction. Pending replication using randomized designs, objective measures, and more diverse samples, the findings may inform further investigation of blended instructional arrangements and the specific pedagogical features associated with learner outcomes.
Article.TopicFields: Arts and Humanities > Language and Linguistics > EFL/ESL Teaching and Learning; Social Sciences > Education > English Language Learning and Teaching; Social Sciences > Education > Online and Blended Learning

Article.Title: Material-dependent structure of roughness representation in generative AI-based texture analysis
Article.Authors: Momiyama Y.; Ishizuka H.; Hiraki T.; Miki N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative image models can produce visually different expressions of surface roughness depending on material context, but the structure of these variations remains unclear. Here, we systematically examined roughness-related image features in textures generated for six material categories at ten prompt-defined roughness levels. Three prompting conditions were compared: a Quantitative Model, a Generic Linguistic Model using common roughness descriptors across materials, and a Material-Specific Linguistic Model using category-specific descriptions. Nine interpretable image features comprising eight luminance-distribution statistics and the FFT spectral centroid were analyzed. Feature–roughness correlations varied substantially across materials, indicating that no single feature within the examined feature set consistently captured roughness-related variation across all categories. Hierarchical clustering revealed significant associations between material category and cluster assignment for both linguistic models but not for the Quantitative Model, with the strongest associations observed for the Material-Specific Linguistic Model. Silhouette scores in the full nine-dimensional feature space were −0.065, −0.001, and 0.271 for the Quantitative, Generic Linguistic, and Material-Specific Linguistic Models, respectively, indicating clearer category-dependent organization with material-specific linguistic conditioning. These findings demonstrate that roughness-related image-feature organization in the examined generative model depends on both material context and linguistic prompting. This framework provides testable hypotheses for future comparison with physically characterized surfaces and human perceptual judgments.
Article.TopicFields: Physics and Astronomy > Instrumentation > Surface Roughness and Optical Measurements; Computer Science > Computer Graphics and Computer-Aided Design > Computer Graphics and Visualization Techniques; Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Performance of five large language models (LLM) on infectious diseases related questions
Article.Authors: Maker J.; Kim M.; Guo X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As there i​s growing interest in utilizing large language models (LLMs) in healthcare education, there are still concerns about their accuracy. The primary study question is to evaluate the accuracy of five LLMs in answering infectious disease (ID) related questions. We compared five LLMs—ChatGPT-4.1, ChatGPT-4o-mini, Claude, Copilot, and Gemini—on 227 exam items from an infectious diseases (ID) course in a Doctor of Pharmacy program. Items were categorized by topic, Bloom’s taxonomy, and format. LLM accuracy across different categories was summarized using descriptive statistics. The Chi-Square test was used to compare results among the different LLMs. Agreement across responses from different LLMs was investigated via Cohen’s Kappa Coefficient. The overall accuracy across all models ranged from 89.4% to 91.2% with ChatGPT 4o-mini scoring highest and Claude and Copilot scoring lowest. LLMs had highest accuracy answering pharmacology questions (93.6%), followed by therapeutics (93.0%), PK/PD (91.1%), microbiology (87.5%), and medicinal chemistry (84%). Medicinal chemistry and microbiology performed significantly worse compared to therapeutics (p < 0.05). Questions categorized as Evaluate/Create performed significantly worse compared to Remember/Understand category (85.6% vs. 92.0%, p < 0.05). The accuracy of questions with a picture was significantly worse than those with no picture (69% vs 91%, respectively). Inter-model agreement was moderate (κ = 0.497–0.613). Contemporary LLMs show high accuracy on ID coursework, with weaknesses in chemistry/microbiology content, higher-order reasoning, and image interpretation; careful integration and guidance are warranted.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
