Article.Title: Reconstructing the human endometrium in vitro using co-cultures of endometrial epithelial organoids and stromal cells
Article.Authors: Agustina-Hernández M.; Bueno-Fernandez C.; Grillo-Risco R.; Galán A.; Alonso-Frías P.; Corpas N.; Francés-Herrero E.; Gómez-Álvarez M.; Faus A.; Romeu M.; Ferrero H.; García-García F.; Cervelló I.
Article.Abstract: Human endometrial epithelial organoids are valuable in vitro models that recapitulate key epithelial features of the endometrium. However, they lack the stromal compartment, preventing the physiological epithelial–stromal crosstalk involved in regulating endometrial homeostasis and function. This study investigated whether co-culturing human endometrial epithelial organoids with stromal cells improves their molecular resemblance to native endometrial tissue. Endometrial biopsies were obtained from healthy donors ( n = 6). Human endometrial epithelial organoids and autologous stromal cells were isolated and cultured for 7 days under monoculture or co-culture conditions using a Transwell system. A human endometrial stromal stem cell line (ICE7) was also evaluated. Five experimental conditions were established: organoid monoculture, primary stromal cell monoculture, ICE7 monoculture, organoids co-cultured with primary stromal cells, and organoids co-cultured with ICE7 cells. Cell identity and viability were assessed by immunocytochemistry and LIVE/DEAD assays. Transcriptomic profiling was performed by RNA sequencing on all cell populations and native tissue, whereas secretomes were characterized by tandem mass spectrometry of conditioned-medium samples. Co-cultured organoids exhibited a transcriptomic profile that more closely resembled native endometrial tissue than did organoid monocultures. Principal component analysis showed a shift in the co-cultured organoid profile toward the native tissue, accompanied by higher transcriptomic correlation coefficients ( r ≈ 0.79 versus r ≈ 0.70) and fewer differentially expressed genes relative to native tissue samples. Co-cultured organoids showed significant upregulation of genes associated with endometrial function and cellular proliferation, including CDK1 , TOP2A , BUB1B , PRC1 , and SOX17 ( p < 0.05). No differentially expressed genes were detected between organoids co-cultured with primary stromal cells and those co-cultured with ICE7 cells. Secretome analysis identified proteins uniquely associated with co-culture conditions, including SOX17, HDAC4, BAG1, and YY1, suggesting active epithelial–stromal communication. Co-culture with stromal cells enhances the molecular fidelity of human endometrial epithelial organoids by promoting transcriptomic and secretome profiles that more closely resemble those of native endometrium. These findings highlight the importance of epithelial–stromal communication in endometrial modeling and support the use of co-culture systems for studies of endometrial physiology, regeneration, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic development.

Article.Title: Effects of shoe longitudinal bending stiffness and runner level on Achilles tendon loading through musculoskeletal modelling
Article.Authors: Lin S.; Yuan H.; Shao J.; Liu D.; Ruan M.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined the effects of runner level and shoe longitudinal bending stiffness (LBS) on estimated AT loading and lower-limb biomechanics. Thirty-one male rearfoot strikers (18 experienced and 13 novice) ran at 4.17 m/s in carbon-plated shoes with three LBS levels (T1: 10.9; T2: 17.5; T3: 32.9 Nm/rad). AT force was estimated using a subject-specific musculoskeletal model with static optimization. Discrete outcomes were analyzed using mixed two-way ANOVA with Holm correction, and waveforms using one-dimensional Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM1D). Experienced runners exhibited greater estimated AT force during 12.7%-18.6%, 23.3%-63.4%, and 79.7%-88.9% of stance (all p < 0.024), but lower force during 3.6–5.7% ( p = 0.046). Discrete AT loading rate was higher in experienced runners ( p holm = 0.030, $$\:{\eta\:}_{p}^{2}$$ = 0.208), whereas group effects on discrete peak AT force and AT impulse were nonsignificant. LBS affected discrete peak AT force ( p holm =0.013, $$\:{\eta\:}_{p}^{2}$$ =0.159; T3 > T1), AT impulse ( p holm = 0.003, $$\:{\eta\:}_{p}^{2}\:$$ = 0.264; T2 and T3 > T1), and peak ankle dorsiflexion angle ( p holm < 0.001, $$\:{\eta\:}_{p}^{2}$$ = 0.472), without significant corresponding SPM1D effects. No runner-level × LBS interaction was detected for AT-loading outcomes. Runner level and shoe LBS therefore influence model-estimated AT loading through distinct, independent pathways.

Article.Title: Effects of delayed inhalation therapy on apoptosis-related proteins and late remodeling after mixed-insult lung injury in rats
Article.Authors: Ziablitsev D.; Kostenko V.; Mykhaylovska V.; Babenko M.; Lykhodiievskyi V.; Kurchenko A.; Ziablitsev S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Introduction: Acute lung injury (ALI) remains a critical condition associated with high mortality despite advances in intensive care. Its pathogenesis involves diffuse bronchoalveolar damage that frequently progresses to fibrotic remodeling of lung tissue. Dysregulated apoptosis of pulmonary parenchymal cells represents a key mechanism linking inflammation to fibrosis and is largely controlled by the balance between proapoptotic and antiapoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins, including Bax and Bcl-xL, as well as activation of caspase-3. Modulation of these pathways represents a promising therapeutic strategy. Aims To evaluate the effects of inhalation therapy with camostat mesylate, methylprednisolone, and enoxaparin sodium on the tissue content of apoptosis-related proteins (caspase-3, Bax, and Bcl-xL) and lung morphology in a rat model of experimental acute lung injury. Material and methods Acute lung injury was induced in male Wistar rats (n = 45) by a combination of aspiration bronchopneumonia and systemic/intratracheal lipopolysaccharide administration. From day 5 to day 21, animals received inhalation therapy with the studied agents or saline (placebo control). On day 21, lung tissue was examined using histological and immunohistochemical analyses to assess caspase-3–positive cells. Tissue levels of caspase-3, Bax (monomer and dimer), and Bcl-xL were quantified by immunoblotting. Results Placebo-treated rats demonstrated pronounced fibrotic remodeling (carnification) accompanied by a high proportion of caspase-3–positive macrophages and fibroblasts (35–75%). This was associated with a marked increase in active caspase-3 (9.3-fold) and Bax monomer (2.8-fold), along with a significant decrease in Bcl-xL (3.2-fold) compared with intact controls (p < 0.05). All inhalation therapies significantly attenuated fibrotic changes, reduced the number of caspase-3–positive cells, and decreased tissue levels of active caspase-3 (1.3–2.1-fold), Bax monomer (1.3–1.9-fold), and Bax dimer (1.3–2.4-fold), while restoring Bcl-xL expression (p < 0.05). Methylprednisolone exerted the strongest effect on Bax dimer reduction, camostat mesylate most effectively increased Bcl-xL levels, and enoxaparin sodium showed the greatest suppression of active caspase-3. Immunohistochemically, methylprednisolone predominantly reduced apoptosis of macrophages and type II alveolocytes, enoxaparin targeted fibroblasts, whereas camostat demonstrated a more uniform antiapoptotic effect. Conclusions Experimental acute lung injury is characterized by excessive apoptosis driven by Bax /Bcl-xL imbalance and caspase-3 activation. Inhalation therapy with camostat mesylate, methylprednisolone, and enoxaparin sodium effectively corrected these alterations through complementary mechanisms, attenuating fibrotic remodeling. These findings support the potential clinical relevance of combined or targeted antiapoptotic strategies in acute lung injury.

Article.Title: MH-EABERT: an adaptive fusion approach with emotion knowledge-enhanced BERT for explainable mental health sentiment analysis from social media
Article.Authors: Rahman S.; Alam T.; Morol M.; Nandi D.; Liew T.
Article.Abstract: While deep learning models achieve high accuracy in mental health screening, their inherent “black box” nature precludes clinical trust, and pure rule-based systems fail to dynamically grasp complex linguistic nuances such as sarcasm. To rigorously bridge this critical research gap, this study introduces MH-EABERT (Mental Health Emotion-Augmented BERT), a novel neuro-symbolic framework that seamlessly integrates domain-specific clinical knowledge with deep semantic learning to heavily enhance both classification accuracy and explicit explainability. We construct a Mental Health Emotion Lexicon (MHEL) that maps 13,872 emotion terms and 181 clinical phrases to six cognitive dimensions. The architecture operates across five distinct computational modules, utilizing an Emotion Knowledge Extraction (EKE) scorer to apply 10 clinical logic rules that distinguish pathological states from general distress. To prevent semantic distortion, a Self-Adaptive Fusion (SAF) algorithm dynamically governs knowledge injection based on continuous confidence calibration. Using mathematical “hard positioning,” we embed clinical context directly into the sentence structure, forcing BERT’s attention mechanism to process it as integral semantics. Comprehensive evaluation utilizing 5-fold cross-validation repeated across 5 random seeds on three diverse datasets—Reddit Communities (151,288 posts), Comprehensive MH (53,043 statements), and Synthetic Posts (1000 samples)—demonstrated statistically significant superiority ( \(p < 0.0001\) ) over state-of-the-art baselines including RoBERTa, XLNet, DistilBERT, MentalBERT, and ClinicalBERT. Crucially, all evaluated models were rigorously trained and tested under the exact same experimental setup. MH-EABERT achieved a peak accuracy of 87.97% on Reddit data and crucially reduced the False Negative Rate for suicidal detection from 14.67 to 8.55%. Extensive ablation studies and SHAP analyses confirmed that predictions are grounded in transparent, auditable clinical features. MH-EABERT represents a significant advancement toward clinically grounded, highly interpretable AI systems capable of reliable, automated triage from unstructured social media text. To ensure absolute reproducibility, the code, lexicon, and framework weights are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23285908 .

Article.Title: Trial of labour versus repeat caesarean in women with one uterine scar: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Mugazov M.; Zharova Z.; Omertayeva D.; Uvasheva A.; Akzhol G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Caesarean delivery rates now exceed 30% in most high-income countries, producing a large cohort of women who face a choice between trial of labour after caesarean (TOLAC) and elective repeat caesarean delivery (ERCD) in a subsequent pregnancy. We performed a meta-analysis of studies published January 2021 – March 2026 to estimate the pooled vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) success rate and compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between strategies. Thirty-two studies ( N = 1,287,757 women) met pre-specified inclusion criteria. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS); pooled odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) used the DerSimonian–Laird random-effects model. The pooled VBAC success rate was 72.4% (95% CI 69.8–74.9%; I² = 63%). Uterine rupture was more frequent with TOLAC than ERCD (0.47% vs. 0.026%; OR 7.21, 95% CI 4.89–10.62; I² = 41%). TOLAC was associated with lower odds of postpartum haemorrhage requiring transfusion (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54–0.86) and wound infection (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39–0.70). NICU admission rates were not significantly different when both groups delivered at ≥ 39 weeks (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.71–1.11). A lower uterine segment (LUS) thickness ≥ 3.0 mm was associated with a VBAC success rate of 76.8% and a rupture rate of 0.31%. Individualised, LUS-informed risk stratification is more consistent with this evidence than blanket institutional restriction of TOLAC.

Article.Title: Krill swarm structure drives trophic partitioning in sympatric baleen whale species on the Northern California Current foraging grounds
Article.Authors: Kaplan R.; Bernard K.; Derville S.; Phillips E.; Warren J.; Torres L.
Article.Abstract: For sympatric species, niche differentiation may manifest through resource selection or spatiotemporal partitioning of shared resources. Traits including body size, physiology, and morphology influence the tactics that predators, such as baleen whales, use to meet their energetic needs. Blue, fin, and humpback whales require rich prey patches, like the extensive swarms the zooplankton krill form, to offset the energetic burden incurred by their large body sizes. Krill swarm characteristics (e.g., length, height, biomass) may influence whale foraging efficiency and therefore habitat selection. We used a Random Forest model to classify blue, fin, and humpback whales based on characteristics of nearby krill swarms acoustically detected in the Northern California Current. Swarm characteristics associated with whale sightings – including depth, krill species, proportion of the swarm occupied by krill rather than water, and internal heterogeneity – indicated species-specific habitat selection and breadth of each whale species’ trophic niches. Despite overall good classification performance (model accuracy = 0.79), erroneous predictions revealed the difficulty of differentiating the niches of generalist humpback and fin whales, while the niche of blue whales, a specialist predator, was clearer. Our results suggest krill swarm characteristics contribute to resource partitioning between baleen whale species on shared foraging grounds.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Ecology > Marine animal studies overview; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Aquatic Science > Marine and fisheries research; Environmental Science > Ecology > Wildlife Ecology and Conservation

Article.Title: The influence mechanism of AIGC-driven “learning-thinking-applying-creating” integrated animation instructional design on college students’ cognitive load and creative thinking
Article.Authors: Zhan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence has entered animation classrooms faster than research has been able to describe what it does to learning. This study developed a “Learning-Thinking-Applying-Creating” (LTAC) integrated teaching model built on an open-source AIGC toolchain and evaluated it in a twelve-week quasi-experiment with second-year animation students, two intact classes being allocated to an experimental or a control condition. Cognitive load was measured with a three-subscale instrument adapted from Paas and from Leppink and colleagues, and divergent thinking with an abbreviated Torrance-type battery scored for fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration by two trained raters who worked blind to group and occasion (intraclass correlations 0.86 to 0.91). Data were collected at pretest, mid-test, and posttest. Analysis of covariance indicated that the intervention lowered extraneous load and raised germane load while leaving intrinsic load unchanged. Repeated-measures analysis revealed selective gains: originality and elaboration improved more in the experimental group, whereas fluency and flexibility rose in both. Structural equation modelling was consistent with a differentiated mechanism, in which lower extraneous load predicted fluency and flexibility, germane load related to originality and elaboration indirectly through a deep-processing strategy, and intrinsic load showed an inverted-U association with the creative-thinking composite. Because the outcome measure is domain-general, the results speak to divergent thinking rather than to animation ability as such. The study extends cognitive load theory into generative-AI-supported creative education and offers animation programmes a reproducible instructional design that lowers production barriers while protecting deep creative work.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Experimental and Cognitive Psychology > Visual and Cognitive Learning Processes; Social Sciences > Education > Artificial Intelligence in Education; Computer Science > Computer Graphics and Computer-Aided Design > Digital Media and Visual Art

Article.Title: ¹H-NMR-based metabolomics reveals amino acid metabolic preferences and a shared metabolic axis across osteoblastic cell lines
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Ziblim Z.; Jaikang C.; Konguthaithip G.; Saenjum C.; Ruangsuriya J.
Article.Abstract: Commercially available osteoblastic cell lines have been widely applied in bone research, yet their metabolic characteristics and metabolic remodeling during osteogenic differentiation remain poorly defined. In this study, 1 H-NMR-based metabolomic technique was used to detect and compare metabolic characteristics and osteogenic phenotypes of three classic osteoblastic cell lines, including MG63, hFOB, and MC3T3. Phenotypic results revealed significant differences in proliferation capacity and osteogenic potential among the three cell lines following osteogenic induction. Metabolomic KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that MG63 was mainly enriched in branched-chain amino acid metabolism, hFOB was primarily enriched in glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, while MC3T3 showed dominant enrichment in arginine and proline metabolism. Exogenous supplementation of the corresponding amino acids (branched-chain amino acids for MG63; glycine for hFOB; arginine for MC3T3) enhanced osteogenic capacity in the respective cell lines. Further cross-group metabolomic analysis revealed that the alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolic pathway was commonly enriched across the three cell lines. Notably, exogenous glutamate supplementation negatively regulated osteogenic differentiation in these cell lines. Overall, this study began with metabolomic screening and discovered the relationships between amino acid-related metabolic remodeling and osteogenic differentiation across the three osteoblastic cell lines. These findings may provide candidate metabolic signatures for further investigations in basic bone biology research.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Bone Metabolism and Diseases; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Metabolomics and Mass Spectrometry Studies; Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Bone Tissue Engineering Materials

Article.Title: Prevalence and factors associated with sexual autonomic dysfunction among type 2 diabetes mellitus patients in Zanzibar
Article.Authors: Haji H.; Ali R.; Khamis A.; Muya M.; Mutagaywa R.; Ramaiya K.; Mashili F.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently complicated by autonomic neuropathy, which impairs sexal function. Sexual dysfunction (SD) is common in T2DM but remains under-recognized due to stigma and lack of screening. Evidence shows higher rates of erectile dysfunction in men and arousal or orgasmic disorders in women with T2DM compared to the general population. However, data on the burden and factors associated with sexual autonomic dysfunction (SEAD) in T2DM are limited in Zanzibar, prompting this study to investigate the prevalence and associated factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted at Mnazi Mmoja Hospital in Zanzibar. A total of 364 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were selected through systematic random sampling. Socio-demographic and lifestyle data were collected using a standardized questionnaire, while physical and biochemical measurements, including BMI, blood pressure, HbA1c, and lipid profile, were obtained following standard procedures. Sexual autonomic function was assessed using the Composite Autonomic Symptom Score (COMPASS) questionnaire. Factors associated with sexual autonomic dysfunction were analyzed using modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals were reported. The prevalence of sexual autonomic dysfunction (SEAD) was 15.9%. In the multivariable analysis, low income (aPR = 3.05, 95% CI: 1.18–7.87, p = 0.021), sedentary lifestyle (aPR = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.10–0.31, p < 0.001), and use of nutritional supplements (aPR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.30–0.82, p = 0.006) remained independently associated with SEAD. However, the association with sedentary lifestyle should be interpreted cautiously because only 7 participants (1.9%) were classified as active. Sexual autonomic dysfunction (SEAD) was found to be among the complications of T2DM in Zanzibar. These findings highlight the need to screen patients early and implement risk-based interventions in diabetes care. Targeting modifiable lifestyle and socioeconomic factors may help prevent progression and improve quality of life.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Psychiatry and Mental health > Sexual function and dysfunction studies; Medicine > Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism > Diabetes, Cardiovascular Risks, and Lipoproteins; Medicine > Urology > Urinary Bladder and Prostate Research

Article.Title: A consensus-based interpretable machine learning framework for robust early diagnosis of ovarian cancer using hematological and tumor biomarkers
Article.Authors: Fahim S.; Hasan E.; Bitto A.; Bijoy M.; Arefin M.; Samad M.; Ohidujjaman N/A.
Article.Abstract: The early and accurate diagnosis of any type of ovarian cancer is one of the key clinical issues because of the heterogeneous expression of biomarkers and the high prices of false-negative diagnosis. The proposed study is a consensus-based machine learning framework that can improve diagnostic stability, interpretability and clinical utility by utilizing routine hematological and tumor marker data. They experimentally tested 15 machine learning classifiers, under three feature selection paradigms: Stability Selection, BorutaSHAP, and a new Consensus Feature Selection paradigm that combines filter and wrapper feature selection. Stratified five-fold cross-validation and independent test set were used to determine its model performance and the measurement scales such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, ROC-AUC, calibration, and analysis of decision curve. A Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) Classifier using Consensus Feature Selection gave the strongest performance, with 97.14% accuracy (95% CI 90.17–99.21%), 100.00% sensitivity (95% CI 90.36–100%), and 94.12% specificity (95% CI 80.91–98.37%), with no false-negative examples among all configurations. Clinical reliability was also established on the basis of probability calibration (Brier score = 0.088), decision curve analysis with better net benefit at clinically relevant thresholds, and robustness to Gaussian noise perturbations up to 20%. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were employed to guarantee model interpretability with the most significant role of HE4, CA125 and menopausal status as shown in the existing clinical knowledge. The proposed pipeline, while constrained by sample size and single-center data, demonstrates strong proof-of-concept performance and may inform future clinical decision support and precision oncology processes, pending prospective multi-center validation.
Article.TopicFields: Health Professions > Health Information Management > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare; Medicine > Oncology > Ovarian cancer diagnosis and treatment; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection

Article.Title: Bayesian Deep Reliability Network for dynamic human reliability analysis in high-risk industrial environments
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Fu S.; Zhong J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial and mining accidents continue to pose significant threats to worker safety and production operations worldwide, with human error accounting for a substantial proportion of high-risk incidents. This paper addresses three critical challenges in contemporary Human Reliability Analysis (HRA): the inability of traditional methods to capture dynamic human-machine-environment interactions, the difficulty in integrating heterogeneous multi-source data, and the lack of interpretable uncertainty quantification in deep learning predictions. To tackle these issues, we propose the Bayesian Deep Reliability Network (BDRN), a novel framework that integrates a Graph Attention Temporal Encoder (GATE) for spatiotemporal dependency modeling, a Multimodal Feature Fusion Network (MFFN) for heterogeneous data integration, and an Evidential Deep Reinforcement Learning (EDRL) module for uncertainty-aware decision support. The proposed model is validated on the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) accident dataset and the New York City Motor Vehicle Collisions dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that BDRN achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 0.892, F1-score of 0.867, and AUC-ROC of 0.921 on the MSHA dataset, numerically higher than traditional Bayesian network HRA models, LSTM-based sequence models, and Transformer-based classifiers. Furthermore, the uncertainty calibration error of 0.068 confirms the model’s reliability in quantifying decision confidence. This research bridges the gap between probabilistic reasoning and deep learning, providing a practical tool for safety decision-making in high-risk industrial environments.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality > Risk and Safety Analysis; Engineering > Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality > Evaluation and Optimization Models; Engineering > Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality > Reliability and Maintenance Optimization

Article.Title: Mechanical performance and pavement response of basalt fiber reinforced coal gangue based composites for sustainable road applications
Article.Authors: Huang P.; Lan Q.; Topal E.; Shao H.; You Z.; Zhao C.; Ma S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coal gangue is widely generated during coal mining, but its application in pavement materials is limited by insufficient mechanical performance. This study developed a gangue–fly ash–cement–fiber (GFCF) composite and evaluated the effects of basalt fiber dosage on mechanical properties, microstructure, and pavement-scale deformation through laboratory tests, XRD, SEM, and three-dimensional numerical simulations. The results showed that unconfined compressive strength and splitting tensile strength increased with fiber content up to 0.6% and slightly decreased at 0.8%. The 0.6% fiber mixture achieved the highest 28 d UCS and splitting tensile strength of 14.47 MPa and 1.51 MPa, respectively. However, the reduction in compressive resilient modulus with increasing fiber content indicated a strength–stiffness trade-off. Numerical simulations revealed that fiber-dependent material differences had limited effects on settlement, whereas vehicle speed and traffic-load magnitude produced greater deformation variations. XRD and SEM observations qualitatively confirmed matrix densification and possible fiber–matrix interaction during curing. Overall, 0.6% fiber provided the most favorable strength-oriented performance within the tested range, while the numerical results provide comparative evidence for evaluating the pavement-scale response of the GFCF base layer and support the high-value utilization of coal gangue in pavement engineering.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: splitting tensile strength; coal gangue; basalt fiber; crack bridging; resilient modulus; fly ash; unconfined compressive strength; solid waste utilization; pavement settlement

Article.Title: The impact of reference data quality on building segmentation: a nationwide comparison of 15 deep learning models and a new benchmark dataset
Article.Authors: Karwowska K.; Tusznio K.
Article.Abstract: The effectiveness of deep learning models in detecting and segmenting buildings on orthophoto maps is usually attributed to the choice of network architecture; however, this study shows that the quality of the reference data can substantially influence measured segmentation performance. To verify this, a new dataset comprising 14,378 samples (11,878 positive and 2,500 negative) from across Poland was prepared, based on WMS services and vector data from the Land and Buildings Register (EGiB), and 15 neural network architectures were then compared on this dataset – ranging from classical convolutional networks, through transformer models, to instance segmentation from the YOLO-Seg family – evaluating them against both the cadastral labels and an independent manually annotated test set. The ranking of architectures differed markedly between the EGiB and manually annotated datasets, showing that the choice of reference labels can influence which model is identified as the best-performing architecture. The magnitude of the label effect was also substantial: across all 15 architectures, fine-tuning on more accurate manual labels increased IoU on the manually annotated test set by 0.128 ± 0.036 on average, whereas hyperparameter optimisation yielded an additional improvement of only 0.008 ± 0.010 – more than sixteen times smaller (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). Under the conditions evaluated, label refinement improved performance considerably more than hyperparameter optimisation, and the reference labels used for evaluation altered architecture rankings, indicating that reference data quality should be treated as a key factor alongside model selection.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Automated Road and Building Extraction; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Remote-Sensing Image Classification

Article.Title: Software-defined polarization-diversity continuous-variable quantum key distribution heterodyne receiver
Article.Authors: Sarmiento S.; Tabares J.; Etcheverry S.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a simple polarization-diversity heterodyne receiver for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) using a symmetric 3 × 3 beam splitter and software-defined polarization demultiplexing. Unlike conventional architectures that duplicate the coherent detection front-end, the proposed design implements polarization diversity in the digital domain, significantly reducing optical hardware complexity. The proposed receiver architecture is validated through simulations and experiments. Results show that the receiver exhibits stable performance under arbitrary states of polarization, achieving a composable finite-size secret key rate (with 10 7 symbols) of 6.98 Mbps in back-to-back operation and 0.29 Mbps over 25 km of fiber, demonstrating robustness and suitability for metro-scale CV-QKD deployment.
Article.TopicFields: Physics and Astronomy > Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics > Quantum Information and Cryptography; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Optical Network Technologies; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > graph theory and CDMA systems

Article.Title: Systemic pathogenesis and complete genome characterization of encephalomyocarditis virus in naturally infected pigs during high‑mortality outbreaks in Brazil
Article.Authors: Gris A.; Silva E.; Menegatt J.; Perosa F.; Alves R.; Budaszewski R.; Camargo L.; Weber M.; Canal C.; Piñeyro P.; Driemeier D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV) is an emerging cardiovirus associated with high mortality in swine, but natural infections in South America have been poorly characterized. We investigated outbreaks of sudden death in growing–finishing pigs from three commercial farms in Brazil using an integrated clinical, pathological, molecular, and genomic approach. Affected herds experienced mortality peaks of up to 19% and necropsies revealed multifocal myocardial necrosis with IBA1⁺ macrophage-predominant inflammation, mineralization, and reparative changes, as well as concentric left ventricular hypertrophy suggestive of viral-induced remodeling. In situ hybridization confirmed active viral replication in cardiomyocytes, macrophages, splenic germinal centers, renal tubular epithelium, and pulmonary inflammatory cells, indicating systemic dissemination and supporting urinary shedding as a possible transmission route. PCR detected EMCV in cardiac and lymphoid tissues, and full-genome sequencing of a cardiac isolate identified a 7.5-kb Cardiovirus A1 strain with > 99% VP1 identity to contemporary Brazilian rodent and swine strains, suggesting sustained circulation at the rodent–swine interface. This study provides the first complete genomic characterization of EMCV in Brazil and South America, expands the recognition of tissue tropism and highlights the need for enhanced surveillance and control strategies in intensive pork production systems.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: myocardial necrosis; encephalomyocarditis virus; pigs; left ventricular hypertrophy; tissue tropism
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Animal Science and Zoology > Animal Virus Infections Studies; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Animal Science and Zoology > Animal Disease Management and Epidemiology; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > Viral Infections and Immunology Research

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of long-term electricity load forecasting using machine learning and meta-heuristic-optimized hybrid architectures
Article.Authors: Hagos L.; Berhe A.; Delelew E.; Abdissa C.
Article.Abstract: Accurate long-term electricity peak load forecasting is essential for modern power system growth, reliability, and effective infrastructure planning. There is no single model for load forecasting that works for all electric utilities, as it can differ from region to region and among customer types. This paper presents a strong, data-driven approach that uses historical economic and demographic data from 2016 to 2025 to predict electrical power loads over a 10-year period for Adigrat city. Using advanced Pandas techniques for imputation of missing data and customer class correlation analysis to identify strongly related attributes, data pretreatment was meticulously carried out. In order to tackle the forecasting problem, we compare our proposed novel hybrid framework Particle Swarm Optimized (PSO) LSTM-NN with Machine Learning (ML) regression, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), LSTM-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and a hybrid LSTM-(NN)-Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model. To address potential out-of-sample scaling issues and risks of performance drop with standard standalone deep learners, we introduce an intelligent input-combination conditional feature selection engine. The uniqueness of this research comes from creating a highly robust, customer-focused framework for long-term load forecasting (LTLF) which combines tailored demographic analysis, automated handling of missing data, and an improved hybrid deep learning structure. This work primarily contributes a stringent preprocessing pipeline (featuring missing data mitigation and multivariate correlation analysis) alongside empirical proof that the LSTM-NN-PSO model delivers superior accuracy and extended stability when projecting intricate macroeconomic variables across a 10-year period.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Energy Load and Power Forecasting; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Stock Market Forecasting Methods; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Forecasting Techniques and Applications

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal trends and clustering of environmental flow components in western Lake Urmia Basin using IHA and multivariate analysis
Article.Authors: Babaie L.; Abghari H.; Mostafazadeh R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite increasing concerns over hydrological degradation and ecosystem decline in the Lake Urmia Basin, comprehensive basin‑scale assessments of long‑term environmental flow alterations across multiple tributary rivers remain limited. The present study was therefore undertaken to quantify spatiotemporal trends in environmental flow components across the Lake Urmia Basin and to identify the key hydrological indicators responsible for differentiating the hydrological regimes of its tributary rivers. Daily discharge data from 44 hydrometric stations, covering periods between 1949 and 2023, were analyzed using the Indicators of Hydrologic Alteration (IHA) framework. The derived 22 environmental flow indicators were subsequently subjected to hierarchical clustering and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to group stations based on hydrological similarity and to identify the most influential discriminating variables. We found considerable spatial heterogeneity in hydrological trends across the basin. Low‑flow persistence indicators, particularly the frequency and duration of extreme low flows, exhibited significant increasing trends at many stations (approximately 17 out of 44 for frequency and 11 out of 44 for duration). Notably, extreme low‑flow frequency contributed 22% to station differentiation, and the first two principal components together explained over 50% of the total variance. Cluster analysis identified two distinct hydrological regimes, a flood‑dominated cluster characterized by high peak flows and rapid rise rates, and a low‑flow cluster marked by prolonged dry periods. Stations located downstream of major storage dams experienced the most pronounced alterations, suggesting a possible influence of anthropogenic interventions on natural flow regimes. We aimed to provide a comprehensive basin-scale assessment of spatiotemporal environmental flow alterations in the western Lake Urmia Basin and present an integrated analytical framework for identifying dominant hydrological change patterns, which may be adapted by water managers in other arid and semi-arid basins facing similar challenges.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Water Science and Technology > Hydrology and Watershed Management Studies; Environmental Science > Nature and Landscape Conservation > Fish Ecology and Management Studies; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Earth-Surface Processes > Hydrology and Sediment Transport Processes

Article.Title: An optimized convolutional dense network for skin cancer detection in dermatological diagnostics
Article.Authors: Rao N.; Vasumathi D.
Article.Abstract: Early skin cancer detection is essential because it improves survival rates, enables timely and less invasive treatment, reduces healthcare costs, prevents disease progression, and increases public awareness, ultimately promoting better long-term health and more effective preventive care strategies. However, prevailing approaches face challenges, namely high false-positive rates, overfitting, and reduced accuracy. This work presents a novel approach named convolutional dense network-caracal narwhal optimization algorithm (CDen-Net), for skin cancer detection leveraging input skin images. The process starts by retrieving the skin image selected from the available dataset, followed by pre-processing with a sharpening filter. Next, the skin lesion is segmented employing an adaptive dual-stream hybrid encoder and focal attention decoder network, where the loss functions are adjusted with the proposed focal-cosh loss. Image augmentation is then performed on the segmented images using region cropping, color jittering, and dihedral transformation. Various features are extracted from the augmented images, and diagnosis of skin cancer is carried out utilizing the convolutional dense network (Conv-DenNet). Finally, the network's parameters are fine-tuned for optimal performance using the proposed caracal narwhal optimization algorithm. Furthermore, the developed CDen-Net achieved a false positive rate of 4.532%, an accuracy of 96.382%, and a true positive rate of 97.592%.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Oncology > Cutaneous Melanoma Detection and Management; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Medical Image Segmentation Techniques

Article.Title: Large animal model of chronic venous occlusion: a pilot study to assess composition and sensitivity to histotripsy
Article.Authors: Zhao K.; Saucedo E.; Antonides-Jensen N.; Hernandez S.; Ostdiek A.; Qin S.; Gao G.; Wool G.; Singh A.; Shekhar H.; Ahmed O.; Patel M.; Paul J.; Bader K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Venous thrombi that transition to chronic occlusions are difficult to address with current interventions. Histotripsy is a focused ultrasound therapy that ablates tissue through bubble cloud activity. Pre-clinical studies indicate acute thrombi are sensitive to histotripsy, but outcomes for aged obstructions require further investigation. In this pilot study, a porcine model was developed to test the hypothesis that histotripsy will disrupt disorganized extracellular matrix within chronic venous occlusions. Thrombi were formed in the femoral vein of female mixed-breed pigs via selective catheterization. The occlusion was monitored for 30 days with ultrasound imaging, after which the femoral bundle was resected for analysis with immunohistochemistry and transcriptomics ( N = 3), or exposed to histotripsy ( N = 3). Changes to the occlusion appearance were noted throughout aging. At 30 days, obstructed venous tissue was composed primarily of collagen (mean: 39.7% by area) with activated macrophages (mean: 22.2% of cells) and fibroblasts (mean: 21.6% of cells). Relative to patient-derived samples of subacute venous thrombi, the occlusions generated in this study exhibited increased coverage by collagen and hematoxylin. Histotripsy resulted in a 59.0% mean reduction in the occlusion area on ultrasound imaging. Tissue components undergoing active remodeling (i.e., disorganized collagen and cells) exhibited increased strong damage. This study demonstrated feasibility for a large animal model of chronic venous thrombosis, and provided proof-of-concept data for targeting the occlusion with histotripsy.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Ultrasound and Hyperthermia Applications; Medicine > Internal Medicine > Venous Thromboembolism Diagnosis and Management; Medicine > Surgery > Diagnosis and Treatment of Venous Diseases

Article.Title: G2RL: grid-aware gated recurrent learning for spatiotemporal urban air quality forecasting
Article.Authors: Chatterjee K.; Bala B.; Khan M.; Prasad M.; Kadurka R.; Altaf M.; Alhayan F.; Alasmari H.; Naayini P.; Jyothi K.
Article.Abstract: Accurate urban air-quality forecasting is critical for addressing the health and environmental impacts of urbanization. Reliable urban air-quality prediction is challenging due to the complex nonlinear dynamics of pollutant concentrations and significant spatial variability influenced by local emissions and changing weather conditions. This paper presents grid-aware gated recurrent learning (G 2 RL), a framework that uses grid-based spatial representation and gated recurrent units (GRUs) for effective spatiotemporal forecasting of air pollutant interactions. Existing forecasting methods have notable limitations. Conventional recurrent models excel in temporal dependencies but struggle with localized spatial interactions. CNN-based approaches require structured spatial data, while graph-based methods rely on complex topologies that are hard to establish for irregular networks. Additionally, complex spatiotemporal architectures often demand substantial computational resources, limiting their scalability and real-time application in urban monitoring systems. G 2 RL overcomes limitations in current frameworks by effectively capturing localized spatial heterogeneity and temporal pollutant dynamics without manual graphs. The study aims to: (i) develop a learnable grid-based model for localized pollutant interactions; (ii) jointly learn spatial and temporal dependencies among pollutant concentrations and meteorological variables; and (iii) assess forecasting accuracy and robustness under realistic monitoring conditions, including missing data. G 2 RL outperforms traditional CNN-GRU and graph-based methods by using a learnable grid embedding to capture localized pollutant interactions. It combines pollutant concentrations and meteorological variables to forecast accurately with sparse sensor data. Tested on 34 New Delhi stations, G 2 RL achieved an RMSE of 14.2, MAE of 9.8, and an R 2 -score of 0.92, outperforming various models. Statistical tests confirm the significance of these improvements, indicating that the observed performance gains are not attributable to random variation. The framework maintains high performance amid sensor dropout, noise, and spatial issues, enabling real-time predictions and making it ideal for smart-city air-quality management.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting; Social Sciences > Transportation > Traffic Prediction and Management Techniques; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Air Quality and Health Impacts

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning reveals the meteorological drivers of ozone exceedances in a high-emission industrial park
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Huang S.; Wu C.; Sheng D.; Zhu C.; Liao Z.; Wang K.; Wang Y.; Jiang Z.; Bi Y.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ground-level ozone exceedances in industrial parks remain poorly understood, as the drivers identified for urban atmospheres have rarely been quantified at the precursor levels typical of these parks. We analyzed a 56-day record of hourly observations from six monitoring sites in a fine-chemical industrial park on Hangzhou Bay, eastern China, and contrasted an eight-day ozone exceedance episode that emerged in early September 2020 with eight non-exceedance control days. The episode coincided with the peripheral subsidence of the successive typhoons Maysak and Haishen, which sustained the clear, dry and stable conditions under which ozone built to exceedance levels. A convolutional neural network trained on the monitored variables reproduces 88% of hourly ozone variability. By combining DeepSHAP attribution with controlled perturbations of the model, we find that meteorological variables, led by relative humidity and temperature, account for 65.9% of the model-attributed ozone variance during the episode versus 54.8% on control days. Perturbation analysis within the observed temperature–humidity domain further shows that the suppression of ozone by water vapor steepens beyond an absolute humidity of 19 g·m −3 , a threshold that reappears in observation-level regressions. Together, these results quantify the contributions of the meteorological variables and precursor concentrations to ozone at the precursor levels typical of high-emission industrial parks, and identify the absolute-humidity threshold beyond which the ozone response changes, providing a quantitative basis for ozone management in such parks.
Article.TopicFields: Earth and Planetary Sciences > Atmospheric Science > Atmospheric chemistry and aerosols; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Atmospheric Science > Atmospheric Ozone and Climate

Article.Title: Screening organic passivation layers for triple-cation triple-halide perovskite solar cells enabling high efficiencies with negligible hysteresis
Article.Authors: Löhr J.; Raugewitz A.; Haase F.; Steckenreiter V.; Grimm B.; Vollbrecht J.; Peibst R.; Schmidt J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We systematically compare various organic materials, namely ethylenediammonium diiodide (EDAI 2 ), n-octylammonium iodide (OAI), phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI), formamidinium iodide (FAI), and guanidinium bromide (GABr), as passivation of the perovskite/electron transport layer (pk/ETL) interface. We use an inverted cell process based on triple-cation triple-halide perovskites ( E g = 1.57 eV) fabricated by wet-chemical spin-coating. The ETL is deposited by vacuum evaporation of C 60 and BCP. We reach efficiencies up to 21.2% for ‘unpassivated’ cells, limited by recombination losses at the pk/ETL interface. EDAI 2 is found to provide the highest efficiencies of up to 25.2% with negligible hysteresis of the J-V -characteristics due to its excellent interface passivation in combination with a low contact barrier, leading to a combination of high open-circuit voltage of 1184 mV and high fill factor of 83.3%. GABr still provides efficiencies up to 23.3%, however, the fill factor is significantly lower compared to the EDAI 2 -passivated interface, possibly due to the formation of a contact barrier. All other examined materials show, despite high open-circuit voltages up to 1204 mV for OAI, worse overall cell performances. EDAI 2 is hence identified as the most effective material for pk/ETL interface passivation amongst the examined materials. The stability of EDAI 2 -passivated cell is found to be 90% of the initial efficiency remaining after 2700 h dark storage.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Perovskite Materials and Applications; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Organic Electronics and Photovoltaics; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Silicon and Solar Cell Technologies

Article.Title: Exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability of the conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Article.Authors: Rimu N.; Islam M.; Hossain M.; Akbar M.; Dey P.; Afikuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (CNLSE) serves as a robust mathematical model for understanding nonlinear wave propagation across various media, including optical fibers and plasma. This study introduces a cohesive analytical-computational framework to explore exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability associated with the CNLSE. By applying a conformable fractional traveling-wave transformation, the governing equation is transformed into an equivalent nonlinear ordinary differential equation. Utilizing the Modified Sardar Sub-Equation Method (MSSEM) and the Extended Generalized Riccati Equation Mapping Method (EGREMM) in conjunction leads to the derivation of extensive families of exact 21 solutions from Modified Sardar Sub-Equation Method and 27 from Extended Generalized Riccati Equation Mapping Method expanding the prior knowledge base significantly. The solutions encompass various wave structures, such as bright, dark, singular, periodic, rational, trigonometric, kink, and anti-kink forms. Notably, the integration of Hamiltonian phase-plane analysis, bifurcation theory, and dynamic stability through Hyers–Ulam stability assessment, alongside verification via the Differential Transform Method (DTM), enhances the study’s depth. The phase-plane analysis reveals critical dynamics such as equilibrium states and bifurcations, while perturbation analysis showcases transitions toward chaotic behaviors. The findings have profound implications on optical-pulse control, plasma-wave regulation, and quantum-wave transport, ultimately providing a comprehensive solution catalogue and deepening the understanding of nonlinear fractional-wave propagation mechanisms and their stability considerations.

Article.Title: Trends in one-year survival and pregnancy termination in congenital heart defects in 1994–2024: a population-based registry
Article.Authors: Derridj N.; Monier I.; Wojciechowski M.; Goffinet F.; Bonnet D.; Lelong N.; Khoshnood B.
Article.Abstract: To assess trends in one-year survival among infants with congenital heart defects (CHD) and in termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly (TOPFA), with particular attention to isolated and severe isolated CHD. 5,898 CHD from the Paris Registry of Congenital Anomalies (1994–2024) were included. Isolated CHD were defined as CHD without associated genetic or extracardiac anomalies, as opposed to non-isolated CHD. One-year survival was estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Temporal trends in survival and TOPFA among pregnancies with a recorded prenatal diagnosis of CHD, were analyzed using logistic regression. Non-linearity (fractional polynomials) and slope changes (segmented models) were assessed. Among 5,898 CHD cases, 4,391 were live births, 1,361 TOPFA and 146 stillbirths. One-year survival was 91.0% (95% CI 90.1–91.8), reaching 95.0% (95% CI 94.2–95.7) in isolated CHD and 84.0% (95% CI 81.4–86.2) in severe isolated CHD. Overall survival improved significantly over time (p < 0.001), with a change in slope around 2007–2009; the absolute annual gain decreased from approximately + 0.5% (95% CI 0.26–0.68) at the beginning of the study period to + 0.2% (95% CI 0.16–0.23) in recent years. Similar improvement was observed in isolated CHD, with smaller gains after approximately 2009, and in severe isolated CHD (+ 0.56% per year; 95% CI 0.28–0.84). Among prenatally diagnosed pregnancies, TOPFA decreased in isolated CHD (− 0.50% per year; 95% CI − 0.74 to − 0.26) and severe isolated CHD (− 0.36%; 95% CI − 0.69 to − 0.03). One-year survival improved over three decades, although gains became smaller over time rather than showing a uniform plateau across CHD subgroups. Improvement extended to severe isolated CHD and occurred alongside declining TOPFA among prenatally diagnosed isolated and severe isolated CHD.

Article.Title: The amplification effect is not driven by perceptual sampling bias
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Liu W.; Li Y.; Lu N.; Fu J.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract When observers are confronted with a set of stimuli of varying sizes, the relatively salient large stimuli among them tend to influence their judgments, leading them to overestimate the average size of the set of stimuli—a phenomenon known as the "amplification effect." This effect is a prevalent phenomenon in the research on ensemble perception, yet its mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to address this issue by manipulating stimulus presentation and introducing adaptation to distinguish between early perceptual encoding and later responding as potential loci of the effect. Firstly, comparing multiple stimuli of varying sizes with a single stimulus produces an amplification effect, resulting in the overestimation of the average size of multiple stimuli, which is in line with the former theory. However, this bias disappears when comparing the sizes of multiple stimuli of varying sizes and multiple stimuli of uniform size. Secondly, the adaptation paradigm provides converging evidence in support of this hypothesis. Adaptation to both multiple large stimuli and a single large stimulus induce adaptation aftereffects, whereas adaptation to multiple stimuli of varying sizes does not, suggesting that stimulus salience does not bias the perception of average size during the adaptation period. Experiment 1 was conducted in the central visual field, and Experiment 2 replicated these findings in the left and right hemifield fields. In conclusion, the amplification effect does not constitute a stable bias arising at the perceptual sampling stage, which is driven by stimulus size salience. Instead, it likely emerges during intermediate processing or the subsequent response selection stage after initial perception. These findings suggest a reassessment of the perceptual saliency-based weighting theory.

Article.Title: Computational and experimental screening identifies 6-chloro-2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde derivatives as disruptors of the HEG1–KRIT1 protein–protein interaction
Article.Authors: Kamel E.; Bin-Jumah M.; Alfassam H.; Alotaibi R.; Alammari B.; Alshabrmi F.; Alkhayl F.; Lamsabhi A.
Article.Abstract: The HEG1–KRIT1 protein–protein interaction is a central regulatory interface in cerebral cavernous malformation signaling and represents a potential target for small-molecule modulation. In this study, a focused library of 1,121 compounds containing a 2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde scaffold was screened to identify candidate HEG1–KRIT1 disruptors. Compounds were prioritized through drug-likeness filtering, PAINS/reactivity assessment, diversity and purchasability evaluation, AutoDock Vina docking, short molecular dynamics refinement, and MM/PBSA rescoring. Three candidates, HN1, HN2, and HN3, were selected for 1000 ns molecular dynamics simulations, free-energy analyses, in silico ADMET profiling, and experimental evaluation using a bead-based flow-cytometry HEG1–KRIT1 competition assay. Docking and simulation analyses suggested that all three candidates could occupy the HEG1-recognition region of the KRIT1 FERM domain and maintain ligand–protein contacts during the simulations. Among the tested compounds, HN1 yielded a modest positive ΔΔG PPI estimate of + 2.66 kcal/mol, whereas HKi2, HN2, and HN3 yielded negative estimates; these values were interpreted descriptively as approximate indicators of ligand-dependent changes in the HEG1–KRIT1 interface. Experimental testing showed concentration-dependent inhibition of EGFP–KRIT1 FERM binding to HEG1-coated beads. Under the applied assay conditions, HN1 produced the numerically lowest IC₅₀ estimate at 3.51 ± 0.14 µM, compared with 3.90 ± 0.13 µM for HKi2, while HN2 and HN3 produced IC₅₀ estimates of 24.12 ± 1.59 and 31.63 ± 1.99 µM, respectively. These numerical differences do not establish superiority or equivalence among the compounds. Collectively, the computational and experimental findings support HN1 as a preliminary hit that warrants further target-engagement, mechanistic, and cellular validation.

Article.Title: Low-carbon alkali-activated concrete production using multi-waste materials
Article.Authors: AL-Tam S.; Riad A.; Mohammed N.; Ghalla M.; Youssf O.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a novel multi-waste binder design approach for high-strength alkali-activated concrete (HSAAC), in which ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) content was reduced to only 20%. Ten mixtures were prepared by replacing up to 80% of GGBFS with various waste materials, including waste charcoal ash (WCA), silica fume (SF), metakaolin (MK), waste ceramic powder (WCP), waste basalt powder (WBP), quartz powder (QP), and coal powder (CP). The influence of different curing regimes, including water, heat, and steam-water curing, was evaluated based on compressive strength development, while the physical, mechanical, durability, and environmental performances of the mixtures were assessed under water curing conditions. The results show that the steam-water treatment system produced higher compressive strengths for all mixtures after 28 days compared to the other curing systems. The WCA20 mixture showed a 3.5% improvement in workability. The control, MK40, and WCP20 mixtures achieved high-strength concrete requirements, with compressive strengths of 87, 75, and 70 MPa, respectively. The QP20 and WBP20 mixtures exhibited enhanced flexural strength, with increases of up to 44% and 25%, respectively, and achieved tensile strengths of 7.16 MPa and 6.21 MPa, respectively. MK20 and QP20 exhibited superior resistance to both sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄) and magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) attack. Microstructural analysis further confirmed the strength enhancement observed after sodium sulfate exposure. The SEM–EDS results revealed denser reaction matrices and increased Ca/Si ratios of 0.31 and 0.27 for MK20 and QP20, respectively, suggesting the formation of additional Ca-bearing reaction products and continued matrix densification. Environmental assessment revealed improved sustainability across all mixtures, with WCP and WBP showing the highest environmental performance among the multi-waste blends.

Article.Title: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma pretreatment as a novel tool to tailor the functional properties of quince seed mucilage biopolymer-based edible films
Article.Authors: Karimi J.; Sohrabi S.; Rad M.; Sharifian M.; Zare L.; Meybodi N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Quince seed mucilage (QSM) is a promising polysaccharide for the fabrication of biodegradable edible films; however, its relatively limited functional performance restricts broader food-packaging applications. Scope and Approach: The present study investigated the effects of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) treatment applied to QSM solutions at 6, 7, and 8 kV for 1, 3, and 5 min, followed by a comprehensive evaluation of the physicochemical, surface, barrier, mechanical, and thermal properties of the resulting films. Key Findings: CAP treatment did not significantly affect film thickness regardless of the applied processing conditions. Contact angle analysis demonstrated that the highest surface hydrophobicity was achieved under a 7 kV for 3 min plasma treatment. Water vapor barrier measurements revealed that films treated for 3 min exhibited the lowest permeability, irrespective of the applied voltage. Surface topography analysis indicated that 6 kV for 1min plasma exposure generated the greatest surface roughness, whereas increasing either the treatment duration or applied voltage produced a denser, more homogeneous, and compact film microstructure. Compared with the untreated control, CAP treatment significantly enhanced the mechanical performance of the films, with the optimum tensile properties obtained following treatment at 6 kV for 1 min. Thermal characterization by TGA and DSC further demonstrated that 5 min plasma exposure time adversely affected the thermal stability of the films, while optimized CAP conditions (3 min) provided the most favorable thermal performance. Conclusions Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriately optimized CAP treatment effectively improves the structural integrity and functional performance of QSM-based biodegradable films.

Article.Title: Self-selection bias impedes electric vehicle adoption
Article.Authors: Hamim O.; Gazmeh H.; Reimer T.; Loaiza-Ramírez J.; Qian X.; Ukkusuri S.
Article.Abstract: Currently, electric vehicle (EV) adoption in the United States is transitioning from early experimentation to stabilized adoption. However, barriers to mass adoption remain, particularly related to user perceptions and behavioral differences between non-EV and EV users. This study analyzes survey data from 996 US adults, including non-EV, plug-in hybrid EV (PHEV) and battery EV (BEV) users, using an econometric model that accounts for self-selection bias in evaluating users’ perceived importance of charging time-related features at EV charging stations (EVCSs). Results show predictive performance in both the selection model classifying EV groups (pseudo- \( {{\rm R}^2=0.05\sim 0.06}\) ) and the outcome model estimating perceived importance ( \( {{\rm R}^2=0.36\sim 0.38}\) ). The estimated treatment effects for current PHEV and BEV users are -0.920 and -0.975, respectively, indicating lower perceived importance under their observed EV adoption states relative to their estimated counterfactual non-EV states. In contrast, perceived importance among non-EV users slightly decreases by 0.016 under the PHEV adoption counterfactual and increases by 0.913 under the BEV adoption counterfactual. On average, transitioning from non-EV status to PHEV or BEV status significantly decreases perceived importance by 0.442 and 0.076, respectively, with these shifts larger than or comparable to corresponding observed simple differences. This suggests that charging-time concerns may be less salient under the estimated EV adoption states after accounting for self-selection. Our results indicate that self-selection bias can impede EV adoption by amplifying perceived barriers among non-EV users. Furthermore, by identifying and adjusting for self-selection effects, this research offers insights for designing targeted outreach strategies and infrastructure policies to support mass diffusion of EVs.

Article.Title: A meta-analysis of four studies identified three new genes associated with allergic asthma
Article.Authors: Orsi L.; Lajunen T.; Madore A.; Hamilton F.; Margaritte-Jeannin P.; Vernet R.; Bouzigon E.; Granell R.; Jaakkola M.; Laprise C.; Jaakkola J.; Nadif R.; Dizier M.
Article.Abstract: Associations between Interleukin 6 (IL-6), a key cytokine in inflammation, and asthma were reported, with results varying across phenotypes. We aimed to identify new asthma-associated genes involved with IL6 in inflammation-related pathways while accounting for phenotypic heterogeneity of asthma according to allergic status and age of onset. This pathway-based strategy identifying 1,323 IL6 -related genes was applied among 3,435 European-ancestry participants (mean age: 31 years, 54% women, 44% asthma, 44% allergy, 26% adult-onset asthma) from four independent epidemiological studies: EGEA, FEAS, and ALSPAC (discovery samples), and SLSJ (replication sample). Associations between all SNPs within these genes and asthma phenotypes were estimated by logistic models in each study, followed by meta-analyses across studies, and conducted separately for childhood-onset and adult-onset asthma. Two SNPs were specifically associated with adult-onset allergic asthma, located in PTPRE ( p-meta=3 × 10 − 6 ) and in FZD7 ( p-meta = 1.7 × 10 − 4 ). Two other SNPs were specifically associated with childhood-onset allergic asthma, located in IL33 ( p-meta = 2.5 × 10 − 7 ), and in SASH1 ( p-meta = 1.1 × 10 − 4 ). The SNPs located in PTPRE and IL33 reached the significance level of association. Applying this approach and accounting for the phenotypic heterogeneity of asthma, we identified three new genes PTPRE , FZD7 and SASH1 associated with asthma, and not detected before by classical approach of GWAS. They play a crucial role in key biological processes involved in asthma development, suggesting potential new targets for asthma prevention.

Article.Title: Bacterial etiologies, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and multidrug resistance trends among patients with sterile body site infections in Northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Assefa M.; Tigabie M.; Tesfa A.; Smineh F.; Worku T.; Shferaw Y.; Worku M.; Mesfin Y.; Girmay G.; Almagharbeh W.; Cherie N.
Article.Abstract: Sterile body site (SBS) bacterial infections are one of the most critical problems in hospital settings. The rise of antimicrobial resistance and empirical treatment of SBS infections without local up-to-date evidence have led to higher patient mortality, representing a research gap in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the bacterial distribution, their antimicrobial resistance patterns, multidrug resistance (MDR) trends, and associated factors in SBS infections at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia. A retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with SBS infection at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital. The Kobo data collection tool was used to extract laboratory records from September 2021 to May 2026 (five years) using a consecutive sampling technique. Sterile body fluid samples were collected and inoculated onto blood agar, chocolate agar, MacConkey agar, and mannitol salt agar plates. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion method. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 software. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test assumptions, and logistic regression models were applied. Bivariate logistic regression results with a p-value < 0.25 were entered into multivariate analysis to control for potential confounding factors. To assess associations between dependent and independent variables, a p-value < 0.05 in multivariate analysis was considered statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. Study findings were presented using tables and charts. A total of 1,368 study participants were included in this study, consisting of 678 (49.6%) males and 690 (50.4%) females. The prevalence of culture-confirmed bacterial SBS infection was 5.48% (95% CI: 4.38%-6.83%), with 75 bacterial isolates identified. No mixed bacterial infections were detected in any patient. There was a high prevalence of Gram-negative bacteria (88.0%, n = 66), while 12.0% ( n = 9) were Gram-positive bacteria. E. coli (33.3%, n = 25) and K. pneumoniae (26.7%, n = 20) were the most predominant pathogens causing SBS infection. Gram-negative bacterial isolates demonstrated resistance to commonly used antibiotics such as ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and ampicillin. An overall prevalence of MDR was 17.3% (13/75), with K . pneumoniae (35%, n = 6), Non-Lactose Fermenting Gram-Negative Rods (28.6%, n = 2), and E. coli (16%, n = 4). Being male ( p = 0.011) and study years 2025/26 ( p < 0.001), 2024/25 ( p < 0.001), and 2023/24 ( p = 0.020) were significantly associated with bacterial SBS infection. In this study, Gram-negative bacteria were the most common cause of SBS infection, with MDR E. coli and K. pneumoniae being frequently identified isolates. Over the five-year trend, a higher MDR rate was observed in 2024/25 (46.2%), with K. pneumoniae exhibiting a high MDR rate in 2024/25 (71.4%); p = 0.03, and the prevalence of MDR E. coli peaked at 50% during 2022/23 and 2024/25 tracking periods. This study highlights the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance surveillance and molecular detection of resistance mechanisms.

Article.Title: Culture-independent detection of Salmonella enterica in cattle feces via digital PCR without pre-enrichment
Article.Authors: Dudley E.; Lamsal K.; Hacker N.; Scott M.; Woolums A.; Karisch B.; Harvey K.; Capik S.; Gouvea V.; Valeris-Chacin R.
Article.Abstract: Salmonella enterica is a significant cause of foodborne illness globally, and pre-harvest methods for detection are key to preventing downstream product contamination. Culture-based methods of detection are time and labor intensive. Real-time PCR assays are faster and less cumbersome but require a pre-enrichment step that can potentially bias detection results. To address these shortcomings, a digital PCR protocol, using invA and pagC as target genes,​ was developed to detect Salmonella DNA in cattle feces without the need for pre-enrichment. The average Salmonella DNA concentration for all samples was 42.1 ng/µL and was, on average, 15.8 ng/µL lower without pre-enrichment (P < 0.001). Prevalence using invA was 53.3% with and 46.7% without pre-enrichment, whereas prevalence with pagC was 38.3 and 28.3%, respectively. Salmonella prevalence using invA and pagC in parallel was 63.3% with and 57.5% without pre-enrichment, respectively, while prevalence calculated in series was 28.3 and 17.5%, respectively. Gwet’s AC1 coefficients showed that Salmonella prevalence in series without pre-enrichment had the highest agreement with prevalence in culture at 82.5% (probabilistic benchmark interval: 60–80%). Our results indicate that this platform is an effective tool for the detection of Salmonella in cattle feces without the need for pre-enrichment.

Article.Title: Complementary spectroscopic methods for simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide and olodaterol hydrochloride with analytical performance and environmental sustainability assessment
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Taha E.; Soliman S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly analytical methods for drug quality control is essential in modern pharmaceutical analysis. This study presents, to the best of our knowledge, two independent and complementary analytical strategies for the simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide (TBM) and olodaterol hydrochloride (OLH) in laboratory-prepared mixtures and the pharmaceutical formulation Stiolto ® Respimat. The first strategy employed UV–Vis spectroscopy combined with Partial Least Squares (PLS), Genetic Algorithm-PLS (GA-PLS), and Multivariate Curve Resolution–Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS), whereas the second employed first-derivative Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy using zero-crossing wavenumbers. Validation mixtures were designed using Latin Hypercube Sampling to provide systematic coverage of the investigated concentration space. First-derivative preprocessing was applied to enhance spectral resolution and minimize baseline effects. The UV–Vis spectra in the range of 222–263 nm and FTIR spectra in the range of 4000–400 cm⁻¹ were used for quantitative analysis. Among the investigated UV–Vis chemometric models, MCR-ALS provided the lowest root mean square errors of calibration and prediction, with RMSEC and RMSEP values of 0.0359 and 0.0329 for TBM and 0.0622 and 0.0375 for OLH, respectively. The developed models provided recoveries of approximately 100%, with precision expressed as RSD values below 2%. Application to the commercial formulation produced satisfactory recoveries ranging from 98% to 101% for both drugs using the developed techniques. Statistical comparison with the reference HPLC method showed no significant differences at the 95% confidence level. Overall, the complementary UV–Vis chemometric and ATR-FTIR approaches provided satisfactory quantitative performance for the simultaneous determination of TBM and OLH within the investigated analytical ranges.

Article.Title: Field-compatible tissue cryopreservation enables delayed endothelial cell culture
Article.Authors: Allen K.; Burns J.; Vázquez-Medina J.; den Heyer C.; Shero M.
Article.Abstract: Decades of biomedical research have developed robust tools in molecular and cell biology, including cell culture systems, for model vertebrate species. Logistical constraints associated with remote fieldwork limit the application of these techniques to non-model species. Traditionally, cell culture requires tissue collection from live or very recently deceased animals, followed by immediate sterile processing and cell isolation, but these requirements are often impractical in field settings. To address this limitation, we developed a field-compatible method to cryopreserve arterial tissue from pinnipeds for delayed endothelial cell isolation. Grey seal placentae were opportunistically collected, and arteries were preserved using benchtop blunt dissection and a portable ​​-80 °C freezer with a standard cell freezing medium. Samples were held in a portable ​-80 °C freezer for ~ 2 months before transfer to LN 2 vapor storage for ~ 1 month, followed by endothelial cell isolation. Cells isolated from cryopreserved arteries are phenotypically endothelial, proliferate in culture and are the first endothelial cell cultures derived from grey seals. Grey seal endothelial cells respire after culture expansion, and ATP production rates are ~ 1.5×​​ greater than those in freshly derived endothelial cell cultures from a related species, though the relative contributions of OXPHOS and glycolysis were comparable between cell preparations. This method is practical for field researchers and supports the generation of primary cell cultures weeks-to-months after initial tissue collection with minimal resources, strengthening the ability to investigate the cellular basis of physiological phenomena in the natural world.

Article.Title: miR-20a promotes cell proliferation and migration by targeting DLC1 in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Mao Y.; Xu R.; Lu H.; Zhou Y.; Bao L.; Zhong L.; Wang P.; Ren C.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: The role of miR-20a in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and its relationship with the tumor suppressor DLC1 remain incompletely understood. We analyzed miR-20a expression in public datasets and clinical samples, assessed cell proliferation and migration, and examined target regulation using a dual-luciferase reporter assay. Tumor growth was evaluated in a subcutaneous xenograft model. miR-20a was elevated in NPC tissues and cell lines, and higher expression was associated with poorer survival in a public dataset. miR-20a overexpression promoted cell proliferation and migration, altered epithelial–mesenchymal transition-associated markers, increased MMP-2, MMP-7 and MMP-9 protein levels, and enhanced xenograft growth. miR-20a inhibition increased DLC1 expression and the activity of a reporter containing the wild-type DLC1 3′ untranslated region, without significantly affecting the corresponding mutant reporter. DLC1 knockdown attenuated the inhibitory effects of miR-20a inhibition on colony formation and migration and counteracted associated protein changes. These findings support DLC1 as a functional mediator of miR-20a-associated malignant phenotypes in NPC and provide a rationale for further preclinical investigation of the miR-20a/DLC1 axis.

Article.Title: Quality characteristics of frozen horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) treated with starch–glycerol coatings containing plant extracts
Article.Authors: Gurdal A.; Caglak E.
Article.Abstract: Starch-based coatings are biodegradable food-contact materials, but their performance depends on plasticizer level, incorporated active compounds, and the food surface to which they are applied. This study developed starch-glycerol polysaccharide coating formulations containing aqueous extracts from persimmon fruit calyces, cherry laurel leaves, and bilberry/likapa leaves and evaluated their application to whole horse mackerel ( Trachurus trachurus ) during frozen storage at -20 ± 2 °C for 6 months. Extract-level antioxidant activity was determined by the DPPH assay and expressed as percentage inhibition and Trolox equivalent antioxidant capacity. Comparable starch-glycerol films containing the same plant extracts had previously been characterized by Gurdal and Caglak and were used here only as formulation-characterization background. During frozen storage, TVB-N values increased but remained below 35 mg/100 g in all groups. Lipid oxidation responses were formulation-dependent: the lowest final TBA values were observed in PA and PB, whereas BA and VC showed the highest final values. pH, water activity, color, texture, and microbial results varied among treatments and storage months without supporting a uniform concentration-dependent response. The findings suggest that selected starch-glycerol formulations containing plant extracts may help modulate lipid oxidation and quality changes in frozen horse mackerel. However, the absence of a plain starch-glycerol-coated fish control, coating-uptake measurements, compound-level extract characterization, and composite-film antioxidant testing limits direct attribution of the observed effects to specific bioactive mechanisms.
