Article.Title: Efficient generation of non‑mosaic genetically modified marmosets via CRISPR/Cas9 delivery into unfertilized MII oocytes
Article.Authors: Kinoshita S.; Xie Y.; Mizukai H.; Adachi H.; Ito K.; Takahashi T.; Sato K.; Kumita W.; Sasaki E.; Ikeda K.; Abe Y.; Aiba A.; Sugao K.; Watanabe T.
Article.Abstract: The common marmoset ( Callithrix jacchus ) is a small nonhuman primate (NHP) with a relatively high reproductive capacity due to its short gestation period and early sexual maturation, making it well suited for producing genetically modified primates. Unlike rodents, marmosets take several years to produce second generation offspring; therefore, analyzing founder-generation animals is especially desirable. However, the frequent occurrence of mosaicism is a major obstacle to this. Our BrdU analyses revealed that DNA replication in marmoset zygotes starts around 8 h after fertilization. We reasoned that the high frequency of mosaicism observed with conventional methods results from genome editing in embryos after or during DNA replication. To induce gene modification before DNA replication, a complex of Cas9 and three or four guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting the same exon was injected into metaphase II (MII) oocytes just before in vitro fertilization (IVF). Using this approach, we generated genetically modified marmosets targeting three genes. All resulting genetically modified animals were likely non-mosaic knockouts. Our MII oocyte injection approach can be used in combination with any oocyte retrieval (ovary or oviduct) and transfer (oviduct and uterus) conditions. Thus, injection of efficient gRNAs in advance of DNA replication enables efficient generation of non-mosaic knockout animals.

Article.Title: Hybrid PER–TD3–HER reinforcement learning for joint UAV trajectory, IRS phase, and resource allocation in energy-harvesting cell-free IoT networks
Article.Authors: Mirzaei Z.; Parzivand H.; Kh T.; Hamian M.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a customized hybrid deep reinforcement learning framework, termed PER–TD3–HER, for joint optimization of three-dimensional UAV trajectory design, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) phase configuration, transmit power allocation, and time-switching energy harvesting in UAV-assisted, IRS-enabled energy-harvesting cell-free IoT networks. The proposed framework integrates the Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) and Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) mechanisms to improve learning efficiency, exploration capability, and robustness in high-dimensional continuous control environments. Unlike conventional approaches that optimize network components separately, the proposed framework provides a unified learning-based solution for the coupled optimization of UAV mobility, IRS-assisted propagation control, resource allocation, and energy sustainability under dynamic network conditions and imperfect channel state information (CSI). In the proposed framework, PER enhances sample efficiency by prioritizing informative experiences associated with critical learning transitions, QoS requirements, energy constraints, and challenging channel conditions. Meanwhile, HER improves goal-oriented learning by transforming unsuccessful trajectories into valuable training experiences through goal relabeling. Furthermore, the continuous action-space formulation enables adaptive and simultaneous control of UAV trajectory, IRS phase shifts, transmit power allocation, and energy-harvesting ratios, overcoming the limitations of discrete decision-making approaches. Comprehensive simulations under realistic channel conditions and imperfect CSI demonstrate that the proposed PER–TD3–HER framework achieves improved convergence behavior, throughput–energy trade-off, and QoS satisfaction compared with TD3-based, DDPG-based, DQN-based, and SAC benchmark methods. The results verify the effectiveness, robustness, and scalability of the proposed framework for sustainable UAV-assisted IRS-enabled cell-free IoT networks and its potential applicability to future intelligent wireless communication systems.

Article.Title: Three-dimensional shape diversity of the fingertips and nails in Japanese adults
Article.Authors: Imaizumi K.; Usui S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In sexual abuse investigations, hand shape comparison is often required to identify the person to whom a hand captured in crime scene images belongs. While this is typically conducted through visual comparison with reference images of suspects, the scientific foundations needed to support the evidential value of such identifications remain scarce. In this study, we examined the three-dimensional (3D) morphological variations of fingertips and nails using principal component analysis (PCA) on 3D homologous shape models, and measured interphalangeal lengths from 3D hand scans. Dominant shape variations in the fingertips included contrasts between wide and narrow forms, relative nail area, and the degree of nail embedding. For the nails, major variations encompassed wide versus narrow forms, flat versus curved shapes at the distal free edge, and the degree of dorso-volar projection. Furthermore, interphalangeal measurements provided basic statistics for segment lengths and revealed strong correlations in relative lengths among corresponding segments across digits. These findings provide a robust scientific foundation and crucial reference criteria for future forensic hand shape comparisons.

Article.Title: Modular control of gait under visual deprivation using muscle-mode UCM analysis of COM and foot trajectory
Article.Authors: Zargaripour E.; Towhidkhah F.; Ghassemi F.; Shoja O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human walking relies on modular neural control that coordinates many muscles into low-dimensional muscle modes (M-modes). Using uncontrolled manifold (UCM) analysis, we assessed whether these modules stabilize swing-phase task outcomes and which outcome, COM motion or swing-foot trajectory, is prioritized with and without vision. Ten healthy adults walked on a treadmill under full vision (FV) and no vision (NV) conditions. EMG signals were factorized to extract M-modes, and a mode-based UCM analysis quantified variance components and synergy strength ( $$\Delta {V}_{z}$$ ) for COM and foot trajectories. Four M-modes were consistently identified across conditions. Synergy strength remained positive for both performance variables and visual conditions throughout swing phase, indicating stabilization by modular coordination. No overall main effects of vision condition or performance variable on $$\Delta {V}_{z}$$ were found, but phase ( p < 0.01), and all two- and three-way interactions were significant ( p < 0.001). The interactions revealed that under NV, $$\Delta {V}_{z}$$ was selectively reduced at mid-swing for both performance variables, whereas $$\Delta {V}_{z}$$ dominated foot trajectory over COM in early-swing-NV and late-swing-FV. No vision increased mid-swing orthogonal variance, although UCM variance remained unchanged. These findings show that modular stabilization persisted without vision but was least efficient at mid-swing, and that in specific subphases the controller emphasized foot-path stabilization over COM.

Article.Title: A generative adversarial network-augmented dual-stream Mamba-transformer framework for advanced intrusion detection and cyber threat mitigation in smart healthcare networks
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Kumar S.; Mukherjee I.
Article.Abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has dramatically expanded the attack surface of smart healthcare networks, with cyber-threats including DDoS, spoofing, reconnaissance, and ransomware targeting IoMT infrastructures and jeopardizing patient safety. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) fail to address protocol heterogeneity, high-dimensional traffic data, and severe class imbalance inherent in IoMT environments. This paper proposes GAN-Mamba Former-IDS, a novel intrusion detection framework for advanced cyber threat detection in smart healthcare networks. Three core innovations are integrated: (i) a Protocol-Aware Feature Router partitioning network traffic features into four semantically coherent protocol groups; (ii) a dual-stream Mamba-Transformer encoder concurrently capturing sequential dependencies via a linear-time state-space model and global feature interactions via multi-head self-attention; and (iii) Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN)-based augmentation addressing minority attack class imbalance. All experiments were implemented in PyTorch 2.1 on an NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU. The proposed framework achieves 97.71% accuracy, 0.7901 macro-F1 score, and 0.9842 ROC-AUC on the 19-class CICIoMT2024 test set, outperforming baseline models including MLP, 1D-CNN, BiLSTM, Transformer-only, and Mamba-only. CTGAN augmentation improves minority-class macro-F1 by up to +0.2109 for the rarest attack classes. Results are confirmed across five random seeds (mean ± std: Accuracy = 97.71 ± 0.38%, Macro-F1 = 0.7901 ± 0.014). GAN-Mamba Former-IDS provides a scalable, reproducible, and effective cybersecurity solution for next-generation IoMT environments, with demonstrated generalization across five heterogeneous IoT security benchmarks.

Article.Title: A hybrid uncertainty-aware deep learning framework for reliable Malayalam fake news detection
Article.Authors: Likha O.; Sachin Kumar S.; Mohan N.; Sikha O.
Article.Abstract: Fake news detection in low resource languages like Malayalam is a challenging task due to linguistic complexity, limited linguistic resources and lack of annotated datasets. The deep learning models has proven good impact in text classification tasks, but they lack reliability and interpretability that are critical for real world deployment. There are some recent studies that focus on explainable artificial intelligence to interpret model predictions but the reliability of these explanations under uncertain predictions has not been addressed. This paper proposes an uncertainty aware framework for Malayalam fake news detection using different deep learning architectures, including Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), CNN-LSTM, Bidirectional GRU (BiGRU), CNN-GRU, and CNN-BiLSTM. Four uncertainty estimation techniques Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, Deep Ensemble Learning, Test Time Augmentation (TTA) and Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) are used and compared with baseline models. Along with fake news classification, the proposed framework quantifies predictive uncertainty through entropy, Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, mutual information, variance, and vacuity measures, enabling the identification of unreliable predictions. A hybrid uncertainty framework combining MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble Learning and Evidential Learning is proposed to jointly capture epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty while providing a complementary evidence based uncertainty estimates. The proposed hybrid framework achieves an accuracy of 96.51%, precision of 96.52%, recall of 96.51%, and F1-score of 96.51%. To assess the robustness of proposed hybrid model result and address variability due to random initialization, an additional five-seed experiment was conducted. The Hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 95.85 ± 0.18, precision of 95.85 ± 0.18%, recall of 95.85 ± 0.18%, and F1-score of 95.85 ± 0.18%, indicating stable performance across multiple runs. Furthermore, the calibration analysis demonstrates substantial improvements in prediction reliability, achieving the lowest Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.0066, Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) of 0.1014, and Brier Score of 0.0546 among all evaluated models. The five seed experiment achieved an ECE of ( $$0.0067 \pm 0.0023$$ ), MCE ( $$0.0955 \pm 0.0494$$ ), NLL ( $$0.1229 \pm 0.0027$$ ), and Brier score ( $$0.0659 \pm 0.0007$$ ) for the proposed hybrid model, which is lower than all other models. Although the Deep Ensemble and MC Dropout + Ensemble models achieve slightly higher mean classification accuracy, the proposed Hybrid Model achieves the lowest ECE, MCE, NLL, and Brier score across the five-seed experiments, indicating improved calibration and probabilistic prediction quality. Additional evaluation using uncertainty specific metrics such as Uncertainty Accuracy Coefficient (UAC), Uncertainty Precision Ratio (UPR), Uncertainty Sensitivity Estimate (USE), and Uncertainty Specificity Percentage (USP) confirms the effectiveness of the proposed framework in identifying uncertain predictions while maintaining high classification performance. The experimental evaluations demonstrates that uncertainty aware models provide better calibration and improved reliability compared to baseline architectures while maintaining competitive classification performance. The results shows that the hybrid uncertainty modeling effectively reduces overconfidence and enhances trustworthiness by distinguishing between confident and uncertain samples, that highlights the importance of uncertainty quantification in low resource language fake news detection.

Article.Title: Oxytetracycline residues in beef in Gomba district, Uganda and farmers’ awareness of their effects on human health
Article.Authors: Peter W.; Aggrey S.; Anne N.; Edward N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oxytetracline is among the antibiotics most widely used to treat diseases in cattle. Its irrational use among cattle farmers has led to its residues ending up in the food chain. Information regarding the Oxytracycline residues in food in developing countries like Uganda is still scanty and this has put consumers at risk. This study thus determined the levels of Oxytetracycline residues in beef and assessed level of awareness of their effects on human health among cattle farmers in Gomba district. A cross-sectional study design involving qualitative and quantitative approaches was employed. A total of 378 cattle farmers were enrolled in the study in addition to collection of 419 beef samples that were analyzed for Oxytetracycline residues using High Performance Liquid Chromatography. Awareness among cattle farmers regarding effects of Oxytetracycline residues to human health was analyzed using STATA. Level of Oxytetracycline residues in beef samples were expressed as means±Standard Deviation in MS Excel. Data from Focus Group Discussions involving cattle farmers was analyzed using Nvivo. Results from this study revealed prevalence of Oxytetracycline residues in beef from Gomba district to be high, 76.6% (321) with 76.0% (244) beef samples having Oxytetracycline residues above permitted maximum residue limits (MRL). The mean concentrations were 881.9 ± 457.8µg/kg for muscle, 1364.8 ± 1227.9µg/kg for liver and 3470.2 ± 1910.2µg/kg for kidney. The level of awareness among farmers on Oxytetracycline residues was significantly associated with education level (p = 0.000), the person who administers the drug (p = 0.000) and gender (p = 0.026). The detected high Oxytetracycline residue levels in beef were attributed to the irrational use of Oxytetracycline by farmers. There is therefore need to sensitize farmers on the effects of Oxytetracycline residues on human health. There should also be strict regulation by the government through legislation against the irrational use of veterinary drugs by non-professionals.

Article.Title: Valve stiffness and aortic hemodynamics: insights from fluid-structure interaction simulations
Article.Authors: Almarashi A.; Alkhafaji A.; Bustanji S.; Singh P.; Mar’ie S.; Jaber M.; Alfqih M.; Singh S.; Rajab H.; Sawaran Singh N.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates how aortic valve leaflet stiffness affects hemodynamics and structural performance using high-fidelity fluid–structure interaction simulations of a patient-specific aortic arch. Three leaflet materials were analyzed (Young’s moduli: 10, 25, and 50 MPa). The most compliant model (10 MPa) exhibited the largest systolic deformation (≈ 5.0 mm), physiological flow patterns, and the lowest wall shear stress (WSS) near the valve (≈ 4 Pa), but also generated the highest peak von Mises stress (> 2.0 MPa) and complex vortex structures. In contrast, the stiffest model (50 MPa) showed minimal deformation (< 0.5 mm), reduced leaflet stress (< 0.5 MPa), but induced locally WSS (> 50 Pa) along the aortic arch. Despite these local variations, the area-averaged WSS profiles remained similar across all models (15.8 Pa for 10 MPa vs. 14.3 Pa for 50 MPa). These results reveal a trade-off: compliant valves closely mimic native motion but experience higher mechanical stress, while stiffer valves lower leaflet stress but increase vascular shear loading. These insights are critical for optimizing material selection in artificial valve design.

Article.Title: Effect of vitamin-C surface modification on Pb2+ and Zn2+ adsorption by nanosilica under saline conditions: influence of surface properties and adsorption performance
Article.Authors: Soltani-Gerdefaramarzi S.; Yazdani M.; Abyar F.; Ghasemi M.; Tabrizi L.
Article.Abstract: The application of nanostructured adsorbents for heavy metal removal from saline industrial wastewater remains challenging because elevated ionic strength can alter surface interactions and reduce adsorption efficiency. This study investigated the effect of vitamin C surface modification on the physicochemical characteristics and adsorption performance of nanosilica (NSi) for the removal of Pb 2 ⁺ and Zn 2 ⁺ under saline conditions. Pristine nanosilica and vitamin C-modified nanosilica (VC–NSi) were evaluated at different salinity levels (1, 10, and 20 dS m⁻ 1 ) and initial metal concentrations (50, 100, and 200 mg L⁻ 1 ). Surface characterization revealed substantial changes in the physicochemical properties of the silica structure after vitamin C modification, with a decrease in specific surface area from 195.47 to 106.90 m 2 g⁻ 1 , while the average pore diameter increased from 12.597 to 22.935 nm and the total pore volume remained nearly unchanged. These changes suggested partial occupation of accessible pores and reduced availability of adsorption sites after vitamin C modification . Although both adsorbents effectively removed Pb 2 ⁺ and Zn 2 ⁺, pristine NSi consistently exhibited superior adsorption performance, particularly under highly saline conditions. The removal efficiency of NSi remained above 90% for most Pb 2 ⁺ and Zn 2 ⁺ treatments, whereas VC–NSi showed a considerable decline in metal uptake across salinity levels. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.997 for Pb 2 ⁺ and 0.996 for Zn 2 ⁺), indicating that surface-mediated interactions controlled the adsorption process, while equilibrium data were better described by the Langmuir isotherm. The results demonstrate that surface modification does not necessarily enhance adsorption capacity and that modification-induced changes in pore accessibility and surface area can outweigh the contribution of newly introduced functional groups. This study provides new insights into the structure performance relationship of silica-based adsorbents for heavy metal remediation in saline wastewater environments.

Article.Abstract: We report the synthesis of novel benzohydrazide incorporated naphthalimide troger’s base systems ( 1–4 ) via condensation of naphthalimide with various aryl hydrazides in high yields (86–94%). 1–4 shows strong absorption (λ max = ~ 385 nm) and emission (λ max = ~ 490 nm, ϕ f = 13–57%) in the visible region. Compound 1 found to exhibit selective fluorescent sensing of fluoride ion. The presence of hydrazine functionality in the molecular framework undergoes deprotonation via H-bonding interactions leading to significant quenching of fluorescence. The limit of detection has been calculated to be 9.05 µM. In addition, compound 1 is highly selective towards the fluoride ions among various anions such as OH − , HSO 4 − , NO 2 − , BF 4 − , CN − and OClO 4 − tested.

Article.Title: Micropropagation protocol of Nepenthes alata Blanco for the enhancement of secondary metabolite biosynthesis and in vitro bioactivity
Article.Authors: Abdulmonem G.; Sayed S.; Aboulthana W.; Sokkar N.; Abdel-dayem S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nepenthes alata Blanco is an ornamental carnivorous plant characterized by its unique pitcher morphology and its potential as a source of valuable bioactive compounds. The present study aimed to develop an efficient micropropagation protocol for large-scale in vitro propagation and to evaluate the phytochemical profile and biological activities of the mother plant and tissue culture-derived shootlets. Micropropagation optimal sterilization conditions were achieved using 0.2% mercuric chloride for 20 min. For shootlet induction, Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with 1–3 mg/L benzylaminopurine (BAP) recorded the highest numbers of shootlet, while 3 mg/L isopentenyl adenine (2iP) produced highest shootlet length and leaf number. For root induction, half MS free of hormone contains 1 g/L activated charcoal (AC) or 2 mg/L naphthalene acetic acid (NAA) observed the highest rooting%. Successful acclimatization was achieved using peat moss alone or mixed 1:1 (v/v) with sand or perlite, resulting in good plantlet length and high leaf number. Analysis of the mother plant (NA) and seven tissue culture lines (NA1–NA7) including hormone-free (NA1), BAP-treated (NA2–NA4, 1–3 mg/L), and 2iP-treated (NA5–NA7, 1–3 mg/L) samples, showed that among the tissue culture lines, NA2 exhibited the highest total phenolic and condensed tannin contents. NA2 was also associated with enhanced antioxidant activity (DPPH and ABTS) and marked in vitro inhibitory activity against the evaluated inflammation-related enzymes, carbohydrate-hydrolyzing enzymes, and acetylcholinesterase. GC–MS analysis of the hexane-soluble fraction demonstrated variation in the non-polar metabolite profiles of the analyzed samples. The tissue culture lines generally exhibited lower relative abundances of triterpenoids and naphthoquinones and higher relative abundances of fatty acids. These results demonstrate that optimized micropropagation provides an efficient approach for the large-scale propagation of N. alata enhancing the production of bioactive metabolites.

Article.Title: Study on the energy evolution law of asymmetric failure in roadway under principal stress rotation and its support optimization
Article.Authors: Bian T.; Cao C.; You K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding energy evolution under principal stress rotation is crucial for controlling asymmetric roadway instability. A combined approach of theoretical analysis and numerical simulation is adopted. Based on the stress tensor transformation, an analytical solution for the strain energy density under principal stress rotation is derived, which reveals how the strain energy evolves under mining-induced disturbance. Taking the 81,209 working face’s main retreating roadway as a case study, numerical simulations reveal the evolution of strain energy and plastic zones under principal stress rotation. The results demonstrate that: (1) Under principal stress rotation, the strain energy density exhibits a centrally symmetric distribution, with high-energy zones rotating counterclockwise and high-risk failure zones migrating from the roadway ribs to the roof and floor; (2) For the main retreating roadway of the 81,209 working face at varying advancement stages of the working face, both strain energy concentration zones and plastic zones display asymmetric expansion trends, with a direct correspondence between them; (3) A support optimization scheme, developed based on the energy migration law, effectively homogenizes high-energy concentration zones, suppresses asymmetric expansion of the plastic zone, and significantly enhances the bearing capacity of the surrounding rock mass. These findings provide a critical theoretical foundation for controlling asymmetric instability in mining-induced roadways.

Article.Title: Linking TMEM106B pathology to flortaucipir signal in FTLD-TDP
Article.Authors: Gatto R.; Uruk G.; Youssef H.; Hossain N.; Reichard R.; Dickson D.; Lowe V.; Whitwell J.; Josephs K.
Article.Abstract: Flortaucipir (FTP) is a tau-PET tracer used to detect mature, phosphorylated tau pathology in neurodegenerative diseases. However, FTP exhibits uptake in frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), particularly in FTLD cases with phosphorylated TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (pTDP-43), raising concerns about its regional specificity. Transmembrane protein 106B (TMEM106B), a lysosomal protein, is genetically and pathologically linked to FTLD. FTP retention in FTLD-TDP spatially overlaps with TMEM106B deposition, suggesting that TMEM106B may represent a candidate substrate contributing to regional off-target signal. Tissue samples were obtained from three cognitively normal controls, seven Alzheimer’s disease (AD) cases, and ten FTLD-TDP cases (five type A, five type C). Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded sections from hippocampal and limbic subregions, including the dentate gyrus, CA1-CA4, subiculum, entorhinal cortex, and choroid plexus, were analyzed. A fluorescent FTP analog (T726) was used to assess tracer binding, and fluorescence immunohistochemistry was employed to detect TMEM106B protein and pTDP-43. Confocal microscopy enabled colocalization analysis. TMEM106B protein was observed in both AD and FTLD-TDP cases across all examined subregions. In the AD cases, there were more extended and larger TMEM106B staining patterns compared to those with FTLD-TDP. Colocalization between T726 and TMEM106B was most prominent in the choroid plexus (a common hotspot for off-target binding) in controls, AD, and FTLD cases. Additional colocalization was observed across hippocampal regions, particularly in FTLD-TDP type C cases. These results suggest that FTP off-target binding in FTLD-TDP may be partially attributable to the TMEM106B protein, particularly in the choroid plexus. Further investigations may enhance our understanding of disease mechanisms and refine FTP imaging interpretation in FTLD-TDP.

Article.Title: Robust beamforming and RIS phase shift design for secure ISAC against a multi-antenna active eavesdropper
Article.Authors: Han J.; Yang L.; Zhan Y.; Wang W.; Ng D.
Article.Abstract: In this paper, we design a secure reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system in the presence of a multi-antenna active eavesdropper. Unlike conventional passive eavesdroppers, the active eavesdropper can intercept confidential information and transmit jamming signals toward legitimate users and the sensing target. To counter this dual threat, the RIS is employed to reconfigure the wireless propagation environment and enhance the effective links from the base station to both communication users and the sensing target. Considering imperfect channel state information of the eavesdropper and target angular uncertainty, we formulate a robust sum secrecy rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the communication and sensing beamforming, artificial noise covariance matrix, and RIS phase shifts, subject to transmit power, unit-modulus, and sensing echo signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio constraints. To solve the resulting highly non-convex problem, we develop an alternating optimization framework that decomposes it into tractable subproblems, which are addressed using semidefinite relaxation, a penalty-based method, and successive convex approximation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the baseline schemes, achieving approximately 55% higher average sum secrecy rate than the random RIS baseline, while maintaining robust secure communication and reliable sensing under channel and angular uncertainties.

Article.Title: First-principles investigation of the electronic, optical, and mechanical properties of β-Si3N4 using rSCAN meta-GGA and DFT-D4 dispersion correction
Article.Authors: Samy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A first-principles study of the electronic, optical, and mechanical properties of hexagonal β-Si 3 N 4 has been conducted within the framework of density functional theory (DFT) using the plane-wave-based CASTEP code, the rSCAN meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) exchange–correlation functional, and the DFT-D4 dispersion correction. The present study aims to investigate the relationship between Si–N bonding characteristics and the electronic, optical, and mechanical properties of β-Si 3 N 4 . The calculations were performed using a 1200 eV plane-wave cutoff, a 4 × 4 × 9 Monkhorst–Pack k-point mesh, and strict convergence criteria. Structural validation shows good agreement with available experimental measurements and previously reported theoretical results, indicating the consistency of the adopted computational framework. The calculated electronic structure reveals a wide weakly indirect band gap of 5.029 eV, with the valence-band maximum located near the Γ–A direction and the conduction-band minimum at Γ. Density-of-states analyses reveal strong Si–N orbital hybridization and the insulating nature of β-Si 3 N 4 . The calculated dielectric constant and refractive index are 3.636 and 1.907, respectively. Optical analysis reveals a weak pre-edge feature at 4.11 eV and a primary absorption onset at 5.29 eV, followed by strong ultraviolet absorption with polarization-dependent maximum absorption peaks occurring at approximately 17.46 eV for E ⊥ c [100] and 17.79 eV for E ∥ c [001]. The electron energy-loss spectrum shows an evident peak at 24.28 eV, indicating a strong collective electronic excitation associated with the bulk electronic response. The calculated elastic constants satisfy the Born stability criteria of mechanical stability for hexagonal crystals, giving C 11 = 454.91 GPa, C 33 = 584.78 GPa, and C 44 = 108.50 GPa. The Hill-averaged elastic moduli yield B = 263.02 GPa, G = 135.26 GPa, and E = 346.40 GPa, while the directional Young’s modulus along the c-axis reaches 539.19 GPa, indicating pronounced elastic anisotropy. Overall, the combined electronic, optical, and mechanical results identify β-Si 3 N 4 as a wide-bandgap dielectric ceramic with potential applications in high-temperature structural components, ultraviolet optical systems, electrical insulation, and microelectronic protection technologies.

Article.Title: Robust spectrogram-based automatic modulation classification via deep CNN-LSTM architecture
Article.Authors: Obead O.; El-Assy A.; El-Din Moustafa H.; Nafea H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a crucial task in modern communication systems, enabling the identification of modulation schemes in received signals. This paper presents a proposed model to achieve AMC more accurately by using hybrid techniques, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with spectrograms as input features. The system is evaluated under the influence of Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) with Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR) set at -5, 5, and 10 dB. The model was trained using the Adam optimizer with a fixed learning rate of 0.00001, mini-batch size of 32, and four epochs. The reported overall accuracies are 75.00%, 87.73%, and 99.68% at − 5, 5, and 10 dB, respectively. CPFSK accuracy is 0% at − 5 and 5 dB and 100% at 10 dB. These results demonstrate strong performance on the evaluated MATLAB/AWGN test configuration, but they do not establish robustness under multipath fading, Doppler, timing offsets, non-Gaussian noise, alternative train/test splits, alternative optimizers or learning-rate schedules, or alternative time–frequency representations. In addition, convergence beyond four epochs, CNN-only/LSTM-only ablations, STFT sensitivity, model parameter count, and inference latency were not experimentally evaluated. Therefore, the reported results should be interpreted as dataset- and channel-specific evidence rather than as a controlled claim of superiority over other AMC approaches.

Article.Title: Tailoring the nanoscale physicochemical properties of V2O5 thin films through Mn doping for enhanced electrochemical performance
Article.Authors: Prashant N/A.; Kondal N.; Jangid N.; Sharma R.; Singh K.; Kumar A.; Somvanshi A.; Panda S.; Sharma R.; Kumari A.; Kumar S.; Pathania M.; Gautam R.
Article.Abstract: Vanadium pentoxide (V 2 O 5 ) is a promising transition-metal oxide for energy storage and optoelectronic applications due to its layered crystal structure, multiple oxidation states, and high theoretical charge-storage capacity. In this study, pure and Mn-doped V 2 O 5 thin films were synthesized on ITO glass substrates using a cost-effective sol-gel spin-coating technique. X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of a polycrystalline orthorhombic V 2 O 5 phase without secondary phases, indicating successful Mn incorporation into the host lattice. Mn doping modified the lattice parameters, crystallite size, strain, defect density, and surface morphology, confirming lattice distortion and defect-state formation. UV-visible spectroscopy revealed enhanced absorbance, reduced transmittance, and a narrowed optical response due to Mn-induced defect states and oxygen vacancies. Electrical measurements showed improved conductivity in Mn-doped films with near-linear current-voltage characteristics, indicating ohmic conduction. CV, GCD, and EIS were used to conduct the electrochemical investigations in a 5 M KOH electrolyte. The findings demonstrated that doping of Mn in V 2 O 5 greatly improved its electrochemical characteristics. Mn 4% doped V 2 O 5 thin film demonstrated the greatest electrochemical performance among all the prepared thin films, exhibiting superior specific capacitance and charge transfer kinetics. The findings suggest that Mn-doped V 2 O 5 thin films might be suitable for high-performance energy storage applications.

Article.Title: Nitrogen-functionalized rigid 3D-spirochroman–cycloalkane hybrids as dual α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitors: synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational insights
Article.Authors: Bakr Y.; Abozeid M.; Abou-Elzahab M.; Khan S.; Elghareeb F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus is a major global health concern that demands robust therapeutic strategies to control postprandial hyperglycemia. In this study, a new series of 3D-spirochroman–cycloalkane hybrids bearing nitrogen-containing moieties, including azines, hydrazides, hydrazones, pyrazoles, and pyrroles were rationally designed and effectively synthesized in moderate to excellent yields. Upon evaluation as dual inhibitors of α -amylase and α -glucosidase enzymes, several compounds surpassed the benchmark drug acarbose (IC 50 = 78.9 and 43.3 µM, respectively). Nicotinonitrile 6 showed the strongest α -amylase inhibition (IC 50 = 21.3 µM), while hydrazone 15 exhibited the highest α -glucosidase inhibition potency (IC 50 = 18.2 µM). Hydrazone 12a displayed the most balanced dual inhibitory profile (IC 50 = 25.3 and 29.1 µM). Cytotoxicity assessments of compounds 6 , 12a , and 15 on Vero and WI-38 cell lines revealed minimal inhibitory effects on cell viability (IC 50 ≈ 316.15–611.52 µM). Molecular docking studies highlighted a favourable binding within enzyme active sites stabilized by hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions, and ADMET predictions indicated improved drug-likeness, gastrointestinal absorption, and high bioavailability of compounds 6 , 12a , and 15 compared with acarbose. DFT calculations showed that the nitrogen substitution modulates molecular orbital energies and reduces HOMO–LUMO gaps, serving as descriptors of electronic structure, while complementary multi-wave function analyses (ESP, NCI, and ELF) revealed charge redistribution and enhanced noncovalent interaction patterns consistent with the observed activity and selectivity.

Article.Title: Vanadium (IV)/Vanadium (V) mixed-valence vanadium oxide hybrid nanoribbons for sensitive and selective detection of 4-nitrophenol
Article.Authors: Narooei A.; Saravani H.; Rezvani A.; Shahbakhsh M.; Narouie S.
Article.Abstract: In this work, we report a novel synthetic strategy for the facile, redox-mediated preparation of vanadium polyoxometalate (POM) nanostructures. The reaction of ammonium vanadate with quercetin under redox conditions yields a mixed-valence nanohybrid, denoted VO IV / V HNR, comprising ammonium trivanadate (NH₄)₂V₃O₈ and ammonium metavanadate (NH₄VO₃) phases. The structure and properties of the resulting nanohybrid were investigated using a range of techniques, including field emission scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry. When used to modify a carbon paste electrode (CPE/VO IV / V HNR), the nanohybrid exhibited a well-defined oxidation peak for 4-nitrophenol at 0.68 V (vs. Ag/AgCl) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer at pH 2. Under these conditions, the electrode response was linear over the concentration range of 5–60 µM, with a detection limit of 0.7 µM. Notably, the sensor demonstrated strong selectivity, remaining largely unaffected by structurally similar nitrophenolic compounds. When applied to real water matrices, the sensor achieved recovery values in the range of 97–101.6% for the determination of 4-nitrophenol in tap water and river water samples. Taken together, these results establish CPE/VO IV / V HNR as a sensitive and selective electrochemical platform for the determination of 4-nitrophenol in environmental water samples.

Article.Title: Dynamical analysis and optimal control of a Hyper-SICR rumor spreading model on hypergraphs
Article.Authors: Zhong W.; Lu Y.; Ren M.; Deng H.; Wei J.; Yu J.; Luo J.; Tang L.
Article.Abstract: Rumor spreading on online social platforms often exhibits group-interaction characteristics involving multiple users. To investigate rumor spreading under higher-order interaction structures, this paper constructs a Hyper-SICR rumor-spreading model based on hypergraph theory and introduces the single-contact transmission probability and saturated incidence rate. First, the basic reproduction number \(R_0\) of the model is derived, and the existence and stability of the rumor-free equilibrium and rumor-prevailing equilibrium are analyzed. Numerical results provide support for the theoretical analysis. Comparison with the degenerated SICR model shows that, under the same parameter conditions, the higher-order structure leads to a lower \(R_0\) . After further matching the same \(R_0\) , effective growth rate, and decay rate, dynamical differences between the two models still remain, further reflecting the influence of the higher-order structure on the system dynamics. Finally, an optimal control model is constructed. Numerical results show that the optimal control can adjust the control intensity according to different hyperdegrees, and larger hyperdegrees require stronger early-stage control. Under the same total cumulative cost, the optimal control achieves a better suppression effect than uniform control.

Article.Title: MR imaging and spectroscopy reveals metabolic changes in glioblastoma driven by treatment with temozolomide and lonidamine
Article.Authors: Alrashidi T.; Bhaduri S.; Gash E.; Alyetama S.; Morgan M.; Sciacovelli M.; Moothanchery M.; Maguire M.; Ressel L.; Poptani H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) limits the efficacy of treatment in glioblastoma (GBM) which is fuelled by a metabolic reprogramming of the cancer cells and alterations in the tumour microenvironment. Lonidamine (LND), a glycolytic and mitochondrial inhibitor, modulates tumour metabolism and can alter tumour response to treatment. This study investigated the effects of LND in combination with TMZ and used MR imaging and spectroscopy to evaluate metabolic and microstructural changes in a syngeneic GBM model. C57BL/6 mice bearing intracranial GL261 tumours (n = 66) were treated with saline, LND, TMZ, or LND + TMZ for five consecutive days. Longitudinal imaging (days 0, 3, 6) included T2-weighted MRI, diffusion weighted imaging (DWI), and conventional and lactate-edited ¹H-MRS. Tumour volume, survival, DWI parameters, MCT4 expression, and mitotic indices were assessed. In vitro, acute and chronic bioenergetic reprogramming of GL261 cells was assessed using the Seahorse extracellular flux analysis. Lactate is a not simply an end product of high glycolytic cancer cells, but it has also emerged as a molecule capable to shaping the tumour microenvironment. A significant decrease in lactate observed in the LND and LND + TMZ groups indicated a reduction in the steady-state lactate pool suggestive of reduced lactate production, utilization or altered glycolytic flux. However, lactate remained high in the control and TMZ-only groups. This metabolic shift in the LND treatment group was consistent with a marked reduction in MCT4 protein, the lactate transporter, in LND-treated tumours. In vitro bioenergetic profiling of GL261 cells revealed an acute decrease in mitochondrial respiration in response to LND, with partial recovery at later time points. Finally, even though not significant, an enhanced survival benefit of the treatment combination was observed, with no significant differences observed between the groups for tumour volume, DWI-derived parameters, or mitotic index after 6 days. LND induces early metabolic changes detectable by MRS. Although a limited therapeutic benefit of addition LND to TMZ was observed in the early stages of tumour development, its tumour-selective activity and effect on tumour microenvironment is promising and its long-term effects on tumour development should be investigated as part of an optimized combination strategy for TMZ treatment.

Article.Title: AI-generated medical advice is rated favourably but GP advice is more trusted in India
Article.Authors: Pandey P.; Veltri G.; Zadorozhny B.; Vlaev I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to provide health information and advice, yet its acceptance depends not only on how credible the information appears but also on whether individuals are willing to rely on it. Existing research has documented resistance to medical AI and source-labelling effects, but evidence from non-Western settings and factorial designs examining source, transparency, and clinical risk together remains comparatively limited. This study examined how individuals evaluate medical advice presented as AI-generated versus general practitioner (GP)-generated, whether source-related differences vary across transparency and clinical-risk conditions, and how these evaluations relate to stated willingness to follow the advice. We conducted a mixed-methods, partially within-subject 2 × 2 × 2 factorial experiment with 797 participants in Mumbai, India. Each participant evaluated four vignettes randomly drawn from eight conditions varying by source (AI or GP), transparency (high or low), and clinical risk (high or low), yielding 3,188 vignette observations. Following examination of the item structure, trustworthiness and a two-item uniqueness-recognition score (α = 0.944) were analysed as separate principal epistemically relevant outcomes. Perceived accuracy and binary behavioural intention were examined separately. The originally constructed three-item epistemic-value composite (α = 0.15) was retained only as an exploratory supplementary analysis. Data were analysed using linear and logistic mixed-effects models, participant-level paired comparisons, and equivalence testing using operational ± 0.20-SD bounds. Qualitative responses were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Perceived recognition of individual uniqueness did not differ significantly between AI-generated and GP-generated advice, and equivalence was supported within the operational bounds. In contrast, GP-generated advice was rated as more trustworthy and more accurate than AI-generated advice and elicited greater stated willingness to follow. Nevertheless, willingness to follow remained high for both sources, with 86.5% of AI-generated advice responses and 97.3% of GP-generated advice responses indicating an intention to follow the advice. Transparency and clinical risk did not significantly influence the continuous evaluative outcomes. Qualitative findings indicated that AI-generated advice was valued particularly for accessibility and informational clarity, whereas GP-generated advice was more strongly associated with professional expertise, accountability, safety, and relational care. Favourable responses to AI-generated medical advice can coexist with a relative preference for advice attributed to a medical professional. Although AI- and GP-generated advice were comparable in perceived recognition of individual uniqueness within the operational equivalence bounds, GP-generated advice retained advantages in trustworthiness, perceived accuracy, and intended reliance. These findings suggest that responses to medical AI are multidimensional and support positioning AI as a complementary source of health information rather than as an interchangeable substitute for human medical expertise.

Article.Title: GridXAI-diffusion an adaptive graph intelligence framework for interpretable data integrity analysis in smart grid cybersecurity systems
Article.Authors: Issac A.; Priya S.
Article.Abstract: Smart-grid cybersecurity is increasingly challenged by sophisticated cyberattacks, evolving operational behaviors, and complex cyber-physical dependencies. Existing machine learning, deep learning, and graph-based detection methods remain limited in jointly modeling dynamic attack behaviors, spatio-temporal dependencies, attack-data scarcity, and interpretable security decisions. This study proposes GridXAI-Diffusion, an adaptive and interpretable graph intelligence framework for smart-grid cyberattack detection and data-integrity analysis. Evaluation was conducted using the Kaggle Smart Grid Security Dataset containing 1,000 samples and 24 features representing operational signals, communication behaviors, extracted characteristics, threat indicators, and attack labels. The framework integrates diffusion-based cyberattack scenario generation, dynamic cyber-physical graph construction, spatio-temporal graph transformer learning, contrastive representation learning, and Graph Temporal Causal Attention Explainability (GTCAE). The principal novelty is the coordinated integration of these established techniques into a unified cybersecurity architecture, where each component addresses attack diversity, topology-aware representation, temporal evolution, robustness, or interpretability. Experimental results achieve 96.18% accuracy, 97.04% precision, 95.71% recall, and 96.82% F1-score, outperforming the evaluated baseline approaches. Ablation analysis further confirms complementary contributions from the integrated components. Overall, GridXAI-Diffusion provides an adaptive and interpretable framework for robust cyberattack detection and data-integrity assessment under evolving smart-grid conditions.

Article.Title: Sleep duration, depressive symptoms, and memory aging: longitudinal patterns and temporal network evidence from four-wave CHARLS study (2011–2018)
Article.Authors: He Y.; Ou Y.; Wang Y.; Li J.; Ma L.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Sleep is a modifiable behavioral factor closely linked to cognitive aging and depressive symptoms. However, evidence remains limited on whether nocturnal sleep and midday nap duration are nonlinearly associated with heterogeneous longitudinal patterns of subjective memory complaints (SMCs), objective episodic memory (OEM), and depressive symptoms, as well as their temporal interrelationships. We analyzed four-wave data (2011–2018) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 7,198 participants aged ≥ 45 years (mean age: 56.12 ± 7.93 years; 51.8% female). Sleep duration was self-reported. SMCs, OEM (Word Recall Test, reverse-coded), and depressive symptoms (CESD-10) were assessed. K-means clustering was applied to identify longitudinal patterns of SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms. Restricted cubic spline models were applied to examine potential nonlinear dose–response associations between sleep duration and longitudinal patterns. Cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis was used to examine the temporal and directional associations among these variables across waves. Distinct longitudinal patterns were identified for SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms. Sleep duration showed nonlinear associations with trajectories reflecting poorer memory outcomes and greater depressive symptoms, with estimated nadirs of approximately 7.6, 6.9, and 7.7 h for SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms, respectively. CLPN analysis demonstrated stable network structures with good centrality stability. SMCs showed the highest out-expected influence, while OEM demonstrated the highest in-expected influence, suggesting a consistent cross-wave predictive association from SMCs to subsequent OEM scores. Deviations from the nocturnal sleep duration at the estimated nadir are associated with adverse memory and depressive symptoms. Longitudinal network analysis suggested a directional pattern from SMCs to OEM, suggesting that SMCs may potentially represent an early indicator of memory decline. These findings highlight the potential value of integrating subjective memory assessment with sleep monitoring for early prevention of cognitive decline in aging populations.

Article.Title: 17β-estradiol increases diet-dependent salt retention in ovariectomized female mice
Article.Authors: Crislip G.; Lee R.; Broderick B.; Cheng K.; Lynch I.; Costello H.; Douma L.; Gumz M.
Article.Abstract: Circadian rhythms heavily influence blood pressure regulation. Genetic manipulation of core circadian clock genes alters blood pressure phenotypes. We have shown that male mice with renal distal segment knockout of the circadian transcription factor BMAL1 (kidney-specific cadherin Cre-positive BMAL1 knockout; KS-BMAL1 KO) exhibit lower blood pressure than wild-type controls, and this phenotype is exacerbated by a salt-sensitive diet. The BMAL1-dependent blood pressure phenotype in male KS-BMAL1 KO is absent in intact female mice. The current study aims to determine if estradiol modulates BMAL1-dependent blood pressure regulation in female mice. We hypothesized that ovariectomized (OVX) female mice would demonstrate a genotype difference in blood pressure and that estradiol would abolish this difference. OVX control and OVX KS-BMAL1 KO female mice subcutaneously received either a 17β‑estradiol pellet or placebo for three weeks prior to dietary treatment. Blood pressure was recorded daily via telemetric devices in OVX mice administered a baseline standard diet followed by 7 days of a low-K+ diet, then 7 days of a low-K+ high-salt diet. Contrary to our hypothesis, OVX mice with placebo pellets did not demonstrate a genotype difference in blood pressure. Furthermore, blood pressure between genotypes remained similar in OVX mice with an estradiol pellet. Estradiol supplementation led to higher mean arterial pressure by ~ 8 mmHg in both genotypes on a low-K+ high-salt diet. During the adaptation period to a low-K+ high-salt diet, OVX KS-BMAL1 KO mice have less sodium retention compared to OVX control mice and estradiol leads to more sodium retention compared to placebo. Under the conditions tested, there is no evidence that estradiol plays a role in BMAL1-dependent blood pressure regulation. These findings provide insight into the sex-specific role of BMAL1 in blood pressure regulation.

Article.Title: Network analysis of symptom severity and symptom distress in hospitalized patients with decompensated cirrhosis
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Luo L.; Zhang Y.; Liu Z.; Zhang Y.; Wen Z.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to explore the network characteristics of symptom severity and symptom distress in hospitalized patients with decompensated cirrhosis, conduct an exploratory comparison of the two networks, and analyze factors associated with the occurrence of the symptom ranked highest in centrality within each network to inform clinical symptom management. Using convenience sampling, we recruited 459 hospitalized patients with decompensated cirrhosis from a tertiary Grade A hospital in China between July 2025 and January 2026. Symptoms were assessed using the Chinese version of the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale, and the correlation between symptom severity and symptom distress was assessed using Spearman’s rank correlation analysis. Symptom severity and symptom distress networks were constructed separately, with node centrality evaluated using expected influence. Network differences were assessed using the Network Comparison Test, and factors associated with the occurrence of the symptom ranked highest in centrality within each network were examined using binary logistic regression. Patient-level mean severity and distress scores across the 16 symptoms included in the primary networks were strongly positively correlated (Spearman’s ρ = 0.957). No statistically significant differences were detected between the two networks in global strength or overall network structure. “Feeling sad” had the highest expected influence in the symptom severity network, while “I don’t look like myself” had the strongest expected influence in the symptom distress network. The occurrence of “Feeling sad” was associated with the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score category and per capita monthly household income. The occurrence of “I don’t look like myself” was associated with the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score category, per capita monthly household income, and primary caregiver. “Feeling sad” and “I don’t look like myself” ranked first in centrality within their respective networks. When considered alongside patients’ actual symptom burden and the patient characteristics associated with the occurrence of these two symptoms, the findings of this study can provide a reference for clinical symptom management.

Article.Title: Copper-dithiocarbamate decorated graphitic carbon nitride as a robust heterogeneous cross-coupling catalyst for diaryl ether synthesis
Article.Authors: Rahimzadeh-oskooee A.; Ghaffarzadeh M.; Azizi N.; Gouranourimi A.
Article.Abstract: A novel copper/dithiocarbamate-decorated graphitic carbon nitride (g-C₃N₄@DTC-Cu) catalyst was developed and applied as a robust, heterogeneous catalytic system for the C–O cross-coupling reaction of aryl halides with phenols to form diaryl ethers for the first time. Interestingly, the dithiocarbamate ligand effectively stabilized Cu(I) species on the carbon nitride surface resulted in enhanced dispersion, redox accessibility, and resistance to leaching under basic conditions. Comprehensive characterizations (XRD, SEM, TEM, IR, AFM, NMR, ICP-OES, BET, and EDS) have confirmed uniform metal–ligand anchoring and strong Cu–N/C coordination in the newly synthesised catalyst. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited high reactivity toward diverse substrates bearing electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups, affording diaryl ether derivatives in excellent yields. Recyclability tests demonstrated sustained catalytic performance over multiple cycles with negligible copper loss. The synergistic interaction between Cu centres and the conjugated C₃N₄ framework underlies the enhanced efficiency and durability of g-C₃N₄@DTC-Cu, offering a green and scalable platform for ether bond formation in fine-chemical synthesis.

Article.Title: AgriVision: adversarial image detection using Deep Learning in agricultural contexts
Article.Authors: Yardimci M.; Sikder M.; Ward T.; Batarseh F.
Article.Abstract: The digital transformation of agriculture has created cyber-physical systems in which biological processes are monitored and adjusted through sensory, digital, and visualpipelines. As these systems increasingly rely on artificial intelligence, controlled agriculture environments use biological inputs such as leaf images for disease detection and yield estimation; amongst other goals. Images used as input for on-the-farm decision making are frequently exposed to adversarial manipulation and to synthetic images created by new generative models. Prior studies in this domain focused mainly on pixel-level attacks or simple binary detection and offered limited support for identifying the generative source of an image and for handling unseen generators. In this work, we propose a unified detection and attribution framework for agricultural cyber-physical systems (namely: AgriVision). Synthetic concealment and fabrication attack scenarios are created using multiple generative adversarial networks (StyleGAN2, StyleGAN3, R3GAN) and diffusion models (Instruct-Pix2Pix, BLIP-Diffusion, DreamShaper-8) across apple, maize, and tomato imagery. These synthetic samples are used to evaluate three vision classifier architectures: EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, and CLIP (ViT-B/32), for binary authenticity classification (Real vs. Synthetic), source identification (Real, GAN, or Diffusion), and detailed plant-health-source attribution. In the in-distribution setting, the convolutional models reach near-saturated performance for the generators and preprocessing conditions present in training, while CLIP performs well on detailed attribution but shows weaker performance on binary authenticity classification. When the models are evaluated on images from generators not seen during training, accuracy drops for source attribution and CLIP shows plant-specific failures. These results demonstrate both the promise and the limits of current generative-image detection methods in controlled agricultural imagery and motivate layered, continuously updated defenses for preserving the integrity of automated agricultural monitoring pipelines.

Article.Title: Emergence of blaNDM−19 on a conserved IncX3 plasmid in a multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli ST167 high-risk clone from Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alomani A.; Alghoribi M.; Alharbi S.; Faqih L.; Alswaji A.; Alzayer M.; Aldakheel F.; Alyami A.; Abdelrahman T.; Alasmari F.; Alotaibi S.
Article.Abstract: The spread of carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria poses a substantial risk to global public health. Metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing bacteria, including those carrying the bla NDM gene, are resistant to most β-lactam antibiotics, limiting treatment options. The dissemination of bla NDM genes is largely driven by horizontal gene transfer facilitated by plasmids. In this work, we report the first detection of a bla NDM−19 -producing Escherichia coli ST167 isolate from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and provide genomic characterization, including analysis of resistance and virulence gene profiles, plasmid backbone, and genetic elements associated with horizontal gene transfer. The isolate was recovered from a blood sample collected from a patient with intra-abdominal infection following prostatocystectomy at King Fahad Medical City (KFMC), Riyadh. Identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed using the BD Phoenix system, and screening for carbapenemase genes was conducted with the Xpert Carba-R ® assay. We performed whole genome sequencing (WGS) using the Illumina MiSeq and Oxford Nanopore GridION platforms, followed by bioinformatic analysis for genome assembly, annotation, and characterization of resistance, virulence, and plasmid features. The isolate, designated EC24_NDM-19, was phenotypically resistant to all tested antibiotics except colistin, tigecycline, gentamicin, and amikacin. Genomic analysis classified it as sequence type (ST) 167, serotype O89-like: H5-like, and phylogroup A. A 49.8-kb plasmid-associated contig, designated pEC24_NDM-19, was recovered from the long-read assembly and found to carry the bla NDM−19 gene. In silico analysis identified it as a conjugative IncX3 plasmid. The bla NDM−19 gene was flanked upstream by Tn2–Tn5403–IS3000–IS Aba125 –IS5 and downstream by ble MBL – trpF – dsbC –IS26–IS Kox3 –Tn552. This structure closely resembled that of IncX3 plasmids carrying the bla NDM−19 gene reported in Switzerland, China, Lebanon, and Palestine. This study represents the first report of bla NDM−19 in Saudi Arabia and demonstrates its location on an IncX3 plasmid-associated contig within a conserved genetic context shared with previously reported bla NDM−19 -carrying IncX3 plasmids. These findings expand current knowledge of the regional and global distribution of bla NDM−19 and highlight the potential for further plasmid-mediated dissemination of carbapenem resistance.

Article.Title: Morphophysiological development, allometric growth, and early ontogeny of the Amazonian ornamental characid Moenkhausia oligolepis (Günther, 1864)
Article.Authors: Coimbra V.; do Nascimento Albuquerque E.; da Silva Ferreira E.; Lacerda O.; de Sousa B.; Rodrigues J.; Maximino C.; de Siqueira-Silva D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study describes, for the first time, the morphophysiological development, allometric growth patterns, and the main initial ontogenetic events of Moenkhausia oligolepis , a species of ecological and ornamental importance in the Amazon region. Hatching occurred 16 h after fertilization, under an average temperature of 25.36 ± 0.64 °C with a pH of 7.28 ± 1.11. From hatching onward, the larvae were sampled at regular intervals (0–6 h post-hatching with collections every 2 h; 6–22 h every 4 h; and subsequently, daily collections) for morphological, morphometric, meristic, and histological analyses. Larval development spanned from the yolk-sac stage to the post-flexion stage (0–30 days after hatching-DAH), with a well-defined sequence of events: mouth opening and initiation of exogenous feeding at 3 DAH, cannibalistic behavior at 4 DAH, notochord flexion at 15 DAH (mean SL = 6.33 ± 0.56 mm), and the larval-juvenile transition at 30 DAH with the development of fin rays and the appearance of scales. Allometric analyses revealed positive cephalic growth relative to standard length (b = 1.389), indicating prioritization of the development of structures associated with feeding and sensory perception. Notochord length and preanal distance showed growth close to isometry relative to standard length, while body height exhibited negative allometry. Histological analysis demonstrated progressive differentiation of the digestive tract, with the presence of a buccopharyngeal cavity, esophagus, segmented intestine (anterior, middle, and posterior regions), and mucosal cells at 3 DAH. Cytoplasmic vacuolization was observed in hepatocytes starting at 23 DAH, associated with the presence of digested material in the intestinal lumen. The secondary lamellae of the gills exhibited evident buds at 4 DAH, and the swim bladder was divided into two regions at the end of flexion stage (22 DAH). Gonadal evaluation indicated undifferentiated gonads up to 50 DAH and ovarian differentiation at 60 DAH, characterized by the presence of primary meiotic oocytes; testicular differentiation was not observed during the analyzed period. Based on the observed morphological and ontogenetic characteristics, four larval stages were described (yolk-sac, pre-flexion, flexion, and post-flexion). The results expand knowledge of the species’ early biology, providing relevant insights for taxonomic, ecological, and conservation studies, as well as for improving management and larviculture strategies for native ornamental fish.

Article.Title: Coupled vibration characteristics analysis and experimental study of a blade-disk-shaft system with breathing cracks
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Chen T.; Guo T.; Yan M.; Wei D.; Yu T.; Yuan H.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The blade-disk-shaft system (BDSS) is an essential aero-engine assembly. The emergence of fatigue cracks on blades significantly alters its dynamic characteristics, inducing complex nonlinear coupled vibrations that are notably difficult to detect. In this study, numerical models of a BDSS with blade root open crack and blade loss corner faults were developed and validated through impact hammer tests. A finite element model (FEM) of a BDSS with breathing cracks was developed to study the influence of crack parameters on its vibration characteristics, including the crack distribution pattern (adjacent or spaced blades), location (root or tip), and propagation direction (axial or radial). Furthermore, key vibration-sensitive features were extracted to identify early damage. Results suggest that cracks produce a detuning effect in the BDSS, leading to frequency splitting and modal localization phenomena. Breathing cracks reduce the peak amplitude of the blade’s time-domain (TD) response and introduce superharmonic nonlinear components in the frequency-domain (FD) response. The orientation of fatigue crack propagation is shown to significantly influence the vibration characteristics, where frequency splitting and frequency change rate can serve as a potential indicator of crack presence. This work provides a theoretical basis for crack identification and the prognosis of fatigue crack propagation trends.

Article.Title: Curcumin nanoparticles attenuate radiation-induced liver and kidney injury in rats: a histopathological evaluation
Article.Authors: Azmoonfar R.; Shiri E.; Khosravi H.; Najafi M.; Varkeshi M.; Salimi M.; Ebrahimi M.
Article.Abstract: Radiation therapy is a common treatment for a variety of malignancies. However, it can have harmful effects on healthy tissues. Curcumin, a compound derived from turmeric, has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and radioprotective properties, making it promising for reducing radiation-induced damage. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the radioprotective effects of curcumin nanoparticles (CurNPs) on the liver and kidneys of rats exposed to radiation. Thirty male Wistar rats were divided into six groups: control, radiation-only, CurNPs (2 mg/kg), CurNPs(4 mg/kg), CurNPs (2 mg/kg) + IR, and CurNPs (4 mg/kg) + IR. The radiation-only group was exposed to a single dose of 6 Gy of radiation, while the CurNPs-treated groups received a dose of CurNPs before radiation exposure. The liver and kidney tissues were collected and subjected to histopathological examination. Histopathological analysis revealed that the radiation-only group exhibited severe damage to the liver and kidney tissues, characterized by hepatocyte degeneration, inflammation, and tubular necrosis. In contrast, the CurNPs-treated group demonstrated a significant reduction in radiation-induced pathological changes, with preserved tissue architecture, decreased inflammation, and enhanced cell viability. In conclusion, our histopathological study demonstrates that both 2 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg CurNPs possess the potential to serve as a promising radioprotective agent for the liver and kidneys but no apparent difference between the two doses.. The use of CurNPs could help mitigate radiation-induced toxicity in cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. These findings warrant further investigation and provide a foundation for developing innovative radioprotective strategies.

Article.Title: Reactive path planning for low speed UAVs and mobile robots in static environments using adaptive block coordinate descent logistic regression
Article.Authors: Pamarthi V.; Yarra K.; Boyapati P.; Puppala R.; Bikku T.; Donapati R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) require efficient and reliable path planning mechanisms for safe navigation in obstacle-constrained environments. This study presents an Adaptive Block Coordinate Descent Logistic Regression (ABCD-LoR) model for reactive path planning in static environments using low-cost sensor inputs. The proposed approach formulates obstacle avoidance as a three-class classification problem (no turn, left turn, right turn), where navigation decisions are made sequentially based on local observations rather than pre-computed global trajectories. The model parameters are optimized using an adaptive block coordinate descent strategy, which improves convergence stability and reduces sensitivity to noisy updates compared to stochastic gradient-based methods. Performance is evaluated using statistical model fit measures, including Pseudo R2, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), log-likelihood, and likelihood ratio tests, along with classification metrics and ROC analysis. Simulation experiments are conducted in dense static environ-ments under varying speed conditions. The proposed method is compared with classical path planning approaches, including A*, Vector Field Histogram (VFH), Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC), Dynamic Window Approach (DWA), Artificial Potential Field (APF), and ASGD-based logistic regression. Results indicate that ABCD-LoR achieves reduced path length and lower computational time while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The study is based on a simu-lated dataset generated from infrared and ultrasonic sensor configurations. While the results demonstrate the feasibility of the approach for real-time reactive nav-igation, the limited dataset size and absence of sensor noise highlight the need for further validation in real-world and dynamic environments.

Article.Title: A shape-control methodology for vehicle aerodynamics based on sectional parametrization
Article.Authors: Chae D.; Lee J.; Oh S.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a novel parametric vehicle design framework based on 2D contour geometry to overcome the limitations of conventional aerodynamic analysis models. The widely used Ahmed model suffers from limited geometric fidelity, while the DrivAer model presents difficulties in systematic shape modification and parameter control. To address these issues, the proposed approach enables both physically realistic aerodynamic representation and flexible geometric parameterization within a unified framework. A 3D vehicle geometry is constructed by extruding and integrating parameterized 2D contours derived from the front, top, and side views, allowing compact yet expressive shape control through a limited set of design variables. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations are performed to validate the aerodynamic accuracy of the generated geometries, yielding drag coefficient errors of 2.31%, 2.44%, and 6.84% for the fastback, notchback, and estate configurations, respectively, relative to the experimental DrivAer data. Parametric investigations reveal that roofline height is the most influential design parameter governing aerodynamic drag characteristics. Furthermore, detailed flow field analyses elucidate the evolution of wake structures and pressure distributions as functions of key geometric variations. The proposed methodology provides a computationally efficient and scalable framework for aerodynamic shape optimization in early-stage vehicle design and is readily extendable to other bluff-body aerodynamic applications.

Article.Title: Agentic AI system for hospital management
Article.Authors: Pati A.; Mohapatra K.; Padhi M.; Tripathy S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In modern-day hospital administration, there are many problems like long waiting time for patients, poor scheduling of physicians, lack of coordination between departments, among others. As such, this research suggests an Agentic AI System for Hospital Administration that utilizes a multi agent architecture and intelligence embedding to automate healthcare processes. This model entails a Patient Interaction Agent, a Care Coordination Agent, a Doctor Interaction Agent, and a Bed Allocation Agent, whose main roles are facilitating patients' entry and sorting out the patients' needs, allocation of doctors to attend to patients, coordination within the hospital, and hospital resource management, respectively.Through reinforcement learning, decision-making based on information processing, and synchronization, the framework becomes more adaptive and scalable. It is expected that due to intelligence distribution and intelligent decision-making, this model will minimize total waiting time, improve physicians' usage, and enhance scheduling of patients. Empirical analysis shows that hospital operations exhibit significant performance superiority of agentic models over the traditional models.Modern hospital administration faces major challenges such as prolonged patient waiting times, inefficient physician scheduling, poor interdepartmental coordination, and suboptimal resource utilization. Traditional hospital management systems often rely on static and centralized approaches that lack adaptability in dynamic healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL)-based intelligent hospital administration framework for workflow optimization and resource management. The proposed system consists of four collaborative agents: a Patient Interaction Agent for patient triage, a Doctor Scheduling Agent for dynamic physician allocation, a Care Coordination Agent for interdepartmental communication, and a Bed Allocation Agent for adaptive resource management. The agents utilize decentralized decision-making and reinforcement learning to optimize hospital operations in real time. The framework is evaluated using a hospital simulation environment and compared with conventional scheduling and management approaches. The results show that the effectiveness of the proposed system model is able to complete the tasks at a rate of 82.50\% in a period of 5.12 seconds with a success rate in handling queries of 79.15\%. Furthermore, the system attains a coordination efficiency of 87.50\%, indicating effective collaboration among agents, while maintaining an agent conflict rate of 5.00\%, ensuring stable and interference-free operations. The framework records a low communication overhead of 0.88, reflecting efficient inter-agent communication, and achieves a convergence rate of 96.4\%, demonstrating learning stability and adaptability.This indicates that the model is efficient, scalable, and adaptable in managing intelligent hospitals.

Article.Title: Changes in the scope and intent of US state legislation on ivermectin and pharmacy dispensing trends, 2020–2026
Article.Authors: Ibiebele J.; Parchure D.; Chen T.; Wirtz V.; Shioda K.; Bhadelia N.
Article.Abstract: State legislation related to ivermectin use has grown in volume and scope since 2020, despite limited evidence for its effectiveness in treating COVID-19. Media reports suggest that public interest in ivermectin continued after the pandemic and has expanded to other indications alongside promotion by social media influencers and podcasters. In this study, we analyzed ivermectin-related bills introduced from January 2020 to September 2026 and assessed their association with ivermectin dispensing trends. We identified 35 states that introduced 129 ivermectin-related bills, with eight enacting legislation. Legislative focus evolved from predominantly off-label use in 2020–2022 to over-the-counter access in 2025–2026. Early legislation specifically mentioned COVID-19 treatment, while later bills omitted specific medical indications. A sub-analysis using Poisson regression to evaluate the association between state-level ivermectin dispensing rates from 2019 to 2023 and legislative trends identified that dispensed ivermectin quantity per 100,000 population was 3.84 (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.96–4.98) times higher during the pandemic and 1.33 (95% CI 1.23–1.43) times higher post-pandemic compared with the pre-pandemic period, regardless of whether states introduced ivermectin-related legislation. Legislative efforts to bypass federal drug regulation and medical oversight for ivermectin access represent a notable trend with potential implications for patient safety.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of eggshells wastes and tricalcium phosphate as substrates for phosphate and calcium solubilization by arid ecosystem fungal isolates
Article.Authors: Khalil D.; El-Sayed M.; El-Zayat S.; Ali A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungi can solubilize tricalcium phosphate and eggshell-derived calcium, thereby accelerating nutrient availability and supporting their sustainable use as biofertilizers. This study investigated the solubilization efficiency of four fungal isolates named, Aspergillus terreus (26L), Aspergillus fumigatus [(7L), Emericella nidulans var cristata (1Fcit) and Asperagillus flavus (4Fcit) as using eggshells (EgSh) and tricalcium phosphate (CPh) as growth media substrates, with emphasis on pH reduction, phosphate, and calcium release. All isolates significantly decreased medium pH, with the strongest acidification recorded for 1Fcit (pH 1.2) and 4Fcit (pH 1.6) on tricalcium phosphate substrate (CPh), while eggshells (EgSh) exhibited more moderate declines due to its carbonate buffering capacity. Phosphate solubilization was higher from CPh, where 26L reached a maximum of 0.26 mg mL⁻ 1 , compared to EgSh, which was the highest at 0.067 mg mL⁻ 1 with 4Fcit fungus. Conversely, calcium release was greater from EgSh, with 4Fcit fungus and 1Fcit fungus reaching 12 and 8.2 mg mL⁻ 1 , respectively, while 26L and 7L fungi were weak Calcium solubilizers. These results demonstrated that fungal activity is closely linked to medium acidification [pH] and that solubilization performance is substrate specific subject, with isolates Aspergillus terreus (26L) and Asperagillus flavus (4Fcit) from ecological view showed the greatest potential as bio- fertilizers.
