Article.Title: Deformable convolution and multi-scale fusion for high-performance transmission line defect detection
Article.Authors: He Y.; Xing B.; Yao X.; Feng X.; Zhang Y.; Long H.
Article.Abstract: This article presents a high-performance defect detection algorithm for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) transmission line inspection, addressing issues such as missed detections, false alarms, and low accuracy. The algorithm combines the C3K2-DCNv4 module, which adopts a hierarchical integration strategy and which leverages deformable convolution to better capture geometric features from irregular targets. It also integrates the SPPF-LSKA module with a large kernel separation convolution attention mechanism, replacing the original SPPF structure to improve multi-scale feature extraction while reducing model redundancy. The neck network is redesigned with a diffuse pyramid structure integrated with DASI to enhance multi-scale feature fusion and context propagation. Additionally, the DyHead module incorporates a dynamic attention mechanism to strengthen feature representation under complex backgrounds. The introduction of the Focal-DIoU loss function and a focus on difficult samples, along with bounding box regression optimization, enhance convergence speed and localization accuracy. The main contribution of this work is the task-driven configuration and coordinated interaction of these modules for UAV-based transmission-line inspection. Specifically, DCNv4 is selectively inserted into the P2-P4 backbone stages, the P2 detection branch is added while the P5 branch is removed to prioritize small and medium-sized defects, SPPF-LSKA is channel-reduced to control computational redundancy, and the diffuse pyramid, DASI, DyHead, and Focal-DIoU are jointly configured to address cross-scale information loss, complex backgrounds, and hard imbalanced samples. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the baseline, with an 8.4-percentage-point increase in mAP@0.5, a 4.8-percentage-point increase in precision, and an 11.8-percentage-point increase in recall. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB platform, the measured TensorRT INT8 latency was 128 ms for a batch of 16 images, corresponding to an effective throughput of 125 images/s. Under FP16 precision, the measured latency was 144 ms per batch, corresponding to 111 images/s. These results demonstrate efficient batched inference under the tested configuration. Because the Jetson evaluation used a batch size of 16, the results should be interpreted as batched throughput rather than single-frame camera latency.

Article.Title: Impact of social media-based health campaigns on knowledge, belief, and self-reported behavior during COVID-19
Article.Authors: Zhou Z.; Kuzmanovic A.; Malik A.; Melchinger H.; Christie S.; Miguens G.; Gulaid M.; Omer S.
Article.Abstract: Digital media has emerged as a vital tool for timely, global dissemination of public health information. From 2020 to 2022, the World Health Organization ran 81 social media health campaigns on COVID-19, the impact of which were assessed using Brand Lift Studies from Meta, Inc. We conducted two meta-analyses, age-stratified and gender-stratified respectively, to assess impact across recall, knowledge, belief, and behavior questions. Overall, we observed improved lift (i.e. higher proportions of individuals giving desired answers in intervention vs. control group) in both models. In the age-stratified model, there was positive and significant lift among recall (3.0%, 95% CI: 2.2–3.8%), knowledge (0.9%, 95% CI: 0.3–1.5) and belief (0.4%, 95% CI: 0.1–0.8) questions; behavior questions showed positive, but insignificant, lift (0.1%, 95% CI: -0.8–1.1). In the gender-stratified model, only recall (2.9%, 95% CI: 2.1–3.6) showed significant lift, but positive lift was seen in knowledge (0.7%, 95% CI: -0.2–1.5), belief (0.1%, 95% CI: -0.1–0.5), and behavior (0.2%, 95% CI: -0.1–0.4) questions. Our results suggest that social media-based health promotion campaigns may be efficient and effective tools for sharing urgent health information with global audiences, with the potential to drive social and behavior change globally during future pandemics.

Article.Title: Genetic predisposition, perceived threat and burden, and sex differences in changes in anxiety symptoms across the COVID-19 pandemic
Article.Authors: Klatzka C.; Rohm T.; Weigel Willenbockel L.; Dißelkamp C.; Spinath F.; Aldisi R.; Maj C.; Nöthen M.; Forstner A.; Mönkediek B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Several meta-analyses have shown that the COVID-19 crisis and the efforts to contain the virus have had a significant impact on mental health, leading to an increase in anxiety-related symptoms, especially in the first phase of the pandemic. The present paper aimed to investigate the development of anxiety symptoms throughout the course of the pandemic in a non-clinical sample. Using longitudinal data from the German TwinLife panel, the study investigates how stressor-related perceptions of threat and burden mediated the development of anxiety symptoms while acknowledging individuals’ genetic susceptibility to developing anxiety symptoms, as well as sex differences. The study expands the understanding of pandemic-specific processes by incorporating pre-pandemic anxiety levels. Anxiety symptoms remained remarkably stable during the pandemic in relation to pre-pandemic anxiety levels, underscoring the relevance of pre-pandemic differences in anxiety as pandemic risk factors. Genetic predispositions explained differences in initial anxiety levels and in perceived threat and burden, but not in anxiety change over time, which calls for research on the environmental factors through which these predispositions are realized. Females showed higher initial anxiety, and perceived threat and burden mediated changes in anxiety significantly only in females. Whether these sex differences in mediation reflect distinct mechanisms remains to be tested in future studies.

Article.Title: T-cell profile and Treg regulation by angiotensin II type 2 receptor in acute kidney injury in male versus female rats
Article.Authors: Faisal T.; Kulkarni K.; Zarezadehmehrizi A.; Ali R.; Rao T.; Lu X.; Mani S.; Hussain T.
Article.Abstract: Sex differences have been suggested in acute kidney injury (AKI), a condition characterized by immune cell infiltration, including T cells. We recently reported that angiotensin type 2 receptor (AT 2 R) activation reduces immune (CD45 + ), T (CD3 + ), and helper T cells (CD4 + ), while increasing anti-inflammatory Treg cells (CD4 + FoxP3 + ) during ischemia-reperfusion (IR) AKI in the kidney. To understand sex differences, male, female, and ovariectomized (OVX) Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to IR with or without the AT 2 R agonist C21. Kidneys and blood were collected three days after reperfusion. Females exhibited less tubular damage than males, which was attenuated by C21 and enhanced by ovariectomy. OVX rats showed reduced basal circulating Tregs and CD4 + AT 2 R + cells, which returned to normal post-IR. Males displayed higher basal CD45 + , CD3 + , and CD4 + cell levels compared to females; however, IR-induced increases and C21-mediated reduction in these immune cells accumulation was independent of sex. Tregs in the kidney remained higher in females, which was affected by OVX. The proportion of renal accumulation of Tregs-AT 2 R + (50% of the CD4 + ) greatly exceeds the kidney CD4 + AT 2 R + cells (~ 30% of CD4 + ). Overall, kidney injury and Tregs accumulation following IR were sex-dependent, which are influenced by ovarian hormonal status (OVX) and the AT 2 R-mediated reprotection and reduction in immune cells accumulation was an independent phenomenon.

Article.Title: Domain-specific variants reshape terpene synthase conformational dynamics and ligand binding in Coffea arabica populations from Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Dirar A.; Alghamdi B.; Ibrahim M.; Osman M.; Omar A.; Alrasheed W.; Alzahrani F.; Mohamed A.; Konozy E.
Article.Abstract: Coffea arabica is an allotetraploid crop with limited genetic diversity, while terpene synthases (TPSs) contribute to specialized metabolism, ecological adaptation, and aroma formation. Whole-genome sequencing of Saudi Arabian C. arabica identified variants in five of 69 TPS genes, including eight missense substitutions in LOC113689980 (XP_071904867.1). Their structural consequences and the influence of TPS lid architecture were investigated using molecular modeling, docking, and three independent 300-ns molecular dynamics simulations per system. p.Glu424Val in 04867_cof_E424V_FPF preserved the global protein fold but altered ligand dynamics, Mg²⁺ coordination, and long-range catalytic coupling. The eight-substitution 04867_cof_mutant_FPF construct reduced ligand RMSD relative to 04867_cof_E424V_FPF (3.162 ± 0.743 vs. 3.831 ± 0.273 Å) and partially restored residue-424 coupling with DDXXD (− 0.138 to + 0.121; WT + 0.245) and NSE/DTE (+ 0.152 to + 0.208; WT + 0.404). However, the predefined statistical criterion for compensatory epistasis was not met (BH-FDR q = 0.549), indicating directional rather than statistically supported compensation. Lid architecture produced a stronger effect: the lid-containing 09630_cof_FPF complex showed significantly lower ligand RMSD (2.910 ± 0.122 vs. 4.166 ± 0.311 Å; q = 0.011) and ligand-contact residue RMSF (0.736 ± 0.064 vs. 1.973 ± 0.158 Å; q = 0.003) than the lid-absent 07178_cof_FPF. PCA/FEL further revealed system- and replicate-dependent redistribution of conformational ensembles rather than uniform changes in global flexibility. Collectively, these findings show that naturally occurring TPS variation can remodel catalytic-site dynamics while preserving overall structural integrity, whereas lid architecture strongly influences ligand confinement. The computationally constructed multi-variant model showed directional compensation in structural and dynamical properties relative to 04867_cof_E424V_FPF; however, this trend was neither statistically supported as positive epistasis nor reflected as stable energetic compensation in the ensemble QM/MM analysis. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for future haplotype-resolved analyses and experimental validation.

Article.Title: Computational screening of pristine and metal doped coronene for limonene adsorption as a Biomarker of Chronic Kidney Disease
Article.Authors: Bagadoodh R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Limonene (LMN) is a volatile biomarker (for hepatic encephalopathy) and a relevant environmental pollutant. This study compares LMN adsorption on pristine coronene (CRN) and idealized Al- and Zn-doped derivatives using B97D/6-31G(d) and ωB97XD/6-31G(d) density functional theory. In CPCM water, the BSSE-corrected adsorption energies are − 10.59/-11.55 kcal.mol − 1 for CRN-LMN, -44.99/-43.72 kcal.mol − 1 for Al-CRN@LMN, and − 13.04/-18.67 kcal.mol − 1 for Zn-CRN@LMN (B97D/ωB97XD). Atom-referenced formation energies are positive for Al-CRN (10.232/10.495 eV) and Zn-CRN (11.341/12.486 eV), showing that formation from isolated atoms is endothermic within this definition. Mulliken and NBO natural-population analyses agree that charge flows from CRN to LMN on pristine CRN but from LMN to the metal-doped platforms. Frequency-derived adsorption free energies give room-temperature recovery times of 2.41 × 10 11 /4.53 × 10 9 s for Al-CRN@LMN and 6.74/1.89 × 10 3 s for Zn-CRN@LMN; heating to 498 K lowers these estimates to 98.1/9.10 s and 4.75 × 10 − 5 /1.38 × 10 − 3 s, respectively. A limited B97D competition screen on Al-CRN gives adsorption energies of -42.38, -23.43, -21.84, and − 19.77 kcal.mol − 1 for H 2 O, CO 2 , N 2 , and CH 4 , compared with − 44.99 kcal.mol − 1 for LMN. Thus, LMN is energetically favored over every tested interferent, supporting the predicted selectivity of Al-CRN toward LMN within the investigated molecular set. Gas-phase B97D/6-31G(d) calculations give adsorption energies of -11.39, -42.73, and − 21.38 kcal.mol − 1 for CRN-LMN, Al-CRN@LMN, and Zn-CRN-LMN, respectively, preserving Al-CRN as the strongest LMN-binding platform. Zn-CRN gives the largest dimensionless HOMO-LUMO-gap response. These results are theoretical pre-screening and require broader competitive adsorption, global structure searches, transport calculations, and experimental validation.

Article.Title: A mixed-methods evaluation of a language model-powered breast cancer note augmentation tool for patients
Article.Authors: Mannhardt N.; Bondi-Kelly E.; Lam B.; Mozannar H.; Stanwyck C.; Asiedu M.; Buendia A.; Urman T.; Riaz I.; Ricciardi C.; Agrawal M.; Ghassemi M.; Sontag D.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to make clinical notes more understandable to patients, but tools must be tested with patients pre-deployment. We developed a patient-facing tool that uses an LLM (GPT-4-031) to generate “augmentations” to notes: simplified note text, defined medical terminology, frequently asked questions, extracted key information, and to-do items. We evaluated the tool with 200 healthy female participants and 8 notes. Compared to control, participants with access to augmentations had greater self-reported confidence (2.83 ± 0.05 augmentations, 2.18 ± 0.07 control, p<0.001) and scored higher on comprehension questions (0.63 ± 0.02 augmentations, 0.54 ± 0.04 control, p<0.001). We conducted interviews with 7 participants with a history of breast cancer and their own notes who described ease of use and perceived improvements in note understanding, but also reported concerns around LLMs. Three clinicians conducted an error analysis and found most errors to be minor and related to assumed context.

Article.Title: Adipose derived small extracellular vesicles improve spermatogenesis and fertility in a mouse model of azoospermia compared with stem cell and combination therapies
Article.Authors: Mirsanei J.; Mehdizadeh M.; Sheibani M.; Ajdary M.; Simorgh S.; Govahi A.; Abroodi Z.; Shabani R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe cause of male infertility with limited treatment options. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have shown regenerative potential. However, the benefit of combining these approaches remains unclear. This study compared adipose-derived MSCs (AD-MSCs), AD-MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles (AD-MSC-sEVs), and their combination in a mouse model of NOA. AD-MSCs and AD-MSC-sEVs were isolated and characterized. Forty-two male mice were assigned to six groups: Control, Sham, NOA, GFP-ASCs, AD-MSC-sEVs, and Combination. NOA was induced with busulfan, followed by treatment with GFP-ASCs, AD-MSC-sEVs, or their combination. Sixty days after treatment, fertility, testicular histology, spermatogenesis-related gene expression, sperm parameters, reproductive hormones, and GFP tracking were evaluated. AD-MSC-sEVs were spherical, expressed CD63, TSG101, and CD81. All treated groups showed increased expression of spermatogonial stem cell markers, whereas AD-MSC-sEVs showed greatest improvements in spermatogenesis-related gene expression, hormonal profiles, sperm quality, and fertility. Although Combination group promoted regeneration, AD-MSC-sEVs showed greater efficacy under the experimental conditions of this study. No GFP-positive spermatozoa were detected, and no GFP signal was observed in F1 testes, although the absence of GFP signal does not definitively exclude germ-cell differentiation. These findings support AD-MSC-sEVs as a potential cell-free therapeutic approach for NOA.

Article.Title: Real-world feasibility of a nutritional frailty score-guided multimodal supportive care pathway in patients with digestive cancer
Article.Authors: Molina Beltran E.; Gentilhomme L.; Vedie A.; Guillemin A.; Pereira S.; Lucchi E.; Fleury A.; Moura A.; Petit De Mirbeck S.; Peignelin B.; Violle A.; Mencarelli C.; Brouillet-Benkirane Y.; Peschaud F.; Micelli-Lupinacci R.; Dussart C.; Carrouel F.; Boisson C.; Neuzillet C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Frailty, malnutrition, and sarcopenia are highly prevalent in digestive oncology and adversely affect treatment tolerance, toxicity, and survival. The integration of multimodal, multidisciplinary supportive care may mitigate these risks, but feasibility and clinical impact in routine practice remain uncertain. Methods We conducted two complementary single-center studies at a French cancer center. We developed a Nutritional Frailty Score to assess the risk of nutritional deterioration in patients receiving first-line chemotherapy for digestive cancers. ParcoursDig (NCT04478175) prospectively assessed the feasibility of systematic multimodal supportive care (dietitian, physiotherapist, palliative care) using risk stratification based on this score in patients with localized or advanced digestive cancers. PrePOP was a retrospective observational study of patients with pancreatic or esophagogastric cancers receiving perioperative chemotherapy and surgery. Outcomes included treatment completion, nutritional changes, toxicities, surgical complications, and survival. Results In ParcoursDig, only 44% of patients completed the full supportive care pathway (63% in sensitivity analysis), falling short of the predefined feasibility threshold. No significant improvements were seen in health-related quality of life or survival, highlighting real-world implementation challenges. In PrePOP, baseline malnutrition prevalence was 71% (31% severe). Malnutrition was clinically associated with higher rates of chemotherapy dose reduction but not with surgical complications or survival. Weight loss during systemic therapy was common, but early nutritional intervention appeared to prevent further deterioration for some patients. Muscle mass loss during follow-up correlated with poorer prognosis, emphasizing the need for longitudinal, muscle-specific assessment. Conclusions Low intensity interventions are not sufficient to improve patient outcomes. High-intensity modalities and individualized care trajectories with longitudinal follow-up warrant further evaluation in this population.

Article.Title: A novel 3D hyperchaotic system for secure RGB image encryption with coupled bidirectional diffusion: design, dynamical analysis, and cryptographic evaluation
Article.Authors: Naeem M.; Ullah A.; Ishaq M.; Maqbool S.; Cham A.
Article.Abstract: The development of nonlinear dynamical systems with complex chaotic behavior has attracted considerable attention for secure information processing and cryptographic applications. In this study, a three-dimensional hyperchaotic (HC-3D) system is introduced using nonlinear state coupling, sinusoidal modulation, and a modulo-one transformation to generate bounded complex dynamics. Its dynamical behavior is investigated through equilibrium analysis, bifurcation diagrams, phase portraits, Lyapunov exponent analysis, complexity evaluation, and parameter-space studies. Based on the generated chaotic sequences, an RGB image encryption scheme is developed using session-dependent spatial and channel permutations, hybrid chaotic–hash-based keystream generation, and coupled bidirectional diffusion. A cryptographic master key and a session-dependent nonce are used to derive session-specific initial conditions and encryption sequences, providing separation between encryption sessions. The security performance is evaluated using histogram analysis, information entropy, adjacent-pixel correlation, chi-square testing, NPCR, UACI, key sensitivity, wrong-key decryption, noise contamination, cropping, ciphertext perturbation, and NIST SP 800-22 statistical randomness tests. The NIST analysis is performed independently on the x -, y -, and z -components of the HC-3D sequences and on the final RGB ciphertext. The experimental results demonstrate near-uniform ciphertext distributions, entropy values close to 8 bits, low adjacent-pixel correlations, and NPCR and UACI values close to their expected ideal ranges. The proposed framework integrates the HC-3D dynamics with session-dependent permutation, keystream generation, and cross-channel diffusion to provide a unified approach for RGB image encryption.

Article.Title: Recognition of intracranial hypertension in children with craniosynostosis using handheld OCT: a diagnostic accuracy study
Article.Authors: Rufai S.; Purohit R.; Bowman R.; Gottlob I.; Bunce C.; Panteli V.; Thompson D.; Marmoy O.; Henderson R.; O’Connor J.; Thomas M.; Silva A.; James G.; Patel C.; Hayward R.; Thomas G.; Dunaway D.; Johnson D.; Proudlock F.; Lawrence T.; Jeelani N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Craniosynostosis is often associated with intracranial hypertension (IH), which can damage the brain and vision if unaddressed. This prospective, multicentre diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of handheld optical coherence tomography (OCT) in recognising IH in craniosynostosis. Handheld OCT was performed in children with craniosynostosis at the time of gold-standard overnight intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring. Mixed model regression assessed for associations with ICP. Qualitative OCT signs of IH were raised cup and rim, cup obliteration, anterior displacement of Bruch’s membrane and severe optic atrophy. Primary quantitative OCT measures were disc width, cup width, rim width, and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness (nasal/temporal). Of 37 eligible children, handheld OCT was successful in 36 (97%). Eighteen children (50%) were female. Eleven children (31%) had syndromic craniosynostosis. Median age at examination was 76 months (range 14–205 months; IQR 46–105 months). When defining IH as mean ICP ≥ 20 mmHg ± prolonged ICP spikes, qualitative OCT sensitivity was 89% (95% CI 65–99) and specificity was 63% (95% CI 38–84). Anterior displacement of Bruch’s membrane delivered 100% specificity for IH. Area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.78 (95% CI 0.67–0.89) for disc width, 0.81 (95% CI 0.71–0.91;) for rim width, and 0.74 (95% CI 0.62–0.86;) for nasal RNFL thickness; all three were significantly associated with IH ( P < 0.004, P < 0.001 and P = 0.014, respectively). In conclusion, handheld OCT can recognise IH in craniosynostosis, and could improve early intervention and clinical outcomes. ISRCTN registration ID: ISRCTN52858719.

Article.Title: Weak electromagnetic field configuration differentially shapes cellular redox and metabolic responses
Article.Authors: Thöni V.; Buchter A.; Flarer A.; Lampe L.; Schlegel C.; Zadeh-Haghighi H.; Egg M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Weak electromagnetic fields (WEMF) can modulate cellular redox biology, but whether biological outcomes are determined by field intensity alone or by field configuration remains unclear. Therapeutic nuclear magnetic resonance (tNMR) combines a low-intensity magnetic sweep field (SF) with an orthogonal radiofrequency (RF) component. Here, we separated the tNMR components and exposed NIH3T3 cells to SF, RF, or full tNMR during hypoxia. Following reoxygenation, cellular responses were analyzed using compartment-specific reactive oxygen species measurements, bioenergetic profiling, metabolite analysis, and redox-cofactor readouts. SF appeared to induce a redox-partitioned response profile marked by increased extracellular H₂O₂​ and reduced mitochondrial H₂O₂. RF produced a metabolite and redox-cofactor profile characterized by an increased calculated cytosolic NAD⁺/NADH ratio and reduced intracellular lactate. Full tNMR, in turn, was associated with a modest increase in the mitochondrial MitoSOX signal, most apparent immediately after reoxygenation, and a larger total cellular NADP(H) pool. Despite these distinct redox-metabolic profiles, the derived respiratory and glycolytic stress-test parameters remained comparable among groups. Together, these findings identify field configuration, rather than field intensity alone, as a key determinant of cellular redox and metabolic responses.

Article.Title: An artifact audit of budget-dependent LoRA rank comparisons
Article.Authors: Tang H.; Zhan J.; Feng Y.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper audits one repository-specific compute-normalization rule for LoRA rank comparison. The rule allocates optimizer updates inversely with rank, but it is an operational proxy rather than a measurement or matching of floating-point operations, accelerator time, or energy. The recovered evidence comprises 30 head-only baseline artifacts and 8 LoRA artifacts on SST-2. We add 56 controlled LoRA runs that hold the effective scaling ratio at $$\alpha /r=2$$ , separate seed from rank, retain and count the jointly trained classifier head, and record GPU runtime. On SST-2 with , the inverse 682/42/10/1-step schedule yields mean accuracies of 0.7909, 0.5700, 0.5046, and 0.4969 for ranks 2, 8, 16, and 64 across three shared seeds. With 42 updates for every rank, five-seed means instead rise with rank: 0.5422, 0.5961, 0.7211, and 0.7475. The same equal-step pattern appears with on SST-2 (0.6307, 0.7454, 0.7943, 0.8024) and with on AG News (0.5645, 0.7093, 0.7852, 0.8242), each across three shared seeds. A warmed timing benchmark gives 100.21–101.18 ms per update across ranks, showing that the extreme update schedule does not match measured runtime: its total time is dominated by the number of updates. The contribution is diagnostic rather than a broad rank recommendation. This normalization rule can make larger ranks look worse through severe undertraining, and the observed ordering is not stable when scaling, seed, and update opportunity are controlled.

Article.Title: Intelligent manufacturing system and hybrid generative-attention framework for quality prediction of high-performance aluminum alloys
Article.Authors: Xie R.; Gou Z.; Sang Y.; Liu J.; Li Z.; Zhao B.; Tan J.; Hou J.; Jia X.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: High-performance aluminum alloys are extensively used in aerospace, rail transit, and new-energy vehicles owing to their high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and formability. Meeting the stringent reliability standards in these sectors relies on the melting–casting process; however, characterized by complex multi-process coupling and small, imbalanced datasets, this process poses significant challenges for conventional modeling approaches in achieving accurate quality classification. To address these challenges, we develop a SCADA–MES integrated intelligent manufacturing data management system tailored to the full aluminum-alloy melting and casting route, providing dynamic, high-dimensional, and cross-process data support for predictive modeling. Building on this end-to-end infrastructure, we propose a deep-learning-based quality classification method that integrates Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), Self-Attention and Inter-sample Transformer (SAINT), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). CTGAN performs data augmentation by generating synthetic samples consistent with the empirical distribution under categorical and process-condition constraints, thereby alleviating the issues of data scarcity and imbalance. SAINT employs a dual-channel attention mechanism to capture nonlinear dependencies across both features and samples, while CNN extracts stable local patterns and attenuates noise. Evaluations of the algorithm’s performance in comparison with the baseline approach indicate the proposed method achieves approximately 5% improvement in all key metrics such as accuracy, macro F1 and recall, which demonstrates outstanding accuracy and stability in multi-stage quality prediction across the entire melting-casting process and thus can provide a practical pathway for data-driven quality control of high-performance aluminum alloy.

Article.Title: Association between time spent on internal medicine attending rounds and in training examination scores among resident physicians in Japan
Article.Authors: Nagasaki K.; Nishizaki Y.; Shimizu T.; Yamamoto Y.; Shikino K.; Kobayashi H.; Tokuda Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attending rounds are central to internal medicine residency, but whether spending more time on rounds improves learning remains unclear. We examined the association between weekly attending round time and in-training examination performance among postgraduate residents in Japan. This nationwide cross-sectional study included postgraduate year 1 and 2 residents who took the 2023 General Medicine In-Training Examination (GM-ITE) and completed a post-examination survey. Weekly internal medicine attending round time was categorized as none, 1–2, 3–5, 6–10, or ≥ 11 h, with 1–2 h as the reference. Mixed-effects linear regression models estimated adjusted mean differences in internal medicine domain and total GM-ITE scores. Among 6,347 residents, 44.1% reported 1–2 h of weekly attending rounds. Compared with 1–2 h, 6–10 h (adjusted mean difference, − 0.47; 95% CI − 0.77 to − 0.17) and ≥ 11 h (− 0.70; 95% CI − 1.22 to − 0.19) were associated with lower internal medicine scores. Longer bedside attending round time during general internal medicine rotations was also associated with lower scores. Longer attending round duration was not associated with better examination performance, suggesting that the educational value of rounds may not be captured by duration alone.

Article.Title: A fractional–order MRSA transmission model: theoretical analysis and screening strategy comparison
Article.Authors: Shqair M.; Almuneef A.; Qazza A.; Albdaiwi R.; Hagag A.
Article.Abstract: Hospital outbreaks of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remain difficult to contain because both patients and healthcare workers can carry and transmit the bacterium, often without symptoms. A Caputo fractional-order model is developed to capture this transmission process at hospital admission and discharge, partitioning the hospital population into uncolonized, colonized, and infected patients, uncontaminated and contaminated healthcare workers, and screened community members classified as flagged or unflagged. The framework is used to compare admission-based against discharge-based screening across several coverage levels. Before any simulation is attempted, the underlying mathematics is examined in detail: recasting the system as an equivalent Volterra integral equation shows that the total hospital census is conserved, that nonnegative initial data produce nonnegative and bounded trajectories, and that a unique solution exists for every admissible initial condition. This solution is shown to depend continuously on both the initial data and the model parameters, the Picard iteration used in its construction converges geometrically, and the system possesses at least one equilibrium state. Having established this analytical foundation, the model is integrated numerically by means of the fractional Adams–Bashforth–Moulton predictor–corrector scheme. The resulting simulations indicate that consistent hygiene and isolation practices progressively suppress transmission: colonized and infected patient numbers decline, contamination among healthcare workers peaks early before receding under sustained protocols, and isolation-unit occupancy falls as fewer patients require it. Once adopted consistently, screening at either admission or discharge stabilizes the flagged-patient population, underscoring the value of the fractional-order framework for anticipating hospital infection trends.

Article.Title: Attention enhanced edge vision measurement for real time pantograph catenary arc monitoring
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Li W.; Shu T.; Chen S.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Reliable pantograph-catenary arc (PCA) monitoring is important for high-speed railway power-supply safety, but field visual measurement is challenged by small arc regions, transient and irregular morphology, intense halos, and background highlights caused by tunnels, stations, rain, snow, and strong sunlight. This paper proposes ACE-PCANet, an attention-enhanced edge vision measurement framework for real-time PCA event localization. In the proposed measurement chain, the onboard visible-light sensor provides image observations, ACE-PCANet performs measurement-oriented data processing, and the output is an arc event indication with a bounding-box location referenced to manual annotations. The framework integrates three task-oriented modifications into a one-stage detector. First, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) reweights channel and spatial features to address high-luminance background interference while retaining arc-related features. Second, a Coordinate Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) is introduced in the neck to fuse low- and high-level features with position-aware attention, providing position-sensitive contextual information for feature fusion. Third, Efficient IoU (EIoU) improves bounding-box regression for arc targets with highly variable aspect ratios. Experiments on 5,625 field images collected under four operating scenarios show that ACE-PCANet achieves 94.1% precision, 92.7% recall, and 91.5% mAP@0.5. Scenario-wise tests further indicate improved robustness under strong light, tunnel, and rain/snow/fog conditions. A lightweight variant, ACE-PCANet-lite, is deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin using TensorRT INT8 acceleration and reaches 89.2% mAP@0.5 and 91.19% F1 after quantization, with 68 FPS, 14.7 ms per-frame latency, and 15.2 W measured system power. The reported results characterize the data-processing accuracy, robustness, and edge-instrument feasibility of the visual measurement framework; they are not intended as a formal metrological uncertainty budget.

Article.Title: A temporal graph transformer neural network for clustering influential control nodes in the controllability processes on of social internet of things networks
Article.Authors: Su Z.; Xiu Y.; Liu X.; Arebi P.
Article.Abstract: The controllability of Social Internet of Things (SIoT) networks becomes particularly challenging when the network topology evolves over time and relationships span multiple layers, including user-to-user, object-to-object, and cross user-object interactions. In this paper, we introduce a novel learning-based framework called the Temporal Graph Transformer Neural Network for Clustering the Influential Nodes (TGCIN), which reformulates the identification of influential control nodes as an unsupervised node clustering problem on a temporal SIoT network. Our approach integrates relation-aware spatial attention to capture structural dependencies within each time snapshot, and a GRU-based temporal encoder combined with self-attention to model how node influence evolves across consecutive time steps. A controllability-informed scoring function is then introduced, which fuses structural driver ranks derived from maximum matching, multi-relational degree centrality, and a temporal stability index computed from embedding trajectory variance. These enriched representations are finally fed into a centroid-based clustering module that partitions nodes into three distinct control roles: critical drivers, bridging relays, and peripheral nodes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing approaches, achieving an average accuracy of approximately 91% and an average F1-score of around 92% across all tested scenarios. Beyond raw performance, the model converges faster than competing methods, maintains competitive runtime even on large-scale graphs, and produces interpretable cluster distributions where critical nodes are few but precisely identified, bridging nodes form a clear intermediate group, and peripheral nodes make up the majority without swallowing higher-impact nodes.

Article.Title: Transformer-based multimodal representation learning for blind acoustic classification
Article.Authors: Tan X.; Yiu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Context recognition and rare event classification in unlabeled audio represent critical challenges in both academic and industrial domains. These technologies hold significant potential for applications such as IoT-based predictive maintenance, surveillance systems (e.g., crime scene analysis or aviation incident investigations), and urban management (e.g., traffic monitoring). While recent research predominantly focuses on supervised methods using labeled datasets, unsupervised approaches remain constrained by limitations in accuracy and stability. This paper introduces a novel AI framework that synergizes a self-supervised audio representation model with a knowledge-enhanced language model to sequentially classify environmental sound types and rare events in unlabeled audio. Our methodology leverages an enhanced Masked Modeling Duo (M2D) —pretrained on datasets including FSD50K, ESC-50, and UrbanSound8K—to process mixed audio inputs, generate discriminative sound labels, and classify unlabeled data. The MPNet-base-v2 then analyzes these labels, establishing semantic relationships to infer environmental context and rare event categories. When evaluated on the TUT-SED dataset (DCASE 2017 Task 2), the framework achieves F-scores of 96% (baby cry) , 98% (glass break) , and 91% (gunshot) for acoustic event detection and classification. For blind environmental classification (DCASE 2017 Task 1), the accuracy of the top five predictions is 95%, and that of the top one prediction is 87%. Although memory constraints may impact classification quality when processing long-duration audio recordings, robustness tests demonstrate resilience to noise. Event classification maintains stable performance at a 0.1 SNR (-10 dB) , with average F-scores of 95% for baby cry , 97% for glass break , and 85% for gunshot . The scene classification accuracy also decreases modestly, reaching 89% at an SNR of -10 dB, but remains comparable to that under noise-free conditions. An extended methodology application to additional datasets—specifically, DESED 2019 for multiple acoustic event classification (MAEC) and TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2020 Mobile for acoustic scene classification (ASC)—further substantiated the algorithmic generalization capability across diverse acoustic contexts. Such a capability can be used for more downstream environmental sound studies, e.g., sound separations. The implementation is publicly accessible on GitHub: https://github.com/sharontan6217/TMRL.

Article.Title: Improved YOLOv7-based surface defect detection method incorporating feature retention and densely-scale spatial attention mechanisms
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Ko C.; Chang Y.; Chang H.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to automated defect detection. However, the feature information of small defects is easily lost during feature extraction, and as the network deepens, the increased computational burden and the insufficient utilization of existing features also affect detection performance. In addition, when the model is trained using stochastic gradient descent (SGD), it may converge to a local optimum, which limits its detection performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a method based on YOLOv7-tiny that integrates feature retaining blocks (FRBs) and densely-scale spatial attention (DSSA) blocks into the backbone network and incorporates a cosine annealing (CA) learning rate schedule during training. The proposed method, termed Cosine Annealing Learning Rate Scheduled YOLOv7 with Densely-Scale Spatial Attention and Feature Retaining Block (CA-YOLOv7-DF), is applied to surface defect detection. Experiments were conducted on the public NEU-DET dataset, and the components were analyzed through gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), confusion matrices, and training convergence analysis. Under a unified training protocol with three random seeds, CA-YOLOv7-DF achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 71.9 ± 1.2%, compared with 70.9 ± 1.0% for YOLOv7-tiny; the FRBs provided the largest average gain, whereas the effects of the DSSA blocks and the CA schedule were within the run-to-run variation. Moreover, the proposed method achieves a detection speed of 11.6 frames per second (FPS) on the Jetson Nano embedded device, which makes it applicable to low- to moderate-speed or sampling inspection. On the GC10-DET dataset, the method did not improve on YOLOv7-tiny, indicating that its benefit depends on defect scale and the amount of training data.
Article.Topic: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Asymmetric visible-infrared cross-fusion for robust bolt localization and missing detection
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Chen X.; Xie K.; Sang J.; Wen C.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and reliable detection of missing bolts remains challenging under exposure anomalies, low illumination, and cluttered backgrounds. Visible images are sensitive to illumination changes and may lose texture and detail, whereas infrared images are more illumination-robust but lack the detail and resolution required for accurate standalone detection. Existing general multimodal fusion models are primarily designed for universal detection scenarios, which fail to adapt to the unique feature distribution characteristics of bolt targets with weak textures and easily degraded deep features. Such methods cannot effectively extract critical fine-grained target features, leading to prominent performance limitations in industrial bolt detection tasks. To address these complementary limitations of dual-modal data and the drawbacks of existing fusion methods, we propose Dual-modal Asymmetric Cross-Fusion YOLO (DACF-YOLO), a lightweight network for bolt localization and missing detection. Modality-specific asymmetric branches and bidirectional shallow high-frequency feature injection exploit cross-modal complementarity and compensate for information loss. A Shallow Feature Screening and Enhancement module suppresses redundant texture noise and background interference, improving early feature quality. A Cross-Modal Guided Fusion mechanism dynamically assigns weights according to modality-specific feature quality, enabling adaptive complementary enhancement. A parameter-shared Lightweight Detail-Enhanced Detection Head preserves critical bolt textures and contours while reducing model complexity. Experiments on a registered visible-infrared bolt dataset show that DACF-YOLO achieves 95.3% mAP50 and 63.2% mAP50-95 with 3.28 M parameters and 9.7 GFLOPs, demonstrating a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational cost under challenging industrial conditions.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: lightweight object detection; illumination robustness; YOLO

Article.Title: Prediction of the maximum available traction boundary for HST-based agricultural tractors
Article.Authors: Ahn H.; An S.; Choi C.; Kim S.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: The traction force of an agricultural tractor with a hydrostatic transmission (HST) is governed jointly by the engine, the hydrostatic unit (HSU) and the gearbox; when these are not matched, part of the engine power cannot be converted into traction within the working speed range. This study proposes a method for determining the boundary of the traction available from an HST-based tractor at the component-matching stage. The boundary was constructed from four limits: the engine power and torque-rise characteristics, the maximum allowable pressure of the HSU with its experimentally measured efficiency map, the gearbox ratios, and tire slip. The workable area was derived for three gear ranges of a 43.3 kW tractor, selected so that the governing limit differed between cases, and verified by measuring the traction force during plowing with a six-component load cell. Where each limit governed, the measured traction force reached 86–96% of the predicted boundary on average and exceeded it only transiently, whereas the predicted vehicle speed deviated by up to 22.7% at high HSU pressure owing to a pressure-dependent loss of volumetric efficiency that a single coefficient corrected. The method allows the engine, HSU and gearbox to be matched to a target traction force.

Article.Title: Horizon-dependent level–shape decomposition for multihorizon ERA5-Land temperature-field forecasting in the Lanzhou–Xining region
Article.Authors: Wang X.; He A.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate monthly reanalysis temperature-field forecasts must recover both regional displacement and the spatial organization of anomalies, particularly when a region changes thermal state. We developed RegimeTransfer-DCSF (Deep–Causal Shape Fusion), a multihorizon framework that separates a forecast-causal regional level from median-centred spatial shape, learns short-lead shape through a compact fine–coarse attention hierarchy, and transfers shape responsibility from the deep branch to a stable anchor as lead increases. Using 12-month histories of 12 ERA5-Land variables, the model directly forecast future ERA5-Land 2-m air temperature at one-, three-, and six-month leads (h1, h3, and h6) over 39 county-level administrative units of the Lanzhou–Xining urban agglomeration. Within two rolling-origin validation folds, 114 horizon-specific cases yielded 114,114 county-domain grid-cell predictions. The selected DCSF fit achieved a pooled MAE of 1.131°C, a root-mean-square error of 1.494°C, and an R² of 0.9767, with 83.68% of absolute errors within 2°C; a fold-wise two-refit county ensemble retained a pooled MAE of 1.135°C. Averaged across the 114 county-area-weighted cases, the selected fit reduced MAE by 9.95% relative to seasonal climatology and by 20.35% relative to TimeFilter. On the complete 3,655-cell support, the four-refit DCSF mean ranked first in the ten-method rolling-validation benchmark at 1.174°C, with an across-refit standard deviation of 0.0024°C. During 25 h1 thermal-state changes, DCSF reduced area-weighted MAE by 0.301°C (19.79%) relative to TimeFilter, with a fold-stratified three-month moving-block bootstrap interval of 0.073–0.526°C. In a separate retrospective ERA5-Land analysis, annual mean warm-area fraction increased by 9.29 percentage points per decade during 2000–2024; the autocorrelation-aware three-year block interval was 2.72–15.52 percentage points per decade. Six of the 48 validation target months met the widespread-warm definition and formed highly connected warm footprints. Within this rolling-validation task, explicit level–shape responsibility delivered high absolute field accuracy and its clearest short-lead value during thermal-state changes.

Article.Title: Novel formula for improving the oral bioavailability of paclitaxel using P-glycoprotein inhibitors
Article.Authors: Gupta A.; Kunkalienkar S.; Saha M.; Rajora A.; Soman S.; Marwaha D.; Moorkoth S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Paclitaxel (PCL), a taxane derivative with potent antimitotic properties, is ubiquitously utilized as a remedy for various cancers. PCL’s therapeutic utility via the oral route is limited by poor water solubility and low permeability, resulting in inadequate bioavailability. This limitation restricts the development of effective oral formulations, particularly for conditions such as gastric cancer. The current research aimed to evaluate the effects of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors, specifically piperine (PIP) and silibinin (SBN), on the pharmacokinetic parameters of orally administered PCL. An in-silico drug-protein docking study was performed to evaluate interactions between PCL and selected P-gp inhibitors. PCL was administered orally at a dose of 40 mg/kg, either as a single treatment or in combination with PIP or SBN at 10, 20, and 40 mg/kg. Plasma samples were obtained at predetermined sampling intervals, followed by Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis using an H-ESI source. Compared with PCL administered alone, combination treatment significantly enhanced key pharmacokinetic indices, including peak plasma concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration–time curve (AUC). After administration of PCL with 10 mg/kg of PIP 1.67 and 1.09 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, 20 mg/kg of PIP 1.79 and 1.16 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, and 40 mg/kg of PIP 2.04 and 1.51 fold increases in Cmax and AUC. After administration of PCL with 10 mg/kg of SBN 1.36 and 1.03 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, 20 mg/kg of SBN 1.73 and 1.69 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, and 40 mg/kg of SBN 2.29 and 2.22 fold increases in Cmax and AUC. Additionally, the elimination half-life (t1/2) of PCL was extended, indicating prolonged persistence of the drug in circulation. It can thus be concluded that PCL, along with PIP or SBN, exhibits increased absorption through P-gp modulation. These findings emphasise the promising potential of incorporating such bioenhancers into the development of effective oral PCL formulations to improve cancer therapy. An AGREE score (0.69) indicates the eco-friendliness of the bioanalytical method.

Article.Title: Exploring the sustainable scaling of AI dilemma: a projective study of corporations’ AI environmental impacts
Article.Authors: Desroches C.; Chauvin M.; Ladan L.; Vateau C.; Gosset S.; Cordier P.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), raises environmental concerns extending beyond greenhouse gas emissions. Limited transparency from major providers hinders companies’ ability to evaluate their AI-related environmental impacts and achieve their net-zero targets. This paper proposes a methodology to estimate the environmental impact of a company’s AI portfolio, delivering actionable insights without requiring deep AI or Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) expertise. Using a modeling approach that incorporates increased AI usage, hardware efficiency, and electricity mix changes aligned with IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) scenarios, we forecast AI impacts through 2030. Under a high adoption scenario, driven by complex generative AI models and frameworks, AI electricity consumption could rise by a factor of 24.4. Mitigating this impact by 2030 demands coordinated efforts across the AI value chain. Isolated measures like hardware or model efficiency alone are insufficient. We call for standardized environmental assessment frameworks, increased transparency, and a “Return on Environment” metric to align AI development with sustainability goals.

Article.Title: Rigosertib promotes expression of the antimicrobial peptide beta-defensin-3 in human cells
Article.Authors: Wozniak W.; Sagnat D.; Dautreppe R.; Bourumeau W.; Khazaal S.; Kurowska A.; Bournet B.; Buscail L.; Buscail E.; Le Cosquer G.; Alric L.; Navarro L.; Vergnolle N.; Sperandio B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial defense in the human gut relies on innate immune recognition of microbes via pattern recognition receptors, triggering antimicrobial peptide (AMP) expression and immune cell recruitment. Among AMPs, beta-defensins are crucial defense effectors, exhibiting broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and immunomodulatory functions. Their inducible expression makes them attractive targets for therapeutic modulation, particularly given the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. Through the evaluation of clinically approved or investigational compounds, we identified the multi-kinase inhibitor Rigosertib as an inducer of the human beta-defensin-3 (HBD3) in colon epithelial cell lines and in organoids. Notably, Rigosertib robustly induced HBD3 even at the lowest concentration tested in vitro, whereas proinflammatory cytokine expression increased only at the highest concentration and to a substantially lesser extent. Mechanistically, Rigosertib-triggered induction of HBD3 expression was found to be primarily dependent on the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and downstream P38 pathway, with ERK1/2 and JNK contributing to a lesser extent. Functionally, Rigosertib enhanced the antimicrobial activity of colon-derived cells and organoids against intestinal bacterial pathogens. Moreover, Rigosertib induced AMP expression in a range of non-intestinal cells from different tissues, including hepatic cells. Collectively, these findings support the potential of Rigosertib to enhance endogenous antimicrobial defense while limiting excessive and potentially detrimental inflammatory responses.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning for postoperative atrial fibrillation after noncardiac surgery
Article.Authors: Zhu S.; Gao Y.; Li L.; Wang P.; Zhang C.; Li Y.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is an important complication after non-cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Accurate perioperative risk stratification remains challenging because POAF risk reflects both baseline atrial substrate and dynamic perioperative physiologic stress. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the INSPIRE perioperative database to develop interpretable prediction models for clinically documented postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after non-cardiac surgery. POAF was defined as new-onset AF captured during the index hospitalization by electrocardiography or rhythm-monitoring documentation; because a uniform cohort-wide measure of monitoring intensity was not available, the endpoint was interpreted as clinically detected POAF. Candidate predictors were grouped by acquisition window into preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative (≤ 24 h) variables to support dynamic perioperative risk assessment rather than a purely preoperative screen. Feature selection was performed with Boruta, model explanation with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and classifier comparison with LASSO logistic regression, AdaBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Because POAF was uncommon, performance was evaluated with AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and F1 score after stratified splitting and threshold evaluation; synthetic resampling was not used in the primary analysis. Among 99,887 patients, 1,058 (1.1%) developed clinically documented POAF. Compared with controls, POAF cases were older (median 70 vs. 55 years) and showed substantially greater burdens of hypotension and hypoxemia, including more frequent and prolonged MAP < 65 mmHg and SpO₂ <90%. Boruta retained average diastolic blood pressure, average heart rate, and left atrial enlargement as informative features. SHAP identified valvular disease, surgical duration, cardiopulmonary instability, and related early postoperative events as major contributors, consistent with a dynamic perioperative risk model. Discrimination was good across classifiers, with AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.85. AdaBoost and CatBoost achieved the best overall performance (both AUC 0.85), while CatBoost showed higher specificity and PPV. In a large non-cardiac surgical cohort, clinically documented POAF was associated with both baseline atrial substrate and perioperative cardiopulmonary stress. Interpretable ML models, particularly boosting-based methods, showed good discrimination and may support dynamic perioperative risk updating and targeted postoperative surveillance, although monitoring heterogeneity, class imbalance, calibration, and external validation remain important considerations.

Article.Title: Proposal for new cut-off points for vital signs used to identify at-risk patients over 65 years old in Emergency Departments
Article.Authors: Pérez-Valencia D.; Barrio I.; del Castillo J.; Fernández-Alonso C.; Miró O.; Larrea N.; Legarreta M.; García-Gutiérrez S.; N/A N/A.; Lamberechts J.; Villalibre A.; Lobé S.; García L.; Blázquez B.; Molina E.; Cuchillo J.; Rebollal M.; del Rio J.; Izquierdo S.; Arrizabalaga O.; Arretxaga Z.; Cantón E.; Bello M.; Perestelo L.; Cabrera C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency Department (ED) overcrowding and non-age-adapted triage criteria increase the risk of delayed recognition of critical conditions in older adults, who face higher morbidity, atypical presentations, and poorer short-term outcomes. We conducted a retrospective multicentre cohort study including 23,278 ED visits (patients ≥ 65 years) from 52 Spanish hospitals, drawn from the EDEN (Emergency Department and Elder Needs) cohort. Triage-recorded vital signs were analysed regarding mortality or Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission within 72 h. Candidate optimal cut-offs were estimated using the BackAddFor algorithm within univariate logistic generalized additive models (GAMs). Thresholds were selected to maximise the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). External validation was performed in an independent cohort. Cut-offs were proposed for five vital signs: systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 115 and 185 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure (DBP) at 97 mmHg, respiratory rate (RR) at 15 and 21 bpm, heart rate (HR) at 45 and 105 bpm, and oxygen saturation (SatO2) at 92%. Compared with conventional values, these adapted cut-offs classified as alarm a greater proportion of patients at risk who would not have been classified as high priority according to traditional criteria: 66.1% for RR, 28.2% for SBP, 14.8% for HR, 8.6% for SatO2, and 6.6% for DBP. Findings support the identification of candidate age-adapted thresholds for older ED patients and motivate future predictive models incorporating vital sign interactions to enhance early warning systems in EDs.

Article.Title: Inflammatory biomarker profiles and their associations with Nordic dietary habits and metabolic outcomes in adults affected by MAFLD
Article.Authors: El-Sehrawy A.; Kandil I.; ELmazny G.; Salah A.; Abohassan M.; Alanazi M.; Elzayyadi I.; Ibrahim R.; Gameil M.; Hamed M.; Rozaik S.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is commonly accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation. The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) is an accessible inflammatory marker, while the Healthy Nordic diet may have favorable metabolic effects. This study investigated relationships among AISI, healthy Nordic Food Index (HNDI), and metabolic health in adults with MAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 253 adults with MAFLD were evaluated. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire and HNFI using a composite score. Anthropometric, biochemical, and hematological variables were assessed. Participants were categorized into AISI quartiles. Mean age was 40.27 ± 8.37 years. Higher AISI was associated with higher triglycerides (adjusted P = 0.031) and lower HDL-cholesterol (adjusted P = 0.004). AISI was positively associated with white blood cell count (β = 0.453, P < 0.001) and MCH (β = 0.191, P = 0.005), and was inversely associated with HDL-cholesterol (β=−0.250, P < 0.001). Higher AISI was associated with lower apple/pear intake (adjusted P = 0.034) and root vegetable intake (P-trend = 0.029). The HNFI score (β=−0.149, P = 0.020) and root vegetable intake (β=−0.154, P = 0.016) were independently associated with lower AISI. Higher AISI was associated with an unfavorable lipid and inflammatory profile and lower adherence to the HNFI. Greater Nordic diet adherence and root vegetable intake were independently associated with lower AISI. Causal relationships cannot be inferred.

Article.Title: Phytotoxicity and germination responses of Zea mays L. to anaerobically digested liquid biofertilizers derived from cattle manure and fish-processing sludge
Article.Authors: Linares-Nima L.; Huaytalla-Galindo B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Valorization of cattle manure and fish-processing sludge as liquid biofertilizers may contribute to waste valorization and potential agricultural reuse within a circular bioeconomy. This study evaluated four formulations (GC, T1, T2, and T3) produced in three biodigesters per formulation and anaerobically digested for 15 weeks. The three biodigesters within each formulation were pooled before preparation of the 5, 10, and 100% (v/v) bioassay dilution levels. Distilled water was retained as an external reference and excluded from factorial inference. Final formulation-level composite samples showed near-neutral pH and formulation-specific nutrient profiles; the measured nitrogen concentration in the analyzed liquid fraction was higher at the final sampling point in all four composite samples, whereas P, K, organic matter, and C/N ratio showed formulation-specific variations. Most final microbiological determinations were lower than their corresponding initial measurements, although variability remained in some T2 and T3 determinations. In Zea mays L. bioassays, germination percentage and germination rate showed significant formulation × dilution-level interactions ( p = 0.0065 and p = 0.015, respectively). Root length differed significantly by formulation ( p = 0.0145) and dilution level ( p = 0.0013), without a significant interaction. The germination index (GI), used as a phytotoxicity indicator, was evaluated descriptively; T2 maintained GI > 1 and comparatively high root length across all evaluated dilution levels, whereas T1 and T3 showed lower GI and root-length responses at 100%. Overall, responses were formulation- and dilution-level dependent, supporting soil-based validation of selected combinations before field recommendation. Because biodigesters were pooled at the formulation level before downstream analyses, these findings characterize the specific composite samples tested and do not represent independent reactor-level replication.

Article.Title: Combining rather than selecting multi-horizon forecasting of an agricultural commodity price index
Article.Authors: Malla S.
Article.Abstract: Wholesale food prices in emerging economies move sharply, with direct consequences for farm incomes and food security. Individual commodity series are short, gap-ridden and shock-dominated, so this study forecasts a composite instead: the Agricultural Commodity Price Index, an inverse-volatility weighted aggregate of 135 daily wholesale series from Nepal’s Kalimati market, 2013–2023, with 55 strictly causal predictors including Nepali festival windows. Twelve architectures spanning penalised linear models, tree ensembles, recurrent networks and direct neural forecasters are compared under a protocol that fits on 2013–2020, chooses every configuration on 2021 to mid-2022 by blocked cross-validation, and reads July 2022 to September 2023 only for reporting. A shrunk combination improves on the model that validation would have selected by 1.3, 1.5, 2.0 and 11.2 %, and on a no-change benchmark by 2.1, 3.2, 7.8 and 22.2 %. The models that proved best on the test window ranked third, seventh, fifth and fourth on validation, so none could have been chosen in advance. A supporting result explains why these models work at all: the recursive, level-target strategy common in this literature caps tree ensembles at their training range and compounds recurrent error, and a direct change target reduces error by 33-53 %.

Article.Title: Dingxiang Guanshitong suppresses ESCC progression by modulating TAK1/NF-κB/GLUT1-associated glycolytic reprogramming
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Wang S.; Li J.; Sun X.; Chen X.; Zheng Y.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive tumor with poor clinical outcomes and limited treatment options. Dingxiang Guanshitong (DGST), a traditional Chinese herbal formulation, has shown potential activity in ESCC, but its molecular mechanisms require further clarification. The current study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic impact and underlying biological actions of DGST on ESCC. Network pharmacology was used to identify candidate DGST constituents and targets, followed by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. Antitumor effects of DGST was examined in a 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (4NQO)-induced ESCC mouse model using H&E staining, immunohistochemistry, TUNEL assay, and flow cytometry. Proteomics analysis identified differentially expressed proteins and enriched pathways. In TE-1 cells, TAK1 knockdown/overexpression stable lines were constructed by lentiviral transduction, and pathway involvement was evaluated using immunofluorescence, luciferase reporter assays, CCK-8, Transwell, scratch assays, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and metabolic indicator assays. DGST showed dose-associated suppression of ESCC tumor progression, cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while promoting apoptosis. Proteomics suggested that DGST affected glycolysis and NF-κB-related pathways. DGST treatment was associated with reduced phosphorylation of TAK1, IκBα, and p65, lower GLUT1, HK2, PFKP, and LDHA expression, decreased ATP levels, and increased MPC1 as well as mitochondrial complex indicators. TAK1 knockdown enhanced the effects of DGST, whereas its overexpression reversed these effects. DGST may inhibit ESCC progression by modulating TAK1/NF-κB/GLUT1 axis-mediated glycolytic reprogramming. The findings elucidate the potential therapeutic value of DGST in the treatment of ESCC and provide mechanistic insights for its clinical application.

Article.Title: Inverse-distance weighting alignment-diversity attention transformer for days ahead particulate matter concentration forecasting
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Loskot P.; Lin Y.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An accurate forecasting of the particulate matter (PM) concentrations including PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations is vital for the publichealth and the environment management. Forecasting highly non-stationary PM time series is challenging due to their complex spatialand temporal dependencies and irregular local correlations. In this paper, an adaptive Inverse-Distance Weighting (IDW) iTransformer-based framework referred to as IDW-ADAFormer is devised for the medium-term joint forecasting of spatially distributed multi-sensorPM data. In particular, the adaptive IDW decomposition first separates the spatial trends from the local temporal variations. The components are aligned by a newly constructed kernel-based alignment diversity attention (ADA) module. The aligned components andthe raw input data are then adaptively fused using learnable weights. The model training minimizes a newly constructed multi-objectiveAQI-aware loss function, which accounts for the prediction accuracy, the trend preservation, and the alignment with the Air-QualityIndicator (AQI) levels. The numerical experiments were performed for a public dataset of hourly PM2.5 and PM10 data. Assuming oneto three days ahead predictions, the proposed IDW-ADAFormer was found to consistently outperform other existing methods, whilemaintaining the interpretability of an iTransformer.

Article.Title: Multi-window HRV and temporal context for sleep staging from ECG and smartwatch PPG-derived intervals
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Peng Y.; Li J.; Zhang Z.; Cao C.; Chai Y.; Cai Z.; Zou Y.; Yan Z.; Tao Z.
Article.Abstract: Sleep staging is essential for evaluating sleep quality, yet conventional polysomnography is costly, intrusive, and difficult to deploy in everyday settings. This study presents an HRV-centered sleep-staging framework for ECG-derived RR intervals and smartwatch PPG-derived IBI sequences. Rather than introducing a new Transformer architecture, the study systematically evaluates multi-window HRV representation and sleep-progress context for four-class sleep staging, while examining demographic information and feature-interaction strategies as auxiliary components. The framework extracts time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features from multiple temporal windows, combines them primarily with sleep-progress context while optionally incorporating demographic context, and uses a lightweight Transformer encoder as a temporal integration module for classifying Wake, Light sleep, Deep sleep, and REM sleep. In the final baseline comparison, the proposed configuration achieved accuracies and Cohen’s Kappa coefficients of 0.6988/0.5326 on the SHHS 1000 subset, 0.6958/0.4830 on Huami ECG, and 0.6915/0.4615 in the Huami smartwatch PPG setting. Ablation analyses showed that multi-window HRV representation and temporal sleep-progress information provided the most consistent contributions, whereas demographic variables and feature-interaction strategies had auxiliary and dataset-dependent effects. For practical interpretation, configurations without the future-context 300-s feature are considered the relevant setting because they exclude explicitly post-epoch information, whereas configurations containing this feature are treated only as offline retrospective analyses. Further validation across independent datasets, wearable devices, prospective deployment settings, and external PPG interval-estimation pipelines is needed before broader real-world use.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal variation of gravity field and inter-seismic correlation analysis of the 2021 Maduo and 2022 Menyuan earthquakes
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Zhu Y.; Zhao Y.; Wei S.; Lv H.; Cao C.
Article.Abstract: The spatiotemporal evolution of the gravity field is a comprehensive response to deep crustal material migration and tectonic deformation processes, and contains key precursory information for the seismogenic stage of earthquakes. Based on mobile gravity observation data collected in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2015 to 2021, this study obtained multi-spatiotemporal-scale gravity field changes before and after the earthquakes through classical adjustment. In light of the regional tectonic framework and deep dynamic background, we systematically analyzed, from a gravity perspective, the relationship between the spatiotemporal dynamic gravity changes and the preparation and occurrence of the 2021 Maduo M S 7.4 earthquake and the 2022 Menyuan M S 6.9 earthquake, and explored the possible association between the two earthquakes. The main findings are as follows: (1) The significant gravity changes observed before the 2021 Maduo M S 7.4 earthquake and the 2022 Menyuan M S 6.9 earthquake are closely related to regional tectonic activity, and these changes may have mainly originated from deep crustal material adjustment and migration processes. (2) The pattern of gravity changes in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau has a clear spatial correspondence with the locations of strong earthquakes. Both the Maduo and Menyuan earthquakes occurred near the turning points of gravity high-gradient zones and around the centers of the four-quadrant pattern. (3) The gravity changes in the Menyuan seismic region were significantly enhanced following the Maduo earthquake, We inferred that the Maduo earthquake may have caused some perturbation to the tectonic stress state in the Menyuan region, indirectly influencing the occurrence of the subsequent Menyuan earthquake. (4) The gravity change maps show that the gravity anomaly areas and gravity gradient zones before the Maduo and Menyuan earthquakes are highly correlated, possibly implying a close relationship between the two events in terms of deep-seated tectonic processes.

Article.Title: Application of the rigid finite element method to modeling multibody systems with redundant constraints
Article.Authors: Tański M.; Wojtyra M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The research aimed to investigate the applicability of the Rigid Finite Element Method (Rigid-FEM), which is an alternative to the classical Finite Element Method, for modeling multibody systems with redundant constraints. The investigation focused on resolving problems with determining reaction forces. Such problems are encountered in classical rigid multibody dynamics formulations. The methods used include the development of an underlying theory, diverse simulations, and experimental verification. Specifically, the theoretical foundation of the Rigid-FEM method—discretizing rigid bodies into smaller rigid finite elements interconnected by spring-damper elements (SDEs) with appropriately defined stiffness and damping properties—was supplemented by proposed methodological modifications that significantly reduce the number of required SDEs and improve computational efficiency. To perform a variety of tests, a spatial parallelogram benchmark mechanism was used. Results from both Rigid-FEM and classic FEM models were analyzed. A comprehensive parametric study was conducted to assess the influence of selected modeling parameters on accuracy and computational efficiency, including the placement of elastic elements, discretization density, and the introduction of a shear coefficient. Ultimately, the simulation results were compared with experimental data obtained from measurements conducted on a hardware mechanism. The findings demonstrate that the modified Rigid-FEM achieves accuracy comparable to the regular FEM model, yet requires significantly fewer elements and delivers results in substantially reduced computational time. Although the Rigid-FEM is limited to plate- and beam-like structures, these components constitute the primary structural elements of many mechanisms, such as parallel robots, where constraint redundancy is frequent and renders classical rigid multibody dynamics formulations incapable of determining reaction forces. The results, validated against experimental data, confirm the suitability of Rigid-FEM as a highly efficient and accurate computational tool for analyzing overconstrained multibody systems.

Article.Title: Sustainable bioactive membranes based on κ-carrageenan and açaí seed extract for potential topical application
Article.Authors: dos Santos É.; de Souza Pagani L.; Dotoli G.; de Andrade G.; da Silva Pinhal M.; Cogo-Müller K.; Rosa P.; Paiva-Santos A.; Fardim P.; Mazzola P.
Article.Abstract: Açaí ( Euterpe oleracea Mart.), an Amazonian fruit widely exported worldwide, generates seeds corresponding to approximately 85% of the fruit weight, which are commonly discarded despite their valorization potential. In this study, κ-carrageenan bioactive membranes containing açaí seed extract were developed and characterized as candidate materials for topical applications. The açaí seed extract showed antioxidant capacity in chemical assays, with a DPPH radical-scavenging activity of 95.75 ± 0.75% at 10 mg/mL and an EC₅₀ of 7.78 ± 0.41 mg/mL, while ferric reducing capacity was 0.19 ± 0.02 mg GAE/g (EC₅₀ = 1.49 ± 0.01 mg/mL). The açaí seed extract showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 3.13 mg/mL. HPLC analysis confirmed the presence of catechin (0.03 mg/mL) and epicatechin (0.01 mg/mL). Membranes were prepared and mechanical analysis showed tensile strength of 3.63 ± 0.34 MPa and elongation at break of 35.97 ± 2.19%. Adhesion force was 26.35 ± 5.53 g and the membranes remained structurally intact for up to 7 days under the evaluated PBS conditions. FTIR analysis showed preservation of the characteristic functional groups of κ-carrageenan after extract incorporation, while SEM revealed increased structural heterogeneity in the açaí membrane. Cytotoxicity assays demonstrated that the extract and membranes were non-cytotoxic at most tested concentrations. The membranes exhibited water vapor permeability of 1.05 ± 0.75 g·mm/kPa·day·m² and swelling capacity of 0.42 ± 0.08 g/g. Overall, the developed membrane showed promising potential as a sustainable platform for topical applications, although further biological studies are required to establish its antimicrobial performance and wound-healing potential.

Article.Title: Little effect of further aging on soil-weathered plastics
Article.Authors: Forsyth H.; Gnoffo C.; Stoll R.; van der Zee M.; Frache A.; Bigalke M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plastic waste accumulates in soils, impacting structure, biota, and ecosystem functioning. Understanding the persistence and aging of plastics in soil is therefore important. However, aging occurs over timescales which cannot be covered in conventional experiments. Many studies therefore focus on simulated weathering of pristine polymers over short timescales, but these experiments do not consider potentially different aging behaviour after extended environmental exposure. To address this, we investigated the continued aging of naturally weathered macroplastics sampled from agricultural soils by reburying them under field conditions for 19 months and comparing properties before and after. Samples of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, and polyethylene terepthalate were analysed for chemical structure, surface oxidation (carbonyl index), crystallinity, molecular weight, thermal stability, and surface morphology. All samples showed signs of oxidative aging and aging-related surface alterations before and after reburial. After reburial, most samples had little to no change in carbonyl index, with several showing significant decreases, likely due to loss of highly oxidised surface layers through fragmentation. Crystallinity, thermal stability, and molecular weight remained largely unchanged. Overall, our results suggest that the further aging of weathered polymers does not follow the same trajectory as the initial aging and that conventional plastics degrade very slowly in soil.

Article.Title: A self-healing secure group communication framework for resource-constrained IoT devices using decentralised key management and trust-based voting
Article.Authors: Patil P.; Ravi Teja S.; Praveen Kumar Y.; Bulagouda R.; Anitha H.; Nalina V.
Article.Abstract: Group communication in resource-constrained IoT deployments still lacks a dependable answer to insider misbehaviour. Sensor networks that grow to hundreds of heterogeneous nodes cannot always afford the memory and CPU budget that conventional cryptographic machinery demands, and Group OSCORE, while shown to be hardware-feasible, offers little protection once a malicious node has already been admitted to the group: a compromised member can quietly drop everything it is asked to forward and the rest of the network has no built-in way of noticing. We present SecureGroup-IoT , which closes this gap through three components working together: (1) a server-coordinated logical key hierarchy giving \(O(\log N)\) re-keying along with forward and backward secrecy; (2) a BLET-IoT-style trust layer that uses subjective logic to turn raw forwarding observations into calibrated, uncertainty-aware opinions about each node; and (3) a multi-watchdog consensus mechanism that automatically evicts a misbehaving node and triggers the corresponding key rotation. We built and ran the protocol in Contiki-NG 4.0 on emulated Zolertia Zoul hardware inside Cooja. Against an active blackhole attacker, the framework pulled packet delivery ratio back up from 43.7% to 93.4%, with a median isolation time of 22.4 seconds, while adding only 6.4% energy overhead. Total memory footprint came to 17.9 kB, leaving 45% headroom on Class 1 hardware.
