Article.Title: Sensitivity to chunk order in a premotor song nucleus of canaries
Article.Authors: Cazala A.; Giret N.; Hinaut X.; Del Negro C.
Article.Abstract: Sequences of distinct, ordered elements can be organized hierarchically across multiple levels. Representing such sequences in the brain may require extracting information about transition probabilities and chunks. How these processes are implemented at the neuronal level and the extent to which they are intermingled remain unclear. To address these questions, we took advantage of the multilevel structure of domesticated canary song, which comprises syllables, phrases, and chunks, as well as the selective auditory responses of neurons in the premotor HVC nucleus to playback of the bird’s own song. Neuronal activity was recorded in response to a selected song bout and to variants of that song bout generated by altering the sequential organization at either the phrase or the chunk level. Reordering chunks could strongly affect responses to one or more phrases. Moreover, the lower the transition probabilities due to chunk rearrangement, the weaker the responses. In contrast, reordering phrases within a given chunk had little impact on responsiveness, despite a dramatic decrease in transition probabilities. The present study also suggests an encoding of chunk sequencing through the integration of information provided at chunk boundaries and over a preceding period of several seconds.

Article.Authors: Shanker N.; Sridevi R.; Harika S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for charging systems integrated with renewable energy sources for efficient operation. Solar-grid integrated systems offer a promising solution; however, photovoltaic (PV) fluctuations and varying grid conditions reduce power efficiency and increase battery stress. To address these challenges, a machine learning-based source selection method for a Quasi-Z-Source Network Converter (QZNC) used in EV charging is proposed. Different machine learning algorithms, including Fine Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Weighted KNN, and Random Forest, are implemented and analyzed. Simulations are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink under different load and power conditions to evaluate system performance. Under the considered MATLAB/Simulink simulation scenarios, the Random Forest classifier achieved the best performance with a classification accuracy of 99.67% and an AUC value of 1.0 on the generated test dataset. The proposed system attains a maximum efficiency of nearly 90%, maintains voltage fluctuations below 2.5 V, and reduces charging cost by about 13% compared to conventional methods. In addition, the use of a fast-recovery diode minimizes switching noise and enhances converter performance while supporting bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation.

Article.Title: Carbon monoxide accumulation and oxygen depletion during butane heater operation in an enclosed tent
Article.Authors: Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations within a tent may vary with height and duration of heater operation, complicating the interpretation of incident reconstructions. We measured CO and oxygen (O₂) at 0–10 cm and 140–150 cm above the floor during three full-scale trials with a liquefied-butane heater. Paired readings were analyzed at 3-min intervals from 3 to 39 min. Mean CO increased from 40.33 to 93.33 ppm at the upper position and from 8.67 to 101.67 ppm near the floor; descriptive linear slopes were 1.509 and 2.684 ppm/min, respectively. At 30 min, upper-minus-lower differences were − 2, −2 and + 4 ppm. All three differences were negative from 33 min onward. The 3–39 min time-weighted mean nevertheless remained higher at the upper position (62.99 versus 51.10 ppm). Mean O₂ declined from 20.03 to 16.80 vol% above and from 20.90 to 17.97 vol% below. Thus, the early upper CO excess was followed by higher near-floor readings in each trial, with variation in transition timing. These findings show why both measurement height and elapsed time matter when interpreting a tent reconstruction; they do not establish an individual inhaled dose.

Article.Title: Proton pump inhibitor/histamine-2 receptor blocker exposure and ocular toxoplasmosis: a nationwide claims-based study
Article.Authors: Park H.; Ro J.; Jung W.; Kim J.; Lee C.; Park T.; Han J.
Article.Abstract: This nationwide, population-based, retrospective case-control study investigated the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) and histamine-2 receptor blocker (H2B) use and recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis using Korean National Health Insurance Service data (2002–2021). Among 7,411 patients diagnosed with toxoplasmosis, 3,353 had recorded ocular involvement and 4,058 did not; PPI/H2B exposure during the preceding year was compared between groups. In multivariate logistic regression, older age (40–69 years: odds ratio (OR) = 2.74; ≥70 years: OR = 6.17), hypertension (OR = 1.63), hyperlipidemia (OR = 1.18), and PPI/H2B use for ≥ 8 weeks (OR = 1.50) were associated with higher odds of this diagnosis, while female sex was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.36; all P < 0.05). Propensity score–weighted analyses confirmed this duration-dependent pattern, with higher odds at longer PPI/H2B exposure durations, particularly ≥ 8 weeks. Self-controlled case series analysis showed an increased relative risk (RR) of recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis during PPI/H2B exposure (RR = 8.26). These findings suggest a possible association between longer PPI/H2B use and recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis among patients with toxoplasmosis.

Article.Title: The effects of fabricated polycaprolactone/gelatin nanofiber scaffolds via various organic solvents and Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) on the metabolic activity of fibroblast cell line L929
Article.Authors: Karimi S.; Mirzaei-Parsa M.; Vahidi R.; Sadeghi Dousari A.; Farsinejad A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrospun Polycaprolactone (PCL)/gelatin(Gel) nanofibrous scaffolds can provide a biomimetic fibrous environment for cell–material interactions. This study investigated how acidic and emulsion solvent environments and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) loading affect fiber morphology, physicochemical characteristics, and the metabolic activity of L929 fibroblasts. PCL/Gel nanofibers were fabricated using acidic and emulsion electrospinning formulations, with 0%, 10%, or 20% PRP. A Trifluoroacetic acid(TFA)-based formulation was evaluated during formulation screening. Scaffolds were cross-linked using 25% glutaraldehyde vapor, and L929 fibroblasts were cultured on selected scaffolds. Scanning electron microscope (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), and simultaneous thermal analysis (Thermogravimetric Analysis—Differential Thermal Analysis) (STA/ TGA-DTA) were used for physicochemical characterization, and Methyl Thiazolyl Tetrazolium (MTT) assay was used to evaluate cellular metabolic activity. Statistical comparisons were performed using two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak multiple-comparisons testing. Emulsion electrospinning produced smaller fibers than the acidic formulation. PRP incorporation was associated with a further reduction in mean fiber diameter. The 10% PRP formulation showed a favorable overall cellular metabolic response, although the emulsion scaffold containing 20% PRP showed the highest numerical metabolic activity in a specific comparison. FTIR supported the presence of PRP-associated chemical functionalities, while STA/TGA demonstrated differences in the thermal behavior of PRP after exposure to the acidic and emulsion solvent systems. Within the conditions tested, solvent environment and PRP loading influenced scaffold morphology and L929 cellular metabolic activity. The emulsion formulation with approximately 10% PRP showed a favorable combination of fiber morphology and cellular response. These findings support further investigation of PRP-containing PCL/gelatin electrospun scaffolds, while additional studies are required to establish PRP growth-factor bioactivity, release behavior, residual cross-linker content, and quantitative cell proliferation.

Article.Title: Micro-needle-dispenser-based direct writing of optical microlenses on optical fiber facets for visible-range applications
Article.Authors: Das S.; Karunakaran Nair N.; Waldhauer S.; Spengler F.; Rüßeler A.; Kaierle S.; Kracht D.; Hinkelmann M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a droplet-based micro-dispensing technique for the fabrication of photopolymer microlenses directly on the end facets of optical single-mode fibers. The process is based on a layer-by-layer droplet stacking approach, where each deposited droplet is individually cured with ultraviolet light to achieve precise control over the microlens height, curvature, and geometry. In contrast to traditional fabrication techniques, this method removes the need for lithographic or molding processes and allows rapid and customizable fabrication. Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD)-based optical simulations agree with the experimental results, confirming accurate control over the beam shaping properties of the fabricated lenses. A focal beam radius down to approximately 1.7 μm with a working distance of 38 μm at a wavelength of 635 nm has been achieved. This facilitates potential applications e.g. where coupling from single-mode fibers to photonic chips with smaller mode field diameter (MFD) is required. The developed approach provides a scalable method for directly integrating microlenses into photonic integrated circuits and other optical platforms for sensing, imaging, and biomedical single-fiber probing applications.

Article.Title: Exosomes from adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells ameliorate bladder dysfunction in diabetic rats by attenuating oxidative stress via the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; Zhang D.; Li H.; Chen H.; Jin R.; Zhao Y.; Sun X.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetic bladder dysfunction (DBD) is a common urinary system complication in diabetic patients, with oxidative stress (OS) being a key factor in its onset and progression. Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-exos) hold potential for treating OS-related diseases. In this study, we established high glucose-induced cell models and diabetic rat models to investigate the role and molecular mechanisms of ADSC-exos in mitigating OS in DBD. The results demonstrated that ADSC-exos inhibited intracellular ROS generation, downregulated PTEN expression, activated the PI3K/AKT pathway, promoted GSK-3β degradation, reversed NRF2 suppression, and enhanced the expression of downstream antioxidant proteins. In diabetic rats, ADSC-exos improved bladder function by reducing maximum voiding pressure, prolonging voiding intervals, and decreasing bladder tissue fibrosis and apoptosis. Further analysis revealed that miRNA-21-5p is highly enriched in ADSC-exos. Bioinformatics predictions identify PTEN as a target of miRNA-21-5p. Overexpression of miRNA-21-5p reversed PTEN-mediated suppression of the antioxidant stress system. In summary, ADSC-exos alleviate OS and improve bladder function in diabetic rats via the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling pathway, in which miRNA-21-5p may play a certain role.

Article.Title: Erector spinae muscle fibre size estimation using high-density surface electromyography in people with and without non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Purushotham S.; Casolo A.; Arvanitidis M.; Grison A.; Gardner A.; Falla D.
Article.Abstract: There is limited evidence on whether lumbar erector spinae (ES) fibre morphology is altered in people with low back pain (LBP), due to the inherent challenges with biopsy studies. High-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) provides an opportunity to assess motor unit properties, allowing non-invasive estimation of muscle fibre morphology. This cross-sectional study compares estimates of ES muscle fibre size and activity in people with and without non-specific chronic LBP and examines correlations with clinical features in those with LBP. HDsEMG data was acquired from the ES from people with and without non-specific chronic LBP (28/group) during isometric lumbar extension at maximum and submaximal levels (10%, 30%, 50%, 70%). HDsEMG signals were decomposed to estimate motor unit conduction velocity (MUCV), fibre diameter (FD), and fibre cross-sectional area (CSA). Additionally, global estimates from topographical HDsEMG amplitude maps were assessed including amplitude, entropy and y- and x- barycentre locations. There were no significant differences between the groups for MUCV ( p = 0.1310), FD ( p = 0.1310), or CSA ( p = 0.2875). Differences in the regional activation of ES along the y-axis ( p = 0.009) and entropy ( p = 0.023) were observed between groups. In conclusion, estimated ES fibre morphology did not differ between people with and without chronic LBP. However, an alteration of the spatial distribution of ES activity was observed for those with chronic LBP. These findings suggest that alterations in neuromuscular function may occur in individuals with non-specific chronic LBP in the absence of detectable differences in estimated ES muscle fibre size.

Article.Title: fNIRS and eye tracking reveal observation-practice ratio-dependent neural efficiency in multi-level 24-style tai chi learning
Article.Authors: Guo C.; Hong Y.; Jiang E.; Long Y.; Wei C.; Liu C.; Shi B.
Article.Abstract: Observation and physical practice are the most frequently used methods in learning 24 Style Taichi. The effective ratio of these methods for enhancing skill acquisition remains unclear. This study aimed to identify effective Observation-Practice Ratios for novice college students learning movements of varying difficulty, and to elucidate associated differences in cognitive neural activity and eye movement performance. A two-factor mixed design was employed. The between-subjects factor was Observation-Practice Ratio (1: 3, 1: 1, 3: 1), and the within-subjects factor was Task Difficulty (Easy, Medium, High). During 24-Style Tai Chi learning, hemodynamic signals were recorded via wearable functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and eye movements were tracked using eyeglass-type eye tracking. Data were analyzed using Three-way ANOVA and Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA. The O1P3 and O1P1 groups exhibited lower oxy-Hb concentration compared to O3P1. They also showed reduced fixation, saccade, and blink counts alongside better motor performance. Taken together, the combination of lower neural activity, improved oculomotor control, and comparable motor performance suggests that the O1P3 and O1P1 ratios may promote more efficient neural processing during learning, consistent with the Neural Efficiency Hypothesis. Additionally, oxy-Hb concentration was higher in the parietal area than in the frontal area, with the premotor cortex (PMC) and supplementary motor area (SMA) regions showing particularly strong activation patterns compared to other measured fronto-parietal regions during Tai Chi learning. O1P3 and O1P1 ratios show better learning efficiency for beginners. These ratios achieve comparable performance with reduced neural resource allocation and improved oculomotor control. These findings collectively provide fNIRS and behavioral support for the Neural Efficiency Hypothesis. Additionally, parietal regions, particularly PMC and SMA, show substantial involvement in the motor learning process for 24-style Tai Chi.

Article.Title: Lesion-aware prototype contrastive learning for port-wine stain classification
Article.Authors: Xiang F.; Yu S.; Xu C.; Qu Y.; Zhang X.; Ding Y.; Kang X.
Article.Abstract: Image-based classification of pink-red and purple-red port-wine stain (PWS) subtypes is a fine-grained visual recognition task. However, subtle chromatic differences, blurred lesion boundaries, and heterogeneous acquisition conditions make this task challenging. To address these issues, we developed LAPC, a lesion-aware prototype contrastive framework that combines dual-statistic channel-spatial attention with prototype-discriminative representation learning. The attention branch combines average and maximum feature statistics with learned directional spatial responses through residual channel and spatial recalibration. The contrastive branch mines lesion representations through supervised contrastive learning, class-prototype aggregation, and inter-class margin separation. On an expanded internal cohort of 887 PWS images, five-fold evaluation showed higher mean Accuracy, Recall, AUC, and BACC for LAPC than the compared methods under both backbones; these numerical comparisons do not establish statistical significance. Ablation experiments evaluated the individual and combined effects of lesion-aware attention and prototype contrastive learning across two backbone architectures, with supplementary experiments conducted on PH2 in a separate dermoscopic setting.

Article.Title: Sex differences in inflammation, mitochondrial function and energy sensing during early recovery from COVID 19 in older adults
Article.Authors: Temp J.; Estepa M.; Nnaji M.; Haritonow N.; Marx L.; Vakhrusheva O.; Wu H.; Ladilov Y.; Barcena M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 infections induce mitochondrial dysfunction and exacerbate systemic inflammation. In the present study, sex differences were investigated among post-COVID-19 patients during the early recovery phase, as emerging evidence indicates that sex critically influences post-COVID-19 outcomes, particularly in older adults. Mitochondrial dysfunction, energy stress signaling through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), and inflammatory dysregulation represent pathogenic mechanisms implicated in prolonged recovery. In this study, we analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and plasma from aged male and female patients during early post-COVID-19 recovery (1–4 weeks after obtaining a negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR test), comparing them to an inflammatory control group. Female post-COVID-19 patients exhibited elevated circulating TNF-α levels and a trend toward increased mRNA levels of proinflammatory interleukins IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs, accompanied by enhanced acetylation and decreased activity of mitochondrial superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2). Both sexes displayed increased phosphorylation of AMPK, suggesting altered energy-sensing pathways. Mitochondrial gene expression was upregulated in female post-COVID-19 patients, potentially indicating compensatory responses to energy deficits. These findings reveal sex-dependent inflammatory and mitochondrial alterations during early recovery, suggesting a mechanistic link to the higher prevalence of long COVID-19 in women. These findings emphasize the need for sex-specific therapeutic approaches targeting mitochondrial and immunometabolic dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients.

Article.Title: Insights into CO₂ adsorption on zeolite ZSM-5: an experimental and advanced modeling approach
Article.Authors: Bouzgarrou S.; Jedli H.; Hassani R.; Sabi E.; Jamel L.; Mahariq I.; Slimi K.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate CO₂ adsorption on ZSM-5 zeolite. The adsorbent was characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The correlation coefficients (R²) obtained from the isotherm models indicate that the classical Langmuir model provides a good fit to the experimental data across different temperatures. In addition, the physicochemical parameters of the advanced multilayer model were examined in detail. Key isotherm parameters, including the number of CO₂ molecules per site (n), receptor site density (Dm), and energy parameters (ΔE₁ and ΔE₂), were also analyzed. The results suggest that CO₂ adsorption on ZSM-5 is spontaneous, exothermic, and governed by physisorption. Overall, the model outcomes can be applied to the design and optimization of a pilot-scale CO₂ adsorption system.

Article.Title: Threat adaptive trust weighted federated learning for Byzantine resilient cybersecurity across healthcare edge networks
Article.Authors: Dalal S.; Kundu S.; Kaushik J.; Alqaisi O.; Rajkhan N.; Dahiya P.; Nirkhi S.; Rakesh S.
Article.Abstract: The rising adoption of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, edge computing, and distributed healthcare platforms brings with it a host of cybersecurity threats, whereas the centralized learning approach also brings with it privacy, communication, and single point of failure concerns. This study introduces the threat-adaptive Trust-weighted Federated Optimization (TrustFedHealth) framework for Byzantine-resilient healthcare cybersecurity, which combines the multi-signal client reliability estimation, temporal trust updating, norm clipping, error-feedback Top-k compression, and threat-guided Multi-Krum aggregation, with trust-weighted FedYogi optimization. The experiments were run on 15 k healthcare records with 52 attributes, with 12 k of them used for training and 3 k of them being future-held-out for testing, in 60 edge-node clients. Three tasks were assessed: security-risk classification, health-risk classification and health-risk regression. FedAdam showed the best security classification, with 93.67% accuracy, 0.9028 Macro-F1, 0.8867 MCC and 0.9898 ROC–AUC, while FedYogi attained the best ROC–AUC of 0.9904 and regression performance with 0.0516 MAE, 0.0651 RMSE and an R 2 of 0.6562. Multi-Krum has 0.8892 ROC–AUC and 75.77% security-classification accuracy when the attack rate is less than 20% malicious-client participation. A gender Macro-F1 gap of 0.0089 was achieved in the subgroup analysis and the expected calibration error was reduced from 0.0274 to 0.0185 by temperature scaling. The highest compressed checkpoint's accuracy is 90.46% and the highest Macro-F1 score is 0.8480, with a 22.25% cumulative communication reduction. The results show the promise of TrustFedHealth for secure, calibrated, equitable and communication efficient collaborative intelligence in the healthcare domain.

Article.Title: Reward-related memory benefits cannot be explained by post-encoding stimulus-related thought
Article.Authors: Chaloupka B.; Fain M.; Cowan E.; Tambini A.; Murty V.
Article.Abstract: There is an active debate regarding whether rehearsal drives memory benefits associated with awake post-encoding consolidation. In the current study, we manipulated conditions designed to encourage or discourage rehearsal during post-encoding wakeful rest to characterize downstream effects on associative memory in the context of a reward-motivated memory paradigm. To manipulate rehearsal during the post-encoding period, participants in the rehearsal group were explicitly instructed to rehearse high-reward memoranda for 15 min and then completed an incentivized mini-retrieval test. In contrast, participants in the rest group completed an incentivized mini-retrieval test immediately, eliminating the need for post-encoding rehearsal, then were instructed to rest for 15 min. A surprise memory test occurred approximately 24 h later. We found that reward significantly enhanced item memory, replicating a large body of work. Importantly, we found that neither encouraging post-encoding rehearsal nor self-reported time spent thinking about high-reward stimuli during the post-encoding period were related to reward memory enhancements. These findings suggest that explicitly encouraging rehearsal during post-encoding rest cannot fully explain consolidation-related memory benefits, consistent with the notion that spontaneous processes support reward memory benefits on long-term memory.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-assisted ECG interpretation for identification of occlusive myocardial infarction following cardiac arrest: a multi-reader, multi-case study
Article.Authors: Silwanis C.; Groche M.; Neunteufel A.; Huss M.; Eder J.; Kirchweger B.; Bruckner M.; Lindner G.; Fellner A.; Nahler A.; Rechberger S.; Blessberger H.; Kellermair J.; Maier J.; Steinwender C.; Lambert T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interpretation of post–return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) electrocardiograms (ECGs) is challenging, yet critical for identifying occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) requiring urgent reperfusion. While artificial intelligence (AI)–based decision-support tools show promising results, their impact on physician decision-making remains unclear. In this multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study​, 69 real-world post-ROSC ECGs were evaluated by 15 physicians from five groups at two timepoints (T1 [without AI] and T2 [with Queen of Hearts (QoH) neural network support]), yielding 2,070 interpretations. At T1, sensitivity/specificity were 77.97%/84.64% (LR + 5.08, LR − 0.26); at T2, 78.55%/90.43% (LR + 8.21, LR − 0.24). For the primary endpoint, MRMC AUC increased from 0.882 to 0.912 (Δ 0.030, 95% CI 0.008–0.058; p ​=0.018). The error rate fell by 2.32% (95% CI − 0.9 to + 5.6; p ​=0.156); odds of correct identification were numerically higher at T2 (aOR 1.29, 95% CI 0.98–1.69). Of 66 changed decisions, 64 (97%) followed QoH: the error rate fell by 5.03% where QoH was correct and rose by 10.56% where it was not. Sensitivity for non-STEMI high-risk OMI did not improve. Confidence increased, and within-group agreement rose through convergence on the algorithm output. The benefit of AI support is tied to algorithm accuracy.

Article.Title: Temporal trends and disparities in cardiac arrest and co-listed acute myocardial infarction-related mortality in the United States, 1999–2025: Insights from CDC WONDER database
Article.Authors: Arsheen F.; Fatima S.; Shaheer M.; Asif A.; Fatima A.; Fareed M.; Farooq A.; Khalid N.; Naz A.; Safeer H.; Khan S.; Aminpoor H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiac Arrest (CA) and Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) are closely linked cardiovascular conditions and major contributors to global mortality. We evaluated national trends in mortality associated with CA co-listed with AMI among United States (U.S) adults from 1999 to 2025 and assessed demographic and geographic disparities. Using CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death, we conducted a retrospective analysis of CA and co-listed AMI-related mortality from 1999 to 2025 among adults aged ≥ 25 years. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated, and joinpoint regression was utilized to estimate annual average percentage changes (AAPCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). There were 747,073 reported deaths due to CA and co-listed AMI. The AAMR decreased from 22.06 in 1999 to 7.37 in 2025 (AAPC: −4.28; p ≤ 0.000001). Men had higher mean AAMRs than women (mean AAMR: men 16.38; women: 9.77). Among races, Non-Hispanic (NH) Black individuals had the highest mean AAMR (17.14). Mortality burden was greatest among older adults aged ≥ 65 years (mean AAMR: 51.35). Regionally, the Northeast had the highest mean AAMR (16.29), and rural areas showed slightly higher mortality compared with urban areas (14.29 vs. 13.53). Most deaths (69.22%) occurred in medical facilities. Mortality associated with CA and co-listed AMI has declined substantially in the U.S over the past two decades, with significant disparities. These findings highlight the importance of improved risk stratification and targeted preventive strategies in high-risk populations.

Article.Title: Hexamerin contributes to nutrient-driven metamorphosis in Anopheles stephensi
Article.Authors: Srivastava V.; Rohilla P.; Saini V.; Yadav P.; Singh T.; Sankhala N.; Sharma G.; Tevatiya S.; Tandon G.; Kumari S.; Kaur J.; Dixit R.
Article.Abstract: The mosquito life cycle involves a rapid transition from aquatic larvae to non-feeding pupae, requiring precise synchronization between nutrient allocation and development. While macronutrients are known to drive metamorphosis, the molecular mechanisms that link amino acids to this transition remain poorly understood. This study investigates the impact of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation on the growth and metamorphosis of Anopheles stephensi . We found that BCAA supplementation to standard insectary food accelerated larval growth, enabling larvae to reach the pupal stage approximately 1.5 days earlier than unsupplemented controls. This transition was accompanied by a marked upregulation of Hexamerin ( AsHex ), a dedicated amino acid storage protein, during the late larval (L4) stage. Notably, RNAi-mediated silencing of AsHex significantly impaired pupation, a defect that could not be rescued by BCAA supplementation, suggesting that AsHex -associated nutrient storage contributes to the successful progression of metamorphosis. Next, we evaluated a possible association between AsHex and the nutrient-sensing TOR pathway. Rapamycin treatment delayed the larval-to-pupal transition, similar to AsHex knockdown, suggesting a possible association between AsHex and TOR-dependent developmental regulation. Collectively, our results indicate that AsHex plays a role in coordinating nutritional status with developmental progression during the larval-to-pupal transition. This discovery provides new insights into mosquito growth regulation and identifies AsHex as a potential physiological target for innovative vector control strategies.

Article.Title: Investigation on mechanical and thermal behavior of geopolymer phase change concrete
Article.Authors: Qin Z.; Liu Z.; Zhang X.; Lin J.; Zhang L.; Liu S.; Yang N.; Tian Y.
Article.Abstract: Phase change concrete (PCC) is gradually gaining traction in engineering applications owing to its superior thermal regulation capabilities. This study investigates the effects of varying paraffin microcapsule (PM) replacement levels on the mechanical and thermal properties of geopolymer-based phase change concrete (GPCC) and ordinary Portland cement-based phase change concrete (CPCC) through macroscopic physical and mechanical testing, complemented by microscopic characterization techniques. The results demonstrate that the compressive strength of both GPCC and CPCC decreases progressively with increasing PM content, accompanied by a continuous rise in porosity. Under identical PM replacement levels and curing ages, GPCC consistently exhibits higher compressive strength than CPCC, despite possessing a relatively looser microstructure. The incorporation of PM enhances the structural integrity and ductility of the failure modes observed in both concrete types. PM addition induces a concurrent increase in porosity and reduction in matrix densification for both GPCC and CPCC. While maintaining a compressive strength threshold of no less than 25 MPa, GPCC-20 achieved a latent heat of phase transition and specific heat capacity that were 2.0 and 1.1 times those of CPCC-10, respectively, with its thermal conductivity being 40.1% lower than that of CPCC-10. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the further research and engineering implementation of phase change concrete.

Article.Title: Genome sequencing reveals a highly divergent genotype II African swine fever virus in Nigeria
Article.Authors: Olono A.; Ogunsanya O.; Sijuwola A.; Saibu F.; O’Donnell V.; Lakin S.; Parker E.; Barette R.; Xu L.; Adedokun O.; Fadele J.; Abiola J.; Tchokote E.; Park D.; Mboowa G.; Tomkins-Tinch C.; Faburay B.; Brown C.; Happi C.; Happi A.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever is a viral disease with major socioeconomic consequences in countries including Nigeria, where pig farming sustains many livelihoods. Despite the critical role of genomic data in outbreak control, Nigeria has remained underrepresented in global African swine fever virus (ASFV) genomic datasets. Here, we report the first in-country sequencing and genomic analysis of ASFV from recent outbreaks in Nigeria, representing the largest dataset of ASFV genomes generated in Nigeria and Africa to date. Using Oxford Nanopore and Illumina Technology platforms, we assembled 27 whole-genome sequences from field samples collected in Ogun, Osun, and Oyo States. Comparative analyses revealed nearly 100 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in coding regions and more than 250 across coding and non-coding regions, alongside multiple insertions and deletions relative to the Georgia 2007 ASFV reference genome. Notably, we report novel large deletions in variable regions, which may affect genes linked to virulence and host adaptation. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the Nigerian ASFV genomes form a distinct clade within biotype II, which also diverges considerably from the genome backbone currently utilized for vaccine designs, highlighting the impact of viral divergence on current control measures.

Article.Title: Balanced-rank policy refinement of discrete molecular graph diffusion for multi-objective molecular generation
Article.Authors: Amiri M.; Azizi A.
Article.Abstract: Generating drug-like molecules while balancing chemical validity, synthetic accessibility, novelty, and distributional fidelity is a multi-objective optimization problem. We present HybridMolGen as a categorical two-dimensional molecular graph diffusion backbone refined with proximal policy optimization (PPO), a balanced within-batch marginal-rank reward, and adaptive objective weights. The evaluated implementation neither generates Cartesian coordinates nor includes an independently evaluated SE(3)-equivariant coordinate generator or cross-attention property-conditioning module. In an eight-seed paired confirmation with 256 samples per condition, refinement increased synthetic-accessibility utility by 0.00610 (95% bootstrap CI 0.00106 to 0.01061), novelty by 0.00928 (0.00342 to 0.01465), and composite utility by 0.00632 (0.00153 to 0.01068). Hypervolume changed by − 0.00021 and satisfied the predefined non-inferiority gate. A frozen checkpoint was subsequently evaluated with the official MOSES implementation on 25,000 requested samples. Relative to the matched backbone, FCD/Test improved from 0.57250 to 0.55633 and scaffold similarity from 0.90221 to 0.91031, whereas validity changed from 0.87756 to 0.87488 and novelty from 0.94076 to 0.93936. The results support a controlled policy-refinement trade-off rather than universal superiority. Article.Title: Shelterwood-managed forest stands show similar soil microbial activity patterns as beech-dominated old-growth forests
Article.Authors: Gömöryová E.; Pichler V.; Leuschner C.; Gömöry D.
Article.Abstract: Close-to-nature silvicultural systems are increasingly applied as an alternative to intensive forest management, but their effects on soil microbial communities remain insufficiently understood. We investigated whether shelterwood management affects soil microbial properties in comparison with old-growth beech forests in three national nature reserves in eastern Slovakia: Havešová, Kyjov and Stužica. In each reserve, data on soil properties and microbial activity were collected from a network of sampling points covering both the core of the reserve and the managed stands (146 plots in total). CLPP was used to assess the responses of soil microbiota to environmental conditions and stand management. While microclimate and vegetation were similar in all three reserves, significant variation was observed among the reserves in soil chemistry and the diversity and activity of soil microbiota. In contrast, differences between old-growth forests and managed stands were few and not consistently statistically significant across the three sites. Substrate availability was the most important determinant of microbial activity in the organo-mineral A-horizon, while soil moisture was the sole factor influencing soil microbiota in the litter O-horizon. Our results suggest that when management mimics natural ecosystem processes, as in the shelterwood system applied in the studied forests, the effect on soil microbial processes need not to be negative.

Article.Title: An engineered SDL variant improves AppDNA-dependent single-stranded DNA ligation
Article.Authors: Miura F.; Shibata Y.; Miura M.; Shibata T.; Suzuki Y.; Ito T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) ligation is required for library preparation from fragmented, chemically modified, and naturally occurring ssDNA. SDL is a recently identified ligase with strong ssDNA ligation activity, but conditions optimized for ATP-dependent ligation do not necessarily translate to reactions using pre-adenylated DNA donors (AppDNA). We first asked whether bypassing donor adenylation by supplying AppDNA could improve SDL-mediated ligation. Wild-type SDL rapidly ligated AppDNA in the absence of ATP, but product formation slowed after approximately 15 min and most AppDNA was converted to its 5′-phosphorylated form. Reasoning that a variant impaired in donor adenylation might also suppress this reverse conversion while retaining strand joining with AppDNA, we screened candidate substitutions and identified SDL-m5 (K239A). SDL-m5 retained efficient AppDNA ligation while markedly reducing AppDNA-to-pDNA conversion under the tested conditions. Wild-type SDL and SDL-m5 displayed distinct pH optima, and ligation efficiency across these conditions was inversely associated with sequence bias at the ligation junction. In cfDNA, replication-associated ssDNA, and bisulfite-converted DNA library workflows, SDL-m5 frequently yielded more library than wild-type SDL under AppDNA conditions. These results establish SDL-m5 as a practical variant for AppDNA-dependent ssDNA ligation and provide guidance for choosing ligation conditions in ssDNA library construction.

Article.Title: Feasibility- and connected-domain-guided multi-objective particle swarm optimization for multi-loop mechanism synthesis
Article.Authors: Cheng R.; Yu Z.; Song H.; Mao S.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dimensional synthesis of multi-loop mechanisms must satisfy loop closure, branch continuity, singularity margin, task coverage and load transfer requirements. Penalty-based treatment is inefficient for fragmented feasible input domains under limited evaluations. This study formulates constrained sizing as a two-objective search that minimizes task-coverage error and a clipped load proxy, while using connected-domain quality as internal guidance. A feasibility- and connected-domain-guided multi-objective particle swarm optimizer (FCD-MOPSO) is proposed, combining mechanism-aware input-space evaluation, feasibility-first comparison, connected-domain-guided archive maintenance, mixed leader selection and bounded perturbation. Under a soft-constrained low-budget protocol, FCD-MOPSO increased the valid-run rate from 0.6 to 0.8 and the high-quality (HQ) and force-aware HQ rates from 0.1 to 0.4 relative to Basic MOPSO. Search histories showed earlier archive formation and more consistent coverage accumulation. Representative inverse-dynamics verification showed lower peak force, RMS force, force-gradient risk and smoothness index than selected Basic MOPSO and PSO representatives. Strict-feasibility diagnosis identified coverage pressure as the limiting factor. FCD-MOPSO is positioned as a mechanism-aware screening optimizer for fragmented feasible active-input domains.

Article.Title: Generational differences in mediterranean diet adherence: associations with hedonic hunger and the obesogenic environment
Article.Authors: Mengi Çelik Ö.; Güler Ü.; Samanci M.; Özer H.; Acar Taşkaya M.; Akçakaya S.; Akay G.; Sözen R.; Yilmaz B.
Article.Abstract: Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet may show intergenerational differences in its association with hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environment. This study aimed to examine the relationship between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet, hedonic hunger, and perceived obesogenic environment among adults in Türkiye from an intergenerational perspective. This cross-sectional intergenerational study was conducted among 1176 adults (845 women, 331 men) aged 18–58 years living in Ankara, Türkiye. Data were collected via a web-based survey using the snowball sampling method. Sociodemographic characteristics and self-reported anthropometric measurements were recorded. Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet (MEDAS), hedonic hunger (Power of Food Scale), and perceived obesogenic environment (Obesogenic Environment Scale) were assessed. Participants were classified into Generations X, Y, and Z based on age groups. Correlation analyses, group comparisons, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed. Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet differed significantly across generations, with the highest adherence observed in Generation X and the lowest in Generation Z ( p < 0.001). Levels of hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environment were significantly higher in Generation Z ( p < 0.05). MEDAS scores showed significant negative correlations with the total and subdimension scores of both the Power of Food Scale and the Obesogenic Environment Scale across all generations ( p < 0.001). Generation-stratified multiple linear regression analyses showed that age and income level were positively associated with MEDAS scores within each generation, whereas men sex, higher hedonic hunger, and greater perceived obesogenic environment were negatively associated with MEDAS scores ( p < 0.05). This study shows that hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environmental factors are inversely associated with adherence to the Mediterranean Diet across all three generations. These findings highlight the potential relevance of considering behavioral and environmental factors in the development of generation-specific public health interventions aimed at promoting diet quality and sustainable healthy eating patterns.

Article.Title: Molecular docking and interaction profiling identify phytochemicals as candidate JAK-STAT pathway inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis
Article.Authors: Gupta K.; Ashma R.; Jonnalagadda M.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains a challenging chronic disease as despite adherence to known therapeutic guidelines nearly half of patients experience persistent moderate to severe disease activity. Pathogenesis is driven by multiple pro-inflammatory signalling pathways that includes Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), NF-κB, Notch and MAPK, thereby driving macrophage polarization toward the pathogenic M1 phenotype. JAKis modulate different cytokine pathways at once causing both benefits and risks, such as improved outcomes in hyperinflammatory conditions and increased susceptibility to certain infections. However standard JAKis’s show adverse side effects motivating the search for safer alternatives. In this study in-silico molecular docking, ligand efficiency and selectivity index (SI) analyses was performed for 10 ligands to identify phytochemicals with high binding affinity to JAK family proteins, to recommend potential safer plant derived alternative inhibitors for RA therapy. Quercetin showed the strongest affinity toward JAK2 (− 9.3 kcal/mol), comparable to the reference drug baricitinib (− 8.2 kcal/mol), and peficitinib against JAK1 and JAK3 (− 9.0 kcal/mol). Similarly, kaempferol and catechin exhibited strong binding to JAK2 (− 8.9 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, respectively) and JAK3 (− 8.5 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, respectively), indicating their potential as pan-JAK inhibitors. SI analysis indicated marginally favourable target-engagement profiles for quercetin (SI = 1.18), naringenin (SI = 1.15), and kaempferol (SI = 1.14) relative to standard JAK inhibitors. In spite of lower SI (1.08), catechin has high absolute binding affinities for all four JAK isoforms, which supports its candidature as pan-JAK modulator. Together, these four phytochemicals warrant further preclinical evaluation as candidate modulators of the JAK/STAT pathway in RA, potentially expanding the therapeutic options available for managing this disease.

Article.Authors: Ukubuiwe C.; Abalaka M.; Ukubuiwe A.; Ossamulu I.; Adabara N.; Olayemi I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes of the Anopheles , Aedes , and Culex genera serve as vectors for significant human and animal diseases. The increasing prevalence of insecticide resistance, primarily mediated by detoxification enzymes, highlights the urgent need for innovative biocontrol strategies. This study assessed the larvicidal activity of secondary metabolites produced by Klebsiella pneumoniae PX652414 and Proteus mirabilis PZ337687, as well as their impact on esterase and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) enzyme activities in three major mosquito species: An. gambiae s.l., Ae. aegypti , and Cx. quinquefasciatus . Conversely, P. mirabilis metabolites resulted in minimal mortality and elevated esterase and GST activity. These results demonstrate enzyme modulation by these metabolites and indicate that K. pneumoniae (PX652414) metabolites may serve as promising agents for integrated vector management.

Article.Title: Improved genetic algorithm based intelligent scheduling model and efficient solution method for green financial resources
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Tang X.
Article.Abstract: Green financial resource scheduling must reconcile heterogeneous project requirements, time-varying capital availability and tail risk exposure within a single allocation decision. Manual review and static rule-based procedures coordinate these dimensions poorly once the number of candidate projects and financial instruments grows. This research formulates the problem as a constrained multi-objective programme in which a continuous decision vector specifies the fraction of each project’s financing demand routed through each eligible instrument, and twelve instrument-by-quarter capital ceilings together with priority-dependent minimum funding requirements define the feasible set. Economic cost, environmental benefit and conditional value at risk at the 95 per cent level are optimised jointly. An improved multi-population genetic algorithm, denoted IMaPGA, integrates subpopulation co-evolution, elite migration, state-dependent crossover and mutation, crowding preservation, reference-direction selection and feasible neighbourhood refinement. Comparative experiments against NSGA-II, MOPSO, SPEA2 and NSGA-III at scales from 50 to 400 projects use an identical budget of one hundred thousand objective-function evaluations with three repetitions per instance and scale, while MOEA/D and an epsilon-constraint sweep are evaluated in a separate comparison under a reduced verification budget. IMaPGA attains the highest hypervolume and the lowest inverted generational distance throughout the tested scales, and paired significance testing identifies the comparisons in which that advantage is statistically reliable. The framework converts green financial scheduling into a quantitative multi-objective decision process.

Article.Authors: Almalki S.; Alshari E.; Almuntashiri A.; Alghamdi T.; Senan E.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Monitoring vegetation stress and land degradation in dryland environments is challenging because short-term spectral variability can obscure persistent ecological change. Complex deep-learning architectures also do not necessarily provide higher predictive performance or independently validated explanations. The study developed and evaluated an explainable Vision Mamba (VMamba)–Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) framework for multi-temporal vegetation monitoring in Badr Al-Janub, Saudi Arabia, using Landsat observations from 2015 to 2025. Multi-temporal vegetation and moisture indices were integrated with terrain variables, while a geographic partition defined training, validation, and locked independent-test subsets. On the locked independent-test set, VMamba–KAN achieved an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 78.76%, frequency-weighted Intersection over Union (FWIoU) of 71.28%, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 20.06%, and Macro-F1 of 25.11%. The CNN baseline achieved higher OA, FWIoU, mIoU, and Macro-F1 values than VMamba–KAN. Cohen's Kappa was 0.424 for VMamba–KAN and 0.404 for the CNN baseline. The Kappa difference is reported separately and is not interpreted as evidence of overall or class-balanced predictive superiority. Temporal analysis identified broad improvement in vegetation condition toward 2023 followed by partial deterioration in 2025 rather than continuous landscape-scale degradation. Integrated Gradients provided descriptive attribution patterns associated with VMamba–KAN predictions. Full-scene softmax probabilities provided descriptive predictive-confidence information and were not interpreted as calibrated uncertainty estimates. The results emphasize temporal persistence, geographic evaluation, class imbalance, predictive performance, and cautious interpretation of attribution evidence.

Article.Abstract: Wilms’ tumor (WT) is the most common renal tumor of childhood. In vivo animal experiments showed that NDP@RBC + US suppressed tumor growth, with a tumor growth inhibition rate of 80.22% compared with the PBS group and 19.27% compared with NDP@RBC alone. Article.Title: Technical validation of a regional landslide forecasting system in the Eastern Himalayas
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Mishra A.; Singh G.; Karmakar R.; Ghosh S.; Bahuguna H.
Article.Abstract: Rainfall-induced landslides pose a recurrent threat in the Darjeeling–Kalimpong Himalaya, India. Here we present the first systematic evaluation of an Indian regional landslide early warning system using the EDuMaP framework. Performance was assessed over 2,316 block-days spanning 373 monsoon days across 11 administrative units. Of 521 landslides analysed, 96.50% of block-days recorded no or only minor activity. Aggregated validation yielded 361 correct predictions, 1,862 true negatives, 19 missed alerts, and 74 false alerts. Green and yellow grades together represented 95.60% of forecast–observation pairs, with a mean combined efficiency index of 0.86 across the nine non-overlapping forecast zones. The system’s error structure was dominated by overwarning rather than catastrophic missed events. A stakeholder-driven transition to finer administrative forecast zones improved skill scores. Because the forecasts combined an automated rainfall-threshold model with expert review, the reported skill reflects this hybrid system, not the model alone.

Article.Authors: Chen D.; Su M.; Wang Z.; Xie Z.; Ye T.; Fan S.; Wu Y.; Luo S.
Article.Abstract: The prognostic value of longitudinal lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) patterns in critically ill adults remains uncertain. In MIMIC-IV, LAR was assessed during 0–<96 h, with mortality follow-up beginning at 96 h. Among 1,456 landmark-eligible patients, higher mean LAR was associated with 30-day and 365-day mortality (adjusted risk ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.11–1.34] and 1.09 [1.02–1.17], respectively), but associations were similar for mean lactate. A descriptive three-class trajectory model identified stable-low, moderate-declining, and high-increasing patterns; neither non-reference trajectory was associated with increased mortality after adjustment. Trajectory structure changed under alternative temporal definitions. In eICU ( n = 1,181), independently estimated trajectories differed, although a stable-high class was associated with higher hospital and ICU mortality. Secondary prediction analyses showed only modest incremental performance for mean LAR and little contribution from trajectory class alone. In this selected population with sufficient serial measurements, longitudinal LAR provides prognostic information but does not establish superiority over lactate, a universal high-risk trajectory phenotype, or clinical utility.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Parallel capacitors across the interrupter contacts of circuit breakers in ultra-high-voltage (UHV) converter stations can be exposed to power-frequency voltage with superimposed harmonics and elevated operating temperatures. Within this test matrix, adding harmonics was associated with lower characteristic breakdown and PD inception field strengths than the power-frequency reference in most comparisons, although the dependence on harmonic proportion was not monotonic for all characteristic-harmonic conditions. Within the high-frequency subset, the measured field strengths were generally lower at 20 kHz than at 10 kHz under matched proportions. Increasing temperature reduced the characteristic breakdown field strength across the tested harmonic conditions; the PD inception field strength was generally lower at elevated temperatures, but some temperature sequences overlapped or were non-monotonic. PRPD and PRPS patterns also varied with waveform. These conclusions provide a solid theoretical reference for insulation condition assessment and fault prevention and control of converter station parallel capacitors.

Article.Title: Mortality and survival rates following lower limb amputation: a national observational cohort study in Sweden
Article.Authors: Jansson S.; Johannesson A.; Carlberg M.; Hiyoshi A.; Jarl G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare the association between initial lower limb amputation (LLA) and mortality risk compared with matched controls, and to determine whether this association varies by amputation level and by region of residence by comparing individuals with and without LLA within each region. We also assessed temporal trends in 1-year post-amputation mortality. This matched cohort study used population-based national registers in Sweden to identify initial LLAs performed from 2008 to 2017. Individual with LLA was matched by age-, sex-, and county with up to 10 individuals without an LLA. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). A total of 16,757 people with LLA and 165,555 without LLA were included, of whom 76.1% and 37.6%, respectively, died during follow-up (until December 31, 2018). LLA was associated with a 4.48-fold higher mortality risk (95% CI 4.39–4.57), after adjusting for age, sex, marital status, education, and birth in Sweden (yes/no). HRs for specific amputation levels were 5.19 (5.05–5.33) for high proximal, 4.05 (3.94–4.16) for low proximal, and 3.93 (3.69–4.19) for partial foot amputations. LLA was associated with higher mortality compared with individuals without LLA within each of Sweden’s 21 regions, HRs ranged from 3.67 (CI 3.26–4.12) in Kalmar to 5.16 (CI 4.56–5.83) in Södermanland. The association varied significantly by regions (global test of interaction, p < 0.001). One-year mortality remained largely stable during the study period, although a small declining trend was observed following high proximal amputation (mortality rate ratio 0.986, 95% CI 0.972–0.999). Lower limb amputation was strongly associated with increased mortality compared with matched individuals without LLA, with poorer survival following more proximal amputation. The association was observed across all Swedish regions, although its magnitude varied significantly between regions. One-year mortality remained largely stable between 2008 and 2017, with a small declining trend following high proximal amputation. Exploratory analyses identified chronic kidney disease and heart failure among the comorbidities associated with increased mortality. These findings highlight the substantial mortality and systemic disease burden among individuals undergoing LLA.

Article.Title: Soil erosion response to future climate variability and best management practices in the Kesinga catchment, India
Article.Authors: Vani P.; Ravali C.; Pandit V.; Mahapatra S.; Chatterjee S.; Noorzai A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil erosion poses a growing threat to watershed sustainability under changing climatic conditions, particularly in monsoon-dominated regions. This study integrates the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) with bias-corrected CORDEX–South Asia climate projections to quantify present and future sediment yield and to evaluate the effectiveness of structural best management practices (BMPs) in the Kesinga catchment, eastern India. The watershed was delineated into 33 sub-catchments, and model calibration and validation (2003–2020) demonstrated very good performance for streamflow during calibration (NSE = 0.86) and good performance during validation (NSE = 0.72). Sediment-yield performance was satisfactory during calibration (NSE = 0.52) but unsatisfactory during validation (NSE = 0.49), according to the performance criteria adopted in this study. Future projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios indicate increases in streamflow (26–73%) and sediment yield (5–36%), with the greatest amplification under end-century RCP8.5 conditions; these sediment projections should be interpreted in light of the unsatisfactory validation performance. Spatial analysis revealed persistent sediment hotspots in central and eastern sub-catchments, where high slope gradients and projected precipitation intensification interact to enhance erosion risk. Across the future periods and scenarios, 40.2–51.2% of the catchment area was projected to fall within the severe-to-extreme erosion categories, with the highest proportion occurring under end-century RCP8.5. Structural BMPs, including grassed waterways (GWW) and vegetative filter strips (VFS), were implemented in priority sub-catchments. Under historical conditions, VFS and GWW reduced soil loss by 13% and 25%, respectively, while their combined application achieved up to 38% reduction. Although absolute sediment loads increased under future climates, combined BMP implementation consistently mitigated erosion by 27–36%, demonstrating potential for reducing sediment losses under intensified rainfall regimes. By explicitly linking projected climatic changes with sediment response and BMP performance at the sub-catchment scale, this study provides a spatially targeted framework for climate-resilient watershed management in monsoon-driven agro-ecosystems. The results highlight the need for proactive and spatially targeted implementation of integrated soil and water conservation measures in erosion-prone sub-catchments.

Article.Title: Multi-task learning for multi-goal path planning with path-cost estimation and heuristic-guided RRT sampling
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Lin W.; Zhai J.; Chen R.; Sun J.
Article.Abstract: Multi-goal path planning (MGPP) requires identifying a closed, collision-free trajectory that visits a set of goals in an optimal sequence. This is typically formulated as a Physical Traveling Salesman Problem, where the quality of the visiting order depends on an undirected complete graph with precise edge weights representing inter-vertex path lengths. However, calculating these weights efficiently in obstacle-rich environments remains a challenge, often leading to a trade-off between sequencing optimality and computational overhead. To address this, we propose a multi-task learning model termed Prior Information Extraction (PIE). The PIE model concurrently estimates inter-vertex path lengths for graph construction and generates “promising regions” and “search guidelines” to serve as low-level heuristics. These outputs are integrated into a sampling-based framework, PIE-MGPP, which bridges high-level sequencing with low-level motion planning. Specifically, PIE-MGPP utilizes the model-generated weights to determine a prioritized visiting order, while the predicted regions and guidelines focus the RRT-based search toward high-probability configuration spaces. Extensive numerical experiments based on training-source and unseen maps demonstrate that PIE-MGPP achieved high planning success rates and shorter paths among successful cases, while using fewer samples than evaluated baselines.

Article.Title: Research on the dimension reduction of the partial discharge feature space for oil-paper insulated power transformer
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang P.; Chu Z.; Gao C.; Fan X.; Du Z.; Zhang Y.; Peng G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oil-paper insulation condition directly affects transformer reliability. This study evaluates how dimensionality-reduction performance varies with feature type and diagnostic task using laboratory-simulated gas-gap, column-to-plate, pin-to-plate, and inter-turn partial discharges. Statistical (67-dimensional), waveform (13-dimensional), dissolved-gas-analysis (17-dimensional), and combined (97-dimensional) feature spaces were reduced using KPCA, CCMDR, and RST. RST produced the greatest separability improvement for statistical, waveform, and combined features, whereas CCMDR performed best for DGA. With BPNN, combined features with CCMDR achieved the highest defect-type accuracy (93.02%), and combined features with RST achieved the highest severity accuracy (91.86%). Matched RBF-SVM and Random Forest experiments preserved the ordering of all 16 feature-space/reduction configurations (Spearman rho = 1.000 for both tasks). In sequential type-severity recognition, combined CCMDR-RST achieved the highest joint accuracy (90.70%), while waveform RST-RST had a lower normalized batch-processing time (0.228 versus 0.923 s per test sample); both were Pareto-efficient. The results provide feature- and task-specific selection guidance among the evaluated methods. Because the evidence is limited to laboratory single-source defects, field validation is required before deployment.

Article.Title: Development of fertilizer spreading mechanism for UAV-based fertilizer applicator
Article.Authors: Soni S.; Singh S.; Sahni R.; Kumar S.; Agrawal K.; Babu V.
Article.Abstract: Efficient fertilizer application is vital for crop productivity, but conventional broadcasting is labor-intensive, time-consuming and often leads to uneven distribution, whereas UAVs offer a precise alternative. This study developed and evaluated a UAV-mounted spreading disc mechanism for urea application to improve distribution uniformity and optimize operational parameters. The system comprises a rectangular hopper (39° slope), a flow control unit, and interchangeable discs with 2–6 vanes. Laboratory trials followed a factorial design with flight height (1–3 m) and vane number (2–6), assessing fertilizer deposition using tray collectors and evaluating uniformity via coefficient of variation (CV). Deposition patterns were consistently right-skewed. Increasing vane number improved uniformity, reducing CV from 55.80% (2 vanes) to 38.21% (6 vanes). Higher flight height and lateral distance decreased uniformity, with CV increasing from 36.04% at 1 m to 56.03% at 3 m, and from 21.08% at 2 m to 70.83% at 20 m. Optimal performance occurred at 2 m flight height with 6 vanes, achieving a CV of 30.37% at 4 m lateral distance. The study demonstrates that UAV-mounted spreading disc mechanisms can effectively complement conventional ground equipment by enhancing efficiency and precision in fertilizer management.

Article.Title: YOLO vs. diffusion networks for underground pipe detection: a case study using ground penetrating radar data
Article.Authors: Senousy D.; Saad O.; Ebrahim S.; Abbas A.; Gody A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The accurate detection and mapping of underground pipelines are critical for urban planning and infrastructure resilience. This process is critical to prevent catastrophic failures, minimize service disruptions, and maintain the structural integrity of public works projects. Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a prominent technology for the automated detection and precise localization of subsurface utilities. However, the current dependence on manual data interpretation is a major bottleneck, often resulting in high temporal and operational costs. Consequently, this research addresses these limitations by presenting a performance analysis of two distinct deep learning architectures–YOLO (You Only Look Once) and Diffusion-based neural networks–for automated underground pipe detection. Utilizing a specific dataset of GPR scans, the models were evaluated using a robust five-fold cross-validation framework to assess mean Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (mAP50) and inference latency. The experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-based architectures provide a superior balance between detection precision and real-time processing efficiency. While five-fold cross-validation established a mean mAP50 of approximately 80% for the YOLO models, the YOLOv12n architecture exhibited superior performance on the independent test set, achieving an mAP50 of 94%. In contrast, DiffusionDet models were characterized by lower precision and significantly higher latency. While this study focuses on a single-site case study, the findings establish a foundational baseline for the selection of deep learning architectures and provide a framework for future research into the adaptation of these models across varying geological conditions.

Article.Title: Cumulative exposure to TyG-BRI and risk of incident cardiovascular disease across CKM syndrome stages 0–3: evidence from the CHARLS Prospective Cohort
Article.Authors: Chen L.; Chen Q.; Fang H.; Zheng H.
Article.Abstract: Despite advances in cardiovascular risk stratification, tools that adequately capture cumulative cardiometabolic burden remain limited, particularly in non-Western populations. The association between cumulative triglyceride–glucose index and body roundness index (cumTyG-BRI) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) across the spectrum of Cardiovascular–Kidney–Metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains to be elucidated. We conducted a prospective cohort analysis of 3,367 adults aged ≥ 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) spanning CKM stages 0–3 (follow-up: 2015–2020). CumTyG-BRI was computed via the trapezoid method. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for incident CVD, with restricted cubic splines assessing nonlinearity and Kaplan–Meier curves illustrating cumulative risk. Robustness was confirmed via subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses. Among 3,367 participants, 638 CVD events occurred (18.9%). Higher CumTyG-BRI was associated with greater CVD risk in a threshold-dependent rather than linear manner (Q4 vs. Q1: HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.19–2.02; P for trend < 0.001), with risk elevation concentrated at the highest exposure quartile and corroborated by restricted cubic spline analysis. Kaplan-Meier curves showed progressively diverging survival probabilities (log-rank P < 0.0001). In this prospective cohort of Chinese adults aged ≥ 45 years, cumTyG-BRI showed a threshold-dependent association with incident CVD risk. Given that its constituent measures require only readily available metabolic parameters, cumTyG-BRI warrants further investigation as a potential index for CVD risk stratification, particularly in populations with high cardiometabolic burden.

Article.Title: Petroleum systems and hydrocarbon prospectivity of the offshore Garad Basin, north-central Somalia
Article.Authors: Ali M.; Hussein H.; Abdelmaksoud A.; Ali M.; Jabir M.
Article.Abstract: The petroleum potential of the offshore Garad Basin in north-central Somalia remains poorly constrained. This study provides an integrated reassessment of the basin’s structural framework and petroleum system using 2D seismic reflection and well data, and 1D/2D basin modeling. Seismic interpretation reveals coast-parallel culminations, tilted fault blocks, and rollover structures at shelf-to-upper slope depths, with several closures identified within the Upper Cretaceous interval. The Upper Jurassic Uarandab marine mudstone is identified as the main source rock in the offshore Garad Basin, with an average thickness of approximately 95 m. Basin modeling results, calibrated to vitrinite reflectance data, indicate that the Uarandab source rock entered the oil window during the Oligocene and reached the main oil window by the Middle–Late Miocene beneath the shelf and upper slope. Transformation ratios increase basinward and approach expulsion thresholds in depocenters during the interval of Oligocene–Miocene trap formation. The Upper Cretaceous Gira rudist-shoal carbonates constitute the main reservoir targets, with dolomitized Hamanlei stringers representing secondary prospects. Key exploration risks include pre-Aptian truncation of the Uarandab source, trap breach during Oligocene–Miocene reactivation, and depth conversion uncertainty. Future work should include long-offset 2D/3D seismic acquisition, checkshot/VSP data, and geochemical calibration to better constrain source kitchens and structural closures.

Article.Title: Creep deformation until failure under constant water content in sandy model slope
Article.Authors: Sasahara K.
Article.Abstract: The measurement of displacement on slopes under excavation or rainfall revealed that the displacement increased not only during excavation or rainfall but also afterward. The increase in displacement after stress loading can be identified as creep displacement under constant stress. However, the conditions for the generation of creep displacements are still unknown. To this end, inclined direct shear tests were conducted under constant stress and rainfall infiltration, and the measured data were analyzed to examine the conditions for creep displacement generation under rainfall infiltration. In some cases, shear displacement grew under constant volumetric water content (VWC) just prior to failure, but not in other cases. In the latter cases, shear displacement grew with increasing VWC. An accelerating increase in shear displacement just prior to failure—referred to as tertiary creep—could be observed in all cases in which shear displacement increased under constant VWC; meanwhile, a decelerating increase in shear displacement just after the start of the constant VWC duration—referred to as primary creep—could not be observed in some cases. The creep displacement normalized by all shear displacements until failure was larger when the increase in VWC corresponding to the shear displacement during soil absorption was greater. Thus, a larger increase in VWC corresponding to shear displacement during the absorption process is a condition for the generation of creep displacement under constant VWC. Primary creep displacement developed under the condition of no normal displacement, indicating a steady state in the shear zone. The primary creep displacement was greater for cases with a higher initial velocity at the start of the constant VWC duration. Thus, the absence of an increase in normal displacement under constant VWC may be a condition for the generation of primary creep, and a larger primary creep might be generated with a larger initial displacement velocity at the start of the constant VWC duration. The relationships between velocity and acceleration derived from the measured shear displacement during both the primary and tertiary creep stages are identical and linear on a logarithmic scale for each case. A future study will establish methods for predicting creep shear displacement based on the simple relationships between the velocity and acceleration derived from the measured displacement.

Article.Title: Association between serum uric acid and elevated blood pressure among pregnant women in Bangladesh: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ali N.; Begum J.; Mou A.
Article.Abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy remain a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity worldwide. Serum uric acid (SUA) has emerged as a potential biomarker of endothelial dysfunction and cardiometabolic risk during pregnancy, yet evidence from Bangladesh is scarce. This study investigated the association between SUA concentrations and elevated blood pressure among pregnant women in Bangladesh. This cross-sectional study included 194 pregnant women attending antenatal care in two districts of Bangladesh. Serum SUA and cardiometabolic biomarkers were measured using standard laboratory methods. Participants were categorized into SUA quartiles, and multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between SUA and elevated blood pressure. The mean age of the participants was 25 ± 5 years, while 16.9% had hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and 12.4% had preeclampsia. Women in the highest SUA quartile (≥ 5.5 mg/dL) had significantly higher systolic blood pressure (129.4 vs. 113.5 mmHg), diastolic blood pressure (81.8 vs. 71.4 mmHg), and mean arterial pressure (97.7 vs. 81.3 mmHg) than those in the lowest quartile (all P < 0.01). Increasing SUA levels were also associated with higher TG, TG/HDL-C ratio, and LDL/HDL-C ratio, whereas HDL-C levels decreased significantly ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of elevated blood pressure increased across SUA quartiles. In multivariable analysis, each 1 mg/dL increase in SUA was associated with a 38% higher odds of elevated blood pressure (adjusted OR: 1.38, 95% CI 1.03–1.86; P < 0.05). Compared with women in the lowest SUA quartile, those in the higher quartiles had approximately three- to four-fold greater odds of elevated blood pressure after adjustment for potential confounders. Overall, in all models SUA showed a significant association with elevated blood pressure. In conclusion, higher SUA concentrations were independently associated with elevated blood pressure and an adverse cardiometabolic profile among pregnant women in Bangladesh. However, due to the cross-sectional design, modest sample size, and lack of temporal assessment, the study findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality or prospective predictive ability. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine whether SUA measured earlier in pregnancy provides additional value for identifying women who subsequently develop gestational hypertension or preeclampsia.

Article.Title: EEG network features and APOE ε4 for amyloid classification in mild cognitive impairment
Article.Authors: Kong J.; So M.; Lee I.; Park H.; Kim Y.; Kim H.; Kim H.; Kang S.; Do S.; Lim D.; Lee C.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) may provide information complementary to apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) for identifying amyloid pathology in mild cognitive impairment. We evaluated this hypothesis in an exploratory cross-sectional study of 93 patients, including 54 with amyloid-positive positron emission tomography, using EEG functional connectivity, graph features and 11 classifiers under nested cross-validation. In the original partition, extreme gradient boosting with all domains achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.806 versus 0.682 for its APOE-only model (paired difference 0.124, 95% confidence interval 0.010–0.238). The median paired difference across 30 additional partitions was 0.088. Among non-carriers, the combined model identified 11 of 16 amyloid-positive patients, with 10 false positives among 31 amyloid-negative patients. The gain was smaller against carrier status used directly (difference 0.057, −0.043–0.157). Nesting classifier selection reduced the median AUC to 0.734, and alternative EEG epoch samples yielded AUCs of 0.571–0.773 on the original partition. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of complementary EEG and genetic information, while demonstrating dependence on the comparator, model selection and epoch sampling. Reliable EEG estimation and external validation are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Genetic Characterization, phytochemical analysis and evaluation of the antioxidant and wound healing activities of Phyllanthus angustifolius Sw. and Phyllanthus emblica L
Article.Authors: Gabr S.; Bakr R.; Okba M.; Elshishtawy H.; ElFishawy A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phyllanthus species are widely recognized for their medicinal value, with Phyllanthus emblica being extensively studied, whereas Phyllanthus angustifolius remains comparatively under-investigated. This study aimed to comparatively characterize the genetic and phytochemical profiles, antioxidant capacity, and in vitro scratch closure activity of P. angustifolius and P. emblica . Genetic characterization was performed using primers targeting chalcone synthase (CHS), cinnamate 4-hydroxylase (C4H), phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL), and D-galacturonate reductase (GalUR). While both species yielded positive amplicons for key biosynthetic genes, distinct differences in the PCR amplification patterns for the phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL) locus were observed. These variations reflect genetic diversity rather than functional gene absence, underscoring the need for sequencing and expression analyses to clarify metabolic regulation. Colorimetric assays showed that P. angustifolius had a higher total flavonoid content, whereas P. emblica had a higher tannin content. HPLC-DAD analysis identified several phenolic acids and flavonoids, with gallic acid and quercetin among the predominant identified constituents. P. emblica exhibited higher antioxidant activity across the DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP assays and showed greater scratch closure than P. angustifolius under the tested conditions. Notably, the stronger antioxidant and scratch closure responses of P. emblica coincided with differences in its overall phytochemical profile, including its higher tannin content and markedly higher gallic acid content, whereas the higher total flavonoid content of P. angustifolius did not correspond to greater antioxidant or scratch closure activity. These findings suggest that the observed biological differences may reflect the combined contribution of the overall phytochemical composition rather than the abundance of a single compound class. Further mechanistic and in vivo studies are required to determine the constituents and pathways contributing to these activities.
