Article.Title: Maternal weight gain at embryonic day 8.5 predicts ongoing pregnancy in timed-mated mice
Article.Authors: Borsboom T.; Munsteren J.; van Leeuwen R.; ter Veld M.; Goumans M.; DeRuiter M.
Article.Abstract: Timed mating is widely used in reproductive and developmental studies in mice, but early pregnancy confirmation remains challenging. Copulation-plug detection is unreliable, whereas palpation or ultrasonography is either suitable only at later stages or requires additional handling, stress, specific expertise, or expensive equipment. In this study, we retrospectively evaluated maternal Δ-weight, relative to body weight at mating, as a simple, non-invasive screening method for early prediction of pregnancy. Body weight was recorded on the presumed day of mating, between ED7.5 and ED10.5, and after ED15.5. Pregnancy outcome was confirmed at the experimental endpoint, before parturition. After excluding records associated with pregnancy loss, we analyzed 877 weight records from 290 unique females. Maternal Δ-weight increased consistently over time, with embryonic day and pregnancy status as the strongest predictors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified Δ-weight measured at ED8.5 as the strongest predictor of pregnancy, with an optimized threshold of 1.59 g yielding 93.5% sensitivity, 92.4% specificity, and an area under the curve of 0.964. Compared with the previously reported 1.75 g threshold, the lower cutoff reduced false-negative classifications while only modestly increasing false positives. Genetic background was not independently associated with weight gain, while baseline maternal weight had only a limited effect. Maternal weight gain at 8.5 days after timed mating provides an alternative screening method for identifying (non-) pregnant females. Its use may reduce unnecessary handling, stress, and experimental interventions, thereby improving not only the efficiency but also the refinement of timed mating studies.

Article.Abstract: Chrysanthemum seticuspe is an herbaceous Asteraceae species with a diploid genome, and investigations of wild traits in Japan led to the discovery of Gojo-0, which shows self-compatibility. When comparing Rhizobium strains by infection efficiency, AGL0 was more transformable than EHA105. Based on these findings, we transformed AGL0 with pBIK201iGs, which expresses the intron- gusA and w- nptII genes under the mas1 ′ -2 ′ bidirectional promoter, and successfully transformed Gojo-1. This protocol will be useful for isolating and functionally analyzing unidentified genes underlying not only physiologically and genetically important events but also metabolically important ones.

Article.Title: Multi-level assessment of Myristica fragrans-induced reproductive toxicity using reciprocal mating crosses in Drosophila melanogaster
Article.Authors: Maged A.; El-Kholy S.; Nagy M.; Elbrense H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Myristica fragrans (nutmeg), a common culinary spice with diverse biological activities, has received little attention regarding its reproductive toxicity following dietary exposure. Therefore, this study investigated the sublethal reproductive toxicity of nutmeg crude extract using Drosophila melanogaster as a model organism. Adult flies were exposed to graded concentrations of the extract through their diet to determine the median lethal concentration (LC 50 ). Following LC 50 determination, sublethal effects were evaluated using reciprocal mating assays, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of reproductive tissues, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis, and molecular docking of the major identified constituent with selected reproductive-related and antioxidant receptors. The extract produced concentration- and time-dependent mortality, with LC₅₀ values decreasing from 0.041 mg/mL fly diet after 24 h to 0.017 mg/ mL fly diet after 72 h. More importantly, sublethal exposure significantly reduced fecundity, delayed offspring development, and decreased adult emergence. TEM analysis revealed pronounced ultrastructural alterations in both ovaries and testes, with male reproductive tissues exhibiting greater susceptibility. GC–MS analysis identified several bioactive constituents previously implicated in reproductive toxicity, while molecular docking predicted favorable binding affinities of the major identified compound toward selected reproductive and antioxidant-related receptors. These findings demonstrate that dietary exposure to M. fragrans extract can adversely affect reproductive function in D. melanogaster with sex-dependent effects.

Article.Title: Calculation of the brilliance of advanced accelerator-based x-ray sources
Article.Authors: Elisii F.; Di Mitri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In regime of diffraction-limited electron beams at x-ray wavelengths, the spectral width of fundamental spontaneous undulator radiation is at ~ 1% level, and down to 0.01% for free-electron lasers. Consequently, the traditional characterization of brilliance in units of 0.1% bandwidth tends to overestimate the actual brilliance of longitudinally coherent sources. An update version of the brilliance plot in units of 0.01% relative bandwidth is proposed. It is shown that, in order to match experimental and simulated data, the calculation has to take into consideration a non-uniform electron current profile in self-amplified spontaneous emission, and the scaling of the light pulse duration with the harmonic jump in seeded architectures. More accurate and general brilliance expressions are therefore provided. A closed-form is found for the saturation length, providing an exact value in place of well-known but semi-quantitative estimations reported in the literature.

Article.Title: Relationship between molecular polarity of exhaled air condensate and interleukin concentrations in asthmatic patients in different body mass index groups
Article.Authors: Khadem Sadigh M.; Seyedrezazadeh E.; Zakerhamidi M.; Ansarin K.
Article.Abstract: Both asthma and obesity can be associated with altered airway inflammatory responses; however, it is unclear whether these changes are also reflected in the physicochemical properties of exhaled breath condensate (EBC). This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between EBC polarity parameters and IL-6, IL-8, and IL-17 concentrations in 88 participants, including 46 asthmatics and 42 healthy controls. Asthmatic subjects were stratified into three groups based on BMI. EBC polarity parameters were described using three parameters: hydrogen bond acidity (α), hydrogen bond basicity (β), and dipolarity/polarizability (π*). Because β and π* polarity parameters showed perfect collinearity, π* was excluded from the multiparameter analysis. Multiparameter linear analysis was used to assess the relationship between polarity parameters (α and β) and cytokine concentrations. The results showed substantial explanatory power for IL-6, IL-8, and IL-17 concentrations. The explanatory power of the models varied across subgroups, with R² values ranging from 0.73 to 0.97; however, estimates obtained from subgroups with smaller sample sizes should be interpreted with caution. The relative contribution of α and β polarity parameters varied according to BMI, asthma status and inflammatory biomarker. Given the correlation between α and β, individual coefficients should be interpreted with caution. Therefore, these findings highlight the potential value of EBC polarity analysis as a complementary physicochemical approach to investigate airway inflammation in asthma and across different BMI groups; however, further confirmation and validation of these results is warranted.

Article.Authors: Liu L.; Ren G.; Fan X.; Yang Q.; Xiao X.; Dai S.; Yu T.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common chronic joint disorder, which is characterized by cartilage deterioration and joint function impairment. Recent studies suggest that mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) methylation is important for OA development. MiRNA-single nucleotide polymorphism-gene network analysis revealed 6 SNPs associated with CALML4 and 58 miRNAs. Valproic acid exhibited the highest correlation with CALML4 . RT-qPCR validation confirmed a statistically significant expression difference for MXRA5 between the OA and control groups, but not for CALML4 . The discrepancy between bioinformatics predictions and clinical validation indicates that CALML4 should be considered a candidate key gene, rather than a validated key gene. At the transcriptomic level, this study suggested that mtDNA methylation-related alterations might be involved in OA and identified CALML4 and MXRA5 as candidate OA-related genes requiring further validation. Of these, differential MXRA5 expression received preliminary support from RT-qPCR in a small sample, whereas the clinical diagnostic value of both genes still requires validation in large independent cohorts.

Article.Authors: Rasti Tadevani A.; Rasti Tadevani H.; Rezaeianzadeh S.; Haghighi A.; Shirazi S.; Pishdad P.; Karami S.; Soleimanpour S.; Moeini O.; Jafari S.
Article.Abstract: While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promise for automated choledocholithiasis detection on magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), transformer-based models have recently emerged as alternatives. However, the relative performance of these approaches for stone classification and localization remains unclear, necessitating systematic comparison. This study therefore compared selected CNN and transformer architectures for MRCP-based choledocholithiasis classification and detection. In this retrospective multicenter study (2022–2025) across two tertiary-care hospitals in Iran, patients with and without common bile duct (CBD) stones were included. CNN (ResNet50, YOLOv12) and transformer-based (Vision Transformer [ViT], RF-DETR) models were evaluated, with an independent dataset from a third institution reserved for external testing. The classification cohort included 1037 patients (523 with CBD stones; mean age 53 ± 14 years), and the detection cohort included 633 patients (523 with CBD stones; mean age 57 ± 16 years). On external cropped images, ResNet50 and ViT achieved accuracies of 96.0% (95% CI 93.5, 98.5) and 97.0% (95% CI 94.0, 99.0), with AUCs of 0.999 and 0.991, respectively; neither the accuracy difference ( P = 0.80) nor the AUC difference (DeLong P = 0.16) was statistically significant. On external uncropped images, ViT yielded significantly higher accuracy than ResNet50 (93.5% [95% CI 90.0, 96.5] vs. 87.0% [95% CI 82.5, 91.5]; P = 0.04), whereas the corresponding AUCs (0.979 vs. 0.969) did not differ significantly (DeLong P = 0.39). For object detection, RF-DETR achieved higher mAP@0.5:0.95 than YOLOv12 in both the internal (0.723 [95% CI 0.703, 0.744] vs. 0.687 [95% CI 0.667, 0.709]) and external test datasets (0.668 [95% CI 0.630, 0.707] vs. 0.626 [95% CI 0.588, 0.664]), with statistically significant differences for this metric in each dataset .In conclusion, selected CNN and transformer architectures demonstrated comparable diagnostic performance for MRCP-based choledocholithiasis classification. For object detection, RF-DETR demonstrated higher localization performance than YOLOv12 on the evaluated metrics.

Article.Authors: Nazarkhani M.; Kahraman S.

The 44.0% figure, not the exploratory 64.0% estimate, is this study’s headline finding; a transaction cost backtest of the four non visual representations shows flat to mildly positive returns despite near chance accuracy. Article.Title: IOT-enabled wearable device and cloud framework for chronic disease identification and health monitoring using LST-BCLNM
Article.Authors: Poongodi J.; Kavitha K.; R L.; P P.
Article.Abstract: The continuous monitoring of healthcare data addresses health anomalies and the timely reduction of the chronic disease risk. None of the existing works considered in mitigating the interference of Internet of Things (IoT) healthcare data meant for actual disease identification, besides monitoring. Therefore, this paper presents the mitigation of IoT data interference and healthcare data analysis. Initially, the data from IoT-based wearable devices, healthcare apps, and patient symptoms data are collected. Then, the interference between the IoT data is mitigated using the Sparsity-inducing Reinforcement Learning Regularized Least Mean Square (S-2(RL)MS) technique. Next, the data is secured using the Hyperbolic Tangent Elliptic Logistic Curve Cryptography (HTELCC). Also, the data is transmitted to the edge node based on Ontology Weighted Fair Queuing (OWFQ). In the edge node, data is filtered and aggregated. Then, the features are extracted, and by utilizing Long Short-Term Batch-Centric Layer Normalization Memory (LST-BCLNM), the anomaly is detected. For the presence of disease (anomaly), information is secured and sent to the cloud server. Apache Kafka processes big data, while LST-BCLNM extracts features and classifies chronic diseases accurately. Finally, to access the healthcare data, the doctor/healthcare provider registers and logs into the cloud server. Experimental evaluation demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed IoT-cloud healthcare framework. The LST-BCLNM model achieved 97.58% classification accuracy, 96.56% precision, 97.24% recall, and 98.95% F-measure, while HTELCC attained 98.82% security and S-2(RL)MS achieved a 98.51% convergence rate. These results confirm improved healthcare data reliability, security, and chronic disease monitoring performance.

Article.Title: Establishment and characterization of an HFD-induced mouse model of obesity-associated male hypogonadism
Article.Authors: Cai Y.; Yao Y.; Xu J.; Chen Q.; Wang B.
Article.Abstract: To establish and characterize a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced mouse model of obesity-associated male hypogonadism (MOSH) with impaired sperm quality and define the minimal modeling duration. Forty 6-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were fed a standard diet or a 60% HFD for 10, 12, or 14 weeks. We analyzed body weight, adiposity, serum lipids, reproductive hormones, sperm quality, and testicular histology/ultrastructure. While 10-week HFD induced only obesity and dyslipidemia, 12- and 14-week HFD elicited a MOSH-like phenotype. These included significant hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (reduced testosterone, LH and FSH, elevated estradiol), impaired sperm quality (decreased concentration, motility and vitality), and structural testicular damage (seminiferous tubule atrophy and spermatogenic epithelial disruption). Notably, ultrastructural analysis revealed ferroptosis-like morphological features in Leydig cells. No significant differences were observed between the 12- and 14-week groups. At 12 weeks, HFD-fed animals exhibit obesity and reproductive alterations consistent with the MOSH phenotype. Although further validation is required, this model represents a promising platform for studying MOSH pathogenesis and assessing potential therapeutic interventions.

Article.Authors: Nanthakumar P.; Balaji K.
Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) flex-banner waste presents long-term persistence and chlorine-related disposal concerns, whereas soapnut seed biomass (SN; Sapindus mukorossi) is an underutilized lignocellulosic residue with thermochemical conversion potential. This study investigates the co-pyrolysis of SN and PVC waste in a 1:1 blend to explore synergistic interactions for enhanced bio-oil and char production. Proximate and ultimate analyses revealed comparable volatile content—71.29% for SN and 68.31% for PVC—supporting an optimal blend ratio. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), conducted at heating rates of 10, 15, 20, and 25 °C/min up to 800 °C, demonstrated a substantial reduction in char residue for the SNPVC blend (10.48%) relative to both the individual feedstocks (20.04% for SN, 27.43% for PVC) and to the non-interacting additive prediction of 23.74%, corresponding to a char suppression of 13.3% points and indicating a pronounced synergistic effect. Kinetic parameters were evaluated using model-free methods—Kissinger, Kissinger-Akahira-Sunose (KAS), Flynn-Wall-Ozawa (FWO), and Starink—yielding activation energy ranges of 132–142 kJ/mol for SN, 90–100 kJ/mol for PVC, and 105–110 kJ/mol for the SNPVC blend. The apparent thermodynamic parameters ΔH, ΔG, and ΔS were evaluated for comparative analysis of the activated-complex energy barrier. Because SNPVC pyrolysis is a multi-component, multi-step process, these quantities are not interpreted as true thermodynamic state functions of the overall conversion. Bio-oil produced at 600 °C was characterized via FTIR revealing functional groups such as O–H, C–H, C = O, C = C, and C–X, confirming the presence of oxygenated and halogenated compounds. The findings demonstrate the potential of co-pyrolysis for synergistically converting biomass and plastic waste into valuable products while reducing solid residue, highlighting its relevance for sustainable waste management.

Article.Title: A region-aware spatial-frequency adaptive fusion framework for robust single image dehazing
Article.Authors: Lam S.; Kandala N.; Sunil Kumar T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Atmospheric haze diminishes image visibility, contrast, and obscure fine details, adversely affecting visual perception and high-level vision tasks. Although prior-based dehazing methods have shown promising performance, these approaches relying solely on either the dark channel or bright channel prior estimates. These estimates, often fail to handle both non-sky and sky regions simultaneously. This paper proposes a region-aware spatial-frequency adaptive fusion framework. It integrates the complementary strengths of dark and bright channel priors transmission maps for effective scene radiance recovery. The fused image is further enhanced using Non-Subsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT) based processing, incorporating gamma correction for low frequency components and wavelet-based denoising for high frequency components. Extensive experiments on five publicly available datasets demonstrate consistent performance based on PSNR, SSIM and other image-quality metrics. The proposed method demonstrates competitive performance with several conventional and deep learning-based dehazing approaches.

Article.Title: Randomised trial of 1-kestose supplementation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
Article.Authors: Mizuno F.; Yamamoto K.; Honda T.; Yokoyama S.; Ito T.; Imai N.; Ishizu Y.; Furukawa K.; Nakamura M.; Kinoshita F.; Kadota Y.; Tochio T.; Kitaura Y.; Shimomura Y.; Hirooka Y.; Kawashima H.
Article.Abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is implicated in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but the clinical utility of prebiotic modulation remains unclear. We conducted a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial of oral 1-kestose in patients with MASLD and chronically elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels. Sixty participants were randomised to receive 1-kestose or placebo for 8 weeks and followed until week 16. The primary endpoint was the change in serum ALT from baseline to week 8, analysed as a continuous outcome. In baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, the between-group difference at week 8 was 3.4 U/L (95% CI, − 11.0 to 17.9; p = 0.636), indicating no significant treatment effect. In a supportive responder analysis, an ALT reduction of ≥ 20 U/L occurred in 20.7% of the 1-kestose group and 27.6% of the placebo group. In contrast, 1-kestose increased the relative abundance of Bifidobacterium at week 8; increased abundance was observed in 23/26 participants in the 1-kestose group and 10/26 in the placebo group. Faecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations did not differ between groups. 1-Kestose was well tolerated and modulated the gut microbiota during treatment but did not demonstrate short-term hepatic efficacy.

Article.Title: Stage harmonized temporal survival comparisons in de novo metastatic breast cancer using SEER
Article.Authors: Fang K.; Jiang S.; Luo M.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Temporal survival comparisons in cancer registries depend on how stage is harmonized across changing coding systems. We analyzed SEER 17 breast cancers diagnosed in 2000–2023 using a year-specific TNM-priority M-stage algorithm. The primary cohort comprised 35,262 de novo M1 cases diagnosed in 2010–2023 with complete covariate and outcome data. Contemporary (2014–2023) versus Transition (2010–2013) diagnosis was associated with lower breast cancer-specific mortality before adjustment (hazard ratio [HR], 0.870; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.845–0.897) and after demographic and organ-site adjustment (HR, 0.844; 95% CI 0.819–0.870). Transition-target inverse probability weighting produced a similar estimate (HR, 0.853; 95% CI 0.827–0.879). A strict TNM analysis was unchanged, whereas the prior any-positive-stage rule yielded a near-null crude estimate. Because proportional hazards were not constant, the overall HR is an average association; adjusted HRs were 0.879 during 0–24 months and 0.801 after 24 months. The 36-month overall-survival restricted mean difference was 0.66 months (95% CI 0.34–0.99). These observational findings show that stage harmonization materially influences temporal comparisons and do not identify effects of imaging or treatment.

Article.Title: Experimental demonstration of the ensemble approach for understanding the principles of drifting chaotic systems
Article.Authors: Dudkowski D.; Wojewoda J.; Herein M.; Tél T.; Haszpra T.; Kapitaniak T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Complex systems subjected to parameter drift require an ensemble approach in their investigation. In such cases, an individual trajectory is insufficient to capture the global changes in the system. In​ this paper we report the first experiment on low–dimensional chaotic mechanical systems subjected to considerable drift, resulting in six measured time series. Our set–up is based on three double pendula excited through the shaker, which allows to control and drift the excitation amplitude applied to the units. The equations of motion used for this system are shown to be consistent with the experiments: any single measurement is within the band of the ensemble simulation and traverses the band occasionally, after a sufficiently long time. The evaluation of the global dynamics can be understood with the concept of snapshot attractors , arising on the route from system initialization to a time–dependent chaotic steady state. The results presented in this paper experimentally confirm earlier simulation–only studies, expanding the concept of ensemble dynamics into more practical scenarios.

Article.Title: Methionine-stabilized Ag@Ag2O nanostructures synthesized using banana peel extract for spectrophotometric biomolecule determination
Article.Authors: Rahmannezhad F.; Tarighat M.; Abdi G.
Article.Abstract: In this study, a colorimetric sensor for determining epinephrine and uric acid is presented, which uses the LSPR property of silver nanostructure for measurement. The Ag@Ag 2 O nanoparticles were synthesized by green method using banana peel extract. To improve selectivity and sensitivity of measurement, the surface of nanostructure was modified by methionine (Met). Morphology of the Ag@Ag 2 O@Met nanocomposite (Ag@Ag 2 O-Met NCs) was investigated by XRD, FTIR and SEM analysis. The zeta potential and DLS characteristics of Ag@Ag 2 O and Ag@Ag 2 O-Met nanocomposites were investigated. The results indicated that surface modification with methionine alters the zeta potential and causes its hydrodynamic size to increase from approximately 38 nm to 206.1 to 326.4 nm in the presence of the analytes. These values suggest that inter-particle interactions and aggregation of nanostructure are enhanced in the presence of analytes. This phenomenon may result from surface variation in the surface interactions following methionine modification, which has led to an LSPR shift and a colorimetric response. The SEM results of Ag@Ag 2 O-Met NCs confirmed the star-like morphology of the nanoparticles and showed that methionine as a coating and stabilizing agent. Therefore, it can control the growth of crystals in certain directions and form a specific nanostructure growth. The effect of important experimental parameters including pH, amount of Met and Ag@Ag 2 O-Met NCs was investigated. Under the optimal conditions, the method provided 0.1–60 µM, and 0.8–20 µM linear dynamic ranges and detection limits 0.06 and 0.08 µM for, uric acid and epinephrine, respectively. To evaluate the performance of the sensor, Ag@Ag 2 O-Met NCs was used for determination of targets in the urine, ampoule and water samples. No significant statistical difference was found between the means of proposed method and standard addition results at the 95% confidence level. Comparing the results of study with the reported methods reveals the advantages of methods such as wide linear ranges and low detection limits. Therefore, it can be used as a sensitive and selective method in determining epinephrine and uric acid in real-complex samples.

Article.Title: Mathematical modelling of ensemble-based federated learning framework for false data injection attacks detection in artificial intelligence of things
Article.Authors: Yakobu D.; Praveena S.; Lydia E.; Rajesh M.; Reddy V.; Pattanaik C.; Saha M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) has allowed intelligent data-driven decision-making under several cyber-physical systems (CPS) like smart cities, smart grids, industrial automation, and healthcare monitoring. AIoT incorporates artificial intelligence (AI) methods with IoT devices to develop large volumes of sensor data and improve system efficacy, automation, and predictive proficiencies. Among different forms of attacks, the false data injection attack (FDIA) has proven that high-priority cyber-related problem and has received more attention recently. The FDIA detection is an important security process in the smart grid controller system and is resolved by data-driven machine learning (ML) algorithms. Now, Federated Learning (FL) is a well-known ML method that assists in addressing data privacy problems by permitting users to collect its raw data locally and transferring it local model parameters only to the aggregator server to collectively train a shared global model. This paper develops a Federated Learning-Based Framework for Detecting Attacks Using an Ensemble Classification Model (FLFDA-ECM) in distributed cybersecurity systems within the Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) environment. The major intention of the FLFDA-ECM paper is to propose an FL-based cybersecurity framework for detecting and classifying FDIA in AIoT- enabled distributed systems while preserving data privacy. At first, the data pre-processing contains dual levels, such as handling missing data and feature scaling to regularize the input data. In the feature selection stage, the hybrid approach integrates minimum redundancy maximum relevance and ReliefF techniques to recognize the most appropriate attributes. Furthermore, an ensemble-based weighted majority voting approach incorporating bi-directional gated recurrent unit, variational autoencoder, and temporal convolutional network models is employed for attack detection. Finally, the parameter fine-tuned model has been executed by the Adan optimizer to enhance the classifier solution. The performance evaluation of the FLFDA-ECM technique occurs using a benchmark dataset. The empirical outcomes specified the boosted performance of the FLFDA-ECM model in comparison with recent techniques.

Article.Title: Exchange property of resolvability parameters in molecular graphs of anti-Oropouche virus drugs with applications to drug delivery
Article.Authors: Ahmad M.; Hasni R.; Kashif A.
Article.Abstract: The exchange property of resolving sets plays an important role in resolvability theory by determining whether elements of one minimum resolving set can be exchanged with those of another while preserving minimality. Although this property has been investigated for several graph classes, it has not been studied for molecular graphs arising from anti-Oropouche virus antiviral drugs. In this paper, we investigate the exchange property associated with the metric dimension, edge metric dimension, and mixed metric dimension of the molecular graph of the antiviral drug Galidesivir. The molecular structure is modeled as a chemical graph in which vertices represent atoms and edges represent chemical bonds. Using graph-distance techniques, resolving-set constructions, distance representations, and rigorous mathematical proofs, we determine minimum metric, edge metric, and mixed resolving sets and establish the corresponding exchange properties. It is proved that the metric dimension, edge metric dimension, and mixed metric dimension of the Galidesivir molecular graph are all equal to 4, and that the exchange property holds for each of these resolvability parameters. These results provide new structural characterizations of the Galidesivir molecular graph, extend the theory of exchange properties to pharmaceutical molecular networks, and offer useful mathematical tools for molecular identification, structural classification, network navigation, and computer-aided drug design.

Article.Title: Predicted enhanced wear resistance and mechanical integrity in AA8011 composites via dual-ceramic ZrB2 and B4C reinforcement
Article.Authors: Anusha P.; Kumar R.; V. S.; Dixit R.; Mehta A.; Singh J.; Kumar N.; Ashok N.; Hussen K.; Bhowmik A.
Article.Abstract: The mechanical and dry-sliding wear characteristics of AA8011 aluminium matrix composites (AMCs) reinforced with 2, 4, 6 and 8 wt% zirconium diboride (ZrB₂) and boron carbide (B₄C) manufactured using the stir casting process at 760 °C and 380 rpm are explored. The microhardness, ultimate tensile strength (UTS), coefficient of friction (COF), and wear rate were systematically investigated as a function of reinforcement type, content and sliding distance. AAZ-8 composite showed that the microhardness was 93 HV, which is 34.78% higher than that of unreinforced AA8011 (69 HV), and ZrB₂ composite showed that its microhardness was 4.71–6.90% higher than AA8011/B₄C composite. The improvements in UTS were 42.2% and 45.5% for AAZ-8 and AA8011/8 wt% B₄C (AAB-8), respectively, when compared to AA8011 with UTS of 154 MPa. AA8011/8 wt% B₄C (AAB-8) resulted in 2.3–4.6% higher UTS than ZrB₂ at the same reinforcement concentration. The results of dry sliding tests with an EN31 steel counterface showed that the wear rate and COF decreased continuously as the reinforcement content increased and sliding distance carried out ranged from 600 m to 2400 m. The reasons for this improvement were attributed to improved load-bearing capacity, surface work hardening, debris redistribution and protective secondary tribological layers. The SEM analysis showed that the particles were evenly dispersed at 2 wt% reinforcement but, when the reinforcement level was increased to 8 wt%, particle clusters and local defects were observed. Worn surface analysis revealed an evolution from two-body abrasion to three-body abrasion, adhesive interaction, and mechanically mixed tribo-film formation with extended sliding. In general, ZrB₂ was mostly effective at increasing the hardness of the cemented materials, while B₄C was most effective at increasing tensile strength, indicating promising role of both reinforcements in engineering applications involving wear.

Article.Title: Effects of smart lighting actuation delay on the duration and stages of older adults’ simulated night-time bedside task
Article.Authors: Qu K.; Zhao Q.
Article.Abstract: Residential smart lighting turns light into an event with an arrival time, yet lighting standards for homes and care spaces address the steady-state environment and lack a checkable timing metric for the process from the bed-exit trigger to the moment the key path reaches the required light level. We ran a randomised two-factor mixed experiment in a house-scale laboratory in Hefei with 80 community-dwelling older adults aged 65 and above. Post-detection actuation delay was manipulated within participants at four levels (0.10, 0.70, 1.40, and 2.00 s), and spatial visual contrast was set between participants at two levels. Event timestamps split post-trigger arrival time into detection, movement-initiation, and walking stages, taken as proximal behavioural measures of task performance. Arrival time rose by 0.990 s from the shortest to the longest delay, and the fitted dose-response across the four tested levels was positive and convex. The movement-initiation stage accounted for 84.5% of the stage sum, walking time increased by a smaller amount, and detection showed no difference. At the longest delay most first steps landed before the switch-on command, so lighting response and user movement became less coordinated in time. In a secondary analysis for which the sample size was not planned, enhanced visual contrast was associated with a 0.808-s smaller delay effect. Exploratory analyses found low agreement between reported and measured event order, and satisfaction met the equivalence criterion among participants with observed paired ratings. Response timing should be specified as an end-to-end total delay in performance assessment.

Article.Title: Sensorless closed-loop speed estimation of BLDC motor drive using physics-informed NN algorithm
Article.Authors: Priyanka S.; Sriranjani R.; Jayalalitha S.
Article.Abstract: Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors are predominantly used in Electric Vehicle (EV) applications because of their higher efficiency, higher torque-to-weight ratio, lower maintenance requirements and capability to operate in a wide speed range. However, conventional sensor-based and traditional sensorless estimation methods experiences inaccurate performance under high-speed operating conditions because of parameter variations and nonlinear system dynamics. To overcome these limitations, this article implemented an improved sensorless Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based closed-loop speed estimation algorithm using Machine Learning (ML) based Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) algorithm specifically designed for high-speed applications. Performance of the implemented sensorless speed estimation scheme is experimentally validated and compared with conventional algorithms using the LAUNCHXL-F28379D development board. The experimental results indicates that the implemented method has a maximum steady-state error of 7 at 500 rpm and 8.95 at 1000 rpm between the actual motor speed and the reference speed. Furthermore, during higher operating speeds of 1500 rpm and 1600 rpm, the motor precisely tracks the reference speed.

Article.Title: Adaptive reinforcement learning-driven personalized training plan generation and effect evaluation for college students’ physical fitness tests
Article.Authors: Zhou Q.; Gao J.
Article.Abstract: Conventional college fitness training in China relies on uniform schedules that ignore between-student variability, producing marginal gains for many and elevated risk for those pushed beyond their adaptive ceiling. We propose an adaptive reinforcement learning framework that generates and revises individualized training plans aligned with the National Student Physical Health Standard. The framework binds five layers—input ingestion, adaptive feature extraction, an improved Proximal Policy Optimization decision module, plan rendering, and dual-rate feedback—into a closed loop that ingests fitness scores, demographic descriptors, and longitudinal training logs to issue weekly prescriptions across endurance, strength, and flexibility components. Because no agent may experiment on students, we treat the historical records as an offline decision problem: a validated student-response model supplies the state transitions, and returns for prescriptions the records never contain are estimated only inside the support of the teaching policy that generated them. Three design elements distinguish the system: a slowly refreshed adaptive state representation that absorbs cohort drift; a four-component reward with deficit-driven scalarization balancing fitness gain, safety, adherence, and plan rationality; and a bounded-staleness prioritized buffer with importance-sampling correction, paired with cosine-annealed learning rates, for stable convergence under noisy educational signals. Experiments on 4128 students from four cohorts, partitioned so that no student ever spans two folds, returned a composite fitness improvement of 14.6% in held-out cross-validation. A 16-week randomized field study with 312 participants produced a 13.8% gain against 7.1% in the control arm; the prespecified intention-to-treat mixed model places the adjusted between-arm effect at 4.71 composite points (95% CI 3.92–5.50), or roughly six percentage points of relative improvement. Plan rationality reached 91.7% and adherence 87.3%, with the largest absolute gains accruing to initially failing students. Adaptive reinforcement learning therefore offers a workable—though not yet longitudinally proven—path toward precision physical education in higher education settings.

Article.Title: Population ageing and the severity of recorded heat-disaster mortality: a global analysis, 2000–2022
Article.Authors: Alghais N.; Charabi Y.
Article.Abstract: Extreme heat is an increasing climate-related health risk, but the relationships among socioeconomic capacity, population ageing and recorded heat-disaster mortality remain uncertain. We analysed a harmonized 2000–2022 dataset comprising 155 EM-DAT heat-wave country-years with positive recorded mortality across 53 countries. Recorded deaths were highly concentrated: Europe accounted for 61.9% of observations and 94.4% of mortality, while three years accounted for 86.6% of deaths. A region-adjusted zero-truncated negative-binomial model estimated associations of GDP per capita, current health expenditure and the population share aged 65 years or older. At the sample means of log GDP per capita and log health expenditure, a one-percentage-point higher population share aged 65 years or older was associated with an approximately 11.0% higher underlying, untruncated NB2 mean parameter µ (95% CI, 1.3%–21.6%), holding national population and region fixed. This percentage describes µ, rather than expected mortality conditional on a positive count. The association remained positive across principal sensitivity analyses and all 53 leave-one-country-out refits, but both mortality-tail exclusion intervals included zero. Interactions of ageing with GDP and health expenditure were imprecisely estimated. Health expenditure showed a more clearly negative marginal association at lower Age 65 values, but these estimates were geographically concentrated. Exploratory nonlinear analysis did not support a robust structural-capacity threshold. These findings identify a sample-conditional association between population ageing and recorded mortality severity without establishing causal effects or systematic demographic modification of socioeconomic capacity.

Article.Authors: Imperio M.; Annibalini G.; Sisti D.; De Santi M.; Gobbi E.; Saltarelli R.; Wu R.; Minnock D.; Natalucci V.; Ferri Marini C.; Micheli L.; Grossi T.; Lucertini F.; Vallorani L.; Rocchi M.; Belli A.; Baldelli G.; Bartolacci A.; Donati Zeppa S.; Benelli P.; Vici G.; Polzonetti V.; Villarini A.; Barocci S.; Flori M.

Both groups improved cardiometabolic health, while the inter-day glucose variability increased in the control group. On exercise days, higher oligosaccharide and fiber intake and lower mean glucose were observed, whereas glucose level increased on non-exercise days, particularly in the control group. These findings support combining CGM with dietary logs and supervised aerobic exercise to assess glycemic variability, thereby potentially contributing to T2D prevention in BCS.

Article.Title: Development of CeO2 coated functional CNT-reinforced thin film for enhanced bonding and electrochemical nitrite sensing
Article.Authors: Alqurashi B.; Marwani H.; Rahman M.
Article.Abstract: Nitrite (NO₂⁻) contamination in water poses serious environmental and health risks, necessitating sensitive and reliable detection platforms. However, achieving strong film adhesion alongside high electrocatalytic performance remains a key challenge in electrochemical sensor design. This study aims to develop a mechanically robust and electrochemically active coating for nitrite sensing by reinforcing cerium oxide (CeO₂) nanoparticles with functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (f-MWCNTs), forming a CeO₂@f-MWCNT nanocomposite (NCs) that combines enhanced substrate bonding with efficient conductive pathways. The NCs was drop-casted onto a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) using a 5% Nafion binder, and its structural, morphological, and thermal properties were confirmed via Raman, XRD, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and TGA analyses. Electrochemical evaluation using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) demonstrated a significant electrocatalytic response toward NO₂⁻ oxidation, with a wide linear range (50.0 –4000.0 µM), high sensitivity (5.923 µA µM⁻¹cm⁻²), and a low detection limit (0.806 µM). The sensor further exhibited excellent selectivity, repeatability, and anti-interference performance, and reliably quantified nitrite in real environmental water samples. These results demonstrate that the CeO₂@f-MWCNT ceramic coating offers a mechanically stable, sensitive, and practical platform for electrochemical nitrite sensing, with strong potential for broader application in environmental water quality monitoring.

Article.Title: Swallowing biomechanics and upper esophageal sphincter pressure remain altered after esophagectomy for thoracic esophageal cancer
Article.Authors: Ono J.; Nishi H.; Ikenaga M.; Kobayashi S.; Kanetaka K.; Makimoto N.; Takashima S.; Mori A.; Nakamura M.; Morotomi Y.; Sawase K.; Soejima S.; Kumai Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative dysphagia is common after esophagectomy for thoracic esophageal cancer, but its long-term mechanisms remain poorly understood. This prospective study evaluated longitudinal changes in swallowing function and pressure dynamics through 6 months postoperatively. Thirteen patients who underwent subtotal esophagectomy with gastric conduit reconstruction were assessed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively using a videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS), fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES), and the Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10). High-resolution manometry (HRM) was performed preoperatively and at 6 months postoperatively. EAT-10 scores increased significantly at 1 and 3 months, while the median score remained above baseline at 6 months without reaching statistical significance. VFSS demonstrated significant reductions in laryngeal elevation distance (LED) and hyoid forward displacement at 6 months. HRM revealed a significant increase in upper esophageal sphincter integrated relaxation pressure (UES-IRP), whereas meso-hypopharyngeal contractile integral (MHPCI) was unchanged. LED was negatively correlated with UES-IRP. Additional analyses showed no significant relationships between EAT-10 and LED or UES-IRP. Exploratory regression analyses suggested an association between anastomotic stricture and higher 6 months EAT-10 scores. These findings indicate that objective biomechanical abnormalities may persist despite an unclear relationship with patient-reported symptoms, supporting multimodal assessment using subjective and objective measures.

Article.Authors: Dadellahi A.; Mohammadi A.
Article.Abstract: A novel sulfamethoxazole-based azo dye was synthesized as a molecular chemosensor and subsequently immobilized onto TiO₂ nanoparticles to fabricate a nanosensor for the selective colorimetric detection of Hg²⁺ ions. The synthesized chemosensors were comprehensively characterized by FT-IR, NMR, XRD, EDX, and FE-SEM analyses. Their sensing performance was evaluated using naked-eye detection and UV-Vis spectroscopy. Both chemosensors exhibited a distinct color change from yellow to orange upon exposure to Hg²⁺, enabling rapid visual detection with high selectivity over competing metal ions. Job’s plot confirmed a 1:1 binding stoichiometry, while the binding constant was determined to be 2.82 × 10 4 M − ¹. The molecular chemosensor showed a lower detection limit (0.37 µM) than the nanosensor (3.11 µM). Moreover, the Hg²⁺ recognition process was reversible, allowing repeated sensing without significant loss of performance. In addition, both the molecular chemosensor and nanosensor exhibited antibacterial effects against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Owing to their selective detection ability, satisfactory sensing performance, reusability, and antibacterial effects, the developed chemosensors represent promising candidates for Hg²⁺ detection in aqueous solutions.

Article.Title: Temperature-dependent buckling and mode jumping analysis of axially compressed composite profiles
Article.Authors: Falkowicz K.; Wysmulski P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper examines the temperature-dependent behavior of composite materials under axial compression across a wide temperature range, focusing on buckling mode transitions. Experimental tests were conducted using a servo-hydraulic MTS system at temperatures from − 20 °C to 80 °C. Load-displacement and load-deflection data were collected via a 3D DIC system, ensuring accurate characterization of the buckling response. Based on Classical Laminate Theory (CLT), the temperature-dependent laminate stiffness components were determined, with particular attention given to D 16 and D 26 , which describe bending–twisting coupling and may influence the evolution of buckling patterns and the susceptibility of the structure to transitions between competing equilibrium states. The main novelty of this study is the application of full-field 3D DIC to identify and track the development of mode-jumping phenomena during loading at different temperatures and to relate the observed changes to the temperature-dependent bending–twisting stiffness of the laminate. Mode transitions were identified from the redistribution of the out-of-plane displacement field and changes in the number and location of longitudinal half-waves. The results demonstrate that temperature significantly affects structural stiffness, deformation capacity, and the evolution of post-buckling patterns. Lower temperatures produced a stiffer structural response, whereas higher temperatures resulted in greater deformability and larger displacements before failure. The study provides new experimental insight into the temperature-dependent evolution of buckling patterns and mode-jumping pathways in thin-walled composite profiles. These findings may support the design and assessment of CFRP load-bearing components operating under variable temperature conditions, particularly in aerospace and other high-performance engineering applications.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware overturning stability and operating boundaries of a compact transport vehicle-mounted crane boom
Article.Authors: Ding W.; Zhang Q.; Dai Y.; Zhao F.; Cui H.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: A compact transport vehicle with a crane boom is assessed using signed moments about support edges. The framework links seven specified configurations to operating boundaries and conditional uncertainty propagation; it introduces no new overturning criterion. A parameter audit separates mechanism-design coefficients from whole-machine screening assumptions, uses a common gravity and inertia centre for each travel state, and corrects the loaded-turn moment. With deliberately enhanced horizontal and payload actions, the baseline stability factors are 2.667 for non-working wind, 1.058 and 3.609 for empty and loaded longitudinal travel, 1.292 and 1.371 for empty and loaded turning, and 1.025 and 1.031 for the two lift orientations. Empty longitudinal moment equality occurs at 15.4742°; at a 15° cross-slope and 5 m radius, turning equality occurs at 3.444 and 3.534 m s −1 . Lift equality areas are 1.5972 and 1.6592 m 2 at 150 N m −2 and a 1.50 m force height. Reproducible Monte Carlo propagation with 100,000 draws per state gives negative-reserve fractions of 39.381%, 31.075% and 27.181% for empty longitudinal travel and the two lifts. These fractions change materially with assumed distributions and dependencies and are not accident probabilities. An additional-roll sensitivity makes both enhanced-action lift reserves negative at 0.5°. Independent vector-moment checks and boundary substitution verify the arithmetic, but no prototype experiments validate the geometry or predictions. The results define preliminary screening and measurement priorities; they do not establish a travel rating, a certified load chart or validated wind limits.

Article.Title: Nutritional quality and seasonal variation characteristics of Pyropia haitanensis, an economic seaweed
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Jiao J.; Yang M.; Lin Z.; Chen B.
Article.Abstract: Pyropia haitanensis is an economically important seaweed that is rich in proteins, polysaccharides, and various medicinal components, and has unique flavor. Although research on P. haitanensis has increased in recent years, relatively few studies have investigated the seasonal dynamics of its key nutritional components. To fill this research gap, monthly sampling was conducted at a coastal P. haitanensis farm in Dongtou District, Wenzhou, China, from November 2024 to January 2025. The results showed that P. haitanensis transitioned physiologically from rapid growth to nutrient accumulation from November 2024 to January 2025. This transition was evidenced by a decline in the daily relative growth rate from 1.19% to 0.68%. Correspondingly, the total amino acid, soluble carbohydrate, and ash contents increased. December represented a critical period for P. haitanensis nitrogen metabolism. During this month, both the nitrogen uptake rate (1.42 ± 0.06 g·g -1 Fw·h -1 ) and nitrogen assimilation rate (0.65 ± 0.04 g·g -1 Fw·h -1 ) reached their annual maximum, and the soluble protein content peaked at 5.79 g/100gDw. Additionally, the photosynthetic pigments concentrations and the expression levels of carbon and nitrogen assimilation metabolic enzymes in P. haitanensis showed coordinated but asynchronous seasonal changes, Photosynthetic pigment concentrations were correlated with light-harvesting efficiency and carbon fixation capacity, while the expression patterns of assimilation enzymes matched the fluctuations in soluble protein and soluble carbohydrate contents. In summary, P. haitanensis redistributes metabolic resources from vegetative growth to nutrient accumulation in the late growth phase, leading to pronounced differences in nutritional quality among thalli harvested in different months.

Article.Title: Assessment of influential geotechnical and seismic features for soil liquefaction using SPT- and Vs-based machine learning models
Article.Authors: Mohamed W.; Yıldız Ö.; Selçuk M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a machine learning-based framework to evaluate soil liquefaction susceptibility using two geotechnical datasets: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Shear Wave Velocity (V s ), integrated with strong ground motion parameters. Feature selection techniques were applied to identify the most influential predictors. For the SPT dataset, corrected blow count, maximum acceleration, and velocity pulse period were identified as key factors. For the Vs dataset, shear wave velocity, epicentral distance, maximum displacement, and the number of effective cycles were found to be critical. Three classification models; Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Neural Networks (NNs) were developed and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC (Area Under Curve). Among them, RF consistently achieved the best performance, with accuracy and AUC values of 0.78 and 0.83 for the SPT dataset, and 0.75 and 0.83 for V s dataset, respectively. The results demonstrate that combining feature selection with ensemble learning enhances the reliability and predictive performance of liquefaction susceptibility assessment across varying site conditions. This study presents a unified machine learning framework integrating multidimensional strong ground motion parameters with both SPT- and Vs-based liquefaction datasets. The results demonstrate that combining advanced seismic features with ensemble learning significantly enhances the reliability of liquefaction susceptibility prediction.

Article.Title: Fracture propagation and damage characterization of a soft coal seam subjected to shaped-charge blasting under in-situ stress
Article.Authors: Cheng G.; Niu X.
Article.Abstract: Loosening blasting in coal seams offers low construction costs and high efficiency for permeability enhancement. However, in-situ stress inhibits the propagation of blast-induced fractures. Understanding how in-situ stress affects fracture propagation is therefore essential for optimizing blasting-based permeability enhancement. To investigate the temporal evolution of fracture propagation and the different responses of the crushing and fracture-propagation stages to increasing in-situ stress in soft coal, this study combined theoretical analysis with numerical simulation. The interaction between in-situ stress and shaped-charge blasting was analyzed, and fracture propagation under different in-situ stress levels was investigated. The mechanism by which in-situ stress suppresses fracture propagation in fractured coal was then clarified. Finally, the relative extent of coal failure during crushing-zone formation and subsequent fracture propagation was characterized using failed-element statistics under different in-situ stress levels. The results showed that when the vertical and horizontal stresses were equal, the circumferential stress was distributed in a regular circle and decreased with distance from the blasthole. In the absence of in-situ stress, fracture length increased nearly linearly. As the in-situ stress increased, the growth rate of the main fracture progressively decreased, and the transition from relatively rapid propagation to slower propagation occurred earlier. The final main-fracture length showed an overall nonlinear reduction with increasing in-situ stress, and fracture extension was strongly restricted under the higher stress conditions. This suppression is consistent with the increase in compressive confinement around the blasthole, which makes continued fracture opening and extension less favorable. In-situ stress had only a limited influence on the failed-element total during crushing-zone formation but substantially reduced the failed-element total during the fracture-propagation stage. The reduction during fracture propagation became progressively greater with increasing stress, with the smallest failed-element totals occurring in the 25–30 MPa cases. These variations represent stress-dependent trends within the investigated numerical conditions rather than universal critical stress thresholds. These results provide theoretical guidance for blasting-based permeability enhancement in deep coal seams.

Article.Title: An advanced power management approach for renewable energy-powered EV charging system with a high-gain extended step-up converter
Article.Authors: Priya N.; Prabaakaran K.
Article.Abstract: Increasing global use of Electric Vehicles necessitates high-efficiency, and durable charging infrastructure. Photovoltaic (PV)-powered EV Charging Stations are an environmentally friendly solution; nevertheless, their effectiveness is limited by PV intermittency, low voltage levels, dynamic load changes, and grid integration issues. To solve these issues, this research proposes a PV-integrated EV charging architecture which includes a Max Gain Extended Step-Up DC-DC converter and a Eurasian Oystercatcher Optimized Proportional-Integral (EOO-PI) control technique. The proposed converter is used to convert the low PV voltage to a higher voltage while minimizing device stress and ripple. The EOO-PI controller employed for fast dynamic response, superior voltage regulation, and increasing resilience under varying circumstances. A Bidirectional DC-DC converter connected to a battery for effective energy buffering, peak load assistance, and power sharing during PV intermittency and outages. Grid integration is accomplished using a three-phase Voltage Source Inverter with an LC filter, which allows smooth bidirectional active and reactive power flow. Furthermore, a PI-controlled inverter-fed Brushless DC motor implemented for steady speed regulation and low torque ripple across all operating conditions. MATLAB/Simulink simulation and hardware outcomes indicate stable DC-link regulation and uninterrupted EV charging with 98.1% efficiency and grid current Total Harmonic Distortion of 0.26% (R-phase), 0.21% (Y-phase), and 0.15% (B-phase) under dynamic operating conditions.

Article.Title: Simulation-based LuGre modelling and voltage-scheduled control of low-voltage stick-slip piezoelectric actuators
Article.Authors: Saxena S.; Barrow J.; Lawrence J.; Omadutt A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Piezoelectric stick-slip actuators are widely used in precision positioning applications, including astronomy, microscopy, and micro-manipulation systems. In this simulation-based study, a low-voltage stick-slip piezoelectric actuator is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink using the LuGre friction model to describe the dynamic friction behaviour at the contact interface. The actuator response is first evaluated in terms of voltage- and frequency-dependent step size and velocity, as these parameters are important for understanding the motion behaviour and designing an effective control strategy. A voltage scheduling scheme is then developed to adjust the driving voltage according to the position error, allowing coarse motion at larger errors and finer positioning near the target. The model is further extended to a three-actuator triangular configuration, where the user-level input is interpreted in terms of desired pitch and roll, and then converted into individual actuator displacement commands. In addition, a discrete move-measure-correct strategy is discussed as a reduced sensing-duty-cycle approach for applications where continuous displacement measurement may not be feasible. The proposed simulation framework demonstrates the feasibility of LuGre-based modelling and voltage-scheduled control for low-voltage stick-slip actuator positioning, and provides a basis for future experimental validation in scalable precision positioning systems.

Article.Title: Regional and severity-specific heterogeneity in meniscal pathology: associations with clinical etiology and patient characteristics
Article.Authors: Gu J.; Wang C.; Zhang Y.; Jiang T.; Zhang L.; Sun Y.; Gu Q.; Mi D.; Yang H.
Article.Abstract: Meniscal injuries vary by subregion, but whether etiology and lesion severity show distinct regional patterns remains unclear. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 979 patients with meniscal pathology. Lesions were classified into six subregions and graded 0–III according to the Stoller classification; etiology was categorized as high-energy, low-energy, or degenerative. Regression analyses assessed associations with etiology, age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). After Bonferroni correction, only medial anterior horn (MAH) and medial posterior horn (MPH) lesions were associated with etiology ( P < 0.001 and P = 0.002, respectively). In unadjusted analyses, degenerative etiology was associated with both MAH and MPH lesions, but this association remained significant only for MAH after adjustment ( OR = 1.875, P = 0.007). Older age ( OR = 1.034 per year, P < 0.001), male sex ( OR = 1.548, P = 0.011), and higher BMI ( OR = 1.060 per kg/m², P = 0.019) were independently associated with MPH lesions. For MAH severity, Grade I lesions were associated with degenerative etiology and higher BMI, whereas Grade III lesions were associated with older age and male sex. These findings demonstrate regional meniscal heterogeneity, with degenerative susceptibility and mechanical loading varying by lesion location and severity.

Article.Title: Standardising bioassays for passive spatial emanators against mosquito vectors
Article.Authors: Silva Martins W.; Hill T.; Lees R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing use of passive spatial emanators (SEs) for vector control has underscored the need for standardised laboratory methods for bioefficacy testing. Peet–Grady (PG) chamber assays are widely used to test volatile insecticides; however, key methodological parameters remain poorly characterised. Here, we investigated how airflow settings (fan speed and baffle setup), mosquito-holding cage design, and cage mesh structure influence mosquito responses to a transfluthrin (TF) passive emanator. Susceptible and pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes were exposed to TF, and effects were assessed using flight inhibition (FI) and 24-hour mortality as endpoints. The assay was highly reproducible, with 83% agreement in FI dynamics across replicate comparisons. Airflow settings were more strongly associated with FI than cage geometry or mesh structure, with 5.86- to 9.57-fold higher odds of FI without a baffle. In contrast, 24-hour mortality varied less across airflow settings, suggesting that FI may be a more sensitive assay endpoint. Time to FI thresholds was up to 4-fold shorter under the medium fan speed setting without a baffle than under the low fan speed setting with a baffle. Cage mesh structure influenced FI responses, with larger mesh apertures showing 10- to 20-fold higher odds of FI in certain configurations, whereas cage geometry had little effect, supporting the use of a higher-throughput dual-cage configuration. These findings highlight the importance of airflow setting, mosquito-holding cage design, and cage mesh structure in determining FI responses in PG-chamber assays and support their consideration when standardising passive spatial emanator bioassays.

Article.Title: Acute effects of unilateral and bilateral split-squat conditioning on change-of-direction performance in elite fencers
Article.Authors: Yildirim E.; Koç H.
Article.Abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the acute effects of unilateral and bilateral split-squat conditioning on change-of-direction (COD) performance in elite sabre fencers, with a particular focus on comparing dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, and bilateral protocols and evaluating how the responses changed over time. Seventeen elite sabre fencers (13 males, 4 females; age range: 15–21 years; mean age: 17.29 ± 1.93 years) from a national Olympic preparation center participated in a within-subject randomized cross-over design. Participants performed three conditioning-activity protocols at 85% of estimated 1RM (dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, and bilateral split squats) and a control condition. COD performance was recorded as time in seconds (s) using the 4-2-2-4 agility test at baseline and at 1, 3, 5, and 7 min post-conditioning activity. Lower time values indicated improved performance. COD time was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with condition, time, and the condition × time interaction as fixed effects and participant as a random intercept. Time was treated as a categorical factor. Secondary participant-level condition-versus-control differences in change from baseline were evaluated using one-sample t tests with Holm correction for 12 comparisons. COD performance changed significantly over time, F(4, 304) = 7.894, p < 0.001. However, neither the overall condition effect, F(3, 304) = 1.866, p = 0.135, nor the condition × time interaction, F(12, 304) = 0.828, p = 0.621, was statistically significant. None of the 12 condition-versus-control comparisons remained statistically significant after Holm correction. These results provide no evidence of differential temporal responses among conditions; they do not demonstrate that the protocols are equivalent. COD performance changed over repeated assessments, including during the control condition. The present data provide no evidence that dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, or bilateral split-squat conditioning produced a temporal response that differed from the control condition. Because the study was not designed or powered to test equivalence, similarity among protocols cannot be inferred. Protocol-specific patterns in the descriptive means should therefore be interpreted as exploratory.

Article.Title: A radio-aware secure routing protocol for wireless sensor networks using predictive Markov filtering and bounded swarm optimization (RSMFSO)
Article.Authors: Jasim A.; Issa N.; Mukhlif F.; Noordin K.; Abdrabou A.; Azzuhri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are one of the key enabling technologies for applications that are energy-constrained and vulnerable to insider attacks in adversarial environments. Conventional protocols optimized for swarms will soon fire up so many multi-hop paths as to exhaust node energy prematurely and yield increasingly higher flat power losses via ongoing over-promotion of available resources ( $$\:{d}^{4}$$ ) that exceed free-space limits. At the same time, traditional clustering mechanisms are susceptible to selective forwarding and blackhole attacks of malicious nodes. In order to address these interdependent problems, RSMFSO, a trust-aware and radio-aware routing protocol, is proposed. RSMFSO localizes a W = 5-round rolling state profile (PMF) to track the 5-round history of rolling state profiles and preemptively isolates compromised nodes prior to topology formation and cluster head selection. Simultaneously, free-space ( $$\:{d}^{2}$$ ) transmission with scene-dependent physical radio constraints is enforced within an optimization engine on the same biological principles. An automated shunting circuit breaker also dynamically circumvents high-effort clustering in late-stage network decay to prevent control packet cascades and dead cascades of control packets. Extensive empirical simulations executed over standard (Scenario A: N = 100 nodes, $$\:{E}_{init}$$ = 0.5 J) and high-density deployments (Scenario B: N = 300 nodes, $$\:{E}_{init}$$ = 0.5 J) verify that RSMFSO substantially extends operational network lifetime compared to evaluated baselines, achieving up to Round 400 with a non-failure node count of approx. 100% across both scales. Scenario B: In this scenario, RSMFSO delays the first node death until Round 500 (298 active nodes) and maintains 98 active operational nodes at Round 1000, compared with LEACH, MMABC, and WIFNCP protocols. Non-parametric statistical evaluations via two-tailed Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests ( p < 0.05) and Friedman Mean Ranks (Rank 1.00) confirm that RSMFSO achieves statistically significant superiority over LEACH, MMABC, and WIFNCP across 30 independent Monte Carlo runs. With a less than 10% malicious node footprint, RSMFSO effectively mitigates the blackhole effect while maintaining high data throughput from the sensor field to the base station, making it ideal for mission-critical WSN deployments.

Article.Title: Less is more: minimal Kolmogorov–Arnold integration enhances efficiency, transparency, and explainability of vision transformers for sedimentary facies classification
Article.Authors: Koeshidayatullah A.
Article.Abstract: Automated petrographic image classification can accelerate sedimentary-facies analysis and support depositional interpretation and subsurface exploration. However, the multiscale textures and visual overlap of carbonate and siliciclastic facies remain challenging for conventional deep-learning models. Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) offer adaptive edge-wise nonlinear functions, but the optimal scope of their integration within pretrained vision transformers is unclear. We introduce KAN-DeiT and compare three integration strategies: replacing only the classification head, extending KAN to the feed-forward sublayers, and further extending it to the attention projections. As a proof of concept, head-only KAN-DeiT achieved 100% accuracy on a held-out eight-class carbonate microfacies test set. On a more ambiguous four-class mudstone dataset, the head-only KAN-DeiT model achieved 91.47% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.9139, outperforming the accuracy of pretrained ResNet-50 (82.95%), EfficientNet-B0 (85.27%), vanilla ViT (88.37%), and MLP-DeiT (89.92%). In contrast, Hybrid and Full KAN integration achieved only 67.44–73.64% and 65.04–65.89% accuracy, respectively, with the same overall pattern observed for RBF and B-spline parameterizations. Deeper integration increased parameter counts by up to 8.8-fold and substantially raised computational cost, whereas head-only integration added less than 0.1% parameters with unchanged GFLOPs and comparable inference latency. Attention rollout, Grad-CAM, and learned edge-function analyses indicated that the head-only model preserved the pretrained spatial representation while modifying how geologically relevant textures contributed to class decisions, although occasional responses to possible image artifacts were observed. These findings indicate that targeted KAN integration at the classification head offers a more accurate and efficient strategy than extensive transformer-wide substitution for data-constrained petrographic classification.

Article.Title: Deep learning for odontoid fractures: the critical role of patient-level partitioning and Grad-CAM assessment in model generalization
Article.Authors: Kıymaz Y.; Taşdemir Ş.; Gezer B.; Uyar Pınar K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Missed diagnoses of odontoid fractures on Computed Tomography (CT) scans can lead to severe morbidity. While Deep Learning (DL) shows promise, many studies report inflated performance metrics due to hidden data leakage (image-level splitting). To evaluate six Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures under a strict zero-leakage protocol for odontoid fracture detection, validating diagnostic reliability and anatomical focus using Explainable AI (XAI). A retrospective cohort of 540 cervical spine CT images from 96 patients was evaluated under a strict zero-leakage protocol. Data was partitioned at the patient level into three disjoint subsets: Training (60 patients, 326 images), Validation (16 patients, 92 images for early stopping), and an independent held-out Test set (20 patients, 122 images touched only once for final evaluation). Six CNN architectures were benchmarked. Statistical robustness was validated via patient-level bootstrapping ( N = 1000 iterations) with Holm-Bonferroni family-wise error rate correction, paired with Grad-CAM visual interpretability. On the untouched test cohort, DenseNet121, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18 achieved similar, leading discriminative performance with AUCs of 0.830 (95% CI: 0.718–0.933), 0.829 (95% CI: 0.714–0.929), and 0.829 (95% CI: 0.697–0.934), respectively, with DenseNet121 demonstrating a balanced diagnostic profile (Accuracy: 73.8%, Sensitivity: 73.0%, Specificity: 75.8%). In stark contrast, SqueezeNet 1.1 and VGG19 suffered complete collapse to majority-class prediction (Specificity: 0.0%) under the evaluated training configuration. Pairwise bootstrap hypothesis testing confirmed that DenseNet121 showed a borderline statistically significant difference over SqueezeNet 1.1 after multiple testing correction ( $$\:{p}_{\text{raw}}=0.0090$$ , Holm-adjusted $$\:p=0.0450$$ on $$\:n=20$$ patients), while differences among DenseNet121, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18 remained statistically non-significant ( $$\:{p}_{\text{adj}}=0.9840$$ ). Architectures incorporating deep feature reuse or residual connections exhibit robust generalization under strict patient-level isolation, whereas compact models and unregularized heavyweight architectures can struggle under small-sample constraints. Rigorous zero-leakage methodology and qualitative XAI assessment are essential prerequisites prior to clinical translation of spinal CAD models.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning estimates clinically significant prostate cancer risk in men with PSA 4–20 ng/mL
Article.Authors: Xie S.; Wang Q.; Wang X.; Jiang X.; Gao H.; Luo Y.; Fan L.; Li Q.; Wang H.; Cai X.; Zhou W.; Wu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Men with prostate-specific antigen (PSA) values of 4–20 ng/mL often have overlapping risks of benign disease, clinically insignificant prostate cancer, and clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). We retrospectively studied 859 men who underwent pathological evaluation; 76 had csPCa. Twelve prediction algorithms were assessed with 500 bootstrap resamples. In every resample, LASSO feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model fitting used only the bootstrap training sample, and performance was estimated from patient-level out-of-bag predictions. C5.0 had the highest AUROC point estimate (0.843, 95% CI 0.801–0.886), an AUPRC of 0.421, and a Brier score of 0.066. Calibration was broadly concordant at low-to-moderate predicted risks but uncertain in the sparse high-risk tail. At a 0.10 risk threshold, the model would avoid 544.8 biopsies per 1,000 men while missing 10.5 csPCa cases per 1,000. PSA-derived measures supplied most of the linear predictive signal, whereas the clearest additional gain arose with nonlinear integration. C5.0 may support pre-biopsy triage, but multicenter external validation, recalibration assessment, and prospective impact studies are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Analysis of stresses and displacements in two-layer inhomogeneous hollow cylinders using the complex potential method
Article.Authors: Youssri Y.; Abbasov Z.; Bouzettouta L.; Alhujaylan A.; Zennir K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an analytical solution for the thermoelastic state of a long, two-layer hollow cylinder composed of inhomogeneous materials under mixed boundary conditions. By accounting for distinct thermoelastic properties and internal heat generation within layered structures, this research addresses a significant gap in the existing literature. The thermal field is determined by expressing the temperature function as a power series. Leveraging the classical and effective Kolosov--Muskhelishvili complex potential method, the thermoelastic problem is transformed into the complex domain. This approach simplifies the analysis of displacements and stresses induced by thermal loading. To ensure high analytical precision, the particular solution for the resulting mixed boundary-value problem is sought in the form of a Laurent series of a complex variable. The surfaces of the layers are assumed to be either thermally insulated or maintained at zero temperature. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the internal stress field is significantly influenced by the intensity of the internal heat source. The derived formulas provide crucial insights into the distribution of thermal stresses and displacements in non-homogeneous layered structures. Given that these results pertain to complex thermal loading conditions, they hold great significance for high-performance engineering applications. Article.Title: Associations among healthy lifestyle behaviors, healthy eating attitudes, picky eating, sustainable nutritional behaviors, and Mediterranean diet adherence: a path analysis
Article.Authors: Oruçoğlu B.; Onbaşı Ö.; Palamutoğlu M.
Article.Abstract: This study examined associations among healthy lifestyle behaviors, attitudes toward healthy eating, picky eating, sustainable nutritional behaviors, and Mediterranean diet (MD) adherence in a large adult sample. In this cross-sectional study, 1,631 adults aged 18 years and older in Türkiye completed validated self-report scales. Associations were tested using path analysis with observed composite scores. The primary model adjusted for gender, age, education, and income (entered as categorical, dummy-coded covariates) and used the healthy lifestyle behavior score with its nutrition component excluded to reduce construct overlap with sustainable nutritional behaviors. Indirect associations were evaluated with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples, and an alternative model reversing the sustainable nutrition–adherence path was also estimated. The final covariate-adjusted model showed good fit, χ²(2) = 1.575, p = 0.455, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.009, RMSEA = 0.000, 90% CI [0.000, 0.046], SRMR = 0.0022; because the model was close to saturated (df = 2), these indices indicate consistency with the data rather than strong confirmation of the hypothesized structure. Healthy lifestyle behaviors (β = 0.519), attitudes toward healthy eating (β = 0.196), and picky eating (β = 0.173) were positively associated with sustainable nutritional behaviors; sustainable nutritional behaviors showed a small positive association with MD adherence (β = 0.087), and attitudes toward healthy eating also showed an independent direct association with adherence (β = 0.176; all p < 0.001). Bias-corrected bootstrap indirect associations through sustainable nutritional behaviors were statistically significant but small (B = 0.003–0.005). The model explained approximately 46% of the variance in sustainable nutritional behaviors but only 8% of the variance in MD adherence. An alternative model reversing the sustainable nutrition–adherence path also fit the data well, and the small difference between models did not provide clear evidence regarding directional ordering, indicating that temporal ordering cannot be established from cross-sectional data. Healthy lifestyle behaviors, healthy eating attitudes, and picky eating were associated with sustainable nutritional behaviors, whereas associations with Mediterranean diet adherence were comparatively small. Given the cross-sectional design and the limited variance explained in adherence, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than as evidence of causal mediation or behavioral spillover.
