Article.Title: Integrated spectroscopic and computational assessment of a new Co(II) Schiff base complex as an anticorrosive and in vitro cytotoxic activities
Article.Authors: Abdelshafi N.; Zaher A.; Shebl M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examines the corrosion inhibition of carbon steel (CS) in 1.0 M HCl using a newly synthesized dimetallic Co(II) Schiff base complex, [Co 2 (H 2 L)(NO 3 ) 2 (H 2 O) 4 ].3.5H 2 O, where H 4 L (DPD) is an amino acid Schiff base derived from 4,6-diacetylresorcinol and alanine. The Co-DPD complex was characterized by elemental analysis, UV–Vis, FTIR, mass spectrometry, thermal analysis, molar conductivity, and magnetic susceptibility measurements. The results showed that DPD behaves as a bis (monoanionic tridentate) ligand, while conductivity measurements confirmed the neutral nature of the complex and spectral data supported an octahedral geometry. Corrosion inhibition performance was evaluated using weight-loss, potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) over the concentration range 10⁻⁶-10⁻ 2 M and temperature range 298–338 K. The inhibition efficiency followed the order Co-DPD > DPD. PDP results indicated mixed-type inhibition, whereas EIS confirmed the formation of a compact protective film. Thermodynamic parameters, including positive ΔH* and negative ΔS*, suggested an adsorption-controlled process. Adsorption obeyed the Langmuir isotherm model. Surface analyses by SEM, EDX, AFM, FTIR, XRD, and contact angle measurements confirmed effective surface shielding. In addition, Co-DPD exhibited promising cytotoxic activity against HepG-2 cells (IC 50 = 9.91 µg/mL). DFT, molecular docking, and Monte Carlo simulations further supported the strong adsorption and high protective performance of Co-DPD.

Article.Title: Effect of seeding rates, bio fertilizations and nitrogen on triticale productivity under new reclaimed soil conditions South Sinai
Article.Authors: Habib A.; El-Aziz M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A two-season field experiment was conducted at El-Tour, South Sinai, Egypt, to evaluate the agronomic and economic efficiency of integrating nitrogen fertilization, biofertilization, and seeding rates on triticale ( Triticosecale Wittmack L.) productivity under newly reclaimed sandy soil conditions. The experiment followed a split–split plot design with three replications, including two microbial inoculation levels (with and without Microbien ), three seeding rates (45, 70, and 95 kg ha⁻ 1 ), and four nitrogen levels (0, 190, 238, and 285 kg N ha⁻ 1 ). Results showed that grain, straw, and biological yields, as well as nitrogen uptake and internal nitrogen use efficiency, were significantly affected by all main factors and their interactions across both seasons. The integrated application of Microbien with moderate-to-high nitrogen rates (N₁₉₀–N₂₃₈) and a high seeding rate (95 kg ha⁻ 1 ) achieved the highest grain yield (> 8.0 t ha⁻ 1 ), biological yield (> 19.0 t ha⁻ 1 ), and protein content, while improving nutrient use efficiency. Economic evaluation indicated that this combination also produced the highest total and net gains, confirming its superiority in profitability compared with the higher nitrogen rate (N₂₈₅), which showed diminishing economic returns. These findings demonstrate that the integration of biofertilizer with optimized nitrogen fertilization and seeding density represents an economically viable and environmentally sustainable approach to enhance triticale productivity and resource-use efficiency under arid sandy soil conditions.

Article.Title: An extended Kalman filtering algorithm based on minimum robust weighted square error
Article.Authors: Liang H.; Huang J.; Zhang J.; Lei H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional Kalman filtering is based on the minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion and has been widely applied in state estimation. However, its performance can be considerably degraded in the presence of abnormal measurements, due to the sensitivity of MMSE to outliers. To address this problem, we design a robust weighted square error and integrate it into the Kalman filtering framework, resulting in the minimum robust weighted square error-based extended Kalman filtering (MRWSE-EKF) algorithm. This unified framework subsumes several existing robust Kalman filtering approaches as special cases. A generalized robust loss function is taken as an example to illustrate the guidelines for parameter settings. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively suppresses the influence of abnormal measurements and significantly improves state estimation accuracy in the presence of outliers. The parameter comparison results also reveal how different parameter settings affect filtering performance, providing practical guidelines for parameter selection.

Article.Title: Kaempferol combined with epigallocatechin-3-gallate enhances bovine oocyte in vitro maturation by attenuating oxidative stress and improving mitochondrial function
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Wang W.; Li Y.; Chen X.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Luan H.; Li X.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated whether combined treatment with kaempferol and epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) offers superior protection during the in vitro maturation (IVM) and subsequent embryonic development of bovine oocytes compared to treatment with either agent alone. The underlying mechanisms were also examined. Preliminary dose–response assays revealed 0.1 µM kaempferol and 20 µM EGCG as the optimal concentrations when used individually. Accordingly, bovine cumulus–oocyte complexes were allocated to the following four groups: control, kaempferol only (0.1 µM), EGCG only (20 µM), and kaempferol + EGCG co-administration (0.05 µM + 10 µM, respectively). The combination treatment yielded the most favorable oocyte maturation and subsequent developmental outcomes. The first polar body extrusion rate was significantly higher in the combination group than in the control and EGCG groups ( P < 0.05), but did not differ significantly from the kaempferol-only group. In addition, cleavage and blastocyst formation rates were significantly higher in the combination group than in both single-treatment groups ( P < 0.05). Meanwhile, oocytes subjected to the combined treatment exhibited markedly lower intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and oocyte apoptosis rates, along with significantly higher glutathione levels, ATP production, and mitochondrial membrane potential than both individual treatment groups and the control ( P < 0.05). Molecular analyses further revealed synergistic effects in the co-administration group, which demonstrated the greater upregulation of SOD3 and SIRT2 (antioxidant defense), DNM1 and MFN2 (mitochondrial dynamics), and BCL2 (anti-apoptosis). Meanwhile, the pro-apoptotic gene BAX was downregulated in the combination treatment group ( P < 0.05). Overall, the results revealed that the combined administration of kaempferol and EGCG synergistically mitigates oxidative stress and preserves mitochondrial activity in bovine oocytes during IVM. This approach may therefore help in enhancing oocyte quality during livestock reproduction.

Article.Title: Early postoperative endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) as a novel biomarker for delirium and mortality after cardiac valve replacement surgery: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Li P.; Duan R.; Sun Q.; Cao L.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) following cardiac valve replacement surgery is a serious complication that impacts patient prognosis. However, effective early postoperative risk stratification tools integrating key pathophysiological mechanisms are currently lacking. Endothelial dysfunction and systemic inflammation are core mechanisms underlying POD, and the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX), as a novel composite biomarker reflecting endothelial injury and inflammatory stress, has not yet been clearly established as a predictive tool in cardiac surgery. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of individuals undergoing cardiac valve replacement surgery based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Individuals were divided into quartile groups according to their early postoperative EASIX levels. The primary outcome was POD, and the secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were adopted to appraise the association between EASIX and the outcomes, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were employed to ascertain the dose-response relationship. Furthermore, a random forest prediction model incorporating EASIX was constructed for POD within 28 days and internally validated using 10-fold cross-validation. Totally 1,543 individuals were finally included, with an incidence rate of POD of 36.2% and an in-hospital mortality rate of 4.3%. Cox regression analysis showed that a higher early postoperative EASIX level was an independent risk determinant for POD (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) = 1.185, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.072–1.309; P < 0.001) and in-hospital mortality (adjusted HR = 1.521, 95% CI: 1.190–1.943; P < 0.001). The trend test revealed a significant increase in the risk of all outcomes across increasing EASIX quartiles (all P for trend < 0.05). RCS analysis demonstrated an approximately linear positive correlation between EASIX and risk. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination in 10-fold cross-validation (area under the curve (AUC) = 63.8%). In conclusion, early postoperative EASIX was substantially linked to POD and in-hospital mortality after cardiac valve replacement surgery. Being easily obtainable from routine tests, it holds potential for clinical translation and provides a novel and practical tool for early postoperative identification of high-risk patients.

Article.Authors: Yao F.; Cai M.; Zhao L.; Ou H.; Zhang J.; Zheng Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early pressurized flowback following large-scale hydraulic fracturing may substantially increase well-control risks under high-temperature, high-pressure, and sand-laden downhole conditions. During shut-in, the sealing interfaces maintained effective contact, with no continuous pressure-penetration path predicted at the verification pressure of 43.75 MPa. The calculated anchoring resistance of the four-slip Y445 packer was approximately 755.6 kN, corresponding to an equivalent anti-uplift pressure limit of 49.3 MPa. Laboratory tests showed stable sealing and anchoring up to 50 MPa, followed by slip-induced anchoring instability at approximately 52.1 MPa, giving a relative difference of 5.37% from the numerical prediction. The controllable blowout-prevention valve remained pressure-tight up to the maximum investigated pressure of 55 MPa. During unsetting and retrieval, the maximum calculated hook load was approximately 321.16 kN, with a minimum structural safety factor of 1.98. The numerical and experimental results consistently identify stage-dependent governing mechanisms and support the proposed framework for evaluating the operating envelope of the investigated workstring under the prescribed conditions.

Article.Authors: Kataoka T.; Tsubouchi Y.; Takase R.; Otsu T.; Kataoka M.; Kaku N.
Article.Abstract: Bisphosphonates such as zoledronate are widely used for osteoporosis treatment; however, their primary effects are limited to suppressing bone resorption. Bone microarchitecture and bone mineral density (BMD) were assessed by micro-CT, histological and histomorphometric analyses of the distal femur were performed using haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained sections, biomechanical properties were measured by three-point bending, and serum bone turnover markers were analysed by ELISA. Compared with Controls, the ZA + MBP group showed significantly higher trabecular bone volume (BV), and both the ZA and ZA + MBP groups exhibited significantly higher BV/TV and Tb.N. No significant differences were observed between the ZA and ZA + MBP groups for these parameters. Cortical bone parameters and BMD did not differ significantly among groups. Histomorphometric analysis did not demonstrate significant differences in tissue area, bone area, or bone area fraction among the Control, ZA, and ZA + MBP groups. No significant differences in biomechanical properties were observed among the groups, except for Young’s modulus, which was significantly lower in the Control and ZA groups than in the Sham group; the difference between the ZA + MBP and Sham groups was not statistically significant. No significant differences were detected in serum osteocalcin (OC), C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX-1), or their ratio. Under the present experimental conditions, no consistent additional skeletal benefit of nutritionally relevant MBP supplementation beyond zoledronate treatment was demonstrated in ovariectomized rats. Q mean , precipitation, and slope together explained 89% variability of fixed and random effects of SSY . Double mass curve analysis showed a significant increase ( p < 0.05) in discharge by17% in JH01 and 43% in JH02 in the post-jhum period. Moreover, post-jhum nutrient loads increased sharply, with potassium increased by 240% in JH01 and 73% in JH02, with corresponding spikes in Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, NO₂⁻, and TDS.

Article.Title: Moisture content modulates DOM thermodynamic regulation of oxygen consumption in drying streambed sediments
Article.Authors: Garayburu-Caruso V.; Roley S.; Danczak R.; Delgado D.; Goldman A.; Forbes B.; Laan M.; Song H.; Tfaily M.; Zheng J.; Stegen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) thermodynamic properties regulate biogeochemical processes (e.g., O 2 consumption rates) in riverbed sediments. This connection has been established under saturated conditions, yet most streams and rivers experience variable inundation in parafluvial zones and go dry at least one day per year. To evaluate how drying and re-inundation influence sediment DOM thermodynamics and their link with O 2 consumption, we conducted wet/dry laboratory experiments using riverbed sediments from 33 sites across the contiguous United States. DOM thermodynamic responses to treatments varied widely by site and were not linked to large-scale or within-sample variables, highlighting the potential importance of additional variables or site-specific processes. Our results further showed that sediment moisture modified the link between DOM thermodynamic favorability and O 2 consumption rates. We found a moisture threshold (~ 46%) below which thermodynamic regulation of O 2 consumption rates was no longer observed. Together, these results imply that drying effects on DOM thermodynamics are not yet predictable, but that temporal shifts in the relative influence of DOM thermodynamics on O 2 consumption may be generalizable across streams experiencing wet-dry cycles. We propose a conceptual model integrating these results to guide development of process-based models of hydrology and biogeochemistry in variably inundated ecosystems.

Article.Title: Composition-dependent charge-storage kinetics and heterojunction charge-transfer dynamics in $$\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}/{\text{BiVO}}_{4}$$ nanocomposites
Article.Authors: Sasikala V.; Arunachalam G.; Nayak A.; Kumar H.; Pachaiappan R.; Pulido E.
Article.Abstract: Optimizing electrode materials for supercapacitors requires a precise balance between electronic conductivity and rapid ion-diffusion kinetics. In this work, a ternary \(\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}/{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) heterostructure nanocomposite was synthesized via hydrothermal and sonication-assisted routes to investigate composition-dependent charge-storage kinetics and interfacial charge-transfer dynamics. Structural (XRD), morphological (SEM/EDX), and chemical (XPS) analyses confirmed multi-phase heterojunction formation, high elemental purity, and intrinsic microstrain ( \(\:\epsilon\:=0.0136\) ). UV–vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) demonstrated enhanced visible-light response with a narrowed bandgap ( \(\:{E}_{g}=2.14\text{\:eV}\) ), indicating improved electronic coupling across phase boundaries. Electrochemical evaluations in a three-electrode setup ( \(\:3\text{\:M\:KOH}\) ) revealed that while the binary \(\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}\) matrix provides high surface-controlled capacity ( \(\:26.85{\text{\:mAh\:g}}^{-1}\) at \(\:2{\text{\:A\:g}}^{-1}\) ), incorporation of \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) modulates the underlying charge-storage mechanism. Power-law kinetic fitting ( \(\:b=0.4071\) ) and low-frequency Warburg impedance analysis confirm that charge storage in the ternary composite ( \(\:{Q}_{s}=4.32{\text{\:mAh\:g}}^{-1}\) at \(\:2{\text{\:A\:g}}^{-1}\) ) is governed by semi-infinite bulk diffusion rather than rapid surface pseudocapacitance. EIS analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in charge-transfer resistance ( \(\:{R}_{ct}\approx\:80\:{\Omega\:}\) ) compared to pristine \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) ( \(\:\sim\:450\:{\Omega\:}\) ), while long-term GCD testing showed stable cycling with \(\:\sim\:75\text{-}76\%\) capacity retention after 5000 cycles and high Coulombic efficiency ( \(\:\sim\:98.5\%\) ). This study clarifies that \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) incorporation acts as a kinetic tuner modulating interfacial mass-transport dynamics rather than a total capacity booster, offering critical insights for engineering multi-phase metal oxide heterostructures.

Article.Title: Disease-specific alterations in plasma fatty acids and arachidonic acid metabolites in ulcerative colitis and crohn’s disease
Article.Authors: Dudzińska E.; Madro A.; Sauer A.; Czerwiński J.; Łopusiewicz Ł.; Czechowska-Kosacka A.; Grabrucker A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD), are characterized by chronic intestinal inflammation and significant clinical variability. Growing evidence suggests that disruptions in systemic lipid metabolism play a role in IBD pathophysiology; however, detailed analysis of circulating fatty acids and arachidonic acid–derived lipid mediators in UC and CD remains limited. Therefore, in this cross-sectional observational study, we measured plasma fatty acids and arachidonic acid–derived oxylipins in patients with UC, patients with CD, and healthy controls. The study analysed 46 patients with UC and 16 with CD, for a total of 62 patients with IBD (UC + CD). These patients were compared to 40 healthy controls. Plasma fatty acids and arachidonic acid–derived oxylipins were measured using targeted high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (HPLC–QTOF–MS). Associations with disease phenotype, sex, disease activity, and pharmacological treatment were analyzed. Both UC and CD showed a global reduction in circulating medium- and long-chain fatty acids compared to controls. Plasma arachidonic acid levels were significantly lower in both diseases, with a more notable reduction in CD. UC was characterized by a selective loss of arachidonic acid epoxide metabolites, while CD exhibited increased levels of alternative arachidonic acid–derived metabolites, with some sex-specific differences. Most lipid changes were not significantly associated with traditional inflammatory markers or disease activity. In exploratory subgroup comparisons, some CD patients receiving biological therapy or corticosteroids exhibited selected fatty acid levels closer to those observed in healthy controls. IBD is linked to disease-specific disruptions in systemic fatty acid profiles and arachidonic acid metabolism. Distinct patterns of lipid alterations were observed in UC and CD, highlighting lipid metabolism as an additional aspect of IBD pathophysiology. These exploratory findings may help identify candidate lipid markers for evaluation in larger, independently validated studies.

Article.Title: How bark beetle–induced dieback and silvicultural harvesting alter carbon and nitrogen pools in mountain Norway spruce monocultures
Article.Authors: Woś B.; Chodak M.; Gruba P.; Misebo A.; Józefowska A.; Pająk M.; Likus-Cieślik J.; Pietrzykowski M.
Article.Abstract: Large-scale forest dieback and other disturbances caused by insect outbreaks, windstorms, or fires are integral components of forest ecosystem dynamics. In managed forests, regeneration occurs through natural or artificial silvicultural practices, including planting or natural regeneration. However, extensive forest dieback can substantially reduce ecosystem services, particularly carbon accumulation and sequestration, and may be accompanied by changes in soil properties and nutrient pools. This study evaluated the recovery of soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (Nt), and selected labile fractions—cold-water-soluble carbon (WSC), water-soluble nitrogen (WSN), hot-water-extractable carbon (HWC), and hot-water-extractable nitrogen (HWN)—in Norway spruce ( Picea abies (L.) H. Karst.) forest ecosystems under two disturbance regimes: (i) bark beetle outbreaks followed by sanitary logging, and (ii) routine silvicultural harvesting in areas without outbreaks or large-scale tree mortality. Soil properties were assessed along chronosequences representing 10–20, 20–40, and 40–60 years post-disturbance, with mature managed stands (> 80 years) serving as reference sites. In the youngest stands recovering from both bark beetle outbreaks and regular harvesting, SOC and Nt were depleted in the upper mineral soil (0–10 cm) and enriched in deeper horizons (10–40 cm) compared with the oldest stands. However, soils beneath regenerated stands exhibited less stable nitrogen pools following bark beetle outbreaks than after silvicultural harvesting. Differences in SOC and Nt between the youngest and oldest stands largely disappeared within 20–40 years following disturbance. These findings suggest that, in spruce monocultures, silvicultural harvesting and outbreak-induced stand replacement have comparable long-term effects on soil carbon storage. In contrast, nitrogen labile fractions respond differently to cyclic stand dieback driven by biotic agents, a disturbance type that is increasing in frequency under ongoing climate change and declining stand resistance.

Article.Title: Piperacillin concentrations in bile—a prospective observational study in ERCP patients
Article.Authors: Pontoppidan L.; Bue M.; Precht H.; Hanberg P.; Houlind K.; Pedersen J.; Knudsen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surgical site infections complicate up to 30% of hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) procedures, with biliary obstruction potentially increasing this risk. Recent studies suggest prophylactic piperacillin/tazobactam (TZP) may offer superior protection compared to cephalosporins. Piperacillin concentrations must exceed the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of key bacterial pathogens in the surgical field, commonly exhibiting MICs of 8 and 16 mg/L. The aim of the study was to ​ evaluate piperacillin concentrations in plasma and bile over time relative to MIC targets (8–16 mg/L), and to evaluate the impact of biliary obstruction. Ninety-nine patients undergoing endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) received an intravenous dose of TZP (4/0.5 g), followed by simultaneously plasma and bile sampling at random intervals. In a post hoc analysis, the patients were stratified by bilirubin levels: non-obstructed (≤ 25 µmol/L) and obstructed (> 25 µmol/L). Piperacillin was quantified using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography. In non-obstructed patients ( n = 77), biliary concentrations exceeded the MIC targets ≥ 245 min (peak 3,105 mg/L), while plasma levels remained above the MIC targets for 190 min (peak 431 mg/L). In the obstructed group ( n = 22), bile concentrations were inconsistent, with malignant obstruction associated with subtherapeutic levels. Plasma concentrations were similar between groups. Piperacillin provides sustained biliary concentrations above MIC targets. Malignant obstruction may compromise biliary drug exposure and warrants consideration of alternative dosing strategies. Clinical trial : The study qualified as a medical trial and was registered at the EU Clinical Trials Register with an EudraCT number: 2021-002629-95. The date of registration and approval for inclusion of patients was November 11th, 2022.

Article.Title: A digital-to-physical-to-digital protocol for comparing 2D Gaussian Splatting, photogrammetry, NeRF and iPad Pro/Polycam RGB-D scanning on a 3D-printed object
Article.Authors: Choi J.; Narzulloev O.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Kwon S.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Comparisons of 3D reconstruction pipelines depend on the reference against which they are scored. We describe a digital-to-physical-to-digital protocol in which a digital design is 3D printed, the print is captured, and every reconstruction is compared with the design that produced it. We applied it to a 19-cm printed sculpture, captured as smartphone video and with an iPad Pro, to compare 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS), photogrammetry, NeRF (nerfacto with NeRF2Mesh) and the iPad Pro/Polycam RGB-D pipeline. Geometry was scored by bidirectional distances to the design, with spatial block bootstrap, registration and fabrication analyses; appearance was scored on 30 views held out from every image-based pipeline, inside object masks derived from the photographs alone. Symmetric root-mean-square deviations from the design were 1.54 mm (2DGS), 1.80 mm (photogrammetry), 3.40 mm (iPad Pro/Polycam) and 5.31 mm (NeRF). The difference between 2DGS and photogrammetry was small relative to its uncertainty, although 2DGS was closer to the design over most of the surface. On the held-out views, object PSNR was 32.4, 26.3, 19.4 and 13.1 dB for 2DGS, NeRF, photogrammetry and iPad Pro/Polycam. For this object and configuration, 2DGS gave the lowest measured geometric deviation and the highest measured photometric fidelity.

Article.Title: Longitudinal monitoring of tumor physiology following cyclophosphamide treatment using diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and diffuse correlation spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Baek J.; Oh Y.; Chaweeruk P.; Jeong H.; Lee S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Monitoring early physiological changes during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is important for treatment assessment, as conventional anatomical assessments often lag behind underlying physiological changes. This study utilized diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) and diffuse correlation spectroscopy (DCS) to longitudinally monitor tumor physiology in a preclinical rat model of breast cancer. Daily measurements of tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂), relative blood flow index (rBFi), and a derived relative tissue metabolic rate of oxygen (rtMRO₂) were obtained in tumors treated with a single dose of cyclophosphamide (CTX) and in untreated controls. Following CTX administration on day 9, treated tumors exhibited a pronounced increase in rBFi and rtMRO₂ on day 11, preceding the onset of tumor volume reduction on day 12; the rise in rtMRO₂ exceeded that of rBFi and was statistically significant ( p < 0.05). The rBFi/rtMRO₂ ratio declined during early growth and increased between the selected early and late intervals in seven of the eight CTX-treated animals with late observations. The present findings support the use of integrated DRS-DCS for early detection and longitudinal monitoring of physiological changes associated with single-agent CTX treatment in this preclinical model. Changes in rBFi and rtMRO₂ were observed prior to the detection of tumor volume reduction by caliper measurements.

Article.Title: An integrated deep learning framework for EEG-based sleep disorder detection
Article.Authors: Kuncha P.; Unhelkar B.; Kumar P.; Chakrabarti P.
Article.Abstract: Sleep disorders require accurate and timely detection to support effective diagnosis and intervention. However, EEG-based sleep disorder detection is challenging due to noise, signal variations, and the difficulty of extracting informative features for reliable classification. To address these limitations, this paper introduces an innovative framework called Enhanced Batch Normalization-based Parallel Convolutional Neural Network for Sleep Disorder Detection (EB-PSDD). The process begins with the acquisition of EEG signals from the CAP Sleep Database. Then the preprocessing using the Adaptive Weighted Moving Average Filtering (AWMAF) technique, which helps reduce noise and smooth the signal, ensuring its suitability for analysis. In the next phase, features are extracted using methods such as Modified Window S-Transform (MWS-T), cross-correntropy, and Common Spatial Pattern (CSP), allowing for the identification of informative characteristics within the EEG signals. For classification, a hybrid deep learning model, Hybrid LeNet-PCNN (HLNet-P), is employed. This model integrates the classic LeNet architecture with the Enhanced Batch Normalization-based Parallel Convolutional Neural Network (EBN-PCNN) to accurately analyze the extracted features and detect signs of sleep disorders. The final output indicates whether a sleep disorder is present, enabling timely detection and intervention. Experimental results show that the proposed EB-PSDD framework outperforms traditional methods, achieving a maximum accuracy of 0.949, precision of 0.799, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.971.

Article.Authors: Wang H.; Hou X.; Li L.; Cui M.; Yu S.; Luo Y.; Wen S.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Numerous studies have shown that transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) can improve cognitive function and symptoms in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). In this study, we established a stress model in non-human primates (NHP) to observe changes in memory and behavior following repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) intervention, and further explored the effects of rTMS on neuronal firing. We found that rTMS promoted the recovery of memory and behavior in cynomolgus monkeys with stress disorder, which may be associated with alterations in neuronal firing frequency. Upon further exploration and research, we found that the 10 Hz protocol elicited a higher proportion of neurons with increased firing rates compared to the 1 Hz protocol. The 1 Hz protocol induced a significant relative increase in firing rates that was predominantly driven by putative excitatory neurons, in which the relative increase was significantly greater than that of the 10 Hz group.

Article.Authors: Shivahare B.; Kapoor A.; Mishra A.; Gupta P.; Mathivanan S.; Sangeetha S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A combination of complex vocabulary, acronyms, and relationships in clinical narratives makes automatic disease classification from clinical narratives challenging. The study proposes the MedClassNet framework that combines Graph Attention Network (GAT) and BioBERT-based contextual embeddings for disease classification in clinical narratives. The MedClassNet framework uses BioBERT embeddings of admission and progress notes and generates a similarity graph for patients by using the cosine similarity between patient contextual embeddings. To classify diseases, the BioBERT framework is combined with the relational embedding learned by the GAT framework for clinically similar patients. An annotated corpus of 1,748 clinical narratives from MIMIC-III dataset containing single-label ICD-9 disease categories is used for experimentation. To avoid label leakage, discharge summaries, final diagnosis, explicit ICD-9 codes, and other post-diagnosis data are excluded from the input for model training. According to the experimental protocol, MedClassNet framework yields an accuracy of 94.2%, a precision of 94.6%, and F1-score of 0.93. Clinically relevant textual features responsible for predictions of the model are discovered by using SHAP-based analysis. The results indicate that combining patient-level relational information with clinical language contextual embeddings can improve disease classification performance as compared with baseline models.

Article.Title: Evaluation of fibrin membrane-embedded adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells for corneal repair in a rabbit corneal alkali-burn model
Article.Authors: Jamshidi F.; Shams M.; Saberi M.; Derakhshani A.; Kheirandish R.; Dehesh T.; Karami N.; Sadeghi Dousari A.; Farsinejad A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the reparative potential of fibrin membranes enriched with adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADMSCs) for addressing corneal injuries in a rabbit model of alkaline burns. This controlled experimental study utilized a preclinical rabbit model to evaluate corneal repair strategies. Twenty-one New Zealand White rabbits were allocated into three groups: Group A (fibrin membranes with ADMSCs), Group B (acellular fibrin membranes), and Group C (untreated controls). Alkaline corneal burns were induced in the left eye of every rabbit on Day 0 following a standardized protocol, and animals were allocated to the three groups on Day 14, once corneal neovascularization had developed. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed through histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluations, focusing on epithelial regeneration, attenuation of inflammation, reduction of neovascularization, and reorganization of stromal collagen fibers. On ordinal histological grading, the three-group overall tests were significant for all outcomes assessed. Epithelial degeneration was absent in all 7 rabbits in Group A but present in all rabbits in Groups B and C (P = 0.000026). Neovascularization (P = 0.00012), stromal inflammation (P = 0.0017), collagen organization (P = 0.00012), and vimentin-positive stromal cell staining (P = 0.0038) also differed significantly among the three groups. Corneal melting was recorded in 1 of 7 rabbits in Group A, compared with all rabbits in Groups B and C (P = 0.00039). In pairwise comparisons after Holm adjustment, Group A differed significantly from Group B for epithelial degeneration, neovascularization, collagen organization, corneal melting and vimentin staining; the Group A versus Group B difference for stromal inflammation did not reach significance after adjustment (adjusted P = 0.077). In this rabbit corneal alkali-burn model, treatment with an ADMSC-seeded fibrin membrane was associated with more favorable terminal histological outcomes than the comparator groups, including improved epithelial integrity and lower grades of neovascularization and corneal melting. Because the study used terminal ordinal histological endpoints, a 14-day post-treatment observation window, and no uninjured normal-cornea comparator, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and require confirmation with molecular outcome measures, longer follow-up, and larger studies before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Prognostic impact of recorded bone, brain, and lung metastatic patterns in hepatocellular carcinoma: a population-based cohort study using the SEER database
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Zhang S.; Liu P.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This retrospective cohort study identified patients diagnosed with HCC between 2010 and 2022 who had at least one recorded bone, brain, or lung metastasis at initial diagnosis in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Metastatic patterns were categorized by the number of recorded sites (one vs. multiple) and by organ involvement (bone, brain, or lung). Kaplan-Meier curves, Cox proportional hazards models, and cause-specific and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to analyze associations of metastatic patterns with overall survival (OS) and with the cumulative incidence of HCC-attributable and other-cause death. A total of 4,282 patients were included, comprising 3,675 with one recorded site and 607 with multiple recorded sites, and 3,932 deaths occurred, including 3,619 HCC-attributable, 252 other-cause, and 61 unknown-cause deaths. Multiple recorded sites were independently associated with worse OS than one recorded site (HR = 1.221, 95% CI: 1.115–1.337, p < 0.001) and with a higher cumulative incidence of HCC-attributable death (SHR = 1.269, 95% CI: 1.160–1.388, p < 0.001), whereas the subdistribution hazard of other-cause death was lower (SHR = 0.508, 95% CI: 0.321–0.804, p = 0.004). Among patients with one recorded site, lung metastasis was associated with higher mortality than bone metastasis (HR = 1.194, 95% CI: 1.101–1.295, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), whereas the brain versus bone (HR = 1.265, 95% CI: 0.955–1.675) and brain versus lung (HR = 1.059, 95% CI: 0.798–1.406) comparisons were not significant. Later year of diagnosis, primary-site surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy were associated with lower hazards of death, and these associations should not be read as causal treatment effects. Both the number and the location of recorded metastatic sites are associated with prognosis in HCC with bone, brain, or lung metastasis at diagnosis. Multiple recorded sites were associated with both higher all-cause mortality and a higher cumulative incidence of HCC-attributable death, so the excess risk is not explained by non-cancer death. Reporting cumulative incidence for both causes avoids the bias introduced by censoring competing events and supports realistic prognostic counselling.

Article.Title: Investigating non-local dynamics in Zika virus transmission: a fractal-fractional approach
Article.Authors: Khirsariya S.; Zahir A.; Yeolekar B.
Article.Abstract: The re-emergence of Zika virus remains a significant public-health concern because its transmission dynamics involve both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections. This paper develops a deterministic Zika virus transmission model using the fractal–fractional Caputo operator to incorporate memory effects and heterogeneous temporal scaling. The model includes susceptible, exposed, symptomatic infectious, asymptomatic infectious, clinically managed infectious, and recovered human classes, together with susceptible, exposed, and infectious vector classes. The Sterile Insect Technique is incorporated through a constant sterile-male mosquito density that suppresses the vector population. Positivity, boundedness, existence, and uniqueness of solutions are established under suitable assumptions. The disease-free equilibrium is obtained, and the basic reproduction number $${\mathcal {R}}_0$$ is derived using the next-generation matrix approach. A generalized Adams–Bashforth–Moulton scheme is used to approximate the resulting nonlinear fractal–fractional system. In the integer-order limit, the numerical solution is compared with a high-accuracy LSODA reference solution, and the observed convergence behavior supports the reliability of the proposed scheme for the selected parameter set. Sensitivity analysis shows that the mosquito biting rate is the dominant risk parameter, whereas sterile-male density contributes to reducing the disease threshold. Numerical simulations further indicate that the fractional order and fractal dimension influence the transient epidemic profile, including the timing and magnitude of infection peaks. The results suggest that SIT-based vector suppression, combined with conventional control measures, may help reduce Zika transmission under suitable parameter conditions.

Article.Title: An integrated analytical framework linking green and blue infrastructure spatial patterns with human thermal stress using UTCI
Article.Authors: Kim I.; Kim Y.; Kim S.; Shin Y.; Jeong D.; Jeon S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban heat stress poses an increasingly critical challenge in the context of climate change and rapid urbanization, prompting the adoption of Green-Blue Infrastructure (GBI) as a key mitigation strategy. Despite its recognized potential, previous studies have reported inconsistent findings regarding the relationship between GBI spatial configuration and urban thermal environments, primarily due to methodological variations and urban structural diversity. To address these limitations, this study proposes a quantitative analytical framework grounded in the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), which captures human-perceived thermal stress more effectively than traditional land surface temperature (LST)-based approaches. Employing data from the Seoul metropolitan area, the study identified 1,800 meters as the optimal spatial scale for capturing GBI-thermal relationships. Through correlation and multicollinearity analyses, seven landscape metrics were selected to characterize GBI morphology, including vegetation condition, spatial composition, configuration, and connectivity. These metrics included NDVI_mean (vegetation vitality), C_G_PLAND (proportional dominance of green infrastructure), C_G_SHAPE_AM and C_GB_SHAPE_AM (area-weighted shape complexity of green and green–blue patches), C_G_SPLIT and L_GB_PD (fragmentation intensity at class and landscape levels), and L_GB_COHESION (spatial connectivity and continuity of GBI). Subsequent application of a Random Forest Regression model revealed that C_G_PLAND, L_GB_COHESION, and NDVI_mean exert the greatest influence on UTCI variation. These findings suggest that the cooling capacity of urban GBI is determined not only by its extent but also by vegetation quality and spatial connectivity. The proposed framework enables consistent time-series analysis and provides a transferable approach for evaluating and optimizing climate-responsive GBI strategies across different urban contexts.

Article.Title: Biodistribution and residue depletion monitoring of 65Zn-labeled sulfadiazine in rainbow trout using PET imaging and HPGe gamma spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Fazaeli Y.; Shahhoseini G.; Neisi A.; Sasanya J.; Feizi S.
Article.Abstract: Monitoring veterinary drug residues in aquaculture is essential for food safety, regulatory compliance, and the determination of reliable withdrawal periods. Sulfadiazine remains one of the therapeutically relevant antibiotics in fish farming, yet characterization of its long-term depletion kinetics in edible tissues is often limited by the sensitivity of conventional analytical methods and by the high cost and synthetic complexity of classical radiotracers such as carbon-14. To address these limitations, the present study employed zinc-65, a relatively cost-effective radionuclide that can be produced in cyclotron facilities available in many countries, to label sulfadiazine and investigate its long-term biodistribution and residue depletion profile in rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). Following co-administration of the zinc-65-labeled sulfadiazine complex and the unlabeled drug, biodistribution studies and whole-body PET imaging were performed at selected time points over an 8-week period to visualize spatial and temporal tracer distribution. After imaging, the fish were sacrificed and dissected, and samples of fillet with skin, internal organs, and other tissues were collected for quantitative analysis using high-purity germanium (HPGe) gamma spectroscopy. This combined imaging and tissue-based radioanalytical approach enabled sensitive tracking of sulfadiazine-associated radiolabeled residues and provided both spatial and quantitative information on their persistence and clearance. The results demonstrated successful PET visualization and biodistribution monitoring throughout the 8-week study period, while HPGe measurements confirmed the gradual depletion and trace persistence of radiolabeled residues in edible fillet tissue and other organs. By using zinc-65 as an economically more accessible alternative to carbon-14, with the additional advantage of domestic cyclotron production, this integrated PET/HPGe methodology provides a sensitive and practical platform for studying long-term veterinary drug kinetics and may support improved residue evaluation and withdrawal-time assessment in aquaculture.

Article.Title: Heart rate deceleration tracks antidepressant response to accelerated dorsomedial prefrontal intermittent theta-burst stimulation in major depression
Article.Authors: Altunç A.; Çiçek Y.; Torun A.; Yoldaş S.; Altunç M.; Velioğlu H.; Poyraz B.
Article.Abstract: Identifying accessible, low-cost biomarkers of treatment response remains a key challenge in personalizing transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) therapy for major depressive disorder (MDD). We tested whether stimulation-evoked heart rate deceleration (HRD) predicts antidepressant response to accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) of the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC). Thirty-two patients with MDD received accelerated bilateral dmPFC-iTBS delivered with a double-cone coil. Heart rate was sampled continuously at 1-second intervals using a low-cost chest-strap sensor, and HRD was quantified as the relative change from a 1-minute pre-stimulation baseline to the mean heart rate across the stimulation window. Response was defined as a 50% or greater reduction in 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score. Response and remission rates were 65.6% and 56.3%, respectively. Responders showed greater HRD than non-responders (Cohen’s d = 1.40). HRD discriminated responders with an area under the curve of 0.905; a 2% cutoff yielded 90.5% sensitivity and 81.8% specificity. Each 1% increase in HRD was associated with approximately 2.5-fold higher odds of response. Stimulation-evoked HRD tracked antidepressant response and is compatible with modulation of a prefrontal-autonomic network; it warrants evaluation in larger sham-controlled studies as a pragmatic, bedside-accessible candidate marker of response. The trial was registered retrospectively at ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier NCT07615387 first posted 29/05/2026).

Article.Title: Analysis of mental disorders and associated factors in high-risk population of colorectal tumors: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Shen Y.; Li Z.; Yu M.; Gao Y.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study focused on high-risk individuals with colorectal tumors, aiming to explore the relationship between psychological factors and colorectal tumors. Additionally, it further analyzed the factors associated with the presence of colorectal tumors. This study included 562 participants, comprising 278 in the low-risk group and 284 in the high-risk group. Participants’ psychiatric symptoms were assessed using HAMD-17, HAMA, and PSQI scales. Based on endoscopic and pathological results, participants were stratified into tumor/non-tumor groups, and advanced adenoma, colorectal cancer, advanced neoplasia subgroups were analyzed. Age-based 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to eliminate confounding. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 24.0 software. After PSM, the high-risk group had significantly higher total HAMD scores and total HAMA scores than the low-risk group ( P < 0.05). The high-risk group also exhibited significantly higher total PSQI scores, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and daytime functioning scores ( P < 0.05). Binary Logistic regression analysis revealed that age (OR = 1.061, 95%CI:1.038–1.083, P < 0.001) and total PSQI score (OR = 1.512, 95%CI:1.003–2.279, P = 0.048) were associated with the presence of colorectal tumors in the high-risk group. This cross-sectional study found that individuals at high risk for colorectal tumors have higher rates of emotional problems and sleep disturbances. Individuals at high risk for colorectal tumors have higher rates of emotional problems and sleep disturbances. Age and sleep quality are independently associated with the colorectal tumors in the high-risk population.

Article.Title: Diagnostic accuracy of transvaginal ultrasound using the IDEA protocol and UBESS staging compared with laparoscopy in deep endometriosis
Article.Authors: Dudekula A.; Manium P.; Eddula V.
Article.Abstract: Deep endometriosis (DE) poses diagnostic and surgical challenges. We evaluated transvaginal sonography (TVS) performed according to the International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) protocol, and the Ultrasound-Based Endometriosis Staging System (UBESS), against laparoscopic findings and surgical complexity. This prospective pilot study enrolled 33 women with suspected DE scheduled for operative laparoscopy at a tertiary referral centre in India. A single experienced radiologist performed IDEA-based TVS and assigned a UBESS stage preoperatively; laparoscopy was the reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy was calculated from 2 × 2 contingency tables with exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs); for UBESS, Stage III (high surgical complexity) was the positive outcome. At laparoscopy, 16 women (48.5%) had UBESS Stage III and 17 (51.5%) Stage II disease; none had Stage I. TVS-derived UBESS correctly classified 13/16 Stage III and 17/17 Stage II cases (sensitivity 81.3%, 95% CI 54.4–96.0%; specificity 100%, 80.5–100%; accuracy 90.9%, 75.7–98.1%); three Stage III cases were under-staged. All laparoscopically confirmed endometriomas were correctly identified by TVS (right 30/30, 95% CI 88.4–100%; left 29/29, 88.1–100%), although specificity rested on only 3–4 endometrioma-negative patients. Sensitivity was 85.7% (18/21; 63.7–97.0%) for pouch of Douglas (POD) obliteration and 81.3–84.2% for ovarian immobility, with no false-positive findings. In this small single-centre cohort, IDEA-based TVS identified endometriomas and POD obliteration with few errors, and UBESS under-staged 3 of 16 high-complexity cases without over-staging any case. Wide CIs, absence of Stage I disease and an expert single-operator setting preclude definitive conclusions; validation in larger multicentre cohorts is required.

Article.Title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine-learning analysis reveals shared molecular signatures linking osteoporosis and atherosclerosis
Article.Authors: Zhou X.; Wei D.; Sun X.; Zhang Z.; Qian Z.; Miao J.
Article.Abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and atherosclerosis (AS) frequently coexist with ageing, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. We separately analyzed femoral-bone OP and arterial AS transcriptomes using Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted differential expression. Arterial-territory adjustment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and repeated-resampling machine learning were applied to the AS cohort, alongside functional enrichment and STRING network analyses. Intersecting OP differentially expressed genes with AS-associated WGCNA modules identified 2788 shared candidates, of which 88 also met stringent differential-expression criteria in both diseases. Functional and network analyses highlighted translation, endosomal–lysosomal biology, endocytosis, sphingolipid metabolism, myeloid-associated processes, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. C1orf174, FBXL18, and RBM4B were consistently prioritized by LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE. A fixed nine-gene candidate panel was evaluated in independent circulating-transcriptome cohorts. In GSE56815, C1orf174 met targeted panel-level correction (FDR = 0.0429), but not genome-wide correction. Exploratory clinical RT-qPCR showed nominally lower FBN1 expression in the OP + AS group, whereas PTEN and SMAD2 showed no statistically significant differences. These findings provide an integrative framework for the bone–vascular axis and prioritize candidate genes for further mechanistic investigation and independent validation.

Article.Title: Physical-layer security analysis of SWIPT-assisted relaying networks with full-duplex active jamming and active eavesdropping
Article.Authors: Thi T.; Le A.; Nguyen T.; Nguyen S.; Vu Q.; Voznak M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examines the security of a simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)-assisted relaying network where both the legitimate destination and eavesdropper operate in full-duplex (FD) mode. Unlike conventional models, the architecture includes active jamming at both ends: the destination injects interference to enhance link confidentiality, while the eavesdropper jams to degrade reliability. The paper develops a unified analytical framework with exact closed-form expressions for key metrics, secrecy outage probability (SOP), outage probability (OP), intercept probability (IP), average secrecy rate (ASR), and effective secrecy throughput (EST) over Rayleigh fading channels. These expressions provide precise characterization under various conditions. Analysis reveals asymptotic behavior at high SNRs and highlights interference-limited aspects of FD-enabled energy-harvesting networks. Emphasis is placed on trade-offs from power-splitting at receivers: allocating more harvested power to jamming enhances security but limits resources for decoding, affecting rate and reliability. Monte Carlo simulations confirm close agreement with analytical results, validating the framework. Overall, this work offers an analytical foundation for designing self-sustained secure wireless systems and practical guidelines for advanced security protocols in energy-constrained IoT networks.

Article.Title: Differences in haemoparasite assemblages of a migratory and sedentary falcon species: first molecular evidence of haemosporidia in Red-footed Falcons (Falco vespertinus)
Article.Authors: Takács P.; Solt S.; Horváth E.; Horváth É.; Asante Firampong N.; Tarján Z.; Erdélyi K.
Article.Abstract: Host life history traits (e.g., migratory strategy) are important factors that influence host-parasite systems, yet empirical evidence remains inconsistent, particularly in birds of prey. We investigated the prevalence and diversity of avian haemosporidian parasites, Plasmodium spp . and Haemoproteus spp ., in a long-distance migratory raptor, the Red-footed Falcon ( Falco vespertinus ) ( n = 139), and compared them with those in sympatric, largely sedentary Common Kestrels ( Falco tinnunculus ) ( n = 468) and Eurasian Jackdaws ( Coloeus monedula ) ( n = 40). Samples collected from shared breeding colonies and pre-migratory roosts in Hungary were screened by PCR targeting haemoparasite mitochondrial DNA. We provide the first evidence of haemosporidian infections in Red-footed Falcons, revealing a markedly low prevalence and limited lineage diversity, with infections restricted to a single Haemoproteus lineage (FALAMU02) in roosting birds and one generalist Plasmodium lineage (SGS1) in a nestling. In contrast, Common Kestrels exhibited higher prevalence and substantially greater haemoparasite diversity, while infections of Eurasian Jackdaws were confined to a single brood. Notably, no Haemoproteus infections were detected in Red-footed Falcon nestlings. These findings reveal contrasting parasite prevalence and lineage diversity among the three host species, with the age-associated increase in infection suggesting that parasite detectability and/or cumulative exposure may contribute to these patterns. The contrasting migratory strategies of the two falcons may represent an ecological trait contributing to these differences, although this hypothesis requires further testing. Overall, our results provide the first evidence of haemosporidian infections in Red-footed Falcons and highlight the importance of host ecology, age, and migratory strategy as potential factors shaping haemosporidian assemblages in raptors.

Article.Title: Tumor size amplifies the effect of minimal extrathyroidal extension on lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma: a population-based study
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Chen H.; Xiao X.; Li C.; Li X.; Xia F.; Ouyang X.; Ouyang H.; Sun B.
Article.Abstract: How minimal extrathyroidal extension (minETE) and tumor size jointly relate to lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains unclear. We analyzed 65,404 patients with PTC from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database (2004–2021). Predictors were ranked by permutation importance and assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Restricted cubic splines were used to model the effect of minETE across tumor size. Interaction was tested on multiplicative and additive scales (relative excess risk due to interaction, RERI), with sensitivity analyses by lymph node compartment and period of diagnosis. minETE was present in 8.9% of patients and showed the strongest association with LNM (adjusted OR 3.53, 95% CI 3.32–3.75). This effect varied non-linearly with tumor size: the OR was stable at 3.5–4.0 for tumors up to 20 mm and exceeded 7.0 for tumors larger than 60 mm. Patients with minETE and 0–10 mm tumors had a higher LNM rate than patients without extension but with tumors larger than 40 mm (54.7% vs. 45.3%; adjusted OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.57–2.14). The interaction was significant on the additive scale (RERI 2.15, 95% CI 1.49–2.80) but not on the multiplicative scale, and was consistent across periods of diagnosis. minETE was strongly associated with LNM and showed a super-additive interaction with tumor size, most evident above 20 mm. Because minETE is usually established on final pathology, these findings mainly inform postoperative risk assessment (nodal staging, adjuvant radioactive iodine, and surveillance) rather than the primary decision on prophylactic central neck dissection.

Article.Title: SABi-YOLO: static axial-bias modelling improves the localization of elongated PCB defects
Article.Authors: She X.; Bao Z.; Wan H.
Article.Abstract: Defects such as open circuits, short circuits and spurs in printed circuit boards (PCBs) are typically small and often extend horizontally or vertically along routing directions, making them difficult for conventional convolutional detectors to localize consistently at stringent intersection-over-union thresholds. Here, we propose SABi-YOLO (Static Axial-Bias YOLO), which introduces a directional inductive bias aligned with PCB routing structures through static dual-axis convolution (SDA). SDA combines parallel local 3 × 3, horizontal 1 × 3 and vertical 3 × 1 convolutional branches, followed by a 1 × 1 convolution that fuses local texture information with bidirectional axial features. Its lightweight implementation further employs depthwise-separable directional convolutions to reduce the parameter count and theoretical computational cost. SDA was integrated into multiple C2f stages of the YOLOv8m backbone and evaluated using a fixed DeepPCB data split, five paired random seeds, validation-based model selection and a locked test set. SABi-YOLO achieved an mAP50–95 of 0.7516 ± 0.0216, with a paired mean improvement of 0.0613 over YOLOv8m (95% confidence interval, 0.0075–0.1150), while reducing the parameter count and GFLOPs by 5.42% and 6.44%, respectively. Under the same evaluation protocol, the DSConv control did not show a stable additional benefit, consistent with the interpretation that static axial inductive bias improves localization at stringent IoU thresholds. SABi-YOLO therefore provides a favourable trade-off between localization quality and theoretical complexity on DeepPCB, although its cross-dataset applicability and efficiency on real-world edge hardware require further validation.

Article.Title: Caffeic acid adaptation alters the antibacterial and anticancer activities of Lactobacillus reuteri cell-free supernatant
Article.Authors: Ghaffari P.; Bahojb Mahdavi S.; Mokhtarzadeh A.; Memar M.; Pourbagherian O.; Ataei G.; Pouladi N.; Eskandani M.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) as a malignancy that develops in the colon and the rectum, is considered one of the most serious health concerns worldwide, with high prevalence and mortality rates. Probiotics are beneficial bacteria commonly found in the gut and have recently attracted scientific attention, due to their potential to prevent or slow the progression of CRC. Probiotics can break down dietary bioactive compounds, such as polyphenols. These compounds may can promote probiotic characteristics, such as antibacterial and anticancer activities, while preventing disorders like cancer. This study aimed to assess the effects of caffeic acid treatment on Lactobacillus reuteri and to determine the impact of the cell-free supernatants obtained from caffeic acid-treated bacteria (CAF-CFS) on the inhibition of growth and proliferation of colorectal cancer cells (HCT-116) compared with the supernatant of untreated bacteria (CFS). This study aimed to determine the potential effect of caffeic acid treatment on the acid resistance and antibacterial properties of L. reuteri . To achieve this, various assays were conducted, including low pH tolerance, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), and antibiofilm formation assays. Additionally, to evaluate the effect of CAF-CFS on colorectal cancer cell viability, apoptosis induction, and migration suppression, MTT assay, Annexin V-FITC/PI staining, cell cycle, colony formation, and scratch (wound healing) assay were performed. Eventually, the expression levels of genes associated with these pathways were determined using the qRT-PCR technique. The acid tolerance assay results indicated that caffeic acid adapted bacteria exhibited elevated acid tolerance compared to the untreated bacteria. Furthermore, MIC and antibiofilm assays revealed that CFS from caffeic acid-adapted L. reuteri showed a significant antibacterial activity relative to the control. Plus, based on MTT assay results, the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of the supernatant from caffeic acid-treated bacteria was determined to be 95.25% (v/v). At 100% (v/v), CAF-CFS reduced cell viability to approximately 38%, compared with approximately 57% following treatment with CFS. Flow cytometry analysis revealed a significant increase in the apoptotic population in cells exposed to CAF-CFS compared to those treated with standard CFS. CFS treatment increased the hypodiploid sub-G1 population, a finding consistent with DNA fragmentation and apoptotic cell death. additionally, the migratory and colony-forming capacities of CAF-CFS-treated cells were significantly dropped compared to both CFS-treated and untreated groups. Finally, qRT-PCR findings demonstrated that HCT-116 cells treated with CAF-CFS exhibited upregulation of Bax and Caspase-3/9 genes, alongside downregulation of MMP3, MMP9, and Bcl-2 genes compared to cells treated with CFS from non-adapted bacteria. Collectively, these findings confirm that caffeic acid-adapted bacteria exert a more potent anticancer effect than the control group. This study showed that caffeic acid adaptation of L. reuteri enhanced the antibacterial properties of its cell-free supernatant and increased the anticancer activity of CAF-CFS against HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells compared with CFS derived from untreated bacteria.

Article.Title: Community-based implementation and feasibility of portable ophthalmic diagnostic devices: a quasi-experimental pre-post study in underserved areas
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Kim J.; Kim S.; Na K.; Lee S.; Jang W.; Cho K.
Article.Abstract: Portable ophthalmic diagnostic devices have emerged as promising tools to improve access to eye care in underserved communities; however, their agreement with conventional equipment and real-world implementation feasibility remain insufficiently evaluated. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic agreement of two portable ophthalmic devices and their real-world implementation feasibility in an underserved rural community. We conducted a two-phase study consisting of an in-hospital agreement study and a community-based implementation study. In the in-hospital phase, a smartphone-based portable slit lamp (TopSlit) and a handheld all-in-one imaging device (Reticapture) were compared with conventional stationary equipment in 72 patients with ocular diseases. Agreement was assessed using Cohen’s κ, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Spearman’s correlation. In the community-based phase, 124 residents aged ≥ 60 years from 10 underserved rural villages underwent baseline ophthalmic screening and a 6-month follow-up assessment. The primary endpoint was the 30-day hospital-visit completion rate among referred participants; secondary outcomes assessed implementation feasibility and participant acceptability, while longitudinal visual-acuity and patient-reported outcomes were exploratory. TopSlit and Reticapture showed moderate to almost perfect agreement with conventional reference equipment (κ = 0.535–0.944). Among 60 participants referred for further evaluation, the 30-day hospital-visit completion rate was 53.3% (32/60; 95% CI, 40.9–65.4%), exceeding the prespecified 40% feasibility threshold (exact p = 0.047). No upload/network or image-quality failures occurred during field implementation, and no additional image reacquisition or remote-grader requests for additional images were required. Participant satisfaction with the program was high (92.9%). These findings support the feasibility and acceptability of integrating portable ophthalmic devices into a community-based eye-care program in an underserved rural setting. The observed agreement with conventional reference equipment, operational performance, and linkage to follow-up care support further evaluation in larger, rigorously controlled studies. The study was approved by the Dankook University Hospital IRB (DKUH IRB 2022-10-016 (Date of Registration: 2022-10-13; Date of Approval: 2022-11-10) and DKUH IRB 2024-06-016 (Date of Registration: 2024-06-13; Date of Approval: 2024-08-02)). The study was registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), Republic of Korea ( https://cris.nih.go.kr ; KCT0012177).

Article.Title: Deconvoluting the influence of environmental forcings on chemical weathering rates using machine learning model
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Liu W.; Zhao M.; Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying the contributions of silicate and carbonate weathering to global carbon dioxide sequestration is crucial for understanding Earth’s climate regulation mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a framework that integrates explainable machine learning with partial dependence analysis to understand the relationships between environmental forcings and chemical weathering rates. We trained machine learning models on a geochemical dataset from the Tibetan Plateau together with climatic and environmental factors, achieving a weathering model with high predictive ability (R 2 = 0.84–0.96). Furthermore, we separated direct environmental driving effects from indirect mediating effects through systemic partial dependence plots. The results indicate that runoff is the dominant controlling factor of both riverine dissolved SiO 2 and HCO 3 ⁻ flux. Warming promotes riverine HCO 3 ⁻ flux in the river, but its effect on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is bidirectional-first inhibiting, then promoting. Further, our analysis reveals that the effect of precipitation on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is mainly mediated indirectly by runoff. Our study establishes a framework for investigating chemical weathering, highlighting the potential of machine learning to advance predictive modeling and reveal complex interactions between environmental forcings and chemical weathering.

Article.Title: Vaginal microbiota composition, inflammation, and preterm birth vary by HIV status and ethnicity in a UK pregnancy cohort
Article.Authors: Watters E.; Quinlan R.; Smith A.; Ferguson H.; Chrysostomou D.; Marchesi J.; MacIntyre D.; Lee Y.; Campos M.; Storch M.; Bennett P.; Taylor G.; Short C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-diversity, Lactobacillus -dominated vaginal microbiota are associated with immune protection in pregnancy, whereas community state types (CST) III and IV have been linked to inflammation and preterm birth (PTB). Pregnant women living with HIV (PWLWH) in the UK experience higher PTB rates than pregnant women without HIV (PWWH). We previously identified an association between PTB and CSTs III and IV among PWLWH in the UK HIV PTB Network study, but the potential contribution of ethnicity was not examined. Here, we build on these findings through a secondary observational analysis comparing vaginal microbiota composition, inflammation, and PTB outcomes in an expanded cohort of self-identified Black and White PWLWH and PWWH. 105 women (57 Black PWLWH, 14 Black PWWH, 15 White PWLWH, and 19 White PWWH) provided vaginal samples at 20–21 (median) gestational weeks. Twelve women experienced PTB, 10 of whom were Black PWLWH (18.2%). White PWWH had the lowest Chao1 richness and composite genital inflammation (PC1). Associations of HIV status with both Chao1 (β = 39.17, 95% CI 18.65–59.68; p < 0.001) and PC1 (β = 3.80, 95% CI 1.39–6.21; p = 0.003) differed by ethnicity, with higher values observed in White PWLWH compared to White PWWH but little difference among Black women. CSTs III and IV were more prevalent in Black women and White PWLWH, whereas CST I was less frequent. Nearly half of Black PWLWH (49%) underwent a CST transition and were more likely to transition than other subgroups (aOR 2.53, 95% CI 1.02–6.52; p = 0.048). Most PTBs in Black PWLWH occurred in CSTs III or IV, and exploratory analyses suggested an association between CST III-IV transitions and higher odds of PTB (OR 7.75, 95% CI 1.57–42.75; p = 0.01). HIV-associated differences in vaginal microbiota richness and genital inflammation varied by ethnicity, with greater differences observed among White than Black women. Black PWLWH had the highest proportion of PTB, and we identified a potential association between CST III-IV transitions and PTB. The observed differences may reflect unmeasured social or structural factors, while the potential contribution of CST dynamics to PTB warrants investigation in larger cohorts.

Article.Title: Well-being and body-related insecurity are associated with cycling status in anabolic-androgenic steroid users
Article.Authors: Bjørnebekk A.; Kaźmierowska A.; Juel J.; Thorsby P.; Scarth M.
Article.Abstract: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with adverse psychological outcomes, yet little is known about how psychological functioning varies across on- and off-cycle phases within individuals. Adult male AAS users ( n = 19) and weightlifting controls (WLC; n = 25) completed biweekly assessments of well-being (WHO-5), psychological distress (HSCL-10), and ten AAS-related symptoms over 6 months. AAS observations were classified as on-cycle (≤ 21 days since last use) or off-cycle (> 21 days), with hormonal measures available in a subset. Exploratory analyses indicated several phase-related differences, with the most consistent findings showing greater body-related insecurity (“feeling small”) and lower well-being during off-cycle periods. These patterns were also supported by within-subject sensitivity analyses, although only 10 participants contributed observations from both phases. Higher anxiety scores were also found in both on- and off-cycle AAS observations than in WLC observations, with no statistically significant difference between cycle phases. Other findings included higher levels of paranoid thoughts and depressive symptoms during off-cycle periods, but these were less consistent across analyses. Little evidence was found for cycle-related changes in impulsivity, irritability, or short temper. These preliminary findings require replication in larger samples.

Article.Title: Primal–dual interior point strategy based parameter identification method for serial industrial robots
Article.Authors: Wan J.; Wu L.; Zhou Z.; He W.; Liu X.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: To accurately identify robot dynamics parameters and improve control performance, this paper proposes a full-parameter identification method based on primal–dual interior-point optimization (FPI-PDIP). Firstly, linearization of the robot dynamics equation combined with QR decomposition is adopted to extract the minimal set of inertial parameters (MSIP). Physical feasibility constraints are constructed according to the intrinsic physical characteristics of inertial parameters, transforming the identification task into a constrained optimization problem solved via the primal–dual interior-point method to acquire physically feasible full dynamics parameters. Optimized Fourier-series excitation trajectories and second-order Butterworth filtering are adopted to guarantee high-quality measurement data. The performance of FPI-PDIP is verified through simulations on a 7-Degree-of-Freedom (7-DOF) manipulator and physical experiments on a SCARA robot. Compared with the conventional MSIP scheme, the mean root-mean-square-error (Mean RMSE) of joint torque estimation is reduced by 46.09% across four joints of the 7-DOF robot in simulation. For the two joints of the SCARA robot, the joint-averaged Mean RMSE decreases by 53.59% on identification trajectories and 40.85% on unseen validation trajectories. The results verify the high accuracy and favorable generalization performance of the proposed FPI-PDIP method for robot dynamics feedforward control.

Article.Title: Pangenome-based design of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Streptococcus pasteurianus with computational evaluation of TLR1–TLR2 interaction
Article.Authors: Aljohani W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Streptococcus pasteurianus is an emerging pathogen causing severe hospital and community-acquired infections. However, there is currently no vaccine, prompting the need for new vaccine strategies. Here, we used a systematic computational workflow combining pangenome analysis, subtractive proteomics, immunoinformatics and molecular dynamics to develop a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting common antigenic epitopes among different strains of S. pasteurianus . Pangenome analysis of 11 strains identified 1,436 core gene clusters (34.2%) conserved within the 11 genomes analyzed. Subtractive proteomics analysis yielded three predicted candidate proteins, DisA, FtsX and FtsW, based on essentiality, limited human sequence similarity and predicted antigenicity; their native surface accessibility remains unconfirmed. Computational epitope prediction identified six cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), four helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and three linear B-cell (LBL) epitopes from these proteins with high antigenicity and immunogenicity. The 344-amino acid multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) design, comprising the Mycobacterium tuberculosis L7/L12 adjuvant and peptide linkers, exhibited enhanced stability and physicochemical characteristics. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations a putative interaction between the MEV and a TLR1–TLR2 ectodomain model derived from PDB 2Z7X; the contact-based predicted was 1.3 × 10⁻²⁴ M, and MM/PBSA binding free energies were − 32.15 and − 16.83 kcal/mol for Replicates 1 and 2, respectively, consistent with a favorable predicted interaction. These computational findings provide a structural basis for further experimental investigation of the proposed vaccine construct. Structural stability was assessed using two independent 100 ns molecular dynamics replicates (200 ns aggregate), and the energetics of the predicted complex were further evaluated using MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations. In silico population coverage analysis estimated 76.87% global population coverage across various geographical and ethnic groups. In silico immune analysis predicted humoral and cellular immune-response patterns, with increased IgG antibody response, prolonged cytokine secretion (IFN-γ and IL-2) and generation of memory cells. Optimized gene sequence and in silico cloning into the pET28a(+) vector provided a proposed construct for experimental expression testing in Escherichia coli. This in silico study presents a computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidate against S. pasteurianus that requires experimental evaluation before any conclusions about immunogenicity or protection.

Article.Title: Influence of charged micrometer-sized particles on the breakdown voltage of air gaps
Article.Authors: Töpper H.; Reding J.; Franck C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Micrometer-sized particles are ubiquitously present and can reduce the breakdown voltage of high-voltage gas insulations by several tens of percent. Despite this influence, a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of how particles determine both the probability and severity of a breakdown is missing. To address this, the breakdown voltage reduction caused by micrometer-sized dielectric $$\hbox {SnO}_{2}$$ particles in a uniform DC ambient air gap is measured and modeled. The experiments cover diameters ranging from $${1}$$ to $${170}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . High-speed macro imaging reveals that the breakdown initiation coincides with a single charged particle approaching an electrode to within approximately $${20}$$ to $${110}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . This occurs for positive and negative particle charges with magnitudes between 130 and 1170 fC. Across the diameters, the breakdown probability increases from 80 to 100%. The mean breakdown voltage reduction increases linearly with the particle diameter from approximately 5 to 28% at approximately $${-19.4} \,\hbox {V }{\upmu }\hbox {m}^{-1}$$ . Outliers are observed to double the breakdown voltage reduction. Increasing the particle number from one to higher quantities raises the likelihood of a breakdown but does not significantly change the worst-case breakdown voltages. Based on a weakest-link distribution scaling, the influence of higher particle quantities is shown to be predictable. Thereby, the system-specific critical particle diameter falls in the range between $${15}$$ and $${54}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . The analytical field distortion calculations demonstrate that the charge dominates the magnitude and spatial extent of the field enhancement. Based on this, a developed streamer integral-based model accounting for the measured charge magnitude, polarity, and particle position during the initiation is evaluated to determine if it can reproduce the experiments. This shows that the particle chargemagnitude cannot be directly mapped to the breakdown voltage reduction without considering the particle-to-electrode distance during the breakdown initiation. Additionally, the significance of the spatial position of the charge on the particle surface is demonstrated based on assumed distributions. Collectively, this provides statistical and charge-resolved breakdown data within a mechanistic framework that can serve as a baseline for quantifying the potential influence of particles on gas insulation systems
