Article.Title: Pan-genomic and pan-transcriptomic analysis of the heavy metal ATPase family reveals diverse expression patterns and putative functional roles in barley
Article.Authors: Shadbolt J.; Schreiber M.; Russell J.; Waugh R.; Houston K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heavy metals act as essential metalloprotein cofactors in numerous physiological processes but can become toxic when non-essential metals accumulate or when essential metals are in excess. As plants continuously encounter heavy metals through their roots, they have evolved complex homeostatic mechanisms to regulate metal uptake and distribution. The Heavy Metal ATPase ( HMA ) gene family encodes a group of heavy metal transporting P-type ATPases that have been linked to stress resistance and nutrient supply. Here, we used a bioinformatics approach to identify and characterise 13 HMA genes containing characteristic P 1B -type ATPase domains and motifs in the barley Morex V3 reference genome. The genes are located on five of the seven barley chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that they cluster into five sub-clades, including one clade containing only barley. Expression profiling across multiple datasets showed distinct temporal and tissue-specific expression patterns among HvHMA s, with several members exhibiting significant transcriptional responses to specific biotic and abiotic stresses. By utilising recently available pan-transcriptomic and pan-genomic resources, we have identified substantial allelic diversity and inter-accession variation in HvHMA s. Our findings suggest that HvHMA s have functions extending beyond canonical heavy metal homeostasis and warrant further investigation for their potential roles in broader physiological and stress-related processes.

Article.Title: Implementation methodologies and socio-technical dynamics as drivers of analytics adoption in ERP systems
Article.Authors: Solano M.; Cruz J.
Article.Abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems increasingly embed Business Intelligence and Analytics (BI&A) capabilities, including real-time dashboards, key performance indicators, and predictive and artificial intelligence (AI) functions. These capabilities often remain underused in implementation projects that prioritize transactional stabilization. Prior studies have explained ERP and analytics adoption mainly through the Technology, Organization, and Environment (TOE) framework and Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory, with limited attention to how implementation processes shape analytical activation. This study examines how implementation methodologies and socio-technical dynamics influence BI&A adoption in ERP systems. Drawing on TOE, DOI, and Actor-Network Theory (ANT), it uses a qualitative multiple-case design based on 43 semi-structured interviews with ERP partners, client organizations, vendors, and industry association representatives in Colombia, combining thematic analysis, theory-based pattern matching, and exploratory network modeling of two partner cases (15 and 14 nodes). The findings suggest that agile and hybrid methodologies, as enacted by implementation partners, are associated with earlier BI&A integration, whereas waterfall-oriented sequencing tends to defer analytical activation. Analytical roles showed limited brokerage over key implementation decisions. The study extends ERP adoption research by showing how methodological sequencing and actor positioning shape whether embedded analytics are activated or remain dormant.

Article.Title: Hybrid feature selection for dimensionality reduction while preserving predictive performance in breast cancer diagnosis
Article.Authors: Mishra S.; Dhakad B.; Ojha S.; Sharma K.; Singh V.; Sharma C.; Tiwari V.
Article.Abstract: Globally, Breast Cancer (BC) is the most common type of cancer among women, which is growing at a high rate. Recently, AI/ML-assisted algorithms have most frequently utilised to accurately, efficiently, and early detection of diseases in healthcare. Though many existing techniques rely on high dimensional features and analysis of performance-feature trade-offs are rarely addressed. This work proposes a novel Hybrid Machine Learning (HML) framework to address three key contributions. Firstly, a unified framework is proposed which integrates filter and wrapper-based Feature Selection (FS) approaches to enhance their feature relevance and subset optimization. Secondly, it presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of diverse hybrid FS models to identify optimal solutions for efficient and high-performance models. Third key contribution of this work demonstrates a quantitative analysis which clearly presents that optimized FS can significantly reduce dimensionality while preserves or gives comparable model predictive performance. Experimental results reveal that the proposed RF hybrid models give comparable performance with significant features reduced from 30 to 10. In the same manner, DT with hybrid models give comparable performance by using only 6–8 significant features i.e., 73 to 80% feature reduction. It is demonstrated that RF based approaches achieves accuracy nearly 98% whereas DT based approaches obtain accuracy nearly 95% in a single split test. Moreover, the reliability of results is assessed by using 10-fold cross-validation with 95% confidence interval and Wilcoxon statistical test. Feature importance analysis is demonstrated to strengthen interpretability as significant features contributes more into model decisions and accuracy. Consequently, the proposed hybrid framework achieves an optimal balance between performance, interpretability, and computational efficiency thereby offers a scalable and practical solution for BC diagnostics. However, this work is limited for subgroup specific performance and needs validation on large, independent, and diverge datasets.

Article.Title: Association of admission acid-base phenotypes with delirium in cardiac critical illness: a multicenter cohort study
Article.Authors: Hwang J.; Jang W.; Kim B.; Chun K.; Kim J.; Park I.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: Acid-base disturbances frequently complicate cardiac critical illness. Although their associations with mortality have been described, their relationship with neurologic complications, particularly delirium, remains poorly defined. We analyzed data from 1259 adults with cardiac critical illness enrolled in an eight-center intensive care unit (ICU) registry (2011–2025). Using a physiological Boston approach, admission arterial blood gas profiles were categorized into six mutually exclusive phenotypes. Sequentially adjusted logistic regression models assessed associations with delirium, and separate adjusted models assessed associations with short-term mortality. Delirium was documented in 555 patients (44.1%). Compared with no acid-base disorder, admission respiratory alkalosis was associated with higher odds of delirium after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.67–4.54; p < 0.001). The association remained statistically significant after accounting for center-level clustering and ICU admission year (adjusted OR, 2.33; 95% CI, 1.20–4.52; p = 0.012). Each 5-mmHg decrease in PaCO₂ was associated with higher odds of documented delirium in Model 3 (adjusted OR, 1.07; 95% CI, 1.02–1.12; p = 0.004), but the association was not statistically significant after additionally accounting for center and admission year (adjusted OR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.99–1.14; p = 0.078). No other phenotype remained significantly associated with delirium after full adjustment. Although metabolic acidosis had the highest crude ICU (22.6%) and in-hospital (29.8%) mortality, no acid-base phenotype remained significantly associated with mortality after adjustment for illness severity and mechanical circulatory support. Admission respiratory alkalosis was associated with delirium documented during the ICU stay in patients with cardiac critical illness. The continuous PaCO₂ association was less consistent across adjustment models. Residual confounding and uncertainty regarding the temporal sequence preclude causal inference.

Article.Title: Enhancing soil creep index prediction accuracy using optimized XGBoost and LightGBM models with bio-inspired optimization algorithms: SHAP- and LIME-based explanation methods
Article.Authors: Ikram R.; Alizamir M.; Heddam S.; Gholampour A.; Kim S.; Yun S.
Article.Abstract: Soil creep, as a form of long-term deformation, significantly influences the performance of foundations and earth structures. As this deformation develops over time, it can lead to major geotechnical issues such as slope failures, differential ground movement, and excessive settlement. Consequently, accurate estimation of the soil creep index is essential for informed geotechnical decision-making. To address this, the primary aim of this study is to develop precise models for estimating the soil creep index using modern machine learning methods. This study develops fourteen predictive models, including seven based on XGBoost and seven based on LightGBM. These include the standard XGBoost and LightGBM models, as well as their optimized variants enhanced using grey wolf optimizer (GWO), whale optimization algorithm (WOA), bat algorithm (BAT), dragonfly algorithm (DOA), crayfish optimization algorithm (COA), and grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA). To assess the reliability of creep index prediction, the models were evaluated under four separate sets of input variables. In addition, SHAP, LIME, and SelectKBest methods were applied to explore the influence of individual input factors on the prediction outcomes. Each model’s effectiveness was assessed through four principal statistical indicators: the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), correlation coefficient (R), and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE). Based on the RMSE values, the top three hybrid XGBoost models were XGBoost-GOA (RMSE = 0.002259), XGBoost-GWO (RMSE = 0.002273), and XGBoost-COA (RMSE = 0.002316). Among the hybrid LightGBM models, the best performers were LightGBM-BAT (RMSE = 0.003813), LightGBM-GWO (RMSE = 0.003884), and LightGBM-COA (RMSE = 0.003885). For the standalone models, XGBoost (RMSE = 0.003084) outperformed CART (RMSE = 0.003398) and LightGBM (RMSE = 0.003972). The testing results indicate that XGBoost-based models provide a reliable and accurate approach for predicting the soil creep index.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate-normalized rainfall rarity may facilitate comparisons across climates, but pooled rainfall–landslide associations can obscure regional structure and rainfall timing. Cell-clustered inference was less decisive. The between-cell coefficient decreased to 0.279 after adjusting for absolute 24-h rainfall and to 0.317 after excluding Typhoon Morakot. When rarity was calculated using only rainfall preceding recorded failure, the positive between-cell association was not recovered ( β between = − 0.276, 95% CI = − 1.115–0.563; 361 volume-bearing records), although analytical populations differed. These findings identify a Morakot-anchored, inventory-specific association that is sensitive to absolute rainfall and exposure timing.

Article.Title: Integrating graph neural networks with urine metabolomics for non-invasive detection of bladder cancer: a multi-centre case–control diagnostic study
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Xu Z.; Zheng S.; Li K.; Wu Q.; Luo Z.
Article.Abstract: Bladder cancer remains a major global health burden, and the stage at which a tumour is found largely determines what follows for the patient. Cystoscopy and urine cytology, the current mainstays, are invasive or insensitive, which keeps the search for accurate non-invasive alternatives open. We therefore asked a narrower question than a screening trial would ask: can a graph-based model separate treatment-naive bladder cancer patients from healthy controls using urinary metabolomic profiles alone? Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry data were acquired for 338 participants (186 patients, 152 controls) at three centres, and 847 reproducible metabolite features passed quality control. Metabolite interaction graphs encoding partial correlations and KEGG pathway co-membership were estimated on training participants only, and a graph attention network (GAT) fusion architecture was trained on the resulting patient-level graphs. Every data-dependent step—quality-control filtering, normalisation, graph estimation, hyperparameter search and selection of the operating threshold—was confined to training and validation data, so that the internal test set and the external cohort were touched once. At the prespecified threshold the model reached an AUROC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.887–0.987), with sensitivity 0.919 (0.781–0.983) and specificity 0.900 (0.735–0.979) in 67 held-out participants, and an AUROC of 0.931 (0.873–0.977) in an independent cohort of 89 participants from a fourth centre. The model ranked above all conventional baselines, although with this sample size none of the pairwise differences survived correction for multiple comparisons, and a control model trained on randomised graph topology performed almost as well. Attention weights, permutation importance, integrated gradients and feature ablation converged on tryptophan catabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis and lipid remodelling. Because cases were histologically confirmed and controls were disease-free volunteers, these results describe case–control diagnostic discrimination; they do not establish detection before clinical presentation, and prospective enrolment of asymptomatic individuals remains necessary before any screening claim can be made.

Article.Title: Effects of corneal cap thickness on corneal morphological and biomechanical properties of rabbits in vivo following SMILE
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Bai H.; Tian M.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the effects of 100 μm and 160 μm corneal cap thicknesses on corneal morphology, endothelial cell density, biomechanics and epithelial thickness in rabbit eyes after SMILE, and to provide experimental reference for clinical surgical parameter selection. SMILE was performed on the right eye of all rabbits using a uniform VisuMax program with programmed refractive correction of − 4.00 D, an optical zone of 6.50 mm, a cap diameter of 7.60 mm, and an incision at the 120° position with a 45° angle. Corneal morphology (Pentacam), endothelial cell density (specular microscopy), biomechanical properties (Corvis ST), and epithelial thickness (anterior-segment OCT) were measured preoperatively and at 1 week, 1 month and 3 months postoperatively. Between-group comparisons at each time point were performed with independent-samples t-tests; longitudinal trajectories were analyzed with a two-way mixed-design analysis of variance (group as the between-subjects factor; time and the group × time interaction as within-subjects effects). Multiplicity was controlled using the Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure for secondary outcomes. Baseline central endothelial cell density was significantly higher in group B than in group A (2994.42 ± 237.96 vs 2693.60 ± 345.72 cells/mm 2 ; P = 0.021); baseline anterior and posterior Km and anterior chamber volume also differed between groups ( P < 0.05), reflecting imperfect baseline balance in this small randomized cohort, whereas the remaining baseline indicators were comparable. Both groups demonstrated comparable postoperative corneal flattening, with comparable central endothelial cell density throughout the 3-month follow-up. Early postoperative intergroup differences in corneal asphericity and Corvis ST parameters were observed but were largely nominal after false-discovery-rate adjustment. Group B had lower Def Amp Max and higher SSI at 1 and 3 months (FDR-corrected). The group × time interaction was significant for Def Amp Max, IR, SP-A1, SSI, ARTh, and corneal epithelial thickness, indicating different postoperative remodeling trajectories between the two caps. No significant intergroup differences in corneal morphological parameters were detected at 3 months. In this rabbit SMILE model, both 100-μm and 160-μm caps produced comparable postoperative corneal flattening and no significant reduction in central endothelial cell density over the 3-month follow-up. Cap thickness was associated with different postoperative biomechanical and epithelial remodeling trajectories (significant group × time interactions for Def Amp Max, SSI, and epithelial thickness), without affecting corneal morphological outcomes at the final follow-up.

Article.Title: The association between cardiovascular disease and cognitive decline varies by long-term depressive symptom trajectories in older adults
Article.Authors: Bao Y.; Wang S.; Lu Y.; Chang F.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depressive symptoms are established risk factors for cognitive decline in later life, but it remains unclear whether long-term depressive symptom burden modifies the association between CVD and cognitive ageing. Participants with moderate-stable and high-stable depressive symptoms had poorer baseline cognitive performance and faster decline in global cognition, memory, and semantic fluency than those with low-stable symptoms. Baseline CVD was associated with faster cognitive decline, but the CVD-related difference was most evident in the low-stable group and attenuated among participants with higher depressive symptom burden. These findings suggest that persistent depressive symptoms may shape the observable association between CVD and cognitive ageing, highlighting the importance of considering long-term mental health burden in cognitive risk assessment.

Article.Authors: Seo H.; Shin J.; Hwang J.
Article.Abstract: This multicenter retrospective study compared cervical vertebrae (CV)-centered region-of-interest input strategies for bone-age estimation from lateral cephalograms and evaluated whether incorporating upper-airway regions provides complementary information, with emphasis on cross-site generalizability. The second to fourth cervical vertebrae and upper airway were manually delineated to generate three input strategies: CV masking, combined CV and airway masking, and CV-centered cropping without masking. Reference bone ages were AI-derived surrogate labels obtained from commercial hand–wrist bone-age software. A deep-learning regression model was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, an internal test set, and an external test set. Performance was comparable across strategies under internal evaluation but differed under external validation. Although overall errors increased substantially in the external test set, CV-only masking showed the largest degradation (mean absolute error, 1.91 years); airway-inclusive masking (1.72 years) and unmasked CV-centered cropping (1.67 years) yielded significantly lower errors. Interpretability analyses highlighted mainly cervical vertebral structures. However, Grad-RAM showed prominent airway activation for airway-inclusive inputs. Together, these findings suggest that CV-centered inputs preserving surrounding anatomical context are more robust for cross-site bone-age estimation than strictly vertebra-only masking.

Article.Title: Boundary-weighted supervision and multi-scale context enhancement for greenhouse tomato instance segmentation using YOLO11n-seg
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Xiong J.; Yang M.; Che W.; Wang S.; Zheng J.; Zhan Y.; Ning Y.

SBD constructs a narrow contour band for each ground-truth instance and increases the contribution of boundary pixels to the mask loss during training without altering the inference graph, whereas CMPRD replaces SPPF near the end of the YOLO11n-seg backbone to enhance multi-scale contextual representation. Across five independent runs on the 128-image validation split (mean ± standard deviation), the combined model increases Mask Recall from \(0.7656\pm 0.0046\) to \(0.7726\pm 0.0039\) and Mask mAP50–95 from \(0.6587\pm 0.0025\) to \(0.6812\pm 0.0026\) relative to YOLO11n-seg, while Mask Precision changes from \(0.7989\pm 0.0037\) to \(0.7961\pm 0.0035\) . In the fixed seed-0 comparison with additional baselines, the larger YOLOv8s-seg and YOLO11s-seg models achieve Mask mAP50–95 values of 0.69161 and 0.69434, respectively, whereas a literature-guided reimplementation of Enhanced YOLO11n-Seg achieves 0.67840 under a comparable lightweight computational budget. On the untouched 161-image official test set, the primary Mask mAP50–95 results, reported as the mean ± standard deviation across all five runs rather than the best-performing run, are \(0.6529\pm 0.0016\) for YOLO11n-seg and \(0.6782\pm 0.0016\) for the proposed model, corresponding to a mean gain of 0.0252 and a paired 95% confidence interval of [0.0227, 0.0277]. Among successfully matched instances with mask IoU \(\ge 0.5\) , Boundary IoU increases from \(0.612\pm 0.004\) to \(0.651\pm 0.003\) , and Boundary F-score increases from \(0.744\pm 0.003\) to \(0.779\pm 0.002\) . On the same validation split and seed-0 development run, a parameter/FLOP-matched convolutional control achieves a Mask mAP50–95 of 0.66530, compared with 0.67007 for CMPRD. The effects of spatial boundary weighting and overall mask-loss scaling are not isolated, and cross-dataset generalization remains unverified.

Article.Title: Lanxangia tsaoko sesquiterpenes inhibit methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by targeting the arginine biosynthesis pathway
Article.Authors: Gu Y.; Tang J.; Chen S.; Dai M.; Pu Z.
Article.Abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), pose a major global health challenge as a difficult-to-treat pathogen. Lanxangia tsaoko is a well-known aromatic herb traditionally used in Chinese medicine. Historically, it has been applied for its antimicrobial and antiparasitic properties, including the treatment of malaria. L . tsaoko essential oil (LEO) exhibit potent anti-MRSA activity both in vitro and in vivo; however, its active components and mechanisms remain unelucidated. We investigated the inhibitory effect and mechanism of bioactive components from LEO on MRSA infection. Bioactive constituents of LEO were retrieved from the literature, and the major bioactive constituents responsible for the anti-MRSA activity were identified through network pharmacology. The antibacterial efficacy of the predicted constituents was subsequently evaluated using in vitro experiments and a mouse model of MRSA infection. Untargeted metabolomics and molecular docking identified potential targets and pathways, which were validated by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting (WB). Notably, five constituents predicted by network pharmacology were all sesquiterpenoids, with trans-farnesol (FAR) exhibiting the strongest anti-MRSA activity (minimum inhibitory concentration = 0.039 mg/mL; minimum bactericidal concentration = 0.078 mg/mL). FAR showed additive effects with antibiotics, inhibited MRSA biofilm formation, and showed preventive efficacy in MRSA-infected mice in vivo. Metabolomics revealed disruption of the arginine biosynthesis pathway, with molecular docking indicating strong binding of FAR to argG and argH. This interaction was further confirmed with RT-qPCR and WB confirming downregulation of argG/argH mRNA in MRSA and upregulation of argininosuccinate synthase (ASS1)/argininosuccinate lyase (ASL) proteins in infected mice. The findings of this study present FAR as the primary active component of LEO, highlighting its potent anti-MRSA effects via the arginine biosynthetic pathway, argG/argH mRNA downregulation in MRSA, and ASS1/ASL upregulation in infected mice.

Article.Title: Modular urban furniture design for young adults’ fragmented time use
Article.Authors: Wu F.; Li C.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: At present, the function of urban furniture is relatively single, which cannot meet the needs of people. In this study, 180 young adults (aged 18–35 years) were interviewed by questionnaires and structured interviews. According to the survey, 86.7% of them want to be configurability, 74.4% focus on the environmental integration, and 76.7% need to use multi-activity support. Based on the above requirements, the study followed the five principles of practicality, economy, aesthetics, modularity and sustainability, and produced a modular urban furniture with a flexible size of 400–500 mm - intelligence landscape seat, and the landscape seat is made of sustainable materials. According to the results of semi-structured interviews, the device can improve the retention intention of users. Through semi-structured interviews, it was found that the retention intention of users was increased compared with that of ordinary seats. Sustainable materials promote the effective implementation of the concept of circular economy in production, procurement and recycling. This study provides theoretical and practical reference for urban furniture design and promoting the sustainable development of public space.

Article.Title: Field-deployable hybrid gravimetry: projecting absolute accuracy across a remote 24 km2 survey via daily quantum calibration
Article.Authors: Shettell N.; Lee K.; Oon F.; Maksimova E.; Chen H.; Dumke R.
Article.Abstract: Hybrid gravimetry combines the mobility of relative gravimeters with the long-term stability of an absolute reference. Following our previous demonstration of this concept under controlled field conditions, we investigate whether quantum-assisted hybrid gravimetry retains its calibration performance during an extended survey under realistic operational constraints. A transportable atomic gravimeter provided routine \(\upmu {\textrm{Gal}}\) -level calibration of two mobile spring gravimeters throughout a seven-day survey spanning 24 km \(^2\) of dense tropical terrain. Despite rainfall, dense canopy, and limited field infrastructure, the atomic reference enabled high-precision asynchronous comparison of relative measurements while suppressing instrumental drift in regions where GPS positioning remained reliable. These results demonstrate that transportable atomic gravimeters can provide practical calibration references for extended geophysical surveys, extending hybrid quantum gravimetry beyond controlled demonstrations toward realistic field deployment.

Article.Title: Magnetic targeting of autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells for knee osteoarthritis: a first-in-human exploratory study
Article.Authors: Kamei N.; Ochi M.; Adachi N.; Ishikawa M.; Nakamae A.; Nekomoto A.; Kawano R.; Tanaka Y.; Hirami N.; Yanada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Knee osteoarthritis lacks disease-modifying therapies, and poor retention of intra-articularly injected mesenchymal stromal cells at cartilage lesions may limit their therapeutic potential. We conducted a physician-initiated, single-center, open-label, first-in-human exploratory trial to assess the safety and feasibility of magnetic targeting–guided delivery of autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells in symptomatic knee osteoarthritis. Five female patients with Kellgren–Lawrence grade 3 osteoarthritis underwent arthroscopic microfracture in areas of full-thickness cartilage loss, followed by intra-articular injection of magnetically labeled autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells under a ring-shaped electromagnetic device. All patients completed 48 weeks of follow-up. No serious adverse events, tumor formation, abnormal tissue proliferation, or device-related complications were observed. Knee joint effusion was the only adverse event considered potentially related to the investigational cell therapy and resolved without additional treatment. Clinical outcomes showed exploratory improvement trends, including an increase in the mean Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score Quality of Life from 15.0 to 50.0 at 48 weeks. Magnetic resonance imaging showed variable structural changes, whereas second-look arthroscopy demonstrated cartilage-like repair tissue in evaluated cases. These findings indicate that magnetic targeting–guided delivery is a feasible cell-delivery strategy for knee osteoarthritis, with no major safety concerns and exploratory signals of therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Interpretable AI for echocardiography-based early screening of rheumatic heart disease in Ethiopia: a cost-effective strategy to tackle a persistent global health disparity
Article.Authors: Tadesse D.; Mekonnen D.; Gonfa O.; Kebede S.; Waldamichael F.; Debele T.; Mekonnen H.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a serious condition that develops from untreated streptococcal throat infections and causes long-term damage to the heart valves. Although it is become rare in wealthier countries, it still affects many people in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), like sub-Saharan Africa, where fragmented healthcare infrastructure and limited access to specialized diagnostics exacerbate diagnostic delays. This study presents an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) framework designed to automate early RHD screening using echocardiographic imaging, with a focus on addressing critical diagnostic gaps in resource-constrained settings such as Ethiopia. Our study explores how Interpretable AI based approach can help identify early signs of RHD using echocardiographic images, primarily mitral regurgitation (MR). Specifically, we focus on detecting mitral regurgitation in two views (A​pical​ ​five chamber (AP5) and Parasternal long axis (PSLAX) views) during the heart’s systolic cycle and measuring the thickness of the anterior mitral valve leaflet (AMVL) from the PSLAX view as part of the old criteria. To do this, we trained and compared two AI models to segment the left atrium (LA) and mitral valve (MV) using annotated echocardiographic datasets. By tracking vol​ume changes in the segmented LA, we identified the frames corresponding to the systolic cycle. To detect MR, which is a key pathological hallmark of RHD, we then overlaid Color Doppler blood flow information on the segmented LA regions of the systolic frames. Additionally, the MV segmentation model was used to measure the AMVL thickness during systole, a critical morphological indicator of chronic valvular damage which was not part of our primary focus. Importantly, this AI framework was developed primarily for the detection of World Heart Federation (WHF) significant MR. While AMVL thickness was examined as an additional morphological parameter, its measurement was performed during sys​tole for methodological convenience and has not been validated for the assessment of mitral stenosis. Furthermore, the framework does not evaluate restricted mitral leaflet motion. Therefore, leaflet thickness measurements should be regarded as exploratory findings and not as diagnostic outputs of the proposed system. Trained on annotated echocardiographic datasets and tested on an independent pilot test set of real-world scans from Ethiopian regional hospitals (patients not seen during training or validation), the AI model demonstrated promis​ing results, achieving precision (1.0), recall (0.7), F1-score (0.82), and accuracy (0.7) metrics that underscore its potential for reliable deployment in low-resource environments. The system’s interpretable design, which visualizes segmentation boundaries, Doppler flow patterns, and anatomical measurements, prioritizes clinical transparency, enabling healthcare workers to validate AI outputs against familiar diagnostic benchmarks. By automating labor-intensive echocardiographic analyses, this AI-driven strat​egy could revolutionize early RHD detection in LMICs, reducing reliance on scarce specialist expertise and paving the way for scalable, cost-effective screening programs. Our findings highlight the transformative role of context-specific AI solutions in bridging global health inequities.

Article.Title: A COI barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods supports biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe
Article.Authors: Sulikowska-Drozd A.; Proćków M.; Kuźnik-Kowalska E.; Maltz T.; Hofman S.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial molluscs are important components of terrestrial ecosystems, yet they remain poorly represented in molecular biodiversity assessments. Although they occur in a wide range of habitats, their inclusion in such studies is constrained by the lack of reliable genetic reference data, particularly in Central Europe. In Poland, despite a well-documented malacofauna comprising approximately 179 species, genetic data remain scarce. At the beginning of our study, 43 species lacked COI sequences in public repositories, while COI sequences from Polish specimens were available for only 11 species. Here, we present the first comprehensive COI DNA barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods, supported by expert morphological identification. We analysed 857 sequences representing 177 species occurring in Central Europe, including 21 species not yet recorded from Poland. The BIN approach yielded 291 molecular operational taxonomic units, 105 of which were unique to our dataset. Among putative species represented by at least five sequences, 83% exhibited a barcode gap, although its position varied considerably among the infraorder-level groups. For example, it occurred at approximately 11–20% K2P divergence in Clausilioidei and 5–10% in Limacoidei. This barcode reference dataset provides a valuable resource for land-gastropod identification and DNA-based biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe, including the detection of non-native species and lineages warranting further taxonomic investigation.

Article.Title: Integrated coffee husk biochar and NPSB fertilizer improve bread wheat productivity in acidic soils
Article.Authors: Bekele K.; Zewide I.; Wato T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The integrated use of organic and inorganic fertilizers improves soil physicochemical properties and wheat productivity, whereas sole reliance on inorganic fertilizers leads to declining soil fertility. In the Bita District of Southwestern Ethiopia, the limited use of lime and coffee husk biochar constrains soil fertility improvement and wheat yields. To address this challenge, a field experiment was conducted during the 2023 main cropping season to evaluate the effects of integrating coffee husk biochar and blended NPSB fertilizer under limed and unlimed conditions on the yield and yield components of bread wheat. The experiment consisted of three levels of coffee husk biochar (2.5, 5, and 7.5 t ha -1 ) combined with three rates of NPSB fertilizer (50, 100, and 150 kg ha -1 ), along with two positive controls (5 t ha -1 biochar and 100 kg ha -1 NPSB) and one negative control (no fertilizer). Treatments were arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications in a factorial arrangement. The results indicated that the interaction between coffee husk biochar and NPSB fertilizer significantly increased grain yield. The highest grain yield (3.59 t ha -1 ) was obtained from the application of 5 t ha -1 coffee husk biochar combined with 100 kg ha -1 NPSB fertilizer under limed conditions. This treatment also provided the greatest economic return, with a net benefit of 276,280 Birr ha -1 and a marginal rate of return (MRR) of 22,076%. Under unlimed conditions, the same combination yielded the highest net benefit (197,080 Birr ha -1 ). Additionally, applying 7.5 t ha -1 coffee husk biochar with 100 kg ha -1 NPSB under limed conditions resulted in a net benefit of 221,440 Birr ha -1 and an MRR of 13,292%. In conclusion, the application of 5 t ha -1 coffee husk biochar combined with 100 kg ha -1 NPSB fertilizer, particularly when applied with lime, significantly enhances both the grain yield and economic profitability of bread wheat production in the Bita district.

Article.Title: Metabolomic profiling and pathway level multiomics integration identify shared stress associated and drug specific responses in the parasitic nematode Anisakis simplex s.s.
Article.Authors: Łopieńska-Biernat E.; Maździarz M.; Polak I.
Article.Abstract: Anthelmintic exposure can perturb multiple cellular processes in parasitic nematodes, but the metabolic response of Anisakis simplex s.s. remains poorly characterized. Here, we generated untargeted metabolomic profiles of L3 larvae exposed for 12 h to albendazole, ivermectin, or pyrantel and integrated these new data at the pathway level with previously reported transcriptomic and treatment-associated single-nucleotide variant (SNV) datasets generated under matched experimental conditions. Fourteen unique LC–MS features were consistently differentially abundant across all three treatments. One shared feature had two alternative Compound Discoverer annotations (5-hydroxylysine and 4-methoxyestrone) and was counted once at the feature level. Shared changes involved membrane lipids, select amino acid related features, folate/one carbon associated metabolites, and ribose 1-phosphate. These patterns were accompanied by treatment specific quantitative differences; under the concentrations and exposure conditions used, albendazole was associated with the broadest metabolomic alteration. Curated, treatment matched pathway level co-mapping identified convergence in amino acid, purine, tryptophan, and arachidonic acid pathways. No direct gene metabolite correlations were calculated, and annotation dependent low confidence connections were excluded from the curated integration. Overall, the data identify a shared metabolic phenotype together with treatment specific molecular perturbations, involving lipid homeostasis, select amino acid and nucleotide pathways, and redox associated processes, rather than a coordinated hierarchical detoxification or resistance program.

Article.Title: A lightweight dual-domain attention YOLO for small object detection in remote sensing images
Article.Authors: Qingxue L.; Guoming W.; Wen X.; Dongyan W.
Article.Abstract: Small object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging due to limited pixel representation, complex background interference, and the requirement for computationally efficient lightweight models. To address these issues, this paper proposes LDA-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework built upon YOLOv8 that integrates adaptive refinement of multi-level features and dual-domain attention to enhance fine-grained perception while maintaining low computational cost. Specifically, we design a Selective Gated Convolution (SGConv) module that adopts a multi-branch convolutional structure with ECA-based channel reweighting to selectively emphasize informative feature responses while suppressing redundant activation. An Improved C2f (IC2f) block is further constructed to strengthen short-range feature reuse and preserve detailed structures during feature refinement. To further refine the multi-level features aggregated by the neck, a Dynamic Convolutional-attention Fusion Module (DCFM) combines lightweight attention with depthwise convolutional enhancement to integrate long-range contextual cues and local structural features with complementary receptive fields. In addition, a Dual-Domain Attention Module (DDAM) is introduced in the prediction stage, where spatial- and frequency-domain responses are jointly modeled to highlight small-object structures and suppress cluttered backgrounds. Extensive experiments on three widely used remote sensing benchmarks, including VisDrone2019, DIOR and DOTA, demonstrate that LDA-YOLO achieves competitive SOD accuracy compared with existing lightweight detectors, while maintaining a compact model size and low computational cost, indicating its potential for resource-constrained deployment.

Article.Title: Towards optimising the combination of non-thermal plasma therapy with immune checkpoint inhibition in melanoma
Article.Authors: Van der heyden L.; Privat-Maldonado A.; Berghmans Y.; Peeters E.; Baroen J.; Hermans C.; Lau H.; Brants L.; Marcq E.; Lardon F.; Vanlanduit S.; Bogaerts A.; Smits E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-thermal plasma (NTP) is a promising cancer therapy that induces immunogenic cell death and may complement immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI). We evaluated NTP as monotherapy and in combination with different ICIs in a syngeneic murine melanoma model. Immune checkpoint-associated ligand and receptor expression was assessed in vitro and in vivo following clinically relevant treatment conditions. NTP largely preserved baseline checkpoint expression, with only limited, treatment-dependent modulations, while maintaining overall immune cell presence within the tumour microenvironment. NTP monotherapy significantly inhibited tumour growth, with the strongest effect observed at 120 s, and was associated with a modest survival benefit in the initial treatment-duration experiment. However, combining NTP with single-agent ICI did not improve tumour control or survival compared to monotherapies, while dual PD-1/CTLA-4 inhibition extended survival independently of NTP. These findings demonstrate that NTP is immunologically compatible with ICI and represents an alternative local therapy for melanoma, although further optimisation is required to unlock its full combinatorial potential.

Article.Title: Kinematic validation of an IMU-based 2-segment foot model using optical motion capture and the oxford foot model
Article.Authors: Bauer L.; Woiczinski M.; Seehaboot K.; Yotnuengnit P.; Vitoonpong T.; Baumbach S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) have emerged as a promising alternative to Optical Motion Capture (OMC) systems. However, many applications simplify biomechanical models, particularly for the foot and ankle, by representing them as a single rigid segment. To address this limitation, a 2-segment Foot Model was developed and validated against the Oxford Foot Model using OMC. Twelve participants were equipped with both systems, and their kinematics were measured during overground walking. The data were compared using statistical parametric mapping (SPM), Pearson correlation, and range of motion (ROM) analysis. The results revealed significant differences in some aspects of the curves according to SPM, but the overall shape demonstrated very high correlation values. Additionally, ROM was not significantly different in six out of nine cases. These findings indicate that, while absolute values were not identical, the IMU-based system provides a valid representation of foot and ankle kinematics when analyzed as two distinct segments.

Article.Title: Intelligent clinical decision support system for intracranial aneurysm lesion-based detection using biomedical imaging data
Article.Authors: Praveena S.; Murali Krishna V.; Sonthi V.; Gottumukkala D.; Pattanaik C.; Behera N.; Bansal K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a type of cerebrovascular condition that occurs due to focal bulging or expansion in the wall of a cerebral artery, most frequently affecting the internal carotid artery. An IA is seemingly connected with conditions such as fibrous dysplasia, adult-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and coarctation of aorta. A ruptured brain aneurysm can result in a severe and life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage if not treated early, often leading to long-lasting neurological damage and a higher chance of death. However, the traditional diagnostic technique is time-consuming, and it necessitates a trained and skilled medical practitioner. Hence, building an automated model to help physicians precisely detect IA can reduce the clinicians’ burden. Recently, deep learning has gained significant interest in the domain of medical imaging as it automatically learns patterns and accurately detects several types of diseases, such as IAs. Therefore, this article introduces a Clinical Decision Support System for Intracranial Aneurysm Lesion-Based Detection (CDSS-IALD). The main purpose of this work is to develop a robust system that can automatically detect and identify intracranial aneurysms using medical imaging data to assist clinicians with treatment decisions. Initially, the proposed CDSS-IALD model pre-processes the input biomedical images using image normalization, noise reduction, contrast improvement, and skull stripping to refine image quality and consistency for subsequent analysis. Following that, a ConvNeXt hierarchical model is employed for feature extraction, which effectively extracts local details and global context from pre-processed images. Finally, these extracted representations are then forwarded to a spiking neural network, which performs accurate aneurysm detection and classification. To ensure the enhanced performance of the CDSS-IALD system, extensive experiments were conducted on the benchmark Intracranial Aneurysm Dataset. The experimental outcomes clearly demonstrate the betterment of the proposed CDSS-IALD system over the other approaches in detecting and localizing intracranial aneurysms from biomedical imaging.

Article.Title: Surveillance epidemiology and an open machine-learning benchmark of antimicrobial-resistant healthcare-associated infections in a Chinese district hospital
Article.Authors: Han D.; Hu Y.; Shu X.; Zou H.; Wang C.; Peng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) drives a growing share of healthcare-associated infection (HAI) mortality; however, data resources from Chinese hospitals outside university referral networks remain scarce. We conducted a retrospective analysis of 39 months of prospectively collected, hospital-wide HAI surveillance data (February 2023–April 2026) from a 1,100-bed district-level general hospital (accredited Class III Grade A) in Chongqing, China, comprising 1,240 episodes among 1,054 patients across 256,993 admissions and 1.14 million patient-days. The hospital-wide episode incidence was stable at 0.48 per 100 admissions and 0.82 per 1,000 patient-days, with no seasonal pattern or residual autocorrelation. Acinetobacter baumannii was the leading pathogen (19.4% of isolates), with carbapenem resistance reaching 92.0% hospital-wide and 98.5% in the intensive care unit, exceeding national benchmarks. Mechanical ventilation, bedridden status, central venous catheterization, and stroke were enriched among resistant infections (odds ratios 2.4–5.2; all Bonferroni-adjusted p ≤ 0.001). We then benchmarked three transparent machine-learning baselines on routinely collected, pre-infection variables using patient-grouped, 10 × 5-fold repeated cross-validation. AMR phenotype prediction achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.74–0.75 (area under the precision–recall curve 0.55–0.56 against a prevalence of 0.31) for logistic regression and random forest, whereas infection-site classification was not clinically useful (accuracy 0.39–0.52 versus a 0.46 majority-class baseline). A previously reported AUROC of 0.91 was traced to two forms of leakage (patient overlap between partitions and inclusion of total length of stay) and is corrected here. The de-identified dataset, bilingual codebook, and complete reproducibility pipeline are deposited under permissive licences, providing an open, leakage-audited benchmark for AMR prediction research in an under-represented hospital tier.

Article.Title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
Article.Authors: Zahrani A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The accelerating adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in human resource management (HRM) raises important questions about which AI-driven interventions most effectively enhance workforce agility, decision-making, and employee outcomes. This study investigated the effects of multiple AI applications—including employee wellbeing (AIEEW), performance management (AIPM), recruitment and selection (AIRS), training and development (AITD), and strategic HR practices (AISHRP), on HR process efficiency (HRPE), decision-making agility (DMA), workplace AI integration (WAI), and enhanced HRM effectiveness (EHRE). Data was collected from 256 professionals in organizational and educational institutions and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS. Results revealed that eight of nine hypothesized paths were supported, with AI-enabled wellbeing exerting the strongest effect on workplace AI integration (β = 0.583, p < .001). Recruitment and performance management systems significantly enhanced HR process efficiency, while strategic HR planning and talent analytics improved decision-making agility. HR performance enhancement strongly predicted HR effectiveness (β = 0.458, p < .001), highlighting process efficiency as a key mediator of AI’s impact. Two paths were weaker: AI in training and development did not significantly affect HR process efficiency, and decision-making agility showed only marginal influence on HRM effectiveness. Theoretically, the study enriches the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory by demonstrating how AI functions as both a strategic resource and a capability-building tool. Practically, findings suggest that organizations should prioritize wellbeing, recruitment, and HR performance systems when investing in AI, while ensuring that training platforms and decision-support tools are better integrated into HR processes.

Article.Title: An AI–IoT enabled upgraded industries framework for sustainable business operations and intelligent decision management
Article.Authors: Kasat K.; Raman M.; Roy D.; Talele G.; Patel V.; Santhosh A.
Article.Abstract: With the advent of Upgraded industries, the shift in focus is now towards an intelligent, human-centric and environmentally-conscious business ecosystem. But the current Upgraded industries approaches are not always very effective in supporting strategic decision making and real-time company operations, as they do not fully include the full integration of AI, IoT, sustainability assessment, and intelligent decision management. This study offers a framework for sustainable business operations and intelligent decision management enabled by AI and IoT to tackle these difficulties. A unified architecture is achieved via the framework’s integration of edge-cloud computing, sustainability assessment, intelligent decision support, AI-driven analytics, and data collecting based on IOTs. A new HLX-DOM is presented to further enhance operational efficiency, decision-making towards sustainability and predictive accuracy. A number of industrial datasets, such as AI4I Predictive Maintenance, Smart Manufacturing, Appliances Energy Prediction, and Industry 4.0 Production, were used to validate the scheme. In the experimental evaluation, efficiency in operations, use of resources, energy consumption, sustainability and accuracy of predictions were some of the performance indicators used. The results demonstrate the optimization of resources (92.3% efficiency), energy saved (91.8% efficiency) and the sustainability increase (91.8% efficiency). The proposed HLX-DOM model outperformed the other models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, XG Boost, ANN, and a single LSTM model, achieving the highest accuracy of 98.7%, precision of 98.1%, recall of 97.9%, and F1-score of 98.0%. The framework’s scalability and resilience are further confirmed by studies of real-world case studies, ablation, sensitivity, and computational complexity. Intelligent, sustainable, and human-centric Upgraded industries ecosystems can be implemented in corporate, healthcare, supply chain, and industrial settings with the help of the suggested solution.

Article.Title: Design and implementation of an industrial software cloud platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Liu H.; Bai Y.; Yang L.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Industrial software is evolving from standalone tools toward collaborative services, increasing the need for heterogeneous resource coordination and industrial knowledge reuse. Integrating knowledge-based planning with shop-floor execution remains a challenge in complex manufacturing workflows. To address this challenge, this study presents the design and engineering implementation of an industrial software cloud platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs). Deployed in a private cloud, the platform comprises resource, enabling, driving, and application layers within a cloud-fog-edge-endpoint framework. A knowledge-model-data-resource operational loop connects data governance, knowledge retrieval, task planning, verification, execution, and feedback. Knowledge graphs provide domain evidence and constraints, LLMs generate candidate plans, and mechanistic models and deterministic software services support verification and execution. Agents coordinate service invocation and feedback across these stages. Two engineering applications demonstrate the platform’s implementation in five-axis blisk computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) and CNC machine-tool prognostics and health management (PHM). Existing CAM records show reductions of 40.27% in aggregate programming and preparation time and 12.29% in single-piece machining time. The PHM application demonstrates the functional integration of data acquisition, fault reasoning, maintenance planning, and knowledge updating. These cases demonstrate the platform’s engineering implementation in manufacturing and maintenance workflows. The current evaluation is based on case-specific CAM records and PHM functional demonstrations, with broader performance and cross-enterprise validation remaining outstanding.

Article.Title: Effect of a Zr seed layer on agglomeration phenomena for Ag nanostructure formation
Article.Authors: Park Y.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Oh D.; Kang H.; Kamiko M.; Ha J.; Rho J.
Article.Abstract: The morphological characteristics of Ag nanostructures strongly influence their plasmonic properties, making morphology control through processing conditions important for optical applications. In this study, Ag nanodots were formed on MgO(001) substrates using a seed-layer-assisted agglomeration (SLAA) process with a Zr seed layer. The effects of Zr seed-layer thickness, Ag deposition thickness, and annealing time on nanodot formation were investigated. Variations in the processing conditions resulted in systematic changes in nanodot density, surface coverage, and three-dimensional morphology, while the introduction of the Zr seed layer influenced the agglomeration and separation behavior of Ag. After annealing, Zr was found to exist predominantly in an oxidized state, suggesting the formation of a ZrOₓ-based interfacial region between Ag and MgO. In contrast, no distinct difference in the crystallographic orientation of Ag was observed with or without the Zr seed layer. These results suggest that the Zr seed layer primarily contributes to modifying the interfacial state and Ag nanodot morphology rather than controlling crystallographic orientation, indicating its potential as a seed layer for process-based morphology control of Ag nanostructures.
Article.Topic: Gold and Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis and Applications

Article.Title: Development and external validation of a predictive model for epithelial ovarian tumors based on MRI features and serum tumor markers
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Niu Z.; Qi L.; Mao S.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ovarian cancer remains a major threat to women’s health, and early-stage disease often lacks specific clinical manifestations, making timely diagnosis challenging. Early and accurate preoperative assessment is essential for improving patient outcomes.To develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and serum tumor markers for distinguishing benign from malignant epithelial ovarian tumors. A total of 222 patients from Huzhou Maternity & Child Health Care Hospital constituted the training cohort, and 102 patients from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine formed the external validation cohort. Independent risk factors for ovarian cancer were identified using multivariate binary logistic regression. A predictive model was then constructed based on the weighted regression coefficients of these factors and subsequently validated in an external cohort. In the training cohort, 168 patients (183 lesions) were benign and 54 patients (68 lesions) were malignant. Multivariate analysis identified tumor morphology, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) signal intensity, presence of ascites, carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125), and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) as independent predictors of malignancy, with AUCs of 0.755, 0.887, 0.749, 0.830, and 0.803, respectively. The combined predictive model achieved an AUC of 0.966, with a sensitivity of 89.6% and specificity of 89.7%. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement (Hosmer–Lemeshow test, P = 0.777).In the external validation cohort, 80 patients (87 lesions) were benign and 22 patients (28 lesions) were malignant. The model achieved an AUC of 0.949, with a sensitivity of 96.6% and specificity of 89.3%. The proposed model integrating MRI features and serum tumor markers demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance and robust external validity. This practical and easily applicable tool may assist in preoperative risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: A lightweight multi-task transformer for joint classification and priority ranking of community service requests on edge devices
Article.Authors: Deng Q.; Suo L.
Article.Abstract: Urban community service platforms receive thousands of textual requests every day, yet most deployed systems still run two separate pipelines: one for category classification and one for urgency ranking. The duplication wastes computation and sits poorly with the memory and power envelope of a community-level edge gateway. We address this gap with EdgeCSR-Net, a multi-task transformer that couples a depth-wise separable encoder, a grouped-query attention block and a convolutional positional encoding, so that thirty-six-way classification and four-level urgency ranking emerge from a single forward pass. Ranking is trained as a pairwise comparison and the resulting score is mapped onto the four operational levels by thresholds fixed on the validation split. The uncompressed encoder carries about 2.02 million parameters; a task-aware pipeline of structured pruning, distillation from a BERT-base teacher and INT8 quantization-aware training trims this to a 1.43-million-parameter, 1.5 MB deployable model. Rather than hand-setting the balance between the two objectives, we weight each loss by a learned task-noise term, an arrangement usually called homoscedastic uncertainty weighting, and pair it with a gradient-projection rule that suppresses conflicting updates on the shared encoder. Evaluated on a corpus of 47,832 requests from three metropolitan districts, EdgeCSR-Net reaches 88.1% macro-F1 and 0.897 NDCG@10. Against BERT-base it gives up 1.4 macro-F1 points and 0.015 NDCG@10 while carrying 77 times fewer parameters; against RoBERTa-base the corresponding figures are 1.8 points, 0.019 and 87 times. Under a matched INT8 pipeline it is significantly more accurate than TinyBERT and DistilBERT, statistically tied with MobileBERT, and six to ten times faster than all three. On an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX the quantized model finishes inference in 7.6 ms per request while occupying 34 MB of peak memory; on a Raspberry Pi 4B it takes 52.3 ms. Temporal and leave-one-district-out protocols cost only 1.7 and 0.8 macro-F1 points respectively, which indicates that neither the joint architecture nor its compression schedule buys real-time latency at the price of cross-region robustness.

Article.Title: Deciphering morphometric and terrain-driven controls on groundwater recharge and agricultural suitability using geospatial and multivariate modeling
Article.Authors: Abishek S.; Pitchaimani V.; Sidhu N.; Singh K.; Sharma A.; Sharma S.; Kaliraj S.; Senagah A.; Thakur C.; Mattar M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of basin morphometry, groundwater recharge potential, and agricultural suitability in the Lower Thamirabarani River Basin, Tamil Nadu, using geospatial datasets and statistical analyses. The morphometric results indicate an elongated basin (Rf = 0.268; Re = 0.584) with a moderate drainage density (1.4 km/km 2 ), reflecting a balanced runoff response and a reduced tendency toward flash flooding. High relief (820 m), steep terrain (17.23%), and a high Melton Ruggedness Number (0.0333) signify strong erosional forces in the western highlands. Flow accumulation analysis shows that 18.7% of the basin experiences concentrated runoff, while curvature mapping identifies concave surfaces that enhance infiltration. Land-use and land-cover mapping indicates agricultural predominance (59.9%) and highlights the influence of expanding settlements on hydrological processes. The Recharge Potential Index (RPI) mapping reveals that moderate recharge zones cover 67.6% of the basin, with high recharge areas primarily located in the eastern floodplains. The Agricultural Suitability Index (ASI) indicates that over half of the basin is of low to moderate suitability, and unsuitable areas coincide with rocky, saline, or steep landscapes. A strong positive correlation exists between ASI and RPI ( R = 0.78, p < 0.001), indicating a close relationship between agricultural potential and groundwater recharge conditions. Principal Component Analysis and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis identify relief-related parameters as the major contributors to spatial variability. The novelty of this study lies in the development of an integrated framework that links basin morphometry, recharge potential, and agricultural suitability, supported by multivariate validation. The results support the prioritization of watersheds, erosion control, and sustainable land and water management practices.

Article.Title: Facial expression recognition based on multi-scale dual-channel attention mechanism
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Ma X.; Yang J.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, with the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the way humans interact with computers has undergone significant changes. Facial expression recognition technology for human faces has increasingly become a hot research topic in computer vision. However, traditional facial expression recognition models are based on deep neural networks, which have problems such as insufficient extraction of image details, poor generalization ability of the model, and low utilization rate of key feature information. To address these issues, in this paper, a Multi-scale Dual-channel Attention Mechanism Facial Expression Recognition Network (MDAMNet) is proposed. Firstly, a Multi-scale Feature Extraction Block with Dilated Convolution (DMFE Block) is designed, which uses ordinary convolution and dilated convolution to form different receptive fields. The model can focus on and extract feature information at different scales at the same time. Then, a Dual-channel Attention Mechanism (DAM) combining channel attention and spatial attention is designed, which can enhance the perception ability and extraction ability of key features, and effectively suppress redundant information. Finally, Focal Loss is employed to dynamically adjust the loss function, with the aim of enhancing the accuracy and stability of the system. During the experimental verification stage, experiments were conducted on three publicly available classic datasets (FER2013, CK + and JAFFE). The final accuracy rates reached 76.87%, 97.52% and 98.34% respectively, effectively demonstrating the feasibility of this method.

Article.Title: Fresh and mechanical properties of hemp fiber-reinforced concrete: an experimental dosage study with multi-output artificial neural network modelling of mechanical strength
Article.Authors: Rajkumar K.; Anandaraj S.; Awoyera P.; Fadugba O.
Article.Abstract: The construction sector’s dependence on carbon-intensive binders and synthetic reinforcement has intensified interest in plant-based fibers as sustainable crack-control reinforcement for concrete. This study experimentally characterises the fresh and 28-day mechanical properties of hemp (Cannabis sativa bast) fiber-reinforced concrete (HFRC) and develops a multi-output Artificial Neural Network (ANN) that predicts its compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strength from fiber dosage. The physical programme comprised eleven dosage levels (0–2.0% by volume in 0.2% steps) of 5% NaOH-treated fiber (aspect ratio ≈ 235) in a fixed M30 base mix (cement 340 kg/m³, water–cement ratio 0.45, superplasticizer 7.48 kg/m³). Slump, compaction factor and Vee-Bee time were measured in triplicate, and three cubes, cylinders and prisms per mix were tested to IS 516; dosage effects were assessed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey and Dunnett comparisons. The 33 physical specimen results per property were kept distinct from 1,100 augmented rows generated from truncated-normal distributions bounded by each mix’s measured mean, standard deviation and range. A 64–32 ReLU multi-output perceptron was evaluated by leave-one-dosage-out cross-validation over ten seeds and benchmarked against polynomial, spline, ridge, tree-ensemble and single-output models. Fiber dosage significantly affected all three strengths ( p < 0.001). Compressive strength peaked at 0.6% (32.8 MPa, + 5.8%), statistically indistinguishable from 0.4 to 0.8%, while splitting tensile and flexural strength peaked at 1.2% (3.95 MPa, + 33.9%; 5.50 MPa, + 31.0%) within statistically equivalent plateaus. On unseen dosages the ANN reproduced the experimental means with RMSE of 0.36, 0.09 and 0.13 MPa, respectively, and outperformed three single-output networks, although a cubic smoothing spline was equally or more accurate. Slump fell from 95 mm to 40 mm and Vee-Bee time rose from 3 s to 20 s across the dosage range, confirming a workability–reinforcement trade-off. The results support hemp fiber dosages of about 0.6–1.2% and show that, for a single-variable dosage study, the multi-output ANN is best used as an exploratory response-curve model rather than as a substitute for physical testing.

Article.Title: Hard attention mechanism integrated with VGG16 for high-precision tomato leaf disease classification
Article.Authors: Laatiri Y.; Mahjoub M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tomato diseases represent a major threat to agricultural productivity and global food security. Early and accurate identification of these diseases is essential for effective crop management and yield preservation. In this study, we propose a hard attention–enhanced VGG16 model for automatic tomato leaf disease identification. By integrating a hard attention mechanism into the VGG16 architecture, the proposed model is able to focus on the most informative regions of the input images, thereby improving its capability to discriminate between healthy and diseased tomato leaves. The proposed approach is evaluated using a publicly available dataset of tomato leaf images. Experimental results demonstrate that the hard attention–based VGG16 model significantly improves classification performance compared to the standard VGG16 architecture and several existing deep learning models. In particular, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.0%, outperforming the baseline VGG16 model, which achieves 92.3% accuracy on the same dataset. Furthermore, the integration of the attention mechanism enhances the interpretability of the model by highlighting the image regions that contribute most to the prediction process. This explainability provides valuable insights into the model’s decision-making process, making it a reliable and transparent tool for intelligent plant disease identification systems.

Article.Title: Evaluation of large language models’ responses to patient questions about avascular necrosis of the femoral head
Article.Authors: Gokalp A.; Cakar A.; Issiz H.; Tepeoglu T.; Erturk S.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence chatbots are rapidly gaining popularity for acquiring health information, but the quality of responses seems to differ between platforms. This study investigated the responses of ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, and DeepSeek to 15 frequently asked questions regarding femoral head avascular necrosis. Each platform answered each question once, for a total of 75 responses. Four orthopedic surgeons assessed the response using the JAMA benchmark criteria, DISCERN, an adapted five-point scale of clinical accuracy, and a binary safety score. Readability was measured by Flesch reading ease score (FRES) and Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FKGL). Models were compared by using Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Claude ranked the highest by JAMA and DISCERN scores and that DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot in terms of DISCERN. Clinical accuracy differed significantly among the models ( p < 0.001). Claude and DeepSeek were rated higher than ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, with no significant difference between Claude and DeepSeek. All responses were rated safe by all four raters. Readability performance scores of the models achieved significant differences on FRES ( p = 0.043) and FKGL ( p < 0.001) measures. The average FKGL score (10.85–13.93) was higher than the grade scores recommended for patient education information. There was heterogeneity in the platforms ability to report on aspects of transparency, information quality and clinical accuracy while consistently failing on readability. Patient comprehension was not evaluated.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

Article.Title: A lightweight closed-loop adaptive intrusion detection framework for cyber resilience in critical infrastructure
Article.Authors: Al Ghamdi M.; Alghamdi I.; Alzahrani R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most operators of energy, health, or transport facilities do not have at their disposal the kind of computational resources that large-scale deep-learning detectors require. Being energy and health care and transportation facility operators, they seek an intrusion detection approach that is responsive to environmental changes. We present one such lightweight alternative. At the core of such an approach is a regularized Logistic Regression-based detector, with the closed loop comprising context-aware thresholding, behavioral profiling, recent error-rate feedback, budget-limited incremental updates, and deception-derived observations from outside. None of these approaches is, in itself, novel. Our contribution lies in the coupling of these mechanisms to displace the decision threshold using contextual and behavioral signals and in detecting confirmed outcomes that are then fed back to update the classifier, the behavioral baseline, and future decisions. We conduct the model evaluation on two levels of abstraction. The confirmation dataset includes 39,919 SWaT instances segmented into 40 nonoverlapping time windows, validated over StratifiedGroupKFold with a per-instance allowance of no more than 256 analyst-validated instances. In an ablation study over 25 such splits comparing the full model to the Logistic Regression with the static threshold, the full model achieved an F1 of 0.7526 ± 0.1074 compared with only 0.5719 ± 0.1578 for the latter (Holm adjusted p < 0.001). Most of the contribution came from budgeted incremental learning; without it, F1 dropped by 0.1704. Feedback using error rates was less important but still significant, returning 0.0048 in F1 together with a lower false positive rate. Behavioral profiling did not affect the F1 and improved specificity. Context-aware thresholding increased the false positive rate while yielding no improvement in the F1; thus, this is reported as a trade-off rather than an improvement. There were no significant contrasts with respect to the Holm correction; hence, we do not claim any synergy. Batch Logistic Regression with matching scored 0.7065 ± 0.1254 in terms of F1 score compared with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Linear SVM, Extra Trees, and MLP, none being significantly different from batch Logistic Regression. Because the labels were equally split among 256, all feedback mechanisms outperformed the case with no feedback, going from an F1 of 0.5845 ± 0.1495 to between 0.7292 and 0.7676. The deception-prioritized proxy did not make it into the winners. It beat no feedback but lost to random sampling on all the metrics that we examined. We have, therefore, referenced the previously published simulation and emulation figures as exploratory studies illustrating the behavior of this architecture. In toto, the framework is efficient and competitive under the tested conditions, and nothing herein suggests classifier superiority or a deception-specific advantage or true zero-day detection or readiness for a live plant.

Article.Title: FS-VMADW: a frequency–spatial vision mamba framework for dual watermarking of medical MRI images
Article.Authors: Ur Rehman A.; Lee C.; Li L.; Khan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Secure transmission and copyright protection of medical images require watermarking methods that preserve image quality and enable reliable payload recovery. However, the currently available deep watermarking architectures either encode only a single watermark or use convolutional networks with inherently restricted receptive fields, which limits their ability to capture long-range anatomical dependencies in medical images. Moreover, spatial modeling alone does not explicitly capture the frequency characteristics that influence watermark imperceptibility and robustness. This work proposes FS-VMADW - a Frequency-Spatial Vision Mamba Dual Watermarking architecture for abdominal MRI security. The proposed encoder combines the Vision Mamba spatial branch with a four-direction selective scan of state-space models applied with linear complexity, along with a two-stage Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform frequency branch, which are fused with a gating module generating location-specific weighting of spatial and frequency feature maps. Two independent spread-spectrum carriers encode two 64-bit binary watermarks, while an adaptively generated Vision Mamba mask controls their embedding. A two-phase training curriculum mitigates the gradient conflict between imperceptibility and extraction fidelity by decoupling the two objectives across successive training phases. Experiments on the CHAOS abdominal MRI benchmark demonstrate PSNR = 42.37 dB, SSIM = 0.9557, NC = 0.9511, BER = 0.0491, and BitAcc = 0.9509 under clean conditions. Controlled backbone comparisons further show that Vision Mamba outperforms CNN and Transformer alternatives, while the addition of DWT provides further improvements in both imperceptibility and watermark recovery. These results demonstrate that long-range spatial modeling and multi-scale frequency information provide complementary benefits for dual watermarking of medical images.

Article.Title: Serial multi‑time‑point assessments of well‑defined somatosensory domains and their associations with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke
Article.Authors: Jing J.; Du R.; Wen L.; Fang Y.
Article.Abstract: The association between post-stroke somatosensory deficits and limb spasticity has been reported. This study aimed to assess patients at multiple time points to further investigate relationships between well-defined somatosensory domains and the occurrence of limb spasticity following ischemic stroke. Briefly, the study enrolled 514 patients with ischemic stroke. Post-stroke proprioceptive deficits, pain-temperature deficits, sensory extinction, and stereognosis deficits were evaluated at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge. Limb spasticity was assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale at 30 and 90 days post-discharge; a score ≥ 1 was defined as spasticity. Multivariate logistic regression models were applied to examine relationships between these variables. The results showed that proprioceptive deficits and pain-temperature deficits at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge were associated with limb spasticity and moderate-to-severe limb spasticity (relative to mild spasticity), and an interaction was observed between these two deficits. Only post‑stroke sensory extinction and stereognosis deficits assessed at 10 days post‑discharge were associated with spasticity, but these associations were attenuated to non‑significance upon additional adjustment for admission affected‑limb muscle strength. In conclusion, proprioceptive and pain-temperature deficits at all three time points were associated with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke in this cohort. These findings guide future stroke‑somatosensory research.

Article.Title: Analysis of a reaction-diffusion SVEIR model for measles geographic spread
Article.Authors: DarAssi M.; AbuHour Y.; Almuneef A.; Alqahtani Z.
Article.Abstract: We formulate and analyze a deterministic reaction-diffusion SVEIR model for the geographic spread of measles, explicitly incorporating vaccination, vaccine efficacy, latency, recovery, demographic turnover, and spatial diffusion. The disease-free equilibrium and the basic reproduction number $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ are obtained using the next-generation matrix, and linear stability analysis identifies the invasion threshold and the critical spatial mode. Because the critical wavenumber is zero, a long-wavelength analysis is used to characterize slow spatial variation near the invasion front. A mathematical consistency check shows that the common-diffusion formulation does not support a finite-wavenumber Turing instability; the roll, square, and hexagonal modes are therefore presented only as generic pattern-theory modes rather than as patterns proved to arise from the present model. Numerical simulations illustrate spatiotemporal propagation and quantify the effects of vaccine efficacy, vaccination rate, and transmission intensity.
