Article.Title: Diagnosis of breast cancer with high accuracy via Petri net modeling of signaling pathways
Article.Authors: Khodaei S.; Sarvari M.; Sajadi E.; Asadzadeh F.; Ebrahimian H.; Rahgozar M.; Kavousi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, affecting millions of people each year. There are many different types of cancer, including breast cancer, colon cancer and endometrial cancer, each with its own unique characteristics and challenges. One of the most crucial aspects of cancer management is early detection. Detecting cancer at an early stage significantly increases the chances of successful treatment and survival. In recent years, much research has been conducted to accelerate the diagnosis and prediction of cancer, especially by examining the role of genes, their effectiveness, and especially the sequence of changes in their activities in relation to this disease. An important part of the results of these studies has been related to KEGG signaling pathways. Many studies have also been conducted to model these signaling pathways via Petri net tools, which have shown good capabilities in this field. This article reveals in part some of these capabilities observed in a recently developed tool that provides a means for diagnosing various types of cancer by modeling their signaling pathways via Petri nets. Compared with other existing methods, the proposed method provides higher accuracy and precision (95–99%) on most related GEO datasets. With this method, blood samples, which are less expensive and easier to obtain for earlier detection, perform as well as tissue samples.

Article.Title: OocystMeter, a machine-learning algorithm to count and measure Plasmodium oocysts, reveals a clustering pattern in the Anopheles midgut
Article.Authors: Peng D.; Marrogi E.; Nelson E.; Liu Q.; Rinvee T.; de Vries L.; Thornburg K.; Singh N.; Shaw W.; Catteruccia F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We present OocystMeter, a machine learning-based software developed to automate the segmentation of malaria oocysts from images of mosquito midguts stained with mercurochrome. Existing bioimage analysis tools, including machine learning-based ones, often struggle with the unique staining patterns, complex midgut backgrounds, and variable morphology of oocysts, making the determination of oocyst size and numbers cumbersome. To overcome these challenges, we curated a high-quality dataset comprised of 11,178 Plasmodium falciparum oocysts in Anopheles gambiae midguts annotated by expert parasitologists. Using this dataset, we fine-tuned a Mask R-CNN object detection model to achieve segmentation accuracy comparable to human parasitologists (Spearman’s correlation of 0.998 for oocyst counts and 0.978 for size measurements). Combining tool-assisted expert annotations with spatial analysis, we identified a non-random oocyst clustering pattern, detectable at shorter spatial scales in infections with 4–74 oocysts/midgut. The analyses did not identify a consistent anatomical region or axis that explains this pattern. Our workflow accelerates image-based oocyst counting and size measurement, standardizes image analysis, and provides spatial coordinates for parasitology studies. Manual dissection, staining, mounting, and image acquisition by human scientists remain necessary. OocystMeter is freely available at https://github.com/duopeng/oocystMeter , and as a web-based tool at http://oocystmeter.org/ , offering a valuable resource for researchers investigating the oocyst stage of malaria development.

Article.Title: Eigenmodes of synthetic antiferromagnetic skyrmions
Article.Authors: Zulfiqar K.; Lang M.; Holt S.; Pathak S.; Bruckner F.; Fangohr H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate the excitation modes of confined synthetic-antiferromagnetic (SAF) skyrmions using micromagnetic eigenvalue and ringdown simulations. Starting from a single skyrmion in a ferromagnetic layer, where the lowest-frequency modes are a gyrotropic and a breathing mode, we study how antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling modifies the dynamics in SAF bilayers. We consider several geometries: single SAF skyrmions in square and rectangular confinement, unequal layer thicknesses, and strips containing multiple skyrmions. The antiferromagnetic coupling strongly modifies the low-frequency dynamics. The square geometry exhibits two nearly degenerate gyrotropic modes, where in each both layers have the same rotation sense. In rectangular geometries, we instead find nearly linear SAF skyrmion translation emerging from opposite gyration sense in the two layers. These translational modes become the characteristic low-frequency excitations of SAF skyrmion chains. For skyrmion chains, we identify collective translational and breathing modes with standing-wave-like spatial profiles. Beyond ferromagnetic-like breathing modes, the SAF geometry supports breathing oscillations in which the two layers oscillate out of phase. We further demonstrate signal propagation along extended SAF skyrmion chains with propagation velocities about 15% larger than in ferromagnetic skyrmion chains. These results provide a systematic description of the collective dynamics of SAF skyrmions arising from the interplay of geometric confinement, intralayer, and interlayer coupling.

Article.Title: A hybrid GA-DL framework for energy-efficient clustering and lifespan extension in RWSNs
Article.Authors: Ti Y.; Cheng R.; Wei S.; Huang W.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The limited energy capacity of sensor nodes remains a central constraint on the operational longevity of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs)—a challenge that is more critical in Rechargeable Wireless Sensor Networks (RWSNs), where sustaining long-term functionality depends on delaying the First Node Death (FND), a key point that often signals the beginning of network problems. While prior research has extensively explored heuristic algorithms coupled with energy-aware routing mechanisms to reduce transmission energy consumption and extend network lifetime, these methods typically require repeated iterations to converge. Such computational demands render them unsuitable for real-time applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a hybrid optimization framework that integrates Genetic Algorithms (GA) with Deep Learning (DL). This framework can run quickly to improve energy efficiency and extend network lifetime in RWSNs. The proposed approach builds upon an energy-aware clustering architecture that incorporates a lightweight version of the Residual Neural Network (ResNet) model. This clustering strategy promotes a more balanced distribution of energy consumption across the network, delaying early node failures caused by localized energy depletion. Based on this setup, we create an optimization scheme using a novel version of GA that helps the ResNet model—simplified for use on regular CPUs—learns an optimal CH selection policy. The GA component employs a custom fitness function designed to maximize the time to FND latency. The synergy between the clustering method and the GA-DL hybrid selection mechanism enables rapid and effective CH assignment without the iterative overhead typical of heuristic algorithms. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only reduces energy consumption and extends the time to FND but also achieves near real-time performance. This makes it a promising alternative to traditional heuristic-based approaches, particularly in latency-sensitive RWSN applications. Together, these contributions mark a significant step toward the development of scalable, efficient, and resilient RWSN architectures.

Article.Title: Compositional inhomogeneity and its impact on the phase transition kinetics of hydrothermally synthesized W-doped VO2
Article.Authors: Cosemans S.; Heirman E.; Broux H.; Volders J.; Leufkens L.; Ghogare D.; Verheijen M.; Paez J.; Elen K.; Mann D.; Hardy A.; Van Bael M.; Buskens P.
Article.Abstract: Tungsten-doped vanadium dioxide is a promising thermochromic material for energy-efficient smart windows. Its performance depends on the thermodynamics and kinetics of the first-order structural phase transition (SPT) between semiconducting monoclinic VO 2 and metallic rutile VO 2 . In this study, W-doped VO 2 microparticles (17–34 μm) were synthesized via a hydrazine-free hydrothermal route using oxalic acid as the reducing agent. The influence of tungsten incorporation on phase formation and on the thermodynamics and kinetics of the SPT was investigated. Structural and morphological analyses show that W 6+ promotes the formation of phase-pure monoclinic and rutile VO 2 . Differential scanning calorimetry revealed switching enthalpies between 15 and 36 J g –1 and a decrease in phase transition temperature with increasing W content. Broad transition profiles and deviations from ideal switching behavior were attributed to compositional and structural inhomogeneities arising from non-uniform tungsten distribution and particle size variation. Isoconversional kinetic analysis demonstrated that the SPT is governed by nucleation kinetics, resulting in a temperature-dependent activation barrier that increases strongly as the temperature approaches the critical switching temperature. Activation energies ranging from 10 3 to 10 4 kJ mol –1 were obtained, indicating that substantial overheating or undercooling is required to achieve rapid thermochromic switching.

Article.Title: Ontogenetic gains in photosynthetic capacity and winter–summer photoprotective contrasts in wild Camellia formosensis across light environments
Article.Authors: Shen J.; Wang C.; Jhou H.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Camellia formosensis , Taiwan’s only native tea-producing tree, is near-threatened and increasingly cultivated as a forest-understory crop, yet light-management guidance derives largely from nursery seedlings. We measured gas exchange of mature wild trees growing in full sun or natural forest shade (10–20% relative light; three trees each) over an annual cycle, and chlorophyll fluorescence, relative chlorophyll content (SPAD) and the photochemical reflectance index (PRI) in winter and summer. Full-sun trees had a higher maximum net photosynthetic rate (Amax) than shaded trees in every season (summer: 14.2 vs. 9.0 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1), together with a higher light compensation point and dark respiration. Light-adapted photosystem II efficiency was markedly lower in winter than in summer in both light environments, coinciding with a site minimum temperature of 5.4 °C; non-photochemical quenching was higher under shade in winter but under full sun in summer. SPAD and PRI were consistently higher under shade. Wild-tree Amax (6.1–14.2 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1) was two- to three-fold that of one-year-old seedlings measured with the same protocol, consistent with an ontogenetic increase in photosynthetic capacity. Moderate shade conferred a pigment-based photoprotective signature shared across life stages, whereas winter chilling emerged as a field-specific constraint not captured by nursery trials.

Article.Title: Spatial multi-omics identifies regional immunometabolic remodeling and macrophage PCK2-associated T-cell activation in lupus nephritis
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Li A.; Guo Q.; Wen M.; Zhao L.; Tan S.; Peng M.; Kong M.; Xu Z.; Zheng L.; Tang Y.
Article.Abstract: Poor response of lupus nephritis (LN) to conventional therapies frequently results in persistent renal inflammation and progression of chronic renal insufficiency. The complex pathogenesis of LN, characterized by microregional immune heterogeneity and interregional crosstalk, greatly hinders identification of the core immune network initiating disease and development of effective therapeutic strategies. Given that metabolic reprogramming drives immune cell activation, exploring region-specific immunometabolic characteristics of LN kidneys is critical for clarifying disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets. This study integrated spatial proteomics, spatial metabolomics and multiplexed immunofluorescence to map the spatial immune landscape of three key regions (glomerulus, renal tubules, medulla) in LN kidneys and analyzed their distinct metabolic profiles. Significant region-specific immunometabolic dysregulation was observed. The glomerular region was enriched with neutrophils and exhibited purine metabolism disorder with upregulated ADCY4; the renal tubules showed obvious T cell aggregation and glycerophospholipid imbalance with elevated Shmt1; the medulla was characterized by macrophage accumulation and increased PCK2 expression within a pyruvate associated metabolic signature. In an inflammatory macrophage–T-cell co-culture model, PCK2 knockdown in macrophages reduced macrophage and T-cell activation readouts. This study delineates distinct region-specific immunometabolic landscapes and key regulatory molecules across different renal compartments in LN. Functional perturbation in vitro further indicated that macrophage PCK2 contributes to T-cell activation under inflammatory co-culture conditions. These findings reveal the heterogeneous immunometabolic pathogenesis of LN and provide promising region-specific metabolic targets for the precise treatment of refractory LN.

Article.Authors: Dai Y.; Zhang Y.; Zhu Y.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a two-stage image translation workflow for urban pocket park design assistance, linking rough line drawings, fine line drawings and spatial semantic layouts. Each setting is trained independently three times and assessed on a common test set using IoU, Dice, boundary F1 and supplementary image and road-representation metrics. Findings show: (1) increasing the number of original image pairs improves final layout reconstruction, with macro-IoU rising from 0.1222 to 0.1516 and Dice from 0.2053 to 0.2494; (2) augmentation provides task-specific benefits: geometric variation improves line-position agreement, while drawing-style perturbation improves selected road graphic properties, but these gains do not consistently translate into better overall layout reconstruction; and (3) comparing reference and automatically refined drawing inputs identifies distinct weaknesses in the transfer of planting information and the interpretation of water and structures. These findings support selecting augmentation according to the intended representation task and reviewing intermediate drawings alongside final layouts. The study provides an experimental basis for training-data organisation, augmentation selection and staged graphic review in generative design assistance for urban pocket parks.

Article.Authors: Alhaj Z.; Alsharafi M.; Altairi A.; AL Naggar N.
Article.Abstract: Reliable comparison of antioxidant potency is complicated by the strong dependence of measured activity on assay conditions. Robustness was examined through repeated compound-grouped cross-validation, scaffold-grouped testing, descriptor-block ablation, architecture controls, response permutation, residual diagnostics, endpoint sensitivity, and applicability-domain analysis. Conditional XGBoost achieved a compound-grouped classification accuracy of \(0.718\pm 0.027\) and known-assay regression performance of \(R^2=0.718\pm 0.053\) . A Morgan ECFP4 random-forest comparator gave the best compound-grouped regression result ( \(R^2=0.739\pm 0.065\) ), but its performance declined under scaffold separation ( \(R^2=0.472\pm 0.303\) ). The connectivity-index blocks did not significantly improve the RDKit-only models after Holm adjustment. These findings support assay-aware modeling for related chemical structures, while showing that predictions for unfamiliar scaffolds require applicability-domain screening and prospective validation.

Article.Title: Rapid residual stress assessment in additively manufactured specimens via standard uniaxial tensile testing
Article.Authors: Voloskov B.; Karpov I.; Em V.; Firsov D.; Simonov A.; Karamov R.; Qian G.; Bryukhanov I.; Fedorenko A.; Evlashin S.; Sergeichev I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High residual stresses (RS) in laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) components present significant structural challenges, yet traditional characterization techniques are cost- and time-intensive. The proposed methods evaluate RS through: (I) plastic work density calculated from cyclic loading-unloading, (II) virtual unloading mathematically projected from standard monotonic tensile data, which also allows the analysis of existing tensile test results, and (III) the detection of a macroscopic micro-yielding threshold (0.01% strain). The estimates were benchmarked against neutron diffraction (ND) measurements across multiple heat-treatment conditions (as-built to 1000 °C). The energy-based approaches (Proposed Methods I and II) demonstrated linear correlations with relative ND stress reductions (R 2 = 0.75 and 0.71, respectively). Furthermore, by subtracting the empirical micro-yielding threshold from condition-specific macroscopic yield strengths, Proposed Method III captured the relative RS relaxation trend. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis supported the proposed mechanistic interpretation by showing localized geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation prior to bulk yielding. These findings show that the proposed mechanical methods can serve as accessible tools for evaluating stress mitigation strategies in additive manufacturing.

Article.Authors: Dickinson M.; Duval M.; Penkman K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hominin and faunal fossil collections are valuable scientific resources for investigating past populations, making it critically important to preserve these rare materials and prioritise minimally destructive methods. Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating of tooth enamel typically requires laboratory irradiation of powdered subsamples; however, the effects of this treatment on organic biomolecules, and therefore their potential reuse for amino acid geochronology (AAG), remain largely unknown. This study investigates the impact of gamma irradiation on amino acids within tooth enamel, and its implications for reuse of leftover ESR-dated enamel for AAG from two palaeolithic sites: Hortus, southern France and Belle-Roche, Belgium (maximum laboratory gamma dose of 1500 and 3000 Gy respectively). Our results show that laboratory irradiation induces negligible racemisation in selected amino acids, although significant correlations between dose and D/L values emerge at higher doses (> 1200 Gy). This demonstrates that while low-level gamma irradiation (e.g. <500 Gy) does not substantially compromise the chemical integrity of amino acids in enamel, higher doses may alter racemisation patterns, potentially affecting AAG interpretation. Consequently, this supports cautious reuse of irradiated ESR powders, preferably those exposed to low laboratory doses, enabling effective reuse of finite fossil tooth enamel resources.

Article.Title: Differential temporal dynamics of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity following minibeam and conventional irradiation
Article.Authors: Bertho A.; Martinez Vicente P.; Fernandez Rodriguez A.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Moros M.; Prezado Y.
Article.Abstract: Minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) improves the therapeutic index by sparing normal tissues while maintaining tumour control, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity showed delayed, dose-dependent and strongly cell-context-dependent responses. Across the three cell lines, MBRT generally produced lower reporter activity than CRT at later measured time points and/or higher doses. These differences were accompanied by distinct cytotoxicity profiles, with CRT generally inducing greater PI positivity than MBRT. MBRT and CRT were associated with different magnitudes and temporal profiles of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity. Because the irradiation modalities also differed in dose rate and cytotoxicity, the present data do not establish that spatial dose heterogeneity itself caused these signalling differences. The findings provide an initial framework for further mechanistic and spatially resolved studies.

Article.Title: O-antigen deficiency in Porphyromonas gingivalis attenuates dendritic cell-driven Th1/Th17-associated CD4+ T-cell responses
Article.Authors: Pavez V.; Melgar-Rodríguez S.; Selman J.; González-Osuna L.; Díaz-Zúñiga J.; Cafferata E.; Carvajal P.; Bravo D.; Vernal R.
Article.Abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a keystone periodontal pathogen whose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contributes to immune dysregulation during periodontitis. Dendritic cells (DCs) link microbial recognition to adaptive immunity; however, how P. gingivalis LPS shapes DC activation and subsequent CD4 + T-cell responses remains incompletely understood. This study examined responses of human monocyte-derived DCs (hMoDCs) and downstream autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to P. gingivalis strains that differ in complete LPS expression. hMoDCs were stimulated with the wild-type W50 strain, the isogenic O-antigen-deficient ΔPG1051 mutant, the complemented cΔPG1051 strain, or left unstimulated. We evaluated hMoDC maturation, cytokine responses, and expression of IRF4, IRF8, NOTCH2, and BATF3 by flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. We then co-cultured stimulated hMoDCs with autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to assess cytokine and RANKL responses by RT-qPCR and ELISA and lineage-associated transcription factor expression by RT-qPCR. All P. gingivalis strains induced comparable maturation of hMoDCs. In contrast, W50 induced robust expression of Th1- and Th17-polarizing cytokines and increased IRF4 and NOTCH2 expression. Notably, ΔPG1051 markedly attenuated these hMoDC responses, and cΔPG1051 restored them. Consistently, CD4 + T lymphocytes co-cultured with ΔPG1051-stimulated hMoDCs showed attenuated Th1- and Th17-type responses, with reduced mRNA expression of Th1- and Th17-related cytokines, T-bet, RORC2, and RANKL, and lower protein levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-17A, IL-23, and RANKL. In contrast, Th2- and Treg-associated cytokines and transcription factors remained largely unchanged. These findings demonstrate that intact P. gingivalis LPS is a major determinant of DC inflammatory programming and its downstream capacity to promote Th1- and Th17-associated CD4 + T-cell responses.

Article.Title: Hemostatic efficacy and safety of oxidized regenerated cellulose hemostatic material in a multi-organ bleeding porcine model
Article.Authors: Li G.; Li Z.; Deng K.; Qiu X.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oxidized regenerated cellulose (ORC) is a widely used absorbable hemostatic agent, but comparative data on its efficacy across different bleeding scenarios remain limited. This study compared the hemostatic efficacy, tissue compatibility, and safety of a domestically produced absorbable ORC (StypCel™) with an imported counterpart (Surgicel® Fibrillar™) in minipig models of liver, gastric wall, and mesenteric bleeding. Sixteen male Bama mini pigs were randomly assigned to StypCel™ or Surgicel® Fibrillar™ groups (n=8 each). Bleeding models were established for each organ, and outcomes including 10‑s blood loss, time to hemostasis, intraoperative blood loss, hematology, liver and kidney function, coagulation parameters, and histological changes were assessed. Both materials exhibited three‑dimensional porous network structures, with StypCel™ showing significantly finer fibers (9.82±0.93 μm vs. 20.59±1.88 μm, P<0.001). In liver, gastric wall, and mesenteric bleeding models, no significant differences were observed between groups in time to hemostasis (P=0.8759, P=0.1578, and P=0.9632, respectively), intraoperative blood loss (P=0.0805, P=0.7673, and P=0.4678, respectively), or any hematological, biochemical, or coagulation parameters at all time points (all P>0.05). Histological analysis revealed similar degradation and absorption profiles, with inflammation essentially resolved by week 4 in both groups. StypCel™ demonstrated equivalent hemostatic efficacy and comparable safety to Surgicel® Fibrillar™ across multiple bleeding models, supporting its use as an effective alternative.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been prominent in our daily lives by means of mobile applications and web search engines. Furthermore, students’ confirmation of AES system positively affects individual innovativeness, reflective thinking and criticism of AES. And students’ individual innovativeness also positively influences students’ reflective thinking of AES. However, students’ individual innovativeness and reflective thinking of AES system doesn’t have a positive relationship with students’ criticism. This study not only reveals Chinese private university EFL students’ attitudes and experiences towards technological tools but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

Article.Title: Time to uptake of long-term postpartum family planning and factors associated with it among Ethiopian mothers: A shared frailty survival analysis
Article.Authors: Kabtyimer A.; Jemil H.; Endalkachew A.; Mankelkl G.; Kassaw A.; Abeje E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-term postpartum family planning (LTPPFP) involves the use of long-acting contraceptive methods within one year after childbirth. Delayed initiation increases the risk of unintended and closely spaced pregnancies, leading to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study assessed the time to LTPPFP uptake and associated factors during the extended postpartum period among mothers in Ethiopia. A secondary analysis of data from the Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia Cohort II, 2021 to 2023 was performed. A total of 2,167 postpartum mothers were included using a multistage stratified sampling technique. Data management and analysis were conducted using Stata 17 and R. Multicollinearity was checked using the variance inflation factor, while the proportional hazards assumption was assessed using the global Schoenfeld residual test. Three shared frailty survival models (cluster-level, region-level, and nested frailty models) were fitted and compared. Adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were presented, and statistical significance was declared at p ≤ 0.05. During the one-year follow-up period, 396 women initiated LTPPFP. Among users, implants accounted for 94% of methods used, while female sterilization represented only 1%. The weighted prevalence of LTPPFP utilization was 14.8% (95% CI: 13.2–16.4). A total of 1,748.37 person-years were observed, yielding an incidence rate of 183.5 per 1,000 person-years. The cumulative survival probability for one year was 0.809. Earlier initiation of LTPPFP was significantly associated with having a plan to use family planning (AHR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.58–3.81), previous family planning use (AHR = 1.90; 95% CI: 1.48–2.43), institutional delivery (AHR = 1.52; 95% CI: 1.03–2.26), postnatal care utilization (AHR = 1.63; 95% CI: 1.00–2.66), complications during delivery (AHR = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.02–1.60), and age at sexual debut > 18 years (AHR = 2.04; 95% CI: 1.20–3.46). LTPPFP initiation remains substantially delayed among postpartum mothers in Ethiopia. Key determinants of earlier uptake included prior family planning experience, service contact points (institutional delivery and postnatal care), and reproductive history characteristics. Strengthening integrated postpartum counseling during maternity care services is essential to facilitate timely LTPPFP adoption.

Article.Authors: Mante P.; Ntewusu J.; Danquah J.; Owusu G.; Dotse D.; Adomako N.
Article.Abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in children is associated with significant morbidity, yet the contribution of systemic inflammation to its clinical expression remains incompletely defined, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study investigated the relationship between systemic inflammatory markers, drug resistance and seizure severity in a paediatric cohort in Ghana. Although these markers were associated with NHS3 seizure-severity scores in pooled analyses, these relationships were substantially attenuated after accounting for DRE status. These findings demonstrate an association between selected systemic inflammatory markers and pediatric DRE and support further prospective evaluation of their clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Imaging shallow magma storage and fluid pathways beneath Aso volcano using ambient-noise tomography
Article.Authors: Tsuji T.; Chhun C.; Andajani R.; Ishikawa Y.; Nishizaka N.; Yano H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the high-resolution three-dimensional internal structure of the large caldera-type volcano Mt. Aso, we deployed a temporary seismometer network and applied ambient-noise surface-wave tomography. We resolve the shallow crustal structure with high spatial resolution and identify an ellipsoidal low S-wave velocity ( Vs ) anomaly at depths of 2.5–4.5 km beneath the Nakadake crater. The Vs within this zone is ~ 1.5 km/s, indicating a highly fractured and pressurized rock, which we interpret as a shallow magma storage zone. Considering the temperature conditions, supercritical fluids could transition to a gas phase beneath the storage zone, leading to volume expansion, fracture opening, and reduced Vs . Furthermore, combined with previously reported temporal variations in seismic velocity and geodetic modeling results, the low- Vs zone could behave as a pressure-sensitive fractured system, potentially connected to the overlying fluid-bearing pathway beneath Aso Volcano. Above the storage zone, we image a narrow, vertically elongated low- Vs structure interpreted as a hydrothermal conduit that likely transports the pressurized fluids to the surface crater and generates very long-period (VLP) tremors.

Article.Title: Network modeling of science teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in science curriculum development
Article.Authors: Ibrahem U.; Alrashood J.; Diab H.; Alrosa T.; Alkhabra Y.; Alotaibi S.; Moussa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employs psychological network modeling to examine the interrelationships among science teachers’ perceptions of benefits, challenges, and attitudes toward integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools in science curriculum development. The estimated network revealed a dense structure. Centrality analyses indicated that curriculum content generation and innovative pedagogical tools were most central, while data processing challenges and algorithmic bias emerged as prominent structural barriers. Centrality metrics identify AI-facilitated curriculum design and innovative pedagogical tools as primary benefits, while challenges such as data processing limitations and algorithmic biases emerge as significant barriers. Teacher attitudes demonstrate ambivalence, characterized by resistance to automating administrative functions alongside guarded optimism for interactive and adaptive learning applications. These insights underscore the imperative to address technical constraints, ethical considerations, and the evolving professional identities of educators to ensure effective AI integration. The study contributes a nuanced, systemic understanding that informs the development of tailored AI tools and support frameworks, ultimately advancing transformative innovation in science education.

Article.Title: HCVSOA: hybrid corona virus–snake optimization for hyperparameter-tuned kinematic handwriting analysis in Parkinson’s disease detection
Article.Authors: Ayus I.; Azad C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working with machine learning models is challenging due to various complex factors such as high-dimensional temporal dependencies, control complexity and poor subject-independent performance. Researchers have identified that the conventional optimization strategies often fail to explore these complex factors fully which limits model robustness and subject-independent performance. The study introduces hybrid heuristic optimization strategy namely, Hybrid Corona Virus-Snake Optimization Algorithm (HCVSOA) which combines the exploratory strengths of Corona Virus Optimization Algorithm (CVOA) with the adaptive exploitation of the Snake Optimization Algorithm (SOA). The HCVSOA framework is capable of tuning model parameters for machine learning models which facilitates more effective temporal feature extraction and structured feature representation for strengthening accurate class-based classification. Experiments are conducted on both handwriting dynamics datasets with meander and spiral patterns. The HCVSOA + Convolutional 1D Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit framework demonstrates superior performance over other considered optimization strategies which records an accuracy of 96.25% on meander New HandPD signals, 97.86% on spiral New HandPD signals and 99.903% on spiral UCI dataset. The observed improvements in performance metrics confirm a well-balanced trade-off between sensitivity and specificity. Further, Area under the Curve and radar analyses confirm enhanced discriminative capability which highlights the consistent advantage across architectures and datasets for hybrid optimization techniques. The proposed HCVSOA significantly improves model subject-independent predictive performance for kinematic handwriting analysis.

Article.Authors: Sridhar J.; Unnissa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blockchain technology has emerged as an innovative digital solution aimed at enhancing transparency, traceability, and trust within closed-loop supply chains, particularly in the domains of remanufacturing and recycling operations. This study formulates a Blockchain-enabled Closed-Loop Supply Chain model that incorporates an original equipment manufacturer $$(M-R)$$ , a retailer-third party $$(R-3p)$$ , and a manufacturer-third party $$(M-3P)$$ . In light of Blockchain investment costs, privacy concerns, information transparency, and competitive dynamics in recycling, a Stackelberg game framework is developed to analyze optimal pricing strategies, collection decisions, and overall profitability. The research investigates the impact of collection competition and Blockchain-related parameters on supply chain performance. Through numerical analysis and sensitivity assessments, the findings reveal that the adoption of Blockchain technology enhances acceptance rates for remanufactured products and influences channel decision-making, whereas intensified competition in collection efforts tends to diminish individual collection performance. The results indicate that the $$M-R$$ model exhibits superior economic performance, while the $$M-3P$$ model demonstrates greater recycling efficiency in the context of intense competition. This research contributes theoretical insights and practical guidance for the design of sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chains through the strategic integration of blockchain technology and optimized recycling channel selection.

Article.Title: Control of source–migration–trap coupling on hydrocarbon accumulation in the Shahejie Formation, Qikou Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Liu W.; Fu G.; Liang M.; Zhang D.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of hydrocarbon accumulation in continental rift basins remains a major challenge in petroleum geoscience because the relative roles of hydrocarbon supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness are often poorly constrained. Focusing on the lower section of the first member of the Shahejie Formation (Es 1 L ), this study formulates a hierarchical control framework that synthesizes source supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness to elucidate the mechanisms of hydrocarbon accumulation. Integrating three-dimensional (3D) seismic, well logging, and geochemical data, this study delineates the distribution of effective source rocks, systematically characterizes vertical and lateral hydrocarbon migration pathways, and identifies the development locations of effective traps in the target interval combined with the evaluation of fault lateral sealing capacity to carry out coupled hydrocarbon accumulation analysis of source-migration-trap. A total of 18 migration pathways and 24 effective trap locations were identified. The hierarchical framework identifies source-rock expulsion intensity as the first-order control, defining the upper limit of hydrocarbon supply; migration-pathway architecture as the second-order control, regulating hydrocarbon focusing, dispersion, and charging efficiency; and trap effectiveness, particularly fault sealing capacity, as the third-order control, governing hydrocarbon preservation and final filling degree. The results indicate that hydrocarbons mainly accumulate in zones with optimal matching of source-migration-trap elements, characterized by sufficient hydrocarbon supply from source rocks, unobstructed migration pathways and effective trap conditions. Production-testing results from Well BS-4, located within one of the predicted favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones, provide field-based support for the proposed coupling framework. The proposed hierarchical source-migration-trap framework provides a process-based approach for evaluating favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones in lower-source upper-reservoir petroleum systems of mature faulted basins.

Article.Authors: Kubota A.; Shinohara Y.; Goto A.; Tajima A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social isolation (SI) during adolescence is associated with neurobiological alterations; however, its effect on the hippocampal epigenome and transcriptome remains unclear. Cell type analyses suggested that SI-downregulated transcriptional signatures were linked to excitatory neurons, whereas SI-upregulated signatures were enriched in non-neuronal populations, particularly oligodendrocytes. Deconvolution suggested higher estimated oligodendrocyte representation and lower estimated excitatory neuron representation in isolated mice. These findings suggest that adolescent SI is associated with significant transcriptomic remodeling and candidate chromatin accessibility changes within hippocampal CA1, accompanied by distinct neuronal- and glial-associated transcriptional signatures.

Younger, smaller individuals in CV showed higher tolerance and lower mortality rates due to milder viral infections. Conversely, larger adults in OA suffered a 100% mortality rate, leading to the extinction of that population by October 2024. Total Hemocyte Count (THC) was lower in OA (1.77 ± 0.16 and.2 ± 5 x 10 4 cells/ml) compared to CV (1.65 ± 8 x 10 5 − 2.62 x 10 5 cells/ml) and with a positive correlation with viral load, connected with percentage of dead cells percentage, in turn correlated with animal size, suggesting that number of immune cells is regulated by the level of infection, and also age. Article.Title: Physical exercise and interviewer-rated appearance: longitudinal evidence from the China family panel studies, 2010–2022
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical appearance is an important form of social capital, yet limited longitudinal evidence exists on whether it can be shaped by modifiable behaviors such as physical exercise. This positive association remains stable across sequentially adjusted model specifications. However, when total weekly exercise duration is used as an alternative measure, the estimated coefficient is no longer statistically significant. The estimated association is somewhat larger among women than among men, although the gender difference is not statistically significant. In addition, lagged exercise frequency is not significantly associated with current appearance ratings, suggesting that the appearance-related benefits of exercise may be more immediate than persistent. This study contributes to the literature by improving identification relative to prior cross-sectional research through panel fixed-effects estimation and by using interviewer-rated appearance. The findings provide longitudinal evidence that physical exercise is associated with external appearance evaluations in a manner that is relevant to real-world social interactions.

Article.Title: High stimulation rate ABR reveals auditory brainstem conduction abnormalities in vestibular migraine
Article.Authors: Li C.; Huang Y.; Wang Y.; Yang S.; Yu W.; Pan Q.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: To explore the application value of high-stimulation-rate auditory brainstem response (ABR) in evaluating auditory pathway conduction in vestibular migraine (VM) patients and to analyze its correlation with clinical symptoms. A prospective case-control study was conducted, including 56 VM patients (56ears) and 56 healthy controls (56 ears). All subjects underwent acoustic immittance testing, pure-tone audiometry, and ABR testing at low (11.1/s) and high (51.1/s) stimulation rates. The interpeak latency variance of wave I–V (ΔI-VIPL) between high and low stimulation rates was calculated, and ≥ 0.28 ms was defined as the abnormal threshold. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) were used to evaluate headache intensity and dizziness-related handicap, respectively. The correlations between these scores and ΔI-VIPL were also analyzed. At the low stimulation rate, no significant differences in ABR parameters were observed between the control and VM groups ( P > 0.05). At the high stimulation rate, the latencies of waves III and V, as well as the I–III, I–V and ΔI-VIPLs, were significantly prolonged in the VM group ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of abnormal ΔI-VIPL was 69.64% (39/56), which was significantly higher than that in the control group 12.50%(7/56), P < 0.05. ROC curve analysis for discriminating VM patients from healthy controls showed that the optimal cutoff value of ΔI-VIPL was 0.265 ms (AUC = 0.791, sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 87.5%, P < 0.05). Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples supported its stability (bootstrap median 0.265 ms, 95% PI 0.215–0.285 ms). Spearman correlation analysis demonstrated that ΔI-VIPL was significantly positively correlated with the total DHI score ( r s =0.623, P < 0.05) and VAS score ( r s =0.534, P < 0.05). High-stimulation rate auditory evoked potential (ABR) can effectively identify abnormal auditory brainstem pathways in VM patients. The ΔI-VIPL parameters show differences among different clinical subtypes, and are closely related to dizziness-related handicap and headache intensity; however, these associations are cross-sectional and should not be interpreted as causal or independently predictive.Therefore, ΔI-VIPL may serve as an auxiliary electrophysiological metric reflecting brainstem auditory conduction stress in VM patients, although further studies with disease controls are required to confirm its clinical utility.

Article.Title: Generative AI-assisted design problem exploration in interaction design: response disclosure, prompt initiative, and cost-sensitive prompting behavior
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Ibrahim F.; Wang Y.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Zhao S.
Article.Abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in early-stage design exploration, yet experimental evidence is limited on how system-side response disclosure and user-side prompt initiative jointly shape the exploration of design problems that are not yet well defined. In a 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, 48 design students completed four interaction-design tasks involving unfamiliar user groups under one-time versus progressive response disclosure and low versus high prompt initiative, with the composition time of every submission logged. Progressive disclosure was associated with greater perceived understanding change, higher self-reported engagement and germane cognitive load, lower extraneous cognitive load, and more prompts. High prompt initiative showed the same pattern on these four self-reported measures but significantly fewer prompts, reversing the predicted direction; composition time accounted for 18% of the exploration window under high initiative and under 2% under low initiative. Both sets of main effects held after multiplicity correction and adjustment for task and period. An exploratory interaction for germane cognitive load did not survive correction. These findings extend a mixed-initiative view of AI-assisted exploration by identifying response structuring and question formulation as separable design levers. They also indicate that prompt frequency should be interpreted together with the cost of producing a submission.

Article.Title: Comparative benchmarking of the small and nano versions YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 for FDM 3D printing fault detection
Article.Authors: Hany H.; Elashry A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printing is widely used in industrial and consumer applications, but printing failures are often detected only after substantial material and production time have been lost. This study presents a controlled benchmark of four lightweight YOLO object detectors, YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s, YOLOv11n, and YOLOv11s, for in-process FDM fault detection. All models were fine-tuned under identical conditions on 5793 annotated images covering six fault classes. Performance was evaluated on clean test images and under three types of synthetic camera degradation: Gaussian blur, directional motion blur, and additive Gaussian noise. Deployment-related metrics, including parameter count, GFLOPs, ONNX model size, GPU latency, and CPU inference latency, were also measured. On clean images, YOLOv8s achieved the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.7905, while YOLOv11n provided comparable nano-scale accuracy with 14% fewer parameters. Stringing remained the most difficult fault class, with AP@0.5 values of approximately 0.45–0.48. The robustness experiments showed that blur caused a gradual reduction in detection performance, while directional motion blur was more severe than Gaussian blur. Additive Gaussian noise produced the largest performance degradation. Across the extended degradation grid, YOLOv11n achieved the lowest Degradation Sensitivity Index (DSI) of 28.80%, and also provided the fastest CPU inference at 48.11 ms/image and the smallest model footprint at 10.61 MB. These results provide a practical benchmark for selecting lightweight YOLO models and designing robust FDM monitoring systems.

Article.Title: Phase-matched ion pre-acceleration by upstream magnetic dipole vortices in relativistic collisionless shocks
Article.Authors: Naseri N.; Turkakin H.; Shvets G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Collisionless shocks are among the most efficient particle accelerators in the Universe, yet the physical mechanism responsible for energetic upstream seed ions remains poorly understood. Using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of unmagnetized relativistic electron-ion shocks, we investigate ion pre-acceleration by self-generated magnetic dipole vortices (MDVs) in the upstream region of the shock. We identify two distinct ion populations: one remains phase matched with the propagating MDV, undergoes substantial energization, and returns toward the shock, whereas the other escapes upstream after gaining only modest energy. We show that the magnetic component of the Lorentz force reduces the ion’s longitudinal velocity relative to the moving MDV, extending the interaction time and allowing the transverse electric field to perform sustained positive work. Decomposition of the electric field shows that both the motional electric field associated with the moving MDV and plasma-generated fields contribute to the observed ion energization. Repeated interactions with successive MDVs can increase ion energy before the particles return to the shock transition region. These results identify upstream MDVs as a self-consistent pre-injection mechanism, providing the energetic seed ions required for subsequent shock acceleration.

Article.Title: Interpretable prediction of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis
Article.Authors: Meng S.; Yu S.; Zhu X.; Zhou S.; Zhu S.; Yu Y.; Xie Y.; Huang Z.; Xiang M.; Ma H.
Article.Abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a concern among critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis, yet individualized risk stratification in this population remains limited. We developed nine prediction models using 8,825 patients from MIMIC-IV and externally validated them in 5,425 eICU records. Fifteen predictors were identified through combined least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Boruta feature selection. XGBoost achieved the highest observed discrimination, with ROC AUCs of 0.764 (95% CI, 0.723–0.805) internally and 0.731 (95% CI, 0.676–0.786) externally. SHAP analysis identified atrial tachycardia/fibrillation, respiratory failure, previous thromboembolism, antiplatelet therapy, and mechanical ventilation within 24 h as the leading contributors to model predictions. External validation highlighted the value of recalibration, with exploratory five-fold cross-fitted intercept recalibration improving overall calibration and predictive accuracy. Decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit at selected low-risk thresholds following recalibration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of an interpretable prediction model based on routinely available clinical data, with potential for integration into ICU workflows to support individualized VTE risk stratification and targeted surveillance.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a multidimensional scale for heat-related health behavior across domains of everyday life
Article.Authors: Schmid-Ellinger J.; Bachner J.; Blaschke S.; Mess F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heat is an escalating global health risk, yet how populations adapt behaviorally remains poorly understood. We developed and psychometrically evaluated a novel instrument to assess heat-related health behavior (HRHB) across domains of everyday life and along a continuum from reactive to anticipatory responses in a large population-based sample in Germany ( N = 3,351). Factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure capturing both domain-specific (diet, housing, clothing, activity/change of location) and temporal adaptations. HRHB showed good reliability and moderate associations with heat-related health literacy and knowledge, indicating related but distinct constructs. Higher levels of reported behavior were associated with greater symptom burden, consistent with behavior being partly driven by experienced heat strain. HRHB explained additional variance in symptoms beyond sociodemographic and cognitive factors, supporting its incremental validity. These findings identify behavioral adaptation as a distinct and measurable dimension of population-level heat resilience, enabling improved identification of vulnerable groups and more targeted public health interventions.

Article.Title: Phytochemical profiling and computational analysis highlight anabsinthin as a potential ligand of coronavirus main protease
Article.Authors: Loukman S.; Hadad S.; Mesrar F.; Talha A.; Tachallait H.; Benmrid R.; Bouchmaa N.; Daoud R.; Fatimy R.; Benhida R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural products remain an important source of diverse structures for antiviral drug development, but pinpointing and prioritizing bioactive metabolites from complex plant extracts remains challenging. We developed an integrated approach combining phytochemical analysis and computational methods to identify sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia absinthium L as potential candidates for interaction with the conserved coronavirus main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), a crucial target for viral replication. Using a Box–Behnken design, we optimized ultrasound-assisted extraction, followed by GC-MS and LC-MS profiling to analyze solvent-dependent phytochemical profiles. Ethanol yielded the highest extraction efficiency and enriched dimeric sesquiterpene lactones such as absinthin and anabsinthin, which were purified via preparative HPLC. These compounds were assessed through molecular docking, ADMET and toxicity predictions, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, with X77 and nirmatrelvir used as reference compounds. Both lactones were predicted to fit within the Mpro active site, with anabsinthin showing the most favorable predicted binding profile. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the anabsinthin–Mpro complex displayed greater stability, lower backbone deviations, reduced residue fluctuations, and persistent interactions with key residues, including Glu166 and Gln189. In silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity predictions suggested generally favorable early drug-like characteristics without prominent predicted toxicity alerts. This integrated workflow combining extraction optimization, phytochemical profiling, purification, and computational assessment provides a rational strategy for prioritizing natural products for further investigation. Among the compounds examined in this study, anabsinthin emerged as the most promising A. absinthium -derived lactone candidate for subsequent experimental evaluation against Mpro. However, these computational predictions require confirmation through biochemical and cellular assays before direct Mpro inhibition or antiviral activity can be established.

Article.Title: Normative OCT-derived ocular measurements in rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Lester J.; Barron Arrambide A.; Burgos-Rodriguez A.; Schwantes G.; Ede E.; Nepal P.; Fasih-Ahmad S.; Huynh L.; Zambrano R.; Lee T.; Kim B.; Schuman J.; N/A N/A.; Antón S.; Brent L.; Higham J.; Martinez M.; Melin A.; Montague M.; Platt M.; Sallet J.; Snyder-Mackler N.; Melin A.; Higham J.; Danias J.
Article.Abstract: To define normative OCT-derived measurements of the retina, optic nerve head (ONH) macrostructure, and lamina cribrosa (LC) microstructure in a large cohort of healthy, predominantly youngadult rhesus macaques, and to investigate their association with demographic traits and image quality. In vivo spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) scans of the macula, peripapillary retina, and ONH were obtained from 52 healthy animals (90 eyes). Macular and peripapillary scans were segmented to measure the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL), and total retinal thicknesses. ONH macrostructure and LC microstructure were quantified using software of our own design. Linear mixed-effects modeling was used to assess association between demographic features, image quality, and OCT-derived ocular measurements. Average macular GCIPL and peripapillary RNFL thicknesses were 80.6 ± 6.4 and 96.8 ± 8.9 µm, respectively. Average cup-to-disc ratio and cup depth were 0.46 ± 0.18 and 75.6 ± 50.3 µm, respectively. Average LC beam-to-pore-ratio was 2.06 ± 0.37. Significant associations existed between LC OCT quality and most LC microstructural parameters. We present robust normative ocular measurements of the healthy rhesus macaque eye and demonstrate LC microstructural measurements are sensitive to image quality, which should be considered in any future analysis of these parameters.

Article.Title: Industrial defect image generation via structured latent-space interpolation
Article.Authors: Cang Y.; Rong H.; Zou R.; Ma J.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial visual defect detection suffers from scarce defect samples, limiting generalization. We propose a novel image generation framework that synthesizes diverse and realistic defect images through three sequential innovations. First, we introduce UMAP-based dimensionality reduction to project VAE latent features onto a low-dimensional manifold while preserving local neighborhood structure, thereby enabling artifact-free sampling in the subsequent stage. Second, we design a PSO-optimized Gaussian mixture model to capture the sparse, multimodal distribution of defect features within this manifold, and sample new coordinates from high-likelihood regions to generate diverse yet realistic defect representations. Third, we employ a non-parametric radial basis function interpolator to map these sampled coordinates back to the original VAE latent space, preserving geometric continuity and restoring high-frequency defect details before decoding. Experiments on bearing-defect and public industrial datasets show that detectors trained with a synthetic-to-real ratio $$\le 1:3$$ achieve superior accuracy and robustness, validating each innovation’s effectiveness.

Article.Title: Simulation-based implementation of the developed system dynamics model for sustainable urban water supply systems
Article.Authors: Hassan Z.; Rehan R.; Khan F.; Khan M.; Ali A.; Nasery M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water is an indispensable resource, underpinning not only domestic livelihoods, but also the social and economic fabric of nations. Climate change serves among the most formidable threats to the world’s freshwater reserves. Naturally, potable water serves as a finite and precious commodity, merely, 3% is fresh, 2% locked within glaciers and polar ice caps, leaving only 1% accessible for human use. As global water consumption increases at an average rate of 1% annually. Projections alarms need of adopting robust and advanced water management policies, as only 60% of the world’s required water supply will be available by 2030. This crisis is most acutely felt, in developing nations with rapid population growth and pervasive poverty compounds water scarcity. In Pakistan, groundwater serves as the cornerstone of the national domestic water supply infrastructure approximately, meeting 70% of drinking water demands nationwide. Moreover, the widening chasm between water demands and supply urgently required, innovative water management strategies. At present, in Pakistan, urban water supply planning, development, and maintenance remain heavily anchored in conventional engineering and demand-driven frameworks. This study develops the first tailored System Dynamics decision-support model for Peshawar’s urban water system, introducing a novel coupling of an age-band leakage formulation with proactive pipe replacement policies tailored for intermittent, groundwater-dependent utilities. At its foundation, lies meticulously on a constructed Causal Loop Diagram, serving as a comprehensive visual map. To capture, the intricate interdependencies in social, financial, and physical/technical sectors of urban water supply systems. The framework was operationalized and demonstrated on Tehsil Peshawar over a 50-year simulation horizon. Currently, the public water supply system in Peshawar, comprising of tube wells collectively discharging approximately 2 million gallons per hour. However, at baseline static conditions, the total water demand is 6.01 MGH with an estimated leakage rate of 1.703 MGH (28.3%). Crucially, comparing these requirements against the actual municipal abstraction capability of 2 million GPH reveals a 3-fold supply deficit. This structural gap highlights the disparity between standard design benchmarks (250 LPCD) and real-world supply capacities, demonstrating how operational intermittent supply acts as a forced rationing mechanism under current system constraints. Critically, energy costs constitute nearly 80% of total tube well operating expenses, positioning energy optimization as a linchpin of financial sustainability. The study advocates for solar-based energy alternatives, demand management interventions and proactive groundwater replenishment strategies as transformative interventions. This paper makes a compelling case of holistic and systems-thinking approaches, embracing full complexity of sustainable water governance, offering a replicable and scalable model for developing nations confronting analogous of water security challenges.

Article.Title: Predicting the number of infant deaths per woman in ethiopia using complementary count regression and machine learning approaches
Article.Authors: Aga M.; Dugasa S.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infant mortality remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding factors associated with cumulative infant deaths and improving their prediction may help identify populations with higher infant-death burdens. This study examined maternal-level counts of infant deaths ever experienced by women in Ethiopia using complementary count-regression and machine-learning approaches. Data from the 2019 Ethiopia Mini Demographic and Health Survey were analyzed among 5,846 women with complete birth histories. The outcome was the cumulative number of infant deaths experienced by each woman. Because the outcome is mechanically related to the number of births, the logarithm of the number of children ever born was incorporated as an exposure offset in the count-regression models and excluded from the machine-learning predictor set. Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP), and zero-inflated negative binomial models were compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. Poisson Random Forest, Extreme gradient boost (XGBoost)-Poisson, and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-Poisson models were evaluated using 70% training and 30% independent testing split, with five-fold cross-validation for hyper-parameter tuning. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). The ZIP model provided the best fit among the evaluated count-regression models, with the lowest AIC (2503) and BIC (2544). In the count component, maternal age, household wealth, postnatal care, child vaccination status, maternal education, and place of delivery were statistically associated with the expected number of infant deaths. In the machine-learning analysis, XGBoost-Poisson achieved the best test-set predictive performance, with an MAE of 0.320 and RMSE of 0.570. Region had the largest relative predictive contribution (gain = 0.190), followed by marital status (0.167), maternal age (0.136), education level (0.125), and wealth index (0.117). These variable-importance measures represent predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Cumulative infant-death counts among women in Ethiopia were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and maternal and child healthcare characteristics. The ZIP model provided interpretable adjusted associations, whereas XGBoost-Poisson provided the best out-of-sample prediction among the evaluated machine-learning models. The findings support the value of combining inferential count regression with count-specific machine-learning methods while emphasizing that predictive importance does not establish causality. Continued attention to maternal education, socioeconomic disadvantage, postnatal care, immunization, and access to appropriate delivery care may help inform child-survival strategies in Ethiopia.

Article.Title: Multi-environment evaluation of finger millet genotypes for agronomic traits, yield stability and adaptability for summer cultivation
Article.Authors: Mishra S.; Rajendran A.; Kumar S.; Thakur M.; Kishor K.; Singh M.; Chandra M.; Banoriya R.; Shivraj G.; Mundakochi M.; Dash P.
Article.Abstract: Identification and advancement of high yielding and early maturing finger millet genotypes for summer season is essential for crop diversification in the Indo-Gangetic flood plains to enhance food security and production efficiency. The current experiment studied 145 finger millet genotypes under six contrasting environments namely: E2, E4, and E6 (summer) and E1, E3, and E5 (rainy) in three consecutive years (2021–2024) to identify parents suitable for the development of specific varieties and superior genotypes for summer cultivation. An integrated analytical framework combining AMMI, GGE biplot, BLUP, WAAS and MTSI were employed to reveal greater insights. REML/BLUP analysis was employed to enhance the reliability of selection, which revealed that genotypic variance accounted for a larger proportion of the phenotypic variance (49.5%) than genotype × environment interaction variance (24.3%), coupled with moderate broad-sense heritability (0.49) and high selection accuracy (0.95). AMMI found C3, C2, C1, G120 and G11 to take the top high yielding genotypes and G111, G12, G7, G65 and G81 were the most stable. GGE mean vs. stability biplot indicated G120, G80 and G29 as broadly adapted and high-yielding, G120 topped as the best performer and G52 and G68 summer-specific adaptors (E2 and E4). BLUP predicted results with re-affirmation of G120, G29 and G80 as the good performers. C3, C2, C1, G120, G29, G28 and G85 were grouped by the WAAS index as ideal (high yield and stable). Multi-Trait Stability Index (MTSI) also identified eighteen genotypes that could be improved simultaneously for multiple traits. Overall, the elite genotypes (G120, G80, G29 and the check varieties C1, C2, and C3) are useful as parents for breeding climate resilient finger millet varieties adapted to summer climatic conditions in the Gangetic plains of India.

Article.Title: Bhallatakadi modaka induces apoptosis of cancer cells via activating ROS/p-ERK pathway
Article.Authors: Dixit A.; Mishra S.; Ghosh D.; Shrivastava N.; Sarkar M.; Paul M.; Bose S.; Kumar D.; Basak S.; Dey R.; Roy S.; Saha S.; Jagtap C.; Nair P.; Bora M.; Babu G.; YR S.; Srikanth N.; Acharya R.; Srivastava A.
Article.Abstract: Bhallatakadi modaka (BM) is an Ayurvedic formulation that has been traditionally used for various therapeutic purposes, but its anticancer effects and underlying molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized.This study aimed to investigate the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of BM in cancer cell lines and a xenograft mouse model. In vitro assays, including MTT and clonogenicity assays, revealed that BM inhibited cancer cell growth and induced apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Flow cytometry, DAPI/PI staining, and Western blotting further confirmed apoptosis induction. Additionally, BM treatment reduced the cancer stem cell population, evidenced by a decrease in CD44+CD117+ cells and reduced sphere formation. Mechanistically, the formulation induced the generation of ROS, which activated the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) pathway, culminating in apoptosis. Increased expression of apoptosis markers such as cleaved caspase-3 and decreased total PARP1 further confirm the apoptotic effect. In vivo, treatment with BM in OVCAR-3 xenograft-bearing mice led to a significant reduction in tumor size compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry showed a marked decrease in Ki-67 expression, indicating suppressed tumor cell proliferation. Overall, the data suggest that BM may inhibit cancer cell growth through mechanisms involving ROS accumulation, p-ERK activation, and induction of apoptosis.

Article.Title: Formononetin-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles attenuate inflammatory signaling in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes
Article.Authors: Faheem M.; Ahmad A.; Munawar N.; Ali M.; Akhtar B.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with persistent synovial inflammation induced by pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases. Formononetin (FN), a plant isoflavone, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties with therapeutic potential for RA. This research aimed to prepare FN-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (FN-SLNPs) and determine whether nanoencapsulation preserves chemical identity, increases antioxidant potential, and enhances anti-inflammatory activity in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes. FN-SLNPs were characterized by particle size and zeta potential analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), UV-visible spectroscopy, and antioxidant profiling, including total flavonoid content, total phenolic content, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity. In vitro biological activity in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A cells was evaluated using cytotoxicity analysis by MTT assay, protein quantification by ELISA, and gene expression analysis by qRT-PCR. FN-SLNPs showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 148 ± 42 nm and a zeta potential of − 27.3 ± 1.3 mV. SEM revealed crystalline lipid domains. FTIR confirmed the chemical retention of isoflavone functional groups. Flavonoid content and total phenolic content increased with FN-SLNP loading compared with pure FN. DPPH radical scavenging activity was highest for FN-SLNPs at 20 mg compared with pure FN. TNF-α increased MH7A cell viability to 145.2 ± 5.8%. FN-SLNPs at 100 µg/mL reduced viability to 85.4 ± 3.1%, decreased interleukin-1β (IL-1β) protein levels from 0.0182 ± 0.0015 to 0.0035 ± 0.0003 µg/mL, and reduced IL1B gene expression from 18.50 ± 1.20 to 2.90 ± 0.25. These findings indicate that FN-SLNPs preserve the chemical identity of FN, enhance its antioxidant activity, and potentiate anti-inflammatory responses in MH7A synoviocytes.

Article.Title: Development of an original PAm@P hydrogel for high-performance cationic dye removal from wastewater
Article.Authors: Nayl A.; Arafa W.; Ahmed I.; Alanazi A.; Alanazi M.; Mostafa A.; Akl M.; Bräse S.; Abd-Elhamid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, an original and simple method was employed to modify polyacrylamide (PAm) with sodium phosphate (Na₃PO₄), yielding a sodium phosphate-modified polyacrylamide hydrogel (PAm@P) with promising swelling and adsorption properties compared to pristine, unmodified polyacrylamide. The PAm@P hydrogel was characterized using various advanced techniques to confirm successful modification of PAm and the formation of the PAm@P hydrogel. Swelling experiments demonstrated that phosphate modification significantly enhanced the swelling capacity of PAm@P hydrogel (%S = 7000 at t = 60 min and pH 9.5) compared to unmodified PAm. The adsorption performance of PAm@P was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) dye. The adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model exhibiting the best fit with the highest value for the correlation factor (R 2 ) of 0.999, comparing with R 2 values obtained for the other investigated models (0.976, 0.976, 0.993, and 0.654 for Pseudo first order, Liquid film diffusion, and intra-particle diffusion (step1 and step 2) kinetic models, respectively. These results demonstrated that the investigated adsorption process may be explained as chemisorption is the dominant mechanism. Also, the Langmuir isotherm model illustrated the R² value (0.999) with a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (q max ) of 746.26 mg g − 1 for MB dye. While the R² values for the other investigated adsorption isotherm models were 0.254, 0.672, and 0.704 for Freundlich, Tempkin, and Flory-Higgins models, respectively. Also, the highest experimental adsorption capacity (q max = 1490 mg g –1 ) was obtained under the optimum adsorption conditions with an initial MB-dye concentration of 300 mg L –1 , PAm@P hydrogel dosage of 0.005 g, solution volume of 25 mL, pH 7, contact time of 120 min, and temperature of 25 °C. Furthermore, the PAm@P hydrogel exhibited selective adsorption and separation of the cationic dye MB in the presence of other dyes, such as Rhodamine B (RhB) and Azorubine (E122). The adsorption selectivity of the fabricated PAm@P hydrogel was quantitatively evaluated by calculating the selectivity factor (SF) where it was 2.31 for MB/Rhodamine B and 3.10 for MB/E122, confirming the preferential adsorption of MB-due over the other investigate dyes under identical experimental conditions. Moreover, the PAm@P hydrogel exhibited good regeneration and reusability performance over three consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. The adsorption efficiency decreased gradually from 96.56% in the first cycle to 62.63% after the third cycle, indicating that approximately 64.9% of the initial adsorption efficiency was retained. Finally, the application of the prepared PAm@P hydrogel to real wastewater samples demonstrated its practical feasibility and highlighted its potential as an efficient adsorbent material for industrial wastewater treatment applications. This confirms that the investigated hydrogel is economical, promising, and can significantly reduce wastewater pollutants.

Article.Title: Mathematical and machine learning analysis of high-density polyethylene thermal degradation
Article.Authors: S S.; M A.
Article.Abstract: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) is widely used to characterize polymer degradation, but repeated experiments and conventional single-step kinetic models can become inefficient or inadequate when degradation is nonlinear, multistage, atmosphere-dependent, or evaluated outside the conditions used for calibration. This study developed a machine learning (ML) regression framework to predict the percentage mass remaining during high-density polyethylene (HDPE) degradation. Twenty-five TGA specimens (8–20 mg) yielded 237,154 observations; time, temperature, and initial mass were used as predictors. Random Forest, Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost), and a multilayer perceptron artificial neural network (MLP–ANN) were compared with a hybrid NGBoost–ETR model. Performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R²), mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). The hybrid model achieved R² = 0.999987, MSE = 0.027042, RMSE = 0.164446, and MAE = 0.015879 on the dataset. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) ranked time and temperature as the dominant predictors, while initial mass had a smaller contribution. The optimized point-prediction model was deployed through a Django web interface. The framework provides rapid within-domain interpolation of HDPE TGA profiles; external validation across polymer grades, heating programs, and laboratories remains necessary before replacing experimental TGA.

Article.Title: Social participation patterns are associated with distinct salutogenic and mental health profiles in older Japanese adults
Article.Authors: Hamada M.; Sawada Y.; Sakano J.; Okata H.; Yajima Y.; Sasahara S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social participation is widely promoted as a key factor in healthy aging, but its configuration may matter beyond participation volume. This cross-sectional web-based study examined social participation patterns and their associations with psychosocial resources and mental health among 998 older adults in Japan. Latent class analysis identified three patterns: Low-engagement ( n = 550, 55.1%), Leisure-oriented engagement ( n = 408, 40.9%), and Broad multi-domain engagement ( n = 40, 4.0%). Covariate-adjusted BCH analyses showed that the Leisure-oriented class had a favorable psychosocial profile. The multi-domain class had the highest adjusted means for positive mental health and social well-being, although neither differed significantly from the Leisure-oriented class. Compared with the Leisure-oriented class, the multi-domain class showed lower sense of coherence, particularly comprehensibility and manageability, and higher psychological distress (|d| = 0.48). Sensitivity analyses provided partial support for this mixed profile, although class proportions and some distal-outcome contrasts varied across model specifications. These findings highlight the importance of social participation configurations beyond participation volume, revealing that favorable positive mental health can coexist with lower salutogenic orientation and elevated psychological distress relative to the Leisure-oriented profile. A person-centered approach may therefore provide a nuanced understanding of social participation and mental health in later life.

Article.Title: Graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for industrial supply chain efficiency optimization
Article.Authors: Yao J.; Aldawood M.; Daghistani A.; Alnowibet K.
Article.Abstract: Industrial supply-chain decisions are affected by variable demand, transportation delays, and inventory uncertainty. This study evaluates an integrated Graph-MAPPO framework that combines graph-based state representation with cooperative multi-agent policy learning in a data-informed supply-chain simulation environment. A deterministic mapping of 1,873 development-period DataCo records produced 140 proxy nodes and 2,626 transaction-induced directed links; the subsequent operational trajectories were generated by explicit simulation rules rather than replayed as observed industrial trajectories. Normal, Surge, Disruption, and Mixed demand/lead-time scenarios were evaluated with fully specified distributions and reserved random seeds. For the controlled comparison, all learning-based baselines used 1,000 training episodes, the same cooperative reward, equivalent tuning effort, and common evaluation seeds; a 10-step rolling-horizon MPC baseline was also implemented. Graph-MAPPO obtained a mean episode reward of − 24.2559, a mean backlog of 41.05 units, and a service level of 99.70%. Several baselines achieved higher reward or lower backlog, and rolling-horizon MPC achieved the strongest scalar reward-backlog score but required substantially greater online computation. The ablation results support a contribution from graph-aware representation within the evaluated architecture, but the findings demonstrate a specific coordination-computation trade-off rather than general superiority or validated industrial deployment.

Article.Title: Association between the Planetary Health Diet and foot ulcer size and renal biomarkers among diabetic patients with foot ulcers in a cohort study
Article.Authors: Geravand F.; Nasli-Esfahani E.; Jalalzadeh M.; Montazer M.; Kazeminejad S.; Javadi F.; Tanha S.; Azadbakht L.
Article.Abstract: Planetary Health diet index (PHDI) has been associated with chronic diseases and mortality. This study examines the relationship between PHDI and foot ulcer indices, as well as renal biochemical markers, in patients with type 2 diabetes and foot ulcers. We prospectively included 219 patients with type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) aged 25–75 years in Tehran, Iran. This study took place at the Diabetes Clinic of Tehran University of Medical Sciences. To assess dietary intake, three 24-h dietary recalls were conducted. We evaluated adherence to the PHDI based on EAT-Lancet guidelines. Length, width, and depth of ulcers and biochemical renal biomarkers were obtained from medical records at baseline. Participants were followed for 1 year. Multivariable linear regression models, adjusted for potential confounders, were used to assess the relationship between adherence to PHDI and the outcomes. Our findings revealed that higher adherence to the PHDI was related to lower serum creatinine (Cr) (β = −0.18, 95% CI: −0.33, −0.03), blood urea (β = −14.18, 95% CI: −22.89, −5.46), and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (β = 17.18, 95% CI: 3.53, 30.82) in fully adjusted models. However, no significant relationship between PHDI and ulcer characteristics (length; β = −0.29, 95% CI: −1.15, 0.55, width; β = −0.07, 95%CI: −0.34, 0.49, and depth; β = −0.10, 95% CI: −0.60, 0.40) was observed. Each 10-point increase in PHDI was not significantly associated with ulcer indices. This study indicated inverse associations between adherence to the PHDI and Cr, urea, and eGFR in diabetic patients with foot ulcers. Further cohort research with larger sample sizes could yield more comprehensive insights.
