Article.Title: Benchmarking machine-learning surrogates for rapid prediction of the reflectance-defined stopband width of finite dielectric Bragg reflectors
Article.Authors: Bouazzi Y.; Esmail M.; Touahmia M.; Elleuch Z.; Alshammari S.; Selmi F.; Kanzari M.; Bouandas H.; Soliman S.
Article.Abstract: Predicting the stopband width of finite one-dimensional dielectric Bragg reflectors requires a transfer-matrix calculation followed by spectrum-level edge extraction for each candidate stack. Although an individual wavelength-vectorized TMM evaluation is inexpensive, this calculation is repeated throughout large screening campaigns. Five supervised regressors are benchmarked as surrogates for the reflectance-defined stopband width Δλ Stop of finite multilayers at normal incidence, in the lossless, non-dispersive limit. TMM spectra were generated for stacks parameterized by the refractive indices n L and n H , the layer thicknesses d L and d H , and the number of bilayers N. For each spectrum, Δλ Stop was taken as the widest continuous interval with R(λ) ≥ 0.95. Designs with no such interval, or with a widest interval below 5 nm, were excluded, retaining 1660 of 2000 sampled designs. Hyperparameters of RF and SVR were selected by 10-fold cross-validation on the 1411-structure development set, while MLP depth was examined from one to ten hidden layers under the same test-isolated protocol. The selected six-hidden-layer MLP (128,64,32,16,16,16) achieved R 2 = 0.9862, RMSE = 10.47 nm, and MAE = 5.92 nm on the independent 249-structure test set. On a structured external set of 120 quarter-wave designs from four dielectric pairs, the final MLP achieved R 2 = 0.9688, RMSE = 5.67 nm, and MAE = 4.44 nm against the TMM reference; 94.17% of the cases had absolute errors below 10 nm and all 120 cases remained below 20 nm. Under an accuracy-controlled benchmark, the wavelength-vectorized TMM required 0.856 ms per structure at the selected 201-point spectral grid, whereas end-to-end single-sample inference with the final MLP, including input standardization, required 0.328 ms, corresponding to a 2.60× speedup. The surrogate is intended as a bounded-domain screening tool complementing, not replacing, full TMM analysis.

Article.Title: Carrier-selective dimensional crossover from bulk stibnite Sb2S3 to the single-chain limit
Article.Authors: Ulian G.; Valdrè G.
Article.Abstract: Low-dimensional materials display physical properties markedly different from their bulk counterparts because of quantum confinement. Chain-based chalcogenides provide pre-formed structural motifs for exploring one-dimensional (1D) electronic behaviour without cutting or passivating an extended two-dimensional lattice. In the present work, we use hybrid density functional calculations and semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory to characterize the mineral stibnite (Sb 2 S 3 ) across its structural hierarchy, from the bulk (3D) crystal to the natural (100) cleavage layer (2D) and finally to the unsupported single-chain limit. Phonon dispersions show that both 2D and 1D models are dynamically stable, while the energy analysis quantifies the progressive removal of inter-chain interactions. The 2D layer retains a slightly enlarged indirect gap and exhibits the most dispersive chain-direction conduction band, giving the lightest electron mass among the three systems. By contrast, complete chain isolation opens a wider direct gap and produces an exceptionally flat, strongly non-parabolic valence-band edge together with finite full-zone dispersion. Transport calculations at equal carrier loading reveal a carrier-polarity-dependent crossover: hole transport evolves comparatively regularly from bulk to layer to chain, whereas the electron branch is non-monotonic because the highly dispersive 2D conduction band combines high conductivity with weak energy selectivity. Water adsorption weakly perturbs the isolated chain, while oxygen produces structural activation and an in-gap hybrid state. These results define the intrinsic single-chain reference for Sb 2 S 3 and clarify how partial and complete inter-chain decoupling reorganize its frontier electronic states.

Article.Title: Knowledge and attitudes of Egyptian medical students towards artificial intelligence application in medical practice: a multicenter cross‑sectional study
Article.Authors: El-Helaly M.; Hussein A.; Taman A.; Farrag N.; Elfeky A.; Elhelaly A.; Essam N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly impacted various fields, including medicine. As AI integration in medicine expands, medical students and professionals need to develop a comprehensive understanding of its applications. This study aimed to explore the self-reported knowledge and attitudes of undergraduate Egyptian medical students regarding artificial intelligence application in medical practice. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between June and August 2025 among undergraduate medical students from seven Egyptian medical schools. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were collected via a validated structured web-based questionnaire distributed through social media to assess students’ demographics, knowledge, and attitudes toward AI applications in medical practice. This study included 1438 medical students with a mean age of 20.3 years ± 1.9 years. Overall, 55.3% demonstrated good knowledge and 66.8% showed a positive attitude toward AI applications in medical practice. Good knowledge was significantly higher among students in higher academic years (3rd year AOR = 1.88, P = 0.006; 4th year AOR = 2.02, P = 0.007; 5th year AOR = 1.86, P = 0.034) and among those reporting peers and mentors (AOR = 1.35, P = 0.017), scientific papers and books (AOR = 1.71, P < 0.001), training courses (AOR = 1.43, P = 0.004), and mass media (AOR = 1.32, P = 0.036) as their main sources of AI information. A positive attitude toward AI was significantly more common among male students (AOR = 1.50, P = 0.001), 4th-year students (AOR = 1.97, P = 0.014), and those willing to enroll in an AI course (AOR = 1.30, P = 0.039). YouTube was perceived as the most valuable social media source for AI-related information (90.4%), followed by Telegram (86.6%) and WhatsApp (65.2%). Although the Egyptian medical students who participated in this study demonstrated generally positive attitudes toward AI and a willingness to learn, they may be navigating this transition with limited institutional guidance. These findings suggest that medical schools should consider integrating AI-related technical literacy and ethical reasoning into the core curriculum.

Article.Title: An integrated wireless sEMG framework with Bayesian-optimized machine learning for multi-task locomotor classification and neuromuscular characterization
Article.Authors: Wagdy D.; Rashad S.; Malek A.; Anwar H.; Kandil A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wearable surface electromyography (sEMG) systems show strong potential for real-time gait analysis, yet few frameworks combine wireless acquisition, standardized normalization, and optimized machine learning within a single validated pipeline, leaving their joint contribution to subject-independent locomotor recognition unclear. This study developed and validated a custom wireless sEMG framework combining hardware design, normalization evaluation, and Bayesian-optimized machine learning for locomotor-task classification and neuromuscular characterization. An ESP32-based system recorded tibialis anterior, soleus, and gastrocnemius lateralis activity in 25 healthy participants during level walking, stair ascent, and ramp ascent. Signals were bandpass filtered (20–500 Hz), rectified, and used to extract 120 time-, frequency-, and time–frequency-domain features. Three normalization strategies, three feature-selection methods, and eight Bayesian-optimized classifiers were evaluated via an exploratory participant-level split, nested 5 × 5 cross-validation, leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation, and an independent test set. Task-dependent EMG differences were significant with large effect sizes (η 2 = 0.183–0.708, p < .001). Level walking was the most electromyographically distinct task, while stair and ramp ascent were similar yet separable; ramp ascent showed multi-muscle co-activation at mid-stance and peak soleus activity at toe-off (50.7 ± 6.2% MVC). Genetic Algorithm feature selection with Z-score normalization gave the best single-split performance (logistic regression: 98.33% accuracy; SVM: 96.33%). Under the stricter LOSO regime, random forest reached 89.02% accuracy with 44 features, while a correlation-pruned 17-feature subset matched or exceeded this across all classifiers—best with SVM (92.40%)—achieving an 85.8% dimensionality reduction from the original feature space (61% relative to the 44-feature set) with no loss in mean accuracy. Two deep-learning baselines (1D-CNN, BiLSTM) achieved comparable LOSO accuracy (91.39% and 87.72%), confirming the feature-based pipeline captures the signal’s discriminative structure without end-to-end deep architectures. These findings support an interpretable, compact, subject-independent framework for multi-task locomotor classification, though broader clinical validation is still needed.

Article.Title: Integrated markov state-space framework for reliability evaluation, failure analysis, and maintenance strategies for high-tension power transmission lines
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Kumar P.; Kumar P.; Kamila P.
Article.Abstract: Overhead transmission lines and high-tension wires represent the critical infrastructure of the world’s electrical power systems. These systems facilitate the bulk transfer of electrical power over vast distances. A significant percentage of the world’s existing power transmission infrastructure has reached an age where it has become increasingly vulnerable to environmental degradation, corrosion, mechanical stress, and thermal effects. These effects may cause critical component failure in power systems, resulting in economic losses. These components include the main transmission line, conductor strands, insulator discs, and insulator strings. The current paper proposes a sophisticated probabilistic mathematical model through Markov state-space modeling that allows for assessment of the efficiency, risk, reliability, and economic feasibility of transmission line systems. Moreover, the paper introduces economic break-even points that define the exact relationships in the form of linear inverse functions between the expected profit and the costs of maintenance in terms of repair, maintenance, and outage cost penalties in comparison with the basic revenues. Therefore, the current paper links the field of reliability engineering with that of economics in relation to the power grid system operation. The numerical results presented in this study are based on hypothetical parameters for demonstrative purposes. The model is analyzed using the regenerative point technique, assuming exponentially distributed failure and repair times, to derive various reliability measures.

Article.Title: Distinct estrogenic transcription programs of estetrol and 17β-estradiol across mammary, uterine, and vaginal cell types of pseudomenopausal mice
Article.Authors: Crevet L.; Dias Da Silva I.; Wuidar V.; Bouvencourt G.; Fioramonti M.; Destrebecq C.; Song Y.; Blacher S.; Foidart J.; Péqueux C.; Van Keymeulen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Menopause results from a marked decline in estrogen production and leads to symptoms that impair quality of life. Menopausal hormone therapy is effective in alleviating these symptoms; however, it is associated with an increased risk of estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Estetrol (E4), a natural fetal estrogen produced by the liver, has emerged as a promising alternative, relieving menopausal symptoms while remaining neutral on tumor growth in mouse models. To further assess its potential, we compared the transcriptional effects of E4 and estradiol (E2) in three estrogen-sensitive tissues: the mammary gland, uterus, and vagina. Ovariectomized adult mice, used to model menopause, were treated for two weeks with either a therapeutic dose of E4 (E4low), a tenfold higher supratherapeutic dose (E4hi), or E2. In mammary luminal cells, E2 induced a proliferative gene signature that was absent following E4 treatment. E4 did not elicit a distinct transcriptional profile, supporting the notion that it acts as a weaker estrogen in this tissue. In contrast, in the uterine and vaginal epithelium, E2, E4low, and E4hi similarly regulated most genes, and all treatments produced comparable morphological effects. However, in fibroblasts of the uterus and vagina, E2 induced a specific transcriptional signature that was not reproduced by E4. Additionally, comparison of gene signatures following E2 treatment across different organs revealed that, beyond proliferative genes, the sets of upregulated genes differed markedly between tissues, both in epithelial and fibroblast compartments, with the exception of a small inflammation-related gene set shared between uterine and vaginal fibroblasts. Overall, this study refines our understanding of estrogen downstream effects and highlights key differences between E2 and E4, supporting the idea that E4 may represent a safer alternative for menopausal hormone therapy in clinical settings.

Article.Title: The clinical and imaging comparisons between sellar extraventricular neurocytoma and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ran C.; Li W.; Liu L.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: We aimed to explore the clinical and imaging features of sellar extraventricular neurocytoma (EVN) through a comparison between sellar EVN and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma. 19 cases of EVN and 27 cases of nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma were retrospectively included, and their clinical and imaging findings were analyzed. Compared with sellar EVNs, nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas were more common with cystic changes (51.9% vs. 21.1%, P = 0.035), intratumoral hemorrhage (29.6% vs. 0, P = 0.027), and vesicle signs (33.3% vs. 0, P = 0.015). Compared with nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas, sellar EVNs were common with solid lesions (78.9% vs. 48.1%, P = 0.035), obvious MR enhancement (89.5% vs. 55.6%, P = 0.014), eccentric cavernous sinus involvement (84.2% vs. 44.4%, P = 0.007), and dural tail sign (68.4% vs. 22.2%, P = 0.002). Compared with nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma, sellar EVN was more common with subtotal resection (37.0% vs. 68.4%, P = 0.036) and postoperative radiotherapy (14.8% vs. 78.9%, P < 0.001). However, there was no significant difference in recurrence and progression-free survival between the two groups, although the gross total resection rate of nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas was higher (59.3% vs. 21.1%, P = 0.010). Solid lesions with obvious MR enhancement, dural tail sign, and eccentric cavernous sinus involvement could suggest sellar EVN in the condition of negative pituitary hormone. The clinical and imaging comparisons between sellar EVN and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma were helpful for clinical diagnosis and treatment.

Article.Title: A multidirectional extradural corridor for pretemporal endoscope-assisted orbitozygomatic–anterior petrosectomy
Article.Authors: Yuncu M.; Bilgin B.; Kartum T.; Karadag A.; Bozkurt B.; Tanriover N.
Article.Abstract: Surgical exposure of the ventral petroclival region remains technically challenging because of the complex three-dimensional relationships among the middle cranial fossa, petroclival junction, cavernous sinus, brainstem, and surrounding neurovascular structures. The orbitozygomatic (OZ) approach, anterior transpetrosal approach (ATPA), and pretemporal corridor are well-established approaches that provide complementary anatomical perspectives. This study aimed to define the continuous ventral petroclival corridor created by integrating extradural OZ–ATPA exposure with the intradural pretemporal corridor under endoscopic assistance. Five silicone-injected human cadaveric heads (10 sides) underwent standardized OZ craniotomy followed by extradural ATPA. The dissection was sequentially extended through a pretemporal intradural corridor and supplemented with 0° and 30° endoscopic inspection to evaluate anatomical continuity beyond the microscopic line of sight. Stepwise dissections were performed to characterize anatomical visualization during the sequential dissection along the ventral petroclival axis. Following anterior petrosectomy and dural opening, the ventrolateral brainstem between the dorsum sellae and the internal auditory canal (IAC) was visualized. Through the combined OZ–pretemporal trajectory, the optic tract, crural cistern, interpeduncular cistern, and mammillary bodies were identified from an inferior-to-superior perspective. Endoscopic inspection demonstrated deep and contralateral petroclival structures, including the contralateral abducens nerve and petrous apex, as well as inferior structures toward the cerebellopontine angle beyond the IAC. These findings document qualitative anatomical visualization; surgical freedom and the safety of instrument manipulation around the inferior and contralateral structures were not assessed. Stepwise integration of extradural OZ–ATPA exposure with the intradural pretemporal corridor and endoscopic inspection provides complementary anatomical views from the mammillary bodies to the cerebellopontine angle. This framework may support three-dimensional anatomical orientation and operative planning, but endoscopic visualization does not establish a safe working corridor to all visualized structures.

Article.Title: Advanced statistical modeling of loading waveform, frequency, temperature, and SBS modification effects on asphalt concrete resilient modulus
Article.Authors: Ghanizadeh A.; Safi Jahanshahi F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resilient modulus (Mr) is one the most important parameter for designing flexible pavements based on different damage criteria. The resilient modulus test measures the recoverable elastic strains of asphalt concrete under repeated loading, and therefore provides a stiffness-related parameter which is affected by temperature and loading conditions. The Mr of asphalt concretes is typically measured at specific temperatures and loading frequencies because of the high cost and time-consuming nature of testing; therefore, predictive models are necessary to predict the Mr at other temperatures and loading frequencies. The aim of this study is to present a framework for modeling and predicting the Mr of asphalt concretes by considering four parameters: loading waveform, loading frequency, temperature, and SBS modification. For this purpose, three advanced statistical techniques including Gene Expression Programming (GEP), Response Surface Methodology (RSM), and Hybrid Multivariate Adaptive Regression Spline-Pelican Optimization Algorithm (MARS-POA) have been employed. SBS, loading waveform, temperature, and loading frequency were used as the input parameters. The statistical comparison of developed models reveals that the MARS-POA method outperformed the others. The R 2 values for training and testing data were 0.9973 and 0.9732, respectively. Temperature has the greatest relative importance, while waveform has the least influence on Mr. In addition, master curves corresponding to waveform type and to SBS-modified or control mixture were calibrated in order to compare the results of MARS-POA model with those of master curves.

Article.Title: Research on fault diagnosis and control strategies for battery packs
Article.Authors: Ye Z.; Zhu Q.; Fu X.; He G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the rapid electrification of the automotive industry, the traction battery pack has become the most safety-critical subsystem of an electric vehicle, and any insulation or communication fault must be identified and managed reliably. This work proposes a fuzzy-theory-based diagnosis and control strategy for battery packs that detects and confirms unpredictable faults under diverse operating conditions. The method couples a fuzzy inference system (FIS) with a calibrated expert database: an adaptive fuzzy matching mechanism continuously adjusts the process and observation noise in the state-of-charge and terminal-voltage correction, while triangular membership functions, an IF–THEN rule base, Mamdani inference and centroid defuzzification convert the diagnostic signals into graded fault levels, with rule weights being refined after each confirmed event. Fault confirmation follows the debounce intervals and consecutive-cycle counts defined in the unified threshold tables, and the resulting fault levels activate power-limitation responses. Validation through simulation and vehicle experiments reveals that the judgment time for insulation faults lengthens by 4.6 s (from 3.0 s to 7.6 s), whereas the corresponding accuracy climbs from 81.1% to 92.3%; for communication faults, the accuracy rises from 91.4% to 97.7%, and the interval between fault confirmation and completed power limitation is 16.1 s in simulation, 8.2 s on the test bench, and 24 s under real-world driving. This modest rise in diagnostic time remains within design tolerances, while the achieved accuracy outperforms that of comparable studies and the protective actions taken after confirmation safeguard vehicle occupants and the overall system.

Article.Title: A drone-assisted deep learning framework for disaster assessment in real time and emergency response
Article.Authors: Aldhahri E.; Almazroi A.; Alkinani M.; Alghamdi E.; Janbi N.; Ayub N.; Al-Sulami Y.
Article.Abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. In catastrophes, traditional evaluation methods may not give accurate and timely information owing to enormous volumes of data and quick changes. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Adaptive Relevance Filtering and Contextual Scaling Transformation increase data dependability and feature relevance, enabling noisy or missing data learning. Testing regularly shows that ACTF-Net outperforms previous systems like BERT and CapsNet. F1-score is 0.981, area under curve is 0.993, and catastrophe severity prediction rate is 0.96. The model’s consistent performance across datasets of different sizes across time supports real-time applications. The proposed method uses multimodal drone data, powerful preprocessing, and novel metrics like the Contextual Sensitivity Index and Temporal Stability Score to reliably categorize and assess catastrophe severity using multiple labels. The results indicate that ACTF-Net may improve situational awareness, resource usage, and response time in high-risk crisis situations.

Article.Title: Assessment of therapeutic effect and residue depletion kinetics of oxytetracycline dihydrate in rainbow trout, Oncorhynchus mykiss (Walbaum, 1792)
Article.Authors: Kala K.; Pathak R.; Shahi N.; Patil P.; Chatterjee N.; Nadella R.; Patiyal R.; Pande V.; Mallik S.
Article.Abstract: Oxytetracycline (OTC) dihydrate, an approved broad-spectrum antibiotic, is widely used in aquaculture to combat bacterial infections like Aeromonas hydrophila in rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). However, its optimal dosing, residue depletion kinetics, and withdrawal times remain underexplored in exotic species under Indian conditions, raising food safety concerns due to maximum residue limits (MRL) of 100 µg kg − 1 in muscle. Survivability and histopathology (liver, kidney, muscle) were assessed post-treatment. Doses of 88.2–176.4 mg kg − 1 day − 1 boosted survivability to 64–74%, with marked histopathological improvements in liver, kidney, and muscle. Peak residues (C max ) reached 2120 µg kg − 1 in plasma and 6740 µg kg − 1 in intestine after day one. At the therapeutic dose of 80 mg kg − 1 day − 1 , muscle residues fell below 100 µg kg − 1 MRL after 35.89 days; notable levels included 78.0 µg kg − 1 (intestine, day 8), 80.1 µg kg − 1 (plasma, day 12), and 46.6 µg kg − 1 (kidney, day 20). The graded OTC concentrations tested (88.2, 132.3, and 176.4 mg kg − 1 day − 1 ) demonstrated a balance between therapeutic efficacy and safety. Among these, 88.2 mg kg − 1 day − 1 is suggested as the minimum effective therapeutic dose for rainbow trout under the present experimental conditions. Residue depletion analysis further indicated a muscle withdrawal period of 35.89 days following administration at 80 mg kg − 1 day − 1 . To our knowledge, this study provides the first data describing OTC dihydrate residue depletion in rainbow trout under Indian aquaculture conditions.

Article.Abstract: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service–National Sample Cohort database, we evaluated the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) exposure and the risk of Parkinson’s disease (PD) among adults aged ≥ 40 years with upper gastrointestinal disorders. This positive dose-response pattern remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including washout period assessments, although statistical precision varied by matching design. Therefore, these findings suggest a potential association between higher cumulative PPI exposure and an increased risk of PD.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Extreme sea levels (ESLs) threaten coastal zones, and global assessments suggest that future ESLs grow with rising mean sea level (MSL) as the main driver. Here, we test this additive assumption and show that it may under- or overestimate ESLs with consequences for coastal protection decisions. We fit stationary and non-stationary generalised extreme value (GEV) models to annual maxima of long hourly tide-gauge records. The non-stationary GEV location parameter may depend on MSL, time, or both. Bayesian model comparison and posterior coefficient support classify 200 of the 386 analysed series (52%) as non-stationary and 186 as stationary. At some stations, ESLs increase more than MSL; at others they increase less than MSL or even decrease. Post-fit grouping by seabed depth and slope also suggests stronger morphology-related differences in the fitted MSL coefficient among non-stationary series than among the stationary comparison series.

Article.Authors: Taşyürek M.; Mutlu O.; Kaygısız Ö.; Teke M.; Adıgüzel Ö.; Şevik U.
Article.Abstract: To develop and internally evaluate You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning models for automated classification of the anatomical relationship between the maxillary sinus floor and maxillary posterior tooth roots on panoramic radiographs, using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) as the reference standard. In this retrospective single-center study, 4,500 CBCT examinations acquired between 2023 and 2025 were screened. A total of 462 patients with paired panoramic radiographs and CBCT scans met the eligibility criteria, yielding 3,691 maxillary posterior tooth regions for analysis. Anatomical relationships were classified using CBCT as Type 1 (non-contact), Type 2 (cortical contact), or Type 3 (intrasinus penetration). The dataset was partitioned at the patient level into training ( n = 370), validation ( n = 46), and test ( n = 46) cohorts. Model stability was assessed using 10-fold cross-validation within the training cohort. Final performance was evaluated on the held-out test set using precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (mAP) at intersection over union (IoU) thresholds of 0.50 (mAP@0.5) and 0.50–0.95 (mAP@0.5:0.95), with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals (CIs). YOLO26 yielded the highest observed test-set performance, with a precision of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.91–0.97), recall of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.93–0.98), F1-score of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.92–0.97), mAP@0.5 of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.92–0.97), and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.71 (95% CI: 0.67–0.75). Corresponding mAP@0.5 values were 0.91 for YOLOv11 and 0.90 for YOLOv12. Type 2 relationships represented the most challenging category across models, particularly at the boundary between cortical contact and intrasinus penetration. Within this single-center retrospective dataset, YOLO26 showed the highest internal test performance among the evaluated models for predicting CBCT-derived maxillary sinus–posterior tooth relationship categories from panoramic radiographs. These findings represent internal validation only and do not establish generalizable clinical performance. CBCT remains the reference standard for three-dimensional assessment. External multicenter validation is required before this approach can be considered for clinical use.

Article.Title: Design and modelling of personalised multifunctional furniture based on smart networks and cloud rendering platforms
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Cao Q.; Xu M.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes an integrated design and modeling method for personalized multifunctional furniture based on intelligent networks and a cloud-rendering platform. A multisource requirement perception model is developed to transform users’ functional preferences, anthropometric dimensions, spatial constraints, aesthetic preferences, and budgets into structured design features. Parametric modeling, functional-module configuration, motion-constraint analysis, and cloud-based collaborative verification are then integrated to support the automatic generation and interactive modification of furniture schemes. A dynamic testing platform is established to evaluate the correspondence between physical furniture operations and cloud-rendered model states. The results show that the median dynamic errors of the m-sequence and OPRM schemes are approximately − 5.3% and − 5.5%, respectively. The OPRM error distribution ranges approximately from − 6.2% to − 4.8%, indicating greater adaptability to complex movements but higher variability. OPRM reduces the testing and model-calibration time from approximately 200 min to 50 min, corresponding to a reduction of about 75%. Its error fluctuations are mainly concentrated within the first one or two measurement cycles and subsequently converge toward a stable state. The proposed method consequently supports rapid personalized scheme generation, dynamic model correction, and reliable cloud-based visualization of multifunctional furniture.

Article.Title: Climate-related shifts in fire-weather regimes across heterogeneous mountain ecosystems: long-term spatiotemporal assessment in the Alborz mountains
Article.Authors: Roshan G.; Saman A.; Arbabi M.; Dogar M.; Ali T.
Article.Abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire-weather activity globally, yet the extent to which ecosystem structure modulates fire-weather regimes in complex mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate contrasting responses of forested and non-forested landscapes to climate-driven fire weather in the Alborz Mountains (1980–2025). Using high-resolution Fire Weather Index (FWI) data, combined with nonparametric trend analysis, structural breakpoint detection, spatial hotspot analysis, and a supplementary machine learning-based statistical extrapolation, we identify a pronounced divergence in fire-weather dynamics across land-cover types. Non-forested areas exhibit up to approximately threefold higher mean annual frequencies of high-FWI days compared with forested areas at the high fire-danger threshold (FWI ≥21.3), together with stronger historical increasing trends, whereas Hyrcanian forests exhibit comparatively muted responses. These differences are consistent with the combined influence of contrasting land-cover environments and the prevailing climatic and topographic gradients across the Alborz Mountains, with forested regions generally experiencing lower fire-weather exposure under their current environmental setting. Spatial analyses reveal persistent and intensifying hotspots concentrated in the western Alborz, alongside a marked west–east gradient in fire-weather evolution. Abrupt shifts detected during the mid-to-late 1990s, particularly around 1996 and 1999, indicate potential transitions in regional fire-weather regimes, although their relationships with large-scale climatic variability require further investigation. As a supplementary analysis, historical fire-weather patterns were statistically extrapolated to 2026–2035, indicating relatively higher frequencies in non-forested summer landscapes. These estimates represent statistical continuation of historical temporal patterns rather than climate projections or deterministic predictions of future wildfire occurrence. Overall, the results highlight pronounced spatial contrasts in climate-driven fire-weather conditions among different land-cover environments. These patterns reflect the combined influence of land-cover distribution, regional climatic gradients, and topographic setting rather than the independent effect of land cover alone.

Article.Title: Creep behavior of lightweight concrete containing fly ash ceramsite aggregate after exposure to high temperatures
Article.Authors: Xiao D.; Chen S.; Wen L.; Dou Y.; Liu H.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence of aggregate types on the long-term deformation performance of concrete after disasters, this paper takes normal-weight aggregate concrete (NWAC) and light weight aggregate concrete (LWAC) as the research objects, and conducts uniaxial step-wise compression creep tests after being subjected to high-temperature treatment ranging from 20 °C to 800 °C. The focus is on comparing and analyzing the effects of aggregate types on total strain, load-induced thermal strain (LITS), creep deformation, and rate patterns. The results show that below 200 °C, LWAC has a higher LITS than NWAC by approximately 83.3% due to its lower lightweight aggregate modulus; above 400 °C, NWAC experiences a rapid increase in creep strain due to the thermal expansion mismatch between the aggregate and the paste at the interface transition zone (ITZ). In contrast, the porous structure of the fly ash ceramic aggregate within LWAC plays a “thermal mitigating” effect, effectively inhibiting the propagation of microcracks. LWAC can maintain a longer steady-state creep period compared to NWAC. SEM confirmed that at high temperatures, the ITZ of NWAC developed tensile cracks of several micrometers, while LWAC maintained a relatively intact structure. Moreover, the fitting degree of the Burgers model for the creep data of LWAC was high ( R 2 = 0.99), verifying the applicability of this model in describing the deceleration and constant-speed creep behavior of LWAC after high-temperature treatment. The research results reveal the deformation mechanism of fly ash ceramic aggregate in the high-temperature environment, providing a theoretical basis for the design and post-disaster assessment of the fire resistance of LWAC structures.

Article.Authors: Chen W.; Fang H.; Zheng Y.; Yuan S.; Lin K.; Wu P.; Xie Y.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Using Shaolin Community in Quanzhou, China, as a case, this study examined artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) for early-stage design and evaluation of age-friendly public-space renovation. A 15-member specialist panel applied the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to determine weights. A separate 15-member evaluation panel, including six older resident representatives, then rated six scheme sets generated by Dreamina AI, MidJourney, and Stable Diffusion for five public-space nodes. Infrastructure Renovation received the highest criterion weight, while accessible facilities, cultural atmosphere, environmental sanitation, spatial accessibility, and quality of life ranked highly among the indicators. Within the case-specific workflows, the two Stable Diffusion scheme sets received the highest composite scores. Panel B ratings showed high concordance in scheme ordering (Kendall’s W = 0.931, p < 0.001), and the complete ranking remained unchanged across 64 one-at-a-time weight-perturbation scenarios (± 10% and ± 20%). However, the study covered one community, six scheme sets, limited resident participation, and platform-specific workflows, and no probabilistic uncertainty analysis was performed. The findings therefore should not be generalized beyond this setup. Article.Authors: Jandia A.; Plantureux C.; Lizarralde-Guerrero M.; Klein C.; Zadigue G.; Deroche L.; Autret G.; Maiuri M.; Kroemer G.; Perez-Lanzon M.; Pol J.

Ultrasound confirmed the presence of cystic hepatic lesions but was used as a qualitative structural assessment rather than a serial quantitative comparator. Day-specific receiver operating characteristic analyses showed that fluid/weight and fat mass/weight ratios increasingly discriminated iCCA-bearing from tumor-free mice as disease progressed. Exploratory within-animal analyses further showed that absolute body-composition ratios, particularly fluid/weight ratio, distinguished terminal clinical assessments from predefined earlier assessments. Daily relative changes in normalized parameters showed more variable performance and did not improve classification of terminal clinical status. Direct quantification of ascites and prospective validation in independent cohorts will be required before deriving generalizable diagnostic or humane-endpoint thresholds.

Article.Title: A machine-learning approach to high-throughput spatially resolved ARPES measurements
Article.Authors: Imamura M.; Koga D.; Takahashi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatially resolved angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is a powerful technique for mapping local electronic structures, but it requires long measurement times to achieve sufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at each spatial point. This constraint limits beamtime efficiency and exacerbates sample degradation. In samples with domain structures, however, similar spectra are repeatedly measured across spatial positions, creating substantial redundancy in spatially resolved ARPES datasets. Here we systematically evaluate how SNR degradation from reduced acquisition times affects unsupervised domain classification. PCA-based dimensionality reduction maintained high agreement with the high-SNR reference classification even under low-SNR conditions, whereas direct clustering of spectral vectors showed rapid degradation beginning at a relatively high-SNR regime. Because dimensionality reduction is applied solely for domain classification, the representative spectrum of each domain is obtained as a direct average of the measured data. These results demonstrate that combining short-acquisition measurements with intra-domain spectral averaging through the co-addition of spectra within each classified domain can substantially accelerate spatially resolved ARPES while preserving classification accuracy.

Article.Title: Rapid expansion and renormalization of parietal gray matter volume following associative learning
Article.Authors: Kleinschroth F.; Villa S.; Lenders A.; Brodt S.; Gais S.; Schönauer M.; Kumral D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The human brain exhibits rapid structural plasticity following learning, yet its temporal dynamics and behavioral relevance remain elusive, particularly for declarative forms of learning. In this study, we tested whether T1-weighted MRI captures rapid structural reorganization following associative memory formation and whether such changes follow an expansion–renormalization trajectory. We observed GMV increases in parietal, lateral occipital, and cerebellar regions at 2 h post-learning ( n = 139), which were no longer detectable relative to baseline at 12 h ( n = 96), consistent with rapid renormalization. Critically, GMV changes in left parietal cortex were further linked to how well participants retained the memory, such that greater maintenance of GMV was associated with better retention ( n = 37). By contrast, in a distinct right parietal region ( n = 32; 17 sleep, 15 wake), GMV increased in the sleep group in the control but not in the learning condition, whereas GMV change did not differ between conditions in the wake group. This sleep-related effect was unrelated to memory retention. Our findings suggest that human gray matter undergoes hour-scale changes, with potentially dissociable memory- and sleep-related components.

Article.Title: Ultra-early tirofiban after failed tenecteplase in branch atheromatous disease: efficacy and safety
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhu L.; Zhang Y.; Yang Y.; Zhang S.; Liu L.; Gao X.; Chen W.; Song L.; Fu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Branch atheromatous disease (BAD), a common acute ischemic stroke subtype with high progression and recurrence risk, often shows limited improvement following intravenous thrombolysis. Article.Title: Automatic unloading control system for corn field residual film baling device based on a load cell
Article.Authors: Jin W.; Liu J.; Jiang T.; Zhang X.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: Residual film in corn fields is readily entangled with corn stubble, yielding variable impurity content in the film bales recovered across different harvest periods. This inconsistency leads to uneven mass among film bales of the same size, makes the unloading timing difficult to determine, and may ultimately cause overload damage to the baling device. To address this issue, an automatic unloading control system for a corn-field residual-film baling device is developed based on an HZC-H1 load cell. By monitoring film-bale mass, the system determines the unloading timing, alerts the driver to stop the machine, and executes automatic unloading. Mechanical analysis is first carried out to calculate the elastic deformation of the baling belt and thus determine the sensor mounting position, ensuring that the baling belt fully contacts the load-cell sensing surface and that the film-bale weight is transmitted to the sensor in a timely and accurate manner. A Wheatstone full-bridge circuit is then used to convert the applied external force into a voltage signal, and a CYBSQ-12 multi-channel signal amplifier converts the weak electrical signal output by the load cell into an analog signal recognizable by the main controller. Finally, with this analog signal as the control input, an Arduino UNO R3 acts as the main controller to achieve precise start–stop control of the electric push rod, thereby realizing automatic film-bale unloading and driver alerting. Field tests indicate that the relative error between the measured film-bale mass and the preset value is no greater than 4%, demonstrating that the proposed system meets the operational accuracy requirements. This work provides both theoretical support and a practical reference for the intelligent upgrading of residual-film recycling equipment and the standardization of recovered film bales.

Article.Authors: Helal Z.; Elshaer S.; El-Mowafy M.; Habib E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. These combinations were divided into three groups: standard, co-isolated (from the same patient), and random combinations. The effect of these interactions on pathogenicity was also evaluated using a mouse model. Co-culture significantly enhanced S. aureus survival following exposure to azithromycin (100%), gentamicin (91.7%), cefepime (91.7%) and ciprofloxacin (58.3%). Likewise, biofilm formation and clot lysis activity were significantly enhanced in 83% and 67% mixtures, respectively. Gene expression analysis revealed significant upregulation of icaD and sspA in 100% and 89% of the tested combinations, respectively, compared with mono-culture. Overall, the results demonstrate an interspecies interaction between the two pathogens which increased antimicrobial tolerance and virulence in S. aureus . Consistent with these findings, co-infected mice exhibited higher mortality rates and elevated bacterial counts in lung and liver tissues. Taken together, these findings highlight the effect of polymicrobial interactions in evaluating bacterial pathogenicity and resistance to antimicrobial agents.

The interaction between the time-dependent structure of fibrous flow and electric wind velocity spatial distribution strongly affects the initial stages of fibrous flow development and propagation as well as the overall process efficiency. It is suggested that known AFES processes may utilize only a fraction of available electric wind energy. Future studies are needed on fibrous flow structure analysis and electric wind - fibrous flow interaction in AFES depending on the AC spinneret design and process parameters to advance the AC electric field-enabled electrospinning instrumentation and technology.

Article.Authors: Mehta R.; Sadia F.; Reddy S.; Vancurova I.; Vancura A.

Efficient termination is required for maintaining a pool of RNAPII that is available for re-entry into new transcription cycle. RNAPII transcription termination of most mRNAs and non-coding RNAs in S. cerevisiae occurs via polyadenylation-dependent and Nrd1p-Nab3p-Sen1p (NNS)-dependent pathways, respectively. Previous results showed that checkpoint kinase Mec1p in the absence of exogenous genotoxic stress promotes transcription termination by the polyadenylation-dependent pathway by facilitating recruitment of termination factor Pcf11p and torpedo exonuclease Rat1p to 3’ ends of genes. Mec1p inactivation causes transcription read-through of snoRNAs, downregulates the efficiency of NNS-mediated transcription termination, and enhances growth defect in cells with compromised NNS complex. Mec1p also promotes the NNS-mediated transcription attenuation. However, Mec1p is not required for phosphorylation of the carboxy-terminal domain of the largest RNAPII subunit Rpb1p at Ser5 and for recruitment of Nrd1p to 5’ ends of genes. Together, our data reveal a new role for checkpoint kinase Mec1p in NNS-mediated transcription termination and suggest that during S phase, Mec1p enforces efficient transcription termination of both mRNAs and non-coding RNAs, perhaps to limit transcription-replication conflicts.

Article.Authors: Hadierbieke A.; Buerlike A.; Xia H.

The middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model was established in C57BL/6 mice, and an in vitro model was generated using oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). The dynamic expression of ACSS2 mRNA and protein was assessed by RT-qPCR and Western blot, respectively. Pharmacological suppression of ACSS2 activity by AD-8007, or blockade of Ser659 phosphorylation by Compound C, obviously restrained I/R-triggered autophagy, accompanied by impaired LC3-II conversion and inhibited p62 degradation. This suppression further aggravated neuronal apoptosis and enlarged cerebral infarct volume. Consistent with in vivo findings, in vitro neuronal OGD/R challenge rapidly elevated ACSS2 Ser659 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and enhanced nuclear acetyl-CoA production, which subsequently increased H3K27 acetylation at the LC3B promoter. Functional validation demonstrated that ACSS2-WT effectively activated autophagy and alleviated neuronal apoptosis under OGD/R, while the ACSS2-Mut lost such protective capacity. Moreover, Compound C administration abolished OGD/R-elicited ACSS2 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, thereby repressing autophagic activation and worsening neuronal damage. ACSS2 confers neuroprotection against cerebral ischemia via Ser659 phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear translocation, which further activates autophagy-related gene expression. In contrast, blockade of ACSS2 activity or its phosphorylation compromises protective autophagy and exacerbates ischemic brain damage. Article.Title: Tourism urbanization and landscape fragmentation in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain: an integrated analysis of intensity and landscape metrics
Article.Authors: Chiu H.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Tourism urbanization prioritizes tourism consumption over traditional residential-focused development, reshaping land use patterns in destination areas. Hotel land expanded from 0.8 to 5.9 km 2 between 1995 and 2020, with the highest interval change rate (177%) occurring in 1995–2006, partly reflecting growth from a very small base. Intensity analysis identified accelerated change during 1995–2006 and 2015–2020, while hotels showed the highest gain intensity in every interval despite their small area. Landscape fragmentation intensified, with patch density increasing 57% while the aggregation index declined 9%, indicating a less clustered landscape. Moving-window and transect analyses revealed spatial heterogeneity in this change, with the landscape becoming more aggregated around urban peripheries but more fragmented across the outer plain. Article.Authors: Prasanna R.; Kiran T.; Vijaya P.; Chandrika G.; Bolisetty V.; Sreenivasulu V.; Kondavitee G.; Karumuri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, we have designed and analysed the dual cavity AlGaN/GaN Metal oxide semiconductor high electron mobility transistor (MOS-HEMT) heterojunction biosensor for biomolecule detection. The proposed biosensor uses triple-metal work functions (M 1 , M 2 and M 3 ) to improve electric field distribution and electrostatic control. The proposed biosensor is evaluated using MCF-10 A (K = 4.5), Keratin(K = 8), Gelatin (K = 12), Hs578T (K = 22), MCF-7 (K = 27.5) and T47D (K = 32) biomolecules using Atlas Silvaco TCAD. The temperature dependent behaviour is examined at different temperatures (250 K, 300 K, 350 K and 400 K) to evaluate its electrical stability and sensing performance. In addition, Self-Heating Effect (SHE) is analysed using Sapphire and Diamonds substrate configurations. Self-heating increases the lattice temperature, leading to enhanced carrier scattering and reduced 2DEG mobility that can affect the electrical and sensing performance. A Diamond substrate AlN/Diamond substrate is used to improve heat dissipation and supress self-heating. The proposed device analyses the lattice temperature, DIBL, drain-current sensitivity and subthreshold swing (SS) sensitivity for different biomolecule effective dielectric constant. The Diamond substrate reduces the lattice temperature from 422 K to 324 K and increases the drain current sensitivity from 5.392 × 10 1 to 9.99 × 10 1 at K = 32. These results demonstrated that the proposed AlN/Diamond substrate device provides improved thermal management and sensing performance, making it suitable for biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Serum relaxin and beta hCG levels in pregnant women with prior recurrent pregnancy loss and composite adverse pregnancy outcomes
Article.Authors: Eleje G.; Ugwu E.; Onah C.; Igbodike E.; Malachy D.; Nwankwo E.; Ugboaja J.; Ikechebelu J.; Onwuegbuna A.; Egbuniwe M.; Edokwe E.; Egwim U.; Umeononihu O.; Ekwuazi K.; Ogelle O.; Okafor C.; Nweze S.; Ezenwaeze M.; Odugu B.; Ortuanya K.; Onah N.; Ezeora N.; Ofojebe C.; Ezeigwe C.; Enechukwu C.
Article.Abstract: To analyse maternal serum relaxin and β-hCG in pregnant women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and compare them with a healthy control group without a history RPL. A prospective cohort study was conducted among pregnant women with prior RPL ( n = 47) and healthy controls ( n = 94). Serum relaxin and β-hCG concentrations were measured between 8 and 20 weeks of gestation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated across the entire study population followed up till birth ( n = 136, combining RPL and control groups) to evaluate the predictive performance of relaxin and beta-hCG for composite adverse pregnancy outcomes. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to adjust for potential confounding variables. Mean levels of relaxin and β-hCG were significantly lower in the RPL group (95.28 ± 24.90pg/mL and 425.24 ± 147.57mIU/mL) than in controls (111.61 ± 41.43pg/mL and 542.26 ± 97.97mIU/mL, respectively; p < 0.001). Across all participants, a serum relaxin cutoff < 109.14pg/Ml was a statistically significant predictor of composite adverse pregnancy outcomes (AUC = 0.63; sensitivity = 72.00%; specificity = 55.00%; p = 0.01). Conversely, β-hCG < 540.48mIU/mL was not predictive (AUC = 0.55; sensitivity = 59.00%; specificity = 58.00%; p = 0.30). In multivariable logistic regression, repeat miscarriage (aOR = 31.01, p < 0.01) and caesarean birth (aOR = 3.92, p = 0.01) remained significantly associated with prior RPL after adjusting for maternal age, BMI, gestational age at sampling, and socioeconomic status. Although maternal serum relaxin levels are significantly lower in women with prior RPL, their predictive performance across the general cohort is modest (AUC = 0.63). Relaxin represents a potential candidate biomarker that warrants validation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.

Article.Title: System dynamics evidence of sub-additive carbon reduction from combined mitigation strategies in multi-echelon logistics networks
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Li L.; Pang Y.; Gu G.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: The transition of multi-echelon logistics networks toward carbon neutrality is constrained by the inability of traditional static models to capture complex emission dynamics and time-delayed effects. To bridge this critical gap, this study develops a comprehensive system dynamics framework that captures non-linear feedback mechanisms, nonlinear interactions and temporal delays across transportation, inventory, and ware-housing operations. By simulating multiple mitigation strategies on a stylized regional distribution network, the analysis reveals strongly asymmetric temporal patterns: annual emissions in the base scenario rise from 2,736 to 3,453 t CO 2 e over five years, an increase of 26.2%. Transportation mode optimization delivers a 21.3% reduction with a 9.8% saving in five-year total cost, network reconfiguration a 22.4% reduction with a 6.5% saving, and technology upgrading a 25.9% reduction at an 8.4% cost increase. Combining all three yields a 47.5% reduction while lowering cumulative expenditure by 9.8%, so the deepest reduction is obtained together with a net cost saving rather than in exchange for one. The combined effect is markedly sub-additive, since the three single strategies sum to 69.6% points against a simulated 47.5. The emission response to modal shift is near-linear in the shifted volume over the range a programme can plausibly reach, and a shift of 57.6% of road line-haul tonne-kilometres is required merely to hold year-five emissions at the base-year level. Theoretically, these findings challenge prevailing static optimization paradigms by reframing logistics networks as complex adaptive systems. Practically, the study provides a transparent and reproducible simulation framework with which logistics managers can examine the sequencing and interaction of decarbonization measures before committing capital.

Article.Title: Quantifying external root resorption associated with various orthodontic tooth movements in clear aligner treatment: a retrospective clinical study
Article.Authors: Kurnaz S.; Buyukcavus M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated associations between tooth movements and external root resorption (ERR) during clear aligner (CA) orthodontic treatment (OT). Forty-eight patients who underwent non-extraction OT using ClearCorrect aligners were included. Maxillary and mandibular incisors and canines were assessed, comprising 576 teeth. Pre- and post-OT digital models were superimposed to quantify intrusion, extrusion, crown tipping, crown torque, rotation, buccolingual translation, and mesiodistal translation. Root length, projected root surface area (PRSA), and ERR were measured on pre- and post-OT panoramic radiographs. Associations between tooth movements and root length, PRSA, and ERR were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses, with correction for multiple comparisons where appropriate. Significant movement-specific associations were observed in the maxillary lateral incisors and canines, with crown torque associated with root length and ERR changes and crown tipping associated with ERR in the lateral incisors, while extrusion was associated with PRSA changes in the canines. No significant movement–resorption associations were observed in the mandibular teeth. The magnitude of the observed resorptive changes was generally limited. Overall, the findings suggest that root responses during CA treatment may vary according to both the type of tooth movement and tooth group; however, the observed movement-specific associations should be interpreted cautiously.

Article.Title: A reconfigurable architecture for CNN acceleration using line buffers
Article.Authors: Sarnala B.; Pillutla S.
Article.Abstract: Computer vision (CV) is experiencing a rapid increase in real-time applications driven by neural network (NN) processing. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are the core architecture of advanced CV applications based on artificial intelligence (AI) for autonomous driving, facial recognition, object detection, and information decryption. However, huge computational complexity and continuous memory bandwidth requirements restrict the efficient hardware implementation of CNNs on FPGA platforms. In this paper proposes a reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture using line buffers for enhancing the resource utilization and reducing delay. The proposed architecture dynamically reconfigured to CNN layer requirements, and line buffers improve the data reuse and reduce redundant memory access. In addition, reconfigurable adder and pooling structures are designed to increase the flexibility of accumulation and down sampling operations, supporting various kernel sizes and layers in CNNs. The proposed reconfigurable architecture is hardware-efficient through control signals and adapts to all CNN layers. FPGA implementation of this proposed reconfigurable architecture is performed using LeNet CNN architecture layers. This flexible and low-cost reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture achieves a 15.25% reduction in LUTs utilization, 75% improvement in throughput, and 2.44% reduction in computational delay in LeNet CNN. The implemented LeNet CNN using proposed reconfigurable architecture is suitable for high performance and hardware efficient CNN applications.

Article.Title: Robust federated learning for detecting false data injection attacks in advanced metering infrastructure under non-IID data
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Gong G.; Cao L.
Article.Abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure exposes fine-grained residential consumption to false data injection attacks that tamper with meter readings while evading conventional bad-data screening. Federated learning keeps raw measurements on the device, yet real smart-meter populations are naturally non-independent and identically distributed and the distributed training loop is open to malicious clients that poison model updates. This study proposes a dual-robust federated detection framework that couples a lightweight two-branch gated recurrent detector with a server-side aggregation pipeline built from exponential moving average smoothing, client-level trimmed filtering, and deviation-aware cosine weighting. Real non-IID scenarios are constructed from the public Low Carbon London dataset by ACORN group, and generalization is checked on the Spanish GoiEner dataset across a different region and period. Under a strict fixed false-positive operating point the framework holds balanced accuracy near 61% from zero to thirty% malicious clients, whereas standard federated baselines collapse toward chance, confirming the value of client-level robust aggregation for edge-deployable attack detection.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: advanced metering infrastructure; false data injection attacks; non-IID data; federated learning; gated recurrent neural networks; malicious client detection

Article.Title: Optimized deep learning based digital twin architecture for system management in heterogeneous IoT system
Article.Authors: Jebasingh G.; Amsaprabhaa M.
Article.Abstract: The rapid explosion of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has introduced significant challenges in network traffic, device reliability, energy efficiency and Quality of Service (QoS) management due to the diversity of devices, communication protocols and application requirements. The existing methods of network management methods are gateway-centric and rule-based approaches that lacks in the intelligence for dynamic and large-scale environments. To address the challenges, this research introduced Digital Twin (DT) based intelligent gateway system for heterogeneous IoT networks, which is the synchronized virtual replica of the physical IoT environment for continuous maintained and analysis of networks. In the proposed DT framework, deep learning–based decision-making based on Cross-Stage Gated Transformer Network (CSG-TNet) is proposed to enable proactive system management. Here, the loss function associated with the CSG-TNet is supplemented by using the proposed Chaotic Blood sucking Leach Optimizer (CBSL) algorithm. The DT model aggregates and harmonizes heterogeneous IoT data related to network traffic, device health, energy consumption and service performance that allows the CSG-TNet to learn complex spatio-temporal correlations across multiple system dimensions. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed DT–enabled gateway significantly improves network efficiency, reliability and service quality for next-generation heterogeneous IoT systems.

Article.Title: A hybrid ANN-metaheuristic framework for vibration-based identification of orthotropic parameters in GFRP laminated plates
Article.Authors: Adimass S.; Żak A.; Doliński Ł.
Article.Abstract: Glass-fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composite plates are widely used in engineering structures, yet their numerical modelling is challenging because their material properties can vary due to anisotropy, manufacturing variability, and uncertainty in input parameters. This study develops a fast numerical framework for vibration-based finite element model updating and inverse identification of orthotropic material properties in GFRP composite plates using analytical modal reference data. A baseline finite element model was developed in Abaqus and compared with modal results obtained using Classical laminate plate theory. To reduce the high computational cost of repeated finite element simulations during model updating, an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate model was trained on parametric FE data and coupled with genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimisation (PSO), and slime mould algorithm (SMA) optimisation methods. The novelty of the study lies in comparing these ANN-assisted optimisation frameworks with direct GA-Abaqus-Python updating under the same modal identification problems. Pearson correlation-based sensitivity analysis showed that the longitudinal elastic modulus E x was the dominant parameter affecting the modal response, with sensitivity values ranging from approximately 0.62 to 0.80. In the representative updated model, ANN-SMA achieved the lowest average frequency-prediction error of 2.289%, compared with 3.821% for the conventional GA-Abaqus-Python updated model. However, statistical analysis over 50 independent runs showed that ANN-PSO provided the best robustness, with the lowest mean frequency error, smallest standard deviation, and lower runtime than ANN-SMA. The ANN-assisted methods reduced the computational time from approximately 5.830 h to 6.617–42.409 s. These results show that ANN-assisted model updating provides an efficient numerical approach for vibration-based material-property identification in composite structures.

Article.Title: Phytochemical-based quality control of cayenne pepper using spectroscopic monitoring of lycopene content and antioxidant capacity
Article.Authors: Putri I.; Kusumiyati K.; Hadiwijaya Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quality control in cayenne pepper fruit is important for maintaining product consistency. The research aimed to evaluate lycopene content and antioxidant capacity as the main indicators of cayenne pepper quality. Visible-near infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy is an emerging technology that can predict lycopene content and antioxidant capacity non-destructively, accurately, and quickly. Spectral data (381–1065 nm) were analyzed using support vector machine regression to develop the calibration model. Reference data on lycopene and antioxidant capacity were determined using spectrophotometry method. The results displayed a robust association between spectra and reference data. The calibration model for lycopene content and antioxidant capacity generated sufficient performance in terms of accuracy. For both parameters, the models showed correlation coefficient ( R ) ≥ 0.85, root mean square error of calibration (RMSEC) ≥ 17.61, root mean square error of cross validation (RMSECV) ≥ 42.01, and ratio of prediction to deviation (RPD) ≥ 1.95. Based on these results, it further strengthens that Vis-NIR technology was able to non-destructively assess lycopene content and antioxidant capacity. In the food and postharvest industries, the developed method shows promise for fast quality screening, automated grading, and real-time monitoring. Additionally, Vis-NIR spectroscopy’s rapidity and non-destructive nature make it scalable for industrial uses, especially in precision agriculture and contemporary quality control systems. These findings support the potential of non-destructive technology as an alternative for the quality control system of cayenne pepper quality in the agricultural and food industries.

Article.Title: Differences in self-stigma and help-seeking among individuals reporting a history of childhood maltreatment: a multi-country study
Article.Authors: Haim-Nachum S.; Pfaltz M.; Jansson B.; Fisch C.; Ayas G.; Şar V.; Lazarov A.; Balle S.; Jenkins D.; Sela Y.; Ahmed F.; Seedat S.; Schnyder U.; Oe M.; Amsalem D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Self-stigma is a significant barrier to help-seeking among survivors of childhood maltreatment (CM). Although context, including cultural context, shapes the way stigma-related beliefs are experienced and translated into help-seeking intentions, most evidence derives from Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) countries/cultures. This multi-national study examined cross-national differences in self-stigma dimensions and help-seeking intentions among CM survivors spanning both WEIRD (United States, Sweden, Switzerland) and non-WEIRD (Japan, South Africa, Türkiye) countries. Young adults with a retrospectively self-reported history of CM ( N = 2,691) completed online self-report measures assessing self-stigma dimensions (alienation, stereotype endorsement, secrecy, and perceived recovery) and help-seeking intentions. Group (WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD) differences were examined using ANCOVAs controlling for age, gender, education, subjective social status, and extent of CM exposure. Pearson correlations assessed associations among stigma-related constructs and help-seeking intentions at both group (regional; WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD) and country levels. Participants from non-WEIRD countries reported lower alienation alongside higher secrecy, perceived recovery, and help-seeking intentions compared to participants from WEIRD countries. Stereotype endorsement did not differ between groups. Correlational patterns among stigma-related constructs were broadly similar across contexts, but associations were descriptively stronger and more interlinked in WEIRD countries. Country-level analyses revealed substantial mean-level variation across countries. Self-stigma-related patterns among CM survivors varied descriptively across countries, with differing configurations of stigma-related dimensions observed across contexts. These findings underscore the importance of moving beyond WEIRD-centric models and support culturally sensitive approaches to stigma reduction and help-seeking promotion.

Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomics-based analysis of cellular heterogeneity in aggrephagy in gastric cancer and development of a prognostic model
Article.Authors: Wan T.; Yang P.; Xu Y.; Shu P.
Article.Abstract: Aggrephagy maintains protein homeostasis through selective autophagy, but its cellular heterogeneity and immune associations in gastric cancer (GC) remain unclear. We integrated GC single-cell RNA sequencing data with TCGA and GEO transcriptomic cohorts to identify aggrephagy-associated genes and develop a prognostic signature. Analyses included immune infiltration, somatic mutations, predicted drug sensitivity, pseudotime trajectories, and virtual gene knockout. Expression of VIM, TUBA1A, and CST3 was examined using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in GC cell lines and Human Protein Atlas immunohistochemical data. Aggrephagy-associated AUCell score distributions varied across the seven major cell types, with overlaps. The VIM–TUBA1A–CST3 signature showed moderate prognostic discrimination in public transcriptomic cohorts and was associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment features, immune checkpoint expression, and predicted drug sensitivity. Virtual VIM knockout predicted network perturbations involving macrophage antigen-presentation and lysosomal pathways, suggesting potential links to the GC immune microenvironment rather than established causal regulation. These findings characterize aggrephagy-associated cellular heterogeneity and provide a basis for further investigation of prognostic stratification and immune-associated mechanisms in GC.

Article.Title: A novel ISSA-GRNN approach for efficient camphor extraction from Artemisia argyi
Article.Authors: Ji P.; Wang D.; Li R.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient extraction of bioactive compounds from plant matrices is essential for pharmaceutical, functional food, and agricultural applications. However, process optimization is often challenged by nonlinear interactions among multiple parameters and limited experimental data. This work presents an optimization framework that combines an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) with a generalized regression neural network (GRNN) to model camphor extraction from Artemisia argyi leaves. The ISSA incorporates three modifications: hybrid chaotic-opposition population initialization, a dual-adaptive discoverer update rule, and a stagnation-triggered hybrid mutation operator. The GRNN leverages its small-sample tolerance to establish a nonlinear relationship between five extraction parameters and camphor yield using 50 experimental runs. Under 5-fold cross-validation, ISSA-GRNN outperformed PSO, GA, and SSA-optimized GRNN models, achieving an R² of 0.931, RMSE of 0.0140, and MAPE of 4.65%. Experimental validation under optimized conditions (58 °C, 0.7% cellulase, 3.8 h hydrolysis, pH 6.0, 32 min ultrasonication) produced a camphor yield of 0.2368 mg/g, an 11.5% increase over RSM, with an RSD of 1.05% (3.74% for RSM). The findings of this study contribute to a better understanding of small-sample nonlinear process modeling and provide a practical framework for bioactive compound extraction under data-scarce conditions, readily extendable to other plant matrices and data-limited regression problems.

Article.Title: The prediction model of social alienation trajectory in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients based on social ecosystem theory: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Huang L.; Zang J.; Chen Z.; Li J.; Ren Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social alienation can adversely affect the psychological well-being, social functioning, and longer-term adjustment of adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). However, longitudinal patterns of social alienation after diagnosis and prediction frameworks integrating multilevel factors remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to identify distinct social alienation trajectories during the first year after AIS diagnosis and to develop a prediction model for trajectory-group membership. In this single-centre prospective cohort study, 276 patients with AIS completed assessments at diagnosis and at 3, 6, and 12 months. Growth mixture modelling (GMM) was used to identify social alienation trajectories. Trajectory classes were subsequently grouped to define a binary outcome for prediction modelling. Candidate predictors underwent univariable screening followed by forward likelihood-ratio logistic regression. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with the selected predictor set held fixed and the regression coefficients re-estimated in each resample. Three trajectories were identified: lower-score increasing ( n = 144), moderate-score increasing ( n = 91), and persistently higher-score ( n = 41). The latter two classes were combined as the elevated-score trajectory group ( n = 132), with the lower-score increasing class as the reference. The final model retained seven predictors: age > 12 years (OR = 6.461; 95% CI, 2.019–20.678), presence of comorbid health conditions (OR = 8.535; 95% CI, 1.803–40.394), positive self-esteem (OR = 0.876; 95% CI, 0.771–0.995), negative self-esteem (OR = 1.243; 95% CI, 1.117–1.383), intra-family support (OR = 0.829; 95% CI, 0.747–0.920), extra-family support (OR = 0.891; 95% CI, 0.826–0.962), and economic discrimination (OR = 2.003; 95% CI, 1.420–2.824). The apparent AUC was 0.913 (95% CI, 0.878–0.948). Fixed-predictor-set bootstrap correction yielded an AUC of 0.902, a Brier score of 0.124, a calibration intercept of − 0.004, and a calibration slope of 0.907. Participants with AIS followed heterogeneous social alienation trajectories during the first year after diagnosis. The model with seven predictors showed promising performance after bootstrap correction and may inform further research on psychosocial risk assessment. However, predictor selection was not repeated during bootstrap validation, and independent external validation is required before routine clinical use.

Article.Title: Nonlinear distortion compensation for high-speed ADC using a diffusion model
Article.Authors: Yan H.; Qian X.
Article.Abstract: To address the amplitude/phase distortion and intermodulation distortion caused by nonlinearity of the sampling switch and front-end amplifier, clock jitter, and frequency coupling in high-speed ADCs (Analog to Digital Converters), this paper proposes a conditional Diffusion framework based on physical constraints for nonlinear distortion compensation in high-speed ADCs. The study uses a one-dimensional time series Temporal-UNet as the denoising backbone and fuses the calibrated hardware parameter vector with jitter spectrum estimation through a conditional encoder. FiLM is used to inject conditional information into the residual block to guide progressive inverse diffusion. Then, in each step of the inverse process, a data consistency projection based on a memory polynomial physical forward model is embedded. The Gauss-Newton approximation solution is used, combined with STFT (Short Time Fourier Transform)-L1 and spectral convergence term to constrain the network output to suppress intermodulation and phase distortion. Finally, in the deployment link, low-latency engineering implementation is achieved through methods such as few-step deterministic sampling, progressive distillation, model pruning, and quantization. Parallel multi-sample uncertainty estimation and lightweight online fine-tuning ensure domain adaptability and reliability. A comprehensive evaluation based on a hybrid simulation and experimental dataset — comprising single-tone sweep, two-tone intermodulation, multi-tone, and modulation signal scenarios over an input frequency range of 10 MHz to 450 MHz and a normalized input amplitude range of 0.1 to 1.0 full scale, with an uncompensated baseline ENOB of 4.37 bits at full-scale high-frequency input — shows that the proposed method achieves suppression of THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) and IMD (Intermodulation Distortion) of approximately 73.04% and 78.15% respectively in the high-frequency band above 300 MHz. The ENOB (Effective Number of Bits) increased by 3.21 ± 0.16 bits, the SNDR (Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio) increased by 11.07 ± 0.76 dB, and the SFDR (Spurious Free Dynamic Range) increased by 9.57 ± 0.99 dB. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can achieve high-fidelity signal reconstruction in different frequency bands and under complex operating conditions, providing a reliable technical solution for accurate measurement and communication link optimization in high-speed ADC systems.

Article.Title: Oxidative stress contributes to persistent pain and central sensitization in a repeated PGE2-induced hyperalgesic priming model
Article.Authors: Arai Y.; Koyama Y.; Kobayashi Y.; Takahashi A.; Kobayashi H.; Yoshida T.; Shimada S.
Article.Abstract: Chronic pain is a global health concern that impairs physical and psychological well-being. Recently, nociplastic pain, characterized by the absence of overt inflammation or nerve injury, has gained attention as a distinct chronic pain condition. Central sensitization is considered a primary mechanism underlying nociplastic pain and the persistence of chronic pain states. Emerging evidence suggests that oxidative stress contributes to central sensitization, through increased neuronal excitability and glial activation; however, its role in nociplastic pain remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the involvement of oxidative stress in a prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)-induced hyperalgesic priming mouse model with features resembling nociplastic pain. Additionally, we examined the effects of modulating oxidative stress on pain progression using a silicon (Si)-based antioxidant agent. Repeated PGE2 administration induced mechanical allodynia and increased circulating reactive oxygen metabolites (d-ROMs), effects that were attenuated in mice treated with the Si-based agent. In the spinal dorsal horn, neuronal activity and astrocyte activation increased in the chronic pain model but not in mice treated with the Si-based agent. These findings support an association between systemic oxidative stress and spinal sensitization in this repeated PGE2-induced hyperalgesic priming model and provide insight into mechanisms underlying persistent pain that may share features with nociplastic pain.
