Article.Title: Harmonizing national drug lists: an eight-pattern ATC/DDD analysis
Article.Authors: Rajabi M.; Mahmoudi Meymand M.; Vesali Sharif M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background The Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification and Defined Daily Dose (DDD) system of the World Health Organization are recognized internationally as the platinum standard in research methodology related to drug use. Our focus is on drugs with multiple ATC codes and those with discrepancies in Administration Routes (Adm.R) and DDDs. A list of these medications was created to alert drug agencies about the critical need for auditing and verifying the accuracy of their national list harmonizations. Methods An 8-Pattern Classification Framework has been accordingly developed from the World Health Organization (WHO) primary data by combining ATC code, DDD values, and Adm.R, in order to classify 913 pair drugs that belong to multiple classifications. Results our analysis shed light that between 2714 medication in WHO/DDD classification that have DDD, 913 pairs have satisfied one of the 8-conditions. that 1 molecule in condition 1 that have similar ATC, DDD and Adm.R to 402 medications in class 2 that have similar ATC, similar DDD and different Adm.R. Conclusion It is very important to correctly classify multi-classified drugs towards just drug procurement and use reporting. We introduce the 8-Pattern Approach to make national list discrepancies conform to the global classifications defined for proper reporting of drug use.

Article.Title: HGCN-GRU: temporal memory learning for hypergraph sequential recommendation
Article.Authors: Saghafi F.; Mirzaei S.
Article.Abstract: Sequential recommendation systems aim to predict users’ future interactions by modeling the temporal evolution of their preferences. Hypergraph-based representations are particularly well suited to this setting because they can capture high-order, non-pairwise dependencies among multiple users and items within a unified relational structure, enabling the modeling of complex collaborative patterns beyond conventional pairwise interactions. Despite this advantage, existing hypergraph-based sequential recommenders often rely on shallow temporal propagation, such as residual gating or single-step hypergraph convolution across adjacent snapshots, which limits their ability to preserve long-range semantic dependencies across distant time periods. Moreover, when trained solely with supervised signals, these models suffer from data sparsity, as the limited interaction density in real-world scenarios provides insufficient supervisory evidence for learning discriminative representations. In this work, we propose HyperGraph Convolutional Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (HGCN-GRU), a sequential recommendation framework that addresses both limitations through two complementary contributions. First, we replace the residual gating mechanism of existing hypergraph-based models with a Gated Recurrent Unit coupled with a temporal attention module. Unlike single-step propagation, the GRU models the sequence of per-period hypergraph embeddings as a temporal process, enabling the accumulation of semantic information across distant time steps, while the attention module adaptively emphasizes the most informative historical periods. Second, we introduce a self-supervised contrastive learning objective that generates auxiliary training signals directly from the hypergraph structure via stochastic hyperedge dropout augmentation. By aligning user representations derived from two independently augmented views, the contrastive module compensates for the scarcity of supervised signals in sparse interaction settings without requiring additional annotations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets of varying density, namely Amazon Review, MovieLens-1 M, and Yelp, demonstrate that HGCN-GRU consistently outperforms seven competitive baselines across all evaluation metrics. The proposed model consistently outperforms the strongest baseline across datasets with varying interaction densities. The improvements remain substantial across datasets, including the sparsest setting, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework under different levels of interaction sparsity. Ablation studies further confirm that the GRU-based temporal memory and the contrastive objective address complementary weaknesses of existing hypergraph recommendation frameworks.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: gated recurrent unit; self-supervised contrastive learning; temporal attention; data sparsity; hypergraph convolutional network; temporal memory; long-range temporal dependencies

Article.Title: Unraveling nonlinear ecosystem water use efficiency dynamics and environmental drivers across Iran using remote sensing and XGBoost-SHAP
Article.Authors: Kazemzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how ecosystems regulate the trade-off between carbon assimilation and water loss is essential for assessing ecohydrological stability in water-limited regions. This study investigated ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE) dynamics across Iran from 2001 to 2025 using an integrated framework combining multi-source remote sensing datasets, polynomial trend analysis, optimized eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Morris global sensitivity analysis (Morris GSA). A polynomial regression approach was employed to characterize linear and nonlinear WUE trends across Köppen–Geiger climate zones and land cover types. In addition, XGBoost-SHAP-Morris GSA modeling identified dominant climatic and environmental drivers, characterized their nonlinear effects, and quantified WUE sensitivity. The results indicated that valid WUE estimates covered approximately 44% of Iran’s total area, of which 23.75% experienced significant long-term WUE trends, with increases (20.39%) substantially exceeding decreases (3.36%). Linear trends were the dominant pattern, covering 17.1% of this area (72.2% of all significant trends), while nonlinear trends accounted for 6.6% of this area. The magnitude of significant WUE trends ranged from –0.97 to 0.90 g C m −2 mm −1 decade⁻ 1 , with increasing trends mainly distributed across western, southwestern, and northern coastal Iran, particularly along the Zagros and Alborz mountain ranges, where changes were more associated with changes in GPP than ET. Among land cover types, grasslands (11.9%) and croplands (5.8%) showed the largest proportions of significant WUE trends. The XGBoost–SHAP analysis revealed that NDVI (50.98% relative contribution), LAI (19.81%), and solar radiation (17.44%) were the dominant factors explaining the variability of WUE. The Morris GSA indicated that modeled WUE responses were primarily sensitive to NDVI (24.00% relative sensitivity, μ* = 0.827), followed by air temperature (20.35%, μ* = 0.701) and solar radiation (16.52%, μ* = 0.569), whereas LST, soil moisture, and wind speed exhibited comparatively weaker overall sensitivity. This study characterizes WUE dynamics across Iran and identifies key environmental factors associated with WUE variability, providing insights into ecosystem water-use dynamics in water-limited regions.

Article.Title: Locomotive dysfunction and spinopelvic sagittal alignment in relation to falls and stumbling in community-dwelling adults: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Nakano T.; Wada K.; Kumagai G.; Kaneko S.; Alnouri M.; Murashita K.; Tanaka S.; Ishibashi Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Falls and stumbling are commonly analyzed as a single outcome, although only falls cause injury and the two events may have different correlates. We examined both in 531 adults from the 2021 Iwaki Health Promotion Project who answered separate questions about falls and stumbling and underwent standing full-spine lateral radiography. Logistic regression models included age, sex, skeletal muscle index, sleep medication use, the 25-question Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale (GLFS-25), and one spinopelvic sagittal parameter. Overall, 83 participants (15.6%) reported a fall, 165 (31.1%) stumbling, and 188 (35.4%) either event. GLFS-25 was associated with all outcomes in every age stratum: the adjusted odds ratio per point was 1.095 (95% CI 1.055–1.137) for either event and 1.062 (1.028–1.098) for falls alone. Removing its two anxiety items reduced the area under the curve only from 0.702 to 0.682. Sagittal alignment was significantly associated only with stumbling: a smaller sagittal vertical axis in participants aged < 65 years and a larger T1 pelvic angle in those aged ≥ 65 years. However, multinomial regression did not distinguish its associations with stumbling and falls. Locomotive dysfunction was associated with both events and can be assessed without equipment, whereas the radiographic findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Risk assessment of insulator contamination in thermal power plants by integrating dynamic physical priors and spatiotemporal heterogeneous graphs
Article.Authors: Qi Z.; Hua Z.; Su Z.; Li W.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: To address the problem of predicting insulator fouling risks at thermal power plants resulting from the combined effects of various source-side facilities and meteorological conditions, we propose the Causal-STHGN model. This spatiotemporal heterogeneous graph model integrates dynamic physical priors. This paper first constructs a semantic graph of power plant entities. Source-side facility nodes are mapped to insulator monitoring points as heterogeneous nodes. Then, by integrating spatial geometric relationships, wind field directionality, source-side state characteristics, and moisture condition modulation, the model calculates dynamic physical causal priors and edge-weight priors. Furthermore, it constrains spatial dependency learning through a prior-bias graph attention mechanism. A parallel temporal structure is employed to jointly model short-term disturbances and long-term evolutionary trends. Finally, leakage current is used as a supervised proxy to calibrate the continuous risk representation, thereby evaluating the model’s ability to characterize key processes such as moisture-induced excitation and rain scouring. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method demonstrates strong overall performance across metrics including overall prediction accuracy, risk alerts, and physical consistency, and exhibits risk responses that are more in line with reality within typical event windows.

Article.Title: Contrasting responses to climate change in two Dianthus species of the Irano-Anatolian biodiversity hotspot
Article.Authors: Behroozian M.
Article.Abstract: The Irano-Anatolian biodiversity hotspot harbors exceptional plant richness and endemism but faces severe threats from climate change. We used MaxEnt-based ecological niche models to evaluate the current and future distributions of two closely related species, Dianthus floribundus and Dianthus szowitsianus. Models were projected for mid-century (2041–2070) and late-century (2071–2100) under SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Temperature-related predictors, particularly annual mean temperature (bio1) and temperature seasonality (bio4), were the dominant drivers, yet the species showed markedly different responses to future climates. D. floribundus, characterized by a narrow thermal niche, is predicted to undergo severe habitat contraction (up to 60%) and pronounced elevational and latitudinal shifts toward northern high-elevation refugia, consistent with the “escalator to extinction” paradigm for cold-adapted mountain taxa. In contrast, D. szowitsianus displayed broader climatic tolerance and ecological plasticity, maintaining most of its core range while expanding into newly suitable habitats, with projected gains exceeding 50%. These asymmetric outcomes highlight the species-specific nature of climate change impacts even among closely related endemics and forecast a decoupling of historical assemblages, with potential consequences for montane community structure and species interactions. Moreover, the reduction of overlap between the two species and the limited representation of persistent habitats within current protected areas underscore the urgent need for forward-looking conservation strategies. Our findings emphasize that conserving montane biodiversity in global hotspots requires species-focused vulnerability assessments, identification of future refugia, and adaptive management frameworks to mitigate differential risks and preserve endemic diversity under climate change.

Article.Title: Prognostic significance and clinicopathologic prediction of tumor deposits in non-metastatic colon mucinous adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Qu Y.; Gong J.; Lan W.; Zhang J.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Colon mucinous adenocarcinoma (CMAC) is a prognostically unfavorable subtype in which tumor deposits (TDs) are an under-recognized adverse feature with uncertain prognostic relevance and a risk of under-detection. From the SEER database we assembled 1372 non‑metastatic CMAC patients (7:3 training/internal‑validation split) plus an external cohort of 398 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, using Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and logistic regression to characterize TD prognosis and to develop a model predicting TD presence. TDs were independently associated with poorer cancer-specific survival after adjustment for positive lymph node (PN) burden; no statistically significant TD × PN interaction was detected ( P > 0.05), although the PN = 0 subgroup estimate was imprecise and not statistically significant. A nomogram using six routine clinicopathologic predictors—tumor size, site, grade, invasion depth, PN count, and perineural invasion—predicted TD presence with good discrimination (AUC = 0.820, 0.768, 0.784 for training, internal‑validation, and external cohorts), good calibration (Brier 0.095, 0.098, 0.086), and positive net benefit at 5–25% threshold probabilities. Collectively, TDs provide adverse prognostic information after accounting for nodal burden in CMAC, and the nomogram, externally validated only for TD prediction, estimates the probability of recorded TD positivity and may help identify cases warranting additional pathological attention; the survival findings require further validation in multicenter studies.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of graph-based metabolic network representations using graph Kernels
Article.Authors: García I.; Palmer-Rodríguez P.; Chouaia B.; Llabrés M.; Simeoni M.
Article.Abstract: Background: Metabolism comprises a series of interconnected chemical reactions, forming a complex network that can be naturally represented as a graph. In this paper, we investigate the expressive power of three graph-based representations of metabolic networks: Abstract Metabolic Networks (AMNs), metabolic Directed Acyclic Graphs (m-DAGs), and Reaction Graphs (RGs). These representations provide a hierarchical view of metabolism, with AMNs being the most abstract, m-DAGs representing an intermediate level of detail, and RGs offering the most fine-grained view. Results: Using a comprehensive set of species from the KEGG database, we construct their metabolic networks with all three representations (i.e., AMN, m-DAG, and RG), resulting in three corresponding datasets. We apply topological analyses to highlight the distinct characteristics of the three datasets and conduct a series of metabolic network comparison tests using five selected graph kernels. The conducted experiments empirically show that, although RGs provide the highest level of detail, their expressiveness is comparable to, and in some cases slightly lower than, that of m-DAGs. AMNs, while less expressive overall, perform comparably to m-DAGs and RGs when comparing organisms from very distant taxonomic groups or those adapted to different environments, suggesting that coarse-grained representations can still capture key metabolic differences under certain conditions. Conclusions: The conducted tests empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of all three representations and the relevance of the chosen kernels for comparing metabolic networks. Additionally, these findings could serve as a useful baseline reference for exploring representation and kernel choices in metagenomic or metatranscriptomic datasets derived, e.g., from environmental samples.

Article.Title: Analytical framework for corona discharge modelling at small distances integrated with established propulsion relationships
Article.Authors: Moshkbar-Bakhshayesh K.
Article.Abstract: Electro-hydrodynamics (EHD) propulsion systems have attracted attention due to its potential for maintenance-free operation, greener energy, quieter, and more efficient technologies. This study aims to develop an analytical framework to investigate corona discharge characteristics in wire-NACA 00xx airfoil electrode configurations, which can serve as a module within a larger modular propulsion system. The analytical method developed in this study follows a step by step aiming for compatibility with experimental results. One of the most critical elements of this approach is creating an accurate approximation for corona discharge, which is rigorously validated against experimental data. The comparison between the proposed analytical results and experimental data shows a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.13% for a 20 mm electrode gap, indicating strong predictive accuracy for corona discharge at small distances. The framework integrates established analytical relationships for EHD force, drag force, thrust, power consumption, and effectiveness to provide a complete engineering analysis tool. Various parameters such as effectiveness (i.e., thrust to power), thrust, power consumption, electric potential, and corona discharge are investigated in relation to each other and in relation to the gap between the electrodes, for the given module. While the corona discharge component is experimentally validated, the remaining propulsion quantities are derived from established physical relationships and are intended for preliminary engineering guidance and parametric studies. The summary of the results can be given in two main parts. (1) The ionic wind propulsion is impractical for large aerodynamic systems (e.g., achieving 330 kN thrust of a commercial jet engine would require approximately 500 million modules) and it can be used as independent propulsion for very small systems and as an auxiliary propulsion for small to medium systems. (2) The ionic wind propulsion is a constrained multi-objective optimization problem with the constraints including the main system parameters (e.g., minimum thrust needed, mass, etc.) and the input parameters (e.g., high voltage power supply (HPVS)), and objectives including thrust, effectiveness, etc.

Article.Title: Prioritizing heat stress indices for cognitive performance assessment using a Fuzzy Delphi–FAHP framework
Article.Authors: Mousavi S.; Dehghan H.; Yazdanirad S.
Article.Abstract: Occupational heat exposure induces physiological strain and can impair cognitive performance, exacerbating occupational error and accident risks. Although numerous heat stress indices exist, their theoretical and practical suitability for cognitive-related assessments remains ambiguous. This study established a structured multicriteria decision-making framework integrating the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM) and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to prioritize candidate heat stress indices for occupational cognitive risk evaluation. Candidate indices and screening criteria identified via literature review and expert consensus ( \(n=25\) ) were evaluated using FDM, followed by FAHP with Chang’s extent analysis to derive criteria weights and overall index priorities. A one-at-a-time \(+10\%\) sensitivity analysis was performed to verify model stability. Following FDM screening, six criteria and seven indices were retained. Predictive capability for cognitive performance (weight: 0.265), physiological relevance (0.229), and reliability/reproducibility (0.177) emerged as the most critical evaluation criteria. Among evaluated indices, the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI, priority: 0.214) ranked highest, followed by Predicted Heat Strain (PHS, 0.201) and Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT, 0.168), whereas traditional empirical indices demonstrated lower suitability. Sensitivity analysis confirmed exceptional rank stability (Spearman’s \(\rho\:=0.964-1.000\) ). Overall, comprehensive, physiologically grounded thermal indices provide superior suitability for cognitive-related heat stress assessment over simple empirical metrics. The proposed framework delivers a transparent, robust decision-support tool for occupational safety and health practitioners.

Article.Title: Development of a nonparametric spatial standardized precipitation–temperature index for regional drought characterization
Article.Authors: Bint E Nasir F.; Khan N.; Ali Z.; Scholz M.
Article.Abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging natural hazards, caused by prolonged shortages of precipitation and changes in temperature that reduce water availability. Reliable assessment of drought conditions across space is essential for sustainable water resource management and effective climate adaptation. However, most existing drought indices are designed for temporal analysis and often rely on probability distribution assumptions that may not adequately capture the spatial variability of drought-related variables. This study proposes a new drought monitoring framework, the Spatial Standardized Precipitation–Temperature Index (SSPTI), for assessing drought conditions across space. The index is based on a precipitation–temperature drought variable and employs a nonparametric standardization procedure applied independently at each time step. To examine the suitability of distribution-based standardization, several probability distributions and three component GMM were evaluated. The results showed considerable variation in distributional behavior over time, indicating that probabilistic framework may not consistently represent the spatial drought variable. The proposed methodology was applied to monthly precipitation and temperature records from 42 spatial locations across Pakistan for the period 1981–2021. Variogram analysis revealed clear seasonal differences in spatial dependence, while geostatistical interpolation techniques were used to generate continuous drought maps. The resulting SSPTI provides a simple, flexible, and distribution-free measure of relative spatial dryness and wetness conditions. By avoiding restrictive distributional assumptions, the proposed framework provides a practical tool for drought monitoring and spatial drought assessment over large geographical regions.

Article.Title: A hybrid artificial intelligence framework for three-dimensional electromagnetic field mapping using airborne measurements in general aviation
Article.Authors: Michałowska J.; Tomiło P.
Article.Abstract: The increasing electrification of aircraft systems and development of autonomous aviation technologies increase the need for accurate characterization of electromagnetic field (EMF) distributions under operational conditions. However, dense three-dimensional EMF measurements in aviation environments are difficult to obtain because airborne observations are typically sparse, irregularly distributed, and collected under varying flight conditions. Here, we present an artificial intelligence-based framework for three-dimensional reconstruction of the electric field component of EMF from real-world airborne measurements in general aviation. The study uses more than 80 h of measurements collected during operational activities involving four aircraft types and a low-cost, high-sensitivity sensing platform recording synchronized electric-field and geospatial data over the 1-8000 MHz frequency range. Geostatistical and machine-learning approaches, including Kriging, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and Exact Gaussian Processes, were evaluated for three-dimensional field reconstruction. Based on this comparison, we developed a hybrid Deep Gaussian Process Kolmogorov-Arnold Feature Extractor (DGKAN), combining nonlinear feature representation with probabilistic spatial modeling and uncertainty estimation. DGKAN achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.0381 and a mean squared error of 0.0071, reducing the mean absolute error by approximately 27.6% relative to the strongest baseline model. These results demonstrate that combining Kolmogorov-Arnold representations with probabilistic Gaussian Process modeling enables accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional electromagnetic field distributions from sparse airborne measurements. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach for electromagnetic environment assessment in general aviation and establishes a basis for further development of intelligent EMF monitoring and prediction methods under operational flight conditions.

Article.Title: Fossil shark teeth record a microscale pathway for ferromanganese oxide nucleation and Li–Ni enrichment in deep-sea biogenic substrates
Article.Authors: Felipe T.; Ferraz A.; Bernardini S.; Chappaz A.; Becker-Kerber B.; Galante D.; Jovane L.; Ulsen C.; Ardakani O.; Czas J.; Moreno V.; Caradec V.; Millo C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. Here, we integrate Micro-CT, SEM-EDS, EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, TEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XANES to reconstruct the initial stages of Fe–Mn oxide (FMO) formation in fossil shark teeth from the Rio Grande Rise (southwestern Atlantic Ocean). We document a four-stage FMO mineralization sequence preserved within dentin tubules: (1) bioapatite alteration and organic matter degradation, potentially associated with endolithic bioerosion; (2) precipitation of nanoscale goethite onto dentin tubule walls, associated with phosphate release and pH buffering; (3) Mn oxidation and precipitation of lithiophorite, a layered Mn(III–IV) oxide enriched in Li (~ 650 µg g –1 ) and Ni (~ 37,000 µg g –1 ) overgrowing goethite, with lithiophorite-bearing domains characterized by a high average Mn oxidation state of ~ 3.6; and (4) selective redistribution of REY into altered bioapatite, while Ce remains preferentially associated with FMO, followed by late clay-rich infilling. These results highlight the importance of biogenic substrates and confined dentin microenvironments in early FMO nucleation and phase-specific metal redistribution and retention, providing a microscale model for metal partitioning during the initial stages of deep-sea FMO mineralization.

Article.Title: Fine-scale characterization of dispersed-village landscapes: data challenges and methodological advances for rural landscape mapping and assessment in Pomerania, Poland
Article.Authors: Piniarski W.; Stępniewska M.; Borysiak J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dispersed-village landscapes in Pomerania are shaped by local environmental conditions and long-term farming practices, yet standard spatial datasets generalize many fine-scale landscape elements. In this pilot study, we developed and tested a fine-scale mapping and assessment approach at the 64-ha Knyki-1 reference site using a custom 3-level land-use/land-cover (LULC) scheme, an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived digital surface model (DSM), field mapping, plant-cover inventories, and GIS analysis. We compared custom mapping with CORINE Land Cover (CLC) and the Topographic Objects Database (BDOT10k) using landscape- and class-level metrics. At the Knyki-1 site, standard datasets strongly generalized or omitted small patches, linear elements, woody structures, and structural transition zones that may correspond to ecotonal structures. The custom mapping represented 21 LULC classes and 148 patches, versus 2–6 classes and 6–28 patches in the standard datasets, showing how dataset choice affects landscape representation and structural inference. Field inventories documented ancient-forest indicators, archaeophytes, and protected vascular-plant taxa across multiple landscape components. The resulting fine-scale baseline may support future repeated monitoring and, after multi-site validation, regional landscape assessment, conservation planning, and management. These natural–cultural rural landscapes remain absent from national landscape classifications and are increasingly vulnerable to pressures from the abandonment of traditional agriculture.

Article.Title: The associations between muscle strength and executive function among Chinese adolescents
Article.Authors: Li L.; Zhang M.; Zhang F.; Bi C.; Sun P.
Article.Abstract: Executive function, as a core cognitive function of the brain, holds significant importance for adolescents’ academic performance and future achievements. However, there has been relatively little research on this topic in the past. This study may provide theoretical support for the promotion and intervention of executive function in Chinese adolescents. A stratified cluster random sampling method was employed to conduct a cross-sectional assessment of grip strength, standing long jump, executive function, and related covariates among 10,145 adolescents aged 13–18 years across five distinct regions of China. In the stratified analyses, higher MSI was associated with progressively lower odds of deficits in executive function in mid-to-late adolescence, and the inverse association between MSI and working-memory insufficiency was stronger in girls(OR = 0.802, 95% CI: 0.763–0.843, P = 0.006) than boys(OR = 0.888, 95% CI: 0.792–0.996, P = 0.006). After controlling for relevant covariates, each 1-SD increase in MSI was associated with decreases of 0.254 ms, 41.185 ms and 20.311 ms in the reaction times for inhibition, working memory, and shifting, respectively (all P < 0.01). Muscle strength in Chinese adolescents correlates with working memory and shifting abilities but shows no associationwith inhibition. These findings suggest that muscle strength is associated with specific components of executive function in Chinese adolescents; because the data are cross-sectional, longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether promoting muscle strength can enhance executive function.

Article.Title: Discovery of natural flavanones as potential PRMT4 inhibitors with antiproliferative activity against colorectal cancer cells
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Li M.; Liu K.; Liang S.
Article.Abstract: Protein arginine N-methyltransferase 4 (PRMT4) has been a novel target to discover anticancer drugs, and PRMT4 inhibitors offer a promising option for the treatment of colorectal cancer. In this work, a series of natural flavanones were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against PRMT4. Lespedezaflavanone H was predicted to form hydrogen bonds with ASN-265 and ARG-267 of PRMT4, as revealed by molecular docking. Chemical descriptors and molecular electrostatic potential analysis of Lespedezaflavanone H were deeply investigated. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that the complex between PRMT4 and Lespedezaflavanone H maintained a stable binding mode. Importantly, Lespedezaflavanone H inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer cell lines RKO, SW620, COLO 205, and LS180 with IC 50 values of 3.93, 2.32, 5.68, and 11.26 µM, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report that Lespedezaflavanone H acts as a PRMT4 inhibitor and exhibits antiproliferative activity against colorectal cancer cells.

Article.Title: Robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework with complex entropy-aware and wavelet convolution
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Li G.; Zhou B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework based on unsupervised domain adaptation with a teacher-student self-training paradigm. The proposed framework introduces complex entropy-aware attention and wavelet convolution to enhance target representation under severe weather degradation. Aiming at the domain distribution differences in multi-weather scenarios, the framework alleviates such differences through more robust category-level prototype matching and global statistical characteristic learning based on DATR (domain adaptive detection transformer model). First, to alleviate feature uncertainty introduced by adverse weather noise, we design a complex entropy-aware attention mechanism that estimates channel-wise Shannon entropy and assigns adaptive weights according to feature information concentration. Instead of simply emphasizing uncertain responses, the proposed mechanism suppresses high-entropy ambiguous features while preserving low-entropy discriminative representations that remain more reliable under weather-induced degradation. Next, to solve the limitations of traditional convolution in capturing the global context of small objects and distinguishing objects from noise, we propose to use wavelet convolution to leverage frequency-domain multi-scale decomposition and large receptive fields, strengthening the capture of global context for small objects and improving the distinction between objects and noise through frequency filtering. Finally, to further improve the stability of teacher model evolution under cross-weather domain shifts, we design a grouped EMA (exponential moving average) strategy. Unlike conventional Mean Teacher or BYOL frameworks that employ a globally fixed decay coefficient, the proposed strategy dynamically adjusts grouped parameter updating rates according to feature adaptation requirements, providing a more flexible optimization trajectory for domain adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves UAV small object detection performance under several adverse weather domain-shift scenarios, while showing promising robustness against weather-induced feature degradation.

Article.Authors: Zhou Z.; Liu J.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address over-engineering risk at the fuzzy front end of multi-attribute-coupled passive wearable wellness devices (PWWDs) development, this study develops a lean-oriented Kano–QFD hierarchical decision framework guided by the lean principles of value maximization and waste elimination. The Kano model classifies and screens customer requirements (CRs), QFD translates the retained requirement information into EC technical weights, and a distribution-referenced parameterized tiering rule converts these continuous weights into high-, intermediate-, and low-priority resource-allocation tiers. A multisensory aromatherapy wearable accessory serves as the empirical case. Distributional diagnostics, sensitivity analysis of the threshold coefficient k , and comparison with Pareto analysis are used to examine tier stability and allocation differences. The case excludes two Indifferent CRs and assigns 13 ECs to a 4–5–4 configuration. Shape–Style Compatibility, Overall Net Weight, Design Symbol Application Rate, and Sustainable Material Ratio form the high-priority tier. Compared with Pareto analysis, parameterized tiering retains the same lower-end EC subset while further dividing the Pareto priority set into high- and intermediate-priority tiers.

Article.Title: Prosthesis embodiment predicts reduced amputation salience as reflected in dreams
Article.Authors: Bekrater-Bodmann R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The amputation of a limb requires substantial physical and psychosocial adjustment to a changed life situation. As a prosthesis often facilitates this process, its integration into one’s body representation, referred to as prosthesis embodiment, has been proposed as a marker of adjustment. Building on previous evidence that negative consequences of limb amputation are reflected in how the own body is experienced in dreams, this study examined whether prosthesis embodiment mitigates such effects. In 192 prosthesis-using individuals with acquired lower limb amputation, dream recall frequency, recalled body appearance in dreams (impaired, intact, or not remembered), and indicators of psychosocial adjustment were assessed. Dreams most frequently featured an intact body. In 113 dream recallers, higher prosthesis embodiment, unlike other psychosocial indicators, was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of recalling an impaired body. No association emerged for recalling an intact body or for absent body recall. This asymmetric pattern supports the continuity hypothesis of dreaming, suggesting that an embodied prosthesis loses salience as an amputation cue, thereby reducing waking concerns about impairment reflected in dreams. The findings provide empirical evidence that prosthesis embodiment represents cognitive integration of the device into the self-model, marking the transition from salient foreign-body representation to non-salient self-representation.

Article.Authors: Inami T.; Kuroko R.; Yoshikawa A.; Yabuno N.; Yamaguchi S.; Nishioka T.; Ikeda N.; Murayama M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigated the acute effects of eccentric exercise on the electrical properties and body water compartments of exercised and non-exercised segments using direct segmental multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (DSMF-BIA), a method that enables assessment of multiple body segments within a single acquisition. They completed five sets of 10 eccentric contractions using a dumbbell load corresponding to 50% of the maximal voluntary contraction force of the left elbow flexors, as determined during a familiarization session. DSMF-BIA parameters were measured before and immediately after exercise. In the exercised segment, exercise significantly altered impedance, resistance, reactance, phase angle, total body water, intracellular water, and extracellular water. Notably, the most pronounced changes in electrical properties occurred at 5 kHz. In the non-exercised segments, electrical properties at several frequencies and body water compartments changed significantly, whereas effect sizes remained uniformly trivial to small. These findings suggest that DSMF-BIA, within a single acquisition, has potential utility for evaluating marked local responses in exercised muscle while distinguishing them from the trivial variations in non-exercised segments.

Article.Title: Transient response of a cylindrical cavity in three-dimensional elastic space under impact loading: an analytical solution
Article.Authors: Ou C.; Liu M.; Li Y.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: The transient dynamic response of a cylindrical cavity in an elastic medium under impact loading is a fundamental problem in geotechnical engineering, with direct applications to tunnel and pipeline safety. While most existing analytical studies adopt two-dimensional plane-strain assumptions or steady-state harmonic incidence, the present work establishes a genuinely three-dimensional analytical model for a cylindrical cavity subjected to a triangular impulse load. Using the wave function expansion method and Laplace transform, we derive general frequency-domain solutions for stresses and displacements in cylindrical coordinates. Time-domain solutions are obtained via Durbin’s numerical inverse Laplace transform and validated against pendulum impact test data. The results show good agreement in first-wave trends and peak values, with peak errors within 20%. Parametric analysis reveals that doubling the cavity diameter reduces the peak longitudinal vibration velocity by 13.4% and the peak longitudinal stress by 3.2%, indicating that velocity is more sensitive to aperture changes. Halving the shear modulus increases the peak longitudinal velocity by 25.5% and decreases the peak longitudinal stress by 23.1%. The distributions of vibration velocity and stress around the cavity edge at different heights (z-axis positions) are presented: radial velocity peaks at 0° and 180° and increases with height; hoop stress exhibits four peak values at 30°, 150°, 210° and 330°, first increasing then decreasing with height. This three-dimensional transient solution provides a theoretical foundation for the dynamic design of underground cavities and highlights limitations of 2D approximations.

Article.Authors: Menda V.; Deepak M.; Gudimetla K.; Sura S.; venkatesh J.; Dasharath S.; Barik D.; Dennison M.; Shanmugapriya D.; Dinesh A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aims to investigate the effect of ethanol and Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) nanoparticles (NPs) as additives in Spirulina platensis oil methyl ester (SPOME)-diesel blends as pilot fuel, along with Hydrogen (H₂) as a secondary fuel, to determine the performance, combustion, and emission characteristics of a dual-fuel Compression Ignition (CI) diesel engine. A B20 blend (20% SPOME + 80% diesel) was initially prepared, followed by B20E20 (20% vol. of Ethanol + B20). Further, TiO₂ NPs (50 mg/L) were dispersed in the B20E20 sample. These additive-enhanced blends were tested in a dual-fuel CI engine, with and without H₂ induction, at varying loads. The stability and homogeneity of the NP-dispersed blends were confirmed through FESEM, HRTEM, FTIR, SAED, and XRD analyses. Performance parameters such as Brake Thermal Efficiency (BTE) increased by 10.4%, and Brake Specific Fuel Consumption (BSFC) decreased by 13.3% significantly for the B20E20 + TiO₂50 + 6H₂ blend at higher load. Emissions of CO, CO₂, and HC reduced by 36.3%, 6.68%, and 8.36%, respectively. Although NOx emissions slightly increased with H₂ induction, the B20E20 blend exhibited reduced NOx at higher load. Combustion characteristics, including Cylinder Pressure (CP) and Heat Release Rate (HRR), were enhanced by 11.53% and 7.91%, respectively, for the H₂-infused B20-alcohol-NP blend. Overall, the B20E20 + TiO₂50 + 6H₂ fuel formulation demonstrates strong potential as a sustainable alternative to conventional diesel in dual-fuel CI diesel engines.

Article.Title: Nonlinear effects and spatial spillovers of emerging industry clustering on welfare performance under renewable energy transition in China''s urban agglomerations
Article.Authors: Tang T.; Mo J.; Wei X.
Article.Abstract: The global energy transition is currently hindered by inefficient welfare conversion and regional disparities, which have precipitated a "new resource curse" across Chinese urban agglomerations. The resulting welfare divergence between production and consumption zones underscores the urgency of optimizing industrial spatial allocation—a prerequisite for fulfilling the nation''s "dual carbon" objectives. Based on 2014–2023 POI data from eight emerging sectors, this study characterizes the spatial patterns of 19 urban agglomerations using Kernel Density Estimation. It employs an improved enhanced group-frontier dynamic SBM model with super-efficiency to gauge the welfare performance under renewable energy transition (WPRE) and develops an integrated XGBoost-SHAP-GEO model to reveal the non-linear associations and spatial spillover effects of industrial agglomeration. The study reveals: ①A "plateaued fluctuation and volatile growth" trajectory defines WPRE of Chinese urban agglomerations; ②emerging industry agglomerations exhibit polycentric evolution and a strengthening core-periphery architecture; ③the association between emerging industry agglomeration and WPRE is non-monotonic, consistent with diminishing rather than reversing returns; ④Geospatial characteristics, together with their interaction effects, constitute the primary predictors of WPRE, with associations exhibiting substantial stage-specific heterogeneity. Uncovering the nonlinear associations and spatial heterogeneity of industrial agglomeration, this work offers a scientific basis for breaking the ''new resource curse'' and enhancing industry-energy-welfare synergy. The conclusions provide significant policy implications for global resource-rich regions striving to promote inclusive welfare distribution within the renewable energy transition.

Article.Title: A multi-task learning approach for consumer sentiment classification and emotion detection via behavioral data
Article.Authors: Alam F.; Kamal A.; Meraj M.; Fazil M.; Kamal A.; Khan S.; Faridi S.; Sejwal V.; Qamar S.; Almakki R.
Article.Abstract: Sentiment analysis captures overall opinion polarity, but it often fails to reveal the key emotions that drive consumer behavior. The recognition of both sentiment and emotions provides crucial information to uncover underlying drivers of consumers behavior and brand loyalty. These important insights enable businesses to detect emerging issues, refine products and services, and personalize consumer experiences. This study proposes a multi-task approach that performs sentiment classification and emotion detection tasks based on consumer reviews and corresponding ratings. To this end, we propose Consumer Sentiment and Emotion Modeling ( COSMO-MT ), a deep learning-based multi-task model for sentiment classification and emotion detection. It begins with an input layer followed by embedding layers that provide sentiment-specific, emotion-specific, and shared embeddings from the input text. Each embedding is processed through shared layers consisting of CNN, BiLSTM, and attention mechanisms. Moreover, several auxiliary features are incorporated into the shared layers to provide explicit linguistic information. The outputs of the shared layers are then passed to task-specific layers for sentiment classification and emotion detection. Finally, corresponding dense and output layers generate predictions for both tasks. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed COSMO-MT model on two publicly available datasets. It significantly outperforms existing studies and baseline methods.

Article.Title: Minocycline attenuates gulf war illness-related pain sensitization and preserves descending control of nociception in mice
Article.Authors: Sanaei Esfahani S.; Sahbaie P.; Shi X.; Mahinparvar N.; Huang T.; Clark J.
Article.Abstract: Gulf War Illness (GWI) is a chronic multisymptom condition characterized by widespread pain. In a murine model of GWI-related chemicals exposure for one month, the efficiency of endogenous pain control systems, latent pain sensitization and anxiety state were examined. Circulating cytokines were quantified with multiplex assay and ELISAs. Effects of minocycline treatment were evaluated in GWI mice. We observed robust periorbital sensitization after exposure to the bright light stress (BLS headache model), increased hindpaw allodynia in osteoarthritis and musculoskeletal pain models in GWI mice. Minocycline reduced or eliminated the GWI chemical-related excess sensitization and loss of descending control of nociception (DCN), suggesting the drug preserves a key component of endogenous pain modulation. GWI-related chemical exposure caused a mild anxiety-like state not prevented by minocycline. Multiplexed analysis of plasma cytokines revealed no significant differences 3 months after completion of chemical administration between control mice and other treatment groups. However, a more sensitive ELISA demonstrated elevation of circulating MCP-1 in GWI chemical-treated mice, which was blocked by co-treatment with minocycline. Our findings suggest that the widespread pain-related complaints characteristic of GWI may be due to loss of DCN. Minocycline, potentially through its anti-neuroinflammatory activity, prevents damage to endogenous pain control systems.

Article.Title: Differential associations of baseline, dynamic change, and cumulative average TyG-BMI with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a longitudinal landmark analysis of CHARLS
Article.Authors: Wu Z.; Guo C.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is common, yet the prognostic relevance of temporal triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) measures remains unclear. A 2015 landmark analysis of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study included 4597 participants. Baseline TyG-BMI was measured in 2011; dynamic change and cumulative average were derived from 2011 and 2015 measurements. Incident CMM was ascertained during 2015–2020. Discrete-time complementary log–log models estimated associations, with supplementary analyses of the 2015 landmark value, disease transitions, component outcomes, and bootstrap validation. Overall, 528 participants developed CMM. Baseline and cumulative average TyG-BMI were associated with CMM (HR per 1-SD increase 1.28, 95% CI 1.17–1.40; and 1.25, 95% CI 1.14–1.37, respectively), with linear dose–response patterns. Dynamic change was not independently associated after baseline adjustment (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.89–1.04). The 2015 landmark value was also associated with CMM (HR 1.19, 95% CI 1.09–1.30), and residualized cumulative average remained associated after accounting for this value (HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.08–1.27). Among cases with complete landmark disease status, 80.7% had one existing condition; baseline and cumulative average associations extended across all three components and CMM transitions with or without newly acquired diabetes. Bootstrap-corrected improvement beyond the 2015 value was small (ΔAUC 0.004, 95% CI − 0.0002 to 0.0076). Baseline, current, and cumulative average TyG-BMI identified higher CMM risk, whereas short-term change added little information. TyG-BMI may complement clinical risk assessment, but its added predictive value was modest.

Article.Title: Two novel Silviavirus phages with lytic activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus: genomic and phenotypic characterization
Article.Authors: VinodKumar C.; Veni Emilda J.; Prasad B.; Arunkumar A.; Jayasimha V.; Nachimuthu R.; Veeraraghavan B.; Kalasuramath S.
Article.Abstract: The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Staphylococcus aureus , particularly methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), necessitates alternative antimicrobial strategies. Here, we isolated and characterized two bacteriophages, CARØ0038 and CARØ0046, from sewage in Davangere, Karnataka, India, using MRSA as the host. Transmission electron microscopy revealed icosahedral heads with short tails, consistent with the class Caudoviricetes . Whole-genome sequencing identified genomes of 120,939 bp and 136,667 bp, with 227 and 225 predicted coding sequences and GC contents of 29.5% and 29.1%, respectively. Whole-genome phylogenomic and taxonomic analyses placed both phages within the genus Silviavirus and supported their distinction from closely related reference phages, although the available analyses did not establish definitive species-level assignment. Both phages exhibited efficient lytic activity against MRSA, with an MOI of 0.1 yielding the highest experimentally observed titres. One-step growth analysis demonstrated apparent latent periods of 15–20 min and burst sizes of 49 and 47 PFU/cell for CARØ0038 and CARØ0046, respectively. Both phages showed high infectivity up to 37 °C, with marked reductions at 45–50 °C and no detectable recovery at 60 °C. Maximum recovery occurred at pH 7, with no detectable infectious phage outside pH 6–8. Host-range analysis demonstrated clear lysis against all 28 MRSA isolates tested and activity against methicillin-susceptible S. aureus , while no detectable lysis was observed against S. epidermidis or S. saprophyticus under the conditions tested. No known antimicrobial resistance-associated or virulence-associated genes were identified. Collectively, these findings support CARØ0038 and CARØ0046 as distinct Silviavirus phages with efficient lytic activity against S. aureus , including MRSA, and provide a basis for further investigation of their potential as phage-based antimicrobial candidates.

Article.Title: Multi-omics analysis reveals protein-driven modulation of growth and metabolism in Gangba sheep under different dietary protein levels
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Jiacuo G.; Bandan P.; Jiba B.; Imran M.; Zhuoga D.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the effects of different dietary protein concentrations’ influence on Gangba sheep’s growth metrics, nutrient absorption efficiency, carcass characteristics, meat quality via integrated 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics and transcriptomic analysis. These multi-omics approaches revealed that moderate protein supplementation coordinately regulated gut microbial composition and host metabolic and immune pathways. Forty one-year-old Gangba sheep were randomly allocated to four dietary treatments (n = 10 per group) receiving protein levels equivalent to 0.9 × (14.25%), 1.0 × (16.12%), 1.1 × (17.84%), and 1.2 × (19.31%) of the standard concentrate feed. Compared with the 0.9 × group, sheep fed higher protein levels exhibited significantly greater final body weight and average daily gain ( p < 0.05). The 0.9 × group also showed significantly higher fecal crude fiber, calcium, phosphorus, neutral detergent fiber, and acid detergent fiber contents, indicating lower nutrient utilization. Antioxidant status improved with increased dietary protein, as evidenced by higher superoxide dismutase and lower malondialdehyde, aspartate aminotransferase, and alanine aminotransferase levels. Carcass weight, dressing percentage, lean weight, and meat-bone ratio were significantly improved in protein-supplemented groups, whereas centrifugal loss and unfavorable meat color parameters were reduced. Higher dietary protein also enhanced gastrointestinal morphology by increasing gastric mucosal thickness and villus height while reducing crypt depth. The 1.1 × protein group showed the most favorable intestinal architecture, with the highest villus height-to-crypt depth ratio. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed increased relative abundance of Firmicutes and reduced Bacteroidota in the 1.1 × group, accompanied by enrichment of beneficial bacteria such as Faecalibaculum and reductions in potentially harmful genera, including Streptococcus, Marvinbryantia, and Eubacterium. Transcriptomic analysis identified 365 differentially expressed genes in the 1.1 × group, mainly enriched in pathways related to immune regulation, protein digestion and absorption, bile secretion, and mineral transport. Correlation analysis further demonstrated strong associations between specific microbial taxa and growth, nutrient utilization, antioxidant status, carcass characteristics, and intestinal morphology. Overall, moderate protein supplementation at 1.1 × the standard level optimally improved growth performance, nutrient utilization, antioxidant capacity, meat quality, gut microbial composition, and metabolic and immune functions in Gangba sheep.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based mitotic quantification for objective adjunct for grading of urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional validation study
Article.Authors: Lee M.; Jang J.; Seo J.; Cho N.; Cha Y.; Park S.; Kim J.; Choe M.; Jung H.; Nahm J.; Yoo S.; Park H.; Park J.; Jang M.; Kim E.; Kim T.; Hong M.; Shin S.; Noh J.; Ha J.; Shin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Histological grading of urothelial carcinoma is subject to interobserver variability. We evaluated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-based whole-slide mitotic quantification provides an objective adjunct to histological grading. We developed and validated a deep learning-based mitotic detection framework trained on 91,183 patches with 318,893 annotations. A multi-reader crossover study was conducted in internal ( n = 149) and external ( n = 316) cohorts, where three independent pathologists graded cases in unassisted and model-assisted phases. In the combined cohort ( n = 465), AI-derived mitotic count showed high diagnostic accuracy for high-grade carcinoma (area under the curve [AUC] 0.91, 95% CI 0.89–0.94) at a cut-off of 17.5 mitoses per 2 mm². AI assistance significantly improved mean reader AUC from 0.90 to 0.98 in the internal cohort ( p = 0.038). In the external cohort, the mean reader AUC increased from 0.84 to 0.95, although this difference did not reach statistical significance ( p = 0.11). AI assistance also significantly reduced interobserver variability (Fleiss’s κ: 0.72 to 0.93 internally; 0.62 to 0.85 externally; both, p < 0.001). AI-based mitotic quantification provides an objective and standardized adjunct to histological grading and reduces interobserver variability. This approach may improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation.

Article.Title: A UCP1-IRES-Cre knock-in mouse enables specific brown adipocyte targeting without CNS off-target expression
Article.Authors: Meyer J.; Williams J.; Bailey J.; Chang J.; Elks C.; Münzberg H.
Article.Abstract: Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) is predominantly expressed in brown adipocytes, where it plays a central role in thermogenesis and energy metabolism. BAC-transgenic UCP1-Cre mouse lines have been widely used to target thermogenic adipocytes, but ectopic Cre activity in the hypothalamus and peripheral organs has raised concerns regarding specificity. Here, we characterize a novel knock-in UCP1-IRES-Cre mouse model that drives Cre expression from the endogenous UCP1 promoter. UCP1-IRES-Cre mice were crossed with Ai14 reporter mice to visualize Cre-dependent tdTomato expression across adipose depots, brain regions, and peripheral tissues and compared with UCP1 protein localization. Reporter expression in male and female UCP1-IRES-Cre mice closely mirrored endogenous UCP1 expression in brown and white adipose tissue depots, with substantially reduced ectopic activity compared with previously reported BAC-transgenic models. Minimal reporter expression was observed in the hypothalamus and peripheral organs, although robust reporter expression was detected in the choroid plexus despite absent UCP1 protein staining. White adipose depots exhibited broader reporter labeling than UCP1 immunoreactivity, consistent with transient or prior UCP1 promoter activation during development or adult life. Together, these findings demonstrate that the UCP1-IRES-Cre model faithfully recapitulates endogenous UCP1 expression while minimizing off-target Cre activity, providing a knock-in alternative for genetic targeting of thermogenic adipocytes.

Article.Title: Evaluation of morphological diversity of wild Iris species in Hatay Province, Türkiye
Article.Authors: Kaya S.; Uzunoğlu F.; Özmen K.; Mavi K.
Article.Abstract: This study, conducted during the 2019 and 2020 flowering seasons, aimed to characterize the morphological diversity of naturally occurring Iris species in the flora of Hatay province, Türkiye, and to evaluate their potential for use in the ornamental plant sector and as breeding material. Field observations showed that the number of flowers per stem ranged from 4 to 7 in I. pseudacorus , whereas I. kirkwoodiae , I. persica , I. histrio , and I. unguicularis generally produced a single flower per stem. Stem branching was absent in I. kirkwoodiae , I. persica , I. histrio , and I. unguicularis , while I. pseudacorus exhibited an average of three lateral branches. Flower longevity was found to be 4–5 days in I. persica , I. histrio , I. pseudacorus , and I. unguicularis , and 3–4 days in I. kirkwoodiae . The flowering periods were recorded as February-March for I. persica and I. histrio , March-April for I. unguicularis , April-May for I. pseudacorus , and May for I. kirkwoodiae . Multivariate analyses revealed clear morphological differentiation among the examined taxa, particularly for I. pseudacorus and I. kirkwoodiae , while I. persica and I. histrio showed relatively greater morphological proximity. The observed variation highlights the potential value of these populations for conservation, further evaluation, and ornamental plant breeding.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of laser diffraction and sieve-pipette techniques for grid-scale hydraulic characterization of lateritic vadose zones
Article.Authors: Biswal S.; Jha M.; Senapati D.
Article.Abstract: The vadose zone plays a vital role in sustaining society and ecosystems on the Earth. The complexity of vadose zones, coupled with expensive and laborious field investigations pose a formidable challenge in their characterization, and hence they are neglected in hydrogeologic studies. This study demonstrates a novel scientific framework for the grid-scale hydraulic characterization of vadose zones using the laser diffraction (LD) technique and grain-size analysis (GSA) models. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, a total of 126 vadose zone samples and 95 core samples were collected from four layers across 33 grids in a lateritic terrain of Eastern India. Thereafter, the efficacy of the advanced LD technique and the conventional sieve-pipette analysis (SP) was compared by generating grain-size distribution curves (GSDCs) and estimating vadose-zone hydraulic conductivity (K vz ) by using selected GSA models at four different depths (0–50 cm, 50–100 cm, 100–150 cm, and 150–200 cm), followed by an uncertainty analysis. Finally, the estimates of K vz based on the SP-GSA and LD-GSA models were verified using field-measured K vz . The analysis of GSDCs for different depths revealed that the LD technique yields smoother S-shaped GSDCs than the SP technique. Consistently, low uncertainty was found in the K vz estimated by the LD-GSA models (0.0002–1.203 m/day) compared to the K vz estimated by the SP-GSA models (0.0008–2.171 m/day). The verification results based on statistical and graphical indicators revealed that the K vz yielded by most of the LD-GSA models for all layers of the vadose zone are in close agreement with the measured K vz values [MAE: 0.38 to 0.89 m/day and RMSE: 0.6 to 0.98 m/day]. On the other hand, the performance of SP-GSA models was also found to be reasonable, yielding K vz values with MAE and RMSE ranging from 0.36 to 1.45 m/day and 0.64–1.74 m/day, respectively, across all the vadose-zone layers. It is concluded that the LD technique provides more reliable GSDCs, whereas both SP and LD techniques yield reliable K vz (using suitably selected GSA models), thereby offering a useful scientific framework for estimating K vz at a grid scale. The proposed framework provides a basis for transferability and future evaluation at a larger spatial scale under different hydrogeologic and hydro-climatic conditions.

Article.Title: Association of pre-existing cardiovascular disease with cardiovascular and clinical outcomes in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors
Article.Authors: Alfehaid L.; Alanazi A.; Alomran M.; Skouri H.; Alsuhebany N.
Article.Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but are increasingly associated with cardiovascular complications. The association between pre-existing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cardiovascular outcomes among patients receiving ICIs remains incompletely characterized, particularly in real-world settings. To evaluate the association between baseline CVD and cardiovascular and clinical outcomes among adult patients treated with ICIs. We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study at two tertiary hospitals in Saudi Arabia, including adult patients who received at least one ICI dose between January 2017 and January 2023. Baseline CVD was defined as documented cardiovascular disease before ICI initiation. The primary outcome was a composite of new cardiovascular events occurring after ICI initiation. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used multivariable logistic regression to identify factors independently associated with cardiovascular events, with sensitivity analyses incorporating additional cardiovascular risk factors. Among 608 patients, 54 (8.9%) had baseline CVD. Patients with baseline CVD were older and had a greater burden of comorbidities than those without baseline CVD. During follow-up, 69 patients (11.3%) experienced at least one cardiovascular event. Cardiovascular events occurred in 27 of 54 patients (50.0%) with baseline CVD compared with 42 of 554 patients (7.6%) without baseline CVD ( p < 0.001). Baseline CVD was independently associated with higher odds of cardiovascular events (adjusted OR, 9.46; 95% CI 4.92–18.17; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR per year, 1.04; 95% CI 1.01–1.06; p = 0.001). The association remained significant after additional adjustment for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and dyslipidemia (adjusted OR, 6.64; 95% CI 3.28–13.47; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was higher among patients with baseline CVD (64.8% vs. 46.4%, p = 0.010), and unadjusted median overall survival was shorter (11.5 vs. 23.8 months; log-rank p = 0.022). Cardiovascular events were predominantly ischemic and heart failure-related, whereas myocarditis was rare, occurring in only one patient overall. In this multicenter cohort, pre-existing CVD was independently associated with higher cardiovascular event odds among ICI patients, even after adjusting for risk factors. These patients also had shorter OS, though survival analysis was unadjusted. Findings suggest baseline CVD patients are vulnerable and may benefit from thorough risk assessment and cardio-oncology care. However, as an observational study without a non-ICI comparator, these associations do not prove ICI caused or worsened CVD.

Article.Title: Hierarchical dual-timescale deep reinforcement learning for mechanically rotatable STAR-RIS assisted mobile edge computing networks
Article.Authors: R D.; K. S P.
Article.Abstract: The integration of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address the challenges of latency-sensitive applications in dynamic wireless environments. This paper proposes a multi-rotational Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting RIS (STAR-RIS) assisted MEC framework that considers both mechanical reorientation and electronic control. Unlike conventional STAR-RIS systems with fixed orientations, the proposed architecture enables physical rotation of STAR-RIS panels to dynamically adjust spatial coverage and achieve improved geometric alignment with mobile users. A comprehensive system model is developed incorporating rotatable STAR-RIS panels, dual-region users, task offloading decisions, and wireless channel dynamics. To address the resulting mixed-timescale, non-convex stochastic optimization problem, a hierarchical dual-timescale Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) - based framework is proposed, where a slow-timescale agent controls mechanical rotation while fast-timescale agents jointly optimize electronic STAR-RIS parameters and MEC offloading decisions. A formal non-stationarity analysis demonstrates the superiority of dual-timescale DRL and a convergence rationale is established through two-timescale stochastic approximation theory. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves stable convergence and significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of task completion rate, fairness, sum rate, and energy efficiency. The findings highlight that mechanical rotation introduces an additional spatial degree of freedom and enhances the MEC performance in dynamic mobile environments.

Article.Title: Prevalence and functional impact of musculoskeletal pain among university students in seven Arab countries and its sociodemographic and lifestyle associations
Article.Authors: Samir A.; El-Ashry A.; Tawfik A.; El-Sayed M.; Abdelaziz O.; Mosali T.; Hamdy A.; Soliman E.; Tiryag A.; Mousalawi I.; Hatem N.; Hemida M.; Alzeer D.; Hachim O.; Howireth A.; Ahmed G.; Al-shayeb L.; Ghazy R.; Kabbash I.
Article.Abstract: Musculoskeletal pain (MSP) represents a major public health challenge globally, particularly among university students who are in a critical transitional phase of life characterized by intense academic demands, lifestyle changes, and increasing reliance on digital technologies. Sedentary behavior (SB) has been identified as a potential risk factor for MSP; however, evidence from the Arab region remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MSP in nine body regions (neck, shoulders, upper back, elbows, wrists/hands, lower back, hips/thighs, knees, and ankles/feet) across four time points (lifetime, past 12 months, past month, and today), to assess the impact of MSP, and examine the association between SB and MSP. A multinational cross-sectional study was conducted among 4300 university students in seven Arab countries (Egypt, Yemen, Iraq, Sudan, Jordan, Syria, and Palestine), using an online Arabic self-administered questionnaire. Convenience and snowball sampling methods were used to recruit eligible study respondents. MSP was assessed using the Arabic version of the Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ-E). SB was assessed using sedentary behavior questionnaire (SBQ). Chi-square tests were used for univariate associations. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with any MSP in the past 12 months, and to identify predictors of high SB. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported, and a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The prevalence of MSP in at least one body region was 84.0% (lifetime), 71.3% (past 12 months), and 64.9% (past month). The neck (49.3%) and lower back (37.3%) were the most affected regions in the past 12 months. Among those affected, preventing usual activities (range: 48.8%–71.7%) and taking medication (range: 37.6–48.2%) were the most reported impacts, while hospitalization remained relatively low (3.2–14.2%). Female sex (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.69–2.31), chronic diseases (aOR = 1.90, 95% CI 1.44–2.49), MSP family history (aOR = 1.96, 95% CI 1.56–2.47), moderate SB (aOR = 1.56, 95% CI 1.32–1.84), and high SB (aOR = 1.42, 95% CI 1.16–1.72) were significantly associated with MSP in the past 12 months, while sleeping 6–8 h was protective (aOR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.67–0.92). This study found a high prevalence of MSP among university students in Arab countries, particularly affecting the neck and lower back. Higher SB, chronic diseases, and a family history of MSP were associated with MSP, whereas adequate sleep appeared to be protective. These findings support the need for university-based strategies that reduce prolonged SB and promote musculoskeletal health, including ergonomic education, active breaks, adjustable study stations, and more active learning environments.

Article.Title: p300 activity and subcellular localization associate with tumor aggressiveness and clinical outcome in triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Fermento M.; Clemente V.; Gallardo G.; Masciovecchio M.; Villegas M.; Alonso E.; Ferronato M.; Coló G.; Arévalo J.; Juri M.; Jung M.; Facchinetti M.; Curino A.
Article.Abstract: Hormone-independent breast cancers are aggressive malignancies with limited targeted therapeutic options. Epigenetic regulators such as the transcriptional cofactor p300 (EP300), which possesses histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity, have been implicated in tumor progression; however, the contribution of p300 functional activity and subcellular localization to tumor aggressiveness and clinical outcome remains incompletely understood. Here, using triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as a model of hormone-independent aggressive tumors, we investigated the role of p300 activity and intracellular distribution through genetic silencing and pharmacological inhibition approaches. p300 depletion or HAT inhibition reduced tumor cell viability, induced apoptosis, and impaired metastatic dissemination both in vitro and in vivo. These effects were associated with alterations in epithelial–mesenchymal transition–related markers and cytoskeletal organization. Analysis of human TNBC specimens revealed a predominant cytoplasmic localization of p300 in tumor cells. Notably, exclusive cytoplasmic localization was associated with lower tumor stage and improved overall survival, independently of mutations affecting the HAT domain. Together, these findings identify p300 functional activity as a regulator of tumor aggressiveness and demonstrate that its subcellular localization provides clinically relevant prognostic information. Our results underscore the importance of considering both the activity and intracellular distribution of epigenetic regulators when evaluating their role as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in aggressive cancers.

Article.Title: Prediagnostic GERD is associated with mortality among patients with gastric cancer in a nationwide cohort
Article.Authors: Choi J.; Song J.; Kim Y.; Kim J.; Han Y.; Lee H.; Lee J.; Park Y.; Yang S.; Han K.
Article.Abstract: We investigated the survival outcomes of patients with newly diagnosed gastric cancer with prior gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). In this nationwide population‑based cohort study using the Korea Central Cancer Registry database (2012–2017), patients with gastric cancer aged ≥ 30 years with national health screening records were classified into the GERD and non-GERD groups. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, with secondary analyses including stage-specific outcomes and cause of death. Among 108,350 patients with gastric cancer, 14,237 (13.1%) were classified into the GERD group. Patients with GERD were diagnosed with gastric cancer at earlier disease stages than were those without GERD. However, all-cause mortality was higher in the GERD than in the non-GERD group (19.78% vs. 17.85%, P < 0.0001), including both gastric cancer-related and non-cancer-related deaths. The association remained after multivariable adjustment (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.13; 95% confidence interval, 1.08–1.17). The association was stage-specific, being strongest in the regional stage, followed by in the localized stage; no significant difference was observed in the distant stage. Presence of GERD in patients with gastric cancer was associated with earlier-stage diagnosis but higher mortality, suggesting that GERD may be associated with prognostic heterogeneity. Further studies should verify its potential role in risk stratification.

Article.Title: Climate-resilient tomato production: potassium nanoparticles regulate carbohydrate metabolism and oxidative defense under nanoplastic stress
Article.Authors: Bengisu G.; Atay U.; Durul M.; Khalofah A.; Faizan M.; Habib Y.
Article.Abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging environmental contaminants that threaten sustainable crop production and food safety by disrupting mineral nutrient homeostasis, impairing physiological processes, and inducing reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress. Nanoparticle-based interventions have emerged as a promising strategy for mitigating nanoplastic-induced phytotoxicity and enhancing plant stress resilience. In the present study, the protective effects of potassium nanoparticles (K-NPs; 10 mmol L⁻ 1 ) against nanoplastic-induced stress (4 mg kg⁻ 1 soil) were investigated in Solanum lycopersicum using a randomized complete block design with five biological replicates per treatment. Nanoplastics were applied to the soil, whereas K-NPs were administered as a foliar spray at 30 days after sowing (DAS). Nanoplastic exposure markedly inhibited plant growth and physiological performance, significantly reducing root length (68.81%), shoot dry weight (20.53%), SPAD chlorophyll value (70.85%), net photosynthetic rate (46.67%), protein content (13.82%), and Ca 2 ⁺ content (41.01%) relative to the control. In contrast, foliar application of K-NPs effectively alleviated these adverse effects, significantly enhancing shoot length (17.25%), leaf area (10.89%), and glucose content (18.62%) under nanoplastic stress. Furthermore, nanoplastic exposure markedly increased oxidative damage, as evidenced by elevated malondialdehyde (40.47%), hydrogen peroxide (26.87%), and superoxide anion (42.35%) levels, indicating severe membrane lipid peroxidation and excessive ROS accumulation. K-NP treatment substantially suppressed the accumulation of these oxidative stress markers while enhancing the activities of key antioxidant enzymes, including superoxide dismutase, catalase, and peroxidase, thereby strengthening the cellular antioxidant defense system. In addition, K-NPs restored mineral nutrient homeostasis and improved physiological and biochemical performance under nanoplastic stress. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that foliar application of K-NPs effectively mitigates nanoplastic-induced phytotoxicity by enhancing antioxidant capacity, maintaining nutrient homeostasis, and preserving physiological functions, highlighting their potential as a sustainable nanotechnology-based strategy for improving crop resilience under emerging nanoplastic pollution.

Article.Title: TAS-VANET: a trust-aware clustering and misbehavior management architecture for vehicular networks with whale-optimized deep detection
Article.Authors: Abdulkadhim F.; Abbas S.; Alashour G.; Mohammed M.; Hashim H.; Tang C.
Article.Abstract: Reliable operation of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) requires more than detecting individual falsified messages: misbehaving vehicles must be identified over time, excluded from privileged roles such as cluster head, and prevented from degrading routing performance. This paper presents TAS-VANET, a trust-aware clustering and misbehavior management architecture that couples (i) a weighted clustering scheme (WCS) for stable cluster-head election, (ii) a per-vehicle trust model updated by detector verdicts, and (iii) a compact supervised sparse autoencoder (SAE) with a skip connection, whose hyperparameters are tuned by the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). The detection component is validated on a public consolidation of the VeReMi Extension benchmark (88,029 records, 17 attack variants) under sender-disjoint 10-fold cross-validation, reaching a mean F1 of 0.8831 (held-out test F1 \(=\) 0.9036); WOA tuning contributes \(+9.34\) F1 points over the default-configured SAE (one-sided Wilcoxon \(p=9.77\times {10}^{-4}\) , paired across identical folds). The integrated system is evaluated in OMNeT + + /SUMO against two trust-based clustering protocols (TACR and QMM-VANET): at 195 vehicles TAS-VANET attains a packet delivery ratio of 89.0%, exceeding TACR by 2.0 percentage points and QMM-VANET by 14.0 percentage points (18.7% relative), with the margin over TACR widening from 2.0 to 3.5 percentage points at 90 km/h; deploying the tuned rather than the default configuration lowers end-to-end delay by 14.3% at the 10% malicious-vehicle ratio. We additionally report two transparent negative findings: strong tabular ensembles remain competitive per-message detectors on this benchmark, and constant-position-offset attacks are essentially undetectable from single-message kinematics alone (AUC \(\approx \) 0.529), which we frame as an open research problem. All reported values trace to released simulation and training artifacts.
